terms.name: Abnormality of body height
terms.definition: Deviation from the norm of height with respect to that which is expected according to age and gender norms.

terms.name: Multicystic kidney dysplasia
terms.definition: Multicystic dysplasia of the kidney is characterized by multiple cysts of varying size in the kidney and the absence of a normal pelvicaliceal system. The condition is associated with ureteral or ureteropelvic atresia, and the affected kidney is nonfunctional.

terms.name: Mode of inheritance
terms.definition: The pattern in which a particular genetic trait or disorder is passed from one generation to the next.

terms.name: Autosomal dominant inheritance
terms.definition: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on one of the autosomes (i.e., the human chromosomes 1-22) in which a trait manifests in heterozygotes. In the context of medical genetics, an autosomal dominant disorder is caused when a single copy of the mutant allele is present. Males and females are affected equally, and can both transmit the disorder with a risk of 50% for each child of inheriting the mutant allele.

terms.name: Autosomal recessive inheritance
terms.definition: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on one of the autosomes (i.e., the human chromosomes 1-22) in which a trait manifests in individuals with two pathogenic alleles, either homozygotes (two copies of the same mutant allele) or compound heterozygotes (whereby each copy of a gene has a distinct mutant allele).

terms.name: Abnormal morphology of female internal genitalia
terms.name_zh: 女性内生殖器形态异常
terms.definition: An abnormality of the female internal genitalia.

terms.name: Functional abnormality of the bladder
terms.definition: Dysfunction of the urinary bladder.

terms.name: Recurrent urinary tract infections
terms.definition: Repeated infections of the urinary tract.

terms.name: Neurogenic bladder
synonyms: Lack of bladder control due to nervous system injury
terms.definition: A type of bladder dysfunction caused by neurologic damage. Neurogenic bladder can be flaccid or spastic. Common manifestatios of neurogenic bladder are overflow incontinence, frequency, urgency, urge incontinence, and retention.

terms.name: Urinary urgency
terms.definition: Urge incontinence is the strong, sudden need to urinate.

terms.name: Hypoplasia of the uterus
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the uterus.

terms.name: Abnormality of the bladder
terms.definition: An abnormality of the urinary bladder.

terms.name: Bladder diverticulum
terms.definition: Diverticulum (sac or pouch) in the wall of the urinary bladder.

terms.name: Urinary retention
terms.definition: Inability to completely empty the urinary bladder during the process of urination.

terms.name: Nocturia
terms.definition: Abnormally increased production of urine during the night leading to an unusually frequent need to urinate.

terms.name: Urinary hesitancy
terms.definition: Difficulty in beginning the process of urination.

terms.name: Urinary incontinence
terms.definition: Loss of the ability to control the urinary bladder leading to involuntary urination.

terms.name: Megacystis
terms.definition: Dilatation of the bladder postnatally.

terms.name: Abnormal male internal genitalia morphology
terms.name_zh: 男性内生殖器形态异常
terms.definition: An abnormality of the male internal genitalia.

terms.name: Inguinal hernia
terms.definition: Protrusion of the contents of the abdominal cavity through the inguinal canal.

terms.name: Prostatitis
terms.definition: The presence of inflammation of the prostate.

terms.name: Functional abnormality of male internal genitalia
terms.name_zh: 男性内生殖器功能异常

terms.name: Male hypogonadism
terms.definition: Decreased functionality of the male gonad, i.e., of the testis, with reduced spermatogenesis or testosterone synthesis.

terms.name: Azoospermia
terms.definition: Absence of any measurable level of sperm,whereby spermatozoa cannot be observed even after centrifugation of the semen pellet.

terms.name: Cryptorchidism
terms.definition: Testis in inguinal canal. That is, absence of one or both testes from the scrotum owing to failure of the testis or testes to descend through the inguinal canal to the scrotum.

terms.name: Testicular atrophy
terms.definition: Wasting (atrophy) of the testicle (the male gonad) manifested by a decrease in size and potentially by a loss of fertility.

terms.name: Testicular gonadoblastoma
terms.definition: The presence of a gonadoblastoma of the testis.

terms.name: Epididymitis
terms.definition: The presence of inflammation of the epididymis.

terms.name: Abnormal male external genitalia morphology
terms.name_zh: 男性外生殖器形态异常
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of male external genitalia.

terms.name: Ambiguous genitalia, male
terms.name_zh: 男性外生殖器性别不清
terms.definition: Ambiguous genitalia in an individual with XY genetic gender.

terms.name: Hydrocele testis
terms.definition: Accumulation of clear fluid in the between the layers of membrane (tunica vaginalis) surrounding the testis.

terms.name: Abnormal testis morphology
terms.definition: An anomaly of the testicle (the male gonad).

terms.name: Abnormal penis morphology
terms.definition: Abnormality of the male external sex organ.

terms.name: Male pseudohermaphroditism
terms.definition: Hermaphroditism refers to a discrepancy between the morphology of the gonads and that of the external genitalia. In male pseudohermaphroditism, the genotype is male (XY) and the external genitalia are imcompletely virilized, ambiguous, or complete female. If gonads are present, they are testes.

terms.name: Epispadias
terms.definition: Epispadias is a urogenital malformation characterized by the failure of the urethral tube to tubularize on the dorsal aspect. Unlike in hypospadias, where the meatus is on the ventral aspect, children with epispadias have a wide-open urethral plate on the dorsum. It is commonly seen as a component in the spectrum of bladder exstrophy-epispadias-complex. Isolated epispadias constitutes less than 10 percent of the total cases of epispadias.

terms.name: Long penis
terms.definition: Penile length more than 2 SD above the mean for age.

terms.name: Chordee
terms.definition: A congenital anomaly of the penis characterized by ventral (i.e., downward), lateral, or ventrolateral curvature of the shaft and glans penis of more than 30 degrees.

terms.name: Absent external genitalia
terms.definition: Lack of external genitalia in a male or female individual.

terms.name: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
terms.name_zh: 低促性腺激素性性腺功能减退症
terms.definition: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism is characterized by reduced function of the gonads (testes in males or ovaries in females) and results from the absence of the gonadal stimulating pituitary hormones: follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH).

terms.name: Abnormal scrotum morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the scrotum, i.e., the sac that contains the testes, epididymis, and the lower part of the spermatic cord.

terms.name: Small scrotum
synonyms: Smaller than typical growth of scrotum
terms.definition: Apparently small scrotum for age.

terms.name: Hypospadias
terms.definition: Abnormal position of urethral meatus on the ventral penile shaft (underside) characterized by displacement of the urethral meatus from the tip of the glans penis to the ventral surface of the penis, scrotum, or perineum.

terms.name: Bifid scrotum
terms.definition: Midline indentation or cleft of the scrotum.

terms.name: Shawl scrotum
terms.definition: Superior margin of the scrotum superior to the base of the penis.

terms.name: Hypoplastic male external genitalia
terms.name_zh: 男性外生殖器发育不全
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of part or all of the male external reproductive organs (which include the penis, the scrotum and the urethra).

terms.name: Perineal hypospadias
terms.definition: Hypospadias with location of the urethral meatus in the perineal region.

terms.name: Urethral atresia, male
terms.definition: Congenital anomaly characterized by closure or failure to develop an opening in the urethra in males.

terms.name: Macroorchidism
terms.definition: The presence of abnormally large testes.

terms.name: Micropenis
terms.definition: Abnormally small penis. At birth, the normal penis is about 3 cm (stretched length from pubic tubercle to tip of penis) with micropenis less than 2.0-2.5 cm.

terms.name: Abnormal female external genitalia morphology
terms.name_zh: 女性外生殖器形态异常
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the female external genitalia.

terms.name: Abnormal clitoris morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the clitoris.

terms.name: Abnormal labia morphology
terms.definition: An anomaly of the labia, the externally visible portions of the vulva.

terms.name: Hypoplastic labia majora
terms.definition: Undergrowth of the outer labia.

terms.name: Clitoral hypoplasia
terms.definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the clitoris.

terms.name: Ambiguous genitalia, female
terms.name_zh: 女性外生殖器性别不清
terms.definition: Ambiguous genitalia in an individual with XX genetic gender.

terms.name: Ambiguous genitalia
terms.definition: A genital phenotype that is not clearly assignable to a single gender. Ambiguous genitalia can be evaluated using the Prader scale: Prader 0: Normal female external genitalia. Prader 1: Female external genitalia with clitoromegaly. Prader 2: Clitoromegaly with partial labial fusion forming a funnel-shaped urogenital sinus. Prader 3: Increased phallic enlargement. Complete labioscrotal fusion forming a urogenital sinus with a single opening. Prader 4: Complete scrotal fusion with urogenital opening at the base or on the shaft of the phallus. Prader 5: Normal male external genitalia. The diagnosis of ambiguous genitalia is made for Prader 1-4.

terms.name: Fused labia minora
terms.definition: Fusion of the labia minora as a result of labial adhesions resulting in vaginal obstruction.

terms.name: Urethral atresia, female
terms.definition: Congenital anomaly characterized by closure or failure to develop an opening in the urethra in females.

terms.name: Urethral atresia
terms.definition: Congenital anomaly characterized by closure or failure to develop an opening in the urethra.

terms.name: Abnormality of the ureter
terms.definition: An abnormality of the ureter. The ureter is the duct by which urine passes from the kidney to the bladder.

terms.name: Ureterocele
terms.definition: A ureterocele is a congenital saccular dilatation of the distal segment of the ureter.

terms.name: Ureteral stenosis
terms.definition: The presence of a stenotic, i.e., constricted ureter.

terms.name: Hydroureter
terms.definition: The distention of the ureter with urine.

terms.name: Ureteral duplication
terms.definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by the presence of two, instead of one, ureter connecting a kidney to the bladder.

terms.name: Ureteropelvic junction obstruction
terms.definition: Blockage of urine flow from the renal pelvis to the proximal ureter.

terms.name: Renal duplication
terms.definition: A congenital anomaly of the urinary tract, in which the kidney is duplicated and is drained via two separate renal pelves and ureters.

terms.name: Vesicoureteral reflux
terms.definition: Abnormal (retrograde) movement of urine from the bladder into ureters or kidneys related to inadequacy of the valvular mechanism at the ureterovesicular junction or other causes.

terms.name: Abnormality of the kidney
terms.definition: An abnormality of the kidney.

terms.name: Abnormality of the genital system
terms.definition: An abnormality of the genital system.

terms.name: Abnormality of the urinary system
terms.definition: An abnormality of the urinary system.

terms.name: Abnormality of reproductive system physiology
terms.name_zh: 生殖系统生理功能异常
terms.definition: An abnormal functionality of the genital system.

terms.name: Duplicated collecting system
synonyms: Double urinary collecting systems on intravenous pyelography
terms.definition: A duplication of the collecting system of the kidney, defined as a kidney with two (instead of, normally, one) pyelocaliceal systems. The pyelocaliceal system is comprised of the renal pelvis and calices. The duplicated renal collecting system can be associated with a single ureter or with double ureters. In the latter case, the two ureters empty separately into the bladder or fuse to form a single ureteral orifice.

terms.name: Renal insufficiency
terms.definition: A reduction in the level of performance of the kidneys in areas of function comprising the concentration of urine, removal of wastes, the maintenance of electrolyte balance, homeostasis of blood pressure, and calcium metabolism.

terms.name: Horseshoe kidney
terms.definition: A connection of the right and left kidney by an isthmus of functioning renal parenchyma or fibrous tissue that crosses the midline.

terms.name: Ectopic kidney
terms.definition: A developmental defect in which a kidney is located in an abnormal anatomic position.

terms.name: Renal hypoplasia
terms.definition: Hypoplasia of the kidney.

terms.name: Nephronophthisis
terms.definition: Presence of cysts at the corticomedullary junction of the kidney in combination with tubulointerstitial fibrosis.

terms.name: Abnormal renal tubule morphology
synonyms: Morphologic abnormality of the renal tubules
terms.definition: An abnormality of the renal tubules.

terms.name: Renal tubular atrophy
terms.definition: The presence of renal tubules with thick redundant basement membranes, or a reduction of greater than 50% in tubular diameter compared to surrounding non-atrophic tubules.

terms.name: Proteinuria
terms.definition: Increased levels of protein in the urine.

terms.name: Abnormal renal glomerulus morphology
synonyms: Morphologic abnormality of the renal glomerulus
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the glomerulus.

terms.name: Glomerular sclerosis
terms.definition: Accumulation of scar tissue within the glomerulus.

terms.name: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
terms.name_zh: 局灶节段性肾小球硬化
terms.definition: Segmental accumulation of scar tissue in individual (but not all) glomeruli.

terms.name: Tall stature
terms.definition: A height above that which is expected according to age and gender norms.

terms.name: Glomerulonephritis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the renal glomeruli.

terms.name: Nephrotic syndrome
terms.definition: Nephrotic syndrome is a collection of findings resulting from glomerular dysfunction with an increase in glomerular capillary wall permeability associated with pronounced proteinuria. Nephrotic syndrome refers to the constellation of clinical findings that result from severe renal loss of protein, with Proteinuria and hypoalbuminemia, edema, and hyperlipidemia.

terms.name: Polyuria
terms.definition: An increased rate of urine production.

terms.name: Renal agenesis
terms.definition: Agenesis, that is, failure of the kidney to develop during embryogenesis and development.

terms.name: Enlarged kidney
terms.definition: An abnormal increase in the size of the kidney.

terms.name: Renal cyst
terms.definition: A fluid filled sac in the kidney.

terms.name: Renal corticomedullary cysts
terms.definition: The presence of multiple cysts at the border between the renal cortex and medulla.

terms.name: Renal dysplasia
terms.definition: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the kidney.

terms.name: Renal juxtaglomerular cell hypertrophy/hyperplasia
terms.definition: Increased number and size of the juxtaglomerular cells.

terms.name: Nephropathy
terms.definition: A nonspecific term referring to disease or damage of the kidneys.

terms.name: Polycystic kidney dysplasia
terms.definition: The presence of multiple cysts in both kidneys.

terms.name: Proximal tubulopathy
terms.definition: Dysfunction of the proximal tubule, which is the portion of the duct system of the nephron of the kidney which leads from Bowman's capsule to the loop of Henle.

terms.name: Renal phosphate wasting
synonyms: Decreased tubular maximum for phosphate reabsorption per glomerular filtration rate
terms.definition: High urine phosphate in the presence of hypophosphatemia.

terms.name: Phenotypic abnormality
terms.definition: A phenotypic abnormality.

terms.name: Abnormality of the genitourinary system
terms.definition: The presence of any abnormality of the genitourinary system.

terms.name: Nephrocalcinosis
synonyms: Too much calcium deposited in kidneys
terms.definition: Nephrocalcinosis is the deposition of calcium salts in renal parenchyma.

terms.name: Unilateral renal agenesis
terms.definition: A unilateral form of agenesis of the kidney.

terms.name: Nephritis
terms.definition: The presence of inflammation affecting the kidney.

terms.name: Renal tubular dysfunction
synonyms: Abnormal function of filtrating structures in kidney
terms.definition: Abnormal function of the renal tubule. The basic functional unit of the kidney, the nephron, consists of a renal corpuscle attached to a renal tubule, with roughly 0.8 to 1.5 nephrons per adult kidney. The functions of the renal tubule include reabsorption of water, electrolytes, glucose, and amino acids and secretion of substances such as uric acid.

terms.name: Pelvic kidney
terms.definition: A developmental defect in which a kidney is located in an abnormal anatomic position within the pelvis.

terms.name: Hydronephrosis
terms.definition: Severe distention of the kidney with dilation of the renal pelvis and calices.

terms.name: Renal salt wasting
terms.definition: A high concentration of one or more electrolytes in the urine in the presence of low serum concentrations of the electrolyte(s).

terms.name: Renal potassium wasting
terms.definition: High urine potassium in the presence of hypokalemia.

terms.name: Abnormality of the uterus
terms.definition: An abnormality of the uterus.

terms.name: Uterine leiomyoma
terms.definition: The presence of a leiomyoma of the uterus.

terms.name: Menorrhagia
terms.definition: Prolonged and excessive menses at regular intervals in excess of 80 mL or lasting longer than 7 days.

terms.name: Gonadal dysgenesis
terms.definition: Gonadal dysgenesis is the name given to any of a multitude of conditions that can cause impaired development of the gonads, i.e., the testes or ovaries, or to the related phenotypic features. The term is to be avoided if possible for new annotations, and more specific terms should be chosen.

terms.name: Female hypogonadism
terms.definition: Decreased functionality of the female gonads, i.e., of the ovary.

terms.name: Hypogonadism
terms.definition: A decreased functionality of the gonad.

terms.name: Bifid uterus
terms.definition: The presence of a bifid uterus.

terms.name: Abnormality of the ovary
terms.definition: An abnormality of the ovary.

terms.name: Ovarian cyst
terms.definition: The presence of one or more cysts of the ovary.

terms.name: Uterine prolapse
terms.definition: The presence of prolapse of the uterus.

terms.name: Abnormality of the menstrual cycle
terms.definition: An abnormality of the ovulation cycle.

terms.name: Amenorrhea
terms.definition: Absence of menses for an interval of time equivalent to a total of more than (or equal to) 3 previous cycles or 6 months.

terms.name: Abnormal vagina morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the vagina.

terms.name: Rectovaginal fistula
synonyms: Abnormal connection between rectum and vagina
terms.definition: The presence of a fistula between the vagina and the rectum.

terms.name: Vaginal atresia
terms.definition: Congenital occlusion of the vagina or adhesion of the walls of the vagina causing occlusion.

terms.name: Ovarian gonadoblastoma
terms.definition: The presence of a gonadoblastoma of the ovary.

terms.name: Gonadoblastoma
terms.definition: The presence of a gonadoblastoma, a neoplasm of a gonad that consists of aggregates of germ cells and sex cord elements.

terms.name: Aplasia of the uterus
terms.definition: A congenital defect characterized by absence of the uterus. Aplasia refers to the failure of an organ to develop during embryonic growth and development due to the absence of primordial tissue.

terms.name: Abnormality of head or neck
terms.definition: An abnormality of head and neck.

terms.name: Abnormality of the mouth
terms.definition: An abnormality of the mouth.

terms.name: Wide mouth
terms.definition: Distance between the oral commissures more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased width of the oral aperture (subjective).

terms.name: Oral ulcer
terms.definition: Erosion of the mucous mebrane of the mouth with local excavation of the surface, resulting from the sloughing of inflammatory necrotic tissue.

terms.name: Abnormality of the tongue
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the tongue.

terms.name: Macroglossia
terms.definition: Increased length and width of the tongue.

terms.name: Abnormal lip morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the lip.

terms.name: Narrow mouth
terms.definition: Distance between the commissures of the mouth more than 2 SD below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently decreased width of the oral aperture (subjective).

terms.name: Median cleft upper lip
terms.definition: A type of cleft lip presenting as a midline (median) gap in the upper lip.

terms.name: Glossoptosis
terms.definition: Posterior displacement of the tongue into the pharynx, i.e., a tongue that is mislocalised posteriorly.

terms.name: Abnormal oral cavity morphology
terms.definition: Abnormality of the oral cavity, i.e., the opening or hollow part of the mouth.

terms.name: Abnormality of the dentition
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the teeth.

terms.name: Severe periodontitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to periodontitis, as manifested by severe periodontal infection with rapid alveolar bone loss, tooth mobility, and premature tooth exfoliation.

terms.name: Abnormality of the gingiva
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the gingiva (also known as gums).

terms.name: Gingival fibromatosis
terms.definition: The presence of fibrosis of the gingiva.

terms.name: Microglossia
terms.definition: Decreased length and width of the tongue.

terms.name: Abnormal uvula morphology
terms.definition: Abnormality of the uvula, the conic projection from the posterior edge of the middle of the soft palate.

terms.name: Abnormal palate morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of the roof of the mouth
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the palate, i.e., of roof of the mouth.

terms.name: Cleft palate
synonyms: Cleft of hard and soft palate
terms.definition: Cleft palate is a developmental defect of the palate resulting from a failure of fusion of the palatine processes and manifesting as a separation of the roof of the mouth (soft and hard palate).

terms.name: Submucous cleft hard palate
terms.definition: Hard-palate submucous clefts are characterized by bony defects in the midline of the bony palate that are covered by the mucous membrane of the roof of the mouth. It may be possible to detect a submucous cleft hard palate upon palpation as a notch in the bony palate.

terms.name: Abnormal upper lip morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the upper lip.

terms.name: Abnormal lower lip morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the lower lip.

terms.name: Thick lower lip vermilion
synonyms: Increased height of lower lip vermilion
Increased volume of lower lip vermilion
Thick vermilion border of lower lip
terms.definition: Increased thickness of the lower lip, leading to a prominent appearance of the lower lip. The height of the vermilion of the lower lip in the midline is more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased height of the vermilion of the lower lip in the frontal view (subjective).

terms.name: Lobulated tongue
terms.definition: Multiple indentations and/or elevations on the edge and/or surface of the tongue producing an irregular surface contour.

terms.name: Tongue muscle weakness
terms.definition: Reduced strength of the tongue musculature, resulting in difficulties moving the tongue and possible accompanied by dysarthria or dysphagia.

terms.name: Cleft soft palate
terms.definition: Cleft of the soft palate (also known as the velum, or muscular palate) as a result of a developmental defect occurring between the 7th and 12th week of pregnancy. Cleft soft palate can cause functional abnormalities of the Eustachian tube with resulting middle ear anomalies and hearing difficulties, as well as speech problems associated with hypernasal speech due to velopharyngeal insufficiency.

terms.name: Short upper lip
synonyms: Decreased vertical length of upper lip
terms.definition: Decreased width of the upper lip.

terms.name: Narrow palate
terms.definition: Width of the palate more than 2 SD below the mean (objective) or apparently decreased palatal width (subjective).

terms.name: Abnormal oral frenulum morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the lingual frenulum, that is of the small fold of mucous membrane that attaches the tongue to the floor of the mouth, or the presence of accessory frenula in the oral cavity.

terms.name: Accessory oral frenulum
terms.definition: Extra fold of tissue extending from the alveolar ridge to the inner surface of the upper or lower lip.

terms.name: Bifid uvula
terms.definition: Uvula separated into two parts most easily seen at the tip.

terms.name: Open mouth
terms.definition: A facial appearance characterized by a permanently or nearly permanently opened mouth.

terms.name: Lower lip pit
terms.definition: Depression located on the vermilion of the lower lip, usually paramedian.

terms.name: Abnormal parotid gland morphology
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the parotid glands, which are the salivary glands that are located in the subcutaneous tissues of the face overlying the mandibular ramus and anterior and inferior to the external ear.

terms.name: Absence of Stensen duct
synonyms: Failure of development of parotid duct
Failure of development of stensen duct

terms.name: Short lingual frenulum
terms.definition: The presence of an abnormally short lingual frenulum.

terms.name: Pierre-Robin sequence
terms.definition: Pierre Robin malformation is a sequence of developmental malformations characterized by micrognathia (mandibular hypoplasia), glossoptosis and cleft palate.

terms.name: Orofacial cleft
terms.definition: The presence of a cleft (gap, opening, or groove) in the oral cavity, including cleft of the upper lip and/or cleft of the palate. Cleft of the upper lip is visible as a groove or fissure in the lip, most frequently due to a congenital failure of the maxillary and median nasal processes to fuse. Cleft palate is characterized by a grooved depression or fissure in the roof of the mouth, most often resulting from a congenital failure of the palate to fuse properly. Clefts of the lip and palate can occur individually or together. It is preferable to code each defect separately.

terms.name: Cleft upper lip
terms.definition: A gap or groove in the upper lip. This is a congenital defect resulting from nonfusion of tissues of the lip during embryonal development.

terms.name: Pursed lips
terms.definition: An abnormality of the appearance of the face caused by constant contraction of the lips leading to a puckered or pursed appearance.

terms.name: Glossitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the tongue.

terms.name: Triangular mouth
terms.definition: The presence of a triangular form of the mouth.

terms.name: Trismus
terms.definition: Limitation in the ability to open the mouth.

terms.name: Gingival overgrowth
terms.definition: Hyperplasia of the gingiva (that is, a thickening of the soft tissue overlying the alveolar ridge. The degree of thickening ranges from involvement of the interdental papillae alone to gingival overgrowth covering the entire tooth crown.

terms.name: Lip telangiectasia
terms.definition: Telangiectasia (that is, the presence of small dilated superficial blood vessels) of the lips.

terms.name: Thick upper lip vermilion
synonyms: Increased height of upper lip vermilion
Increased volume of upper lip vermilion
Thick vermilion border of upper lip
terms.definition: Height of the vermilion of the upper lip in the midline more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased height of the vermilion of the upper lip in the frontal view (subjective).

terms.name: Xerostomia
terms.definition: Dryness of the mouth due to salivary gland dysfunction.

terms.name: High palate
terms.definition: Height of the palate more than 2 SD above the mean (objective) or palatal height at the level of the first permanent molar more than twice the height of the teeth (subjective).

terms.name: Thin upper lip vermilion
synonyms: Decreased height of upper lip vermilion
Decreased volume of upper lip vermilion
Thin vermilion border of upper lip
terms.definition: Height of the vermilion of the upper lip in the midline more than 2 SD below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently reduced height of the vermilion of the upper lip in the frontal view (subjective).

terms.name: Velopharyngeal insufficiency
terms.definition: Inability of velopharyngeal sphincter to sufficiently separate the nasal cavity from the oral cavity during speech.

terms.name: Furrowed tongue
terms.definition: Accentuation of the grooves on the dorsal surface of the tongue.

terms.name: Gingival hyperkeratosis
terms.definition: Hyperkeratosis of the gingiva.

terms.name: Hypogeusia
terms.definition: A decreased ability to perceive flavor.

terms.name: Gingival bleeding
terms.definition: Hemorrhage affecting the gingiva.

terms.name: Tongue telangiectasia
terms.definition: Telangiectasia (that is, the presence of small dilated superficial blood vessels) of the tongue.

terms.name: Oral cavity telangiectasia
synonyms: Spider veins of the oral cavity
terms.definition: Presence of telangiectases in the oral cavity.

terms.name: Gingivitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the gingiva

terms.name: Everted lower lip vermilion
terms.definition: An abnormal configuration of the lower lip such that it is turned outward i.e., everted, with the Inner aspect of the lower lip vermilion (normally opposing the teeth) being visible in a frontal view.

terms.name: Thin vermilion border
terms.definition: Height of the vermilion of the medial part of the lip more than 2 SD below the mean, or apparently reduced height of the vermilion of the lip in the frontal view. The vermilion is the red part of the lips (and confusingly, the vermilion itself is also often referred to as being equivalent the lips).

terms.name: Abnormality of the head
terms.definition: An abnormality of the head.

terms.name: Abnormal cranial suture/fontanelle morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of the fontanelles or cranial sutures
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the fontanelles (the regions covered by a thick membrane that normally ossify in the first two years of life) or the cranial sutures (the fibrous joints in which the articulating bones or cartilages of the skull are connected by sutural ligaments).

terms.name: Abnormal anterior fontanelle morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of the forehead soft spot
terms.definition: An abnormality of the anterior fontanelle, i.e., the cranial fontanelle that is located at the intersection of the coronal and sagittal sutures.

terms.name: Small anterior fontanelle
terms.definition: Abnormally decreased size of the anterior fontanelle with respect to age-dependent norms.

terms.name: Hydrocephalus
synonyms: Too much cerebrospinal fluid in the brain
terms.definition: Hydrocephalus is an active distension of the ventricular system of the brain resulting from inadequate passage of CSF from its point of production within the cerebral ventricles to its point of absorption into the systemic circulation.

terms.name: Large fontanelles
terms.definition: In newborns, the two frontal bones, two parietal bones, and one occipital bone are joined by fibrous sutures, which form a small posterior fontanelle, and a larger, diamond-shaped anterior fontanelle. These regions allow for the skull to pass the birth canal and for later growth. The fontanelles gradually ossify, whereby the posterior fontanelle usually closes by eight weeks and the anterior fontanelle by the 9th to 16th month of age. Large fontanelles are diagnosed if the fontanelles are larger than age-dependent norms.

terms.name: Abnormality of skull size
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the size of the skull.

terms.name: Parietal bossing
terms.definition: Parietal bossing is a marked prominence in the parietal region.

terms.name: Trigonocephaly
terms.definition: Wedge-shaped, or triangular head, with the apex of the triangle at the midline of the forehead and the base of the triangle at the occiput.

terms.name: Brachyturricephaly
terms.definition: Abnormal vertical height of the skull and a shortening of its anterior-posterior length, frequently combined with malformations of the occipital region.

terms.name: Abnormal paranasal sinus morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of the sinuses of the head
terms.definition: Abnormality of the paranasal (cranial) sinuses, which are air-filled spaces that are located within the bones of the skull and face and communicate with the nasal cavity. They comprise the maxillary sinuses, the frontal sinuses, the ethmoid sinuses, and the sphenoid sinuses.

terms.name: Sinusitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the paranasal sinuses owing to a viral, bacterial, or fungal infection, allergy, or an autoimmune reaction.

terms.name: Brachycephaly
terms.definition: An abnormality of skull shape characterized by a decreased anterior-posterior diameter. That is, a cephalic index greater than 81%. Alternatively, an apparently shortened anteroposterior dimension (length) of the head compared to width.

terms.name: Dense calvaria
terms.definition: An abnormal increase of density of the bones making up the calvaria.

terms.name: Microcephaly
terms.definition: Head circumference below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender.

terms.name: Progressive microcephaly
terms.definition: Progressive microcephaly is diagnosed when the head circumference falls progressively behind age- and gender-dependent norms.

terms.name: Acute sinusitis
terms.definition: An acute form of sinusitis.

terms.name: Macrocephaly
terms.definition: Occipitofrontal (head) circumference greater than 97th centile compared to appropriate, age matched, sex-matched normal standards. Alternatively, a apparently increased size of the cranium.

terms.name: Wide anterior fontanel
terms.definition: Enlargement of the anterior fontanelle with respect to age-dependent norms.

terms.name: Turricephaly
terms.definition: Tall head relative to width and length.

terms.name: Oxycephaly
terms.definition: Oxycephaly (from Greek oxus, sharp, and kephalos, head) refers to a conical or pointed shape of the skull.

terms.name: Abnormal mastoid morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of mastoid process of temporal bone
terms.definition: An abnormality of the mastoid process, which is the conical prominence projecting from the undersurface of the mastoid portion of the temporal bone.

terms.name: Mastoiditis
terms.definition: Infection of the mastoid air cells, arising as a complication of otitis media or occurring in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Cranial asymmetry
terms.definition: Asymmetry of the bones of the skull.

terms.name: Dolichocephaly
terms.definition: An abnormality of skull shape characterized by a increased anterior-posterior diameter, i.e., an increased antero-posterior dimension of the skull. Cephalic index less than 76%. Alternatively, an apparently increased antero-posterior length of the head compared to width. Often due to premature closure of the sagittal suture.

terms.name: Prominent occiput
terms.definition: Increased convexity of the occiput (posterior part of the skull).

terms.name: Delayed cranial suture closure
terms.definition: Infants normally have two fontanels at birth, the diamond-shaped anterior fontanelle at the junction of the coronal and sagittal sutures, and the posterior fontanelle at the intersection of the occipital and parietal bones. The posterior fontanelle usually closes by the 8th week of life, and the anterior fontanel closes by the 18th month of life on average. This term applies if there is delay of closure of the fontanelles beyond the normal age.

terms.name: Abnormality of the face
terms.definition: An abnormality of the face.

terms.name: Malar flattening
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the malar prominence of the jugal bone (zygomatic bone in mammals), appreciated in profile, frontal view, and/or by palpation.

terms.name: Small face
terms.definition: A face that is short and narrow.

terms.name: Narrow face
terms.definition: Bizygomatic (upper face) and bigonial (lower face) width are both more than 2 standard deviations below the mean (objective); or, an apparent reduction in the width of the upper and lower face (subjective).

terms.name: Long face
terms.definition: Facial height (length) is more than 2 standard deviations above the mean (objective); or, an apparent increase in the height (length) of the face (subjective).

terms.name: Abnormal mandible morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of the lower jaw bone
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the mandible, the bone of the lower jaw.

terms.name: Retrognathia
terms.definition: An abnormality in which the mandible is mislocalised posteriorly.

terms.name: Coarse facial features
terms.definition: Absence of fine and sharp appearance of brows, nose, lips, mouth, and chin, usually because of rounded and heavy features or thickened skin with or without thickening of subcutaneous and bony tissues.

terms.name: Broad face
terms.definition: Bizygomatic (upper face) and bigonial (lower face) width greater than 2 standard deviations above the mean (objective); or an apparent increase in the width of the face (subjective).

terms.name: Epicanthus
terms.definition: A fold of skin starting above the medial aspect of the upper eyelid and arching downward to cover, pass in front of and lateral to the medial canthus.

terms.name: Increased facial adipose tissue
synonyms: Increased amount of facial adipose tissue
Increased volume of facial adipose tissue
terms.definition: An increased amount of subcutaneous fat tissue in the face.

terms.name: Abnormality of the philtrum
terms.definition: An abnormality of the philtrum.

terms.name: Broad philtrum
terms.definition: Distance between the philtral ridges, measured just above the vermilion border, more than 2 standard deviations above the mean, or alternatively, an apparently increased distance between the ridges of the philtrum.

terms.name: Abnormal forehead morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of the frontal region of the face
terms.definition: An anomaly of the forehead.

terms.name: Loss of facial adipose tissue
synonyms: Decreased amount of facial adipose tissue
Decreased volume of facial adipose tissue
Loss of facial subcutaneous adipose tissue
Loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue from face
terms.definition: Loss of normal subcutaneous fat tissue in the face.

terms.name: Full cheeks
terms.definition: Increased prominence or roundness of soft tissues between zygomata and mandible.

terms.name: Low anterior hairline
terms.definition: Distance between the hairline (trichion) and the glabella (the most prominent point on the frontal bone above the root of the nose), in the midline, more than two SD below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently decreased distance between the hairline and the glabella.

terms.name: Doll-like facies
terms.definition: A characteristic facial appearance with a round facial form, full cheeks, a short nose, and a relatively small chin.

terms.name: Facial hypotonia
terms.definition: Reduced muscle tone of a muscle that is innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).

terms.name: Mask-like facies
terms.definition: A lack of facial expression often with staring eyes and a slightly open mouth.

terms.name: Oval face
terms.definition: A face with a rounded and slightly elongated outline.

terms.name: Abnormality of facial musculature
terms.definition: An anomaly of a muscle that is innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).

terms.name: Mandibular prognathia
terms.definition: Abnormal prominence of the chin related to increased length of the mandible.

terms.name: Abnormality of the chin
terms.definition: An abnormality of the chin, i.e., of the inferior portion of the face lying inferior to the lower lip and including the central prominence of the lower jaw.

terms.name: Pointed chin
terms.definition: A marked tapering of the lower face to the chin.

terms.name: Microretrognathia
terms.definition: A form of developmental hypoplasia of the mandible in which the mandible is mislocalised posteriorly.

terms.name: Abnormal midface morphology
terms.definition: An anomaly of the midface, which is a region and not an anatomical term. It extends, superiorly, from the inferior orbital margin to, inferiorly, the level of nasal base. It is formed by the maxilla (upper jaw) and zygoma and cheeks and malar region. Traditionally, the nose and premaxilla are not included in the midface.

terms.name: Round face
terms.definition: The facial appearance is more circular than usual as viewed from the front.

terms.name: Hypertelorism
terms.definition: Interpupillary distance more than 2 SD above the mean (alternatively, the appearance of an increased interpupillary distance or widely spaced eyes).

terms.name: Facial myokymia
terms.definition: Facial myokymia is a fine fibrillary activity of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).

terms.name: Smooth philtrum
terms.definition: Flat skin surface, with no ridge formation in the central region of the upper lip between the nasal base and upper vermilion border.

terms.name: Square face
terms.definition: Facial contours, as viewed from the front, show a broad upper face/cranium and lower face/mandible, creating a square appearance.

terms.name: Short philtrum
terms.definition: Distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border more than 2 SD below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently decreased distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border.

terms.name: Facial asymmetry
synonyms: Asymmetry of right and left side of face
terms.definition: An abnormal difference between the left and right sides of the face.

terms.name: Triangular face
synonyms: Face with broad temples and narrow chin
terms.definition: Facial contour, as viewed from the front, triangular in shape, with breadth at the temples and tapering to a narrow chin.

terms.name: Abnormal maxilla morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of the upper jaw bone
Abnormality of the upper jaw bones
terms.definition: An abnormality of the Maxilla (upper jaw bone).

terms.name: Hypoplasia of the maxilla
terms.definition: Abnormally small dimension of the Maxilla. Usually creating a malocclusion or malalignment between the upper and lower teeth or resulting in a deficient amount of projection of the base of the nose and lower midface region.

terms.name: Facial hemangioma
terms.definition: Hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, occurring in the face.

terms.name: Short chin
terms.definition: Decreased vertical distance from the vermilion border of the lower lip to the inferior-most point of the chin.

terms.name: Prominent supraorbital ridges
terms.definition: Greater than average forward and/or lateral protrusion of the supraorbital portion of the frontal bones.

terms.name: Broad forehead
terms.definition: Width of the forehead or distance between the frontotemporales is more than two standard deviations above the mean (objective); or apparently increased distance between the two sides of the forehead.

terms.name: Hypomimic face
terms.definition: A reduced degree of motion of the muscles beneath the skin of the face, often associated with reduced facial crease formation.

terms.name: Pugilistic facies
terms.definition: Coarse facial features reminiscent of those of a boxer.

terms.name: Sloping forehead
terms.definition: Inclination of the anterior surface of the forehead from the vertical more than two standard deviations above the mean (objective); or apparently excessive posterior sloping of the forehead in a lateral view.

terms.name: Narrow forehead
terms.definition: Width of the forehead or distance between the frontotemporales is more than two standard deviations below the mean (objective); or apparently narrow intertemporal region (subjective).

terms.name: Long philtrum
terms.definition: Distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border.

terms.name: Whistling appearance
terms.definition: An abnormality of facial morphology characterized by a small mouth opening and constant contraction of the lips as if the patient were whistling.

terms.name: Micrognathia
terms.definition: Developmental hypoplasia of the mandible.

terms.name: High forehead
terms.definition: An abnormally increased height of the forehead.

terms.name: Widow's peak
synonyms: Pointed hairline at front of head
terms.definition: Frontal hairline with bilateral arcs to a low point in the midline of the forehead.

terms.name: Small forehead
synonyms: Decreased size of frontal region of face
terms.definition: The presence of a forehead that is abnormally small.

terms.name: Abnormality of the outer ear
terms.definition: An abnormality of the external ear.

terms.name: Abnormal location of ears
terms.definition: Abnormal location of the ear.

terms.name: Posteriorly rotated ears
synonyms: Ears rotated toward back of head
terms.definition: A type of abnormal location of the ears in which the position of the ears is characterized by posterior rotation (the superior part of the ears is rotated towards the back of the head, and the inferior part of the ears towards the front).

terms.name: Abnormality of the inner ear
terms.definition: An abnormality of the inner ear.

terms.name: Tinnitus
terms.definition: Tinnitus is an auditory perception that can be described as the experience of sound, in the ear or in the head, in the absence of external acoustic stimulation.

terms.name: Otosclerosis
terms.definition: In otosclerosis, a callus of bone accumulates on the stapes creating a partial fixation. This limits the movement of the stapes bone, which results in hearing loss.

terms.name: Abnormal earlobe morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the lobule of pinna.

terms.name: Hearing abnormality
terms.definition: An abnormality of the sensory perception of sound.

terms.name: Hearing impairment
terms.definition: A decreased magnitude of the sensory perception of sound.

terms.name: Abnormality of the nose
terms.definition: An abnormality of the nose.

terms.name: Low-set ears
terms.definition: Upper insertion of the ear to the scalp below an imaginary horizontal line drawn between the inner canthi of the eye and extending posteriorly to the ear.

terms.name: Abnormality of the middle ear
terms.definition: An abnormality of the middle ear.

terms.name: Acute otitis media
terms.definition: Acute otitis media is a short and generally painful infection of the middle ear.

terms.name: Abnormal auditory canal morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the external acoustic tube (also known as the auditory canal).

terms.name: Abnormal cochlea morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the cochlea.

terms.name: Incomplete partition of the cochlea type II
terms.definition: With incomplete partition II, the cochlea consists of 1.5 turns; the apical and middle cochlea turns are undifferentiated and form a cystic apex. The vestibule is normal while the vestibular aqueduct is always enlarged. Developmental arrest occurs at the seventh week of gestation.

terms.name: Abnormal pinna morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the pinna, which is also referred to as the auricle or external ear.

terms.name: Cupped ear
terms.definition: Laterally protruding ear that lacks antihelical folding (including absence of inferior and superior crura).

terms.name: Stapes ankylosis
terms.definition: Stapes ankylosis refers to congenital or acquired fixation of the stapes (the stirrup-shaped small bone or ossicle in the middle ear), which is associated with conductive hearing resulting from impairment of the sound-conduction mechanism (the external auditory canal, tympanic membrane, and/or middle-ear ossicles).

terms.name: Preauricular skin tag
terms.definition: A rudimentary tag of skin often containing ear tissue including a core of cartilage and located just anterior to the auricle (outer part of the ear).

terms.name: Small earlobe
terms.definition: Reduced volume of the earlobe.

terms.name: Absent earlobe
terms.definition: Absence of fleshy non-cartilaginous tissue inferior to the tragus and incisura.

terms.name: Otitis media
terms.definition: Inflammation or infection of the middle ear.

terms.name: Chronic otitis media
synonyms: Chronic infections of the middle ear
terms.definition: Chronic otitis media refers to fluid, swelling, or infection of the middle ear that does not heal and may cause permanent damage to the ear.

terms.name: Thickened helices
terms.definition: Increased thickness of the helix of the ear.

terms.name: Lop ear
terms.definition: Anterior and inferior folding of the upper portion of the ear that obliterates triangular fossa and scapha.

terms.name: Prominent antihelix
terms.definition: The presence of an abnormally prominent antihelix.

terms.name: Overfolded helix
terms.definition: A condition in which the helix is folded over to a greater degree than normal. That is, excessive curling of the helix edge, whereby the free edge is parallel to the plane of the ear.

terms.name: Prelingual sensorineural hearing impairment
terms.definition: A form of sensorineural deafness with either congenital onset or infantile onset, i.e., before the acquisition of speech.

terms.name: Macrotia
terms.definition: Median longitudinal ear length greater than two standard deviations above the mean and median ear width greater than two standard deviations above the mean (objective); or, apparent increase in length and width of the pinna (subjective).

terms.name: Stenosis of the external auditory canal
synonyms: Narrowing of passageway from outer ear to middle ear
terms.definition: An abnormal narrowing of the external auditory canal.

terms.name: Recurrent otitis media
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to otitis media, as manifested by recurrent episodes of otitis media.

terms.name: Conductive hearing impairment
terms.definition: An abnormality of vibrational conductance of sound to the inner ear leading to impairment of sensory perception of sound.

terms.name: Sensorineural hearing impairment
terms.definition: A type of hearing impairment in one or both ears related to an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve.

terms.name: Progressive sensorineural hearing impairment
terms.definition: A progressive form of sensorineural hearing impairment.

terms.name: Mixed hearing impairment
terms.definition: A type of hearing loss resulting from a combination of conductive hearing impairment and sensorineural hearing impairment.

terms.name: Protruding ear
terms.definition: Angle formed by the plane of the ear and the mastoid bone greater than the 97th centile for age (objective); or, outer edge of the helix more than 2 cm from the mastoid at the point of maximum distance (objective).

terms.name: Atresia of the external auditory canal
synonyms: Atresia of the external auditory canals
terms.definition: Absence or failure to form of the external auditory canal.

terms.name: Bulbous nose
terms.definition: Increased volume and globular shape of the anteroinferior aspect of the nose.

terms.name: Abnormal choanae morphology
terms.definition: Abnormality of the choanae (the posterior nasal apertures).

terms.name: Narrow nasal ridge
synonyms: Decreased width of dorsum of nose
terms.definition: Decreased width of the nasal ridge.

terms.name: Abnormal nasal septum morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the nasal septum.

terms.name: Short nasal septum
synonyms: Decreased length of septum of nose
terms.definition: Reduced superior to inferior length of the nasal septum.

terms.name: Epistaxis
terms.definition: Epistaxis, or nosebleed, refers to a hemorrhage localized in the nose.

terms.name: Abnormal nasal bridge morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of the bridge of the nose
terms.definition: Abnormality of the nasal bridge, which is the saddle-shaped area that includes the nasal root and the lateral aspects of the nose. It lies between the glabella and the inferior boundary of the nasal bone, and extends laterally to the inner canthi.

terms.name: Prominent nasal bridge
terms.definition: Anterior positioning of the nasal root in comparison to the usual positioning for age.

terms.name: Abnormal morphology of the nasal alae
terms.definition: An abnormality of the Ala of nose.

terms.name: Underdeveloped nasal alae
terms.definition: Thinned, deficient, or excessively arched ala nasi.

terms.name: Wide nasal bridge
synonyms: Increased breadth of bridge of nose
Increased width of bridge of nose
terms.definition: Increased breadth of the nasal bridge (and with it, the nasal root).

terms.name: Abnormal nasal mucosa morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of mucous membrane of nose

terms.name: Nasal mucosa telangiectasia
synonyms: Angioectasia of mucous membrane of nose
Spider veins of mucosa of nose
Spider veins of mucous membrane of nose
Spider veins of nasal mucous membrane
Telangiectasia of mucous membrane of nose
terms.definition: Telangiectasia of the nasal mucosa.

terms.name: Abnormal nasal tip morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the nasal tip.

terms.name: Depressed nasal tip
terms.definition: Decreased distance from the nasal tip to the nasal base.

terms.name: Convex nasal ridge
terms.definition: Nasal ridge curving anteriorly to an imaginary line that connects the nasal root and tip. The nose appears often also prominent, and the columella low.

terms.name: Wide nose
terms.definition: Interalar distance more than two standard deviations above the mean for age, i.e., an apparently increased width of the nasal base and alae.

terms.name: Narrow nasal bridge
terms.definition: Decreased width of the bony bridge of the nose.

terms.name: Prominent nose
terms.definition: Distance between subnasale and pronasale more than two standard deviations above the mean, or alternatively, an apparently increased anterior protrusion of the nasal tip.

terms.name: Choanal stenosis
synonyms: Narrowing of the rear opening of the nasal cavity
terms.definition: Abnormal narrowing of the choana (the posterior nasal aperture).

terms.name: Choanal atresia
synonyms: Blockage of the rear opening of the nasal cavity
terms.definition: Absence or abnormal closure of the choana (the posterior nasal aperture). Most embryologists believe that posterior choanal atresia results from a failure of rupture between the 35th and 38th day of fetal life of the partition which separates the bucconasal or buccopharyngeal membranes. The resultant choanal atresia may be unilateral or bilateral, bony or membranous, complete or incomplete. In over 90 per cent of cases the obstruction is bony, while in the remainder it is membranous. The bony type of atresia is commonly located 1-2 mm. anterior to the posterior edge of the hard palate, and the osseous septum varies in thickness from 1 to 10 mm. In the membranous form of choanal atresia the obstruction usually occurs further posteriorly. In approximately one third of cases the atresia is bilateral.

terms.name: Broad nasal tip
synonyms: Increased breadth of tip of nose
Increased width of tip of nose
terms.definition: Increase in width of the nasal tip.

terms.name: Bifid nasal tip
terms.definition: A splitting of the nasal tip. Visually assessable vertical indentation, cleft, or depression of the nasal tip.

terms.name: Depressed nasal ridge
terms.definition: Lack of prominence of the nose resulting from a posteriorly-placed nasal ridge.

terms.name: Anosmia
terms.definition: An inability to perceive odors. This is a general term describing inability to smell arising in any part of the process of smelling from absorption of odorants into the nasal mucous overlying the olfactory epithelium, diffusion to the cilia, binding to olfactory receptor sites, generation of action potentials in olfactory neurons, and perception of a smell.

terms.name: Narrow nose
terms.definition: Interalar distance more than 2 SD below the mean for age, or alternatively, an apparently decreased width of the nasal base and alae.

terms.name: Anteverted nares
terms.definition: Anteriorly-facing nostrils viewed with the head in the Frankfurt horizontal and the eyes of the observer level with the eyes of the subject. This gives the appearance of an upturned nose (upturned nasal tip).

terms.name: Abnormality of the neck
terms.definition: An abnormality of the neck.

terms.name: Webbed neck
terms.definition: Pterygium colli is a congenital skin fold that runs along the sides of the neck down to the shoulders. It involves an ectopic fibrotic facial band superficial to the trapezius muscle. Excess hair-bearing skin is also present and extends down the cervical region well beyond the normal hairline.

terms.name: Neck muscle weakness
terms.definition: Decreased strength of the neck musculature.

terms.name: Increased adipose tissue around the neck
terms.definition: An increased amount of subcutaneous fat tissue around the neck.

terms.name: Short neck
terms.definition: Diminished length of the neck.

terms.name: Gastrointestinal angiodysplasia
terms.definition: Dysplasia affecting the vasculature of the gastrointestinal tract.

terms.name: Long neck
terms.definition: Increased inferior-superior length of the neck.

terms.name: Torticollis
terms.definition: Involuntary contractions of the neck musculature resulting in an abnormal posture of or abnormal movements of the head.

terms.name: Thickened nuchal skin fold
terms.definition: A thickening of the skin thickness in the posterior aspect of the fetal neck. A nuchal fold (NF) measurement is obtained in a transverse section of the fetal head at the level of the cavum septum pellucidum and thalami, angled posteriorly to include the cerebellum. The measurement is taken from the outer edge of the occiput bone to the outer skin limit directly in the midline. An NF measurement greater than 5 mm at 14 to 17+6 weeks of gestation, or 6 mm at 18 to 28 weeks has been associated with a markedly increased risk for Down syndrome.

terms.name: Broad neck
terms.definition: Increased side-to-side width of the neck.

terms.name: Cystic hygroma
terms.definition: A cystic lymphatic lesion of the neck.

terms.name: Abnormality of the eye
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the eye, including location, spacing, and intraocular abnormalities.

terms.name: Abnormal retinal morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the retina.

terms.name: Retinal coloboma
synonyms: Hole in the back of the eye
terms.definition: A notch or cleft of the retina or choroid, located vertically below the optic disc.

terms.name: Abnormal cornea morphology
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the cornea, which is the transparent tissue at the front of the eye that covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.

terms.name: Microcornea
synonyms: Cornea of eye less than 10mm in diameter
terms.definition: A congenital abnormality of the cornea in which the cornea and the anterior segment of the eye are smaller than normal. The horizontal diameter of the cornea does not reach 10 mm even in adulthood.

terms.name: Astigmatism
synonyms: Abnormal curving of the cornea or lens of the eye
terms.definition: A type of refraction error associated with abnormal curvatures on the anterior and/or posterior surface of the cornea.

terms.name: Hyperopic astigmatism
terms.definition: A form of astigmatism in which one meridian is hyperopic while the one at a right angle to it has no refractive error.

terms.name: Megalocornea
terms.definition: An enlargement of the cornea with normal clarity and function. Megalocornea is diagnosed with a horizontal corneal diameter of 12 mm or more at birth or 13 mm or more after two years of age.

terms.name: Strabismus
terms.definition: A misalignment of the eyes so that the visual axes deviate from bifoveal fixation. The classification of strabismus may be based on a number of features including the relative position of the eyes, whether the deviation is latent or manifest, intermittent or constant, concomitant or otherwise and according to the age of onset and the relevance of any associated refractive error.

terms.name: Retinopathy
terms.definition: Any noninflammatory disease of the retina. This nonspecific term is retained here because of its wide use in the literature, but if possible new annotations should indicate the precise type of retinal abnormality.

terms.name: Deeply set eye
terms.definition: An eye that is more deeply recessed into the plane of the face than is typical.

terms.name: Keratitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the cornea.

terms.name: Abnormal eyelid morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the eyelids.

terms.name: Abnormal foveal morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the fovea centralis, the central area of the macula that mediates central, high resolution vision and contains the largest concentration of cone cells in the retina.

terms.name: Downslanted palpebral fissures
synonyms: Downward slanting of the opening between the eyelids
terms.definition: The palpebral fissure inclination is more than two standard deviations below the mean.

terms.name: Recurrent corneal erosions
synonyms: Recurrent breakdown of clear protective layer of eye
terms.definition: The presence of recurrent corneal epithelial erosions. Although most corneal epithelial defects heal quickly, some may show recurrent ulcerations.

terms.name: Abnormality of eye movement
synonyms: Abnormal motility of the globe of the eye
Abnormal movement of the globe of the eye
terms.definition: An abnormality in voluntary or involuntary eye movements or their control.

terms.name: Globe retraction and deviation on abduction
Blepharitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the eyelids.

terms.name: Abnormal eyelash morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the eyelashes.

terms.name: Glaucoma
terms.definition: Glaucoma refers loss of retinal ganglion cells in a characteristic pattern of optic neuropathy usually associated with increased intraocular pressure.

terms.name: Abnormal conjunctiva morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the conjunctiva.

terms.name: Tortuosity of conjunctival vessels
terms.definition: The presence of an increased number of twists and turns of the conjunctival blood vessels.

terms.name: Abnormality of vision
terms.definition: Abnormality of eyesight (visual perception).

terms.name: Visual impairment
terms.definition: Visual impairment (or vision impairment) is vision loss (of a person) to such a degree as to qualify as an additional support need through a significant limitation of visual capability resulting from either disease, trauma, or congenital or degenerative conditions that cannot be corrected by conventional means, such as refractive correction, medication, or surgery.

terms.name: Telecanthus
terms.definition: Distance between the inner canthi more than two standard deviations above the mean (objective); or, apparently increased distance between the inner canthi.

terms.name: Ptosis
terms.definition: The upper eyelid margin is positioned 3 mm or more lower than usual and covers the superior portion of the iris (objective); or, the upper lid margin obscures at least part of the pupil (subjective).

terms.name: Conjunctivitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the conjunctiva.

terms.name: Rod-cone dystrophy
terms.definition: An inherited retinal disease subtype in which the rod photoreceptors appear to be more severely affected than the cone photoreceptors. Typical presentation is with nyctalopia (due to rod dysfunction) followed by loss of mid-peripheral field of vision, which gradually extends and leaves many patients with a small central island of vision due to the preservation of macular cones.

terms.name: Vertical supranuclear gaze palsy
terms.definition: A supranuclear gaze palsy is an inability to look in a vertical direction as a result of cerebral impairment. There is a loss of the voluntary aspect of eye movements, but, as the brainstem is still intact, all the reflex conjugate eye movements are normal.

terms.name: Abnormal electroretinogram
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the electrical responses of various cell types in the retina as measured by electroretinography.

terms.name: Slow saccadic eye movements
terms.definition: An abnormally slow velocity of the saccadic eye movements.

terms.name: Abnormal lens morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the lens.

terms.name: Cataract
synonyms: Clouding of the lens of the eye
terms.definition: A cataract is an opacity or clouding that develops in the crystalline lens of the eye or in its capsule.

terms.name: Developmental cataract
synonyms: Clouding of the lens of the eye at birth
terms.definition: A cataract that occurs congenitally as the result of a developmental defect, in contrast to the majority of cataracts that occur in adulthood as the result of degenerative changes of the lens.

terms.name: Proptosis
synonyms: Anterior bulging of the globe of eye
terms.definition: An eye that is protruding anterior to the plane of the face to a greater extent than is typical.

terms.name: Alacrima
synonyms: Absence of tears in the eyes
terms.definition: Absence of tear secretion.

terms.name: Subcapsular cataract
terms.definition: A cataract that affects the region of the lens directly beneath the capsule of the lens.

terms.name: Conjunctival telangiectasia
synonyms: Small dilated blood vessels near membrane covering front of eye and eyelids
terms.definition: The presence of small (ca. 0.5-1.0 mm) dilated blood vessels near the surface of the mucous membranes of the conjunctiva.

terms.name: Abnormality iris morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the iris, which is the pigmented muscular tissue between the cornea and the lens, that is perforated by an opening called the pupil.

terms.name: Aniridia
terms.definition: Abnormality of the iris characterized by, typically bilateral, complete or partial iris hypoplasia. The phenotype ranges from mild defects of anterior iris stroma only to almost complete absence of the iris.

terms.name: Long eyelashes
terms.definition: Mid upper eyelash length >10 mm or increased length of the eyelashes (subjective).

terms.name: Anophthalmia
terms.definition: Absence of the globe or eyeball.

terms.name: Progressive visual loss
terms.definition: A reduction of previously attained ability to see.

terms.name: Abnormal chorioretinal morphology
terms.name_zh: 脉络膜视网膜形态异常
terms.definition: An abnormality of the choroid and retina.

terms.name: Chorioretinal atrophy
terms.definition: Atrophy (wasting) of the choroid and retinal layers of the fundus.

terms.name: Abnormal eyebrow morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the eyebrow.

terms.name: Epicanthus inversus
terms.definition: A fold of skin starting at or just below the medial aspect of the lower lid and arching upward to cover, extend in front of and lateral to the medial canthus.

terms.name: Pseudopapilledema
terms.definition: Apparent optic disc swelling in the absence of increased intracranial pressure.

terms.name: Abnormality of refraction
terms.definition: An abnormality in the process of focusing of light by the eye in order to produce a sharp image on the retina.

terms.name: Hypermetropia
terms.definition: An abnormality of refraction characterized by the ability to see objects in the distance clearly, while objects nearby appear blurry.

terms.name: Retinal detachment
terms.definition: Separation of the inner layers of the retina (neural retina) from the pigment epithelium.

terms.name: Impaired ocular adduction
terms.definition: Reduced ability to move the eye in the direction of the nose.

terms.name: Optic disc pallor
terms.definition: A pale yellow discoloration of the optic disc (the area of the optic nerve head in the retina). The optic disc normally has a pinkish hue with a central yellowish depression.

terms.name: External ophthalmoplegia
synonyms: Paralysis or weakness of muscles within or surrounding outer part of eye
Progressive paralysis or weakness of muscles of eye motility
Progressive paralysis or weakness of muscles of eye movement
terms.definition: Paralysis of the external ocular muscles.

terms.name: Myopia
terms.definition: An abnormality of refraction characterized by the ability to see objects nearby clearly, while objects in the distance appear blurry.

terms.name: Retinal degeneration
terms.definition: A nonspecific term denoting progressive loss of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and/or neurosensory retinal cells.

terms.name: Cone/cone-rod dystrophy
terms.name_zh: 视锥/视锥-杆细胞营养不良

terms.name: Abnormal conjugate eye movement
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal motor coordination of the eyes that allows for bilateral fixation on a single object.

terms.name: Undetectable electroretinogram
terms.definition: Lack of any response to stimulation upon electroretinography.

terms.name: Color vision defect
terms.definition: An anomaly in the ability to discriminate between or recognize colors.

terms.name: Tritanomaly
terms.definition: Difficulty distinguishing between yellow and blue, possible related to dysfunction of the S photopigment.

terms.name: Abnormal uvea morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the uvea, the vascular layer of the eyeball.

terms.name: Uveitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of one or all portions of the uveal tract.

terms.name: Leukocoria
terms.definition: An abnormal white reflection from the pupil rather than the usual black reflection.

terms.name: Retinal dystrophy
synonyms: Breakdown of light-sensitive cells in back of eye
terms.definition: Retinal dystrophy is an abnormality of the retina associated with a hereditary process. Retinal dystrophies are defined by their predominantly monogenic inheritance and they are frequently associated with loss or dysfunction of photoreceptor cells as a primary or secondary event.

terms.name: Buphthalmos
terms.definition: Diffusely large eye (with megalocornea) associated with glaucoma.

terms.name: Rieger anomaly
terms.definition: A congenital malformation of the anterior segment characterized by iridicorneal malformation, glaucoma, iris stroma hypoplasia, posterior embryotoxon, and corneal opacities.

terms.name: Absent eyelashes
terms.definition: Lack of eyelashes.

terms.name: Keratoconus
terms.definition: A cone-shaped deformity of the cornea characterized by the presence of corneal distortion secondary to thinning of the apex.

terms.name: Lacrimal duct atresia
terms.definition: A developmental disorder of the lacrimal drainage system that most often affects the lacrimal ostium and resulting in non-opening of the nasolacrimal duct. It usually results from a non-canalization of the nasolacrimal duct.

terms.name: Esotropia
terms.definition: A form of strabismus with one or both eyes turned inward ('crossed') to a relatively severe degree, usually defined as 10 diopters or more.

terms.name: Chorioretinal coloboma
synonyms: Birth defect that causes a hole in the innermost layer at the back of the eye
terms.definition: Absence of a region of the retina, retinal pigment epithelium, and choroid.

terms.name: Microphthalmia
terms.definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal smallness of one or both eyes.

terms.name: Abnormal saccadic eye movements
terms.definition: An abnormality of eye movement characterized by impairment of fast (saccadic) eye movements.

terms.name: Hypometric saccades
terms.definition: Saccadic undershoot, i.e., a saccadic eye movement that has less than the magnitude that would be required to gain fixation of the object.

terms.name: Visual loss
terms.definition: Loss of visual acuity (implying that vision was better at a certain time point in life). Otherwise the term reduced visual acuity should be used (or a subclass of that).

terms.name: Retinal hemorrhage
terms.definition: Bleeding located within the retina. Retinal hemorrhages range from the smallest dot and blot hemorrhage to massive sub-hyaloid hemorrhage.

terms.name: Thick eyebrow
terms.definition: Increased density/number and/or increased diameter of eyebrow hairs.

terms.name: Scotoma
terms.definition: A regional and pathological increase of the light detection threshold in any region of the visual field surrounded by a field of normal or relatively well-preserved vision.

terms.name: Centrocecal scotoma
terms.definition: A scotoma (area of diminished vision within the visual field) located between the central point of fixation and the blind spot with a roughly horizontal oval shape.

terms.name: Exotropia
terms.definition: A form of strabismus with one or both eyes deviated outward.

terms.name: Nasolacrimal duct obstruction
terms.definition: Blockage of the lacrimal duct.

terms.name: Pigmentary retinopathy
terms.definition: An abnormality of the retina characterized by pigment deposition. It is typically associated with migration and proliferation of macrophages or retinal pigment epithelial cells into the retina; melanin from these cells causes the pigmentary changes. Pigmentary retinopathy is a common final pathway of many retinal conditions and is often associated with visual loss.

terms.name: Blepharophimosis
terms.definition: A fixed reduction in the vertical distance between the upper and lower eyelids with short palpebral fissures.

terms.name: Upslanted palpebral fissure
synonyms: Upward slanting of the opening between the eyelids
terms.definition: The palpebral fissure inclination is more than two standard deviations above the mean for age (objective); or, the inclination of the palpebral fissure is greater than typical for age.

terms.name: Band keratopathy
terms.definition: An abnormality of the cornea characterized by the deposition of calcium in a band across the central cornea, leading to decreased vision, foreign body sensation, and ocular irritation.

terms.name: Shallow orbits
terms.definition: Reduced depth of the orbits associated with prominent-appearing ocular globes.

terms.name: Abnormal optic nerve morphology
terms.definition: Abnormality of the optic nerve.

terms.name: Optic disc coloboma
terms.definition: A cleft of the optic nerve that extends inferiorly.

terms.name: Coloboma
terms.definition: A developmental defect characterized by a cleft of some portion of the eye or ocular adnexa.

terms.name: Progressive external ophthalmoplegia
terms.definition: Initial bilateral ptosis followed by limitation of eye movements in all directions and slowing of saccades.

terms.name: Abnormal sclera morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the sclera.

terms.name: Blue sclerae
synonyms: Whites of eyes are a bluish-gray color
Whites of eyes are a bluish-gray colour
terms.definition: An abnormal bluish coloration of the sclera.

terms.name: Abnormal anterior chamber morphology
terms.definition: Abnormality of the anterior chamber, which is the space in the eye that is behind the cornea and in front of the iris.

terms.name: Shallow anterior chamber
terms.definition: Reduced depth of the anterior chamber, i.e., the anteroposterior distance between the cornea and the iris is decreased.

terms.name: Ophthalmoparesis
synonyms: Weakness of muscles controlling eye movement
terms.definition: Ophthalmoplegia is a paralysis or weakness of one or more of the muscles that control eye movement.

terms.name: Abnormality of the ear
terms.definition: An abnormality of the ear.

terms.name: Abnormality of the frontal hairline
synonyms: Abnormality of hairline at front of head
terms.definition: An anomaly in the placement or shape of the hairline (trichion) on the forehead, that is, the border between skin on the forehead that has head hair and that does not.

terms.name: Abnormality of the pharynx
terms.definition: An anomaly of the pharynx, i.e., of the tubular structure extending from the base of the skull superiorly to the esophageal inlet inferiorly.

terms.name: Hypotelorism
terms.definition: Interpupillary distance less than 2 SD below the mean (alternatively, the appearance of an decreased interpupillary distance or closely spaced eyes).

terms.name: Ophthalmoplegia
terms.definition: Paralysis of one or more extraocular muscles that are responsible for eye movements.

terms.name: Central scotoma
terms.definition: An area of depressed vision located at the point of fixation and that interferes with central vision.

terms.name: Supranuclear gaze palsy
terms.definition: A supranuclear gaze palsy is an inability to look in a particular direction as a result of cerebral impairment. There is a loss of the voluntary aspect of eye movements, but, as the brainstem is still intact, all the reflex conjugate eye movements are normal.

terms.name: Abnormality of the periorbital region
terms.definition: An abnormality of the region situated around the orbit of the eye.

terms.name: Macular degeneration
terms.definition: A nonspecific term denoting degeneration of the retinal pigment epithelium and/or retinal photoreceptor cells of the macula lutea.

terms.name: Optic nerve hypoplasia
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the optic nerve.

terms.name: Abnormal choroid morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the choroid (the posterior part of the uvea, the middle tunic of the eye, consisting mainly of blood vessels).

terms.name: Iris coloboma
terms.definition: A coloboma of the iris.

terms.name: Photophobia
synonyms: Extreme sensitivity of the eyes to light
terms.definition: Excessive sensitivity to light with the sensation of discomfort or pain in the eyes due to exposure to bright light.

terms.name: Abnormal nasolacrimal system morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the nasolacrimal drainage system, which serves as a conduit for tear flow from the external eye to the nasal cavity.

terms.name: Abnormal pupil morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the pupil.

terms.name: Miosis
terms.definition: Abnormal (non-physiological) constriction of the pupil.

terms.name: Abnormality of ocular smooth pursuit
terms.definition: An abnormality of eye movement characterized by impaired smooth-pursuit eye movements.

terms.name: Blindness
terms.definition: Blindness is the condition of lacking visual perception defined as a profound reduction in visual perception. On the 6m visual acuity scale, blindness is defined as less than 3/60. On the 20ft visual acuity scale, blindness is defined as less than 20/400. On the decimal visual acuity scale, blindness is defined as less than 0.05. Blindness is typically characterized by a visual field of no greater than 10 degrees in radius around central fixation.

terms.name: Impaired convergence
