terms.definition: All of the metacarpal bones of the hand have a pointed proximal appearance.

terms.name: Abnormality of the thenar eminence
terms.definition: An abnormality of the thenar eminence, i.e., of the muscle on the palm of the human hand just beneath the thumb.

terms.name: Broad metacarpals
terms.definition: Abnormally broad metacarpal bones.

terms.name: Abnormal fingernail morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the fingernails.

terms.name: Nail bed telangiectasia
terms.definition: Telangiectases in the area of the nails.

terms.name: 2-3 finger cutaneous syndactyly
terms.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the second to the third fingers that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints.

terms.name: Hitchhiker thumb
terms.definition: With the hand relaxed and the thumb in the plane of the palm, the axis of the thumb forms an angle of at least 90 degrees with the long axis of the hand.

terms.name: Slender finger
terms.definition: Fingers that are disproportionately narrow (reduced girth) for the hand/foot size or build of the individual.

terms.name: Wrist flexion contracture
terms.definition: A chronic loss of wrist joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevent normal movement of the joints of the wrist.

terms.name: Small thenar eminence
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the thenar eminence with reduced palmar soft tissue mass surrounding the base of the thumb.

terms.name: Short tubular bones of the hand
synonyms: Long bone shortening of the hand
Short long bones of the hand
Shortened long tubular bones of the hand
Shortened tubular bones of the hand
terms.definition: Decreased length of the tubular bones of the hand, that is, the phalanges and metacarpals.

terms.name: Intellectual disability
terms.definition: The term intellectual disability or intellectual developmental disorder is used to describe significantly sub-average intellectual and adaptive functioning based on clinical assessment and as measured by individually administered, appropriately normed, standardized and validated tests of intellectual functioning and adaptive behavior, with onset during the developmental period from infancy through adolescence.

terms.name: Seizure
terms.definition: A seizure is an intermittent abnormality of nervous system physiology characterized by a transient occurrence of signs and/or symptoms due to abnormal excessive or synchronous neuronal activity in the brain.

terms.name: Ataxia
terms.definition: Ataxia refers to impaired coordination of voluntary muscle movement. Cerebellar ataxia refers to ataxia due to dysfunction of the cerebellum. This causes a variety of elementary neurological deficits including asynergy (lack of coordination between muscles, limbs and joints), dysmetria (lack of ability to judge distances that can lead to under- or overshoot in grasping movements), and dysdiadochokinesia (inability to perform rapid movements requiring antagonizing muscle groups to be switched on and off repeatedly).

terms.name: Hypotonia
terms.definition: Hypotonia is an abnormally low muscle tone (the amount of tension or resistance to movement in a muscle). Even when relaxed, muscles have a continuous and passive partial contraction which provides some resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia thus manifests as diminished resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia is not the same as muscle weakness, although the two conditions can co-exist.

terms.name: Lethargy
terms.definition: A state of fatigue, either physical or mental slowness and sluggishness, with difficulties in initiating or performing simple tasks. Distinguished from apathy which implies indifference and a lack of desire or interest in the task. A person with lethargy may have the desire, but not the energy to engage in personal or socially relevant tasks.

terms.name: Mild intellectual disability
terms.definition: Mild intellectual disability (ID) is defined as a type of ID characterized by mildly sub-average adaptive functioning and intellectual functioning, with an intelligence quotient (IQ) the range of 50-69.

terms.name: Spasticity
synonyms: Involuntary muscle stiffness, contraction, or spasm
terms.definition: A motor disorder characterized by a velocity-dependent increase in tonic stretch reflexes with increased muscle tone, exaggerated (hyperexcitable) tendon reflexes.

terms.name: Spastic paraplegia
terms.definition: Complete loss of the ability to move the lower limbs accompanied by spasticity of the lower limbs.

terms.name: Coma
terms.definition: The complete absence of wakefulness and consciousness, which is evident through a lack of response to any form of external stimuli.

terms.name: Dysarthria
terms.definition: Dysarthric speech is a general description referring to a neurological speech disorder characterized by poor articulation. Depending on the involved neurological structures, dysarthria may be further classified as spastic, flaccid, ataxic, hyperkinetic and hypokinetic, or mixed.

terms.name: Excessive daytime somnolence
synonyms: More than typical sleepiness during day
terms.definition: A state of abnormally strong desire for sleep during the daytime.

terms.name: Global developmental delay
terms.definition: A delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child, including motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and emotional skills. This term should only be used to describe children younger than five years of age.

terms.name: Spastic diplegia
terms.definition: Spasticity (neuromuscular hypertonia) primarily in the muscles of the legs, hips, and pelvis.

terms.name: Hyporeflexia
terms.definition: Reduction of neurologic reflexes such as the knee-jerk reaction.

terms.name: Choreoathetosis
terms.definition: Involuntary movements characterized by both athetosis (inability to sustain muscles in a fixed position) and chorea (widespread jerky arrhythmic movements).

terms.name: Mental deterioration
terms.definition: Loss of previously present mental abilities, generally in adults.

terms.name: Hemiparesis
synonyms: Weakness of one side of body
terms.definition: Loss of strength in the arm, leg, and sometimes face on one side of the body. Hemiplegia refers to a complete loss of strength, whereas hemiparesis refers to an incomplete loss of strength.

terms.name: Motor delay
synonyms: Delay in development of motor milestones
terms.definition: A type of Developmental delay characterized by a delay in acquiring motor skills.

terms.name: Polyneuropathy
terms.definition: A generalized disorder of peripheral nerves.

terms.name: Cerebellar atrophy
terms.definition: Cerebellar atrophy is defined as a cerebellum with initially normal structures, in a posterior fossa with normal size, which displays enlarged fissures (interfolial spaces) in comparison to the foliae secondary to loss of tissue. Cerebellar atrophy implies irreversible loss of tissue and result from an ongoing progressive disease until a final stage is reached or a single injury, e.g. an intoxication or infectious event.

terms.name: Abnormal corpus callosum morphology
terms.definition: Abnormality of the corpus callosum.

terms.name: Agenesis of corpus callosum
terms.definition: Absence of the corpus callosum as a result of the failure of the corpus callosum to develop, which can be the result of a failure in any one of the multiple steps of callosal development including cellular proliferation and migration, axonal growth or glial patterning at the midline.

terms.name: Hypertonia
terms.definition: A condition in which there is increased muscle tone so that arms or legs, for example, are stiff and difficult to move.

terms.name: Orthostatic hypotension
synonyms: Decrease in blood pressure upon standing up
terms.definition: A form of hypotension characterized by a sudden fall in blood pressure that occurs when a person assumes a standing position.

terms.name: Syncope
terms.definition: A transient loss of consciousness (i.e., characterized by a rapid onset, a short duration, and a spontaneous and complete recovery) due to cerebral hypoperfusion.

terms.name: Tetany
terms.definition: A condition characterized by intermittent involuntary contraction of muscles (spasms) related to hypocalcemia or occasionally magnesium deficiency.

terms.name: Bulbar palsy
terms.definition: Bulbar weakness (or bulbar palsy) refers to bilateral impairment of function of the lower cranial nerves IX, X, XI and XII, which occurs due to lower motor neuron lesion either at nuclear or fascicular level in the medulla or from bilateral lesions of the lower cranial nerves outside the brain-stem. Bulbar weakness is often associated with difficulty in chewing, weakness of the facial muscles, dysarthria, palatal weakness and regurgitation of fluids, dysphagia, and dysphonia.

terms.name: Areflexia
terms.definition: Absence of neurologic reflexes such as the knee-jerk reaction.

terms.name: Spastic tetraparesis
terms.definition: Spastic weakness affecting all four limbs.

terms.name: Meningitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the meninges.

terms.name: Gait disturbance
terms.definition: The term gait disturbance can refer to any disruption of the ability to walk.

terms.name: Confusion
terms.definition: Lack of clarity and coherence of thought, perception, understanding, or action.

terms.name: Generalized hypotonia
terms.definition: Generalized muscular hypotonia (abnormally low muscle tone).

terms.name: Abnormal cranial nerve morphology
terms.definition: Structural abnormality affecting one or more of the cranial nerves, which emerge directly from the brain stem.

terms.name: Stroke
terms.definition: Sudden impairment of blood flow to a part of the brain due to occlusion or rupture of an artery to the brain.

terms.name: Encephalopathy
terms.definition: Encephalopathy is a term that means brain disease, damage, or malfunction. In general, encephalopathy is manifested by an altered mental state.

terms.name: Parkinsonism
terms.definition: Characteristic neurologic anomaly resulting from degeneration of dopamine-generating cells in the substantia nigra, a region of the midbrain, characterized clinically by shaking, rigidity, slowness of movement and difficulty with walking and gait.

terms.name: Chronic sensorineural polyneuropathy
terms.name_zh: 慢性感觉神经性多神经病

terms.name: Pachygyria
synonyms: Fewer and broader ridges in brain
terms.definition: Pachygyria is a malformation of cortical development with abnormally wide gyri with sulci 1,5-3 cm apart and abnormally thick cortex measuring more than 5 mm (radiological definition). See also neuropathological definitions for 2-, 3-, and 4-layered lissencephaly.

terms.name: Torsion dystonia
terms.definition: Sustained involuntary muscle contractions that produce twisting and repetitive movements of the body.

terms.name: Dandy-Walker malformation
terms.definition: A congenital brain malformation typically characterized by incomplete formation of the cerebellar vermis, dilation of the fourth ventricle, and enlargement of the posterior fossa. In layman's terms, Dandy Walker malformation is a cyst in the cerebellum (typically symmetrical) that is involved with the fourth ventricle. This may interfere with the ability to drain cerebrospinal fluid from the brain, resulting in hydrocephalus. Dandy Walker cysts are formed during early embryonic development, while the brain forms. The cyst in the cerebellum typically has several blood vessels running through it connecting to the brain, thereby prohibiting surgical removal.

terms.name: Tongue fasciculations
terms.definition: Fasciculations or fibrillation affecting the tongue muscle.

terms.name: Dysmetria
terms.definition: A type of ataxia characterized by the inability to carry out movements with the correct range and motion across the plane of more than one joint related to incorrect estimation of the distances required for targeted movements.

terms.name: Abnormal nervous system electrophysiology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the function of the electrical signals with which nerve cells communicate with each other or with muscles as measured by electrophysiological investigations.

terms.name: Giant somatosensory evoked potentials
terms.definition: An abnormal enlargement (i.e. increase in measured voltage) of somatosensory evoked potentials.

terms.name: Diminished deep tendon reflex
synonyms: Absent or decreased deep tendon reflexes
Decreased to absent deep tendon reflexes
Diminished or absent deep tendon reflexes
Hypoactive to absent deep tendon reflexes
Weak or absent deep tendon reflexes
terms.definition: A reduction (hyporeflexia) or complete absence (areflexia) of the involuntary muscle contraction normally elicited by a reflex stimulus, such as tapping a deep tendon.

terms.name: Abnormal cerebellum morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the cerebellum.

terms.name: Neonatal hypotonia
synonyms: Low muscle tone, in neonatal onset
terms.definition: Muscular hypotonia (abnormally low muscle tone) manifesting in the neonatal period.

terms.name: Cerebellar vermis hypoplasia
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the vermis of cerebellum.

terms.name: Cerebellar hypoplasia
terms.definition: Cerebellar hypoplasia is a descriptive term implying a cerebellum with a reduced volume, but a normal shape and is stable over time.

terms.name: Muscle weakness
terms.definition: Reduced strength of muscles.

terms.name: Hypoglycemic coma
synonyms: Coma caused by low blood sugar
Loss of consciousness due to hypoglycemia
terms.definition: Coma induced by low blood sugar.

terms.name: EEG with irregular generalized spike and wave complexes
terms.name_zh: 脑电图不规则全面性棘慢复合波
synonyms: EEG with irregular generalised spike and wave complexes
terms.definition: EEG shows spikes (<80 ms) and waves, which are recorded over the entire scalp and do not have a specific frequency.

terms.name: Photosensitive myoclonic seizure
terms.definition: Generalised myoclonic seizure provoked by flashing or flickering light.

terms.name: Specific learning disability
terms.definition: Impairment of certain skills such as reading or writing, coordination, self-control, or attention that interfere with the ability to learn. The impairment is not related to a global deficiency of intelligence.

terms.name: Absent septum pellucidum
terms.definition: Absence of the septum pellucidum (meaning translucent wall in Latin - SP), also known as the ventricle of Sylvius. The septum pellucidum is a thin, triangular double membrane separating the frontal horns of the right and left lateral ventricles of the brain. It extends between the anterior portion of the corpus callosum, and the body of the fornix and its width varies from 1.5 to 3.0 mm.

terms.name: Dystonia
terms.definition: An abnormally increased muscular tone that causes fixed abnormal postures. There is a slow, intermittent twisting motion that leads to exaggerated turning and posture of the extremities and trunk.

terms.name: Communicating hydrocephalus
terms.definition: A form of hydrocephalus in which there is no visible obstruction to the flow of the cerebrospinal fluid between the ventricles and subarachnoid space.

terms.name: Bimanual synkinesia
terms.definition: Involuntary movements of one hand that accompany and mirror intentional movements of the opposite hand.

terms.name: Myoclonus
terms.definition: Very brief, involuntary random muscular contractions occurring at rest, in response to sensory stimuli, or accompanying voluntary movements.

terms.name: Tremor
terms.definition: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement about a joint axis.

terms.name: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum
synonyms: Partial or complete agenesis of corpus callosum
Partial or complete agenesis of the corpus callosum
Partial to complete agenesis of corpus callosum
terms.definition: A partial failure of the development of the corpus callosum.

terms.name: Lissencephaly
synonyms: Fewer or absent grooves in brain
terms.definition: A spectrum of malformations of cortical development caused by insufficient neuronal migration that subsumes the terms agyria, pachygyria and subcortical band heterotopia. See also neuropathological definitions for 2-, 3-, and 4-layered lissencephaly.

terms.name: Enhancement of the C-reflex
terms.definition: Increase in amplitude of a long-loop response upon somatosensory evoked potential testing, representing an electrically evoked myoclonic response.

terms.name: Cerebral hemorrhage
terms.definition: Hemorrhage into the parenchyma of the brain.

terms.name: Kernicterus
terms.definition: Damage to cerebral nuclei caused in infants by highly increased levels of unconjugated bilirubin. The basal ganglia and brainstem nuclei could be shown to have a yellow staining historically in infants who died of kernicterus, that is, kernicterus is strictly speaking a pathological diagnosis. The presence of kernicterus may be inferred in infants with characteristic acute or chronic bilirubin-induced neurological dysfunction.

terms.name: Absent speech
terms.definition: Complete lack of development of speech and language abilities.

terms.name: Psychotic mentation
terms.definition: A pattern of thinking and perceiving characterized by a loss of contact with reality, leading to significant changes in thoughts, perceptions, and behaviors.

terms.name: Hyperreflexia
terms.definition: Hyperreflexia is the presence of hyperactive stretch reflexes of the muscles.

terms.name: Brisk reflexes
terms.definition: Tendon reflexes that are noticeably more active than usual (conventionally denoted 3+ on clinical examination). Brisk reflexes may or may not indicate a neurological lesion. They are distinguished from hyperreflexia by the fact that hyerreflexia is characterized by hyperactive repeating (clonic) reflexes, which are considered to be always abnormal.

terms.name: Facial diplegia
terms.definition: Facial diplegia refers to bilateral facial palsy (bilateral facial palsy is much rarer than unilateral facial palsy).

terms.name: Slurred speech
terms.definition: Abnormal coordination of muscles involved in speech.

terms.name: Jerk-locked premyoclonus spikes
terms.name_zh: 抽动锁定的肌阵挛前棘波
terms.definition: Jerk-locked averaging (JLA) is used to record the timing and distribution of brain activity preceding brisk involuntary movements such as those observed in patients with myoclonus. JLA is capable of revealing a premyoclonus spike in the absence of paroxysmal activity in the routine EEG.

terms.name: Megalencephaly
terms.definition: Diffuse enlargement of the entire cerebral hemispheres leading to macrocephaly (with or without overlying cortical dysplasia).

terms.name: Plagiocephaly
terms.definition: Asymmetric head shape, which is usually a combination of unilateral occipital flattening with ipsilateral frontal prominence, leading to rhomboid cranial shape.

terms.name: Holoprosencephaly
terms.definition: Holoprosencephaly is a structural anomaly of the brain in which the developing forebrain fails to divide into two separate hemispheres and ventricles.

terms.name: Nystagmus-induced head nodding
terms.definition: Head movements associated with nystagmus, that may represent an attempt to compensate for the involuntary eye movements and to improve vision.

terms.name: Calvarial skull defect
terms.definition: A localized defect in the bone of the skull resulting from abnormal embryological development. The defect is covered by normal skin. In some cases, skull x-rays have shown underlying lytic bone lesions which have closed before the age of one year.

terms.name: Craniosynostosis
terms.definition: Craniosynostosis refers to the premature closure of the cranial sutures. Primary craniosynostosis refers to the closure of one or more sutures due to abnormalities in skull development, and secondary craniosynostosis results from failure of brain growth.

terms.name: Abnormal joint morphology
terms.definition: An abnormal structure or form of the joints, i.e., one or more of the articulations where two bones join.

terms.name: Arthritis
terms.definition: Inflammation of a joint.

terms.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
terms.definition: Inflammatory changes in the synovial membranes and articular structures with widespread fibrinoid degeneration of the collagen fibers in mesenchymal tissues, as well as atrophy and rarefaction of bony structures.

terms.name: Flexion contracture
synonyms: Flexed joint that cannot be straightened
terms.definition: A flexion contracture is a bent (flexed) joint that cannot be straightened actively or passively. It is thus a chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement of joints.

terms.name: Joint dislocation
terms.definition: Displacement or malalignment of joints.

terms.name: Limitation of joint mobility
terms.definition: A reduction in the freedom of movement of one or more joints.

terms.name: Limited elbow extension
terms.definition: Limited ability to straighten the arm at the elbow joint.

terms.name: Joint hypermobility
synonyms: Joints move beyond expected range of motion
terms.definition: The capability that a joint (or a group of joints) has to move, passively and/or actively, beyond normal limits along physiological axes.

terms.name: Abnormal hip joint morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the hip joint.

terms.name: Hip dysplasia
terms.definition: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the hip.

terms.name: Joint stiffness
terms.definition: Joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in a joint or joints when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity. Joint stiffness typically subsides over time.

terms.name: Abnormality of the liver
terms.definition: An abnormality of the liver.

terms.name: Cirrhosis
synonyms: Scar tissue replaces healthy tissue in the liver
terms.definition: A chronic disorder of the liver in which liver tissue becomes scarred and is partially replaced by regenerative nodules and fibrotic tissue resulting in loss of liver function.

terms.name: Hepatic fibrosis
terms.definition: The presence of excessive fibrous connective tissue in the liver. Fibrosis is a reparative or reactive process.

terms.name: Cholestasis
synonyms: Slowed or blocked flow of bile from liver
terms.definition: Impairment of bile flow due to obstruction in bile ducts.

terms.name: Hepatic steatosis
terms.definition: Steatosis is a term used to denote lipid accumulation within hepatocytes.

terms.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma
terms.definition: A kind of neoplasm of the liver that originates in hepatocytes and presents macroscopically as a soft and hemorrhagic tan mass in the liver.

terms.name: Macrovesicular hepatic steatosis
terms.definition: A form of hepatic steatosis characterized by the presence of large, lipid-laden vesicles in the affected hepatocytes.

terms.name: Periportal fibrosis
terms.definition: The presence of fibrosis affecting the interlobular stroma of liver.

terms.name: Intrahepatic cholestasis
terms.definition: Impairment of bile flow due to obstruction in the small bile ducts within the liver.

terms.name: Bile duct proliferation
terms.definition: Proliferative changes of the bile ducts.

terms.name: Portal hypertension
terms.definition: Increased pressure in the portal vein.

terms.name: Decreased liver function
terms.definition: Reduced ability of the liver to perform its functions.

terms.name: Enteroviral hepatitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the liver due to infection with enterovirus.

terms.name: Micronodular cirrhosis
terms.definition: A type of cirrhosis characterized by the presence of small regenerative nodules.

terms.name: Microvesicular hepatic steatosis
terms.definition: A form of hepatic steatosis characterized by the presence of small, lipid-laden vesicles in the affected hepatocytes.

terms.name: X-linked inheritance
terms.definition: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on the X chromosome.

terms.name: X-linked recessive inheritance
terms.definition: A mode of inheritance that is observed for recessive traits related to a gene encoded on the X chromosome. In the context of medical genetics, X-linked recessive disorders manifest in males (who have one copy of the X chromosome and are thus hemizygotes), but generally not in female heterozygotes who have one mutant and one normal allele.

terms.name: Abnormality of the musculature of the hand
X-linked dominant inheritance
terms.definition: A mode of inheritance that is observed for dominant traits related to a gene encoded on the X chromosome. In the context of medical genetics, X-linked dominant disorders tend to manifest very severely in affected males. The severity of manifestation in females may depend on the degree of skewed X inactivation.

terms.name: Non-Mendelian inheritance
terms.definition: A mode of inheritance that depends on genetic determinants in more than one gene.

terms.name: Mitochondrial inheritance
terms.definition: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on the mitochondrial genome. Because the mitochondrial genome is essentially always maternally inherited, a mitochondrial condition can only be transmitted by females, although the condition can affect both sexes. The proportion of mutant mitochondria can vary (heteroplasmy).

terms.name: Hepatosplenomegaly
terms.definition: Simultaneous enlargement of the liver and spleen.

terms.name: Abnormality of the shoulder girdle musculature
terms.definition: A structural or functional anomaly of the shoulder girdle, which which connects the upper limb to the axial skeleton via the sternoclavicular joint.

terms.name: Abnormality of the foot musculature
terms.definition: An anomaly of the musculature of foot.

terms.name: Abnormality of the musculature of the lower limbs
Abnormal abdomen morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the abdomen ('belly'), that is, the part of the body between the pelvis and the thorax.

terms.name: Metatarsal synostosis
synonyms: Fusion of the long bones of the feet

terms.name: Abnormality thigh musculature morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of the musculature of the thigh

terms.name: Typified by somatic mosaicism
terms.definition: Description of conditions in which affected individuals typically display somatic mosaicism, i.e., genetically distinct populations of somatic cells in a given organism caused by DNA mutations, epigenetic alterations of DNA, chromosomal abnormalities or the spontaneous reversion of inherited mutations. In many conditions typified by somatic mosaicism, constitutive mutation is lethal and cases are exclusively or predominantly mosaic.

terms.name: Abnormality of the musculature of the upper limbs
Duplication of metatarsal bones
synonyms: Duplication of long bones of foot

terms.name: Y-linked inheritance
terms.definition: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on the Y chromosome.

terms.name: Abnormality of the musculature of the upper arm
1-3 toe syndactyly
terms.definition: Syndactyly with fusion of toes one to three.

terms.name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the skeletal musculature
terms.name_zh: 骨骼肌发育不全/发育不良
terms.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the musculature.

terms.name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the shoulder musculature
terms.name_zh: 肩部肌肉组织发育不全/发育不良
terms.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the muscles of the shoulder.

terms.name: Contiguous gene syndrome
terms.definition: A syndrome caused by the effects of abnormality (typically a deletion or duplication) of 2 or more adjacent genes

terms.name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the musculature of the upper limbs
terms.name_zh: 上肢肌肉组织发育不全/发育不良
terms.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the musculature of the upper limbs.

terms.name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia involving the musculature of the upper arm
terms.name_zh: 上臂肌肉组织发育不全/发育不良
terms.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the muscles of the upper arm.

terms.name: Abnormal morphology of the pelvis musculature
terms.name_zh: 骨盆肌肉组织形态异常
synonyms: Abnormality of the musculature of the pelvis

terms.name: Sex-limited expression
terms.definition: Sex limitation is used to refer to a monogenic trait linked to an autosomal locus in which the phenotypic effects of allelic differences are expressed only in one sex.

terms.name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
terms.name_zh: 骨盆肌肉组织发育不全/发育不良

terms.name: Metatarsal osteolysis
terms.definition: Osteolysis involving metatarsal bones.

terms.name: Sclerotic scapulae
terms.definition: Increased density of the bony tissue of the scapula.

terms.name: Male-limited expression
terms.definition: Used to refer to a monogenic trait linked to an autosomal locus in which the phenotypic effects of allelic differences are expressed only in the male sex.

terms.name: Delayed closure of the anterior fontanelle
synonyms: Delayed closure of the bregma sutures
Late closure of large anterior fontanel
Late closure of the bregma sutures
Later than typical closing of soft spot of skull
terms.definition: A delay in closure (ossification) of the anterior fontanelle, which generally undergoes closure around the 18th month of life.

terms.name: Compensatory chin elevation
terms.definition: A tendency to hold the chin elevated by about 20 to 30 degrees to compensate for a limitation of eye movement.

terms.name: Freckling
terms.definition: The presence of an increased number of freckles, small circular spots on the skin that are darker than the surrounding skin because of deposits of melanin.

terms.name: Subcutaneous nodule
synonyms: Growth of abnormal tissue under the skin
terms.definition: Slightly elevated lesions on or in the skin with a diameter of over 5 mm.

terms.name: Eye poking
terms.definition: Repetitive pressing, poking, and/or rubbing in the eyes.

terms.name: Posterior vitreous detachment
terms.definition: Separation of the vitreous humor from the retina.

terms.name: Congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles
synonyms: Congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles
terms.definition: Congenital non-progressive ophthalmoplegia with multiple extraocular muscle restrictions. Typically, there is ptosis and variable degrees of restriction of horizontal and vertical eye movements.

terms.name: Axenfeld anomaly
terms.definition: Axenfeld's anomaly is a bilateral disorder characterized by a prominent, anteriorly displaced Schwalbe's line (posterior embryotoxon) and peripheral iris strands which span the anterior chamber angle to attach to Schwalbe's line.

terms.name: Falciform retinal fold
terms.definition: An area of the retina that is buckled so that a sector-shaped sheet of retina lies in front of the normal retina. This feature is of congenital onset.

terms.name: Carpal osteolysis
terms.definition: Osteolysis affecting carpal bones.

terms.name: Carpal bone hypoplasia
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of one or more carpal bones.

terms.name: Broad finger
terms.definition: Increased width of a non-thumb digit of the hand.

terms.name: Failure to thrive
terms.definition: Failure to thrive (FTT) refers to a child whose physical growth is substantially below the norm.

terms.name: Growth delay
terms.definition: A deficiency or slowing down of growth pre- and postnatally.

terms.name: Intrauterine growth retardation
terms.definition: An abnormal restriction of fetal growth with fetal weight below the tenth percentile for gestational age.

terms.name: Obesity
terms.definition: Accumulation of substantial excess body fat.

terms.name: Small for gestational age
terms.definition: Smaller than normal size according to sex and gestational age related norms, defined as a weight below the 10th percentile for the gestational age.

terms.name: Disproportionate tall stature
terms.definition: A tall and slim body build with increased arm span to height ratio (>1.05) and a reduced upper-to-lower segment ratio (<0.85), i.e., unusually long arms and legs. The extremities as well as the hands and feet are unusually slim.

terms.name: Large for gestational age
terms.definition: The term large for gestational age applies to babies whose birth weight lies above the 90th percentile for that gestational age.

terms.name: Death in infancy
terms.definition: Death within the first 24 months of life.

terms.name: Hemihypertrophy
terms.definition: Overgrowth of only one side of the body.

terms.name: Mild postnatal growth retardation
synonyms: Postnatal onset of mild growth retardation
terms.definition: A mild degree of slow or limited growth after birth, being between two and three standard deviations below age- and sex-related norms.

terms.name: Failure to thrive in infancy
synonyms: Failure to thrive in first year of life

terms.name: Slender build
terms.definition: Asthenic habitus refers to a slender build with long limbs, an angular profile, and prominent muscles or bones.

terms.name: Umbilical hernia
terms.definition: Protrusion of abdominal contents through a defect in the abdominal wall musculature around the umbilicus. Skin and subcutaneous tissue overlie the defect.

terms.name: Protuberant abdomen
terms.definition: A thrusting or bulging out of the abdomen.

terms.name: Omphalocele
terms.definition: A midline anterior incomplete closure of the abdominal wall in which there is herniation of the abdominal viscera into the base of the abdominal cord.

terms.name: Diastasis recti
synonyms: Gap between large left and right abdominal muscles
terms.definition: A separation of the rectus abdominis muscle into right and left halves (which are normally joined at the midline at the linea alba).

terms.name: Ascites
synonyms: Accumulation of fluid in the abdomen
terms.definition: Accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity (between the layers of the peritoneum that lines the abdomen).

terms.name: Gastroschisis
terms.definition: A type of congenital ventral incomplete closure of the abdominal wall in which the intestines and sometimes other organs extend freely into the amniotic fluid space through a small opening in the abdomen, usually to the right of the umbilicus.

terms.name: Prominent umbilicus
terms.definition: Abnormally prominent umbilicus (belly button).

terms.name: Anteriorly placed anus
terms.definition: Anterior malposition of the anus.

terms.name: Abnormal rib cage morphology
terms.definition: A morphological anomaly of the rib cage.

terms.name: Overgrowth
terms.definition: Excessive postnatal growth which may comprise increased weight, increased length, and/or increased head circumference.

terms.name: Abnormal umbilicus morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the structure or appearance of the umbilicus.

terms.name: Barrel-shaped chest
terms.definition: A rounded, bulging chest that resembles the shape of a barrel. That is, there is an increased anteroposterior diameter and usually some degree of kyphosis.

terms.name: Asymmetry of the thorax
terms.definition: Lack of symmetry between the left and right halves of the thorax.

terms.name: Prenatal movement abnormality
terms.definition: An abnormality of fetal movement.

terms.name: Decreased fetal movement
synonyms: Less than 10 fetal movements in 12 hours
Less than 10 foetal movements in 12 hours
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction in quantity or strength of fetal movements.

terms.name: Abnormality of the amniotic fluid
terms.definition: Abnormality of the amniotic fluid, which is the fluid contained in the amniotic sac surrounding the developing fetus.

terms.name: Polyhydramnios
terms.definition: The presence of excess amniotic fluid in the uterus during pregnancy.

terms.name: Oligohydramnios
terms.definition: Diminished amniotic fluid volume in pregnancy.

terms.name: Fetal polyuria
terms.definition: Abnormally increased production of urine by the fetus resulting in polyhydramnios.

terms.name: Widely-spaced maxillary central incisors
synonyms: Wide gap between upper central incisors
terms.definition: Increased distance between the maxillary central permanent incisor tooth.

terms.name: Multiple impacted teeth
terms.definition: The presence of multiple impacted teeth.

terms.name: Macrodontia
terms.definition: Increased size of the teeth, which can be defined as a mesiodistal tooth diameter (width) more than 2 SD above mean for age. Alternatively, an apparently increased maximum width of the tooth.

terms.name: Abnormality of the integument
terms.definition: An abnormality of the integument, which consists of the skin and the superficial fascia.

terms.name: Primary hypercortisolism
terms.definition: Hypercortisolemia associated with a primary defect of the adrenal gland leading to overproduction of cortisol.

terms.name: Recurrent skin infections
terms.definition: Infections of the skin that happen multiple times.

terms.name: Redundant skin
terms.definition: Loose and sagging skin often associated with loss of skin elasticity.

terms.name: Rotary nystagmus
terms.definition: A form of nystagmus in which the eyeball makes rotary motions around the axis.

terms.name: Vesicovaginal fistula
terms.definition: The presence of a fistula connecting the urinary bladder to the vagina.

terms.name: Bell-shaped thorax
terms.definition: The rib cage has the shape of a wide mouthed bell. That is, the superior portion of the rib cage is constricted, followed by a convex region, and the inferior portion of the rib cage expands again to have a large diameter.

terms.name: Selective tooth agenesis
synonyms: Failure of development of a tooth
terms.definition: Agenesis specifically affecting one of the classes incisor, premolar, or molar.

terms.name: Maxillary lateral incisor microdontia
synonyms: Decreased width of upper lateral incisor
terms.definition: Decreased size of the maxillary permanent incisor.

terms.name: Abnormal hair morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the hair.

terms.name: Alopecia
terms.definition: A noncongenital process of hair loss, which may progress to partial or complete baldness.

terms.name: Abnormal nail morphology
terms.definition: Abnormal structure or appearance of the nail.

terms.name: Concave nail
terms.definition: The natural longitudinal (posterodistal) convex arch is not present or is inverted.

terms.name: Abnormality of the larynx
terms.definition: An abnormality of the larynx.

terms.name: Laryngomalacia
terms.definition: Laryngomalacia is a congenital abnormality of the laryngeal cartilage in which the cartilage is floppy and prolapses over the larynx during inspiration.

terms.name: Laryngeal stenosis
terms.definition: Stricture or narrowing of the larynx that may be associated with symptoms of respiratory difficulty depending on the degree of laryngeal narrowing.

terms.name: Vocal cord paresis
synonyms: Hoarse voice due to vocal cord paresis
Vocal cord paresis in severe cases
terms.definition: Decreased strength of the vocal folds.

terms.name: Vocal cord paralysis
terms.definition: A loss of the ability to move the vocal folds.

terms.name: Hoarse voice
terms.definition: Hoarseness refers to a change in the pitch or quality of the voice, with the voice sounding weak, very breathy, scratchy, or husky.

terms.name: Hypernasal speech
terms.definition: A type of speech characterized by the presence of an abnormally increased nasal airflow during speech associated with structural abnormality of the nasal passages.

terms.name: Dysphonia
terms.definition: Difficulty in speaking due to a physical disorder of the mouth, tongue, throat, or vocal cords. Associated with a known physical or neurological cause.

terms.name: Abnormally high-pitched voice
terms.definition: A persistent (minutes to hours) abnormal increase in the pitch (frequency) of the voice for the context or social situation or significantly different from baseline of the individual.

terms.name: Weak voice
terms.definition: Reduced intensity (volume) of speech.

terms.name: Premature birth
terms.definition: The birth of a baby of less than 37 weeks of gestational age.

terms.name: Breech presentation
synonyms: Feet or buttocks of fetus positioned near opening of uterus
Feet or buttocks of foetus positioned near opening of uterus
terms.definition: A position of the fetus at delivery in which the fetus enters the birth canal with the buttocks or feet first.

terms.name: Abnormality of the cardiovascular system
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the cardiovascular system.

terms.name: Abnormal heart morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the heart.

terms.name: Ventricular septal defect
synonyms: Hole in heart wall separating two lower heart chambers
terms.definition: A hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart. The defect is centered around the most superior aspect of the ventricular septum.

terms.name: Atrial septal defect
synonyms: An opening in the wall separating the top two chambers of the heart
Hole in heart wall separating two upper heart chambers
terms.definition: Atrial septal defect (ASD) is a congenital abnormality of the interatrial septum that enables blood flow between the left and right atria via the interatrial septum.

terms.name: Abnormal mitral valve morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the mitral valve.

terms.name: Mitral valve prolapse
terms.definition: One or both of the leaflets (cusps) of the mitral valve bulges back into the left atrium upon contraction of the left ventricle.

terms.name: Congestive heart failure
terms.definition: The presence of an abnormality of cardiac function that is responsible for the failure of the heart to pump blood at a rate that is commensurate with the needs of the tissues or a state in which abnormally elevated filling pressures are required for the heart to do so. Heart failure is frequently related to a defect in myocardial contraction.

terms.name: Tetralogy of Fallot
terms.definition: A congenital cardiac malformation comprising pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta, ventricular septum defect, and right ventricular hypertrophy. The diagnosis of TOF is made if at least three of the four above mentioned features are present.

terms.name: Abnormal myocardium morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the muscle layer of the heart wall.

terms.name: Cardiomyopathy
terms.definition: A myocardial disorder in which the heart muscle is structurally and functionally abnormal, in the absence of coronary artery disease, hypertension, valvular disease and congenital heart disease sufficient to cause the observed myocardial abnormality.

terms.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
terms.definition: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is defined by the presence of increased ventricular wall thickness or mass in the absence of loading conditions (hypertension, valve disease) sufficient to cause the observed abnormality.

terms.name: Cardiomegaly
terms.definition: Increased size of the heart, clinically defined as an increased transverse diameter of the cardiac silhouette that is greater than or equal to 50% of the transverse diameter of the chest (increased cardiothoracic ratio) on a posterior-anterior projection of a chest radiograph or a computed tomography.

terms.name: Abnormal pulmonary valve morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the pulmonary valve.

terms.name: Pulmonic stenosis
terms.definition: A narrowing of the right ventricular outflow tract that can occur at the pulmonary valve (valvular stenosis), below the pulmonary valve (infundibular stenosis), or above the pulmonary valve (supravalvar stenosis).

terms.name: Patent ductus arteriosus
terms.definition: In utero, the ductus arteriosus (DA) serves to divert ventricular output away from the lungs and toward the placenta by connecting the main pulmonary artery to the descending aorta. A patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in the first 3 days of life is a physiologic shunt in healthy term and preterm newborn infants, and normally is substantially closed within about 24 hours after bith and completely closed after about three weeks. Failure of physiologcal closure is referred to a persistent or patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). Depending on the degree of left-to-right shunting, PDA can have clinical consequences.

terms.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy
terms.definition: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is defined by the presence of left ventricular dilatation and left ventricular systolic dysfunction in the absence of abnormal loading conditions (hypertension, valve disease) or coronary artery disease sufficient to cause global systolic impairment. Right ventricular dilation and dysfunction may be present but are not necessary for the diagnosis.

terms.name: Sudden cardiac death
terms.definition: The heart suddenly and unexpectedly stops beating resulting in death within a short time period (generally within 1 h of symptom onset).

terms.name: Abnormal aortic valve morphology
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the aortic valve.

terms.name: Bicuspid aortic valve
synonyms: Aortic valve has two leaflets rather than three
terms.definition: The presence of an aortic valve with two instead of the normal three cusps (flaps). Bicuspid aortic valvue is a malformation of a commissure (small space between the attachment of each cusp to the aortic wall) and the adjacent parts of the two corresponding cusps forming a raphe (the fused area of the two underdeveloped cusps turning into a malformed commissure between both cusps; the raphe is a fibrous ridge that extends from the commissure to the free edge of the two underdeveloped, conjoint cusps).

terms.name: Cor pulmonale
terms.definition: Right-sided heart failure resulting from chronic hypertension in the pulmonary arteries and right ventricle.

terms.name: Tachycardia
terms.definition: A rapid heartrate that exceeds the range of the normal resting heartrate for age.

terms.name: Aortic valve stenosis
terms.definition: The presence of a stenosis (narrowing) of the aortic valve.

terms.name: Dextrocardia
synonyms: Heart tip and four chambers point towards right side of body
terms.definition: The heart is located in the right hand sided hemithorax. That is, there is a left-right reversal (or \

terms.name: Mitral regurgitation
terms.definition: An abnormality of the mitral valve characterized by insufficiency or incompetence of the mitral valve resulting in retrograde leaking of blood through the mitral valve upon ventricular contraction.

terms.name: Abnormal heart valve morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of a cardiac valve.

terms.name: Patent foramen ovale
terms.definition: Failure of the foramen ovale to seal postnatally, leaving a potential conduit between the left and right cardiac atria.

terms.name: Prolonged QT interval
terms.definition: Increased time between the start of the Q wave and the end of the T wave as measured by the electrocardiogram (EKG).

terms.name: Myocardial infarction
terms.definition: Necrosis of the myocardium caused by an obstruction of the blood supply to the heart and often associated with chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, and anxiety as well as characteristic EKG findings and elevation of serum markers including creatine kinase-MB fraction and troponin.

terms.name: Aortic regurgitation
terms.definition: An insufficiency of the aortic valve, leading to regurgitation (backward flow) of blood from the aorta into the left ventricle.

terms.name: Truncus arteriosus
terms.definition: A single arterial trunk arises from the cardiac mass. The pulmonary arteries, aorta and coronary arteries arise from this single trunk with no evidence of another outflow tract.

terms.name: Bradycardia
terms.definition: A slower than normal heart rate (in adults, slower than 60 beats per minute).

terms.name: Ventricular fibrillation
terms.definition: Uncontrolled contractions of muscles fibers in the left ventricle not producing contraction of the left ventricle. Ventricular fibrillation usually begins with a ventricular premature contraction and a short run of rapid ventricular tachycardia degenerating into uncoordinating ventricular fibrillations.

terms.name: Torsade de pointes
terms.definition: A type of ventricular tachycardia characterized by polymorphioc QRS complexes that change in amplitue and cycle length, and thus have the appearance of oscillating around the baseline in the EKG.

terms.name: Right ventricular hypertrophy
terms.definition: In this case the right ventricle is more muscular than normal, causing a characteristic boot-shaped (coeur-en-sabot) appearance as seen on anterior- posterior chest x-rays. Right ventricular hypertrophy is commonly associated with any form of right ventricular outflow obstruction or pulmonary hypertension, which may in turn owe its origin to left-sided disease. The echocardiographic signs are thickening of the anterior right ventricular wall and the septum. Cavity size is usually normal, or slightly enlarged. In many cases there is associated volume overload present due to tricuspid regurgitation, in the absence of this, septal motion is normal.

terms.name: Transposition of the great arteries
terms.definition: A complex congenital heart defect in which the aorta arises from the morphologic right ventricle and the pulmonary artery arises from the morphologic left ventricle.

terms.name: Asymmetric septal hypertrophy
terms.definition: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with an asymmetrical pattern of hypertrophy, with a predilection for the interventricular septum and myocyte disarray.

terms.name: Abnormal cardiac septum morphology
terms.definition: An anomaly of the intra-atrial or intraventricular septum.

terms.name: Complete atrioventricular canal defect
terms.definition: A congenital heart defect characterized by a specific combination of heart defects with a common atrioventricular valve, primum atrial septal defect and inlet ventricular septal defect.

terms.name: Coronary artery atherosclerosis
synonyms: Plaque build-up in arteries supplying blood to heart
terms.definition: Reduction of the diameter of the coronary arteries as the result of an accumulation of atheromatous plaques within the walls of the coronary arteries, which increases the risk of myocardial ischemia.

terms.name: Atrioventricular block
synonyms: Interruption of electrical communication between upper and lower chambers of heart
terms.definition: Delayed or lack of conduction of atrial depolarizations through the atrioventricular node to the ventricles.

terms.name: Abnormal aortic morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the aorta.

terms.name: Coarctation of aorta
terms.definition: Coarctation of the aorta is a narrowing or constriction of a segment of the aorta.

terms.name: Angina pectoris
terms.definition: Paroxysmal chest pain that occurs with exertion or stress and is related to myocardial ischemia.

terms.name: Subvalvular aortic stenosis
synonyms: Narrowing of blood vessel below aortic heart valve
terms.definition: A fixed form of obstruction to blood flow across the left-ventricular outflow tract related to stenosis (narrowing) below the level of the aortic valve.

terms.name: Ectopia cordis
terms.definition: Congenital malformation of the ventral wall with partial or total evisceration of the heart outside the thoracic cavity and through the defect in the ventral wall.

terms.name: Secundum atrial septal defect
synonyms: Atrial septal defect, ostium secundum type
terms.definition: A kind of atrial septum defect arising from an enlarged foramen ovale, inadequate growth of the septum secundum, or excessive absorption of the septum primum.

terms.name: Myocardial fibrosis
terms.definition: Myocardial fibrosis is characterized by dysregulated collagen turnover (increased synthesis predominates over unchanged or decreased degradation) and excessive diffuse collagen accumulation in the interstitial and perivascular spaces as well as by phenotypically transformed fibroblasts, termed myofibroblasts.

terms.name: Sinus bradycardia
terms.definition: Bradycardia related to a mean resting sinus rate of less than 50 beats per minute.

terms.name: Muscular subvalvular aortic stenosis
terms.definition: A type of subvalvular aortic stenosis resulting from thickening of the musculature of the interventricular septum, which results in obstruction to blood flow through the left-ventricular outflow tract.

terms.name: Atrial arrhythmia
terms.definition: A type of supraventricular tachycardia in which the atria are the principal site of electrophysiologic disturbance.

terms.name: Cardiac shunt
terms.definition: Pattern of blood flow in the heart that deviates from the normal circuit of the circulatory system.

terms.name: Right-to-left shunt
terms.definition: Pattern of blood flow in the heart that deviates from the normal circuit of the circulatory system from the right side of the heart to the left.

terms.name: Cardiac arrest
terms.definition: An abrupt loss of heart function.

terms.name: Situs inversus totalis
synonyms: All organs on wrong side of body
terms.definition: A left-right reversal (or mirror reflection) of the anatomical location of the major thoracic and abdominal organs.

terms.name: Abnormal pericardium morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the pericardium, i.e., of the fluid filled sac that surrounds the heart and the proximal ends of the aorta, vena cava, and the pulmonary artery.

terms.name: Pericardial effusion
terms.definition: Accumulation of fluid within the pericardium.

terms.name: Sudden death
terms.definition: Rapid and unexpected death.

terms.name: Myocardial necrosis
terms.definition: Irreversible damage to heart tissue (myocardium) due to lack of oxygen after a heart attack (myocardial infarction).

terms.name: Pericarditis
synonyms: Swelling or irritation of membrane around heart
terms.definition: Inflammation of the sac-like covering around the heart (pericardium).

terms.name: Abnormal tricuspid valve morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the tricuspid valve.

terms.name: Tricuspid valve prolapse
terms.definition: One or more of the leaflets (cusps) of the tricuspid valve bulges back into the right atrium upon contraction of the right ventricle.

terms.name: Right ventricular outlet tract obstruction
terms.definition: An obstruction to the forward flow of blood in the outflow tract of the right ventricle.

terms.name: Endocardial fibroelastosis
terms.name_zh: 心内膜弹力纤维增生症
terms.definition: Diffuse thickening of the ventricular endocardium and by associated myocardial dysfunction

terms.name: Abnormal right ventricle morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the right ventricle of the heart.

terms.name: Right ventricular failure
terms.definition: Reduced ability of the right ventricle to perform its function (to receive blood from the right atrium and to eject blood into the pulmonary artery), often leading to pitting peripheral edema, ascites, and hepatomegaly.

terms.name: Third degree atrioventricular block
terms.definition: Third-degree atrioventricular (AV) block (also referred to as complete heart block) is the complete dissociation of the atria and the ventricles. Third-degree AV block exists when more P waves than QRS complexes exist and no relationship (no conduction) exists between them.

terms.name: Conotruncal defect
terms.definition: A congenital malformation of the outflow tract of the heart. Conotruncal defects are thought to result from a disturbance of the outflow tract of the embryonic heart, and comprise truncus arteriosus, tetralogy of Fallot, interrupted aortic arch, transposition of the great arteries, and double outlet right ventricle.

terms.name: Abnormal left ventricle morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the left ventricle of the heart.

terms.name: Left ventricular hypertrophy
terms.definition: Enlargement or increased size of the heart left ventricle.

terms.name: Abnormal cardiac ventricle morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of a cardiac ventricle.

terms.name: Ventricular hypertrophy
terms.definition: Enlargement of the cardiac ventricular muscle tissue with increase in the width of the wall of the ventricle and loss of elasticity. Ventricular hypertrophy is clinically differentiated into left and right ventricular hypertrophy.

terms.name: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
terms.definition: A disorder of the cardiac conduction system of the heart characterized by ventricular preexcitation due to the presence of an abnormal accessory atrioventricular electrical conduction pathway.

terms.name: Coronary artery calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in a coronary artery.

terms.name: Mitral stenosis
terms.definition: An abnormal narrowing of the orifice of the mitral valve.

terms.name: Double outlet right ventricle
terms.definition: Double outlet right ventricle (DORV) is a type of ventriculoarterial connection in which both great vessels arise entirely or predominantly from the right ventricle.

terms.name: High-output congestive heart failure
terms.name_zh: 高输出量充血性心力衰竭
terms.definition: A form of heart failure characterized by elevated cardiac output. This may be seen in patients with heart failure and hyperthyroidism, anemia, pregnancy, arteriovenous fistulae, and others.

terms.name: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
terms.definition: Restrictive left ventricular physiology is characterized by a pattern of ventricular filling in which increased stiffness of the myocardium causes ventricular pressure to rise precipitously with only small increases in volume, defined as restrictive ventricular physiology in the presence of normal or reduced diastolic volumes (of one or both ventricles), normal or reduced systolic volumes, and normal ventricular wall thickness.

terms.name: Thromboembolic stroke
terms.definition: A cerebrovascular accident (stroke) that occurs because of thromboembolism.

terms.name: Progressive hearing impairment
terms.definition: A progressive form of hearing impairment.

terms.name: Abnormality of the pancreas
terms.definition: An abnormality of the pancreas.

terms.name: Pancreatitis
terms.definition: The presence of inflammation in the pancreas.

terms.name: Annular pancreas
terms.definition: A congenital anomaly in which the pancreas completely (or sometimes incompletely) encircles the second portion of duodenum and occasionally obstructs the more proximal duodenum.

terms.name: Acute pancreatitis
terms.definition: A acute form of pancreatitis.

terms.name: Pancreatic cysts
terms.definition: A cyst of the pancreas that possess a lining of mucous epithelium.

terms.name: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
synonyms: Inability to properly digest food due to lack of pancreatic digestive enzymes
terms.definition: Impaired function of the exocrine pancreas associated with a reduced ability to digest foods because of lack of digestive enzymes.

terms.name: Abnormal nasopharynx morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the nasopharynx.

terms.name: Phimosis
terms.definition: The male foreskin cannot be fully retracted from the head of the penis.

terms.name: Nasal congestion
terms.definition: Reduced ability to pass air through the nasal cavity often leading to mouth breathing.

terms.name: Abnormality of the spleen
terms.definition: An abnormality of the spleen.

terms.name: Splenomegaly
terms.definition: Abnormal increased size of the spleen.

terms.name: Asplenia
terms.definition: Absence (aplasia) of the spleen.

terms.name: Accessory spleen
terms.definition: An accessory spleen is a round, iso-echogenic, homogenic and smooth structure and is seen as a normal variant mostly on the medial contour of the spleen, near the hilus or around the lower pole. This has no pathogenic relevance.

terms.name: Polysplenia
terms.definition: Polysplenia is a congenital disease manifested by multiple small accessory spleens.

terms.name: Single ventricle
terms.definition: The presence of only one working lower chamber in the heart, usually with a virtual absence of the ventricular septum and usually present in conjunction with double inlet left or right ventricle.

terms.name: Abnormal vestibular function
terms.definition: An abnormality of the functioning of the vestibular apparatus.

terms.name: Vestibular hyporeflexia
terms.definition: A general descriptive term that describes impaired functioning of the vestibular apparatus that leads to manifestations such as dizziness or postural imbalance

terms.name: High-frequency sensorineural hearing impairment
terms.name_zh: 高频感音神经性听力损害
terms.definition: A form of sensorineural hearing impairment that affects primarily the higher frequencies.

terms.name: Abnormal foot morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the skeleton of foot.

terms.name: Pes cavus
terms.definition: An increase in height of the medial longitudinal arch of the foot that does not flatten on weight bearing (i.e., a distinctly hollow form of the sole of the foot when it is bearing weight).

terms.name: Talipes equinovarus
terms.definition: Talipes equinovarus (also called clubfoot) typically has four main components: inversion and adduction of the forefoot; inversion of the heel and hindfoot; equinus (limitation of extension) of the ankle and subtalar joint; and internal rotation of the leg.

terms.name: Pes planus
terms.definition: A foot where the longitudinal arch of the foot is in contact with the ground or floor when the individual is standing; or, in a patient lying supine, a foot where the arch is in contact with the surface of a flat board pressed against the sole of the foot by the examiner with a pressure similar to that expected from weight bearing; or, the height of the arch is reduced.

terms.name: Hammertoe
terms.definition: Hyperextension of the metatarsal-phalangeal joint with hyperflexion of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint.

terms.name: Broad foot
terms.definition: A foot for which the measured width is above the 95th centile for age; or, a foot that appears disproportionately wide for its length.

terms.name: Toe syndactyly
terms.definition: Webbing or fusion of the toes, involving soft parts only or including bone structure. Bony fusions are referred to as \

terms.name: Achilles tendon contracture
terms.definition: A contracture of the Achilles tendon.

terms.name: Talipes equinovalgus
terms.definition: A deformity of foot and ankle in which the foot is bent down and outwards.

terms.name: Short foot
terms.definition: A measured foot length that is more than 2 SD below the mean for a newborn of 27 - 41 weeks gestation, or foot that is less than the 3rd centile for individuals from birth to 16 years of age (objective). Alternatively, a foot that appears disproportionately short (subjective).

terms.name: Bilateral talipes equinovarus
terms.definition: Bilateral clubfoot deformity.

terms.name: Abnormal toe morphology
terms.definition: An anomaly of a toe.

terms.name: Bulbous tips of toes
terms.definition: An abnormality of the morphology of the toes, such that the tips of the toes are prominent and bulbous.

terms.name: Broad metatarsal
terms.definition: Increased side-to-side width of a metatarsal bone.

terms.name: Narrow foot
terms.definition: A foot for which the measured width is below the 5th centile for age; or, a foot that appears disproportionately narrow for its length.

terms.name: Abnormal delivery
terms.definition: An abnormality of the birth process.

terms.name: Premature rupture of membranes
terms.definition: Premature rupture of membranes (PROM) is a condition which occurs in pregnancy when the amniotic sac ruptures more than an hour before the onset of labor.

terms.name: Hydrops fetalis
terms.definition: The abnormal accumulation of fluid in two or more fetal compartments, including ascites, pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, and skin edema.

terms.name: Nonimmune hydrops fetalis
terms.definition: A type of hydrops fetalis in which there is no identifiable circulating antibody to red blood cell antigens .

terms.name: Fetal ascites
terms.definition: Accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity during the fetal period.

terms.name: Small nail
terms.definition: A nail that is diminished in length and width, i.e., underdeveloped nail.

terms.name: Hyperconvex nail
terms.definition: When viewed on end (with the digit tip pointing toward the examiner's eye) the curve of the nail forms a tighter curve of convexity.

terms.name: Anonychia
terms.definition: Aplasia of the nail.

terms.name: Short nail
terms.definition: Decreased length of nail.

terms.name: Hypoplastic toenails
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the toenail.

terms.name: Absent toenail
terms.definition: Congenital absence of the toenail.

terms.name: Nail pits
terms.definition: Small (typically about 1 mm or less in size) depressions on the dorsal nail surface.

terms.name: Hypoplastic fingernail
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of a fingernail.

terms.name: Onychogryphosis
terms.definition: Onychogryphosis is a disorder of nail plate growth that is clinically characterized by an opaque, yellow-brown thickening of the nail plate with associated gross hyperkeratosis, elongation, and increased curvature.

terms.name: Onycholysis
terms.definition: Detachment of the nail from the nail bed.

terms.name: Ridged nail
terms.definition: Longitudinal, linear prominences in the nail plate.

terms.name: Fragile nails
terms.definition: Nails that easily break.

terms.name: Split nail
terms.definition: A nail plate that has a longitudinal separation and the two sections of the nail share the same lateral radius of curvature.

terms.name: Dystrophic toenail
terms.definition: Toenail changes apart from changes of the color of the toenail (nail dyschromia) that involve partial or complete disruption of the various keratinous layers of the nail plate.

terms.name: Hyperconvex fingernails
terms.definition: When viewed on end (with the finger tip pointing toward the examiner's eye) the curve of the fingernail forms a tighter curve of convexity.

terms.name: Deep-set nails
terms.definition: Deeply placed nails.

terms.name: Thin nail
terms.definition: Nail that appears thin when viewed on end.

terms.name: Absent fingernail
terms.definition: Absence of a fingernail.

terms.name: Paronychia
terms.definition: The nail disease paronychia is an often-tender bacterial or fungal hand infection or foot infection where the nail and skin meet at the side or the base of a finger or toenail. The infection can start suddenly (acute paronychia) or gradually (chronic paronychia).

terms.name: Leukonychia
terms.definition: White discoloration of the nails.

terms.name: Broad nail
terms.definition: Increased width of nail.

terms.name: Hallux valgus
terms.definition: Lateral deviation of the great toe (i.e., in the direction of the little toe).

terms.name: Weight loss
terms.definition: Reduction of total body weight.

terms.name: Genital tract atresia
terms.definition: Congenital occlusion of a tube in the genital tract.

terms.name: Foot polydactyly
synonyms: Duplication of bones of the toes
terms.definition: A kind of polydactyly characterized by the presence of a supernumerary toe or toes.

terms.name: Postaxial foot polydactyly
synonyms: Extra toe attached near the little toe
terms.definition: Polydactyly of the foot most commonly refers to the presence of six toes on one foot. Postaxial polydactyly affects the lateral ray and the duplication may range from a well-formed articulated digit to a rudimentary digit.

terms.name: Short toe
terms.definition: A toe that appears disproportionately short compared to the foot.

terms.name: Abnormal metatarsal morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of the long bone of foot
terms.definition: Abnormalities of the metatarsal bones (i.e. of five tubular bones located between the tarsal bones of the hind- and mid-foot and the phalanges of the toes).

terms.name: Long foot
terms.definition: Increased back to front length of the foot.

terms.name: Camptodactyly of toe
terms.definition: Camptodactyly is a painless flexion contracture of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint that is usually gradually progressive. This term refers to camptodactyly of one or more toes.

terms.name: Broad toe
terms.definition: Visible increase in width of the non-hallux digit without an increase in the dorso-ventral dimension.

terms.name: Rocker bottom foot
terms.definition: The presence of both a prominent heel and a convex contour of the sole.

terms.name: Split foot
terms.definition: A condition in which middle parts of the foot (toes and metatarsals) are missing giving a cleft appearance. The severity is very variable ranging from slightly hypoplastic 3rd toe over absent 2nd or 3rd toes as far as oligo- or monodactyl feet.

terms.name: Metatarsus adductus
synonyms: Front half of foot turns inward
terms.definition: The metatarsals are deviated medially (tibially), that is, the bones in the front half of the foot bend or turn in toward the body.

terms.name: Preaxial foot polydactyly
synonyms: Partial/complete duplication of the phalanges of the big toe
terms.definition: Duplication of all or part of the first ray.

terms.name: Abnormal hallux morphology
terms.definition: This term applies for all abnormalities of the big toe, also called hallux.

terms.name: Overlapping toe
terms.definition: Describes a foot digit resting on the dorsal surface of an adjacent digit when the foot is at rest. Initially clawing may be dynamic and only noticeable on walking. Over time the plantar plate tears, subluxation occurs at the metatarsophalangeal joint (MTPJ), and the deformity becomes permanent.

terms.name: Long hallux
terms.definition: Increased length of the big toe.

terms.name: Calcaneovalgus deformity
terms.definition: This is a postural deformity in which the foot is positioned up against the tibia. The heel (calcaneus) is positioned downward (that is, the ankle is flexed upward), and the heel is turned outward (valgus).

terms.name: Foot oligodactyly
terms.definition: A developmental defect resulting in the presence of fewer than the normal number of toes.

terms.name: Abnormality of the tarsal bones
terms.definition: An abnormality of the tarsus are the cluster of seven bones in the foot between the tibia and fibula and the metatarsus, including the calcaneus (heel) bone and the talus (ankle) bone.

terms.name: Sandal gap
synonyms: Gap between first and second toe
Increased space between first and second toes
Sandal gap between first and second toes
Space between great toe and second toe
Wide space between first and second toes
Widely spaced first and second toes
Widened gap first and second toe
terms.definition: A widely spaced gap between the first toe (the great toe) and the second toe.

terms.name: Podagra
terms.definition: Gout affecting the Metatarsophalangeal joint of big toe.

terms.name: Short distal phalanx of toe
terms.definition: Short distance from the end of the toe to the most distal interphalangeal crease or distal interphalangeal joint flexion point, i.e., abnormally short distal phalanx of toe.

terms.name: Distal toe symphalangism
terms.definition: Bony fusion at the distal interphalangeal joint of the second, third, fourth, or fifth toe.

terms.name: Toe clinodactyly
terms.definition: Bending or curvature of a toe in the tibial direction (i.e., towards the big toe).

terms.name: Clinodactyly of the 5th toe
terms.definition: Bending or curvature of a fifth toe in the tibial direction (i.e., towards the big toe).

terms.name: Autoamputation of foot
terms.definition: The spontaneous detachment of a foot from the body due to long standing pathology.

terms.name: Deep plantar creases
synonyms: Deep wrinkles in soles of feet
terms.definition: The presence of unusually deep creases (ridges/wrinkles) on the skin of sole of foot.

terms.name: Acroosteolysis of distal phalanges (feet)
terms.name_zh: 足远端指骨肢端骨溶解
synonyms: Acroosteolysis of distal phalanges of feet

terms.name: Abnormality of blood and blood-forming tissues
synonyms: Abnormality of blood and blood-forming tissues
terms.definition: An abnormality of the hematopoietic system.

terms.name: Abnormality of thrombocytes
terms.definition: An abnormality of platelets.

terms.name: Thrombocytopenia
terms.definition: A reduction in the number of circulating thrombocytes.

terms.name: Abnormality of neutrophils
terms.definition: A neutrophil abnormality.

terms.name: Decreased total neutrophil count
terms.name_zh: 总中性粒细胞计数降低
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of absolute number of neutrophils in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Pancytopenia
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction in numbers of all blood cell types (red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets).

terms.name: Abnormal erythrocyte morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of erythrocytes (red-blood cells).

terms.name: Hemolytic anemia
terms.definition: A type of anemia caused by premature destruction of red blood cells (hemolysis).

terms.name: Abnormal eosinophil morphology
terms.name_zh: 嗜酸性粒细胞形态异常
terms.definition: An abnormal count or structure of eosinophils.

terms.name: Increased total eosinophil count
terms.name_zh: 总嗜酸性粒细胞计数升高
terms.definition: Increased count of eosinophils in the blood.

terms.name: Abnormal leukocyte morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of leukocytes.

terms.name: Decreased total leukocyte count
terms.definition: An abnormal decreased number of leukocytes in the blood.

terms.name: Talipes
terms.definition: A deformity of foot and ankle that has different subtypes that are talipes equinovarus, talipes equinovalgus, talipes calcaneovarus and talipes calcaneovalgus.

terms.name: Talipes calcaneovalgus
terms.definition: Talipes calcaneovalgus is a flexible foot deformity (as opposed to a rigid congenital vertical talus foot deformity) that can either present as a positional or structural foot deformity depending on severity and/or causality. The axis of calcaneovalgus deformity is in the tibiotalar joint, where the foot is positioned in extreme hyperextension. On inspection, the foot has an \

terms.name: Short 2nd toe
terms.definition: Underdevelopment (hypoplasia) of the second toe.

terms.name: Foot osteomyelitis
terms.definition: An infection of bone of the foot.

terms.name: Decreased total lymphocyte count
terms.definition: A reduced number of lymphocytes in the blood.

terms.name: Megaloblastic anemia
terms.definition: Anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal (megaloblasts).

terms.name: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia
terms.name_zh: 自身免疫性溶血性贫血
terms.definition: An autoimmune form of hemolytic anemia.

terms.name: Abnormal bleeding
terms.definition: An abnormal susceptibility to bleeding, often referred to as a bleeding diathesis. A bleeding diathesis may be related to vascular, platelet and coagulation defects.

terms.name: Thrombocytosis
synonyms: Increased number of platelets in blood
terms.definition: Increased numbers of platelets in the peripheral blood.

terms.name: Reticulocytopenia
terms.definition: A reduced number of reticulocytes in the peripheral blood.

terms.name: Normocytic anemia
terms.definition: A kind of anemia in which the volume of the red blood cells is normal.

terms.name: Increased red blood cell mass
terms.definition: The presence of an increased mass of red blood cells in the circulation.

terms.name: Increased hematocrit
terms.definition: An elevation above the normal ratio of the volume of red blood cells to the total volume of blood.

terms.name: Increased circulating hemoglobin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环血红蛋白浓度升高
terms.definition: Concentration of hemoglobin in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Polycythemia
terms.definition: Polycythemia is diagnosed if the red blood cell count, the hemoglobin level, and the red blood cell volume all exceed the upper limits of normal.

terms.name: Giant platelets
terms.definition: Giant platelets are larger than 7 micrometers and usually 10 to 20 micrometers. The term giant platelet is used when the platelet is larger than the size of the average red cell in the field. (Description adapted from College of American Pathologists, Hematology Manual, 1998).

terms.name: Anemia
synonyms: Low number of red blood cells or haemoglobin
Low number of red blood cells or hemoglobin
terms.definition: A reduction in erythrocytes volume or hemoglobin concentration.

terms.name: Autoimmune neutropenia
terms.name_zh: 自身免疫性中性粒细胞减少症
synonyms: Neutropenia in presence of anti-neutropil antibodies
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of the absolute number of neutrophils in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group, accompanied by the detection of anti-neutrophil antibodies.

terms.name: Congenital thrombocytopenia
terms.definition: Thrombocytopenia with congenital onset.

terms.name: Thromboembolism
terms.definition: The formation of a blood clot inside a blood vessel that subsequently travels through the blood stream from the site where it formed to another location in the body, generally leading to vascular occlusion at the distant site.

terms.name: Hypoplastic anemia
terms.definition: Anemia with varying degrees of erythrocytic hypoplasia without leukopenia or thrombocytopenia.

terms.name: Leukemia
terms.definition: A cancer of the blood and bone marrow characterized by an abnormal proliferation of leukocytes.

terms.name: Abnormal granulocyte morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality or abnormal count of granulocytes.

terms.name: Abnormal basophil morphology
terms.name_zh: 嗜碱性粒细胞形态异常
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality or abnormal count of basophils.

terms.name: Decreased total granulocyte count
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of absolute number of granulocytes in the blood, per microliter, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Aplastic anemia
terms.definition: Aplastic anemia is defined as pancytopenia with a hypocellular marrow.

terms.name: Renal amyloidosis
terms.definition: A form of amyloidosis that affects the kidney. On hematoxylin and eosin stain, amyloid is identified as extracellular amorphous material that is lightly eosinophilic. These deposits often stain weakly for periodic acid Schiff (PAS), demonstrate a blue-to-gray hue on the trichrome stain and are typically negative on the Jones methenamine silver (JMS) stain. These tinctorial properties contrast with the histologic appearance of collagen, a major component of basement membranes, mesangial matrix and areas of sclerosis, which demonstrates strong positivity for PAS and JMS (See Figure 1 of PMID:25852856).

terms.name: Acute kidney injury
terms.definition: Sudden loss of renal function, as manifested by decreased urine production, and a rise in serum creatinine or blood urea nitrogen concentration (azotemia).

terms.name: Renal artery stenosis
terms.definition: The presence of stenosis of the renal artery.

terms.name: Vacuolated lymphocytes
terms.definition: The presence of clear, sharply defined vacuoles in the lymphocyte cytoplasm.

terms.name: Reticulocytosis
synonyms: Increased number of immature red blood cells
terms.definition: An elevation in the number of reticulocytes (immature erythrocytes) in the peripheral blood circulation.

terms.name: Sideroblastic anemia
