terms.definition: Sideroblastic anemia results from a defect in the incorporation of iron into the heme molecule. A sideroblast is an erythroblast that has stainable deposits of iron in cytoplasm (this can be demonstrated by Prussian blue staining).

terms.name: Acanthocytosis
terms.definition: Acanthocytosis is a type of poikilocytosis characterized by the presence of spikes on the cell surface. The cells have an irregular shape resembling many-pointed stars.

terms.name: Abnormality of coagulation
terms.definition: An abnormality of the process of blood coagulation. That is, altered ability or inability of the blood to clot.

terms.name: Reduced factor XI activity
terms.definition: Decreased activity of coagulation factor XI. Factor XI, also known as plasma thromboplastin antecedent, is a serine proteinase that activates factor IX.

terms.name: Hypochromic anemia
terms.definition: A type of anemia characterized by an abnormally low concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes.

terms.name: Subcutaneous hemorrhage
terms.definition: This term refers to an abnormally increased susceptibility to bruising (purpura, petechiae, or ecchymoses).

terms.name: Microcytic anemia
terms.definition: A kind of anemia in which the volume of the red blood cells is reduced.

terms.name: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia
terms.name_zh: 微血管病性溶血性贫血

terms.name: Acidosis
terms.definition: Abnormal acid accumulation or depletion of base.

terms.name: Metabolic acidosis
terms.definition: Metabolic acidosis (MA) is characterized by a fall in blood pH due to a reduction of serum bicarbonate concentration. This can occur as a result of either the accumulation of acids (high anion gap MA) or the loss of bicarbonate from the gastrointestinal tract or the kidney (hyperchloremic MA). By definition, MA is not due to a respirary cause.

terms.name: Hypoglycemia
terms.definition: A decreased concentration of glucose in the blood.

terms.name: Fever
terms.definition: Body temperature elevated above the normal range.

terms.name: Ketosis
terms.definition: Presence of elevated levels of ketone bodies in the body.

terms.name: Renal tubular acidosis
synonyms: Accumulation of acid in body due to kidney problem
terms.definition: Acidosis owing to malfunction of the kidney tubules with accumulation of metabolic acids and hyperchloremia, potentially leading to complications including hypokalemia, hypercalcinuria, nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis.

terms.name: Alkalosis
terms.definition: Depletion of acid or accumulation base in the body fluids.

terms.name: Respiratory alkalosis
terms.definition: Alkalosis due to excess loss of carbon dioxide from the body.

terms.name: Glucose intolerance
terms.definition: Glucose intolerance (GI) can be defined as dysglycemia that comprises both prediabetes and diabetes. It includes the conditions of impaired fasting glucose (IFG) and impaired glucose tolerance (IGT) and diabetes mellitus (DM).

terms.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
terms.definition: A type of diabetic metabolic abnormality with an accumulation of ketone bodies.

terms.name: Recurrent fever
terms.definition: Periodic (episodic or recurrent) bouts of fever.

terms.name: Unexplained fevers
terms.definition: Episodes of fever for which no infectious cause can be identified.

terms.name: Truncal obesity
terms.definition: Obesity located preferentially in the trunk of the body as opposed to the extremities.

terms.name: Polydipsia
terms.definition: Excessive thirst manifested by excessive fluid intake.

terms.name: Hypoplastic ventricle
terms.definition: A congenital defect characterized by underdevelopment of a ventricle of the heart.

terms.name: Palpitations
terms.definition: A sensation that the heart is pounding or racing, which is a non-specific sign but may be a manifestation of arrhythmia.

terms.name: Abnormal speech discrimination
terms.definition: A type of hearing impairment prominently characterized by a difficulty in understanding speech, rather than an inability to hear speech. Poor speech discrimination is a very common symptom of high frequency hearing loss.

terms.name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of metatarsal bones
terms.name_zh: 跖骨发育不全/发育不良
terms.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the metatarsal bones.

terms.name: Abnormal scalp morphology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the scalp, the skin an subcutaneous tissue of the head on which head hair grows.

terms.name: Abnormal glomerular mesangium morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the mesangium, i.e., of the central part of the renal glomerulus between capillaries.

terms.name: Diffuse mesangial sclerosis
terms.definition: Thickening and scarring (sclerosis) of the mesangium (a structure in the glomerulus). The sclerosis affects a large portion of the mesangium across multiple glomeruli. Histologic features include an increase in the mesangial matrix, thickened glomerular basement membrane, tubular casts, and interstitial inflammation. Diffuse mesangial sclerosis presents with nephrotic syndrome at birth or within the first year of life. Glomeruli are small and condensed in appearance, with early lesions showing increased loose mesangial collagen that progress to sclerosis with dense collagen without hypercellularity. Podocytes do not show hyperplasia but may be immature and cobblestone-like. Electron microscopy shows extensive foot process effacement without deposits, but increased collagen within mesangial areas.

terms.name: Abnormal tubulointerstitial morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality that involves the tubules and interstitial tissue of the kidney.

terms.name: Tubulointerstitial nephritis
terms.definition: A form of inflammation of the kidney affecting the interstitium of the kidneys surrounding the tubules.

terms.name: Hypersplenism
terms.definition: A malfunctioning of the spleen in which it prematurely destroys red blood cells.

terms.name: Macrocytic anemia
terms.definition: A type of anemia characterized by increased size of erythrocytes with increased mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and increased mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH).

terms.name: Autoimmune thrombocytopenia
terms.name_zh: 自身免疫性血小板减少症
terms.definition: The presence of thrombocytopenia in combination with detection of antiplatelet antibodies.

terms.name: Increased total leukocyte count
terms.definition: An abnormal increase in the number of leukocytes in the blood.

terms.name: Decreased platelet glycoprotein IIb-IIIa
synonyms: Reduced level of platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa complex
terms.definition: Decreased cell membrane concentration of glycoprotein IIb-IIIa.

terms.name: Reduced antithrombin III activity
terms.definition: An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of antithrombin-III.

terms.name: Abnormal thrombosis
terms.definition: Venous or arterial thrombosis (formation of blood clots) of spontaneous nature and which cannot be fully explained by acquired risk (e.g. atherosclerosis).

terms.name: Extramedullary hematopoiesis
terms.definition: The process of hematopoiesis occurring outside of the bone marrow (in the liver, thymus, and spleen) in the postnatal organisms.

terms.name: Megaloblastic bone marrow
terms.definition: Abnormal increased number of megaloblasts in the bone marrow.

terms.name: Schistocytosis
terms.definition: The presence of an abnormal number of fragmented red blood cells (schistocytes) in the blood.

terms.name: Sea-blue histiocytosis
terms.definition: An abnormality of histiocytes, in which the cells take on a sea blue appearance due to abnormally increased lipid content. Histiocytes are a type of macrophage. Sea-blue histiocytes are typically large macrophages from 20 to 60 micrometers in diameter with a single eccentric nucleus whose cytoplasm if packed with sea-blue or blue-green granules when stained with Wright-Giemsa.

terms.name: Reduced lymphocyte surface expression of CD43
synonyms: Cd43 defectively expressed on surface of blood cells
Reduced lymphocyte surface expression of sialophorin
terms.definition: A reduction in the expression of CD43 on the cell surface of lymphocytes.

terms.name: Hypoketotic hypoglycemia
terms.definition: A decreased concentration of glucose in the blood associated with a reduced concentration of ketone bodies.

terms.name: Hyperammonemia
terms.definition: An increased concentration of ammonia in the blood.

terms.name: Recurrent hypoglycemia
terms.definition: Recurrent episodes of decreased concentration of glucose in the blood.

terms.name: Fetal akinesia sequence
terms.definition: Decreased fetal activity associated with multiple joint contractures, facial anomalies and pulmonary hypoplasia. Ultrasound examination may reveal polyhydramnios, ankylosis, scalp edema, and decreased chest movements (reflecting pulmonary hypoplasia).

terms.name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of toe
terms.name_zh: 足趾发育不全/发育不良
terms.definition: Absence or hypoplasia of toes.

terms.name: Organic aciduria
terms.definition: Excretion of non-amino organic acids in urine.

terms.name: Ketoacidosis
terms.definition: Acidosis resulting from accumulation of ketone bodies.

terms.name: Renal Fanconi syndrome
terms.definition: An inability of the tubules in the kidney to reabsorb small molecules, causing increased urinary loss of electrolytes (sodium, potassium, bicarbonate), minerals, glucose, amino acids, and water.

terms.name: Hyperchloremic acidosis
terms.definition: Acidosis (pH less than 7.35) that develops with an increase in ionic chloride.

terms.name: Chronic metabolic acidosis
terms.definition: Longstanding metabolic acidosis.

terms.name: Gout
terms.definition: Recurrent attacks of acute inflammatory arthritis of a joint or set of joints caused by elevated levels of uric acid in the blood which crystallize and are deposited in joints, tendons, and surrounding tissues.

terms.name: Abnormal facial shape
terms.definition: An abnormal morphology (form) of the face or its components.

terms.name: Short columella
terms.definition: Reduced distance from the anterior border of the naris to the subnasale.

terms.name: Deep philtrum
terms.definition: Accentuated, prominent philtral ridges giving rise to an exaggerated groove in the midline between the nasal base and upper vermillion border.

terms.name: Large forehead
synonyms: Increased size of frontal region of face

terms.name: Tessier cleft
terms.definition: A congenital malformation with a cleft (gap or opening) in the face.

terms.name: Frontal bossing
terms.definition: Bilateral bulging of the lateral frontal bone prominences with relative sparing of the midline.

terms.name: Potter facies
terms.definition: A facial appearance characteristic of a fetus or neonate due to oligohydramnios experienced in the womb, comprising ocular hypertelorism, low-set ears, receding chin, and flattening of the nose.

terms.name: Narrow maxilla
synonyms: Decreased breadth of upper jaw bones
Decreased width of upper jaw bones

terms.name: Morphological central nervous system abnormality
terms.name_zh: 中枢神经系统形态异常
synonyms: Abnormality of the central nervous system
Morphological abnormality of the central nervous system
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the central nervous system.

terms.name: Abnormality of the abdominal organs
terms.definition: An abnormality of the viscera of the abdomen.

terms.name: Vomiting
terms.definition: Forceful ejection of the contents of the stomach through the mouth by means of a series of involuntary spasmic contractions.

terms.name: Diarrhea
terms.definition: Abnormally increased frequency (usually defined as three or more) loose or watery bowel movements a day.

terms.name: Dysphagia
terms.definition: Difficulty in swallowing.

terms.name: Nausea and vomiting
terms.definition: Nausea is a commonly encountered symptom that has been defined as an unpleasant painless subjective feeling that one will imminently vomit. Vomiting has been defined as the forceful expulsion of the contents of the stomach, duodenum, or jejunum through the oral cavity. While nausea and vomiting are often thought to exist on a temporal continuum, this is not always the case. There are situations when severe nausea may be present without emesis and less frequently, when emesis may be present without preceding nausea.

terms.name: Nausea
terms.definition: A sensation of unease in the stomach together with an urge to vomit.

terms.name: Constipation
terms.definition: Infrequent or difficult evacuation of feces.

terms.name: Gastroesophageal reflux
terms.definition: A condition in which the stomach contents leak backwards from the stomach into the esophagus through the lower esophageal sphincter.

terms.name: Pyloric stenosis
terms.definition: Pyloric stenosis, also known as infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis, is an uncommon condition in infants characterized by abnormal thickening of the pylorus muscles in the stomach leading to gastric outlet obstruction. Clinically infants are well at birth. Then, at 3 to 6 weeks of age, the infants present with projectile vomiting, potentially leading to dehydration and weight loss.

terms.name: Anal atresia
terms.definition: Congenital absence of the anus, i.e., the opening at the bottom end of the intestinal tract.

terms.name: Malabsorption
terms.definition: Impaired ability to absorb one or more nutrients from the intestine.

terms.name: Anal stenosis
terms.definition: Abnormal narrowing of the anal opening.

terms.name: Abdominal pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) and perceived to originate in the abdomen.

terms.name: Chronic diarrhea
terms.definition: The presence of chronic diarrhea, which is usually taken to mean diarrhea that has persisted for over 4 weeks.

terms.name: Abnormal esophagus morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the esophagus.

terms.name: Esophageal atresia
synonyms: Birth defect in which part of esophagus did not develop
Birth defect in which part of oesophagus did not develop
terms.definition: A developmental defect resulting in complete obliteration of the lumen of the esophagus such that the esophagus ends in a blind pouch rather than connecting to the stomach.

terms.name: Poor suck
terms.definition: An inadequate sucking reflex, resulting in the difficult of newborns to be breast-fed.

terms.name: Abnormal rectum morphology
terms.definition: An abnormaltiy of the rectum, the final segment of the large intestine that stores solid waste until it passes through the anus.

terms.name: Rectal prolapse
terms.definition: Protrusion of the rectal mucous membrane through the anus.

terms.name: Hiatus hernia
terms.definition: The presence of a hernia in which the upper part of the stomach, i.e., mainly the gastric cardia protrudes through the diaphragmatic esophageal hiatus.

terms.name: Inflammation of the large intestine
terms.definition: Inflammation, or an inflammatory state in the large intestine.

terms.name: Anorexia
terms.definition: Lack of desire to eat (loss of appetite).

terms.name: Esophageal varix
terms.definition: Extreme dilation of the submucusoal veins in the lower portion of the esophagus.

terms.name: Esophageal stricture
synonyms: Narrowing of esophagus due to inflammation and scar tissue
Narrowing of oesophagus due to inflammation and scar tissue
terms.definition: A pathological narrowing of the esophagus that is caused by the development of a ring of scar tissue that constricts the esophageal lumen.

terms.name: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
terms.definition: A condition in which there is increased production of gastrin by a gastrin-secreting tumor (usually located in the pancreas, duodenum, or abdominal lymph nodes) that stimulates the gastric mucosa to maximal activity, with consequent gastrointestinal mucosal ulceration.

terms.name: Hypothermia
terms.definition: Reduced body temperature due to failed thermoregulation.

terms.name: Heat intolerance
terms.definition: The inability to maintain a comfortable body temperature in warm or hot weather.

terms.name: Malignant hyperthermia
terms.definition: Malignant hyperthermia is characterized by a rapid increase in temperature to 39-42 degrees C. Malignant hyperthermia may occur in response to either inhalational anesthetics such as halothane, to muscle relaxants such as succinylcholine, or to exercise.

terms.name: Renal cortical atrophy
terms.definition: Atrophy of the cortex of the kidney.

terms.name: Proximal renal tubular acidosis
terms.definition: A type of renal tubular acidosis characterized by a failure of the proximal tubular cells to reabsorb bicarbonate, leading to urinary bicarbonate wasting and subsequent acidemia.

terms.name: Curved linear dimple below the lower lip
Abnormality of the glabella
synonyms: Abnormality of the area between the eyebrows
terms.definition: An abnormality of the glabella.

terms.name: Prominent glabella
terms.definition: Forward protrusion of the glabella.

terms.name: Myopathic facies
terms.definition: A facial appearance characteristic of myopathic conditions. The face appears expressionless with sunken cheeks, bilateral ptosis, and inability to elevate the corners of the mouth, due to muscle weakness.

terms.name: Cerebral atrophy
terms.definition: Atrophy (wasting, decrease in size of cells or tissue) affecting the cerebrum.

terms.name: Abnormal cerebral morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the telencephalon, which is also known as the cerebrum.

terms.name: Lower limb spasticity
terms.definition: Spasticity (velocity-dependent increase in tonic stretch reflexes with increased muscle tone and hyperexcitable tendon reflexes) in the muscles of the lower limbs, hips, and pelvis.

terms.name: Abnormal pyramidal tract morphology
synonyms: Morphological abnormality of the pyramidal tract
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the pyramidal tract, whose chief element, the corticospinal tract, is the only direct connection between the brain and the spinal cord. In addition to the corticospinal tract, the pyramidal system includes the corticobulbar, corticomesencephalic, and corticopontine tracts.

terms.name: Rigidity
terms.definition: Continuous involuntary sustained muscle contraction. When an affected muscle is passively stretched, the degree of resistance remains constant regardless of the rate at which the muscle is stretched. This feature helps to distinguish rigidity from muscle spasticity.

terms.name: Spastic gait
terms.definition: Spasticity is manifested by increased stretch reflex which is intensified with movement velocity. This results in excessive and inappropriate muscle activation which can contribute to muscle hypertonia. Spastic gait is characterized by manifestations such as muscle hypertonia, stiff knee, and circumduction of the leg.

terms.name: Gait ataxia
synonyms: Inability to coordinate movements when walking
terms.definition: A type of ataxia characterized by the impairment of the ability to coordinate the movements required for normal walking. Gait ataxia is characteirzed by a wide-based staggering gait with a tendency to fall.

terms.name: Bradykinesia
terms.definition: Bradykinesia literally means slow movement, and is used clinically to denote a slowness in the execution of movement (in contrast to hypokinesia, which is used to refer to slowness in the initiation of movement).

terms.name: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure
synonyms: Generalised tonic-clonic seizure (without specification of onset)
Generalized tonic-clonic seizure (without specification of onset)
terms.definition: A bilateral tonic-clonic seizure is a seizure defined by a tonic (bilateral increased tone, lasting seconds to minutes) and then a clonic (bilateral sustained rhythmic jerking) phase.

terms.name: Limb ataxia
terms.definition: A kind of ataxia that affects movements of the extremities.

terms.name: Abnormality of extrapyramidal motor function
terms.name_zh: 锥体外系运动功能异常
terms.definition: A neurological condition related to lesions of the basal ganglia leading to typical abnormalities including akinesia (inability to initiate changes in activity and perform volitional movements rapidly and easily), muscular rigidity (continuous contraction of muscles with constant resistance to passive movement), chorea (widespread arrhythmic movements of a forcible, rapid, jerky, and restless nature), athetosis (inability to sustain the muscles of the fingers, toes, or other group of muscles in a fixed position), and akathisia (inability to remain motionless).

terms.name: Chorea
terms.definition: Chorea (Greek for 'dance') refers to widespread arrhythmic involuntary movements of a forcible, jerky and restless fashion. It is a random-appearing sequence of one or more discrete involuntary movements or movement fragments. Movements appear random because of variability in timing, duration or location. Each movement may have a distinct start and end. However, movements may be strung together and thus may appear to flow randomly from one muscle group to another. Chorea can involve the trunk, neck, face, tongue, and extremities.

terms.name: Increased neuronal autofluorescent lipopigment
terms.name_zh: 神经元自身荧光脂色素增多
terms.definition: Lipofuscin, a generic term applied to autofluorescent lipopigment, is a mixture of protein and lipid that accumulates in most aging cells, particularly those involved in high lipid turnover (e.g., the adrenal medulla) or phagocytosis of other cell types (e g., the retinal pigment epithelium or RPE; macrophage). This term pertains if there is an increase in the neuronal accumulation of lipofuscin (also known as autofluorescent lipoprotein) more than expected for the age of the patient.

terms.name: Dysdiadochokinesis
synonyms: Difficulty performing quick and alternating movements
terms.definition: A type of ataxia characterized by the impairment of the ability to perform rapidly alternating movements, such as pronating and supinating his or her hand on the dorsum of the other hand as rapidly as possible.

terms.name: Migraine
terms.definition: Migraine is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by episodic attacks of headache and associated symptoms.

terms.name: Migraine with aura
terms.definition: A type of migraine in which there is an aura characterized by focal neurological phenomena that usually proceed, but may accompany or occur in the absence of, the headache. The symptoms of an aura may include fully reversible visual, sensory, and speech symptoms but not motor weakness. Visual symptoms may include flickering lights, spots and lines and/or loss of vision and/or unilateral sensory symptoms such as paresthesias or numbness. At least one of the symptoms of an aura develops gradually over 5 or more minutes and/or different symptoms occur in succession.

terms.name: Truncal ataxia
synonyms: Instability or lack of coordination of central trunk muscles
terms.definition: Truncal ataxia is a sign of ataxia characterized by instability of the trunk. It usually occurs during sitting.

terms.name: Hypoplasia of the corpus callosum
synonyms: Underdevelopment of part of brain called corpus callosum
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the corpus callosum.

terms.name: Intention tremor
terms.definition: A type of kinetic tremor that occurs during target directed movement is called intention tremor. That is, an oscillatory cerebellar ataxia that tends to be absent when the limbs are inactive and during the first part of voluntary movement but worsening as the movement continues and greater precision is required (e.g., in touching a target such as the patient's nose or a physician's finger).

terms.name: Migraine without aura
terms.definition: Repeated headache attacks lasting 4-72 h fulfilling at least two of the following criteria: 1) unilateral location, 2) pulsating quality, 3) moderate or severe pain intensity, and 4) aggravation by or causing avoidance of routine physical activity such as climbing stairs. Headache attacks are commonly accompanied by nausea, vomiting, photophobia, or phonophobia.

terms.name: Encephalocele
terms.definition: A neural tube defect characterized by sac-like protrusions of the brain and the membranes that cover it through openings in the skull.

terms.name: Occipital encephalocele
synonyms: Brain tissue sticks out through back of skull
terms.definition: A type of encephalocele (that is, a a protrusion of part of the cranial contents including brain tissue through a congenital opening in the cranium, typically covered with skin or mucous membrane) in the occipital region of the skull. Occipital encephalocele presents as a midline swelling over the occipital bone. It is usually covered with normal full-thickness scalp.

terms.name: Abnormality of the respiratory system
terms.definition: An abnormality of the respiratory system, which include the airways, lungs, and the respiratory muscles.

terms.name: Abnormality of the upper respiratory tract
synonyms: Abnormality of the upper respiratory tract
terms.definition: An abnormality of the upper respiratory tract.

terms.name: Abnormal lung morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the lung.

terms.name: Pneumonia
terms.definition: Inflammation of any part of the lung parenchyma.

terms.name: Restrictive ventilatory defect
synonyms: Restrictive deficit on pulmonary function testing
Restrictive deficit on pulmonary function tests
Stiff lung or chest wall causing decreased lung volume
terms.definition: A functional defect characterized by reduced total lung capacity (TLC) not associated with abnormalities of expiratory airflow or airway resistance. Spirometrically, a restrictive defect is defined as FEV1 (forced expiratory volume in 1 second) and FVC (forced vital capacity) less than 80 per cent. Restrictive lung disease may be caused by alterations in lung parenchyma or because of a disease of the pleura, chest wall, or neuromuscular apparatus.

terms.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension
synonyms: Increased blood pressure in blood vessels of lungs
terms.definition: Pulmonary hypertension is defined mean pulmonary artery pressure of 25mmHg or more and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure of 15mmHg or less when measured by right heart catheterisation at rest and in a supine position.

terms.name: Dyspnea
terms.definition: Difficult or labored breathing. Dyspnea is a subjective feeling only the patient can rate, e.g., on a Borg scale.

terms.name: Respiratory distress
terms.definition: Respiratory distress is objectively observable as the physical or emotional consequences from the experience of dyspnea. The physical presentation of respiratory distress is generally referred to as labored breathing, while the sensation of respiratory distress is called shortness of breath or dyspnea.

terms.name: Asthma
terms.definition: Asthma is characterized by increased responsiveness of the tracheobronchial tree to multiple stimuli, leading to narrowing of the air passages with resultant dyspnea, cough, and wheezing.

terms.name: Recurrent aspiration pneumonia
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to aspiration pneumonia, defined as pneumonia due to breathing in foreign material, as manifested by a medical history of repeated episodes of aspiration pneumonia.

terms.name: Abnormal lung lobation
terms.definition: A developmental defect in the formation of pulmonary lobes.

terms.name: Pleuritis
synonyms: Inflammation of tissues lining lungs and chest
terms.definition: Inflammation of the pleura.

terms.name: Abnormal pleura morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary pleura, the thin, transparent membrane which covers the lungs and lines the inside of the chest walls.

terms.name: Apnea
terms.definition: Lack of breathing with no movement of the respiratory muscles and no exchange of air in the lungs. This term refers to a disposition to have recurrent episodes of apnea rather than to a single event.

terms.name: Hemoptysis
synonyms: Coughing up blood or blood-stained mucus
terms.definition: Coughing up (expectoration) of blood or blood-streaked sputum from the larynx, trachea, bronchi, or lungs.

terms.name: Pneumothorax
terms.definition: Accumulation of air in the pleural cavity leading to a partially or completely collapsed lung.

terms.name: Spontaneous pneumothorax
terms.definition: Pneumothorax occurring without traumatic injury to the chest or lung.

terms.name: Bronchiectasis
synonyms: Permanent enlargement of the airways of the lungs
terms.definition: Persistent abnormal dilatation of the bronchi owing to localized and irreversible destruction and widening of the large airways.

terms.name: Abnormal cerebral ventricle morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the cerebral ventricles.

terms.name: Ventriculomegaly
terms.definition: An increase in size of the ventricular system of the brain.

terms.name: Cerebral cortical atrophy
synonyms: Decrease in size of the outer layer of the brain due to loss of brain cells
terms.definition: Atrophy of the cortex of the cerebrum.

terms.name: Generalized non-motor (absence) seizure
terms.name_zh: 全身性非运动（失神）发作
terms.definition: A generalized non-motor (absence) seizure is a type of a type of dialeptic seizure that is of electrographically generalized onset. It is a generalized seizure characterized by an interruption of activities, a blank stare, and usually the person will be unresponsive when spoken to. Any ictal motor phenomena are minor in comparison to these non-motor features.

terms.name: Generalized myoclonic seizure
terms.definition: A generalized myoclonic seizure is a type of generalized motor seizure characterized by bilateral, sudden, brief (<100 ms) involuntary single or multiple contraction of muscles or muscle groups of variable topography (axial, proximal limb, distal). Myoclonus is less regularly repetitive and less sustained than is clonus.

terms.name: Polymicrogyria
terms.definition: Polymicrogyria is a congenital malformation of the cerebral cortex characterized by abnormal cortical layering (lamination) and an excessive number of small gyri (folds).

terms.name: Abnormal upper motor neuron morphology
terms.name_zh: 上运动神经元形态异常
synonyms: Abnormal shape of upper motor neuron
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly that affects the upper motor neuron.

terms.name: Episodic ataxia
terms.definition: Periodic spells of incoordination and imbalance, that is, episodes of ataxia typically lasting from 10 minutes to several hours or days.

terms.name: Porencephalic cyst
terms.definition: A cavity within the cerebral hemisphere, filled with cerebrospinal fluid, that communicates directly with the ventricular system.

terms.name: Status epilepticus
synonyms: Repeated seizures without recovery between them
terms.definition: Status epilepticus is a type of prolonged seizure resulting either from the failure of the mechanisms responsible for seizure termination or from the initiation of mechanisms which lead to abnormally prolonged seizures (after time point t1). It is a condition that can have long-term consequences (after time point t2), including neuronal death, neuronal injury, and alteration of neuronal networks, depending on the type and duration of seizures.

terms.name: Abnormal basal ganglia morphology
terms.definition: Abnormality of the basal ganglia.

terms.name: Basal ganglia calcification
terms.definition: The presence of calcium deposition affecting one or more structures of the basal ganglia.

terms.name: Broad-based gait
terms.definition: An abnormal gait pattern in which persons stand and walk with their feet spaced widely apart. This is often a component of cerebellar ataxia.

terms.name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
terms.definition: Hemorrhage occurring between the arachnoid mater and the pia mater.

terms.name: Arrhinencephaly
terms.definition: A defect of development of the brain characterized by congenital absence of the part of the brain that includes the olfactory bulbs, tracts, and other structures associated with the sense of smell.

terms.name: Ischemic stroke
terms.definition: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is defined by the sudden loss of blood flow to an area of the brain with the resulting loss of neurologic function. It is caused by thrombosis or embolism that occludes a cerebral vessel supplying a specific area of the brain. During a vessel occlusion, there is a core area where damage to the brain is irreversible and an area of penumbra where the brain has lost function owing to decreased blood flow but is not irreversibly injured.

terms.name: Abnormal spinal cord morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the spinal cord (myelon).

terms.name: Tethered cord
terms.definition: During normal embryological development, the spinal cord first occupies the entire length of the vertebral column but goes on to assume a position at the level of L1 due to differential growth of the conus medullaris and the vertebral column. The filum terminale is a slender, threadlike structure that remains after the normal regression of the distal embryonic spinal cord and attaches the spinal cord to the coccyx. A tethered cord results if there is a thickened rope-like filum terminale which anchors the cord at the level of L2 or below, potentially causing neurologic signs owing to abnormal tension on the spinal cord.

terms.name: Frontotemporal dementia
terms.definition: A dementia associated with degeneration of the frontotemporal lobe and clinically associated with personality and behavioral changes such as disinhibition, apathy, and lack of insight. The hallmark feature of frontotemporal dementia is the presentation with focal syndromes such as progressive language dysfunction, or aphasia, or behavioral changes characteristic of frontal lobe disorders.

terms.name: Hypophosphatemia
synonyms: Decreased phosphate ion level in blood
Reduced phosphate ion level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of phosphate ion in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Hyperuricemia
synonyms: Elevated uric acid level in blood
Increased uric acid level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of uric acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Increased circulating lactate concentration
terms.definition: Abnormally increased level of blood lactate (2-hydroxypropanoic acid). Lactate is produced from pyruvate by lactate dehydrogenase during normal metabolism. The terms lactate and lactic acid are often used interchangeably but lactate (the component measured in blood) is strictly a weak base whereas lactic acid is the corresponding acid. Lactic acidosis is often used clinically to describe elevated lactate but should be reserved for cases where there is a corresponding acidosis (pH below 7.35).

terms.name: Hyperproteinemia
terms.definition: An increased concentration of proteins in the blood.

terms.name: Hyperkalemia
terms.definition: The concentration of potassium(1+) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Hyperglycinemia
terms.definition: An elevated concentration of glycine in the blood.

terms.name: Hypertriglyceridemia
terms.definition: An abnormal increase in the level of triglycerides in the blood.

terms.name: Homocystinuria
terms.definition: An increased concentration of homocystine in the urine.

terms.name: Azotemia
terms.definition: An increased concentration of nitrogen compounds in the blood.

terms.name: Heparan sulfate excretion in urine
terms.definition: An increased concentration of heparan sulfates in the urine.

terms.name: Hyperhomocystinemia
terms.definition: An increased concentration of homocystine in the blood.

terms.name: Hyperlysinemia
terms.definition: The concentration of lysine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Low posterior hairline
synonyms: Low hairline at back of neck
terms.definition: Hair on the neck extends more inferiorly than usual.

terms.name: Nail dysplasia
terms.definition: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the nail.

terms.name: Nail pterygium
terms.definition: Inward advance of skin over the nail plate.

terms.name: Impaired vibration sensation in the lower limbs
synonyms: Decreased vibratory sense in lower limbs
Decreased vibratory sense in the lower extremities
Decreased vibratory sense in the lower limbs
Diminished vibratory sensation in the legs
Distal sensory loss, especially vibratory sense
Distal vibratory impairment of the lower limbs
Impaired vibration sensation in the lower limbs
terms.definition: A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration in the legs.

terms.name: Abnormal speech pattern
terms.definition: An abnormality in the sound (volume) or cadence (rate) of speech.

terms.name: Scanning speech
terms.definition: An abnormal pattern of speech in which the words are as if measured or scanned; there is a pause after every syllable, and the syllables themselves are pronounced slowly.

terms.name: Clonus
synonyms: Involuntary rhythmic muscular contractions and relaxations
terms.definition: A series of rhythmic and involuntary muscle contractions (at a frequency of about 5 to 7 Hz) that occur in response to an abruptly applied and sustained stretch.

terms.name: Intracranial hemorrhage
terms.definition: Hemorrhage occurring within the skull.

terms.name: Gliosis
terms.definition: Gliosis is the focal proliferation of glial cells in the central nervous system.

terms.name: Postural instability
terms.definition: A tendency to fall or the inability to keep oneself from falling; imbalance. The retropulsion test is widely regarded as the gold standard to evaluate postural instability, Use of the retropulsion test includes a rapid balance perturbation in the backward direction, and the number of balance correcting steps (or total absence thereof) is used to rate the degree of postural instability. Healthy subjects correct such perturbations with either one or two large steps, or without taking any steps, hinging rapidly at the hips while swinging the arms forward as a counterweight. In patients with balance impairment, balance correcting steps are often too small, forcing patients to take more than two steps. Taking three or more steps is generally considered to be abnormal, and taking more than five steps is regarded as being clearly abnormal. Markedly affected patients continue to step backward without ever regaining their balance and must be caught by the examiner (this would be called true retropulsion). Even more severely affected patients fail to correct entirely, and fall backward like a pushed toy soldier, without taking any corrective steps.

terms.name: Postural tremor
terms.definition: A type of tremors that is triggered by holding a limb in a fixed position.

terms.name: Spinal cord compression
terms.definition: External mechanical compression of the spinal cord.

terms.name: Opisthotonus
terms.definition: Opisthotonus is defined as a dramatic abnormal posture due to spastic contraction of the extensor muscles of the neck, trunk, and lower extremities that produces a severe backward arching from neck to heel. In most cases, the trunk is elevated off the ground by a few inches. It is usually sudden in onset and can be sustained or repetitive. It can be considered a variant of decerebrate posturing involving a hyperextension of the neck, back, and limbs.

terms.name: Neurodegeneration
terms.definition: Progressive loss of neural cells and tissue.

terms.name: Cerebral edema
terms.definition: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in the brain.

terms.name: Phonophobia
terms.definition: An abnormally heightened sensitivity to loud sounds.

terms.name: Neurofibrillary tangles
synonyms: Neurofibrillary tangles composed of disordered microtubules in neurons
terms.definition: Pathological protein aggregates formed by hyperphosphorylation of a microtubule-associated protein known as tau, causing it to aggregate in an insoluble form.

terms.name: Apraxia
terms.definition: A defect in the understanding of complex motor commands and in the execution of certain learned movements, i.e., deficits in the cognitive components of learned movements.

terms.name: Profound intellectual disability
terms.definition: Profound intellectual disability (ID) is defined as a type of ID characterized by profoundly sub-average adaptive functioning and intellectual functioning, with an intelligence quotient (IQ) below 20.

terms.name: Delayed CNS myelination
terms.name_zh: 中枢神经系统髓鞘形成延迟
synonyms: Delay in central nervous system myelination
terms.definition: Delayed myelination in the central nervous system.

terms.name: Choroid plexus cyst
terms.definition: A cyst occurring within the choroid plexus within a cerebral ventricle.

terms.name: Progressive spasticity
terms.definition: Spasticity that increases in degree with time.

terms.name: Pseudobulbar affect
terms.definition: Pseudobulbar affect (PBA) is characterized by uncontrolled crying or laughing which may be disproportionate or inappropriate to the social context. Thus, there is a disparity between the patient's emotional expression and his or her emotional experience.

terms.name: Delayed gross motor development
synonyms: Delayed attainment of gross motor milestones
Delayed attainment of gross motor skills
Delayed development of gross motor milestones
Delayed development of gross motor skills
terms.definition: A type of motor delay characterized by a delay in acquiring the ability to control the large muscles of the body for walking, running, sitting, and crawling.

terms.name: Dysgenesis of the cerebellar vermis
terms.definition: Defective development of the vermis of cerebellum.

terms.name: Myelopathy
terms.definition: Myelopathy is an descriptive term, referring to pathology leading to a neurologic deficit related to the spinal cord. The clinical diagnosis of myelopathy requires a detailed history and physical examination to define the clinical syndrome. Neuroimaging is indicated in most instances of new-onset myelopathy. It is indicated also when the worsening of a myelopathy is unexplained.

terms.name: Generalized-onset seizure
terms.definition: A generalized-onset seizure is a type of seizure originating at some point within, and rapidly engaging, bilaterally distributed networks. The networks may include cortical and subcortical structures but not necessarily the entire cortex.

terms.name: Dilated fourth ventricle
terms.definition: An abnormal dilatation of the fourth cerebral ventricle.

terms.name: Pseudobulbar signs
terms.definition: Pseudobulbar signs result from injury to an upper motor neuron lesion to the corticobulbar pathways in the pyramidal tract. Patients have difficulty chewing, swallowing and demonstrate slurred speech (often initial presentation) as well as abnormal behavioral symptoms such as inappropriate emotional outbursts of uncontrolled laughter or weeping etc.

terms.name: Pleural effusion
terms.definition: The presence of an excessive amount of fluid in the pleural cavity.

terms.name: Respiratory paralysis
terms.definition: Inability to move the muscles of respiration.

terms.name: Pulmonary embolism
synonyms: Blood clot in artery of lung
terms.definition: An embolus (that is, an abnormal particle circulating in the blood) located in the pulmonary artery and thereby blocking blood circulation to the lung. Usually the embolus is a blood clot that has developed in an extremity (for instance, a deep venous thrombosis), detached, and traveled through the circulation before becoming trapped in the pulmonary artery.

terms.name: Recurrent respiratory infections
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to respiratory infections as manifested by a history of recurrent respiratory infections.

terms.name: Pulmonary fibrosis
terms.definition: Replacement of normal lung tissues by fibroblasts and collagen.

terms.name: Diffuse reticular or finely nodular infiltrations
terms.name_zh: 弥漫性网状或细结节状浸润

terms.name: Coarse hair
terms.definition: Hair shafts are rough in texture.

terms.name: Sparse scalp hair
synonyms: Reduction in the number of scalp follicles
terms.definition: Decreased number of hairs per unit area of skin of the scalp.

terms.name: White forelock
synonyms: White part of hair above forehead
terms.definition: A triangular depigmented region of white hairs located in the anterior midline of the scalp.

terms.name: Fine hair
terms.definition: Hair that is fine or thin to the touch.

terms.name: Sparse axillary hair
terms.definition: Reduced number or density of axillary hair.

terms.name: Premature graying of hair
terms.definition: Development of gray hair at a younger than normal age.

terms.name: Slow-growing hair
terms.definition: Hair whose growth is slower than normal.

terms.name: Silver-gray hair
terms.definition: Hypopigmented hair that appears silver-gray.

terms.name: Facial hypertrichosis
terms.definition: Excessive, increased hair growth located in the facial region.

terms.name: Melanin pigment aggregation in hair shafts
Absent axillary hair
terms.definition: Absence of axillary hair.

terms.name: Absent eyebrow
terms.definition: Absence of the eyebrow.

terms.name: Woolly hair
terms.definition: The term wooly hair refers to an abnormal variant of hair that is fine, with tightly coiled curls, and often hypopigmented. Optical microscopy may reveal the presence of tight spirals and a clear diameter reduction as compared with normal hair. Electron microscopy may show flat, oval hair shafts with reduced transversal diameter.

terms.name: Sparse pubic hair
terms.definition: Reduced number or density of pubic hair.

terms.name: White eyebrow
terms.definition: White color (lack of pigmentation) of the eyebrow.

terms.name: White eyelashes
terms.definition: White color (lack of pigmentation) of the eyelashes.

terms.name: Generalized hirsutism
terms.definition: Abnormally increased hair growth over much of the entire body.

terms.name: Sparse body hair
terms.definition: Sparseness of the body hair.

terms.name: Patchy alopecia
terms.definition: Transient, non-scarring hair loss and preservation of the hair follicle located in in well-defined patches.

terms.name: Early balding
terms.definition: Loss of scalp hair at an earlier than normal age.

terms.name: Pili canaliculi
terms.definition: A characteristic triangular, kidney- or heat-shaped diameter of hair shafts with typical longitudinal canalicular deformation as observable by scanning electron microscopy.

terms.name: Frontal upsweep of hair
terms.definition: Upward and/or sideward growth of anterior hair.

terms.name: Gastrointestinal hemorrhage
terms.definition: Hemorrhage affecting the gastrointestinal tract.

terms.name: Hepatomegaly
terms.definition: Abnormally increased size of the liver.

terms.name: Abnormal intestine morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the intestine. The closely related term enteropathy is used to refer to any disease of the intestine.

terms.name: Protein-losing enteropathy
terms.definition: Abnormal loss of protein from the digestive tract related to excessive leakage of plasma proteins into the lumen of the gastrointestinal tract.

terms.name: Abnormal small intestine morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the small intestine.

terms.name: Meckel diverticulum
terms.definition: Meckel's diverticulum is a congenital diverticulum located in the distal ileum.

terms.name: Abnormal duodenum morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the duodenum, i.e., the first section of the small intestine.

terms.name: Duodenal atresia
synonyms: Absence or narrowing of first part of small bowel
terms.definition: A developmental defect resulting in complete obliteration of the duodenal lumen, that is, an abnormal closure of the duodenum.

terms.name: Hematemesis
terms.definition: The vomiting of blood.

terms.name: Melena
terms.definition: The passage of blackish, tarry feces associated with gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Melena occurs if the blood remains in the colon long enough for it to be broken down by colonic bacteria. One degradation product, hematin, imbues the stool with a blackish color. Thus, melena generally occurs with bleeding from the upper gastrointestinal tract (e.g., stomach ulcers or duodenal ulcers), since the blood usually remains in the gut for a longer period of time than with lower gastrointestinal bleeding.

terms.name: Abnormal large intestine morphology
terms.definition: Any abnormality of the large intestine.

terms.name: Aganglionic megacolon
terms.name_zh: 无神经节细胞性巨结肠
terms.definition: An abnormality resulting from a lack of intestinal ganglion cells (i.e., an aganglionic section of bowel) that results in bowel obstruction with enlargement of the colon.

terms.name: Colonic diverticula
terms.definition: The presence of multiple diverticula of the colon.

terms.name: Intermittent diarrhea
terms.definition: Repeated episodes of diarrhea separated by periods without diarrhea.

terms.name: Chronic rhinitis
terms.definition: Chronic inflammation of the nasal mucosa.

terms.name: Exaggerated cupid's bow
terms.definition: More pronounced paramedian peaks and median notch of the Cupid's bow.

terms.name: Focal clonic seizure
terms.definition: A focal clonic seizure is a type of focal motor seizure characterized by sustained rhythmic jerking, that is regularly repetitive.

terms.name: Exaggerated startle response
terms.definition: An exaggerated startle reaction in response to a sudden unexpected visual or acoustic stimulus, or a quick movement near the face.

terms.name: Paroxysmal dystonia
terms.definition: A form of dystonia characterized by episodes of dystonia (often hemidystonia or generalized) lasting from minutes to hours. There are no dystonic symptoms between episodes.

terms.name: Abnormality of neuronal migration
terms.definition: An abnormality resulting from an anomaly of neuronal migration, i.e., of the process by which neurons travel from their origin to their final position in the brain.

terms.name: Abnormality of the autonomic nervous system
terms.definition: An abnormality of the autonomic nervous system.

terms.name: Tetraparesis
terms.definition: Weakness of all four limbs.

terms.name: Horner syndrome
terms.definition: An abnormality resulting from a lesion of the sympathetic nervous system characterized by a combination of unilateral ptosis, miosis, and often ipsilateral hypohidrosis and conjunctival injection.

terms.name: Enlarged cisterna magna
terms.definition: Increase in size of the cisterna magna, one of three principal openings in the subarachnoid space between the arachnoid and pia mater, located between the cerebellum and the dorsal surface of the medulla oblongata.

terms.name: Gray matter heterotopia
terms.definition: Heterotopia or neuronal heterotopia are macroscopic clusters of misplaced neurons (gray matter), most often situated along the ventricular walls or within the subcortical white matter.

terms.name: Global brain atrophy
terms.definition: Unlocalized atrophy of the brain with decreased total brain matter volume and increased ventricular size.

terms.name: Fair hair
terms.definition: A lesser degree of hair pigmentation than would otherwise be expected.

terms.name: Progressive alopecia
terms.definition: Progressive loss of hair.

terms.name: Alopecia universalis
terms.definition: Loss of all hair on the entire body.

terms.name: Poliosis
terms.definition: Circumscribed depigmentation of the hair of the head or the eyelashes.

terms.name: Frontal balding
terms.definition: Absence of hair in the anterior midline and/or parietal areas.

terms.name: Progressive hypotrichosis
terms.definition: Progressively reduced or lacking hair growth.

terms.name: Brittle hair
terms.definition: Fragile, easily breakable hair, i.e., with reduced tensile strength.

terms.name: Mutism
terms.definition: Complete lack of speech or verbal communication in a person despite attempts to engage in conversation. Mutism as a phenomena assumes the individual has previous capacity for speech and in the pediatric population it assumes that the person is past the age of typical language development.

terms.name: Hemiplegia
synonyms: Paralysis on one side of body
terms.definition: Paralysis (complete loss of muscle function) in the arm, leg, and in some cases the face on one side of the body.

terms.name: Akinesia
terms.definition: Inability to initiate changes in activity or movement and to perform ordinary volitional movements rapidly and easily.

terms.name: Athetosis
synonyms: Involuntary writhing movements in fingers, hands, toes, and feet
terms.definition: A slow, continuous, involuntary writhing movement that prevents maintenance of a stable posture. Athetosis involves continuous smooth movements that appear random and are not composed of recognizable sub-movements or movement fragments. In contrast to chorea, in athetosis, the same regions of the body are repeatedly involved. Athetosis may worsen with attempts at movement of posture, but athetosis can also occur at rest.

terms.name: Drooling
terms.definition: Habitual flow of saliva out of the mouth.

terms.name: Chiari malformation
terms.definition: Chiari malformation consists of a downward displacement of the cerebellar tonsils and the medulla through the foramen magnum, sometimes causing hydrocephalus as a result of obstruction of CSF outflow.

terms.name: Incoordination
terms.definition: A deficit in coordination of muscle movements. Coordination is defined as the orchestrated movement of multiple body parts as required to accomplish intended actions, like walking.

terms.name: Clumsiness
terms.definition: Lack of physical coordination resulting in an abnormal tendency to drop items or bump into objects.

terms.name: Spastic paraparesis
terms.definition: Partial loss of the ability to move the lower limbs accompanied by spasticity of the lower limbs.

terms.name: Degeneration of the lateral corticospinal tracts
terms.definition: Deterioration of the tissues of the lateral corticospinal tracts.

terms.name: Headache
terms.definition: Cephalgia, or pain sensed in various parts of the head, not confined to the area of distribution of any nerve.

terms.name: Cervical myelopathy
terms.definition: A collection of pathologic conditions that result from progressive spinal cord dysfunction secondary to cord compression in the cervical spine.

terms.name: Vertigo
terms.definition: An abnormal sensation of spinning while the body is actually stationary.

terms.name: Resting tremor
terms.definition: A resting tremor occurs when muscles are at rest and becomes less noticeable or disappears when the affected muscles are moved. Resting tremors are often slow and coarse.

terms.name: Anencephaly
terms.definition: Anencephaly is a developmental anomaly characterized by a fetus that has no calvarium, with a lack of most or all of the fetus' brain tissue. Anencephaly belongs to a collective group known as neural tube defects (NTD) and is a result of the neural tube failing to close in its rostral end during fetal development.

terms.name: Hydranencephaly
terms.definition: A defect of development of the brain characterized by replacement of greater portions of the cerebral hemispheres and the corpus striatum by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and glial tissue.

terms.name: Drowsiness
terms.definition: Abnormal feeling of sleepiness or difficulty staying awake.

terms.name: Sleep attack
terms.definition: A sleep attack is a sudden, irresistable episode of sleep that occurs during waking hours.

terms.name: Recurrent paroxysmal headache
terms.definition: Repeated episodes of headache with rapid onset, reaching a peak within minutes and of short duration (less than one hour) with pain that is throbbing, pulsating, or bursting in quality.

terms.name: Lack of peer relationships
terms.definition: The state of not having relationships with peers outside of school or organized activity appropriate to developmental level. This may be caused by behavioral or physical barriers.

terms.name: Motor deterioration
terms.definition: Loss of previously present motor (i.e., movement) abilities.

terms.name: Abnormal cerebellar vermis morphology
terms.definition: An anomaly of the vermis of cerebellum.

terms.name: Agenesis of cerebellar vermis
terms.definition: Congenital absence of the vermis of cerebellum.

terms.name: Abnormal caudate nucleus morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the caudate nucleus.

terms.name: Cervical cord compression
terms.definition: Compression of the spinal cord in the cervical region, generally manifested by paresthesias and numbness, weakness, difficulty walking, abnormalities of coordination, and neck pain or stiffness.

terms.name: Moderate intellectual disability
terms.definition: Moderate intellectual disability (ID) is defined as a type of ID characterized by moderately sub-average adaptive functioning and intellectual functioning, with an intelligence quotient (IQ) the range of 35-49.

terms.name: Normal pressure hydrocephalus
terms.definition: A form of hydrocephalus characterized by enlarged cerebral ventricles and normal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) pressure upon lumbar puncture.

terms.name: Action tremor
terms.definition: A tremor present when the limbs are active, either when outstretched in a certain position or throughout a voluntary movement.

terms.name: Head tremor
terms.definition: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement affecting head movement.

terms.name: Focal aware seizure
synonyms: Focal seizure without impairment of awareness
Focal seizure without impairment of consciousness or awareness
Focal seizures without impairment of consciousness or awareness
Partial seizure without impairment of awareness
terms.definition: A type of focal-onset seizure in which awareness is preserved. Awareness during a seizure is defined as the patient being fully aware of themself and their environment throughout the seizure, even if immobile.

terms.name: Leukoencephalopathy
terms.definition: This term describes abnormality of the white matter of the cerebrum resulting from damage to the myelin sheaths of nerve cells.

terms.name: EEG abnormality
terms.definition: Abnormality observed by electroencephalogram (EEG), which is used to record of the brain's spontaneous electrical activity from multiple electrodes placed on the scalp.

terms.name: Memory impairment
terms.definition: An impairment of memory as manifested by a reduced ability to remember things such as dates and names, and increased forgetfulness.

terms.name: Writer's cramp
terms.definition: A focal dystonia of the fingers, hand, and/or forearm that appears when the affected person attempts to do a task that requires fine motor movements such as writing or playing a musical instrument.

terms.name: Sleep disturbance
terms.definition: An abnormal pattern in the quality, quantity, or characteristics of sleep.

terms.name: Psychomotor deterioration
terms.definition: Loss of previously present mental and motor abilities.

terms.name: Shuffling gait
terms.definition: A type of gait (walking) characterized by by dragging one's feet along or without lifting the feet fully from the ground.

terms.name: Abnormal brainstem morphology
terms.definition: An anomaly of the brainstem.

terms.name: Hypoplasia of the brainstem
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the brainstem.

terms.name: Abnormal lower motor neuron morphology
terms.name_zh: 下运动神经元形态异常
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the lower motor neuron.

terms.name: Visual hallucination
terms.definition: Visual perception in the absence of a visual stimulus.

terms.name: Normal interictal EEG
terms.definition: Lack of observable abnormal electroencephalographic (EEG) patterns in an individual with a history of seizures. About half of individuals with epilepsy show interictal epileptiform discharges upon the first investigation. The yield can be increased by repeated studies, sleep studies, or by ambulatory EEG recordings over 24 hours. Normal interictal EEG is a sign that can be useful in the differential diagnosis.

terms.name: Febrile seizure (within the age range of 3 months to 6 years)
terms.definition: A febrile seizure is any type of seizure (most often a generalized tonic-clonic seizure) occurring with fever (at least 38 degrees Celsius) but in the absence of central nervous system infection, severe metabolic disturbance or other alternative precipitant in children between the ages of 3 months and 6 years.

terms.name: Hypokinesia
terms.definition: Abnormally diminished motor activity. In contrast to paralysis, hypokinesia is not characterized by a lack of motor strength, but rather by a poverty of movement. The typical habitual movements (e.g., folding the arms, crossing the legs) are reduced in frequency.

terms.name: Developmental regression
terms.definition: Loss of developmental skills, as manifested by loss of developmental milestones.

terms.name: Hand tremor
terms.definition: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement affecting the hand.

terms.name: Fasciculations
terms.definition: Fasciculations are observed as small, local, involuntary muscle contractions (twitching) visible under the skin. Fasciculations result from increased irritability of an axon (which in turn is often a manifestation of disease of a motor neuron). This leads to sporadic discharges of all the muscle fibers controlled by the axon in isolation from other motor units.

terms.name: Aphasia
terms.definition: An acquired language impairment of some or all of the abilities to produce or comprehend speech and to read or write.

terms.name: Infectious encephalitis
terms.definition: A disorder of the brain caused by an infectious agent that presents with fever, headache, and an altered level of consciousness. There may also be focal or multifocal neurologic deficits, and focal or generalized seizure activity.

terms.name: Focal impaired awareness seizure
terms.name_zh: 局灶性意识障碍性发作
synonyms: Focal seizure with impairment of awareness
Focal seizure with loss of awareness
Focal seizures with impairment of consciousness or awareness
Localised seizure with loss of awareness
Localized seizure with loss of awareness
Partial seizure with impairment of awareness
Partial seizure with loss of awareness
terms.definition: Focal impaired awareness seizure (or focal seizure with impaired or lost awareness) is a type of focal-onset seizure characterized by some degree (which may be partial) of impairment of the person's awareness of themselves or their surroundings at any point during the seizure.

terms.name: Paraparesis
terms.definition: Weakness or partial paralysis in the lower limbs.

terms.name: Cavum septum pellucidum
terms.definition: If the two laminae of the septum pellucidum are not fused then a fluid-filled space or cavum is present. The cavum septum pellucidum is present at birth but usually obliterates by the age of 3 to 6 months. It is up to 1cm in width and the walls are parallel. It is an enclosed space and is not part of the ventricular system or connected with the subarachnoid space.

terms.name: EEG with polyspike wave complexes
synonyms: EEG: spike and multispike waves, 3-4 hz
terms.definition: The presence of complexes of repetitive spikes and waves in EEG.

terms.name: Lower limb hyperreflexia
synonyms: Increased deep tendon reflexes in the lower limbs
terms.definition: Increased intensity of the a reflex in the leg.

terms.name: Cogwheel rigidity
terms.definition: A type of rigidity in which a muscle responds with cogwheellike jerks to the use of constant force in bending the limb (i.e., it gives way in little, repeated jerks when the muscle is passively stretched).

terms.name: Degeneration of anterior horn cells
synonyms: Degeneration of alpha-motor neurons in anterior horn cells of the spinal cord
Degeneration of spinal cord anterior horn cells
Loss of spinal cord anterior horn cells
Progressive loss of anterior horn cells
Spinal cord anterior horn cell degeneration

terms.name: Stroke-like episode
terms.definition: No consensus exists on what a stroke-like episode is, but these episodes can be functionally defined as a new neurological deficit, occurring with or without the context of seizures, which last longer than 24 hours.

terms.name: Positive Romberg sign
terms.definition: The patient stands with the feet placed together and balance and is asked to close his or her eyes. A loss of balance upon eye closure is a positive Romberg sign and is interpreted as indicating a deficit in proprioception.

terms.name: Thickened superior cerebellar peduncle
terms.definition: Increased width of the superior cerebellar peduncle.

terms.name: Limb dysmetria
terms.definition: A type of dysmetria involving the limbs.

terms.name: Cerebral arteriovenous malformation
terms.definition: An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries and that is located in the brain.

terms.name: Aqueductal stenosis
terms.definition: Stenosis of the cerebral aqueduct (also known as the mesencephalic duct, aqueductus mesencephali, or aqueduct of Sylvius), which connects the third cerebral ventricle in the diencephalon to the fourth ventricle, which is between the pons and cerebellum.

terms.name: Myokymia
terms.definition: Myokymia consists of involuntary, fine, continuous, undulating contractions that spread across the affected striated muscle.

terms.name: Spina bifida
terms.definition: Incomplete closure of the embryonic neural tube, whereby some vertebral arches remain unfused and open. The mildest form is spina bifida occulta, followed by meningocele and meningomyelocele.

terms.name: Leukodystrophy
synonyms: Degeneration of white matter of brain
terms.definition: Leukodystrophy refers to deterioration of white matter of the brain resulting from degeneration of myelin sheaths in the CNS. Their basic defect is directly related to the synthesis and maintenance of myelin membranes. Symmetric white matter involvement at MRI is a typical finding in patients with leukodystrophies.

terms.name: Subependymal cysts
terms.definition: Cerebral cysts, usually located in the wall of the caudate nucleus or in the caudothalamic groove. They are found in up to 5.2% of all neonates, using transfontanellar ultrasound in the first days of life.

terms.name: Abnormal midbrain morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the midbrain, which has as its parts the tectum, cerebral peduncle, midbrain tegmentum and cerebral aqueduct.

terms.name: Molar tooth sign on MRI
synonyms: Molar tooth sign on brain imaging
terms.definition: An abnormal appearance of the midbrain in axial magnetic resonance imaging in which the elongated superior cerebellar peduncles give the midbrain an appearance reminiscent of a molar or wisdom tooth.

terms.name: Poor head control
terms.definition: Difficulty to maintain correct position of the head while standing or sitting. Infant head lag is observed when the head seems to flop around or lags posteriorly behind the trunk. Several articles have maintained that head lag should be absent by age 3 to 4 months.

terms.name: Long-tract sign
terms.definition: Long-tract signs refer to symptoms that are attributable to the involvement of the long fiber tracts in the spinal cord, which connect the spinal cord to the brain and mediate spinal and motor functions. These include spasticity, hyperreflexia, and abnormal reflexes such as Babinski or Hoffman's sign. If possible, it is preferable to use the precise HPO terms for these abnormalities.

terms.name: Anarthria
terms.definition: A defect in the motor ability that enables speech.

terms.name: Expressive aphasia
terms.definition: Impairment of expressive language and relative preservation of receptive language abilities. That is, the patient understands language (speech, writing) but cannot express it.

terms.name: Meningocele
terms.definition: Protrusion of the meninges through a defect of the skull or vertebral column.

terms.name: Occipital meningocele
terms.definition: A herniation of meninges through a congenital bone defect in the skull in the occipital region.

terms.name: Dyscalculia
terms.definition: A specific learning disability involving mathematics and arithmetic.

terms.name: Hypothalamic hamartoma
terms.definition: The presence of a hamartoma of the hypothalamus.

terms.name: Tetraplegia
terms.definition: Paralysis of all four limbs, and trunk of the body below the level of an associated injury to the spinal cord. The etiology of quadriplegia is similar to that of paraplegia except that the lesion is in the cervical spinal cord rather than in the thoracic or lumbar segments of the spinal cord.

terms.name: Astrocytosis
terms.definition: Proliferation of astrocytes in the area of a lesion of the central nervous system.

terms.name: Abnormal motor neuron morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly that affects the motor neuron.

terms.name: Limb dystonia
terms.definition: A type of dystonia (abnormally increased muscular tone causing fixed abnormal postures) that affects muscles of the limbs.

terms.name: Abnormal globus pallidus morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the globus pallidus.

terms.name: Eye of the tiger anomaly of globus pallidus
terms.definition: The presence, on T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging, of markedly low signal intensity of the globus pallidus that surrounds a central region of high signal intensity in the anteromedial globus pallidus, producing an eye-of-the-tiger appearance. The sign is thought to represent iron accumulation in the globus pallidus.

terms.name: Distal muscle weakness
synonyms: Distal limb muscle weakness due to peripheral neuropathy
Muscle weakness, distal limbs, due to neuronopathy
terms.definition: Reduced strength of the musculature of the distal extremities.

terms.name: Cerebellar dentate nucleus calcification
terms.definition: Pathological deposition of calcium salts in the dentate nucleus of the cerebellum.

terms.name: Language impairment
terms.definition: Language impairment is a deficit in comprehension or production of language that includes reduced vocabulary, limited sentence structure, or impairments in written or spoken communication. Language abilities are substantially and quantifiably below age expectations.

terms.name: Spastic dysarthria
terms.definition: A type of dysarthria related to bilateral damage of the upper motor neuron tracts of the pyramidal and extra- pyramidal tracts. Speech of affected individuals is slow, effortful, and has a harsh vocal quality.

terms.name: Small cerebral cortex
terms.definition: Reduced size of the cerebral cortex.

terms.name: Expressive language delay
terms.definition: A delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.

terms.name: Myelomeningocele
terms.definition: Protrusion of the meninges and portions of the spinal cord through a defect of the vertebral column.

terms.name: Primitive reflex
terms.definition: The primitive reflexes are a group of behavioral motor responses which are found in normal early development, are subsequently inhibited, but may be released from inhibition by cerebral, usually frontal, damage. They are thus part of a broader group of reflexes which reflect release phenomena, such as exaggerated stretch reflexes and extensor plantars. They do however involve more complex motor responses than such simple stretch reflexes, and are often a normal feature in the neonate or infant.

terms.name: Hepatic encephalopathy
terms.definition: Central nervous system dysfunction in association with liver failure and characterized clinically (depending on degree of severity) by lethargy, confusion, nystagmus, decorticate posturing, spasticity, and bilateral Babinski reflexes.

terms.name: Myotonia
synonyms: Delayed relaxation of muscle fibers after contraction
Delayed relaxation of muscle fibres after contraction
terms.definition: An involuntary and painless delay in the relaxation of skeletal muscle following contraction or electrical stimulation.

terms.name: Hyperkinetic movements
terms.definition: Motor hyperactivity with excessive movement of muscles of the body as a whole.

terms.name: Acute leukemia
terms.definition: A clonal (malignant) hematopoietic disorder with an acute onset, affecting the bone marrow and the peripheral blood. The malignant cells show minimal differentiation and are called blasts, either myeloid blasts (myeloblasts) or lymphoid blasts (lymphoblasts).

terms.name: Increased CSF lactate
terms.definition: Increased concentration of lactate in the cerebrospinal fluid.

terms.name: Spasticity of facial muscles
terms.definition: Spasticity of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve.

terms.name: Abnormal corticospinal tract morphology
synonyms: Morphological abnormality of the corticospinal tract
terms.definition: Abnormality of the corticospinal tract, which is the chief element of the pyramidal system (the principle motor tract) and is the only direct connection between the cerebrum and the spinal cord.

terms.name: Upper motor neuron dysfunction
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the upper motor neuron. The upper motor neurons are neurons of the primary motor cortex which project to the brainstem and spinal chord via the corticonuclear, corticobulbar and corticospinal (pyramidal) tracts. They are involved in control of voluntary movements. Dysfunction leads to weakness, impairment of fine motor movements, spasticity, hyperreflexia and abnormal pyramidal signs.

terms.name: Abnormal rapid eye movement sleep
terms.definition: Abnormality of REM Sleep are phases of REM sleep are characterized by desynchronized EEG patterns, increases in heart rate and blood pressure, sympathetic activation, and a profound loss of muscle tone except for the eye and middle-ear muscles. There are also phases of rapid eye movements.

terms.name: Impaired vibratory sensation
terms.definition: A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration. Clinically, this is usually tested with a tuning fork which vibrates at 128 Hz and is applied to bony prominences such as the malleoli at the ankles or the metacarpal-phalangeal joints. There is a slow decay of vibration from the tuning fork. The degree of vibratory sense loss can be crudely estimated by counting the number of seconds that the examiner can perceive the vibration longer than the patient.

terms.name: Abnormal cerebral white matter morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of the cerebral white matter
Cortical white matter abnormalities seen on MRI
terms.definition: An abnormality of the cerebral white matter.

terms.name: Calcification of the small brain vessels
terms.definition: Deposition of calcium salts within small blood vessels of the brain.

terms.name: Loss of ambulation
terms.definition: Inability to walk in a person who previous had the ability to walk.

terms.name: Diffuse cerebral atrophy
terms.definition: Diffuse unlocalised atrophy affecting the cerebrum.

terms.name: Semilobar holoprosencephaly
terms.definition: A type of holoprosencephaly in which the left and right frontal and parietal lobes are fused and the interhemispheric fissure is only present posteriorly.

terms.name: Brainstem dysplasia
terms.definition: A developmental structural anomaly of the stalk-like part of the brain that comprises the midbrain (aka mesencephalon), the pons (aka pons Varolii), and the medulla oblongata, and connects the cerebral hemispheres with the cervical spinal cord.

terms.name: Limb hypertonia
synonyms: Increased muscle tone of arm or leg

terms.name: Spastic tetraplegia
terms.definition: Spastic paralysis affecting all four limbs.

terms.name: Alzheimer disease
synonyms: Late-onset form of familial Alzheimer disease
terms.definition: A degenerative disease of the brain characterized by the insidious onset of dementia. Impairment of memory, judgment, attention span, and problem solving skills are followed by severe apraxia and a global loss of cognitive abilities. The condition primarily occurs after age 60, and is marked pathologically by severe cortical atrophy and the triad of senile plaques, neurofibrillary tangles, and neuropil threads.

terms.name: Cerebral calcification
synonyms: Abnormal deposits of calcium in the brain
terms.definition: The presence of calcium deposition within the cerebrum.

terms.name: Waddling gait
terms.definition: Weakness of the hip girdle and upper thigh muscles, for instance in myopathies, leads to an instability of the pelvis on standing and walking. If the muscles extending the hip joint are affected, the posture in that joint becomes flexed and lumbar lordosis increases. The patients usually have difficulties standing up from a sitting position. Due to weakness in the gluteus medius muscle, the hip on the side of the swinging leg drops with each step (referred to as Trendelenburg sign). The gait appears waddling. The patients frequently attempt to counteract the dropping of the hip on the swinging side by bending the trunk towards the side which is in the stance phase (in the German language literature this is referred to as Duchenne sign). Similar gait patterns can be caused by orthopedic conditions when the origin and the insertion site of the gluteus medius muscle are closer to each other than normal, for instance due to a posttraumatic elevation of the trochanter or pseudarthrosis of the femoral neck.

terms.name: Increased intracranial pressure
terms.definition: An increase of the pressure inside the cranium (skull) and thereby in the brain tissue and cerebrospinal fluid.

terms.name: Abnormal periventricular white matter morphology
terms.name_zh: 脑室周围白质形态异常
synonyms: Abnormality of the periventricular white matter
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the myelinated axons (white matter) located near the cerebral ventricles.

terms.name: Hypnagogic hallucination
terms.definition: Hypnagogic hallucinations are brief hallucinations that occur when falling asleep.

terms.name: Hypsarrhythmia
terms.definition: Hypsarrhythmia is abnormal interictal high amplitude waves and a background of irregular spikes. There is continuous (during wakefulness), high-amplitude (>200 Hz), generalized polymorphic slowing with no organized background and multifocal spikes demonstrated by electroencephalography (EEG).

terms.name: Areflexia of lower limbs
terms.definition: Inability to elicit tendon reflexes in the lower limbs.

terms.name: Cataplexy
terms.definition: A sudden and transient episode of bilateral loss of muscle tone, often triggered by emotions.

terms.name: Deficit in nonword repetition
terms.definition: Impaired ability to repeat non-word sounds. Nonword repetition (NWR) is a measure of short-term phonological memory.

terms.name: Granulovacuolar degeneration
terms.definition: Electron-dense granules within double membrane-bound cytoplasmic vacuoles.

terms.name: Neuronal loss in central nervous system
Axial dystonia
terms.definition: A type of dystonia that affects the midline muscles, i.e., the chest, abdominal, and back muscles.

terms.name: Abnormal posturing
terms.definition: Involuntary flexion or extension of the arms and legs.

terms.name: Abnormal cortical gyration
terms.definition: An abnormality of the gyri (i.e., the ridges) of the cerebral cortex of the brain.

terms.name: Abnormal cerebral cortex morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the cerebral cortex.

terms.name: Cortical dysplasia
terms.definition: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the cerebral cortex.

terms.name: Inability to walk
terms.definition: Incapability to ambulate.

terms.name: Olivopontocerebellar atrophy
