terms.definition: Delivery of newborn by means of a ventouse, a vacuum device used to assist the delivery of a baby when the second stage of labor has not progressed adequately.

terms.name: Shoulder dystocia
terms.definition: Shoulder dystocia occurs when the fetal anterior shoulder impacts against the maternal symphysis following delivery of the vertex.

terms.name: Hydropic placenta
terms.definition: An abnormality of the placenta in which there are numerous cystic spaces within the placenta as well as placental enlargement.

terms.name: Long umbilical cord
terms.definition: Increased length of the umbilical cord.

terms.name: Abnormal insertion of umbilical cord
terms.definition: Anomalous location of the insertion of umbilical cord in the placenta. Normally, the insertion is at least two centimers distant from the edge of the placenta.

terms.name: Placental abruption
terms.definition: Separation of the placenta from the uterus wall before delivery.

terms.name: Age of death
terms.definition: The age group when the cessation of life happens.

terms.name: Death in adolescence
terms.definition: Death during adolescence, the period between childhood and adulthood (roughly between the ages of 10 and 16 years).

terms.name: Abnormal circulating chloride concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of chloride in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Hyperchloremia
terms.definition: The concentration of chloride in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Increased serum zinc
terms.definition: An increased concentration of zinc in the blood.

terms.name: Fetal ultrasound soft marker
terms.definition: An finding upon obstetric ultrasound examination performed at around 16 to 20 weeks of gestation that is abnormal but not clearly identifiable as a fetal anatomic malformation or growth restriction. Such findings are known as soft markers since they are associated with increased risk for fetal aneuploidy or other disorders.

terms.name: Fetal choroid plexus cysts
terms.definition: Fetal choroid plexus cysts (CPCs) are sonographically discrete, small cysts found in the choroid plexus within the lateral cerebral ventricles of the developing fetus at 14 to 24 weeks gestation. Imaging of the choroid plexus is performed in the transverse plane of the fetal head at the same level that the lateral cerebral ventricle is evaluated. The choroid plexus should be inspected bilaterally for the presence of cysts. The size of CPCs is not of clinical relevance (PMID:16100637).

terms.name: Enlarged fetal cisterna magna
terms.definition: The cisterna magna is measured on a transaxial view of the fetal head angled 15 degrees caudal to the canthomeatal line. The anterior/posterior diameter is taken between the inferior/posterior surface of the vermis of the cerebellum to the inner surface of the cranium. An enlarged cisternal magna is defined by an anterior/posterior diameter of 10 mm or more (PMID:16100637).

terms.name: Short fetal femur length
terms.definition: A short femur length is defined as either a measurement below the 2.5th percentile for gestational age or a measurement that is less than 0.9 of that predicted by the measured biparietal diameter. The femur should be measured with the bone perpendicular to the ultrasound beam and with epiphyseal cartilages visible but not included in the measurement (PMID:16100637).

terms.name: Short fetal humerus length
synonyms: Short fetal long bone in upper arm length
Short foetal long bone in upper arm length
terms.definition: A short humerus length is defined as a length below the 2.5th percentile for gestational age or as a measurement less than 0.9 of that predicted by the measured biparietal diameter. The humerus should be measured with the bone perpendicular to the ultrasound beam and with epiphyseal cartilages visible but not included in the measurement (PMID:16100637).

terms.name: Hypoplasia of fetal nasal bone
terms.definition: On prenatal ultrasound, the nasal bone is a thin echogenic line within the bridge of the fetal nose. The fetus is imaged facing the transducer with the fetal face strictly in the midline. The angle of insonation is 90 degrees, with the longitudinal axis of the nasal bone as the reference line. Calibres are placed at each end of the nasal bone. Absence of the nasal bone or measurements below 2.5th percentile are considered significant (PMID:16100637).

terms.name: Fetal fifth finger clinodactyly
terms.definition: Fifth finger clinodactyly is defined by a hypoplastic or absent mid-phalanx of the fifth digit. Ultrasound identification of the fetal hand must first be undertaken and then appropriate magnification accomplished. The evaluation requires stretching of the 5 fingers. The diagnosis is established when the middle phalanx of the fifth finger is markedly smaller than normal or absent, which often causes the finger to be curved inward (PMID:16100637).

terms.name: Elevated maternal circulating alpha-fetoprotein concentration
terms.name_zh: 母体循环甲胎蛋白浓度升高
terms.definition: Increase in the levels of maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein levels during pregnancy.

terms.name: High maternal circulating chorionic gonadotropin concentration
terms.name_zh: 母体循环绒毛膜促性腺激素浓度高
terms.definition: An abnormally high concentration of maternal serum human chorionic gonadotropin as compared to normal values for gestational-age.

terms.name: Low maternal circulating chorionic gonadotropin concentration
terms.name_zh: 母体循环绒毛膜促性腺激素浓度低
terms.definition: An abnormally low concentration of maternal serum human chorionic gonadotropin as compared to normal values for gestational-age.

terms.name: Low maternal circulating PAPP-A concentration
terms.name_zh: 母体循环妊娠相关血浆蛋白A浓度低
terms.definition: An abnormally low concentration of serum PAPP-A (pregnancy associated plasma protein A), as compared to normal values for gestational-age.

terms.name: Abnormal maternal serum screening
terms.definition: An abnormally elevated or decreased level of a maternal serum marker analytes used in screening for aneuploidy.

terms.name: Maternal autoimmune disease
terms.definition: A medical history of a fetus or child born to a mother with an autoimmune disease.

terms.name: Maternal teratogenic exposure
terms.definition: A medical history of exposure of the mother of a child or fetus to a teratogenic substance during pregnancy.

terms.name: Anesthetic-induced rhabdomylosis
terms.definition: Rhabdomyolysis induced by anesthesia.

terms.name: Alcohol-induced rhabdomyolysis
terms.definition: Rhabdomyolysis induced by intake of alcohol.

terms.name: Abnormal medulla oblongata morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the medulla oblongata, the lower half of the brainstem.

terms.name: Abnormal central motor function
terms.definition: An anomaly of the control or production of movement in the central nervous system.

terms.name: Decorticate rigidity
terms.definition: A type of rigidity in which the arms are in flexion and adduction and the legs are extended. This signifies a lesion in the cerebral white matter, internal capsules, or thalamus.

terms.name: Athetoid cerebral palsy
terms.definition: A type of cerebral palsy characterized by slow, involuntary muscle movement and mixed muscle tone.

terms.name: Abnormality of mental function
terms.definition: Cognitive, psychiatric, or memory anomaly.

terms.name: Hyposegmentation of neutrophil nuclei
terms.name_zh: 中性粒细胞核分叶减少
synonyms: Hyposegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in peripheral blood
terms.definition: Hyposegmented (hypolobulated) or bilobed neutrophil nuclei.

terms.name: Ankle clonus
terms.definition: Clonus is an involuntary tendon reflex that causes repeated flexion and extension of the foot. Ankle clonus is tested by rapidly flexing the foot upward.

terms.name: Knee clonus
terms.definition: Clonus is an involuntary tendon reflex that causes repeated flexion and extension of the foot. Knee clonus can be tested by rapidly pushing the patella towards the toes.

terms.name: Unusual CNS infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infections of the central nervous system, as manifested by recurrent, severe, or invasive infections involving the brain, meninges, or spinal cord. This can include infections caused by opportunistic or atypical pathogens, or common pathogens presenting with unusual severity or in anatomical locations.

terms.name: Primary microcephaly
synonyms: Decreased head circumference present at birth
Head circumference small for gestational age
terms.definition: Head circumference below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender at birth.

terms.name: Functional abnormality of the middle ear
synonyms: Functional abnormality of the middle ear
terms.definition: An abnormality of the function of the middle ear.

terms.name: Abnormal incus morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the incus, an ossicle in the middle ear.

terms.name: Abnormal malleus morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the malleus, an ossicle in the middle ear.

terms.name: Absent malleus
terms.definition: Aplasia of the malleus.

terms.name: Absent stapes
terms.definition: Aplasia of the stapes.

terms.name: Loss of eyelashes
terms.definition: This term refers to the loss of eyelashes that were previously present.

terms.name: Abdominal symptom
terms.definition: A subjective manifestation of disease localized to the abdomen.

terms.name: Esophageal carcinoma
terms.definition: The presence of a carcinoma of the esophagus.

terms.name: Embryonal onset
terms.definition: Onset of disease at up to 8 weeks following fertilization (corresponding to 10 weeks of gestation).

terms.name: Fetal onset
terms.definition: Onset prior to birth but after 8 weeks of embryonic development (corresponding to a gestational age of 10 weeks).

terms.name: Young adult onset
terms.definition: Onset of disease at the age of between 16 and 40 years.

terms.name: Childhood onset
terms.definition: Onset of disease at the age of between 1 and 5 years.

terms.name: Aganglionosis of the small intestine
terms.name_zh: 小肠神经节细胞缺失症
terms.definition: A lack of intestinal ganglion cells (i.e., an aganglionic section of bowel) affecting the small intestine.

terms.name: Duodenal aganglionosis
terms.name_zh: 十二指肠无神经节细胞症
terms.definition: A lack of intestinal ganglion cells (i.e., an aganglionic section of bowel) affecting the duodenum.

terms.name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the gallbladder
terms.definition: Absence or underdevelopment of the gallbladder.

terms.name: Absent gallbladder
terms.definition: A developmental defect in which the gallbladder fails to form.

terms.name: Facial tics
terms.definition: Sudden, repetitive, nonrhythmic motor movements (spasms), involving the eyes and muscles of the face.

terms.name: Nasal regurgitation
terms.definition: Regurgitation of milk through the nose.

terms.name: Nasogastric tube feeding in infancy
terms.definition: Feeding problem necessitating nasogastric tube feeding.

terms.name: Gastrostomy tube feeding in infancy
terms.definition: Feeding problem necessitating gastrostomy tube feeding.

terms.name: Abnormal small intestinal villus morphology
synonyms: Abnormal shape of small intestinal villus
Abnormality of small intestinal villus morphology

terms.name: Villous atrophy
synonyms: Small intestine biopsy shows villous atrophy
terms.definition: The enteric villi are atrophic or absent.

terms.name: Childhood onset sensorineural hearing impairment
terms.name_zh: 儿童期起病感音神经性听力障碍
terms.definition: Sensorineural hearing impairment with childhood onset.

terms.name: Persistent stapedial artery
terms.definition: Persistence of the stapedial artery, which normally regresses during embryonic life.

terms.name: Profound sensorineural hearing impairment
terms.definition: Complete loss of hearing related to a sensorineural defect.

terms.name: Upbeat nystagmus
terms.definition: In primary position, the eyes drift slowly downward and then spontaneously beat upward. Upward gaze accentuates the nystagmus. The associated oscillopsias are often very irritating, but the symptoms are usually transient.

terms.name: True anophthalmia
terms.definition: Absence of globe, optic nerve, chiasm and optic tracts. No evidence of ocular tissue on MRI scan or examination.

terms.name: Abnormal lacrimal punctum morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the lacrimal punctum, an opening on the eyelid close to the medial canthus that drains tears from the conjunctival sac into the lacrimal duct in the same eyelid.

terms.name: Unilateral microphthalmos
synonyms: Abnormally small eyeball on one side
terms.definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal smallness of one eye.

terms.name: Abnormal lacrimal duct morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the lacrimal duct, a duct that drain tears from the conjunctiva, via the lacrimal puncta, into the lacrimal sac.

terms.name: Abnormal lacrimal gland morphology
terms.definition: Abnormality of the lacrimal gland, i.e., of the almond-shaped gland that secretes the aqueous layer of the tear film for each eye.

terms.name: Anterior synechiae of the anterior chamber
terms.definition: Adhesions between the iris and the cornea.

terms.name: Posterior synechiae of the anterior chamber
terms.definition: Adhesions between the iris and the lens.

terms.name: Corneolenticular adhesion
terms.definition: Developmental abnormality in which the lens and cornea are not separated.

terms.name: Abnormal corneal thickness
terms.definition: An abnormal anteroposterior thickness of the cornea.

terms.name: Increased corneal thickness
terms.definition: A increased anteroposterior thickness of the cornea.

terms.name: Abnormal corneal endothelium morphology
terms.definition: Abnormality of the corneal endothelium, that is, the single layer of cells on the inner surface of the cornea.

terms.name: Abnormal migration of corneal endothelium
terms.definition: Abnormal migration of corneal endothelium.

terms.name: Abnormal Descemet membrane morphology
terms.definition: Abnormality of Descemet's membrane, which is the basement membrane of the corneal endothelium.

terms.name: Reduced number of corneal endothelial cells
terms.definition: A reduction in the number of corneal endothelial cells.

terms.name: Abnormal corneal stroma morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the stroma of cornea, also known as the substantia propria of cornea.

terms.name: Central opacification of the cornea
terms.definition: Reduced transparency of the central portion of the corneal stroma.

terms.name: Generalized opacification of the cornea
terms.definition: Generalized reduced transparency of the stroma of the cornea.

terms.name: Abnormal corneal epithelium morphology
terms.definition: Abnormality of the corneal epithelium, that is of the epithelial tissue that covers the front of the cornea.

terms.name: Corneal neovascularization
synonyms: New blood vessel formation in cornea
terms.definition: Ingrowth of new blood vessels into the cornea.

terms.name: Rubeosis iridis
synonyms: New blood vessel formation in iris
terms.definition: Formation of new blood vessels on the iris. The new vessels do not display the typical radially symmertic growth pattern of normal iris blood vessels, but rather appear disorganized. Rubeosis usually starts from the pupillary border with tiny tufts of dilated capillaries or red spots that can only be appreciated with high magnification.

terms.name: Mydriasis
terms.definition: Abnormal dilatation of the iris.

terms.name: Polycoria
terms.definition: Multiple pupils.

terms.name: Anterior lenticonus
terms.definition: A conical projection of the anterior surface of the lens, occurring as a developmental anomaly.

terms.name: Posterior lenticonus
terms.definition: A conical projection of the posterior surface of the lens, occurring as a developmental anomaly.

terms.name: Aplasia of the fovea
terms.definition: Congenital absence of the fovea.

terms.name: Bull's eye maculopathy
terms.definition: Progressive maculopathy characterized by concentric regions of hyper- and hypopigmentation, with an initial foveal sparing and whose appearance is said to resemble the central target of a dart board.

terms.name: Cystoid macular edema
terms.definition: Cystoid thickening of the retina that takes place due to accumulation of extracellular fluid in the macula as a nonspecific response to blood-retinal barrier breakdown. Histological studies show that radially orientated cystoid spaces consisting of ophthalmoscopically clear fluid are often clinically detectable in the macula area.

terms.name: Choroidal neovascularization
terms.definition: Choroidal neovascularization (CNV) is the inward growth of new blood vessels arising from the choriocapillaris. Depending on the stage of development, they can be external (type 1 NV) or internal (type 2 NV) to the retinal pigment epithelium.

terms.name: Macular flecks
terms.definition: Pale, often indistinct, multiple lesions of the macula, of variable shape that is not round. The lesions can be notched, angular, or pisciform (said to resemble a fish).

terms.name: Macular hole
terms.definition: A macular hole is a full thickness gap in the macula, located in the center of the retina.

terms.name: Macular hyperpigmentation
terms.definition: Increased amount of pigmentation in the macula.

terms.name: Drusen
terms.definition: Drusen (singular, 'druse') are tiny yellow or white accumulations of extracellular material (lipofuscin) that build up in the Bruch membrane of the eye.

terms.name: Macular schisis
terms.definition: Splitting of the retina in the macular region.

terms.name: Fundus hyperpigmentation
terms.definition: Increased pigmentation of the fundus

terms.name: Retinal cavernous hemangioma
terms.definition: A benign tumor of the retina that appears as a grouping of blood-filled saccules within the inner retinal layers or on the surface of the optic disc. Retinal cavernous hemangioma are described as having a 'cluster of grapes' appearance.

terms.name: Abnormality of binocular vision
terms.definition: An abnormality of binocular vision, that is of the ability to synthesize the visual inputs from both eyes to a single image with perception of depth.

terms.name: Abnormal stereopsis
terms.definition: Inability to make fine depth discriminations from parallax provided by the two eyes' different positions on the head.

terms.name: Achromatopsia
terms.definition: A condition where the retina contains no functional cone cells, so that in addition to the absence of color discrimination, vision in lights of normal intensity is difficult.

terms.name: Cone monochromacy
terms.definition: The condition of having both rods and cones, but only a single kind of cone. Affected individuals have good pattern vision in daylight, but cannot distinguish between colors.

terms.name: Dichromacy
terms.definition: Individuals affected by dichromacy possess only two types of cones, instead of three.

terms.name: Anomalous trichromacy
terms.definition: Individuals with anomalous trichromacy possess three types of cones, but one of the three types of cones has an abnormal spectral sensitivity compared to normal cones.

terms.name: Deuteranomaly
terms.definition: A type of anomalous trichromacy associated with abnormal M photopigment, such that the absorption spectrum is shifted toward L wavelengths. Affected individuals have difficulties distinguishing between red and green.

terms.name: Deuteranopia
terms.definition: Complete lack of the M photopigment, which is replaced with the L photopigment. Affected individuals tend to confuse red and green.

terms.name: Protanopia
terms.definition: Blue and green cones only; no functional red cones.

terms.name: Iris cyst
terms.definition: An iris cyst is composed of a single cell layer of epithelium and is filled with fluid.

terms.name: Iris melanoma
terms.definition: Malignant tumor of melanocytes affecting the iris.

terms.name: Iris nevus
terms.definition: A benign brown pigmented area over the iris representing proliferation of melanocyte cells in the stromal layer of the iris. An iris nevus can be flat or occasionally slightly elevated.

terms.name: Abnormality of lens shape
terms.definition: An abnormal shape of the lens.

terms.name: Lentiglobus
terms.definition: Exaggerated curvature of the lens of the eye, producing an anterior or posterior spherical bulging.

terms.name: Solitary congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
synonyms: Single isolated congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
terms.definition: Sharply demarcated hyperpigmentation of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) that is congenital and of no functional significance.

terms.name: Multiple congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
terms.name_zh: 多发性先天性视网膜色素上皮肥厚
synonyms: Multiple bilateral congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium
terms.definition: Unilateral or bilateral small, well-demarcated pigmented lesions localized in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). Lesions are dark in the center, with a pale circumference and are mostly located in the periphery.

terms.name: Retinal hole
terms.definition: A full-thickness defect in the retina.

terms.name: Vitritis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the vitreous body, characterized by the presence of inflammatory cells and protein exudate in the vitreous cavity.

terms.name: Subretinal exudate
terms.definition: A type of retinal exudate located in the subretinal space between the sensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium.

terms.name: Snowflake vitreoretinal degeneration
terms.definition: The appearance of yellow/white crystalline-like (hence the name) spots in the retina and thickening of the peripheral part of the vitreous.

terms.name: Abnormal spatial orientation of the cardiac segments
terms.definition: Abnormality of the spatial relationship of the cardiac segments to other components of the heart.

terms.name: Abnormal atrial arrangement
terms.definition: Abnormality of the spatial relationship of the atria to other components of the heart.

terms.name: Right atrial isomerism
terms.definition: Right atrial isomerism is characterized by bilateral triangular, morphologically right atrial, appendages, both joining the atrial chamber along a broad front with internal terminal crest.

terms.name: Left atrial isomerism
terms.definition: In left atrial isomerism there is a bilateral small finger-shaped morphologically left atrial appendage joining the atrial chamber along a narrow front without an internal terminal crest.

terms.name: Atrial situs inversus
terms.definition: Mirror image atrial arrangement, with morphologic right atrium on the left hand side and morphologic left atrium on the right hand side.

terms.name: Atrial situs ambiguous
terms.definition: Common atrium without defining morphologic features.

terms.name: Levotransposition of the great arteries
synonyms: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
Physiologically corrected transposition of the great vessels
terms.definition: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (ccTGA) is a discordance of atrioventricular (AV) and ventriculoarterial connections. The anatomy of ccTGA involves systemic venous drainage to the morphologic right atrium (mRA), which is connected via the mitral valve to the morphologic left ventricle (mLV) whose outflow is the pulmonary arterial system. The pulmonary venous drainage arrives at the morphologic left atrium (mLA), which crosses the tricuspid valve into the morphologic right ventricle (mRV) with outflow into the systemic arterial system. In isolation, ccTGA has an in-series circulation without mixing; therefore, the presence or absence of associated defects dictates the patient's clinical presentation.

terms.name: Criss-cross atrioventricular valves
terms.definition: Crossing of the inflow streams of the two ventricles, due to an apparent twisting of the heart about its long axis.

terms.name: Criss-cross atrioventricular valves with superior-inferior ventricles
terms.name_zh: 十字交叉房室瓣伴上下位心室
terms.definition: Criss-cross atrioventricular valves with a rare cardiac malformation characterized by the two ventricles lying one above the other instead of side by side.

terms.name: Superior-inferior ventricles without criss-cross atrioventricular valves
Abnormal connection of the cardiac segments
synonyms: Abnormal connexion of the cardiac segments
Discordant connection of the cardiac segments
terms.definition: A deviance in the normal connections between two cardiac segments.

terms.name: Abnormal atrioventricular connection
terms.definition: An abnormality of the circulatory connection between atria and ventricles.

terms.name: Absent left sided atrioventricular connection
terms.definition: A defect where there is no connection between the left atrium and left ventricle.

terms.name: Absent right sided atrioventricular connection
terms.definition: A defect where there is no connection between the right atrium and right ventricle.

terms.name: Univentricular heart with absent left sided atrioventricular connection
synonyms: Univentricular heart with absent left sided atrioventricular connexion

terms.name: Biventricular heart with straddling right sided atrioventricular valve and absent left sided atrioventricular connection
terms.name_zh: 双心室心脏伴右侧房室瓣跨位及左侧房室连接缺如

terms.name: Right sided atrium to left ventricle and absent left sided atrioventricular connection
synonyms: Right sided atrium to left ventricle and absent left sided atrioventricular connexion

terms.name: Ambiguous atrioventricular connection
terms.definition: With left or right cardiac isomerism in a biventricular, the atrioventricular connections are perforce ambiguous, in that one of the connections is concordant (e.g., right-sided morphologic right atrium connected to a morphologic right ventricle) and one of the connections is discordant (e.g., left-sided morphologic right atrium connected to a morphologic left ventricle).

terms.name: Discordant atrioventricular connection
terms.definition: Connection of the right atrium to the left ventricle and of the left atrium to the right ventricle in a biventricular heart.

terms.name: Double inlet atrioventricular connection
terms.definition: The condition in which both atria are joined to a single ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve.

terms.name: Double inlet left ventricle
terms.definition: The condition in which both atria are joined to the left ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve. Usually there is a hypoplastic right ventricle, which may be on the opposite side of the heart as usual.

terms.name: Double inlet right ventricle
terms.definition: The condition in which both atria are joined to the right ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve. Usually, the left ventricle is hypoplastic.

terms.name: Double inlet to single ventricle of indeterminate morphology
terms.name_zh: 形态未定单心室双入口
terms.definition: The condition in which both atria are joined to a single ventricle each by its own atrioventricular valve. The morphology of this ventricle does not allow one to determine if it corresponds to the left or right ventricle.

terms.name: Double inlet to single ventricle with common atrioventricular orifice
terms.name_zh: 共同房室口单心室双入口

terms.name: Double inlet to single ventricle with two atrioventricular valves
terms.name_zh: 双房室瓣单心室双入口

terms.name: Mitral atresia
terms.definition: A congenital defect with failure to open of the mitral valve orifice.

terms.name: Overriding atrioventricular valve
terms.definition: An atrioventricular valve that empties into both ventricles. The valve overrides the interventricular septum above a ventricular septum defect.

terms.name: Straddling atrioventricular valve
terms.definition: Anomalous insertion of the chordae tendinae or papillary muscles into the contralateral ventricle in the presence of a ventricular septum defect.

terms.name: Abnormal ventriculoarterial connection
terms.definition: An abnormality of the circulatory connection between the ventricles and the pulmonary artery and aorta.

terms.name: Mitral valve arcade
terms.definition: Anomalous mitral valve arcade is diagnosed based on the following features (1) An adequately sized mitral valve orifice; (2) short, thick, and poorly differentiated chordae with direct union of the papillary muscles to the anterior leaflet; (3) narrow or nearly nonexistent spaces between the abnormal chordae; and (4) greater differentiation of the chordae attached to the posterior papillary muscle.

terms.name: Common atrium
terms.definition: Complete absence of the interatrial septum with common atrioventricular valve and two atrioventricular connections.

terms.name: Cor triatriatum dexter
terms.definition: A congenital anomaly with partitioning of the right atrium to form a triatrial heart caused by persistence of the right valve of the sinus venosus. Typically, the right atrial partition is due to exaggerated fetal eustachian and thebesian valves, which together form an incomplete septum across the lower part of the atrium. This septum may range from a reticulum to a substantial sheet of tissue.

terms.name: Sinus venosus atrial septal defect
terms.definition: An interatrial communication caused by a deficiency of the common wall between the superior vena cava (SVC) and the right-sided pulmonary veins. SVASD is commonly associated with anomalous pulmonary venous connection (APVC) of some or all of the pulmonary veins, which produces additional left-to-right shunting.

terms.name: Double orifice mitral valve
terms.definition: The left atrio-ventricular connection consists of two anatomically distinct orifices separated by accessory fibrous tissue.

terms.name: Cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet
terms.definition: Cleft in the anterior mitral valve leaflet not associated with an atrioventricular canal defect.

terms.name: Congenital mitral stenosis
terms.definition: Mitral stenosis with congenital onset.

terms.name: Parachute mitral valve
terms.definition: Abnormality of the mitral valve apparatus, whereby chordae attach to a single papillary muscle or hypoplastic papillary muscles.

terms.name: Supramitral ring
terms.definition: A congenital stenotic mitral valvular anomaly with a ring of tissue above the mitral valve.

terms.name: Hypoplastic tricuspid valve
terms.definition: Congenital defect characterized by underdevelopment of the tricuspid valve.

terms.name: Imperforate atrioventricular valve
terms.definition: An atrioventricular valve that has failed to open (atretic).

terms.name: Imperforate tricuspid valve
terms.definition: A tricuspid valve that has failed to open.

terms.name: Intermediate atrioventricular canal defect
terms.definition: A specific combination of heart defects with a primum atrial septal defect, cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet, and inlet ventricular defect. There is one valve annulus and two valve orifices.

terms.name: Partial atrioventricular canal defect
terms.definition: A specific combination of heart defects including a primum atrial septal defect and cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet. There is not an inlet ventricular septal defect present. There are two valve annuluses and two valve orifices.

terms.name: Transitional atrioventricular canal defect
terms.definition: A specific combination of heart defects with a primum atrial septal defect, cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet, and an inlet ventricular septal defect. There are two valve annuli and two valve orifices.

terms.name: Unbalanced atrioventricular canal defect
terms.definition: Anatomic features of unbalanced atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) include varying amounts of ventricular hypoplasia, as well as malalignment of the atrioventricular junction. In complete AVSD, the common AV valve can be situated either equally over the right and left ventricles (balanced) or unequally over the ventricles (unbalanced).

terms.name: Short chordae tendineae of the mitral valve
terms.definition: Abnormally short chordae tendineae of the mitral valve.

terms.name: Double outlet left ventricle
terms.definition: A congenital defect of heart development characterized by origin of both pulmonary artery and aorta from the morphological left ventricle.

terms.name: Abdominal ectopia cordis
terms.definition: Displacement of the heart outside the thoracic cavity and into the abdomen.

terms.name: Cervical ectopia cordis
terms.definition: A type of ectopia cordis with the heart partially in the cervical region and without a defect of the sternum.

terms.name: Thoracocervical ectopia cordis
terms.definition: A type of ectopia cordis with the heart partially in the cervical region with a defect of the superior portion of the sternum.

terms.name: Thoracic ectopia cordis
terms.definition: Congenital malformation of the thoracic wall with partial or total displacement of the heart outside the thoracic cavity. This feature is associated with sternal cleft or absence of the sternum.

terms.name: Thoracoabdominal ectopia cordis
terms.definition: Congenital malformation of the ventral wall with partial or total evisceration of the heart outside the thoracic cavity and displacement partially into the abdominal cavity.

terms.name: Abnormal branching pattern of the aortic arch
terms.name_zh: 主动脉弓分支模式异常
terms.definition: A deviance from the norm of the origin or course of the right brachiocephalic artery, the left common carotid artery, the left subclavian artery or the proximal vertebral arteries.

terms.name: Cervical aortic arch
terms.definition: The aortic arch extends into the soft tissues of the neck before turning down into to become the descending aorta.

terms.name: Common origin of the right brachiocephalic artery and left common carotid artery
terms.name_zh: 右头臂干与左颈总动脉共干
terms.definition: The left common carotid artery has a common origin with the innominate artery.

terms.name: Double aortic arch
terms.definition: A conenital abnormality of the aortic arch in which the two embryonic aortc arches form a vascular ring that surrounds the trachea or esophagus and then join to form the descending aorta. Double aortic arch can cause symptoms because of compression of the esophagus (dysphagia, cyanosis while eating) or trachea (stridor).

terms.name: Left aortic arch with cervical origin of the right subclavian artery
terms.name_zh: 左主动脉弓伴右锁骨下动脉颈段起源

terms.name: Left aortic arch with isolated subclavian artery
terms.name_zh: 左主动脉弓伴孤立性锁骨下动脉
terms.definition: The subclavian artery arises from ductus arteriosus. While the ductus arteriosus is patent its blood supply comes from the ductus, hence from the pulmonary artery. After it closes, the blood supply is retrogradely from the vertebral artery via the circle of Willis.

terms.name: Left aortic arch with retroesophageal diverticulum of Kommerell
terms.name_zh: 左主动脉弓伴食管后Kommerell憩室
terms.definition: A patent ductus arteriosus or ductal ligament completes the ring.

terms.name: Right aortic arch with retroesophageal diverticulum of Kommerell
terms.definition: Aortic arch crosses the right mainstem bronchus. The left carotid artery is the first branch, right carotid artery the second branch and right subclavian artery as the third branch.

terms.name: Left aortic arch with retroesophageal right subclavian artery
terms.name_zh: 左主动脉弓伴食管后右锁骨下动脉
terms.definition: Aortic arch crosses the left mainstem bronchus. The first branch is the right carotid artery, the second branch is the left carotid artery, the third branch is the subclavian artery, the fourth branch is the right subclavian artery arising from the posteromedial aspect of the distal aortic arch and continuing posterior to the esophagus to the right hand side of the body.

terms.name: Left aortic arch with right descending aorta and right ductus arteriosus
terms.name_zh: 左主动脉弓伴右降主动脉及右动脉导管
terms.definition: The ring may be completed by the ductal ligament.

terms.name: Right aortic arch with left descending aorta and left ductus arteriosus
Right aortic arch with retroesophageal left subclavian artery
synonyms: Right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery
Right aortic arch with anomalous left subclavian artery

terms.name: Mesocardia
terms.definition: Mesocardia is an abnormal location of the heart in which the heart is in a midline position and the longitudinal axis of the heart lies in the mid-sagittal plane.

terms.name: Abnormal direction of ventricular apex
terms.definition: Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex. Left sided is normal.

terms.name: Rightward direction of ventricular apex
terms.definition: Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex towards the right. Left sided is normal.

terms.name: Midline direction of ventricular apex
terms.definition: Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex in the midline. Left sided is normal.

terms.name: Congenital malformation of the great arteries
terms.definition: Defect or defects of the morphogenesis of the aorta and pulmonary arteries.

terms.name: Aortopulmonary window
terms.definition: A congenital anomaly with an abnormal connection between the aorta and the main pulmonary artery resulting in an aortopulmonary shunt.

terms.name: Type II truncus arteriosus
terms.definition: Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) with each pulmonary artery arising separate from each other on the posterior or lateral aspect of the truncus.

terms.name: Type III truncus arteriosus
terms.definition: Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) whereby one of the two pulmonary artery branched does not arise from the common pulmonary trunk, but instead from the ductus arteriosus or directly from the aorta.

terms.name: Type IV truncus arteriosus
terms.definition: Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) whereby the aortic arch is hypoplastic or interrupted, and a large patent ductus arteriosus is present.

terms.name: Interrupted aortic arch
terms.definition: Non-continuity of the arch of aorta with an atretic point or absent segment.

terms.name: Interrupted aortic arch type A
terms.definition: Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment at the level of the isthmus.

terms.name: Interrupted aortic arch type B
terms.definition: Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment between the left carotid and subclavian arteries.

terms.name: Interrupted aortic arch type C
terms.definition: Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment between the innominate and left carotid arteries.

terms.name: Abnormal pulmonary situs morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, which is defined by characteristics such as the number of lobes per lung and the relationship of the pulmonary arteries to their bronchi.

terms.name: Pulmonary situs inversus
terms.definition: Mirror image arrangement of the mainstem bronchi with the right pulmonary artery posterior to the right upper lobe bronchus and the left pulmonary artery anterior to the left upper lobe bronchus.

terms.name: Pulmonary situs ambiguus
terms.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which the morphology of both left and right lungs is the same.

terms.name: Pulmonary situs ambiguus with bilateral morphologic right lungs
terms.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which both lungs have the morphology of a right lung.

terms.name: Pulmonary situs ambiguus with bilateral morphologic left lungs
terms.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which both lungs have the morphology of a left lung.

terms.name: Abnormality of abdominal situs
terms.definition: An abnormality of the abdominal situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the abdomen and its organs.

terms.name: Gerbode ventricular septal defect
terms.definition: A type of ventricular septal defect communicating directly between the left ventricle and right atrium. This is anatomically possible because the normal tricuspid valve is more apically displaced than the mitral valve.

terms.name: Inlet ventricular septal defect
synonyms: Atrioventricular canal type ventricular septal defect
terms.definition: A ventricular septal defect that involves the inlet of the right ventricular septum immediately inferior to the AV valve apparatus.

terms.name: Muscular ventricular septal defect
terms.definition: The trabecular septum is the largest part of the interventricular septum. It extends from the membranous septum to the apex and superiorly to the infundibular septum. A defect in the trabecular septum is called muscular VSD if the defect is completely rimmed by muscle.

terms.name: Apical muscular ventricular septal defect
terms.name_zh: 心尖部肌部室间隔缺损
terms.definition: A muscular ventricular septal defect located at the apex of the heart.

terms.name: Multiple muscular ventricular septal defects
terms.definition: A type of muscular ventricular septal defect characterized by the presence of multiple small defects in the ventricular septum.

terms.name: Scimitar anomaly
terms.definition: Right pulmonary venous return to the inferior vena cava.

terms.name: Aorto-ventricular tunnel
terms.definition: Aorto-ventricular tunnel is a congenital, extracardiac channel which connects the ascending aorta above the sinotubular junction to the cavity of the left, or (less commonly) right ventricle.

terms.name: Congenital defect of the pericardium
terms.definition: A developmental defect of the pericardium with congenital onset.

terms.name: Total absence of the pericardium
terms.definition: No pericardium around the heart, occurring as a congenital defect, not the result of a surgical pericardectomy.

terms.name: Complete diaphragmatic absence of pericardium
terms.definition: No pericardium over the diaphragmatic surface of the heart. It is a congenital defect, not the result of a pericardectomy. Pericardium is present on other parts of the heart.

terms.name: Complete right sided absence of pericardium
terms.definition: No pericardium is present on the righthand side of the heart. It is a congenital absence of pericardium rather than the result of a pericardectomy.

terms.name: Partial right sided absence of pericardium
terms.definition: A congenital anomaly with lack of part of the pericardium on the righthand side of the heart.

terms.name: Complete left sided absence of pericardium
synonyms: Absent lining around of left side of heart
terms.definition: A congenital anomaly with complete lack of the pericardium on the lefthand side of the heart.

terms.name: Partial left sided absence of pericardium
terms.definition: A congenital anomaly with lack of part of the pericardium on the lefthand side of the heart.

terms.name: Partial diaphragmatic absence of pericardium
terms.definition: Lack of a part of the pericardium over the diaphragmatic surface of the heart. It is a congenital defect, not the result of a pericardectomy. Pericardium is present on other parts of the heart.

terms.name: Abnormal coronary artery origin
terms.definition: Isolated abnormalities of the coronary artery origins. This may be in associated with other structural heart malformations but not the patterns of complex structural heart malformations which result in abnormal course of the coronary arteries.

terms.name: Anomalous origin of coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
terms.name_zh: 冠状动脉异常起源于肺动脉
terms.definition: A coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta.

terms.name: Anomalous origin of left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
terms.name_zh: 左冠状动脉异常起源于肺动脉
synonyms: Anomalous left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
terms.definition: Left main coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta, above the left cusp of the aortic valve.

terms.name: Anomalous origin of right coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
terms.name_zh: 右冠状动脉异常起源于肺动脉
terms.definition: Right coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta, above the right cusp of the aortic valve.

terms.name: Single coronary artery origin
terms.definition: The presence of a single coronary artery ostium from which both coronary arteries arise.

terms.name: Coronary artery fistula
terms.definition: A congenital malformation with abnormal connection between one of the coronary arteries and a heart chamber or another blood vessel.

terms.name: Abnormal coronary sinus morphology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the coronary sinus, which is formed by the union of the great cardiac vein and the left marginal vein and terminates in the right atrium. The coronary sinus functions to o collect deoxygenated blood from the myocardium of the heart and drain it into the right atrium.

terms.name: Coronary sinus atrial septal defect
terms.definition: An atrial septal defect characterized by a deficiency in the tissue separating the coronary sinus from the left atrium (LA). This results in partial or complete unroofing of the coronary sinus leading to a predominantly left-to-right shunt through the coronary sinus (LA to coronary sinus to right atrium [RA]). The orifice of the ostium is frequently large because of the increased flow. From the RA side, the defect is located at the level of the coronary sinus ostium and may also include some deficiency in atrial tissue around the ostium. From the LA side, the size can be variable depending on the degree of unroofing of the coronary sinus. There is partial (either focal or fenestrated) or complete absence of the roof of the CS, which results in a communication between the CS and the LA. Unroofed CS is the rarest type of atrial septal defect. It is often associated with persistent left superior vena cava (LSVC) and other forms of complex congenital heart disease, usually heterotaxia syndromes.

terms.name: Coronary sinus diverticulum
terms.definition: A venous pouch within the left ventricular wall, with a neck opening into the coronary sinus.

terms.name: Dilatation of the sinus of Valsalva
terms.definition: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation of one of the anatomic dilations of the ascending aorta, which occurs just above the aortic valve.

terms.name: Juxtaductal coarctation of the aorta
terms.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized at the insertion of the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the juxtaductal region of aortic arch.

terms.name: Postductal coarctation of the aorta
terms.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized distal to the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the postductal region of aortic arch.

terms.name: Patent ductus arteriosus after birth at term
terms.definition: Abnormal persistent patency of the ductus arteriosus in postnatal life when birth was at 37 completed weeks of gestation or greater.

terms.name: Patent ductus arteriosus after premature birth
terms.definition: Abnormal persistent patency of the ductus arteriosus when birth was at less than 37 weeks completed gestation.

terms.name: Bilateral ductus arteriosus
terms.definition: The presence of both a left and a right ductus arteriosus.

terms.name: Double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
terms.name_zh: 右室双出口伴双关型室间隔缺损及肺动脉狭窄
synonyms: DORV with doubly committed VSD and pulmonary stenosis
terms.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a subaortic ventricular septal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that extends anterosuperiorly and are closely related to the pulmonary artery as well, are considered to be doubly committed. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.

terms.name: Double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
terms.name_zh: 右室双出口伴双关型室间隔缺损无肺动脉狭窄
synonyms: Double outlet right ventricle, doubly committed ventricular septal defect
terms.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a subaortic ventritricular septal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that extends anterosuperiorly and are closely related to the pulmonary artery as well, are considered to be doubly committed. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.

terms.name: Double outlet right ventricle with non-committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
terms.name_zh: 右室双出口伴非关型室间隔缺损及肺动脉狭窄
synonyms: DORV with non-committed VSD and pulmonary stenosis
terms.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a non-committed ventricular septal defect (VSD), which is a VSD that is anatomically related to, or close to, neither great vessel, being separated from both by considerable muscle, and also has a pulmonary stenosis; abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.

terms.name: Double outlet right ventricle with non-committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
terms.name_zh: 右室双出口伴非关型室间隔缺损无肺动脉狭窄
synonyms: DORV with non-committed VSD without pulmonary stenosis
Double outlet right ventricle, noncommitted ventricular septal defect
terms.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a non-committed ventricular septal defect (VSD), which is a VSD that is anatomically related to, or close to, neither great vessel, being separated from both by considerable muscle, but there is not accompanying pulmonary stenosis; the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.

terms.name: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
terms.name_zh: 右室双出口伴主动脉下室间隔缺损及肺动脉狭窄
synonyms: DORV with subaortic VSD and pulmonary stenosis
terms.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the aortic origin. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.

terms.name: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
terms.name_zh: 右室双出口伴主动脉下室间隔缺损无肺动脉狭窄
synonyms: DORV with subaortic VSD without pulmonary stenosis
terms.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the aortic origin. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.

terms.name: Double outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
terms.name_zh: 右室双出口伴肺动脉下室间隔缺损及肺动脉狭窄
synonyms: DORV with subpulmonary VSD and pulmonary stenosis
terms.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the pulmonary origin. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.

terms.name: Double outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
terms.name_zh: 右室双出口伴肺动脉下室间隔缺损无肺动脉狭窄
synonyms: DORV with subpulmonary VSD without pulmonary stenosis
terms.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the pulmonary origin. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.

terms.name: Tetralogy of Fallot with absent pulmonary valve
synonyms: Tetralogy of Fallot with absent pulmonary valve syndrome
terms.definition: Features of tetralogy of Fallot with either rudimentary ridges or the complete absence of pulmonic valve tissue.

terms.name: Anomalous origin of one pulmonary artery from ascending aorta
terms.name_zh: 单侧肺动脉异常起源于升主动脉
terms.definition: Anomalous origin of one pulmonary artery from the ascending aorta with the contralateral pulmonary artery arising from the right ventricle.

terms.name: Anomalous origin of left pulmonary artery from ascending aorta
terms.name_zh: 左肺动脉异常起源于升主动脉
terms.definition: The left pulmonary artery originates from the ascending aorta in the presence of a pulmonary valve and main pulmonary artery.

terms.name: Tricuspid atresia
terms.definition: Failure to develop of the tricuspid valve and thus lack of the normal connection between the right atrium and the right ventricle.

terms.name: Right ventricular cardiomyopathy
terms.definition: Right ventricular dysfunction (global or regional) with functional and morphological right ventricular abnormalities, with or without left ventricular disease.

terms.name: Left ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy
terms.name_zh: 左心室心肌致密化不全心肌病
terms.definition: Left ventricular non-compaction (LVNC) is characterized by prominent left ventricular trabeculae and deep inter-trabecular recesses. The myocardial wall is often thickened with a thin, compacted epicardial layer and a thickened endocardial layer. In some patients, LVNC is associated with left ventricular dilatation and systolic dysfunction, which can be transient in neonates.

terms.name: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
terms.definition: Transient left ventricular apical ballooning syndrome or takotsubo cardiomyopathy is characterized by transient regional systolic dysfunction involving the left ventricular apex and/or mid-ventricle in the absence of obstructive coronary disease on coronary angiography. Patients present with an abrupt onset of angina-like chest pain, and have diffuse T-wave inversion, sometimes preceded by ST-segment elevation, and mild cardiac enzyme elevation.

terms.name: Absent right superior vena cava
terms.definition: Absence of the right superior vena cava (RSVC). An absent RSVC is always associated with a persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC). During normal fetal development, the left-sided anterior venous cardinal system regresses, leaving the coronary sinus (CS) and the ligament of Marshall. Failure of the closure of the left anterior cardinal vein results in PLSVC. In general, PLSVC is associated with the right superior vena cava (RSVC) and drains into the RA via a dilated CS. When developmental arrest occurs at an earlier stage, the CS is absent and the PLSVC drains into the left atrium.

terms.name: Bilateral superior vena cava with bridging vein
terms.name_zh: 双侧上腔静脉伴桥静脉

terms.name: Bilateral superior vena cava with no bridging vein
terms.name_zh: 双侧上腔静脉无桥静脉

terms.name: Left superior vena cava draining directly to the left atrium
terms.name_zh: 左上腔静脉直接引流入左心房
terms.definition: A persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) that drains into the left atrium instead of the right atrium via the coronary sinus, resulting in a right to left sided shunt.

terms.name: Left superior vena cava draining to coronary sinus
terms.name_zh: 左上腔静脉引流入冠状窦
terms.definition: A persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) that drains into the right atrium via the coronary sinus. This is the case in 80-92% of cases of PLSVC and results in no hemodynamic consequence.

terms.name: Interrupted inferior vena cava with azygous continuation
terms.name_zh: 下腔静脉离断伴奇静脉延续
terms.definition: Interrupted inferior vena cava with azygous continuation is the result of connection failure between the right subcardinal vein and the right vitelline vein. Consequently, venous blood from the caudal part of the body reaches the heart via the azygous vein and superior vena cava.

terms.name: Cardiac myxoma
terms.definition: A myxoma (tumor of primitive connective tissue) of the heart. Cardiac myxomas consist of stellate to plump, cytologically bland mesenchymal cells set in a myxoid stroma. Cardiac myxomas are of endocardial origin and general project from the endocardium into a cardiac chamber.

terms.name: Cardiac hemangioma
terms.definition: Abnormal proliferation of blood vessels within the cardiac cavities attached to the endocardium.

terms.name: Cardiac teratoma
terms.definition: A teratoma within the heart. Most commonly, these tumors are detected in the pericardial cavity attached to the pulmonary artery and aorta. The tumor size within the heart varies from 2 to 9 cm in diameter, and intrapericardial tumors as large as 15 cm have been reported. Intracardiac tumors arise from the atrial or ventricular wall as nodular masses protruding into the cardiac chambers. Cardiac and pericardial teratomas are easily detected in the fetus and neonate by two-dimensional echocardiography as heterogeneous and encapsulated cystic masses. Histologically, cardiac teratomas contain multiple immature elements including epithelium, neuroglial tissue, thyroid, pancreas, smooth and skeletal muscle, cartilage and bone.

terms.name: Arrhythmia
terms.definition: Any cardiac rhythm other than the normal sinus rhythm. Such a rhythm may be either of sinus or ectopic origin and either regular or irregular. An arrhythmia may be due to a disturbance in impulse formation or conduction or both.

terms.name: Tetralogy of Fallot with absent subarterial conus
Tetralogy of Fallot with atrioventricular canal defect
Tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia and major aortopulmonary collateral arteries
terms.definition: A type of tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia in which all pulmonary blood flow is derived from major aortopulmonary collateral arteries (MAPCA).

terms.name: Tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary stenosis
terms.definition: The commonest form of tetralogy of Fallot characterized by pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta, ventricular septum defect, and right ventricular hypertrophy, without pulmonary atresia, absent pulmonary valve, atrioventricular canal defect or absent subarterial conus.

terms.name: Subarterial ventricular septal defect
terms.definition: A ventricular septal defect that lies beneath the semilunar valve(s) in the conal or outlet septum.

terms.name: Perimembranous ventricular septal defect
terms.definition: A ventricular septal defect that is confluent with and involves the membranous septum and is bordered by an atrioventricular valve, not including the type 3 VSDs.

terms.name: Restrictive ventricular septal defect
terms.definition: Any ventricular septal defect (VSD) that is small enough to restrict flow across it such that a pressure gradient exists between the two sides of the VSD.

terms.name: Non-restrictive ventricular septal defect
terms.definition: Any ventricular septal defect (VSD) that does not restrict flow across it sufficiently to generate a pressure gradient between the two sides of the VSD.

terms.name: Infra-aortic superior vena cava
terms.definition: The superior vena cava passes below the aortic arch.

terms.name: Abnormal coronary artery course
terms.definition: An abnormal path of a coronary artery.

terms.name: AV nodal tachycardia
terms.name_zh: 房室结折返性心动过速
terms.definition: A type of supraventricular tachycardia that originates in the atrioventricular node.

terms.name: Supraventricular tachycardia with an accessory connection mediated pathway
synonyms: Supraventricular tachycardia with an accessory connexion mediated pathway
terms.definition: Supraventricular tachycardia in which an accessory pathway connecting the atria and ventricles, apart from the AV node, participates as a necessary part of a reentrant mechanism.

terms.name: Supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory connection
synonyms: Supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory connexion
terms.definition: Supraventricular tachycardia with an accessory connection mediated pathway that is called concealed because it is not seen on the ECG during sinus rhythm.

terms.name: Permanent junctional reciprocating tachycardia
terms.definition: An incessant orthodromic tachycardia with anterograde conduction over the atrioventricular node and by retrograde conduction via an accessory pathway usually located in the posteroseptal region with slow and decremental conduction.

terms.name: Supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory pathway on the left free wall
Supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory pathway on the right free wall
Supraventricular tachycardia with a concealed accessory pathway on the septum
Supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway
Cerebellar hemorrhage
terms.definition: Hemorrhage into the parenchyma of the cerebellum.

terms.name: Supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway on the left free wall
Supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway on the right free wall
Supraventricular tachycardia with a manifest accessory pathway on the septum
Automatic atrial tachycardia
terms.definition: Chronic supraventricular tachycardia predominantly seen in childhood.

terms.name: Multifocal atrial tachycardia
terms.definition: Multifocal atrial tachycardia is a rare supraventricular arrhythmia in neonates and young infants that is characterized by multiple P waves with varying P wave morphology and is usually asymptomatic.

terms.name: Abnormal electrophysiology of sinoatrial node origin
terms.name_zh: 窦房结起源电生理异常
terms.definition: An abnormality of the sinoatrial (SA) node in the right atrium. THe SA node acts as the pacemaker of the heart.

terms.name: Sinus tachycardia
terms.definition: Heart rate of greater than 100 beats per minute.

terms.name: Sick sinus syndrome
terms.definition: An abnormality involving the generation of the action potential by the sinus node and is characterized by an atrial rate inappropriate for physiological requirements. Manifestations include severe sinus bradycardia, sinus pauses or arrest, sinus node exit block, chronic atrial tachyarrhythmias, alternating periods of atrial bradyarrhythmias and tachyarrhythmias, and inappropriate responses of heart rate during exercise or stress.

terms.name: First degree atrioventricular block
terms.definition: Delay of conduction through the atrioventricular node, which is manifested as prolongation of the PR interval in the electrocardiogram (EKG). All atrial impulses reach the ventricles.

terms.name: Second degree atrioventricular block
terms.definition: An intermittent atrioventricular block with failure of some atrial impulses to conduct to the ventricles, i.e., some but not all atrial impulses are conducted through the atrioventricular node and trigger ventricular contraction.

terms.name: Mobitz I atrioventricular block
terms.definition: Progressive PR interval prolongation with the subsequent occurrence of a single nonconducted P wave that results in a pause. The pause that follows the nonconducted impulse is less than fully compensatory (less than the sum of two normal sinus intervals).

terms.name: Mobitz II atrioventricular block
terms.definition: A type of second degree atrioventricular (AV) block characterized by sudden failure to conduct an impulse through the AV node without a preceding change in the PR interval.

terms.name: Atrioventricular dissociation
terms.definition: Atrioventricular (AV) dissociation is present if the atria and the ventricles are under the control of two separate pacemakers. AV dissociation can occur in the absence of a primary AV conduction disturbance.

terms.name: Bundle branch block
terms.definition: Block of conduction of electrical impulses along the Bundle of His or along one of its bundle branches.

terms.name: Left anterior fascicular block
terms.definition: Conduction block in the anterior division of the left bundle branch of the bundle of His.

terms.name: Complete right bundle branch block
terms.name_zh: 完全性右束支传导阻滞
terms.definition: A conduction block of the right branch of the bundle of His. This manifests as a prolongation of the QRS complex (greater than 0.12 s) with delayed activation of the right ventricle and terminal delay on the EKG.

terms.name: Left bundle branch block
terms.definition: A conduction block of the left branch of the bundle of His. This manifests as a generalized disturbance of QRS morphology on EKG.

terms.name: Libman-Sacks lesions
terms.definition: Libman-Sacks valvular lesions are sterile fibrofibrinous vegetations that favor the left-sided heart valves and usually form on the ventricular surface of the mitral valve.

terms.name: Trifascicular block
terms.definition: Abnormal conduction in all three divisions of the intraventricular conducting tissue.

terms.name: Junctional ectopic tachycardia
terms.definition: Junctional ectopic tachycardia (JET) is a unique type of supraventricular arrhythmia defined by narrow QRS complex and atrioventricular (AV) dissociation or retrograde atrial conduction in a 1:1 pattern.

terms.name: Atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia
terms.definition: Accessory pathway-related atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT) involves an abnormal electrical conduction of the accessory pathway. The accessory pathway connecting impulses between the atrium and the ventricle can be seen at any site in the AV groove.

terms.name: Abnormality of the pulmonary veins
terms.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary veins.

terms.name: Supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
synonyms: Supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connexion
Total anomalous pulmonary venous connection, supracardiac
Type 1 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
terms.definition: Type 1 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.

terms.name: Cardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
terms.name_zh: 完全性肺静脉异位连接
synonyms: Cardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connexion
Total anomalous pulmonary venous connection, intracardiac
Type 2 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
terms.definition: Type 2 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.

terms.name: Infracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
terms.name_zh: 心下型完全性肺静脉异位连接
synonyms: Infracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connexion
Type 3 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
terms.definition: Type 3 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.

terms.name: Mixed total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
terms.name_zh: 混合型完全性肺静脉异位连接
synonyms: Mixed total anomalous pulmonary venous connexion
Total anomalous pulmonary venous connection, mixed
Type 4 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
terms.definition: Type 4 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.

terms.name: Congenital malformation of the right heart
terms.definition: Defect or defects of the morphogenesis of the right heart identifiable at birth.

terms.name: Uhl's anomaly
terms.definition: Uhl anomaly of the right ventricle refers to the almost complete absence of right ventricular myocardium, normal tricuspid valve, and preserved septal and left ventricular myocardium.

terms.name: Chaotic multifocal atrial tachycardia
terms.name_zh: 紊乱性多灶性房性心动过速

terms.name: Persistent fetal circulation
terms.definition: Systemic desaturation of a liveborn baby resulting from persistent pulmonary hypertension with a patent ductus arteriosus and patent foramen ovale, such that the circulation in postnatal life follows the fetal course.

terms.name: Peroneal muscle weakness
terms.definition: Weakness of the peroneal muscles.

terms.name: Elbow clonus
terms.definition: Clonus at the elbow joint, i.e., an exaggerated phasic stretch reflex characterized by repetitive, rhythmic contractions at the elbow, generated by rapid passive stretch at the elbow joint.

terms.name: Abnormality of joint mobility
terms.definition: An abnormality in the range and ease of motion of joints across their normal range.

terms.name: Abnormal central sensory function
terms.definition: An abnormality of sensation related to CNS function. Assuming the primary sensory modalities are intact and the patient is alert and cooperative, the presence of an abnormality of sensory function may indicate a lesion of a parietal cortex, the thalamocortical projections to the parietal cortex, or the spinal cord.

terms.name: Abnormality of circulating cortisol level
terms.definition: An abnormality of the concentration of cortisol in the blood.

terms.name: Abnormal adrenal morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the adrenal glands.

terms.name: Abnormality of adrenal physiology
terms.definition: A functional abnormality of the adrenal glands.

terms.name: Central adrenal insufficiency
terms.name_zh: 中枢性肾上腺皮质功能减退症
terms.definition: A form of adrenal insufficiency related to a lack of ACTH, which leads to a decrease in the production of cortisol by the adrenal glands. Aldosterone production is not usually affected.

terms.name: Adrenocorticotropin deficient adrenal insufficiency
terms.name_zh: 促肾上腺皮质激素缺乏性肾上腺功能不全
terms.definition: Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in ACTH production.

terms.name: Primary hyperaldosteronism
terms.definition: A form of hyperaldosteronism caused by a defect within the adrenal gland.

terms.name: Corticotropin-releasing hormone deficient adrenal insufficiency
terms.name_zh: 促肾上腺皮质激素释放激素缺乏性肾上腺皮质功能减退症
terms.definition: Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in corticotropin-releasing hormone production.

terms.name: Corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor defect
terms.name_zh: 促肾上腺皮质激素释放激素受体缺陷
terms.definition: Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in the corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor.

terms.name: Dexamethasone-suppressible primary hyperaldosteronism
terms.name_zh: 地塞米松可抑制性原发性醛固酮增多症
terms.definition: A form of primary hyperaldosteronism in which the overproduction of aldosterone can be suppressed by the administration of dexamethasone.

terms.name: Glucocortocoid-insensitive primary hyperaldosteronism
terms.name_zh: 糖皮质激素不敏感性原发性醛固酮增多症
terms.definition: A form of primary hyperaldosteronism in which the overproduction of aldosterone cannot be suppressed by the administration of dexamethasone or similar glucocorticoids.

terms.name: Secondary hyperaldosteronism
terms.definition: A form of hyperaldosteronism caused by abnormally increased renin levels.

terms.name: Ectopic adrenal gland
terms.definition: Abnormal anatomical location of the adrenal gland.

terms.name: Adrenal gland agenesis
synonyms: Congenital absence of the adrenal glands
terms.definition: Absent development of the adrenal gland.

terms.name: Secondary hypercortisolism
terms.definition: Hypercortisolemia associated with a overproduction of ACTH (often from a tumor), leading secondarily to overproduction of cortisol.

terms.name: Non-secretory adrenocortical adenoma
terms.definition: An hormonally inactive adrenocortical adenoma, that is, an adenoma that does not secrete excessive amounts of adrenal hormones.

terms.name: Secretory adrenocortical adenoma
terms.definition: An hormonally active adrenocortical adenoma, that is, an adenoma that secretes excessive amounts of adrenal hormones.

terms.name: Abnormality of the anterior pituitary
terms.definition: An abnormality of the adenohypophysis, which is also known as the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland.

terms.name: Adrenocorticotropic hormone deficiency
terms.name_zh: 促肾上腺皮质激素缺乏
terms.definition: A reduced ability to secrete adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), a hormone that stimulates the adrenal cortex to secrete of glucocorticoids such as cortisol.

terms.name: Adrenocorticotropic hormone excess
terms.name_zh: 促肾上腺皮质激素过多
terms.definition: Overproduction of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), which generally leads secondarily to overproduction of cortisol by the adrenal cortex.

terms.name: Neoplasm of the anterior pituitary
terms.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the adenohypophysis, which is also known as the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland.

terms.name: Abnormal posterior pituitary morphogenesis
terms.name_zh: 垂体后叶形态发生异常
terms.definition: An abnormality of the neurohypophysis, which is also known as the posterior lobe of the hypophysis.

terms.name: Neoplasm of the posterior pituitary
terms.definition: The presence of a neoplasm (tumor) in the neurohypophysis, which is also known as the posterior lobe of the hypophysis.

terms.name: Posterior pituitary dysgenesis
terms.definition: Abnormal development of the neurohypophysis during embryonic growth and development.

terms.name: Pituicytoma
terms.definition: A solid, low grade, spindle cell, glial neoplasm of adults that originates in the neurohypophysis or infundibulum. Clinical signs and symptoms include visual disturbance, headache and features of hypopituitarism. Pituicytomas are well-circumscribed, solid masses that can measure up to several centimeters. Histologically, they show a compact architecture consisting of elongate, bipolar spindle cells arranged in interlacing fascicles or assuming a storiform pattern.

terms.name: Ectopic posterior pituitary
terms.definition: An abnormal anatomical location of the posterior lobe of the hypophysis, also known as the neurohypophysis. The posterior pituitary is normally present in the dorsal portion of the sella turcica, but when ectopic is usually near the median eminence. This defect is likely to be due to abnormal migration during embryogenesis.

terms.name: Posterior pituitary agenesis
terms.definition: Absence of the neurohypophysis owing to a developmental defect.

terms.name: Posterior pituitary hypoplasia
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the neurohypophysis.

terms.name: Pituitary gonadotropic cell adenoma
terms.definition: A type of pituitary adenoma that produces gonadotropins.

terms.name: Pituitary growth hormone cell adenoma
terms.definition: A type of pituitary adenoma that produces growth hormone.

terms.name: Pituitary null cell adenoma
terms.definition: A type of pituitary adenoma that is of unknown cellular origin and that lacks immunocytochemical or fine structural markers. Null cell adenomas are not associated with hormone excess.

terms.name: Pituitary thyrotropic cell adenoma
terms.definition: A type of pituitary adenoma that produces thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH).

terms.name: Pituitary carcinoma
terms.definition: A pituitary tumor with subarachnoid, brain, or systemic metastasis. The diagnosis of a pituitary carcinoma requires evidence of metastatic disease, either outside the central nervous system (CNS) or as separate noncontiguous foci within the CNS.

terms.name: Pituitary spindle cell oncocytoma
terms.definition: A spindled-to-epithelioid, oncocytic, nonendocrine neoplasm of the anterior hypophysis that manifests in adults and follows a benign clinical course. Pituitary spindle cell oncocytomas are firm, fibrous, and adherent to surrounding structures and are highly vascular.

terms.name: Abnormal parathyroid morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the parathyroid gland.

terms.name: Abnormality of the parathyroid physiology
terms.name_zh: 甲状旁腺生理功能异常
terms.definition: A functional abnormality of the parathyroid gland.

terms.name: Parathyroid dysgenesis
terms.definition: Abnormal embryonic development of the parathyroid gland.

terms.name: Ectopic parathyroid
terms.definition: An abnormal anatomical location of the parathyroid gland.

terms.name: Tertiary hyperparathyroidism
terms.definition: A type of hyperparathyroidism that occurs following kidney transplantation, which is a treatment for secondary hyperparathyroidism. Although kidney transplantation leads to a normalization of serum calcium and parathyroid hormone in most patients. The state of persistent hypercalcemia and hyperparathyroidism is referred to as tertiary hyperparathyroidism.

terms.name: Autoimmune hypoparathyroidism
terms.name_zh: 自身免疫性甲状旁腺功能减退症
terms.definition: A type of hypoparathyroidism with circulating antiparathyroid or anti-calcium sensing receptor antibodies indicative of autoimmunity.

terms.name: Abnormal thyroid morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the thyroid gland.

terms.name: Uninodular goiter
terms.definition: Enlargement of the thyroid gland related to a singular nodule in the thyroid gland.

terms.name: Thyroid hemiagenesis
terms.definition: Absence of a lobe of the thyroid gland related to a failure of its embryologic development.

terms.name: Thyroid C cell hyperplasia
terms.definition: An abnormal growth of parafollicular (C-cells) cells.

terms.name: Thyrotoxicosis with toxic single thyroid nodule
Central hypothyroidism
terms.name_zh: 中枢性甲状腺功能减退症
terms.definition: A type of hypothyroidism due to an insufficient stimulation of an otherwise normal thyroid gland. Central hypothyroidism is caused by either pituitary (secondary hypothyroidism) or hypothalamic (tertiary hypothyroidism) defects.

terms.name: Increased circulating free T3
terms.definition: An elevated concentration of free 3,3',5-triiodo-L-thyronine in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Impaired sensitivity to thyroid stimulating hormone
terms.name_zh: 促甲状腺激素敏感性减退
terms.definition: Reduced sensitivity of thyroid follicle cells to stimulation by biologically active thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH).

terms.name: Activating thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor defect
terms.name_zh: 促甲状腺激素受体激活缺陷
terms.definition: Gain-of-function thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor (TSHR) defect.

terms.name: Inactivating thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor defect
terms.name_zh: 促甲状腺激素受体失活缺陷
terms.definition: Loss-of-function thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor (TSHR) defect.

terms.name: Neoplasm by histology
terms.definition: Neoplasm categorized according to type of histological abnormality.

terms.name: Neoplasm by anatomical site
terms.definition: Neoplasm categorized according to the anatomical site of origin of the neoplasm.

terms.name: Embryonal renal neoplasm
terms.definition: The presence of an embryonal neoplasm of the kidney that primarily affects children.

terms.name: Intralobar nephroblastomatosis
terms.definition: Presence of persistent islands of renal blastema in the postnatal kidney, anywhere within a renal lobe (a portion of a kidney consisting of a renal pyramid and the renal cortex above it).

terms.name: Perilobar nephroblastomatosis
terms.definition: Abnormally persistent foci of embryonal immature blastema located in the superficial cortical region (perilobar).

terms.name: Papillary renal cell carcinoma type 1
terms.definition: A type of papillary renal cell carcinoma that is characterized by small cuboidal cells covering thin papillae with a single line of uniform nuclei and small nucleoli.
