terms.definition: A deviation from normal in the ratio of choline to creatine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.name: Ingrown nail
terms.definition: Excessive growth of a nail laterally into the nail fold.

terms.name: Delayed ossification of vertebral epiphysis
synonyms: Delayed maturation of the end part of the vertebral bone
terms.definition: A delay in the process of formation and maturation of the epiphysis of one or more vertebrae.

terms.name: Mild hearing impairment
terms.definition: The presence of a mild form of hearing impairment.

terms.name: Moderate hearing impairment
terms.definition: The presence of a moderate form of hearing impairment.

terms.name: Severe hearing impairment
terms.definition: A severe form of hearing impairment.

terms.name: Profound hearing impairment
terms.definition: A profound (essentially complete) form of hearing impairment.

terms.name: Moderate conductive hearing impairment
terms.definition: The presence of a moderate form of conductive hearing impairment.

terms.name: Severe conductive hearing impairment
terms.definition: A severe form of conductive hearing impairment.

terms.name: Abnormal gastrointestinal tract morphology
synonyms: Abnormal shape of the digestive system
Morphological abnormality of the GI tract
Morphological abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract
Morphological anomaly of the digestive system
terms.definition: Abnormal structure of the gastrointestinal tract.

terms.name: Functional abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract
synonyms: Functional abnormality of the GI tract
terms.definition: Abnormal functionality of the gastrointestinal tract.

terms.name: Neoplasm of the nose
terms.definition: Tumor (An abnormal mass of tissue resulting from abnormally dividing cells) of the nasal cavity.

terms.name: Venous malformation
terms.definition: A vascular malformation resulting from a developmental error of venous tissue composed of dysmorphic channels lined by flattened endothelium and exhibiting slow turnover. A venous malformation may present as a blue patch on the skin ranging to a soft blue mass. Venous malformations are easily compressible and usually swell in thewhen venous pressure increases (e.g., when held in a dependent position or when a child cries). They may be relatively localized or quite extensive within an anatomic region.

terms.name: Heart block
terms.definition: Impaired conduction of cardiac impulse occurring anywhere along the conduction pathway.

terms.name: Sinoatrial block
terms.definition: Disturbance in the atrial activation that is caused by transient failure of impulse conduction from the sinoatrial node to the cardiac atria.

terms.name: Upper eyelid edema
terms.definition: Edema in the region of the upper eyelid.

terms.name: Cutaneous syndactyly
terms.definition: A soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two digits that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints, or a soft tissue continuity in the A/P axis between two digits that lies significantly distal to the flexion crease that overlies the metacarpophalangeal or metatarsophalangeal joint of the adjacent digits.

terms.name: Episodic hypokalemia
terms.definition: An abnormally decreased potassium concentration in the blood occurring periodically with a return to normal between the episodes.

terms.name: Thoracic aortic aneurysm
terms.definition: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the thoracic aorta.

terms.name: Fusiform descending thoracic aortic aneurysm
terms.definition: A concentric abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the descending thoracic aorta that involves the full circumference of the vessel wall

terms.name: Saccular descending thoracic aortic aneurysm
terms.definition: An eccentric abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the descending thoracic aorta that involves only a portion of the circumference of the vessel wall

terms.name: Aglossia
terms.definition: Absence of the tongue owing to a developmental abnormality.

terms.name: Ectopic anterior pituitary gland
terms.definition: Abnormal anatomic location of the anterior pituitary gland.

terms.name: Anorectal anomaly
terms.definition: An abnormality of the anus or rectum.

terms.name: Macule
terms.definition: A flat, distinct, discolored area of skin less than 1 cm wide that does not involve any change in the thickness or texture of the skin.

terms.name: Ketotic hypoglycemia
terms.definition: Low blood glucose is accompanied by elevated levels of ketone bodies in the body.

terms.name: Cough
terms.definition: A sudden, audible expulsion of air from the lungs through a partially closed glottis, preceded by inhalation.

terms.name: Profound global developmental delay
terms.definition: A profound delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child.

terms.name: Small intestinal polyp
terms.definition: A discrete abnormal tissue mass that protrudes into the lumen of the small intestine and is attached to the intestinal wall either by a stalk, pedunculus, or a broad base.

terms.name: Agenesis of canine
synonyms: Failure of development of eye tooth
terms.definition: Agenesis of canine tooth.

terms.name: Agenesis of the small intestine
terms.definition: Failure to develop of the small intestine.

terms.name: Papilloma
terms.definition: A tumor of the skin or mucous membrane with finger-like projections.

terms.name: Unilateral cryptorchidism
terms.definition: Absence of a testis from the scrotum on one side owing to failure of the testis or testes to descend through the inguinal canal to the scrotum.

terms.name: Thin fingernail
terms.definition: Fingernail that appears thin when viewed on end.

terms.name: Abdominal obesity
terms.definition: Excessive fat around the stomach and abdomen.

terms.name: Femoral aplasia
terms.definition: Failure of the femur to develop.

terms.name: Short palpebral fissure
terms.definition: Distance between the medial and lateral canthi is more than 2 SD below the mean for age (objective); or, apparently reduced length of the palpebral fissures.

terms.name: Thin toenail
terms.definition: Toenail that appears thin when viewed on end.

terms.name: Abnormal brainstem MRI signal intensity
terms.definition: A deviation from normal signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brainstem.

terms.name: Focal T2 hyperintense brainstem lesion
terms.name_zh: 脑干局灶性T2高信号病变
terms.definition: A lighter than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brainstem. This term refers to a localized hyperintensity affecting a particular region of the brainstem.

terms.name: Focal T2 hypointense brainstem lesion
terms.name_zh: 脑干局灶性T2低信号病变
terms.definition: A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brainstem. This term refers to a localized hypointensity affecting a particular region of the brainstem.

terms.name: T2 hypointense brainstem
terms.definition: A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brainstem. This term refers to a diffuse hypointensity affecting the entire brainstem.

terms.name: Abnormal basal ganglia MRI signal intensity
terms.definition: A deviation from normal signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the basal ganglia.

terms.name: Focal T2 hypointense basal ganglia lesion
terms.name_zh: 基底节局灶性T2低信号病变
terms.definition: A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the basal ganglia. This term refers to a localized hypointensity affecting a particular region of the basal ganglia.

terms.name: T2 hypointense basal ganglia
terms.definition: A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the basal ganglia. This term refers to a diffuse hypointensity affecting all of the basal ganglia.

terms.name: CNS hypermyelination
terms.name_zh: 中枢神经系统髓鞘过度形成
terms.definition: Increased amount of myelin in the central nervous system.

terms.name: Enlarged brainstem
terms.definition: Abnormal increase in size of the brainstem.

terms.name: CSF polymorphonuclear pleocytosis
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液多形核白细胞增多
terms.definition: An increased polymorphonuclear cell count in the cerebrospinal fluid.

terms.name: Abnormal neuron morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of a neuron. Neurons are electrically excitable cells that transmit signals throughout the body. Neurons employ both electrical and chemical components in the transmission of information. Neurons are connected to other neurons at synapses and connected to effector organs or cells at neuroeffector junctions.

terms.name: Neurodevelopmental delay
terms.definition: Neurodevelopmental delay (NDD) refers to delays in the maturation of the brain and central nervous system; infants and young children with NDD may experience delays in the development of one or more skills including gross motor abilities, fine-motor coordination, language abilities and ability to solve increasingly complex problems.

terms.name: Neurodevelopmental abnormality
terms.definition: A deviation from normal of the neurological development of a child, which may include any or all of the aspects of the development of personal, social, gross or fine motor, and cognitive abilities.

terms.name: Reduced social responsiveness
terms.definition: A reduced ability to participate in the back-and-forth flow of social interaction appropriate to culture and developmental level, which is normally characterized by an influence of the behavior of one person on the behavior of another person. This results in difficulty interacting with others through emotional, physical, or verbal communication.

terms.name: Absent mastoid
terms.definition: A developmental anomaly in which the mastoid process fails to form and is thus found to be congenitally absent.

terms.name: Cerebral white matter atrophy
terms.definition: The presence of atrophy (wasting) of the cerebral white matter.

terms.name: Paroxysmal dyspnea
terms.definition: A sudden attack of dyspnea that occurs while the affected person is at rest.

terms.name: Orthopnea
terms.definition: A sensation of breathlessness in the recumbent position, relieved by sitting or standing.

terms.name: Widened cerebellar subarachnoid space
terms.definition: An increase in size of the anatomic space between the arachnoid membrane and pia mater in the region surrounding the cerebellum.

terms.name: Widened cerebral subarachnoid space
terms.definition: An increase in size of the anatomic space between the arachnoid membrane and pia mater in the region surrounding the cerebrum.

terms.name: Abnormal placental size
terms.definition: A deviation from normal size of the placenta.

terms.name: Neonatal asphyxia
terms.definition: Respiratory failure in the newborn.

terms.name: Abnormal arm span
terms.definition: A deviation from normal of the length of the arm span (length from one end of an individual's arms measured at the fingertips to the other when raised parallel to the ground at shoulder height at a one-hundred eighty degree angle)

terms.name: Reduced arm span
terms.definition: Decreased length of the arm span (length from one end of an individual's arms measured at the fingertips to the other when raised parallel to the ground at shoulder height at a one-hundred eighty degree angle).

terms.name: Increased arm span
terms.definition: Increased length of the arm span (length from one end of an individual's arms measured at the fingertips to the other when raised parallel to the ground at shoulder height at a one-hundred eighty degree angle).

terms.name: Abnormal upper to lower segment ratio
terms.definition: A deviation from normal of the relation between the upper and the lower segment of the body, where the lower segment is defined as the length between the top of pubic symphysis to floor, and the upper segment is defined as the top of head to top of pubic symphysis.

terms.name: Reduced upper to lower segment ratio
terms.definition: Decreased ratio between the upper and the lower segment of the body, where the lower segment is defined as the length between the top of pubic symphysis to floor, and the upper segment is defined as the top of head to top of pubic symphysis. Consider the term Disproportionate tall stature (HP:0001519) if tall stature is also present.

terms.name: Increased upper to lower segment ratio
terms.definition: Elevated ratio between the upper and the lower segment of the body, where the lower segment is defined as the length between the top of pubic symphysis to floor, and the upper segment is defined as the top of head to top of pubic symphysis.

terms.name: Stellate iris
terms.definition: A lacy pattern or iris pigmentation that resembles the spokes of a bicycle wheel.

terms.name: Abnormal ciliary body morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the ciliary body.

terms.name: Retinal neoplasm
terms.definition: A benign or malignant tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the retina.

terms.name: Retinal astrocytic hamartoma
terms.definition: A glial tumor of the retinal nerve fiber layer arising from a retinal astrocyte.

terms.name: Transient hearing impairment
terms.definition: Hearing loss that occurs acutely and resolves completely.

terms.name: Neoplasm of the ear
terms.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the ear.

terms.name: Mid-frequency hearing loss
terms.definition: A type of hearing impairment affecting primarily the middle frequencies of sound (1000 Hz to 3000 Hz).

terms.name: Perilobar nephrogenic rest
terms.definition: A type of nephrogenic rest associated with multiple lesions in the periphery of the renal lobe.

terms.name: Intralobar nephrogenic rest
terms.definition: A type of nephrogenic rest usually representing single lesions within the renal lobe, renal sinus, or calyceal walls.

terms.name: Perinephritis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the connective and adipose tissues surrounding the kidney.

terms.name: Flexion contracture of finger
terms.definition: Chronic loss of joint motion in a finger due to structural changes in non-bony tissue.

terms.name: Recurrent cystitis
terms.definition: Repeated infections of the urinary bladder.

terms.name: Recurrent pyelonephritis
terms.definition: Repeated episodes of pyelonephritis.

terms.name: Reticulate pigmentation of oral mucosa
synonyms: Reticulate pigmentation of oral mucous membrane
terms.definition: A net-like pattern of increased pigmentation of the oral cavity.

terms.name: Hypoplasia of the calcaneus
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the heel bone.

terms.name: Abnormal intramembranous ossification
terms.definition: An anomaly in the process of intramembranous ossification by which flat bones (cranial bones of the skull, i.e., the frontal, parietal, occipital, and temporal bones, and the clavicles) are formed.

terms.name: Abnormal humeral ossification
synonyms: Abnormal maturation of long bone in upper arm
terms.definition: An anomaly of the process of formation of bone in the humerus.

terms.name: Absent ossification of thoracic vertebral bodies
terms.definition: A lack of bone mineralization of one or more body of thoracic vertebra.

terms.name: Kinked brainstem
terms.definition: A kinked appearance of the brainstem, i.e., an exaggerated flexure.

terms.name: Periventricular white matter hypodensities
terms.definition: Multiple areas of darker than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the cerebral white matter that surrounds the cerebral ventricles.

terms.name: Abnormal optic disc morphology
terms.definition: A morphological abnormality of the optic disc, i.e., of the portion of the optic nerve clinically visible on fundoscopic examination.

terms.name: Increased cup-to-disc ratio
terms.definition: An elevation in the ratio of the diameter of the cup of the optic disc to the total diameter of the disk. The optic disc has an orange-pink rim with a pale center (the cup) that does not contain neuroretinal tissue. An increase in this ratio therefore may indicate a decrease in the quantity of healthy neuroretinal cells.

terms.name: Lymphatic vessel neoplasm
terms.definition: A benign or malignant neoplasm arising from the lymphatic vessels.

terms.name: Pulmonary lymphangiomyomatosis
terms.definition: Infiltration of smooth muscle-like cells in lymph vessels as well as the lung (pleura, alveolar septa, bronchi, pulmonary vessels and lymphatics as well as lymph nodes, especially in posterior mediastinum and retroperitoneum). Focal emphysema can develop because of airway narrowing, and the thoracic duct may be obliterated. Pulmonary lymphangiomyomatosis may lead to multiple small cysts with a hamartomatous proliferation of smooth muscle in their walls.

terms.name: Unilateral facial palsy
synonyms: Paralysis of one side of the face
Weakness of one side of the face
terms.definition: One-sided weakness of the muscles of facial expression and eye closure.

terms.name: Accessory cranial suture
terms.definition: A cranial suture that is in addition to canonical membrane-covered openings in the incompletely ossified skull of the fetus or newborn infant.

terms.name: Narrow jaw
terms.definition: Bigonial distance (lower facial width) more than 2 standard deviations below the mean (objective); or an apparently decreased width of the lower jaw (mandible) when viewed from the front (subjective).

terms.name: Broad jaw
terms.definition: Bigonial distance (lower facial width) more than 2 SD above the mean (objective); or an apparently increased width of the lower jaw (mandible) when viewed from the front (subjective).

terms.name: Anisometropia
terms.definition: Inequality of refractive power of the two eyes.

terms.name: Corneal ulceration
terms.definition: Disruption of the epithelial layer of the cornea with involvement of the underlying stroma.

terms.name: Iris transillumination defect
terms.definition: Transmission of light through the iris as visualized upon slit lamp examination or infrared iris transillumination videography. The light passes through defects in the pigmentation of the iris.

terms.name: Proboscis
terms.definition: A fleshy, tube-like structure usually located in the midline of the face or just to one side of the midline.

terms.name: High insertion of columella
terms.definition: Insertion of the posterior columella superior to the nasal base.

terms.name: Abnormal nasal base norphology
terms.definition: An anomaly of the nasal base, which can be conceived of as an imaginary line between the most lateral points of the external inferior attachments of the alae nasi to the face.

terms.name: Narrow nasal base
synonyms: Decreased width of base of nose
terms.definition: Decreased distance between the attachments of the alae nasi to the face.

terms.name: Wide nasal base
synonyms: Increased width of base of nose
terms.definition: Increased distance between the attachments of the alae nasi to the face.

terms.name: Wide nasal ridge
synonyms: Increased width of dorsum of nose
terms.definition: Increased width of the nasal ridge.

terms.name: Fullness of paranasal tissue
synonyms: Fullness of tissue around the nose
terms.definition: Increased bulk of tissue alongside the nose. The fullness can be caused by both bony and soft tissues.

terms.name: Unilateral breast hypoplasia
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the breast on one side only.

terms.name: Bilateral breast hypoplasia
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the breast on both sides.

terms.name: Hypoplastic female external genitalia
terms.name_zh: 女性外生殖器发育不全
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of part or all of the female external reproductive organs (which include the mons pubis, labia majora, labia minora, Bartholin glands, and clitoris).

terms.name: Right ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy
terms.definition: A predominantly right ventricular variant of isolated noncompaction cardiomyopathy.

terms.name: Noncompaction cardiomyopathy
terms.definition: A type of cardiomyopathy characterized anatomically by deep trabeculations in the ventricular wall, which define recesses communicating with the main ventricular chamber.

terms.name: Biventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy
terms.name_zh: 双心室致密化不全心肌病
terms.definition: Noncompaction cardiomyopathy that affects both ventricles.

terms.name: Myocarditis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the myocardium.

terms.name: Bilateral vocal cord paralysis
terms.definition: A loss of the ability to move the vocal fold on both sides.

terms.name: Unilateral vocal cord paresis
terms.definition: Decreased strength of the vocal fold on one side.

terms.name: Bilateral vocal cord paresis
terms.definition: Decreased strength of the vocal fold on both sides.

terms.name: Clinical modifier
terms.definition: This subontology is designed to provide terms to characterize and specify the phenotypic abnormalities defined in the Phenotypic abnormality subontology, with respect to severity, laterality, age of onset, and other aspects.

terms.name: Severity
terms.definition: The intensity or degree of a manifestation.

terms.name: Mild
terms.definition: Having a relatively minor degree of severity. For quantitative traits, a deviation of between two and three standard deviations from the appropriate population mean.

terms.name: Moderate
terms.definition: Having a medium degree of severity. For quantitative traits, a deviation of between three and four standard deviations from the appropriate population mean.

terms.name: Borderline
terms.definition: Having a minor degree of severity that is considered to be on the boundary between the normal and the abnormal ranges. For quantitative traits, a deviation of that is less than two standard deviations from the appropriate population mean.

terms.name: Severe
terms.definition: Having a high degree of severity. For quantitative traits, a deviation of between four and five standard deviations from the appropriate population mean.

terms.name: Profound
terms.definition: Having an extremely high degree of severity. For quantitative traits, a deviation of more than five standard deviations from the appropriate population mean.

terms.name: Position
terms.definition: The anatomical localization of the specified phenotypic abnormality.

terms.name: Laterality
terms.definition: The localization with respect to the side of the body of the specified phenotypic abnormality.

terms.name: Bilateral
terms.definition: Being present on both sides of the body.

terms.name: Unilateral
terms.definition: Being present on only the left or only the right side of the body.

terms.name: Right
terms.definition: Being located on the right side of the body.

terms.name: Left
terms.definition: Being located on the left side of the body.

terms.name: Spatial pattern
terms.definition: The pattern by which a phenotype affects one or more regions of the body.

terms.name: Generalized
terms.definition: Affecting all regions without specificity of distribution.

terms.name: Localized
terms.definition: Being confined or restricted to a particular location.

terms.name: Distal
terms.definition: Localized away from the central point of the body.

terms.name: Proximal
terms.definition: Localized close to the central point of the body.

terms.name: Retinal vascular tortuosity
terms.definition: An increased number of twists and turns of the retinal blood vessels. This can affect either arteries, veins or both.

terms.name: Skin appendage neoplasm
terms.definition: A benign or malignant neoplasm that arises from the hair follicles, sebaceous glands, or sweat glands.

terms.name: Hair follicle neoplasm
terms.definition: An uncontrolled autonomous cell-proliferation originating in a hair follicle, which is an epidermal adnexal structures responsible for hair growth.

terms.name: Trichilemmoma
terms.definition: A benign tumor originating from the outer root sheath of the hair follicle.

terms.name: Single trichilemmoma
terms.definition: Presence of a unitary trichilemmoma, a benign tumor originating from the outer root sheath of the hair follicle.

terms.name: Multiple trichilemmomata
terms.definition: Presence of multiple trichilemmomata, a benign tumor originating from the outer root sheath of the hair follicle.

terms.name: Epilepsia partialis continua
terms.definition: Epilepsia partialis continua (also called Kojevnikov's or Kozhevnikov's epilepsia) is a type of focal motor status epilepticus characterized by repeated stereotyped simple motor manifestations such as jerks, typically of a limb or the face, recurring every few seconds or minutes for extended periods (days or years).

terms.name: Small intestinal stenosis
terms.definition: The narrowing or partial blockage of a portion of the small intestine.

terms.name: Small intestinal bleeding
terms.definition: Bleeding from the small intestine.

terms.name: Small intestinal dysmotility
terms.definition: Abnormal small intestinal contractions, such as spasms and intestinal paralysis related to the loss of the ability of the gut to coordinate muscular activity because of endogenous or exogenous causes.

terms.name: Colonic stenosis
terms.definition: A narrowing of a segment of colon whereby bowel continuity is maintained.

terms.name: Hepatic bridging fibrosis
terms.definition: Hepatic fibrosis that reaches from a portal area to another portal area.

terms.name: Scrotal hypospadias
terms.definition: Hypospadias with location of the urethral meatus in the scrotum.

terms.name: Midshaft hypospadias
terms.definition: Hypospadias with location of the urethral meatus in the middle of the inferior shaft of the penis.

terms.name: Scrotal hyperpigmentation
terms.definition: Increased pigmentation (skin color) of the scrotum.

terms.name: Abnormal scrotal rugation
terms.definition: Anomaly of the folded ridges (wrinkles) of skin of the scrotum.

terms.name: Increased scrotal rugation
terms.definition: Increased number or density of the folded ridges (wrinkles) of skin of the scrotum.

terms.name: Decreased scrotal rugation
terms.definition: Decreased number or density of the folded ridges (wrinkles) of skin of the scrotum.

terms.name: Esophageal leukoplakia
terms.definition: A white patch or plaque occurring on the surface of the esophageal mucous membranes that cannot be rubbed off and cannot be characterized clinically as any other disease.

terms.name: Testicular fibrosis
terms.definition: Formation of excess connective tissue in the testicle.

terms.name: Ovotestis
terms.definition: A gonad that contains both ovarian follicles and testicular tubular elements.

terms.name: Abnormal germ cell morphology
synonyms: Abnormal shape of a reproductive cell
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of a reproductive cell.

terms.name: Abnormal male germ cell morphology
terms.name_zh: 男性生殖细胞形态异常
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of a male reproductive cell.

terms.name: Abnormal sperm morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of sperm.

terms.name: Abnormal sperm head morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the sperm head.

terms.name: Abnormal sperm neck morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the sperm neck.

terms.name: Abnormal sperm mid-piece morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the sperm mid-piece.

terms.name: Abnormal sperm tail morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the sperm tail.

terms.name: Acephalic spermatozoa
terms.definition: Spermatozoa with very small cranial ends devoid of any nuclear material, that is, lacking a typical sperm head.

terms.name: Vanishing testis
terms.definition: A condition which is considered to be due to the subsequent atrophy and disappearance in fetal life of an initially normal testis. In the presence of spermatic cord structures is evidence of the presence of the testis in early intrauterine life. When associated with a blind-ending spermatic cord, this entity is named as his absence of a testis in an otherwise normal 46XY male is usually unilateral and is assumed to be a consequence of intrauterine or perinatal torsion or infarction.

terms.name: Varicocele
terms.definition: A varicocele is a widening of the veins along the spermatic cord, leading to enlarged, twisted veins in the scrotum, and manifested clinically by a painless testicle lump, scrotal swelling, or bulge in the scrotum.

terms.name: Abnormal vas deferens morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the secretory duct of the testicle that carries spermatozoa from the epididymis to the prostatic urethra where it terminates to form ejaculatory duct.

terms.name: Absent vas deferens
synonyms: Congenital absence of the vas deferens
terms.definition: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the vas deferens.

terms.name: Abnormal male reproductive system physiology
terms.name_zh: 男性生殖系统生理异常
terms.definition: An abnormal functionality of the male genital system.

terms.name: Abnormal ejaculation
terms.definition: Abnormality in the process of ejection of semen (usually carrying sperm) from the male reproductive tract.

terms.name: Premature ejaculation
terms.definition: The emission of semen and seminal fluid during the act of preparation for sexual intercourse, i.e. before there is penetration, or shortly after penetration.

terms.name: Retrograde ejaculation
terms.definition: The emission of semen and seminal fluid into the bladder instead of through the penis during orgasm.

terms.name: Retarded ejaculation
terms.definition: Difficulty of a male in achieving orgasm.

terms.name: Anejaculation
terms.definition: Inability to ejaculate.

terms.name: Abnormal labia minora morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of the inner vaginal lips
terms.definition: An anomaly of the labia minora, the folds of skin between the outer labia.

terms.name: Abnormal labia majora morphology
terms.definition: An anomaly of the outer labia.

terms.name: Hyperplastic labia majora
terms.definition: Overgrowth of the outer labia.

terms.name: Fallopian tube cyst
terms.definition: A fluid filled sac located in the Fallopian tube.

terms.name: Fallopian tube torsion
terms.definition: A twisting of the Fallopian tube. Sudden onset with sharp, colicky pelvic pain associated with nausea, vomiting, bowel, and bladder symptoms is the usual presentation.

terms.name: Fallopian tube duplication
terms.definition: The presence of a supernumerary Fallopian tube.

terms.name: Hemorrhagic ovarian cyst
terms.definition: An abdominal mass formed by bleeding into a follicular ovarian cyst or corpus luteum cyst.

terms.name: Ovarian serous cystadenoma
terms.definition: A cystic tumor of the ovary, containing thin, clear, yellow serous fluid and varying amounts of solid tissue.

terms.name: Abnormal uterine cervix morphology
terms.definition: An anomaly of the neck of the uterus (lower part of the uterus), called the uterine cervix.

terms.name: Cervical endometriosis
terms.definition: Abnormal growth of endometrial cells (which are normally limited to the uterus) within the cervix.

terms.name: Posteriorly placed anus
terms.definition: Posterior malposition of the anus.

terms.name: High posterior hairline
synonyms: High hairline at back of head
terms.definition: Hair on the neck extends less inferiorly than usual.

terms.name: Facial muscle hypertrophy
terms.definition: Hypertrophy of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).

terms.name: Neck muscle hypertrophy
terms.definition: Muscle hypertrophy affecting the muscles of the neck.

terms.name: Paraspinal muscle hypertrophy
terms.definition: Muscle hypertrophy affecting the paraspinal muscles.

terms.name: Scapular muscle hypertrophy
terms.definition: Muscle hypertrophy affecting the scapular muscles.

terms.name: Abnormal motor evoked potentials
terms.definition: An anomaly identified by motor evoked potentials (MEPs). MEPs are measured following single-pulse or repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and can be used for the assessment of the excitability of the motor cortex and the integrity of conduction along the central and peripheral motor pathways.

terms.name: Abnormal upper-limb motor evoked potentials
terms.name_zh: 上肢运动诱发电位异常
synonyms: Abnormal motor evoked potentials in the upper limb
terms.definition: An anomaly identified by motor evoked potentials (MEPs) in the arm.

terms.name: Abnormal lower-limb motor evoked potentials
terms.name_zh: 下肢运动诱发电位异常
synonyms: Abnormal motor evoked potentials in the lower limb
terms.definition: An anomaly identified by motor evoked potentials (MEPs) in the leg.

terms.name: Handgrip myotonia
terms.definition: Difficulty releasing one's grip associated with prolonged first handgrip relaxation times.

terms.name: Myotonia of the face
terms.definition: Slowed relaxation of muscles in the face.

terms.name: Myotonia of the jaw
terms.definition: Slowed relaxation of muscles in the jaw.

terms.name: Myotonia of the lower limb
terms.definition: Slowed relaxation of muscles in the leg.

terms.name: Myotonia of the upper limb
terms.definition: Slowed relaxation of muscles in the arm.

terms.name: Cold-sensitive myotonia
terms.definition: An involuntary and painless delay in the relaxation of skeletal muscle following contraction or electrical stimulation that is induced by exposure to cold.

terms.name: Euryblepharon
terms.definition: Euryblepharon is a congenital eyelid anomaly characterized by horizontal enlargement of the palpebral fissure. The eyelid is shortened vertically compared with the horizontal dimension, with associated lateral canthal malpositioning and lateral ectropion abnormally wide lid opening.

terms.name: Clinical anophthalmos
terms.definition: Congenital anophthalmos is a rare ocular anomaly in which histologically detectable eyeball structures are absent due to poor development of the primary optic nerve vesicle. However, with appropriate imaging or intraoperatively, rudimentary remains of this structure can usually be detected. Therefore, the term clinical congenital anophthalmos seems more appropriate and denotes a phenotypic range between microphthalmos and anophthalmos.

terms.name: Ileal stricture
terms.definition: A pathological narrowing of the ileum that is caused by the development of a ring of scar tissue that constricts the ileal lumen.

terms.name: Embryo developmental arrest
terms.definition: A failure of an embryo to progress through the early stages of preimplantation development (typically from fertilization, i.e., 1-cell zygote, to blastocyst on day 5-6), and is used clinically when embryos fail to reach transferable stages in assisted reproductive technologies (ARTs) such in vitro fertilization (IVF). Arrested embryo development is characterized by downregulation of metabolic activity and cessation of cell division. In order for an embryo to be characterized as non-viable, i.e., arrested, it should present with a lack of cleaving activity and fail to show a sign of mitotic cellular division for at least 24 hours. One can observe failure of a zygote to cleave, cleavage stage arrest either on day 2 or day 3 when the embryo is expected to be between the 2 and 8-cell stage, failure to compact to morula, or failure to form a blastocyst.

terms.name: Abnormal CSF guanidinoacetic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液胍基乙酸浓度异常
terms.definition: The concentration of guanidinoacetic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is outside the limits of normal.

terms.name: Decreased CSF guanidinoacetic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液胍基乙酸浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of guanidinoacetic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Ciliary body coloboma
terms.definition: A coloboma of the ciliary body.

terms.name: Abnormal affect regulation
terms.definition: A disturbance in the processes by which emotional responses are initiated, modulated, sustained, or terminated in a contextually appropriate manner. Abnormal affect regulation involves maladaptive patterns in the generation, intensity, or control of affective experience and expression, leading to inconsistent, excessive, or insufficient modulation of emotion relative to situational demands.

terms.name: History of disease onset in winter
terms.definition: The initial manifestation of a disease or symptom occurring during the winter season.

terms.name: History of disease onset in summer
terms.definition: The initial manifestation of a disease or symptom occurring during the summer season.

terms.name: Cutaneous lesion morphology
terms.definition: A description of structural or physical characteristics of a skin lesion, describing how the lesion appears or is composed.

terms.name: Bleeding into skin lesions
terms.definition: Presence of bleeding within (pre-existing) cutaneous lesions such as blisters or vesicles, resulting in blood-filled lesions.

terms.name: Crusted skin lesions
terms.definition: Lesions covered by a hardened layer of dried exudate, blood, or serum.

terms.name: Slough
terms.definition: Slough is a type of necrotic skin lesion that is characterized as being yellow, tan, green or brown in color and may be moist, loose and stringy in appearance.

terms.name: Local paresthesia at bite site
terms.name_zh: 咬伤部位局部感觉异常
terms.definition: Abnormal tingling, burning, or itching sensation localized to the site of an animal bite, typically occurring after the wound has healed.

terms.name: Amyloid deposition by anatomical site
terms.name_zh: 按解剖部位分类淀粉样沉积
terms.definition: Amyloid deposition categorized according to the anatomical site of deposition.

terms.name: Amyloid deposition by type of amyloid
terms.name_zh: 按淀粉样蛋白类型分类淀粉样沉积
terms.definition: Amyloid deposition categorized according to the category of pathological amyloid fiber being deposited.

terms.name: Transthyretin amyloid deposition
terms.definition: Deposition of misfolded transthyretin (TTR) protein in tissue.

terms.name: Cerebral transthyretin amyloid deposition
terms.name_zh: 脑转甲状腺素蛋白淀粉样沉积
terms.definition: Accumulation of misfolded transthyretin protein in brain tissue.

terms.name: Abnormal CSF 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液5-羟吲哚乙酸浓度异常
terms.definition: The concentration of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above or below the limits of normal.

terms.name: Decreased CSF 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液5-羟吲哚乙酸浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Hip external rotation contracture
terms.definition: A condition where the hip joint is limited in its range of motion due to the shortening of muscles that externally rotate the hip, causing the leg and foot to point outward when standing or walking. The knee is turned past neutral in the direction moving away from the midline, where the neutral position for the hip is with knee pointing directly anteriorly.

terms.name: Hip abduction contracture
terms.definition: Abduction contracture of the hip is characterized by the limitation of active and/or passive adduction of the hip joint in the coronal plane; a chronic reduction in the ability to move the proximal segment of the lower extremity actively or passively medially towards the body midline past the sagittal plane of the body.

terms.name: Hip adduction contracture
terms.definition: Inability of hip to bring from medial side to neutral position, where the neutral position for the hip is with the thigh segment in line with the anatomic plane of the pelvis, both in the coronal and sagittal planes.

terms.name: Hip extension contracture
terms.definition: Inability to flex the hip past the extension range from the neutral position, where the neutral position for the hip is with the hip and thigh segment in line in the same coronal plane as the pelvis.

terms.name: Hip flexion contracture
terms.definition: The inability to bring a flexed hip to neutral in the sagittal plane, where the neutral position for the hip is with the thigh segment in line with the anatomic plane of the pelvis, both in the coronal and sagittal planes.

terms.name: Positive Coombs test
terms.definition: A positive (abnormal) result of the direct antiglobulin test (DAT; sometimes referred to as the Coombs test). The test is a method of demonstrating the presence of antibody or complement bound to red blood cell (RBC) membranes by the use of anti-human globulin to form a visible agglutination reaction. The DAT tests for antibodies or complement bound directly to erythrocytes, indicating in vivo sensitization.

terms.name: Direct antiglobulin test positive for IgG
terms.name_zh: 直接抗球蛋白试验IgG阳性
terms.definition: Demonstration of the presence of IgG antibodies bound to red blood cell (RBC) membranes by the use of anti-human globulin to form a visible agglutination reaction.

terms.name: Direct antiglobulin test positive for IgM
terms.name_zh: 直接抗球蛋白试验IgM阳性
terms.definition: Demonstration of the presence of IgM antibodies bound to red blood cell (RBC) membranes by the use of anti-human globulin to form a visible agglutination reaction.

terms.name: Abnormal spinal cord white matter morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality affecting the white matter of the spinal cord, including sensory tracts (dorsal columns) and motor tracts (corticospinal tracts). Abnormalities may involve myelin, axons, or tract organization and can result in sensory, motor, or autonomic deficits.

terms.name: Abnormal spinal cord lateral corticospinal tract morphology
terms.name_zh: 脊髓皮质脊髓侧束形态异常
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality affecting the lateral corticospinal tracts of the spinal cord, which may involve axonal loss, demyelination, or tract degeneration, and can result in motor deficits such as weakness, spasticity, or impaired voluntary movement.

terms.name: Direct antiglobulin test positive for C3d
terms.name_zh: 直接抗球蛋白试验C3d阳性
terms.definition: Demonstration of the presence of C3d complement fragments bound to red blood cell (RBC) membranes using anti-human globulin (Coombs reagent), which produces a visible agglutination reaction.

terms.name: Hyperreflective retinal dots on OCT
terms.definition: Abnormal hyperreflective dots (HRDs) detected in Optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans. The HRDs are scattered, punctiform, small in size, mainly located in the outer retinal layers and/or around pockets of fluid accumulation and are typically not confluent.

terms.name: Irregularity of the retinal pigment epithelium layer on OCT
terms.name_zh: OCT示视网膜色素上皮层不规则
terms.definition: Lack of uniformity in the morphology of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) layer observed on optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging. The RPE lies between the neurosensory retina (photoreceptors) and Bruch membrane/choroid, and normally appears as a thin, hyperreflective (bright) band on OCT imaging. This term comprises irregularities which may manifest as thickening, thinning, undulations, or loss of normal reflectivity, potentially affecting retinal structure or function.

terms.name: Diffuse
terms.definition: A spatial pattern that is spread out, i.e., not localized.

terms.name: Lower limb dysmetria
terms.definition: A lack of coordination of leg movement manifested by undershoot or overshoot of the intended position of the leg.

terms.name: Upper limb dysmetria
terms.definition: A lack of coordination of arm movement manifested by undershoot or overshoot of the intended position of the arm.

terms.name: Astasia
terms.definition: A postural abnormality characterized by the inability to stand without external support despite having sufficient muscle strength.

terms.name: Vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia
terms.definition: Elongation, dilatation, and/or tortuosity of the vertebrobasilar segment. The definition of VBD includes: (i) diameter of basilar or vertebral artery over 4.5 mm; or (ii) deviation of any portion more than 10 mm from the shortest expected course; and (iii) length of basilar artery over 29.5 mm or length of intracranial vertebral artery over 23.5 mm.

terms.name: Retinal thickening on OCT
terms.definition: Anteroposterior thickness of the retina above the upper limit of normal. This phenotype can be appreciated by retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT).

terms.name: Abnormal anteroposterior retina thickness on OCT
terms.name_zh: OCT示视网膜前后厚度异常
terms.definition: Anteroposterior thickness of the retina outside the limits of normal. This phenotype can be appreciated by retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT).

terms.name: Double elevator palsy
terms.definition: A type of incomitant strabismus in which both elevator muscles (i.e., the inferior oblique and superior rectus muscles) of the same eye are weak leading to restricted elevation and hypotropia.

terms.name: Double depressor palsy
terms.definition: An ocular movement abnormality characterized by simultaneous weakness of the inferior rectus muscle and superior oblique muscle of the same eye.

terms.name: Vertical incomitant strabismus
terms.definition: A type of incomitant strabismus in which the angle of deviation varies as the patient's gaze shifts upwards and/or downwards.

terms.name: Esodeviation
terms.definition: A manifest or latent ocular deviation in which one or both eyes tends to deviate nasally.

terms.name: Accommodative esotropia
terms.definition: A form of esotropia (convergent deviation of the eyes) associated with activation of the accommodative reflex.

terms.name: Abnormal myeloid cell morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of a cell of the monocyte, granulocyte, mast cell, megakaryocyte, or erythroid lineage.

terms.name: Reduced bone-marrow pro-B cell count
terms.definition: A reduction in the numbers of pro-B cells (defined by coexpression of CD34 and CD19). Earlier B-cell precursors are defined by expressing surface CD34 and cytoplasmic TdT in the absence of CD19.

terms.name: Exodeviation
terms.definition: A manifest or latent ocular deviation in which one or both eyes tends to deviate temporally.

terms.name: Anti-granulocyte-macrophage colony stimulating factor antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗粒细胞-巨噬细胞集落刺激因子抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against granulocyte-macrophage colony stimulating factor.

terms.name: Abnormal seminiferous tubule morphology
terms.definition: Any anomaly in the structure or density (count of tubules per volume) of the seminiferous tubules, i.e., the coiled structures within the testis that contain Sertoli cells, which support and nurture germ cells as they develop into mature spermatozoa.

terms.name: Necrotizing lymph node granuloma
terms.definition: A granuloma located within a lymph node that is associated with necrosis. Usually, the necrosis is surrounded by collections of histiocytes. A granuloma is a focal aggregate of immune cells that forms in response to a persistent inflammatory stimulus. It characteristically demonstrates the compact organization of mature macrophages, which may or may not be associated with other inflammatory cell types.

terms.name: Abnormal marker expression
terms.definition: Aberrant marker expression is a phenomenon of abnormal gain or loss of lineage specific or associated antigens. It involves changes in the presence, absence, quantity, or localization of molecular or immunohistochemical markers.

terms.name: Abnormal erythrocyte physiology
terms.definition: Any functional abnormality of erythrocytes (red-blood cells).

terms.name: Diminished MLH1 expression
terms.definition: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrating loss of expression of the mismatch repair gene product mutL homolog 1 (MLH1).

terms.name: Diminished MSH2 expression
terms.definition: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrating loss of expression of the mismatch repair gene product mutS homolog 2 (MSH2).

terms.name: Diminished MSH6 expression
terms.definition: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrating loss of expression of the mismatch repair gene product mutS homolog 6 (MSH6).

terms.name: Abnormal red blood cell count
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal number of red blood cells per volume in the circulation.

terms.name: Increased red blood cell count
terms.definition: An abnormal elevation above the normal number of red blood cells per volume in the circulation.

terms.name: Decreased red blood cell count
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction below the normal number of red blood cells per volume in the circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal hemoglobin concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of hemoglobin in the blood.

terms.name: Decreased hemoglobin concentration
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction below normal hemoglobin concentration in the circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal total eosinophil count
terms.name_zh: 总嗜酸性粒细胞计数异常
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of absolute number of eosinophils in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Diminished PMS2 expression
terms.definition: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrating loss of expression of the mismatch repair gene product PMS1 homolog 2 (PMS2).

terms.name: Pathological inclusion body by subcellular location
Pathological inclusion body by anatomical location
Intranuclear inclusion bodies
terms.definition: Inclusion bodies (deposits of stainable material, usually misfolded proteins) localized in the nucleus.

terms.name: Appendicular location
terms.definition: Applies to a lesion that is localized on the arm or leg.

terms.name: Exposure to humid conditions
terms.definition: A history of living in an environment characterized by excess moisture and heat, tropical conditions, or muggy weather.

terms.name: Viremia
terms.definition: The presence of virus in the blood.

terms.name: Persistent EBV viremia
terms.definition: Persistent or recurrent detection of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in the blood that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Hypopigmented macule
terms.definition: A white or lighter patch of skin that may appear anywhere on the body and are caused by decreased skin pigmentation.

terms.name: Crystalluria
terms.definition: The presence of crystals in the urine.

terms.name: Leucine crystalluria
terms.definition: The presence of leucine crystals in the urine.

terms.name: Wrist ganglion
terms.definition: A benign soft tissue tumor of the wrist usually found in the dorsal aspect of the wrist and communicate with the joint via a pedicle. This pedicle usually originates not only at the scapholunate ligament, but also may arise from a number of other sites over the dorsal aspect of the wrist capsule.

terms.name: Carnitinuria
terms.definition: An elevated level of carnitine in the urine.

terms.name: Alaninuria
terms.definition: An increased level of alanine in the urine.

terms.name: Beta-alaninuria
terms.definition: The amount of beta-alanine in the urine, when normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Erythrocyte inclusion bodies
terms.definition: Nuclear or cytoplasmic aggregates of substances in red blood cells.

terms.name: Pappenheimer bodies
terms.definition: A type of erythrocyte inclusion characterized by basophilic stippling of erythrocytes, that is, by numerous very small coarse or fine blue granules within the cytoplasm with the additional stipulation that the stippled particles are due to iron granules (demonstrable by the Prussian blue stain).

terms.name: Heinz bodies
terms.definition: A type of erythrocyte inclusion composed of denatured hemoglobin.

terms.name: Furuncle
terms.definition: An infection of a hair follicle that extends subcutaneously, forming an abscess.

terms.name: Carbuncle
terms.definition: A pustular lesion of the skin emerging from group of infected hair follicles, characterized by a deep location and dissecting through tissue planes. A carbuncle is larger and deeper than a furuncle.

terms.name: Infection following live vaccination
terms.definition: An infection resulting from live attenuated vaccines (LAV), that is, a vaccine prepared from living viruses or bacteria that have been weakened under laboratory conditions. LAV vaccines will replicate in a vaccinated individual and produce an immune response but usually cause mild or no disease. are derived from disease-causing pathogens.

terms.name: BCGitis
terms.definition: Local or regional infection with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) following vaccination.

terms.name: BCGosis
terms.definition: Distant, or disseminated infection with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) following vaccination associated with failure to contain thebacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) following vaccination leading to spread of BCG to many sites in the body. The tuberculosis vaccine BCG contains live attenuated Mycobacterium bovis.

terms.name: Post-vaccination measles
terms.definition: Infection with the measles virus of the live-attenuated vaccine. This is an extremely rare event and may indicate immunocompromise in some cases.

terms.name: Post-vaccination rubella
terms.definition: Infection with the rubella virus of the live-attenuated vaccine.

terms.name: Post-vaccination polio
terms.definition: Infection with live attenuated polio vaccine following vaccination. This is an extremely rare event that may indicate immunocompromise.

terms.name: Post-vaccination rotavirus infection
terms.definition: Infection with live attenuated rotavirus vaccine following vaccination.

terms.name: Histopathological abnormality
terms.definition: Any microscopic alteration in the cellular or tissue morphology of a biospecimen, identified through histologic examination, including changes in differentiation, organization, or cytologic features.

terms.name: Recurrent deep organ abscess formation
terms.definition: Repeated episodes of the formation of abscesses in organs. An abscess is a circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the parenchyma or an organ.

terms.name: Squamous metaplasia
terms.definition: Metaplasia of an epithelium (normally a unilayer of cuboidal or columnar cells) with squamous epithelium (squamous means scale-like). Metaplastic squamous epithelium becomes stratified (i.e., has multiple layers).

terms.name: Prolonged need of intravenous antibiotic therapy
terms.definition: The requirement for prolonged antibiotic treatment beyond what would be expected for a given infection in a healthy individual of the same age, suggesting unusual susceptibility to infection or failure to respond to standard therapy.

terms.name: Recurrent streptococcal infections
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to streptococcal infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of streptococcal infections.

terms.name: Infection due to encapsulated bacteria
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infections with encapsulated bacteria, as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with encapsulated bacterial organisms such as Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae type b, or Neisseria meningitidis.

terms.name: Severe norovirus infection
terms.definition: An unusually severe course of infection with Human norovirus, previously known as Norwalk virus. Norovirus, an RNA virus of the family Caliciviridae, is a human enteric pathogen. Norovirus infection-associated illness may also be more prolonged and severe in immunocompromised individuals and may be associated with remarkably persistent viral excretion in some of these individuals.

terms.name: Unusual fungal infection
terms.definition: An unusual fungal infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection by a fungal agent.

terms.name: Invasive fungal infection
terms.definition: Fungal infection characterized by invasion of host tissues.

terms.name: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
terms.definition: An opportunistic disease caused by invasion of unicellular fungus Pneumocystis jirovecii. Transmission of P. jirovecii cysts takes place through the airborne route, and usually, its presence in lungs is asymptomatic. However, people with impaired immunity, especially those with CD4+ T cell count below 200/microliter, are still at risk of the development of Pneumocystis pneumonia due to P. jirovecii invasion. Symptoms induced by this disease are not specific: progressive dyspnea, non-productive cough, low-grade fever, arterial partial pressure of oxygen below 65 mmHg, and chest radiographs demonstrating bilateral, interstitial shadowing.

terms.name: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis
terms.definition: Infection of the lungs with aspergillus. In the respiratory mucosa, the spores may germinate into hyphae, which in turn can invade the mucosa leading to invasive pulmonary aspergillosis.

terms.name: Unusual protozoan infection
terms.definition: An unusual protozoan infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection by a protozoal agent.

terms.name: Severe Toxoplasma infection
terms.definition: Toxoplasmosis is a widespread parasitic infection that is frequently asymptomatic in immunocompetent patients. However, this obligate intracellular protozoan parasite can evade the immune system and persist for the life of its host in cyst form, predominantly in the brain, retina, and muscles. Reactivation of latent cysts may occur when the immune system fails to maintain cytokine pressure, which mainly relies on gamma interferon (IFN-gamma). Toxoplasmosis is a life-threatening infection in immunocompromised patients (ICPs).

terms.name: Severe giardiasis
terms.definition: An unusually severe infection due to Giardia lamblia, also called Giardia duodenalis or Giardia intestinalis, which is a protozoan parasite of the small intestine that causes extensive morbidity worldwide.

terms.name: Unusual helminthic infection
terms.definition: An unusual helminthic infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection by a worm (helminth).

terms.name: Unusual parasitic infection
terms.definition: An unusual parasitic infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection by a parasite.

terms.name: Glomerular basement membrane duplication
synonyms: Double contour of glomerular basement membrane
terms.definition: Glomerular basement membrane duplication (GBM-DP) can be seen with Periodic acid-Schiff and silver stains. This appearance results from the presence of subendothelial deposits and the so-called mesangial interposition whereby mesangial cells, infiltrating mononuclear cells, or even portions of endothelial cells interpose themselves between the endothelium and basement membrane, with new, inner GBM-like material being laid down. This produces a double contour or tram-track appearance on light or electron microscopy. This finding often reflects splitting of the lamina densa and is associated with disease processes such as membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis, transplant glomerulopathy, and diabetic nephropathy.

terms.name: Bone fracture
terms.definition: A partial or complete breakage of the continuity of a bone.

terms.name: Abnormal regulatory T cell proportion
synonyms: Abnormal CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cell proportion
Abnormal CD4-positive, CD25-positive regulatory T cell count
Abnormal proportion of regulatory T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of the regulatory (Treg) CD4+ T cell subpopulation, commonly characterized by the CD127lowCD25hi phenotype, with the optional additional positivity for FoxP3, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Increased regulatory T cell proportion
synonyms: Elevated CD4-positive, CD25-positive regulatory T cell count
Elevated proportion of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells
Increased proportion of CD4+CD25+ Treg cells
Increased proportion of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells
Increased proportion of regulatory T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of the regulatory (Treg) CD4+ T cell subpopulation, commonly characterized by the CD127lowCD25hi phenotype, with the optional additional positivity for FoxP3, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Decreased regulatory T cell proportion
synonyms: Decreased proportion of CD4+CD25+ Treg cells
Decreased proportion of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells
Decreased proportion of regulatory T cells
Reduced proportion of CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of the regulatory (Treg) CD4+ T cell subpopulation, commonly characterized by the CD127lowCD25hi phenotype, with the optional additional positivity for FoxP3, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Persistent human papillomavirus infection
terms.definition: Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are small oncogenic viruses. HPV has been shown to cause a variety of lesions and malignancies, which predominantly affect the anogenital region. Low-risk, non-oncogenic HPV types are associated with anogenital warts and recurrent respiratory papillomatosis while high-risk, oncogenic types are associated with cervical, penile, anal, vaginal, vulvar, and oropharyngeal cancers. Infection with anogenital HPV is usually asymptomatic and resolves spontaneously without consequences in the immunocompetent host. When disease does occur, the most common manifestation is genital warts, which may be small papules, or flat, smooth or pedunculated lesions. This resolution of HPV lesions is not generally seen in the immunosuppressed, resulting in severe, persistent and extensive manifestations of HPV disease.

terms.name: Abnormal CD8+ T cell subset proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of any CD8+ T cell subpopulation, measured as percentage of total CD8+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Subcutaneous abscess
terms.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris located in the subcutaneous tissue (subcutaneous fat layer), below the dermis.

terms.name: Hypoplastic dermoepidermal hemidesmosomes
terms.name_zh: 皮肤表皮半桥粒发育不全
terms.definition: Underdeveloped hemidesmosomes at the dermoepidermal junction. Hemidesmosomes are the specialized junctional complexes, that contribute to the attachment of epithelial cells to the underlying basement membrane in stratified and other complex epithelia, such as the skin.

terms.name: Radial artery aplasia
terms.definition: Congenital absence of the radial artery.

terms.name: Abnormal retinal nerve fiber layer morphology
terms.name_zh: 视网膜神经纤维层形态异常
synonyms: Abnormal retinal nerve fibre layer morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the retinal nerve fiber layer

terms.name: Retinal nerve fiber edema
terms.definition: Swelling (edema) of the retinal nerve fibers.

terms.name: Conception by assisted reproductive technology
terms.definition: A history of conception by an assisted reproductive technology such as in vitro fertilization (IVF), intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), and cryopreservation.

terms.name: Bite cells
terms.definition: Red blood cells that appear to have parts of them bitten away.

terms.name: Tympanosclerosis
terms.definition: A stiffening of the tympanic membrane due to calcification, typically presents as white plaque-like lesions, involving discrete regions of the tympanic membrane and/or middle ear.

terms.name: Spontaneous conjunctival filtering bleb
terms.definition: Avascular cystic elevations of the superior conjunctiva not related to ocular surgery or trauma.

terms.name: Prostate mass
terms.definition: A lump detected in the prostate. In this context, mass is a general term for a lump or growth that may be caused by the abnormal growth of cells, a cyst, hormonal changes, or an immune reaction.

terms.name: Periarticular soft-tissue mass
terms.definition: A lump detected in the region that surrounds a joint. In this context, mass is a general term for a lump or growth that may be caused by the abnormal growth of cells, a cyst, hormonal changes, or an immune reaction.

terms.name: Aplasia of the olfactory tract
terms.definition: Aplasia (congenital absence) of the olfactory tract, which causes anosmia, a complete loss of the sense of smell.

terms.name: Abnormal urine protein level
terms.definition: Any deviation of the concentration of one or more proteins in the urine.

terms.name: Increased urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin
terms.name_zh: 尿中性粒细胞明胶酶相关脂质运载蛋白升高
terms.definition: An increased concentration of neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin in the urine (there is no generally accepted threshold, but some studies choose a threshold of above 150 nanogram per milliliter).

terms.name: Abnormal tubular basement membrane morphology
terms.name_zh: 肾小管基底膜形态异常
terms.definition: Abnormal structure of the basement membrane of the renal tubulus.

terms.name: Thickening of the tubular basement membrane
terms.definition: Increase in thickness of the basement membrane of the tubulus of the kidney.

terms.name: Podocyte hypertrophy
terms.definition: Increased visceral epithelial cell size, with or without cytoplasmic protein droplets.

terms.name: Increased urine neutrophil count
terms.name_zh: 尿中性粒细胞计数增多
terms.definition: Abnormally increased count of neutrophils in urine.

terms.name: Myofibromatosis
terms.definition: A mesenchymal neoplasm characterized by solitary or multiple nodules involving the skin, striated muscles, bones and, sometimes, viscera. It usually appears as a subcutaneous nodule, but can also appear as an ulcer, pedunculated lesion, or similar to a hemangioma. Histology shows well-circumscribed tapered cell lobes, resembling smooth muscle cells. At its center, perivascular round cells (hemangiopericitoides) are usually observed, giving a biphasic appearance.

terms.name: Anticardiolipin IgG antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of circulating IgG autoantibodies to cardiolipin.

terms.name: Anticardiolipin IgM antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of circulating IgM autoantibodies to cardiolipin.

terms.name: History of recent animal bite
terms.definition: Medical history of a recent bite injury due to an animal.

terms.name: History of recent insect bite
terms.definition: Medical history of a recent bite injury due to an insect.

terms.name: History of recent tick bite
terms.definition: Medical history of a recent bite injury due to a tick.

terms.name: Blood pressure substantially higher in legs than arms
terms.name_zh: 下肢血压显著高于上肢
synonyms: Blood pressure substantially higher in lower than upper extremities
Blood pressure substantially lower in arms than legs
Blood pressure substantially lower in upper than lower extremities
terms.definition: An abnormal blood pressure discrepancy between the upper and lower extremities with the blood pressure measured in the legs being much higher than the blood pressure measure in the arms. In healthy individuals, ankle systolic blood pressures are only slightly higher than the systolic blood pressure measured in the arm.

terms.name: Blood pressure substantially higher in arms than legs
terms.name_zh: 上肢血压显著高于下肢
synonyms: Blood pressure substantially higher in upper than lower extremities
terms.definition: An abnormal blood pressure discrepancy between the upper and lower extremities with the blood pressure measured in the arms being much higher than the blood pressure measure in the legs. In healthy individuals, ankle systolic blood pressures are only slightly higher than the systolic blood pressure measured in the arm.

terms.name: Tracheal duplication cyst
terms.definition: A cyst in the trachea, whose wall is made up by tissue similar to the bronchial tree, including cartilage and smooth muscle, and is lined by secretory respiratory epithelium composed of cuboid or columnar ciliated epithelium.

terms.name: Calcium phosphate crystalluria
terms.definition: The presence of calcium phosphate crystals in the urine.

terms.name: Calcium oxalate crystalluria
terms.definition: The presence of calcium oxalate crystals in the urine.

terms.name: Calcium carbonate crystalluria
terms.definition: The presence of calcium carbonate crystals in the urine.

terms.name: 2-Methylbutyryl glycinuria
terms.definition: Increased concentration of 2-methylbutyryl glycine in the urine.

terms.name: Increased circulating mead acid level
terms.name_zh: 血循环米德酸水平升高
terms.definition: An abnormally elevated concentration od mead acid in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating succinate
terms.definition: An increase concentration of succinate in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated urinary uromodulin level
terms.definition: The concentration of uromodulin (also known as Tamm Horsfall protein) in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Anti-dsDNA antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against double-stranded DNA.

terms.name: Distal joint hypermobility
terms.definition: Lack of stability of a distal joint (e.g., finger).

terms.name: Positive blood 1,3 beta glucan test
terms.definition: Beta-1,3-glucan is a major constituent of all of the characterized fungal cell walls, making up between 30-80 percent of the mass of the wall. It is a biomarker of fungal infections such as invasive pulmonary aspergillosis.

terms.name: Nevus comedonicus
terms.definition: A type of epidermal nevus characterized by closely arranged, dilated follicular openings with keratinous plugs resembling classical comedones.

terms.name: Abnormal oocyte morphology
terms.definition: An abnormal structure of the female germ cell (egg cell).

terms.name: Abnormal zona pellucida morphology
terms.definition: Abnormal structure of the oocyte extracellular matrix region known as the zona pellucida.

terms.name: Thin zona pellucida
terms.definition: Reduced thickness of the zona pellucida.

terms.name: Increased circulating adrenic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环肾上腺酸浓度升高
terms.definition: An increased concentration of adrenic acid (also known as cis-7,10,13,16-Docosatetraenoic acid) in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Reduced response to gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulation test
synonyms: Reduce response to GnRH stimulation test
terms.definition: Failure of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test to induce an appropriate increased in luteinizing hormone (LH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels.

terms.name: GM1-ganglioside accumulation
terms.definition: Cellular accumulation of GM1 gangliosides.

terms.name: Branch retinal artery occlusion
terms.definition: Blockage of a branch of the retinal artery. This can cause loss of a section of visual field.

terms.name: Abnormal neoplastic cell morphology
terms.definition: A morphological abnormality of of tumor or neoplastic cells, characterized by atypical size, shape, cytoplasmic or nuclear features, or other deviations from normal cellular architecture.

terms.name: Cilioretinal arteriolar hypoperfusion
terms.name_zh: 睫状视网膜小动脉低灌注
terms.definition: Ischemia in the territory of the cilioretinal artery causing opacification of the inner retina and visual loss. This is most commonly seen in central retinal vein occlusion in the young.

terms.name: Ophthalmic artery occlusion
terms.definition: Acute complete obstruction of the ophthalmic artery (branch of the internal carotid artery) that may lead to severe ischemia of the affected globe and associated ocular tissues. It can present with a similar picture to central retinal artery occlusion associated with choroidal ischemia.

terms.name: Branch retinal vein occlusion
terms.definition: Blockage of a branch of the retinal vein. It may present with sudden-onset of painless vision loss or visual field defect correlating to the area of perfusion of the obstructed vessels.

terms.name: Central retinal vein occlusion
terms.definition: Central retinal vein occlusion is an occlusion of the main retinal vein posterior to the lamina cribrosa of the optic nerve and is typically caused by thrombosis.

terms.name: Hemiretinal vein occlusion
terms.definition: A variant of central retinal vein occlusions that involves the superior or inferior half of the retina.

terms.name: Tumor signet ring cell
terms.definition: A signet ring has a flattened surface at the top of the ring with an engraved or raised symbol, historically used to stamp a seal into correspondence. Comparatively, these cells acquire a signet cell morphology due to accumulation of abundant mucin in cytoplasm, leading to nuclei dislocation to the periphery.

terms.name: Abnormal drug response
terms.definition: An anomalous response to a medication related to individual variation in metabolic or immune response to drugs varying from potentially from potentially life-threatening adverse drug reactions to alteration of therapeutic efficacy.

terms.name: Increased blood drug concentration
terms.definition: High plasma concentration of a drug as compared to previously measured thresholds given the expected concentration for the applied dosage regime.

terms.name: Decreased blood drug concentration
terms.definition: Low plasma concentration of a drug as compared to previously measured thresholds given the expected concentration for the applied dosage regime.

terms.name: Adverse drug response
terms.definition: An unpleasant or harmful reaction resulting from treatment with a drug.

terms.name: Reduced drug efficacy
terms.definition: Decreased response to a drug intervention in comparison to the expected response.

terms.name: Refractory drug response
terms.definition: Absent or significantly reduced efficacy of drug intervention characterized by lack of measurable benefit or deterioration of disease course.

terms.name: Reduced circulating cholinesterase activity
terms.definition: Activity or concentration of cholinesterase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Cholesterol crystalluria
terms.definition: The presence of cholesterol crystals in the urine.

terms.name: Abnormal CD8+ TEMRA T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: CD8+终末分化效应记忆T细胞比例异常
synonyms: Abnormal CD8-positive TEMRA T cell proportion
Abnormal proportion of effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells, terminally differentiated
terms.definition: An abnormal proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta effector memory RA TEMRA T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CD45RA-positive, CD45RO-negative, and CCR7-negative.

terms.name: Abnormal dendritic cell count
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal count of dendritic cells in the peripheral blood circulation. Dendritic cells are of hematopoietic origin, typically resident in particular tissues, specialized in the uptake, processing, and transport of antigens to lymph nodes for the purpose of stimulating an immune response via T cell activation. These cells are lineage negative (CD3-negative, CD19-negative, CD34-negative, and CD56-negative).

terms.name: Abnormal circulating haptoglobin concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环结合珠蛋白浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of haptoglobin in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating haptoglobin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环结合珠蛋白浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of haptoglobin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Decreased circulating haptoglobin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环结合珠蛋白浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of haptoglobin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating A-type atrial natriuretic peptide concentration
synonyms: Abnormal A-type atrial natriuretic peptide level
terms.definition: A measurable change in circulating levels of Atrial natriuretic peptide hormone, a protein which plays an important role in the regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.

terms.name: Increased circulating A-type natriuretic peptide concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环A型利钠肽浓度升高
synonyms: Increased circulating A-type natriuretic peptide level
terms.definition: A measurable elevation in circulating levels of Atrial natriuretic peptide hormone, a protein which plays an important role in the regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.

terms.name: Decreased circulating A-type natriuretic peptide concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环A型利钠肽浓度降低
synonyms: Decreased circulating A-type natriuretic peptide level
terms.definition: A measurable reduction in circulating levels of Atrial natriuretic peptide hormone, a protein which plays an important role in the regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.

terms.name: Superior cerebellar dysplasia
terms.definition: Abnormal morphological development of the superior part of the cerebellum.

terms.name: Multilobulated spleen
terms.definition: The fetal spleen is lobulated, and these lobules normally disappear before the birth. Lobulation of the spleen may persist into adult life and be typically seen along the medial part of the spleen. A persisting lobule results in a variation in shape of the spleen.

terms.name: Thick pachygyria
synonyms: Pachygyria with cortical thickness above 10 mm
terms.definition: Pachygyria with a very thick cerebral cortex measuring 10-20 mm. Note that cortical thickness cannot be measured reliably on scans done between 3 and 24 months of age.

terms.name: Anterior predominant pachygyria with 5-10 mm cortical thickness
terms.name_zh: 前为主型巨脑回伴皮质厚5-10mm
terms.definition: Pachygyria with cortical thickness between 5 and 10 mm with and a posterior predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically over 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Posterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.

terms.name: Posterior predominant thick cortex pachygyria
synonyms: Pachygyria with cortical thickness over 10 mm posterior predominant
terms.definition: Pachygyria with cortical thickness above 10 mm with and a posterior predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Posterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.

terms.name: Perisylvian predominant thick cortex pachygyria
synonyms: Pachygyria with cortical thickness > 10 mm perisylvian predominant
terms.definition: Pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm and a perisylvian predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Perisylvian predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.

terms.name: Anterior predominant thick cortex pachygyria
terms.name_zh: 前为主型厚皮质巨脑回
synonyms: Pachygyria with cortical thickness > 10 mm anterior predominant
terms.definition: Pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm and an anterior predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions.
