Anterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe over the frontal and temporal lobes.

terms.name: Pachygyria with 5-10 mm cortical thickness
terms.definition: Pachygyria with a mildly thickened cerebral cortex measuring 5-10 mm. Note that cortical thickness cannot be measured reliably on scans done between 3 and 24 months of age.

terms.name: Prolonged reptilase time
terms.definition: An abnormally increased duration of the reptilase time. Reptilase time is a functional plasma clotting assay, which is based on the enzymatic activity of batroxobin. By specifically cleaving fibrinogen A from fibrinogen, batroxobin leads to the formation of a stable fibrin clot. The time, starting from the addition of batroxobin to the plasma sample, until clot formation is the reptilase time and is given in seconds.

terms.name: IgA heavy chain paraproteinemia
terms.definition: An abnormal IgA heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

terms.name: IgG heavy chain paraproteinemia
terms.definition: An abnormal IgG heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

terms.name: IgM heavy chain paraproteinemia
terms.definition: An abnormal IgM heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

terms.name: Increased circulating arachidonic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环花生四烯酸浓度升高
terms.definition: An increased circulation of arachidonic acid in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating 18-hydroxycorticosterone level
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of 18-Hydroxycorticosterone level in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Decreased circulating 18-hydroxycortisone level
terms.name_zh: 循环18-羟可的松水平降低
terms.definition: A subnormal concentration of 18-Hydroxycorticosterone level in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Increased circulating 18-hydroxycortisone level
terms.name_zh: 循环18-羟可的松水平升高
terms.definition: An abnormally elevated concentration of 18-Hydroxycorticosterone level in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal sarcomere morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the sarcomere, which is unit of a myofibril in a muscle cell, composed of an array of overlapping thick and thin filaments between two adjacent Z disks.

terms.name: Abnormal Z disk morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the Z disk, which is the platelike region of a muscle sarcomere to which the plus ends of actin filaments are attached.

terms.name: Z-band streaming
terms.definition: Streaming or smearing of the Z band, which is then no longer confined to a narrow zone which bisects the I band. The Z disk may extend across the I band or the entire sarcomere in a zigzag manner. Focal thickening, smudging, and blurring of the Z band takes place concurrently. Myofibrillar disorganization is a frequent but not invariable accompanying change.

terms.name: Tubulointerstitial bacterial infiltration
terms.definition: Tubulointerstitial infiltration of bacteria identified on routine and/or special (Brown-Hopps) stains.

terms.name: Tubulointerstitial fungal infiltration
terms.definition: Tubulointerstitial infiltration of yeast or hyphal-microrganisms identified on routine and/or special (PAS, silver) stains.

terms.name: Simple ear
terms.definition: The pinna has fewer folds and grooves than usual.

terms.name: Reflex seizure
terms.definition: Seizures precipitated by exogenous stimuli.

terms.name: Eating-induced seizure
terms.definition: A seizure precipitated by aspects of anticipating food, eating itself, or the post-prandial period.

terms.name: Hot water-induced seizure
terms.definition: A seizure precipitated by pouring cupfuls of very hot water (40 to 50 degrees Celsius) in rapid succession over the head. Bathing in this manner is the most common trigger.

terms.name: Praxis-induced seizure
terms.definition: A seizure precipitated by complex, cognition-guided tasks often involving visuomotor coordination and decision-making.

terms.name: Proprioceptive-induced seizure
terms.definition: A seizure precipitated by movement or a change in posture.

terms.name: Reading-induced seizure
terms.definition: A seizure precipitated by reading.

terms.name: Somatosensory-induced seizure
terms.definition: A somatosensory reflex seizure is a seizure precipitated by somatic stimulation of a specific part of the body in the absence of startle or surprise.

terms.name: Startle-induced seizure
terms.definition: Startle-induced seizures are triggered by multiple and non-specific stimuli (auditory, somatosensory, and rarely visual) and are characterized by their sudden unexpected nature. Sudden noise rather than pure sound is the most effective acoustic stimulus.

terms.name: Thinking-induced seizure
terms.definition: Seizures induced by thinking and decision-making.

terms.name: Visually-induced seizure
terms.definition: Seizures evoked by visual stimuli. This includes clinical seizures induced by strobe lighting, television and other screens, flickering environmental lighting and self-induction by causing a strobe effect.

terms.name: Focal aware motor seizure
terms.name_zh: 局灶清醒性运动性发作
terms.definition: A type of focal motor seizure in which awareness is retained throughout the seizure.

terms.name: Focal aware atonic seizure
terms.name_zh: 局灶性有意识失张力发作
terms.definition: A type of focal atonic seizure during which awareness is fully retained throughout.

terms.name: Motor seizure
terms.definition: A motor seizure is a type of seizure that is characterized at onset by involvement of the skeletal musculature. The motor event could consist of an increase (positive) or decrease (negative) in muscle contraction to produce a movement.

terms.name: Focal atonic seizure
terms.definition: A focal seizure characterized at onset by sudden loss or diminution of muscle tone without apparent preceding myoclonic or tonic activity, typically lasting more than 500 ms but less than 2 seconds. It may involve the head, trunk, jaw or limb musculature.

terms.name: Clonic seizure
terms.definition: A clonic seizure is a type of motor seizure characterized by sustained rhythmic jerking, that is regularly repetitive.

terms.name: Hypohomocysteinemia
terms.definition: A decreased concentration of homocysteine in the blood.

terms.name: Dermal sinus tract
terms.definition: A dermal sinus tract is an abnormality present at birth over the dorsal midline where an abnormal epithelialized connection from the skin tracks inwards towards the spine, most commonly seen in the lumbosacral region.

terms.name: Mammary duct ectasia
terms.definition: A non-proliferative inflammatory disorder of the large duct (milk duct) of the breast; as such, it affects nipple and areola complex. The condition is characterized by focal dilatation of the lactiferous duct system is due to endoluminal changes, as well as the loss of duct wall elastin, leading to abnormally dilated and tortuous lactiferous ducts with associated periductal inflammation and fibrosis. Mammary duct ectasia may present with nipple discharge or palpable mass.

terms.name: Breast abscess
terms.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the breast.

terms.name: Nipple tenderness
terms.definition: Pain or discomfort produced by touching the nipple.

terms.name: Floating gallbladder
terms.definition: An abnormal configuration in which the gallbladder is pedunculated, hanging free of the liver, and attached only by the cystic mesentery,

terms.name: Biospecimen phenotypic feature
terms.definition: A phenotypic abnormality obvserved in a biospecimen such as a biopsy or an extirpated tumor or tissue.

terms.name: Abnormal lymph-node biospecimen
terms.definition: Any abnormal phenotypic feature observed in a biospecimen derived from a lymph node, generally obtained by lymph node biopsy (removal of lymph node tissue for microscopic examination).

terms.name: Abnormal lymph-node tissue architecture
terms.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of the architecture of the tissue of a lymph node.

terms.name: Abnormal lymph-node cellular finding
terms.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality within cells located in a lymph node.

terms.name: Abnormal Q wave
terms.definition: An anomaly of the Q wave of the electrocardiogram.

terms.name: Abnormal lymph-node cellular antigen expression
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结细胞抗原表达异常
terms.definition: Abnormal expression of an antigen (marker) by cells located in a lymph node.

terms.name: Altered lymph-node tissue architecture
terms.definition: An alteration that affects multiple components of the architecture of a lymph node.

terms.name: Effaced lymph-node architecture
terms.definition: Effacement of architecture typically refers to a cellular infiltrate destroying the normal follicular architecture of a lymph node. This effacement may result in sheets of cells that do not form clear architecture (seen in many lymphomas) or may lead to replacement of the normal architecture by atypical architecture, for example effacement of normal lymph node architecture (including normal follicles and patent lymph node sinuses) by many abnormal follicles in follicular lymphoma.

terms.name: Vaguely nodular lymph-node architecture
terms.definition: In contrast to normal lymph node architecture or that of follicular lymphoma, where follicles are typically distinct and readily identifiable on H&E stained biopsy sections, the cells within an atypical lymph node may show what appear to groups of cells forming vague nodules but not forming clear follicles.

terms.name: Lymph-node capsular invasion by lymphocytes
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结被膜淋巴细胞侵犯
terms.definition: Migration of substantial numbers of lymphocytes into the capsule of a lymph node.

terms.name: Lymph-node extracapsular extension by lymph-node lymphocytes
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结淋巴细胞被膜外延伸
terms.definition: Migration of lymphocytes into the soft tissues surrounding the lymph node.

terms.name: Increased lymph-node epithelioid histiocyte count
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结上皮样组织细胞计数升高
terms.definition: Number of epithelioid histiocytes (histiocytes are tissue-resident macrophages) located within a lymph node above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Scattered lymph node individual epithelioid histiocytes
terms.definition: Many individual (not clustered) epithelioid histiocytes throughout at least part of a lymph node.

terms.name: Clustered lymph node epithelioid histiocytes
terms.name_zh: 簇状淋巴结上皮样组织细胞
terms.definition: Formation of clusters (group of cells positioned near each other) of epithelioid histiocytes within a lymph node.

terms.name: Abnormal lymph-node follicle architecture
terms.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of the architecture of follicles of a lymph node.

terms.name: Floral-pattern lymph node follicles
terms.definition: Atypical lymph node follicles that have mantle zone cells invaginating/infiltrating into the follicle centers, which is said to confer a flower-like appearance.

terms.name: Colonization of follicles by lymphoma cells
terms.definition: In contrast to follicular lymphoma, which typically is a lymphoma that forms follicles or potentially completely replaces normal follicles, some lymphomas (most commonly marginal zone lymphoma) can infiltrate normal follicles so both normal lymphocytes and the infiltrating lymphoma cells are present. This is called colonization of follicles by the lymphoma cells.

terms.name: Crowded lymph-node follicles
terms.definition: Reduction in the average distance between adjacent lymph node follicles.

terms.name: Lymph-node follicular lysis
terms.definition: An abnormal morphology of hyperplastic lymph node follicles characterized by distortion of the follicular architecture by tongues and clusters of dark blue mantle cells impinging on and invading the reactive germinal center (Mostly T cells and mantle-zone B cells).

terms.name: Non-polarized lymph node germinal centers
terms.definition: A loss of the typical polarization of the architecture of a lymph node germinal center.

terms.name: Irregularly shaped lymph node germinal centers
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结生发中心形态不规则
terms.definition: A deviation from the typically fairly round or oval form of a lymph node germinal center.

terms.name: Abnormal lymph-node marginal or mantle zone morphology
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结边缘区或套区形态异常
terms.definition: An abnormality of the structure of the mantle or marginal zone of a lymph node.

terms.name: Abnormal lymph node marginal zone morphology
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结边缘区形态异常

terms.name: Abnormal lymph node mantle zone morphology
Abnormal bursal fluid morphology
terms.definition: An anomaly of the synovial-like fluid found within a bursa, which is a small, closed sac lined by synovial membrane that reduces friction between tissues such as tendons, muscles, ligaments, and bones.

terms.name: Lymph node with expanded mantle zones
synonyms: Germinal centers with expanded mantle zones
Germinal centres with expanded mantle zones
terms.definition: Enlargement of the typical outer ring of small lymphocytes (mantle zone) surrounding a germinal center of a lymph node.

terms.name: Lymph node with poorly defined germinal center borders
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结生发中心边界不清
terms.definition: Reduced demarcation of the border between germinal centers and mantle zones. This border is typically seen as a crisp line on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained lymph node sections.

terms.name: Abnormal lymph-node germinal center morphology
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结生发中心形态异常
terms.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of germinal centers of a lymph node.

terms.name: Elevated bursal fluid leukocyte count
terms.definition: The count of leukocytes per unit volume in a bursa aspirate specimen is above the uppper limit of normal.

terms.name: Mantle zone pattern
terms.definition: This refers to an architectural pattern of infiltration where atypical lymphocytes surround germinal centers, often expanding the mantle zones but without effacing architecture.

terms.name: Germinal centers with absent marginal zones
Decreased biparietal diameter
terms.definition: Fetal head width measurement, taken between the outer edge of the proximal parietal bone and the inner edge of the distal parietal bone, below the lower limit of normal, usually taken to be two standard deviations below the norm or above the 3rd percentile for the gestational age.

terms.name: Increased biparietal diameter
terms.definition: Fetal head width measurement, taken between the outer edge of the proximal parietal bone and the inner edge of the distal parietal bone, above the upper limit of normal, usually taken to be two standard deviations above the norm or above the 97th percentile for the gestational age.

terms.name: Poorly defined primary lymph-node follicles
terms.definition: Lack of the typical easily recognized delineation of primary follicles within lymph nodes.

terms.name: Progressive transformation of germinal centers
terms.definition: This is a condition sometimes seen in a subset of germinal centers of reactive lymph nodes where germinal centers become enlarged and infiltrated by benign mantle zone cells and some T cells.

terms.name: Absent germinal center tingible body macrophages
terms.name_zh: 生发中心可染小体巨噬细胞缺如
terms.definition: Lack of observable tingible body macrophages (TBMs) in germinal centers (GCs) of secondary lymphoid follicles. TBMs represent unique, large phagocytic cells that reside and are a subset of mononuclear phagocytes.

terms.name: Lack of germinal center mitotic figures
terms.name_zh: 生发中心核分裂象缺失
terms.definition: Absence of extreme paucity of mitotic figures in a lymph node germinal center.

terms.name: Non-polarized mantle zones
terms.definition: Lack of the typical polarization of the outer ring of small lymphocytes (mantle zone) surrounding a germinal center of a lymph node.

terms.name: Hyalinized lymph-node vessels
terms.definition: Hyalinized means to become clear/translucent such as collagen becoming more pale staining (collagen is typically quite eosinophilic, meaning attracted to the pink/red dye eosin); however, with regard to vessels in the lymph node, hyalinization is often used to describe vessel walls that appear markedly thickened or surrounded by eosinophilic material such as collagen, not necessarily translucent appearing.

terms.name: Lymph-node follicular sclerosis
terms.definition: Collagen deposition, typically with decreased cellularity, within lymph-node follicles.

terms.name: Compressed lymph-node sinuses
terms.definition: Loss of the typical patency (openness) of lymph node sinuses.

terms.name: Lymph-node proliferation centers
terms.definition: Proliferation centers are a finding specific to chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma where regions (typically relatively small, comparable to the size of a lymph node follicle) appear more pale on H&E stained sections (though they may become enlarged to merge together). These areas contain increased numbers of enlarged lymphoma cells with nucleoli (prolymphocytes and paraimmunoblasts) and show a higher proliferation rate (readily visualized with a Ki-67 immunohistochemical stain) than surrounding lymphoma cells. They can be mistaken as vague follicle formation and are therefore sometimes referred to as pseudofollicles.

terms.name: Cytologic atypia in mantle cells
terms.definition: Lymphocytes in the mantle zones of lymph node secondary follicles show cellular atypia such as enlarged size, increased cytoplasm, atypical distribution of chromatin, or irregular nuclear contours.

terms.name: Increased lymph-node eosinophils
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结嗜酸性粒细胞增多
terms.definition: Eosinophils count within a lymph node above normal limits.

terms.name: Increased lymph-node plasma cells
terms.definition: Number of plasma cells per lymph node above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: High lymph node non-germinal center mitotic activity
terms.name_zh: 高淋巴结非生发中心有丝分裂活性
terms.definition: Increased numbers of mitotic figures outside of germinal centers.

terms.name: Lymph-node lymphocyte monocytoid morphology
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结淋巴细胞单核细胞样形态
terms.definition: Lymphocytes that show morphologic features resembling monocytes, such as increased cytoplasm and slightly enlarged nuclei that are more irregular than most lymph node lymphocytes.

terms.name: Reduced lymph node lymphocyte morphological variability
terms.definition: Decreased morphological variability of lymph node lymphocytes as compared to the typically somewhat heterogeneous morphology of populations of benign lymph node lymphocytes.

terms.name: Increased large lymphocytes in lymph node
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结大淋巴细胞增多
terms.definition: An increased number of large lymphocytes within a lymph node compared to a normal non-reactive lymph node.

terms.name: Hodgkin morphology cells
terms.definition: Hodgkin cells are typically large and often show very large nucleoli and sometimes binucleation or multinucleation. Reed-Sternberg cells are a type of Hodgkin cell that is binucleated with very large nucleoli that stains slightly red on H&E stained sections (often said to mimic owl eyes). Other Hodgkin cell morphologies include cells that are dying with dark basophilic (blue) nuclei that appear somewhat smudged (mummified cells) and cells with a large space around or adjacent to the nuclei and retracted cytoplasm after tissue fixation (lacunar cells). Hodgkin cells are characteristic of Hodgkin lymphoma, however several non-Hodgkin lymphomas and noN-neoplastic conditions are known to sometimes show a few similar morphology cells.

terms.name: Abnormal lymph-node lymphoctye nuclear morphology
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结淋巴细胞核形态异常

terms.name: Irregular lymph-node lymphocyte nuclei
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结淋巴细胞核不规则
terms.definition: Lymph node lymphocyte nuclei that are more irregular than the typical round to slightly oval shapes of the majority of lymph node lymphocytes.

terms.name: Lymph-node Dutcher bodies
terms.definition: Dutcher bodies are collections of immunoglobulin protein that overlie or invaginate into the nucleus of plasma cells. These nuclear pseudoinclusions can occasionally be seen in reactive states and may be increased in specific neoplastic conditions.

terms.name: Finely dispersed lymph node lymphocyte chromatin
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结淋巴细胞染色质细颗粒状分散
terms.definition: Nuclei of lymphocytes with less dense, evenly distributed chromatin than the normal densely packed, often clumped chromatin of mature lymphocytes.

terms.name: Abnormal lymph-node lymphocyte chromatin
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结淋巴细胞染色质异常
terms.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of the chromatin (complex of DNA and protein which comprises chromosomes) of lymphocytes that are located within a lymph node.

terms.name: Clumping of lymph node lymphocyte chromatin
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结淋巴细胞染色质聚集
terms.definition: Nuclei of lymphocytes show multiple small densely packed areas of chromatin that appear as relatively evenly spaced clumps of basophilic (blue) staining within the nuclei on Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained sections.

terms.name: Abnormal lymph-node lymphocyte cytoplasm morphology
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结淋巴细胞胞质形态异常
terms.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of the cytoplasm (material located within the cell membrane but excluding the nucleus) of lymphocytes that are located within a lymph node.

terms.name: Decreased lymph node lymphocyte cytoplasm
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结淋巴细胞胞质减少
terms.definition: The amount of cytoplasm in lymphocytes is even less than the relatively little cytoplasm found in the majority of lymphocytes within lymph nodes.

terms.name: Increased lymph node lymphocyte cytoplasm
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结淋巴细胞胞质增多
terms.definition: Increased amount of cytoplasm compared to the majority of lymphocytes in a benign lymph node.

terms.name: Abnormal level of lymph-node cellular CD19 expression
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结细胞CD19表达水平异常
terms.definition: Detection of an abnormal level of CD19 on the cell(s) of interest in a lymph node with the use of anti-CD19 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).

terms.name: Abnormal lymph-node cellular B-cell marker expression
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结细胞B细胞标志物表达异常
terms.definition: Abnormal expression of an antigen (marker) that is normally expressed by B lymphocytes.

terms.name: Abnormal level of lymph-node cellular CD20 expression
terms.name_zh: 淋巴结细胞CD20表达水平异常
terms.definition: Detection of abnormal levels of CD20 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD20 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).

terms.name: CD79a expression
terms.definition: Detection of the presence of CD79a on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD79a antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).

terms.name: Increased lymph-node cellular CD20 expression
terms.definition: Increased levels of CD20 expression compared to normal B cells.

terms.name: Decreased lymph-node cellular CD20 expression
terms.definition: Decreased levels of CD20 expression compared to normal B cells.

terms.name: Decreased lymph-node cellular CD19 expression
terms.definition: Decreased levels of CD19 expression compared to normal B cells.

terms.name: Increased lymph-node cellular CD19 expression
terms.definition: Increased levels of CD19 expression compared to normal B cells.

terms.name: PAX5 expression
terms.definition: Detection of the presence of PAX5 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-PAX5 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry).

terms.name: Germinal center B-lymphocyte BCL2 expression
terms.name_zh: 生发中心B淋巴细胞BCL2表达
terms.definition: Positive staining for BCL2 apoptosis regulator protein in lymph-node germinal center B cells.

terms.name: Abnormal occipitofrontal diameter
terms.definition: Abnormal occipitofrontal diameter (OFD) refers to a fetal head width measurement, taken between the root of the nose to the most prominent part of the occiput on an ultrasound image that lies outside the expected range for a given gestational age. The expected range typically falls between the 3rd percentile (or more than 2 standard deviations below the mean) and the 97th percentile (or more than 2 standard deviations above the mean).

terms.name: Decreased occipitofrontal diameter
terms.definition: Occipitofrontal diameter, measured with fetal sonography, below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Increased occipitofrontal diameter
terms.definition: Occipitofrontal diameter, measured with fetal sonography, above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal elbow morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the joint that connects the upper and the lower arm.

terms.name: Abnormal elbow physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the joint that connects the upper and the lower arm.

terms.name: Restrictive eating
terms.definition: A behavioral pattern characterized by a deliberate and sustained limitation of food intake, often involving avoidance of certain foods, restriction of portion size, or prolonged fasting, resulting in reduced energy or nutrient consumption relative to physiological needs.

terms.name: Abnormal fetal abdominal circumference
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal range of the fetal abdominal circumference, which is typically measured sonographically in a transverse view using the outer borders of the skin line at the plane where the fetal stomach, umbilical vein and portal sinus is visible. Abnormal fetal abdominal circumference is defined as less than the 10th or greater than the 90th percentile for gestational age.

terms.name: Increased fetal abdominal circumference
terms.definition: The distance around the abdomen of a fetus, generally as measured by prenatal sonography, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal fetal head circumference
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal range of the fetal head circumference, which is typically measured sonographically in the axial plane at the level of the thalami and cavum septic pellucidi, using the outer border of the bony calvarium. Abnormal fetal head circumference is defined as less than the thrid percentile or 2 standard deviations below the mean or greater than the 97the percentile or 2 standard deviations above the mean.

terms.name: Decreased fetal head circumference
terms.definition: Fetal head circumference less than the third percentile or 2 standard deviations below the mean.

terms.name: Increased fetal head circumference
terms.definition: Fetal head circumference above the 97th percentile or 2 standard deviations above the mean.

terms.name: Increased anteroposterior lens thickness
terms.definition: Increase in the anteroposterior (axial) dimension of the crystalline lens relative to the overall length of the globe.

terms.name: Ankle instability
terms.definition: Failure of ligamentous and muscular structures of the ankle to maintain normal joint alignment during movement, resulting in excessive motion that causes manifestations such as subjective or objective feeling of clunking/clicking in the ankle with movement, ankle 'giving way' or sensation of ankle dislocating.

terms.name: Retinal phlebitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of retinal venules as manifested by perivascular sheathing or cuffing, vascular leakage and/or occlusion.

terms.name: Ophthalmic artery hypoperfusion
terms.definition: Chronic hypoperfusion due to large vessel disease e.g. carotid artery stenosis, Takayasu disease. Typically presents dilated veins, low retinal arterial pressure, peripheral microaneurysms, ocular hypotension and may lead to iris neovascularisation. Patients may have postural hypotension.

terms.name: Focal hyperpigmented area associated with subretinal scar tissue
terms.name_zh: 伴视网膜下瘢痕组织的局灶性色素沉着区
terms.definition: Localized hyperpigmented areas, in the context of subretinal scar tissue, as seen after subretinal neovascularisation.

terms.name: Discrete fundus hypopigmentation
terms.definition: Well-demarcated areas of the fundus, with relative reduction in pigment, with respect to the rest of the fundus.

terms.name: Macular pseudohole
terms.definition: A macular pseudohole is a partial-thickness gap in a normal-thickness fovea, located in the center of the macula.

terms.name: Lamellar macular hole
terms.definition: A lamellar macular hole is a structural abnormality of the macula, characterized by a partial-thickness gap in a thinner fovea, located in the center of the macula.

terms.name: Middle cerebral artery berry aneurysm
terms.name_zh: 大脑中动脉浆果样动脉瘤
terms.definition: A small, sac-like aneurysm (outpouching) of the middle cerebral artery (MCA). MCA berry aneurysms may occur at the MCA bifurcation, on the anterior communicant artery, the anterior cerebral artery, the internal carotid artery, or on the posterior communicant artery.

terms.name: Abnormal abdominal aorta branch artery morphology
terms.name_zh: 腹主动脉分支形态异常
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of an artery that originates from the abdominal aorta.

terms.name: Posterior humeral circumflex artery occlusion
terms.definition: Blockage of the posterior circumflex humeral artery (PCHA), which arises from the third part of the axillary artery and supplies the shoulder joint and a number of its associated muscles. The lesion can be ascertained angiographically, whereby dye is injected both with patient's humerus at the side of the body and again with shoulder held in abduction and external rotation. Test is positive if there is evidence of PCHA occlusion with arm in abduction and external rotation but artery is patent when arm is held at the side.

terms.name: Scapulothoracic incongruity
terms.definition: A lack of smooth, physiological alignment or movement between the scapula (shoulder blade) and the posterior thoracic wall (the rib cage). The scapulothoracic joint is unique, as it lacks true synovial articulation and is dynamically controlled through surrounding muscular contractions. The scapula glides on the posterior thorax covered with muscle layers rather than a cartilaginous surface. This feature can be ascertained by radiography or CT scan of the scapula showing incongruity of the scapulothoracic space.

terms.name: Latissimus dorsi rupture
terms.definition: A tear of the latissimus dorsi (LD). Injury to the LD can occur at various locations, from the tendon to the muscle belly. The LD is a broad, flat muscle occupying most of the lower posterior thorax. The muscle's primary function is to move the upper extremity, but it is also considered an accessory muscle of respiration.

terms.name: Distal clavicular osteolysis
terms.definition: Degeneration and resorption of the distal part of the clavicle near the acromioclavicular (AC) joint. Distal clavicular osteolysis (DCO) is an atypical injury occurring most often in athletes and weight lifters, specifically those who perform repetitive overhead movements. DCO results from repetitive excess load to the AC joint, typically through horizontal adduction, adduction, internal rotation, and forward/lateral flexion of the shoulder, such as bench pressing or overhead lifting. Imaging (AP clavicle and/or Zanca view of the AC joint) of DCO often demonstrates microcysts, loss of subchondral bone detail, and osteolysis of the distal clavicle.

terms.name: Abnormal breast-tissue biospecimen
terms.name_zh: 乳腺组织生物标本异常
terms.definition: Any abnormal phenotypic feature observed in a biospecimen derived from breast tissue.

terms.name: Abnormal breast-tissue cellular antigen expression
terms.name_zh: 乳腺组织细胞抗原表达异常
terms.definition: Abnormal expression of an antigen (marker) by cells located in breast tissue.

terms.name: Increased breast-tissue HER2 expression
terms.definition: Increased level of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) expression in breast tissue.

terms.name: Increased breast-tissue estrogen receptor expression
terms.name_zh: 乳腺组织雌激素受体表达升高
terms.definition: Increased level of estrogen receptor expression in breast tissue.

terms.name: Increased breast-tissue progesterone receptor expression
terms.name_zh: 乳腺组织孕激素受体表达升高

terms.name: Abnormal breast-tissue cellular finding
terms.name_zh: 乳腺组织细胞检查结果异常
terms.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality within cells located in breast tissue.

terms.name: Mammary ductal epithelial cell hyperplasia
terms.name_zh: 乳腺导管上皮细胞增生
terms.definition: Abnormal (increased) proliferation of epithelial cells in a mammary duct. Intraductal papilloma is a benign tumor found within breast ducts. The abnormal proliferation of ductal epithelial cells causes growth. A solitary intraductal papilloma is usually found centrally posterior to the nipple, affecting the central duct.

terms.name: Mammary ductal apocrine metaplasia
terms.definition: A biopsy finding in breast tissue of enlarged epithelial cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm that can show apical snouting. Metaplastic apocrine cells within the breast are similar to normal axillary, areolar and perineal apocrine cells, having apocrine secretions and identical staining reactions. One of the reasons, however, that these are often not regarded as normal components is that examples of gradual metaplastic change from the normal cuboidal epithelium can be seen and cells with intermediate features can also be discerned on careful examination, suggesting that these are true metaplasia.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating inorganic anion concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环无机阴离子浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of inorganic anion in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Blue-field entoptic phenomenon
terms.definition: Unremitting, positive visual phenomena, present in the entire visual field and characterized by uncountable tiny flickering dots interposed between the person's vision and the background. The dots are said to resemble static and are typically black and white but can also be colored, flashing, or transparent. In addition to the static, or snow, patients can experience additional visual symptoms of either direct neurological origin, such as palinopsia, photophobia, and nyctalopia (i.e., impaired night vision), or that arise from the optic apparatus.

terms.name: Phosphene
terms.definition: A phosphene is the perception of light without light actually entering the eye, for instance caused by pressure applied to the closed eyes.

terms.name: Palinopsia
terms.definition: Palinopsia refers to visual images that persist despite removal of the eliciting object; plainopsia presents as persistent afterimages of stationary objects or trailing of images behind moving objects.

terms.name: Positive scapular compression test
terms.definition: A type of function test in which the examiner uses one hand to apply a posterior to anterior force is directly over the scapula and the anterior chest wall is stabilized with the other hand. Test is positive if this scapular stabilization allows for increased shoulder flexion compared to when no stabilization is applied.

terms.name: Pectoralis major tear
terms.definition: Injury with partial or complete tear of the pectoralis major tendon, muscle, or myotendinous junction.

terms.name: Increased urinary 18-oxocortisol level
terms.name_zh: 尿18-氧代皮质醇水平升高
terms.definition: The amount of 18-oxocortisol in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Increased urinary 18-hydroxycortisol level
terms.definition: The amount of 18-hydroxycortisol in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Malignant melanotic nerve sheath tumor
terms.definition: Malignant melanotic nerve sheath tumors (MMNSTs) are uncommon pigmented tumors of Schwann cell origin, most often found along the spinal nerves. MMNSTs were formerly known as melanotic schwannoma. Although MMNSTs can occur along cranial nerves, they tend to grow along the dorsal spinal nerve roots, and patients often present with indolent pain, weakness, or paresthesia along a corresponding dermatome. On imaging, spinal MMNSTs generally appear similar to the appearance presented in the current case: intradural, extramedullary tumors. In the spine, the tumors typically grow along spinal nerve roots, sometimes assuming a dumbbell configuration if they extend through a foramen. Tumors demonstrate enhancement on CT and are FDG-avid on PET.

terms.name: Increased mucosal-associated invariant T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: 黏膜相关恒定T细胞比例升高
terms.definition: An increased proportion of mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells among peripheral blood T lymphocytes, above the upper reference limit for age. MAIT cells are innate-like T cells that recognise riboflavin metabolite antigens presented by MR1.

terms.name: Abnormal mucosal-associated invariant T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: 黏膜相关恒定T细胞比例异常
terms.definition: An increased or decreased proportion of mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells among peripheral blood T lymphocytes, above the upper reference limit for age. MAIT cells are innate-like T cells that recognise riboflavin metabolite antigens presented by MR1.

terms.name: Unusual pharyngitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection of the pharynx, as manifested by recurrent or severe episodes of pharyngitis.

terms.name: Abnormal mental imagery
terms.definition: A deviation from the typical ability to voluntarily generate, maintain, or experience mental images representing sensory properties of objects or events without a direct external stimulus.

terms.name: Aphantasia
terms.definition: Absence or near-absence of voluntary visual mental imagery, such that an individual is unable to intentionally generate visual images in the mind.

terms.name: Hyperphantasia
terms.definition: Exceptionally vivid voluntary visual mental imagery, in which internally generated images are experienced as vivid, despite intact reality testing and the absence of sensory hallucinations.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating monosaccharide concentration
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of a monosaccharide in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating disaccharide concentration
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of a disaccharide in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating sugar alcohol concentration
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of a sugar alcohol in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating vitamin concentration
terms.definition: The concentration of one or more vitamins is outside the reference range.

terms.name: Abnormal CSF folate concentration
terms.definition: The concentration of folate or one of its metabolites in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is outside the limits of normal.

terms.name: Lisfranc injury
terms.definition: Lisfranc injuries refer to bony or ligamentous compromise of the tarsometatarsal and intercuneiform joint complex and include a spectrum of injuries ranging from a stable, partial sprain to a grossly displaced and unstable fracture or fracture-dislocation of the midfoot. Foot x-ray shows either widening of the space between the 1st and 2nd metatarsal to over 2mm at the base, dorsal displacement of the base of the 1st or 2nd metatarsal, discontinuity of a line drawn from the medial base of the 2nd metatarsal to the medial side of the medial cuneiform, irregularity between the medial side of the 5th metatarsal base and the medial side of the cuboid, or disruption of the line connecting the medial aspect of the navicular bone to the medial cuneiform.

terms.name: Abnormal cecum morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the cecum, which is the proximal blind pouch of the ascending colon, is located at the ileocecal junction in the right iliac fossa.

terms.name: Flail chest
terms.definition: Flail chest is a physical exam finding that can be present in the setting of chest wall trauma or injury. When multiple adjacent ribs are fractured in 2 or more places, this can create a focal \

terms.name: Hallux rigidus
terms.definition: Osteoarthritis of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the first toe.

terms.name: Thickening of glomerular capillary wall
terms.definition: Widening of the wall of capillary blood vessels in the glomerulus. This feature may be produced by deposits and other changes affecting either subepithelial and subendothelial regions or the glomerular basement membrane itself.

terms.name: Abnormal glomerular capillary morphology
terms.name_zh: 肾小球毛细血管形态异常
synonyms: Abnormalities of the glomerular capillary wall
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the capillary blood vessels in the renal glomerulus.

terms.name: Ectopic fovea
terms.definition: An abnormal anatomic position of the fovea.

terms.name: Tracheal tug on inspiration
terms.definition: Downward movement of the trachea during inspiration due to downward traction on the tracheobronchial tree.

terms.name: Forward slanting upper incisors
terms.definition: The upper incisors deviate from the normal angle of being roughly parallel to the surface of the face and instead slant outwards.

terms.name: Foveal atrophy
terms.definition: A nonspecific term denoting wasting, especially as a result of degeneration, of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and neurosensory retinal cells in the fovea.

terms.name: Pyriform aperture stenosis
terms.definition: Narrowing of the anterior nasal aperture (piriform or pyriform aperture), which is a pear-shaped opening in the skull that forms the bony inlet of the nose.

terms.name: Status cribrosum
terms.definition: Diffusely widened perivascular spaces in the basal ganglia, affecting especially the corpus striatum. Status cribrosum is usually symmetrical, with the perivascular spaces showing CSF signal and without diffusion restriction. The word cribriform means sievelike, with multiple perforations.

terms.name: Decerebrate rigidity
terms.definition: A type of rigidity that is manifested by an exaggerated extensor posture of all extremities.

terms.name: Subcutaneous spheroids
terms.definition: Small, hard cyst-like nodules, freely moveable in the subcutis over the bony prominences of the legs and arms, which have an outer calcified layer with a translucent core on x-ray.

terms.name: Abnormal capillary morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the tiny blood vessels that connect arterioles with venules and whose walls act as semipermeable membranes that mediate the diffusion of fluids and gases between the blood circulation and body tissues.

terms.name: Capillary fragility
terms.definition: Reduced resistance to rupture of capillary blood vessels. Capillary fragility may manifest as a bleeding diathesis with spontaneous ecchymoses (bruises).

terms.name: Abnormal capillary physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the tiny blood vessels that connect arterioles with venules and whose walls act as semipermeable membranes that mediate the diffusion of fluids and gases between the blood circulation and body tissues.

terms.name: Arterial rupture
terms.definition: Sudden breakage of an artery leading to leakage of blood from the circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating prostate-specific antigen concentration
terms.name_zh: 血前列腺特异性抗原浓度升高
synonyms: Elevated prostate-specific antigen level in blood
Increased prostate-specific antigen level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of prostate-specific antigen in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal erythrocyte sedimentation rate
terms.definition: A deviation from normal range of the erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), a test that measures the distance that erythrocytes have fallen after one hour in a vertical column of anticoagulated blood under the influence of gravity. The ESR is a nonspecific finding. An elevation may indicate inflammation or may be caused by any condition that elevates fibrinogen. A decreased ESR may be seen in polycythemia or in certain blood diseases in which red blood cells have an irregular or smaller shape that causes slower settling.

terms.name: Decreased erythrocyte sedimentation rate
terms.definition: A reduced erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). The ESR is a test that measures the distance that erythrocytes have fallen after one hour in a vertical column of anticoagulated blood under the influence of gravity. The ESR is a nonspecific finding. A decreased ESR may be seen in polycythemia or in certain blood diseases in which red blood cells have an irregular or smaller shape that causes slower settling.

terms.name: Rectal atresia
terms.definition: A developmental defect resulting in complete obliteration of the lumen of the rectum. That is, there is an abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the rectum.

terms.name: Megarectum
terms.definition: An abnormal dilation of the rectum. There is a large filled rectum as a result of underlying innervation or muscular abnormalities, which remains after disimpaction of the rectum.

terms.name: Rectovestibular fistula
terms.definition: A congenital malformation characterized by an abnormal connection (fistula) between the rectum and the vulval vestibule, at the lower aspect of the vaginal opening.

terms.name: H-type rectovestibular fistula
terms.definition: Rectovestibular fistula with a normal anus is known as H-type fistula or double termination of the alimentary tract.

terms.name: Osteoma cutis
terms.definition: The term osteoma refers to the anomalous presence of ossification (bone formation) in the interior of the dermis or epidermis. The dermal or subcutaneous bone formation presents as stony hard nodules. The osteomata appear as irregular, hardened small nodules that are well circumscribed and generally of the same color as the skin.

terms.name: Abnormal enteric nervous system morphology
synonyms: Abnormality of enteric nervous system morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of nerves of the enteric nervous system.

terms.name: Enteric neuronal degeneration
terms.definition: Deterioration of enteric neurons with impairment of enteric neuronal structure. Typical neuropathological findings include qualitative (e.g., neuronal swelling, intranuclear inclusions, axonal degeneration) and quantitative (e.g., reduction in the number of neurons) abnormalities of the enteric neurons.

terms.name: Abnormality of digestive system physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the digestive system.

terms.name: Abnormal digestive system morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the digestive system.

terms.name: Abnormal morphology of erythroid progenitor cell
terms.definition: Abnormal form of the progenitor cells committed to the erythroid lineage.

terms.name: Abnormal proerythroblast morphology
terms.definition: Anomalous form of the proerythroblast, i.e., the immature, nucleated erythrocyte occupying the stage of erythropoeisis that follows formation of erythroid progenitor cells. This cell is CD71-positive, has both a nucleus and a nucleolus, and lacks hematopoeitic lineage markers.

terms.name: Type I radial ray deficiency
terms.definition: A type of radial ray deficiency characterized by short distal radius. The distal radial epiphysis is present but delayed in appearance. The growth of the distal radial epiphysis is decreased causing a normal appearing but short radius. There is little radial deviation of the hand due to adequate radial carpal support. The radius has normal proximal epiphyseal growth. Thumb hypoplasia is almost always present.

terms.name: Hypothalamic gliosis
terms.definition: Focal proliferation of glial cells in the hypothalamus.

terms.name: Intratesticular abscess
terms.definition: A collection of pus within a testicle. Ultrasonographic features include shaggy, irregular walls, intratesticular location, low-level internal echoes, and occasionally, hypervascular margins.

terms.name: Basal ganglia edema
terms.definition: Swelling within the basal ganglia due to the accumulation of fluid.

terms.name: Thalamic edema
terms.definition: Swelling within the thalamus due to the accumulation of fluid.

terms.name: Thalamic calcification
terms.definition: Calcium deposition in the thalamus.

terms.name: Abnormality of mesenteric lymph nodes
terms.definition: A morphological anomaly of lymph nodes in the mesenteric root or throughout the mesentery.

terms.name: Enlarged mesenteric lymph node
terms.definition: Increase in size of one or more mesenteric lymph nodes.

terms.name: Lung abscess
terms.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in lung parenchyma, which leads to a cavity, and after formation of bronchopulmonary fistula, can manifest as an air-fluid level inside the cavity.

terms.name: Abnormal brain lactate level by MRS
terms.name_zh: 磁共振波谱示脑乳酸水平异常
synonyms: Abnormal lactate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
terms.definition: A deviation from normal of the level of lactate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.name: Reduced brain lactate level by MRS
synonyms: Reduced brain lactate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
terms.definition: A decrease in the level of lactate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.name: Abnormal brain choline level by MRS
terms.name_zh: 磁共振波谱示脑胆碱水平异常
synonyms: Abnormal brain choline level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
terms.definition: A deviation from normal in the level of choline-containing compounds in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.name: Reduced brain choline level by MRS
synonyms: Reduced brain choline level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
terms.definition: An decrease in the level of choline-containing compounds in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.name: Abnormal brain creatine level by MRS
terms.name_zh: 磁共振波谱示脑肌酸水平异常
synonyms: Abnormal brain creatine level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

terms.name: Elevated brain creatine level by MRS
synonyms: Elevated brain creatine level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
terms.definition: An increase in the level of creatine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.name: Reduced brain creatine level by MRS
synonyms: Reduced brain creatine level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
terms.definition: A decrease in the level of creatine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.name: Abnormal brain N-acetyl aspartate level by MRS
terms.name_zh: 磁共振波谱示脑N-乙酰天门冬氨酸水平异常
synonyms: Abnormal brain N-acetyl aspartate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
terms.definition: A deviation from normal in the level of N-acetyl aspartate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.name: Elevated brain N-acetyl aspartate level by MRS
terms.name_zh: MRS示脑N-乙酰天冬氨酸水平升高
synonyms: Elevated brain N-acetyl aspartate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
terms.definition: An increase in the level of N-acetyl aspartate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.name: Type II radial ray deficiency
terms.definition: A type of radial ray deficiency characterized by a hypoplastic radius. The radius has both proximal and distal epiphyses but growth is defective in both. This type is essentially a radius in miniature. Growth of the radius proceeds at a decreased rate.

terms.name: Type III radial ray deficiency
terms.definition: A type of radial ray deficiency characterized by partial absence of the radius. The radius is partially absent. The defect can be in the proximal, middle, or distal third. All have been reported , but the most frequent is the absence of the distal one or two thirds. The hand is radially displaced . The ulna is thickened, shortened , and bowed radially, and the wrist is unsupported.

terms.name: Type IV radial ray deficiency
terms.definition: A type of radial ray deficiency characterized by total absence of the radius. This represents the most common type of radial deficiency. The hand is unsupported and is usually severely radially displaced.

terms.name: Abnormal olfactory lobe morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the olfactory lobe, the structure within the brain that receives neural input from the nasal cavity and thereby processes the sense of smell.

terms.name: Hypothalamic atrophy
terms.definition: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of hypothalamus tissue that was once present.

terms.name: Splenic abscess
terms.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the parenchyma of the spleen.

terms.name: Multifocal splenic abscess
terms.definition: Multiple abscess lesions in the spleen.

terms.name: Unifocal splenic abscess
terms.definition: Single (solitary) abscess in the spleen.

terms.name: Geophagia
terms.definition: The practice of eating earth or soil-like substrates such as clay or chalk.

terms.name: Scaphoid abdomen
terms.definition: The anterior abdominal wall is sunken and presents a concave rather than a convex contour.

terms.name: Thalamic hemorrhage
terms.definition: Bleeding in the thalamus.

terms.name: Abnormal mean corpuscular volume
terms.definition: A deviation from normal of the mean corpuscular volume, or mean cell volume (MCV) of red blood cells, usually taken to be 80 to 100 femtoliters.

terms.name: Decreased mean corpuscular volume
terms.definition: A reduction from normal of the mean corpuscular volume, or mean cell volume (MCV) of red blood cells (usually defined as an MCV below 80 femtoliters).

terms.name: Recurrent sepsis
terms.definition: Repeated bouts of sepsis, defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection.

terms.name: Incomitant strabismus
terms.definition: Strabismus in which the angle of deviation differs depending upon the direction of gaze or according to which eye is fixing, associated with: (i) defective movement of the eye, (ii) asymmetrical accommodative effort.

terms.name: Concomitant strabismus
terms.definition: Strabismus in which the angle of deviation of the squiting eye remains the same in relation to the other eye, in all directions of gaze, and whichever eye is fixing.

terms.name: Abnormal U wave
terms.definition: An anomaly of the U wave of the electrocardiogram (EKG). The U wave is a small (0.5 mm) deflection immediately following the T wave, usually in the same direction as the T wave. It is best seen in leads V2 and V3.

terms.name: U wave inversion
terms.definition: Direction of the U wave opposite to the T wave (i.e., below baseline) in leads with upright T waves.

terms.name: Prominent U wave
terms.definition: Increased amplitude of the U wave, defined as an amplitude greater than 1-2mm or 25 percent of the height of the T wave.

terms.name: Exercise-induced U wave inversion
terms.definition: U wave inversion that is induced by exercise stress testing.

terms.name: Abnormal QRS complex
terms.definition: An anomaly of the complex formed by the Q, R, and S waves, which occur in rapid succession on the electrocardiogram.

terms.name: Increased QRS voltage
terms.definition: Elevation of the voltage (height) of the QRS complex. There are several criteria in use, but the most common is the Sokolov-Lyon criterion (S wave depth in V1 + tallest R wave height in V5-V6 greater than 35 mm).

terms.name: Abnormal QRS voltage
terms.definition: Abnormal amplitude of the QRS complex of the electrocardiogram (EKG).

terms.name: Decreased QRS voltage
terms.definition: Reduced amplitude (height) of the QRS complex of the electrocardiogram (EKG), defined as amplitudes of all the QRS complexes in the limb leads are less than 5 mm or amplitudes of all the QRS complexes in the precordial leads less than 10 mm.

terms.name: Electrical alternans
terms.definition: The QRS complexes of the electrocardiogram alternate in height.

terms.name: Pancreatic abscess
terms.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the parenchyma of the pancreas.

terms.name: Orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
terms.definition: A form of hyperkeratosis characterized by thickening of the cornified layer without retained nuclei.

terms.name: Darier's sign
terms.definition: A skin change elicited by briskly rubbing the skin lesion in urticaria pigmentosa (UP), whereby the area begins to itch and becomes raised and surrounded by erythema. Unlike other forms of dermatographism, Darier's sign refers to urtication that is limited to the UP involved areas and, as in this case, spares the skin unaffected by UP.

terms.name: Abnormal cutaneous elastic fiber morphology
terms.name_zh: 皮肤弹性纤维形态异常
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the elastic fibers of the skin. Elastic fibers are the essential extracellular matrix macromolecules comprising an elastin core surrounded by a mantle of fibrillin-rich microfibrils.

terms.name: Elevated dermal desmosine content
terms.definition: An increased amount of desmosine measure in the skin. Desmosine is a cross-linking amino acid formed from lysyl residues in elastin.

terms.name: Folliculitis
terms.definition: Inflammatory cells within the wall and ostia of the hair follicle, creating a follicular-based pustule.

terms.name: Bloody diarrhea
terms.definition: Passage of many stools containing blood.

terms.name: Bloody mucoid diarrhea
terms.definition: Passage of many stools containing blood and mucus.

terms.name: Delayed recoil upon stretching of skin
terms.definition: Area of skin requiring an increased amount of time to return to its original shape after being stretched.

terms.name: Onychomadesis
terms.definition: Complete shedding (separation) of the nail from the proximal matrix. Onychomadesis is the proximal separation of the nail plate from the nail matrix due to a temporary cessation of nail growth.

terms.name: Feculent vomiting
terms.definition: Vomiting of material that is of fecal origin.

terms.name: Abnormal large intestinal mucosa morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the mucous lining of the large intestine.

terms.name: Wrist sign
terms.definition: The wrist sign is positive when the tip of the thumb covers the entire fingernail of the fifth finger when wrapped around the contralateral wrist.

terms.name: Epidermal acanthosis
synonyms: Thickening of upper layer of skin
terms.definition: Diffuse hypertrophy or thickening of the stratum spinosum of the epidermis (prickle cell layer of the skin).

terms.name: Peripapillary exudate
terms.definition: A retinal exudate in the area surrounding the optic nerve head.

terms.name: Disciform macular scar
terms.definition: A scar with a disc-like shape localized in the macula.

terms.name: Sneeze
terms.definition: A sudden violent, spasmodic, audible expiration of breath through the nose and mouth.

terms.name: Paroxysmal sneezing
terms.definition: Unprovoked explosive pathological sneezing.

terms.name: Eyelid myoclonus
terms.definition: Marked, involuntary jerking of the eyelids.

terms.name: Dysgenesis of the hypothalamus
terms.definition: Structural abnormality of the hypothalamus related to defective development.

terms.name: Dysgenesis of the thalamus
terms.definition: Structural abnormality of the thalamus related to defective development.

terms.name: Abnormal hippocampus morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the hippocampus,

terms.name: Dysgenesis of the hippocampus
terms.definition: Structural abnormality of the hippocampus related to defective development.

terms.name: Dysgenesis of the basal ganglia
terms.definition: Structural abnormality of the basal ganglia related to defective development.

terms.name: Umbilicated nodule
terms.definition: A type of skin nodule that has a small depression that resembles a navel (i.e., is umbilicated).

terms.name: Capillary malformation
terms.definition: A capillary malformation is a flat, sharply defined vascular stain of the skin. It may cover a large surface area or it may be scattered and appear as little islands of color. In a capillary maformation, the predominant vessels are small, slow-flow vessels (i.e., arterioles and postcapillary venules).

terms.name: Nevus anemicus
terms.definition: A congenital skin lesion characterized by irregular hypopigmented macules that coalesce to form plaques and occur particularly on the chest. It is generally present at birth or develops in the first days of life. It is more common in females. Diagnosis is confirmed by applying gentle friction to the lesion and the surrounding skin and checking that the erythema produced in the healthy skin does not appear in the hypopigmented lesion. This pale macule becomes more conspicuous when the lesion and its surroundings are rubbed. The margin of the naevus is ill-defined and consists of an archipelago of small anemic spots.

terms.name: Nevus roseus
terms.definition: A variant of port-wine stain characterized by a pale red or even pink tone, in contrast to the darker hue of the port-wine stain. By analogy with the term port-wine stain, this variant rose-wine stain, or nevus roseus. Nevus roseus, however, cannot be definitely diagnosed until adulthood as port-wine stains are sometimes pink in children. While the natural history of port-wine stains includes hypertrophy, darkening, and nodularity, nevus roseus remains unchanged for life.

terms.name: Cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita
terms.name_zh: 先天性毛细血管扩张性大理石样皮肤
terms.definition: A congenital vascular malformation that presents as localized or generalized erythematous-telangiectatic lesions with a reticular pattern; the lesions are almost always present at birth or develop in the first days of life. Cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita (CMTC) appears as marble-like pattern (mottling) on the surface of the skin. In contrast to cutis marmorata, the marbling is more severe and always visible.

terms.name: Angioma serpentinum
terms.definition: Angioma serpiginosum consists of punctate, tightly packed telangiectatic lesions. Characteristic histopathological features are dilated and tortuous capillaries involving the uppermost part of the dermis.

terms.name: Reduced red cell pyruvate kinase level
terms.definition: Decrease in the level of pyruvate kinase (PK) within erythrocytes. PK catalyzes the reaction: ATP + pyruvate = ADP + phosphoenolpyruvate.

terms.name: Placoid macular lesion
terms.definition: Large yellow/white, sharply delineated lesion, typically of inflammatory nature, involving the macula, more specifically at the outer retinal level (RPE/photoreceptor).

terms.name: Acquired aphakia
terms.definition: Absence of the crystalline lens in the eye known to be the result of a non-congenital condition, e.g., following surgical removal of the lens for cataracts or trauma.

terms.name: Auditory sensitivity
terms.definition: Decreased tolerance to sound.

terms.name: Misophonia
terms.definition: Misophonia is characterized by strong physiological, emotional, and behavioral reactions to auditory, visual, and/or kinesthetic stimuli of different nature regardless of their physical characteristics. These misophonic responses include anger, general discomfort, disgust, anxiety, and avoidance and escape behaviors.

terms.name: Hypergranulosis
terms.definition: Hypergranulosis is an increased thickness of the stratum granulosum.

terms.name: Civatte bodies
terms.definition: Eosinophilic hyaline ovoid bodies which are often found in the subepidermal papillary regions or sometimes in the epidermis. Civatte bodies (CBs) are seen as rounded, homogenous, eosinophilic masses on routine H and E staining lying in the deeper parts of epidermis/epithelium and more frequently in dermis/connective tissue. They are known as CBs (in epithelium/epidermis), colloid bodies, or hyaline bodies (in connective tissue). They are 10-25 micrometers in diameter and situated mostly within or above the inflammatory cell infiltrate. In lichen planus, the number of necrotic keratinocytes may be so large that they are seen lying in clusters in the uppermost dermis. These bodies show a positive periodic acid Schiff reaction and are diastase resistant

terms.name: Fetal distress
terms.definition: An intrauterine state characterized by suboptimal values in the fetal heart rate, oxygenation of fetal blood, or other parameters indicative of compromise of the fetus. Signs of fetal distress include repetitive variable decelerations, fetal tachycardia or bradycardia, late decelerations, or low biophysical profile.

terms.name: Rete ridge flattening
terms.definition: Rete pegs (or ridges) are the epithelial extensions that project into the underlying connective tissue in both skin and mucous membranes. Rete ridge flattening refers to the loss of these projections so that the skin epithelium acquires a relatively flat appearance.

terms.name: Lip discoloration
terms.definition: Lightening or darkening of the lips from their usual coloring.

terms.name: Violet lip discoloration
terms.definition: An alteration of the color of the lip to take on a violet color. This term does not include cyanosis.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating reverse T3 concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环反三碘甲状腺原氨酸浓度异常
terms.definition: Concentration of reverse T3 (3,3',5'-triiodothyronine or rT3) in the blood circulation is ouside of the limits of normal.

terms.name: Sawtooth acanthosis
terms.definition: A type of epidermal acanthosis characterized by a jagged (sawtooth) appearance of the rete ridges of the epidermis.

terms.name: White streaks/specks on enamel
terms.definition: Areas of white discoloration visible on the surface of the teeth (enamel) in the form of streaks or specks.

terms.name: Fragile teeth
terms.definition: A tendency of teeth to fracture as manifested by a history of repeated fracture of the dental enamel without adequate trauma.

terms.name: White lesion of the oral mucosa
terms.definition: White lesions of the oral mucosa are generally caused by a condition that increases the thickness of the epithelium. This increases the distance to the vascular bed and thereby tends to change the usual reddish color of the oral mucosa to white. Common causes include hyperkeratosis (thickening of the keratin layer), acanthosis (thickening of the spinous cell layer), increased edema in the epithelium (leukoedema), and reduced vascularity of the underlying lamina propria. Additionally, fibrin caps or surface ulcerations and collapsed bullae can appear white.

terms.name: Oral hairy leukoplakia
terms.definition: A corrugated white lesion of the oral mucosa that usually occurs on the lateral or ventral surfaces of the tongue and may have a shaggy or frayed appearance.

terms.name: Actinic keratosis
terms.definition: A scaly, crusty lesion caused by damage from the ultraviolet radiation of the sun, with typical location on sun-exposed areas of the skin. Actinic keratosis lesions are often elevated, rough, and wartlike, and may be red, or occasionally tan, pink, or flesh-toned in color.

terms.name: Reduced intraabdominal adipose tissue
terms.definition: An abnormally reduced amount of adipose tissue in the abdominal cavity.

terms.name: Abnormal small intestinal mucosa morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the mucous lining of the small intestine.

terms.name: Decreased small intestinal mucosa lactase level
terms.name_zh: 小肠黏膜乳糖酶水平降低
terms.definition: Lactase is produced in the small intestine in humans, Lactase is a member of the beta-galactosidase family of enzymes, and hydrolyzes D-lactose to form D-galactose and D-glucose, which can be absorbed by the small intestine. There are many ways of assessing lactase activity. In one test, an endoscopic biopsy from the postbulbar duodenum is incubated with lactose on a test plate, and a color reaction develops within 20 min as a result of hydrolyzed lactose (a positive result) in patients with normolactasia, whereas no reaction (a negative result) develops in patients with severe hypolactasia. Other, less direct, tests include the hydrogen breath test, and blood tests following lactose challenges.

terms.name: Finger swelling
terms.definition: Enlargement of the soft tissues of one or more fingers.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating estrogen level
terms.definition: A deviation from normal concentration of the hormone estrogen in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal serum estradiol
terms.definition: A deviation from normal concentrations of estradiol in the circulation.

terms.name: Increased serum estradiol
terms.definition: An elevation above normal limits of the concentration of estradiol in the circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal serum estriol
terms.definition: A deviation from normal concentration of estriol in the circulation.

terms.name: Increased serum estriol
terms.definition: An elevation above normal limits of estriol concentration in the circulation.

terms.name: Decreased serum estriol
terms.definition: A reduction below normal limits of estriol in the circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal serum estrone
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of circulating estrone.

terms.name: Increased serum estrone
terms.definition: An elevation above normal limits of the concentration of estrone in the circulation.

terms.name: Decreased serum estrone
terms.definition: A reduction below normal limits of the concentration of estrone in the circulation.

terms.name: Gingival calcification
terms.definition: Ectopic deposition of calcium salts found in the gingiva.

terms.name: Constitutional symptom
terms.definition: A symptom or manifestation indicating a systemic or general effect of a disease and that may affect the general well-being or status of an individual.

terms.name: Chills
terms.definition: A sudden sensation of feeling cold.

terms.name: Shivering
terms.definition: Involuntary contraction or twitching of the muscles.

terms.name: Rigors
terms.definition: Severe chills with violent shivering. A rigor is an episode of shaking or exaggerated shivering which can occur with a high fever.

terms.name: Foveal degeneration
terms.definition: A nonspecific term denoting progressive loss of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and/or neurosensory retinal cells within the fovea.

terms.name: Beaten bronze macular sheen
terms.name_zh: 古铜色 beaten 斑样光泽
terms.definition: An irregular grayish appearance of the macula, which is said to resemble beaten bronze or hammered metal.

terms.name: Dark choroid
terms.definition: A fluorescein angiographic finding of absence of the normal background fluorescence (a dark choroid).

terms.name: Atrophic muscularis propria
terms.definition: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of muscularois propria tissue that was once present. The atrophy may involve a marked vacuolar degeneration of myocytes, loss of muscle fibers and some cases a highly characteristic honeycomb fibrosis.

terms.name: Hypoganglionosis
terms.definition: Sparse and small myenteric ganglia

terms.name: Ganglioneuromatosis
terms.definition: Hyperplastic submucosal and myenteric plexus containing an increased number of ganglion cells, glial cells and nerve fibers.

terms.name: Poor visual behavior for age
terms.definition: Lack of visual responsiveness or decrease in visual capabilities suggesting a lack of visual responsiveness or decrease in visual capabilities in an infant or young child in which visual behavior fails to meet normal developmental milestones.

terms.name: Transient
terms.definition: Short-lived and not permanent. This term applies to a phenotypic abnormality that is temporary and of short duration.

terms.name: Portosystemic collateral veins
terms.definition: Presence of biliary veins that serve as a collateral channel to the systemic circulation

terms.name: Abnormal hepatobiliary system physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the hepatobiliary system

terms.name: Dependency on intravenous nutrition
terms.definition: Inability to be weaned from intravenous (parenteral) nutrition, as judged by the hydration status (urine output, blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, urine sodium concentration), ability to maintain weight, stool output, and serum electrolyte status.

terms.name: Increased urinary sedoheptulose
terms.definition: An increased concentration of sedoheptulose in the urine. Sedoheptulose is a monosaccharide with seven carbon atoms and a ketone functional group.

terms.name: Hyperautofluorescent retinal lesion
terms.name_zh: 视网膜高自发荧光病灶
terms.definition: Increased amount of autofluorescence in the retina as ascertained by fundus autofluorescence imaging.

terms.name: Hypoautofluorescent retinal lesion
terms.name_zh: 视网膜低自发荧光病灶
terms.definition: Decreased amount of autofluorescence in the retina as ascertained by fundus autofluorescence imaging.

terms.name: Abnormal temper tantrums
terms.definition: Temper tantrums are brief episodes of extreme, unpleasant, and sometimes aggressive behaviors in response to frustration or anger, which are a normal part of development in toddlers. Temper tantrums that occur more frequently in a given time and/or are more severe in symptomatology and/or longer in duration and/or inappropriate for the given age compared to a temper tantrum that naturally occurs as a part of the developmental process are classified as abnormal temper tantrums.

terms.name: Frequent temper tantrums
terms.definition: Temper tantrums that occur more frequently compared to the temper tantrums that are a part of the normal developmental process.

terms.name: Severe temper tantrums
terms.definition: Temper tantrums, which occur with more severe symptomatology compared to a temper tantrum that occurs as a part of normal developmental process.

terms.name: Abnormal optic chiasm morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the optic chiasm.The optic chiasm, located below the hypothalamus, is a partial crossing of the optic nerves.

terms.name: Increased number of elastic fibers in the dermis
terms.name_zh: 真皮弹性纤维数量增多
synonyms: Increased number of elastic fibres in the dermis
terms.definition: An elevated number of elastic fibers, that is of bundles of proteins and glycoproteins in the extracellular matrix in the reticular dermis. Elastic fibers can stretch and recoil back to their original length. This feature can be appreciated on histology with hematoxylin and eosin or other staining methods.

terms.name: Clumping of elastic fibers in the dermis
synonyms: Clumping of elastic fibres in the dermis
terms.definition: Formation of clumps or aggregates that make up small protuberances from elastic fibers within the dermis (especially the reticular dermis).

terms.name: Thickened elastic fibers in the dermis
synonyms: Thickened elastic fibres in the dermis
terms.definition: An increase of the diameter of elastic fibers in the dermis.

terms.name: Fragmented elastic fibers in the dermis
synonyms: Fragmented elastic fibres in the dermis
terms.definition: Elastic fibers in the dermis exhibit an increased number of breaks associated with disorganization of the structure of the elastic fibers.

terms.name: Left ventricular diastolic dysfunction
terms.definition: Abnormal function of the left ventricule during left ventricular relaxation and filling.

terms.name: Left ventricular systolic dysfunction
terms.definition: Abnormality of left ventricular contraction, often defined operationally as an ejection fraction of less than 40 percent.

terms.name: Neuronal/glioneuronal neoplasm of the central nervous system
terms.definition: A central nervous system neoplasm with neuronal and, less consistently, glial differentiation.

terms.name: Rosette-forming glioneuronal tumor
synonyms: Rosette-forming glioneuronal tumor of the fourth ventricle
Rosette-forming glioneuronal tumour of the fourth ventricle
terms.definition: A tumor of the central nervous system that has components of both neurocytic and glial areas, whereby usually the glial component of the tumor predominates. Rossette-forming glioneuronal tumors (RGNT) have biphasic cytoarchitecture with two elements; neurocytic rosettes resembling Homer-Wright rosettes, and astrocytic component resembling a pilocytic astrocytoma. RGNTs are low-grade tumors that lack histopathological signs of malignancy.

terms.name: Smooth septal thickening on pulmonary HRCT
terms.definition: Thickening of the interlobular septa of the lungs as seen on a high-resolution computed tomography scan with a smooth appearance of the interlobular septa.

terms.name: Nodular septal thickening on pulmonary HRCT
terms.definition: Thickening of the interlobular septa of the lungs as seen on a high-resolution computed tomography scan with a nodular or beaded appearance of the interlobular septa.

terms.name: Irregular septal thickening on pulmonary HRCT
terms.name_zh: 肺部高分辨率CT示间隔不规则增厚
terms.definition: Thickening of the interlobular septa of the lungs as seen on a high-resolution computed tomography scan with an irregular appearance of the interlobular septa. THis feature is often associated with distortion of lung architecture.

terms.name: Honeycomb lung
terms.definition: Honeycombing represents destroyed and fibrotic lung tissue containing numerous cystic airspaces with thick fibrous walls, representing the late stage of various lung diseases, with complete loss of acinar architecture. The cysts range in size from a few millimeters to several centimeters in diameter, have variable wall thickness, and are lined by metaplastic bronchiolar epithelium. On chest radiographs, honeycombing appears as closely approximated ring shadows, typically 3-10 mm in diameter with walls 1-3 mm in thickness, that resemble a honeycomb; the finding implies end-stage lung disease. On CT scans, the appearance is of clustered cystic air spaces, typically of comparable diameters on the order of 3-10 mm but occasionally as large as 2.5 cm. Honeycombing is usually subpleural and is characterized by well-defined walls. It is a CT feature of established pulmonary fibrosis. Because honeycombing is often considered specific for pulmonary fibrosis and is an important criterion in the diagnosis of usual interstitial pneumonia, the term should be used with care, as it may directly impact patient care.

terms.name: Intralobular interstitial thickening
terms.definition: A fine reticular pattern on high-resolution computed tomography, with the visible lines separated by a few millimeters. Regions of the lung with intralobular interstitial thickening characteristically show a fine lacelike or netlike appearance.

terms.name: Peribronchovascular interstitial thickening
terms.definition: Thickening of the peribronchovascular interstitium, a connective tissue sheath that surrounds the central bronchi and pulmonary arteries. The peribronchovascular interstitium extends from the level of the pulmonary hila into the peripheral lung. This feature may be ascertained on high-resolution computer tomography.

terms.name: Subpleural interstitial thickening
terms.definition: Increase in thickness of the subpleural interstitium.

terms.name: Ground-glass opacification
terms.definition: On chest radiographs, ground-glass opacity appears as an area of hazy increased lung opacity, usually extensive, within which margins of pulmonary vessels may be indistinct. On CT scans, it appears as hazy increased opacity of lung, with preservation of bronchial and vascular margins. It is caused by partial filling of airspaces, interstitial thickening (due to fluid, cells, and/or fibrosis), partial collapse of alveoli, increased capillary blood volume, or a combination of these, the common factor being the partial displacement of air.
