Ground-glass opacity is less opaque than consolidation, in which bronchovascular margins are obscured.

terms.name: Centrilobular ground-glass opacification on pulmonary HRCT
terms.name_zh: 肺部高分辨率CT示小叶中心磨玻璃影
terms.definition: A hazy area of increased attenuation in centrilobular areas of the lung with preserved bronchial and vascular markings seen on a computer tomography scan. Centrilobular refers to a location that is central within secondary pulmonary lobules.

terms.name: Abdominal aseptic abscess
terms.definition: An abscess-like lesion located within the abdomen. The lesions are localized in the spleen, liver, abdominal lymph nodes. The lesions represent visceral sterile collections of mature neutrophils that do not respond to antibiotics but regress quickly when treated with corticosteroids, but relapses occur frequently.

terms.name: Localized area of pendulous skin
terms.definition: A confined region of lax skin that hangs below the level of the surrounding skin. Histopatholigically, there is a loss of elastic fibers in the dermis of the affected region.

terms.name: Abnormal total CD4+ T cell number
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of absolute number of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells (either count per volume or percentage of total lymphocytes), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Arousal parasomnia
terms.definition: An altered state of arousal during sleep that may be reported by the individual or an observation of others.

terms.name: Marcus Gunn jaw winking synkinesis
terms.name_zh: 马库斯·冈恩颌动瞬目联带运动
terms.definition: Unilateral ptosis with associated upper eyelid contraction and contraction of either the external or the internal pterygoid muscle. It is thought to occur because of congenital miswiring of a branch of the fifth cranial nerve into the branch of the third cranial nerve supplying the levator muscle. In Marcus Gunn jaw winking synkinesis, elevation and even retraction of the affected eyelid is triggered by chewing, suction, lateral mandible movement, smiling, sternocleidomastoid contraction, protruding tongue, Valsalva maneuver and even by breathing.

terms.name: Sleep talking
terms.definition: Vocalization (production of recognizable words or other sounds) during sleep with lack of awareness.

terms.name: Retinal vasculitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of retinal blood vessels as manifested by perivascular sheathing or cuffing, vascular leakage and/or occlusion. It can affect veins, arteries or both.

terms.name: Hypnic jerks
terms.definition: Hypnic jerks are characterized by sudden and brief (less than 1 second), non-periodic simultaneous contractions of the whole body or one or more extremities at the onset of sleep.

terms.name: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with generalized onset
terms.name_zh: 全面起始双侧强直-阵挛发作
synonyms: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with generalised onset
Generalised tonic-clonic seizure without focal onset
Generalised tonic-clonic seizure without partial onset
Generalised tonic-clonic seizures without focal onset
Generalized tonic-clonic seizure without focal onset
Generalized tonic-clonic seizure without partial onset
Generalized tonic-clonic seizures without focal onset
terms.definition: A bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with generalized onset is a type of bilateral tonic-clonic seizure characterized by generalized onset; these seizures rapidly engage networks in both hemispheres at the start of the seizure.

terms.name: Subtentorial periventricular white matter hyperdensity
terms.definition: Areas of brighter than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the cerebral white matter that surrounds the fourth cerebral ventricle (which is located beneath the tentorium of the cerebellum).

terms.name: Posterolateral diaphragmatic hernia
terms.definition: A posterolateral defect in the diaphragm, commonly referred to as a Bochdalek hernia, which is often accompanied by herniation of the stomach, intestines, liver, and/or spleen into the chest cavity.

terms.name: Morgagni diaphragmatic hernia
terms.definition: An anterior retrosternal or parasternal hernia that can result in the herniation of liver or intestines into the chest cavity.

terms.name: Central diaphragmatic hernia
terms.definition: A congenital diaphragm defect involving the central tendinous (e.g., amuscular) portion of the diaphragm, whereby the entire rim of diaphragmatic musculature is present.

terms.name: Increased total iron binding capacity
terms.definition: An elevation in the total-iron binding capacity, which measures how much serum iron is bound if an excess of radioactive iron is added. A high TIBC corresponds to a high transferrin concentration. The latent (or free) iron binding capacity is the difference between the TIBC and the measured serum iron, corresponding to the transferrin not bound to iron, i.e., free iron binding capacity.

terms.name: Inclusion body fibromatosis
terms.definition: A benign tumor made up of mostly myofibroblasts that appears almost exclusively on the digits of the hands and feet, rarely involving the thumb or big toe. The lesion displays a proliferation of bland intradermal spindle cells arranged in whorls, fascicles, or a storiform pattern in a collagenous background of varying degrees. Also usually present are perpendicular tumor cell fascicles that extend to the epidermis. The small intracytoplasmic inclusions are said to appear similar to red blood cells. The inclusion bodies have been shown to be made up of densely packed vimentin and actin filaments. The tumor often causes a dome-shaped elevation of the overlying structures, forming a protuberant or polypoid nodule. The overlying epidermis can display a host of changes, including acanthosis, hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, rete ridge flattening, entrapment of adnexal structures, and, rarely, ulceration.

terms.name: Inflammatory cap polyp
terms.definition: A non-malignant sessile or pedunculated polyp in the colon and rectum that displays a cap of inflammatory granulation tissue with fibrinopurulent exudate that covers the polyp.

terms.name: Fragmented sleep
terms.definition: Sleep characterized by frequent interruptions, stopping and starting, which disrupt the normal progression of sleep stages.

terms.name: Muscle fiber actin filament accumulation
terms.definition: Accumulation in muscle cells of filaments composed of actin.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating apolipoprotein concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of apolipoprotein in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating apolipoprotein A-IV concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环载脂蛋白A-IV浓度升高
synonyms: Elevated apolipoprotein A-IV level in blood
Increased apolipoprotein A-IV level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of apolipoprotein A-IV in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Caput medusae
terms.definition: Distended and engorged umbilical veins which are seen radiating from the umbilicus across the abdomen to join systemic veins.

terms.name: Triggered by
terms.definition: A trigger is defined as an external factor that leads to the manifestation of a sign or symptom in a person with a susceptibility to developing that manifestation.

terms.name: Triggered by breast feeding
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by breast feeding in an infant.

terms.name: Triggered by cold
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to cold surroundings.

terms.name: Triggered by dehydration
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by being dehydrated, i.e., by a deficit in total body water.

terms.name: Triggered by carbohydrate ingestion
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking carbohydrates.

terms.name: Triggered by fructose ingestion
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking fructose.

terms.name: Triggered by glucose ingestion
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking glucose.

terms.name: Triggered by ethanol ingestion
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by drinking or otherwise ingesting ethanol.

terms.name: Triggered by fasting
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by abstaining from eating food (fasting).

terms.name: Triggered by galactose ingestion
synonyms: Triggered by ingestion of lactose-containing milk
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking galactose. Galactose usually is ingested as lactose, which is composed of equimolar amounts of glucose and galactose.

terms.name: Triggered by heat
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to heat.

terms.name: Triggered by febrile illness
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by febrile illness.

terms.name: Triggered by heavy meal
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating large quantities of food, for instance, by a heavy meal.

terms.name: Triggered by high-fat diet
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating a diet high in lipids.

terms.name: Triggered by hyperventilation
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by excessively rapid and deep breathing.

terms.name: Triggered by vaccination
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a vaccination.

terms.name: Triggered by menstruation
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by menstruation in a female.

terms.name: Triggered by pregnancy
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by pregnancy in a female.

terms.name: Triggered by sleep deprivation
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a lack of sufficient sleep.

terms.name: Triggered by smoking
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by smoking.

terms.name: Triggered by sodium ingestion
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking sodium.

terms.name: Triggered by sound
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to sound or noise.

terms.name: Triggered by stress
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a physical, mental, or emotional factor associated with bodily or mental tension.

terms.name: Triggered by excitement
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a a state of excitement or by being startled.

terms.name: Triggered by sudden movement
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a sudden movement.

terms.name: Triggered by vestibular stimulation
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by vestibular stimulation, including head turning, cold calorics, postural changes, or rotating chair.

terms.name: Tendonitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of a tendon.

terms.name: Abnormal synovial bursa morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of a synovial bursa, which is a synovium-lined, sac-like structure found throughout the body near bony prominences and between bones, muscles, tendons, and ligaments. The bursa itself is a synovial lining that represents a potential space insofar as it is collapsed upon itself until a resulting trigger causes the bursa to become irritated and fill with synovial fluid.

terms.name: Bursitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of a synovial bursa.

terms.name: Sleep paralysis
terms.definition: Inability to move trunk and limbs and inability to speak during transition into or out of sleep; awareness is preserved and recall is present.

terms.name: Parasomnia
terms.definition: A clinically observable or self-reported abnormal behavior, experience, or physiological event that occurs in association with sleep, specific sleep stages, or sleep-wake transitions.

terms.name: NREM parasomnia
terms.definition: A parasomnia that occurs during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.

terms.name: Sleep walking
terms.definition: Ambulation during sleep with lack awareness and limited or no recall of the event.

terms.name: Foot pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the foot.

terms.name: Preretinal hemorrhage
terms.definition: An accumulation of blood that is located between the retina and the detached posterior hyaloid, or in the vitreous cavity. Subhyaloid premacular hemorrhage is typically characterized by a circumscribed, round or dumb-bell shaped, bright red mound of blood beneath the internal limiting membrane (ILM) or between the ILM and hyaloid face, in or near to the central macular area.

terms.name: Flame-shaped retinal hemorrhage
terms.definition: A type of retinal hemorrhage that is located within the nerve fiber layer (NFL) of the retina and that exhibits a characteristic flame shape which results from constraints by the structure of the NFL (axons of the ganglion cells).

terms.name: Dot-and-blot retinal hemorrhage
terms.name_zh: 点状斑片状视网膜出血
terms.definition: Accumulation of blood located in the retina's inner nuclear and outer plexiform layers, and having a dot-like or blot-like shape. THe shape results from intraretinal compression, restricting the hemorrhages within a specific location.

terms.name: Subretinal hemorrhage
terms.definition: Accumulation of blood located beneath the neurosensory retina in the space between the neurosensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium.

terms.name: Sub-retinal pigment epithelium haemorrhage
terms.definition: An accumulation of blood located between the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and Bruch membrane.

terms.name: Cutaneous cyst
terms.definition: A hollow mass located in the skin that is surrounded by an epithelium-lined wall and is well demarcated from the adjacent tissue. Cysts are often said to be sac-like and may contain serous liquid or semisolid material.

terms.name: Trichilemmal cyst
terms.definition: Nontender, round and firm, but slightly compressible, intradermal or subcutaneous cyst measuring 0.5-5 cm in diameter. Trichilemmal cysts are acquired rather than congenital, and tend to appear on the scalp rather than the face, and to be intradermal rather than subcutaneous.

terms.name: Dermoid cyst
terms.definition: A congenital subcutaneous cyst that arises from entrapment of skin along the lines of embryonic fusion. In contrast to epidermal cysts, dermoid cysts tend to contain various adnexal structures such as hair, sebaceous, eccrine or apocrine glands. Dermoid cysts are present at birth, and are indolent, firm, deep, subcutaneous nodules. They are often located on the head and neck, and rarely in the anogenital area. Dermoid cysts are slowly progressive and can grow to a size of 1 to 4 cm.

terms.name: Eruptive vellus hair cyst
terms.definition: A cutaneous cyst that is small (one or two millimeters in diameter) and painless, presenting as a follicular papule that usually is skin colored but may have a reddish or brownish tinge.

terms.name: Comedo
terms.definition: A clogged cutaneous sebaceous follicle, which is a cutaneous gland that secretes sebum (usually into a hair follicle).

terms.name: Closed comedo
terms.definition: A comedo in which the top of the pore is not stretched open and thus does not expose the clogged portion (which would appear black), hence the name whitehead.

terms.name: Open comedo
terms.definition: A comedo in which the part of the pore at the surface of the skin is stretched and open, exposing the contents of the comedo, which appear black.

terms.name: Geographic tongue
terms.definition: An anomaly of the tongue characterized by loss (atrophy) of filiform papillae of the tongue, leaving areas of erythema (redness), surrounded by a serpiginous, white, hyperkeratotic border. The name geographic tongue refers to an appearance that is said to be similar to a map.

terms.name: Claustrophobia
terms.definition: An abnormal fear of being in a closed or narrow space with no escape is called claustrophobia.

terms.name: Ameliorated by
terms.definition: An ameliorating factor is defined as an external factor that leads to a sign or symptom that is already present improving or becoming more bearable

terms.name: Ameliorated by pregnancy
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by pregnancy in a female.

terms.name: Ameliorated by heat
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by heat (including fever).

terms.name: Ameliorated by carbohydrate ingestion
terms.name_zh: 摄入碳水化合物可缓解
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by eating or drinking carbohydrates including glucose (sugar).

terms.name: Stiff neck
terms.definition: A sensation of tightness in the neck when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity. Neck stiffness often involves soreness and difficulty moving the neck, especially when trying to turn the head to the side.

terms.name: Stiff elbow
terms.definition: A sensation of tightness in the elbow joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

terms.name: Stiff wrist
terms.definition: A sensation of tightness in the wrist joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

terms.name: Stiff finger
terms.definition: A sensation of tightness in a finger joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

terms.name: Stiff hip
terms.definition: A sensation of tightness in the hip joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

terms.name: Stiff knee
terms.definition: A sensation of tightness in the knee joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

terms.name: Stiff ankle
terms.definition: A sensation of tightness in the ankle joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

terms.name: Stiff toe
terms.definition: A sensation of tightness in a toe joint when attempting to move it, especially after a period of inactivity.

terms.name: Snoring
terms.definition: Deep, noisy breathing during sleep, accompanied by hoarse or harsh sounds, is caused by the vibration of respiratory structures, especially the soft palate. This vibration results in sound due to obstructed air movement during breathing while sleeping.

terms.name: Stuttering
terms.definition: Disruptions in the production of speech sounds, with involuntary repetitions of words or parts of words, prolongations of speech sounds, or complete blockage of speech production for several seconds.

terms.name: Panic attack
terms.definition: A sudden episode of intense fear in a situation where there is no danger or apparent cause.

terms.name: Abnormal esophagus physiology
terms.definition: Any physiological abnormality of the esophagus.

terms.name: Esophageal spasms
terms.definition: Involuntary contractions of the esophagus that are irregular, uncoordinated, and painful.

terms.name: Melasma
terms.definition: Symmetrical, blotchy, brownish facial pigmentation.

terms.name: Achilles tendonitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the Achilles tendon.

terms.name: Ovarian dermoid cyst
terms.definition: An cystic ovarian teratoma composed of dermal and epidermal elements and containing tissue components including hair, teeth, bone, thyroid, and others.

terms.name: Lateral
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality that is located farther from the median plane or midline of the body or of the referenced structure.

terms.name: Abnormality of skin adnexa physiology
terms.name_zh: 皮肤附属器生理功能异常
terms.definition: Any functional anomaly of the skin adnexa (skin appendages), which are specialized skin structures located within the dermis and focally within the subcutaneous fatty tissue, comprising three histologically distinct structures: (1) the pilosebaceous unit (hair follicle and sebaceous glands); (2) the eccrine sweat glands; and (3) the apocrine glands.

terms.name: Gustatory sweating
terms.definition: Hyperhidrosis that occurs with gustatory stimulation (e.g., moisture on face from sweating that occurs after eating).

terms.name: Cold-induced sweating
terms.definition: Sweating provoked by cold temperature rather than by heat.

terms.name: Pain characteristic
terms.definition: A pain characteristic is defined as a subjective category or type of pain.

terms.name: Sharp
terms.definition: Applied to pain that is described as sharp, i.e., sudden and severe.

terms.name: Dull
terms.definition: Applied to pain that is dull, i.e., not severe but that continues over a long period of time.

terms.name: Tender
terms.definition: Applied to pain that is tender, i.e., elicited by touching the affected body part.

terms.name: Sleep-interrupting
terms.definition: Applied to pain that wakes the affecting individual from sleep.

terms.name: Aggravated by
terms.definition: An aggravating factor is defined as an external factor that leads to a sign or symptom that is already present getting worse or becoming more severe.

terms.name: Aggravated by activity
terms.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is aggravated by activity, exertion, or exercise.

terms.name: Axial
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in the central part of the body, in the head and trunk as distinguished from the limbs.

terms.name: Excessive sleep
terms.definition: A clinical phenomenon characterized by sleeping longer than what is typical or necessary for a person's age and context, or by recurrent episodes of sleep that intrude upon the waking hours. Excessive sleep is identified through self-reports or observations and may involve prolonged nighttime sleep, frequent daytime naps, or episodes of unintentional sleep.

terms.name: Cervical lymphadenopathy
synonyms: Swollen lymph nodes in the neck
terms.definition: Enlarged lymph nodes in the neck.

terms.name: Upper-body predominance
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality that affects the arms, trunk, head more than the legs.

terms.name: Lower-body predominance
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality that affects the legs more than the arms, trunk, head.

terms.name: Acral
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality that affects the distal portions of limbs (hand, foot) and head (ears, nose).

terms.name: Distributed along Blaschko lines
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality whose localization corresponds to the lines of Blaschko, which correspond to the lineage of epithelia cells. Blaschko lines are normally invisible but may become apparent with certain skin diseases and then can be seen to be distributed in lines horizontal to the body.

terms.name: Dermatomal
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality whose localization corresponds to the dermatomes, i.e., the nerve root distribution.

terms.name: Herpetiform
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance resembles that of the grouped umbilicated vesicles seen in herpes simplex and herpes zoster infections.

terms.name: Morbilliform
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance resembles that of measles, i.e., maculopapular lesions that are red and roughly 2 to 10 mm in diameter and may be partially confluent.

terms.name: Prolonged
terms.definition: Applied to an abnormality whose duration is extended over a longer period of time than is expected or usual (e.g., prolonged fever lasts longer than one usually sees with an infection).

terms.name: Extended nighttime sleep
terms.definition: Sleeping for a longer duration than usual during the night.

terms.name: Frequent napping
terms.definition: Regular episodes of sleep that occur during the day outside of the main sleep period.

terms.name: Malar rash
terms.definition: An erythematous (red), flat facial rash that affects the skin in the malar area (over the cheekbones) and extends over the bridge of the nose.

terms.name: Nocturnal
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality that occurs in or is exacerbated during the night.

terms.name: Diurnal
terms.definition: Applies to a sign, symptom, or other abnormality that occurs in or is exacerbated in the day time.

terms.name: Episodic
terms.definition: Applied to a sign, symptom, or other manifestation that occurs multiple times at usually irregular intervals. The occurrences are separated by an interval in which the sign, symptom, or manifestation is not present.

terms.name: Periodic
terms.definition: Applies to a sign, symptom, or other manifestation that recurs with a fixed time interval, i.e., the symptom-free periods are always of the same length.

terms.name: Quotidian
terms.definition: Applies to a sign, symptom, or other manifestation that is episodic with a fixed time interval of one day (24 hours).

terms.name: Acute emergence over minutes
terms.definition: Acute appearance of disease manifestations in a period of minutes.

terms.name: Acute emergence over hours
terms.definition: Acute appearance of disease manifestations in a period of hours.

terms.name: Acute emergence over days
terms.definition: Acute appearance of disease manifestations in a period of days.

terms.name: Abnormal pupil shape
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal circular shape of the pupil

terms.name: Oval pupil
terms.definition: An abnormal pupil shape that is elliptical, i.e., egg-like.

terms.name: Anterior chamber cyst
terms.definition: A closed sac, having a distinct membrane and division compared to the nearby tissue located within the anterior chamber. The sac that may contain air, fluids, or semi-solid material.

terms.name: Esophoria
terms.definition: A form of strabismus with both eyes turned inward to a relatively mild degree, usually defined as less than 10 prism diopters.

terms.name: Exophoria
terms.definition: A form of strabismus with one or both eyes deviated outward to a milder degree than with exotropia.

terms.name: Choroidal nevus
terms.definition: A benign, flat or slightly elevated melanocytic lesions of the posterior uvea with clearly defined margins. Choroidal nevi tend to remain stable in size, and to display features such as overlying drusen as well as retinal pigment epithelial atrophy, hyperplasia or fibrous metaplasia.

terms.name: Exacerbated by head trauma
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is worsened, aggravated, or exacerbated by head trauma.

terms.name: Cubitus varus
terms.definition: A deformity of the elbow in which there is a deviation of the forearm toward the midline of the body.

terms.name: Ovarian carcinoma
terms.definition: A malignant neoplasm originating from the surface ovarian epithelium.

terms.name: Leakage of dye on fundus fluorescein angiography
terms.name_zh: 眼底荧光血管造影染料渗漏
terms.definition: Leakage of fluorescein dye observed upon retinal fluorescein angiography. Areas of leakage can be appreciated as showing gradual enlargement with blurring of margins.

terms.name: Copper accumulation in liver
terms.definition: An anomalous build up of copper (Cu) in the liver.

terms.name: Venous occlusion
terms.definition: Blockage of venous return (flow of blood from the periphery back towards the right atrium) in a vein.

terms.name: Abnormal arterial physiology
terms.definition: An anomaly of arterial function.

terms.name: Arterial occlusion
terms.definition: Blockage of blood flow through an artery.

terms.name: Sparse medial eyebrow
terms.definition: Decreased density/number and/or decreased diameter of medial eyebrow hairs.

terms.name: Retinal arterial occlusion
terms.definition: Blockage of the retinal artery, generally associated with interruption of blood flow and oxygen delivery to the retina.

terms.name: Decreased renal parenchymal thickness
terms.definition: Reduced dimension of the solid part of the kidney (parenchyma, the renal cortex and medulla) as measured from the collecting system (renal calyces and pelvis) to the border of the kidney. This measurement can be performed by measuring the thickness of the parenchyma in computed tomography scans.

terms.name: Antepartum hemorrhage
terms.definition: Significant maternal hemorrhage/bleed in the second half of pregnancy and prior to the birth of the baby.

terms.name: Anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗谷氨酸脱羧酶抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against glutamic acid decarboxylase.

terms.name: Downgaze palsy
terms.definition: A limitation of the ability to direct one's gaze below the horizontal meridian.

terms.name: Upgaze palsy
terms.definition: A limitation of the ability to direct one's gaze above the horizontal meridian.

terms.name: Abnormality of foot cortical bone
synonyms: Abnormality of the cortex of foot bones
terms.definition: An anomaly of the outer shell (cortex) of a foot bone.

terms.name: Cortical thinning of foot bones
terms.definition: A reduction in the thickness of the outer shell (cortex) of foot bones.

terms.name: Triggered by emotion
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a strong spontaneously arising mental state, reaction or feeling (emotion).

terms.name: Delayed ability to stand
terms.definition: A failure to achieve the ability to stand up at an appropriate developmental stage. Most children begin to walk alone at 11 to 15 months of age. On average, children can stand while holding on at the age of 9 to 10 months, can pull up to stand and walk with one hand being held at 12 months, and can stand alone and walk well at 18 months.

terms.name: Delayed ability to sit
terms.definition: A failure to achieve the ability to sit at an appropriate developmental stage. Most children sit with support at 6 months of age and sit steadily without support at 9 months of age.

terms.name: Red eye
terms.definition: A reddish appearance over the white part (sclera) of the eye ranging from a few enlarged blood vessels appearing as wiggly lines over the sclera to a bright red color completely covering to sclera.

terms.name: Circumlimbal hyperemia
terms.definition: A ring of redness at the limbus of the eye, the border between the cornea and the sclera.

terms.name: Superficial episcleral hyperemia
terms.definition: Prominence of blood vessels of the superficial episcleral tissues.

terms.name: Deep episcleral hyperemia
terms.definition: Prominence of blood vessels of the deep episcleral tissues.

terms.name: Corneal keratic precipitates
terms.definition: An inflammatory cellular deposit deposited on the corneal endothelium and visible as spots on the cornea.

terms.name: Central retinal artery occlusion
terms.definition: Blockage of the main artery in the retina. In the acute phase, the fundus may show cherry red spot and stasis of retinal flow. The typical presentation is one of profound monocular visual loss.

terms.name: Lupus anticoagulant
terms.definition: Presence of lupus anticoagulant (LA) autoantibodies. LA represent a heterogeneous group of autoantibodies, IgG, IgM, or a mixture of both classes, that interfere with standard phospholipid-based coagulant tests (this is only an in vitro phenomenon, LA do not cause reduction of coagulation in vivo). The antibodies are directed against plasma proteins which also bind to phospholipid surfaces.

terms.name: Interlobular bile duct destruction
terms.definition: Damage to and obliteration of intrahepatic bile ducts (bile ducts that transport bile between the Canals of Hering and the interlobar bile ducts).

terms.name: Abnormal circulating beta-2-microglobulin concentration
synonyms: Abnormality of circulating beta2 microglobulin level
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of beta-2-microglobulin in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating beta-2-microglobulin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环β2微球蛋白浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of beta-2-microglobulin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Decreased circulating beta-2-microglobulin concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环β2-微球蛋白浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of beta-2-microglobulin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal corneal limbus morphology
terms.definition: An anomaly of the margin of the cornea overlapped by the sclera.

terms.name: Limbal edema
terms.definition: Swelling of the margin of the cornea overlapped by the sclera.

terms.name: Giant conjunctival papillae
terms.definition: Conjunctival papillae with a diameter greater than 1 millimeter. They characteristically have flattened tops which sometimes demonstrate staining with fluorescein.

terms.name: Recurrent interdigital mycosis
terms.definition: A history of repeated fungal infections located between the fingers or toes, usually manifested by scaling, maceration, and itching. The toes are more commonly affected than the fingers.

terms.name: Typically de novo
synonyms: Autosomal dominant germline de novo mutation
terms.definition: Description of conditions that are exclusively or predominantly observed to display de novo variants. In some cases, this may be due to the limited reproductive fitness of affected individuals.

terms.name: Anti-multiple nuclear dots antibody positivity
terms.definition: A type of antinuclear antibody (ANA) positivity revealed by indirect immunofluorescence (IFL). The multiple nuclear dots (MND) pattern is immunomorphologically characterized by the staining of 3-20 dots of variable size distributed all over the cell nucleus, but sparing the nucleoli, and, in contrast to the anticentromere pattern, MND reactivity does not stain the chromosomes in mitotic cells.

terms.name: Abnormal cellular phenotype
terms.definition: An anomaly of cellular morphology or physiology.

terms.name: Retinal arteriolar macroaneurysms
terms.definition: Acquired focal dilatations of branches of the retinal artery, usually second-order retinal arterioles, that range in size from 100 to 200 micrometers in diameter. Macroaneurysms are generally located at the temporal retina and may be hemorrhagic or exudative.

terms.name: Erratic myoclonus
terms.definition: A type of myoclonus in which the myoclonias shift from body region to another in a random and asynchronous fashion. Erratic myoclonus can affect the face or limbs, are brief, single or repetitive, very frequent and nearly continuous.

terms.name: Uveal ectropion
terms.definition: Presence of iris pigment epithelium on the anterior surface of the iris.

terms.name: Polygonal renal calices
terms.definition: An abnormal polygonal shape of the calices of the kidney (which normally have a rounded or cup-shaped appearance).

terms.name: Polycalycosis
terms.definition: Increased number of calices of the kidney.

terms.name: Abnormal medullary pyramid morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the pyramid of the adult kidney, cone-shaped structures with a broad base adjacent to the renal cortex and the narrow apex that is termed papilla.

terms.name: Renal medullary pyramid hypoplasia
terms.definition: Undergrowth of the pyramid of the adult kidney, cone-shaped structures with a broad base adjacent to the renal cortex and the narrow apex that is termed papilla.

terms.name: Glomerular endocapillary hypercellularity
terms.name_zh: 肾小球毛细血管内细胞增多
terms.definition: Hypercellularity due to increased number of cells within glomerular capillary lumina, causing narrowing of the lumina.

terms.name: Glomerular extracapillary hypercellularity
terms.name_zh: 肾小球毛细血管外细胞增多
terms.definition: Hypercellularity (increased number of cells) in the renal glomerulus but external to the glomerular capillaries, i.e., in the Bowman space or more than one layer of parietal or visceral epithelial cells.

terms.name: Free-running sleep pattern
terms.definition: A condition in which the intrinsic circadian rhythm is no longer entrained to the 24-h schedule. Normal individuals who are exposed to an environment devoid of zeitgebers develop free-running rhythms with a period longer than 24 h.

terms.name: Trichoepithelioma
terms.definition: A benign hair follicle tumor whose tumor cells form rudimentary hair follicles but not actual hair shafts. A trichoepithelioma is usually less than one centimeter, firm, round, and shihy with yellow, pink, brown, or bluish color. They may occur multiply, usually on the face, and may gradually increase in number with age.

terms.name: Abnormal growth plate morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the growth plates (epiphyseal plates), areas of cartilage located near the ends of long bones that are located between the metaphysis (widened part of the shaft of the bone) and the epiphysis (end of the bone) and in which growth occurs in the developing bone. After conclusion of bone growth, the growth plates ossify (harden into solid bone).

terms.name: Thick growth plates
terms.definition: Increased thickness (dimension along the axis of the bone) of the growth plate.

terms.name: Abnormal ossification of the sacrum
terms.definition: Abnormal bone tissue formation (ossification) affecting the sacrum.

terms.name: Delayed ossification of the sacrum
terms.definition: Formation of the sacrum bone tissue occurs later than age-adjusted norms.

terms.name: Loud snoring
terms.definition: Snoring at a particularly loud or abnormally high volume.

terms.name: Interictal EEG abnormality
terms.definition: Interictal refers to a period of time between epileptic seizures. Electroencephalographic (EEG) patterns are important in the differential diagnosis of epilepsy, and the EEG is almost always abnormal during a seizure. Some persons with seizures may show EEG abnormalities between seizures, while others do not. In some cases, multiple interictal EEGs must be recorded before an abnormality is observed. In most cases the electrographic pattern of seizure onset is completely different from the activity recorded during interictal discharge.

terms.name: Duplicated odontoid process
terms.definition: The presence of two distinct odontoid processes. The odontoid process, also known as the dens of the axis, is a protuberance of the C2 vertebral body around which the first vertebra rotates.

terms.name: Orthotopic os odontoideum
terms.definition: Os odontoideum is classified into two anatomic types (orthotopic and dystopic). Os odontoideum is defined as an ossicle that consists of smooth and separate caudal portions of the odontoid process.With dystopic os odontoideum, the ossicle is located near the basion or is fused with the clivus.

terms.name: Hyperglutaminuria
terms.definition: An increased concentration of glutamine in the urine.

terms.name: Triggered by exertion
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exertion or physical exercise.

terms.name: Anti-thyroid peroxidase antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗甲状腺过氧化物酶抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against thyroid peroxidase.

terms.name: Increased circulating androstenedione concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环雄烯二酮浓度升高
terms.definition: Increased concentration of androstenedione in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Anti-pituitary antibody positivity
terms.definition: Circulating antipituitary antibodies (APA) are markers of autoimmune hypophysitis, which may cause deficient pituitary function.

terms.name: Hypodipsia
terms.definition: Reduced fluid intake (drinking) in a clinical situation where the plasma molarity or sodium concentration normally would induce greater fluid intake.

terms.name: Dorsocervical fat pad
terms.definition: An area of fat accumulation at the back of the neck in the form of a hump.

terms.name: Diet-resistant subcutaneous adipose tissue
terms.name_zh: 抗节食性皮下脂肪组织
terms.definition: Areas of subcutanous fat tissue that are resistant to (do not respond as expected to) diet, life-style alteration, or bariatric surgery.

terms.name: Diet-resistant subcutaneous adipose tissue below waist
terms.name_zh: 腰以下抗节食性皮下脂肪组织
terms.definition: Areas of subcutanous fat tissue below the waist that are resistant to (do not respond as expected to) diet, life-style alteration, or bariatric surgery.

terms.name: Bitemporal hollowing
terms.definition: Depression of profile in both temporal regions.

terms.name: Pill-rolling tremor
terms.definition: A type of resting tremor characterized by simultaneous rubbing movements of thumb and index fingers against each other.

terms.name: Thyroid nodule
terms.definition: A nodular lesion that develops in the thyroid gland. The term \

terms.name: Pulmonary interstitial high-resolution computed tomography abnormality
terms.definition: High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) can distinguish findings that characterize characterize interstitial lung diseases in a way not possible with other modalities.

terms.name: Reticular pattern on pulmonary HRCT
terms.definition: On pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography, reticular pattern is characterized by innumerable interlacing shadows suggesting a mesh.

terms.name: Crazy paving pattern
synonyms: Crazy paving pattern on pulmonary HRCT
terms.definition: The so-called crazy paving pattern appears as thickened interlobular septa and intralobular lines superimposed on a background of ground-glass opacity, resembling irregularly shaped paving stones. The crazy-paving pattern is often sharply demarcated from more normal lung and may have a geographic outline. It was originally reported in patients with alveolar proteinosis and is also encountered in other diffuse lung diseases that affect both the interstitial and airspace compartments, such as lipoid pneumonia.

terms.name: Nodular pattern on pulmonary HRCT
terms.definition: A nodular pattern is characterized on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography by the presence of numerous rounded opacities that range from 2 mm to 1 cm in diameter, with micronodules defined as smaller than 3 mm in diameter.

terms.name: Reticulonodular pattern on pulmonary HRCT
terms.definition: Co-occurrence of reticular and micronodular patterns on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography.

terms.name: Cystic pattern on pulmonary HRCT
terms.name_zh: 肺部高分辨率CT囊性征象
terms.definition: On pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography, the cystic pattern is composed by well-defined, round and circumscribed air-containing parenchymal spaces with a well-defined wall and interface with normal lung. The wall of the cysts may be uniform or varied in thickness, but usually is thin (less than 2 mm) and occurs without associated emphysema.

terms.name: Combined cystic and ground-glass pattern on pulmonary HRCT
terms.name_zh: 肺部高分辨率CT囊性磨玻璃混合征
terms.definition: Co-occurrence of the cystic pattern and the ground-glass pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography,

terms.name: Decreased attenuation pattern on pulmonary HRCT
terms.name_zh: 肺部高分辨率CT衰减模式降低
synonyms: Black lung pattern on pulmonary HRCT
terms.definition: Areas of low density corresponding to parenchymal destruction and reduced perfusion, and attenuation of the pulmonary vasculature, as visualized on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography.

terms.name: Mosaic attenuation pattern on pulmonary HRCT
terms.name_zh: 肺部高分辨率CT马赛克衰减征
terms.definition: A patchwork of intermingled areas of increased and decreased attenuation visualized on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography.

terms.name: Nodular-perilymphatic pattern on pulmonary HRCT
terms.definition: A nodular pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography that has a perilymphatic distribution.

terms.name: Nodular-centrilobular with tree-in-bud pattern on pulmonary HRCT
terms.definition: A nodular pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography that displays a tree-in-bud pattern, representing centrilobular branching structures that resemble a budding tree.

terms.name: Nodular-random pattern on pulmonary HRCT
terms.definition: A nodular pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography that has an apparently random pattern.

terms.name: Staring gaze
terms.definition: An abnormality in which the eyes are held permanently wide open.

terms.name: Square-wave jerks
terms.definition: Square wave jerks are saccadic eye movements which, when recorded with open eyes are considered to be a pathological sign, caused by fixation instability, and pointing to a central neurological lesion.

terms.name: Stooped posture
terms.definition: A habitual positioning of the body with the head and upper back bent forward.

terms.name: Abnormal visual fixation
terms.definition: Any anomaly in the process of ocular fixation, which is the maintaining of the visual gaze on a single location.

terms.name: Visual fixation instability
terms.definition: A deficit in the ability to fixate eye movements in order to stabilize images on the retina

terms.name: Asthenia
terms.definition: A state characterized by a feeling of weakness and loss of strength leading to a generalized weakness of the body.

terms.name: Rectourethral fistula
terms.definition: An abnormal connection (fistula) between the rectum and the urethra.

terms.name: Abnormal spleen morphology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the structure of the spleen.

terms.name: Abnormal spleen physiology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the function of the spleen.

terms.name: Splenogonadal fusion
terms.definition: Joining of the spleen and a gonad during embryological development.

terms.name: Fossa navicularis urethral stricture
terms.definition: A type of urethral stricture affecting the fossa navicularis, which is the spongy part of the male urethra located at the glans penis.

terms.name: Pendulous urethral stricture
terms.definition: A type of urethral stricture affecting the pendulous urethra, which is straight and fixed to the corpora cavernosa.

terms.name: Bulbar urethral stricture
terms.definition: A type of urethral stricture affecting the bulbar urethra, which is the part of the urethra that traverses the root of the penis.

terms.name: Vaginal stricture
terms.definition: A narrowing of the vagina owing to scar formation.

terms.name: Patulous urethra
terms.definition: Urethra more open or expanded than normal.

terms.name: Renal cortical necrosis
terms.definition: Patchy or diffuse ischemic destruction of all the elements of renal cortex resulting from significantly diminished renal arterial perfusion. Coagulative necrosis may be present, involving all tubular segments and glomeruli. Nuclei may be pale and pyknotic, or may no longer be apparent. Thrombi may be present in vessels at the edge of the infarct.

terms.name: Pulmonary pneumatocele
terms.definition: A pneumatocele is a thin walled, gas-filled space in the lung. It is most frequently caused by acute pneumonia, trauma, or aspiration of hydrocarbon fluid and is usually transient. The mechanism is believed to be a combination of parenchymal necrosis and check-valve airway obstruction. A pneumatocele appears as an approximately round, thin-walled airspace in the lung.

terms.name: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
terms.definition: A type of of pulmonary hemorrhage that originates from the pulmonary microcirculation, including the alveolar capillaries, arterioles, and venules. It presents with hemoptysis, anemia, diffuse lung infiltration, and acute respiratory failure. The diagnosis is confirmed by the observation of the accumulation of red blood cells, fibrin, or hemosiderin-laden macrophage in the alveolar space on pathologic biopsy. Hemosiderin, a product of hemoglobin degradation, appears at least 48-72 hours after bleeding and is helpful in distinguishing diffuse alveolar hemorrhage from surgical trauma. Mild interstitial thickening, organizing pneumonia, or diffuse alveolar damage can also be seen.

terms.name: Pneumomediastinum
terms.definition: The presence of free air in the mediastinum.

terms.name: Pleural cyst
terms.definition: A closed sac-like structure originating from the pleura that contains a liquid, gaseous, or semisolid substance.

terms.name: Abnormal larynx morphology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the structure of the larynx.

terms.name: Abnormal larynx physiology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the function of the larynx.

terms.name: Laryngospasm
terms.definition: A spasm (involuntary contraction) of the vocal cords that can make it difficult to speak or breathe.

terms.name: Abnormal bronchus morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the bronchi, i.e., of the airways leading from the trachea to the lungs.

terms.name: Abnormal bronchus physiology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the function of the bronchi.

terms.name: Abnormal cry
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the vocalizing of an infant's crying, i.e.,the typically loud voice production that is accompanied by tears and agitation.

terms.name: High-pitched cry
terms.definition: A type of crying in an abnormally high-pitched voice.

terms.name: Staccato cry
terms.definition: A type of cry that is abnormal because it is consists of unusually shortened and detached vocalizations.

terms.name: Acanthoma
terms.definition: A benign epithelial skin tumor manifesting as a slightly elevated circular plaque or nodule with a red, pink or brown color and a diameter up to 22 mm.

terms.name: Decreased lecithin cholesterol acyl transferase level
terms.name_zh: 卵磷脂胆固醇酰基转移酶水平降低
terms.definition: Reduced level of the enzyme lecithin cholesterol acyl transferase.

terms.name: Reduced circulating CH50 activity
terms.definition: A diminished activity of the classical complement pathway as measured by the assay for 50% haemolytic complement (CH50) activity of serum.

terms.name: Increased circulating lactate dehydrogenase concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环乳酸脱氢酶浓度升高
terms.definition: An elevated level of the enzyme lactate dehydrogenase in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated serum 11-deoxycortisol
terms.definition: Increased concentration of 11-deoxycortisol in the circulation. 11-deoxycorticosterone, which is also known as simply deoxycorticosterone and 21-hydroxyprogesterone, is a steroid hormore that is produces in the adrenals and is a precursor to aldosterone.

terms.name: Macrozoospermia
terms.definition: Increased size of the head of sperm.

terms.name: Pharyngitis
terms.definition: Inflammation (due to infection or irritation) of the pharynx.

terms.name: Warm reactive autoantibody positivity
terms.definition: Warm reactive autoantibodies are RBC-directed immune responses that are maximally reactive at 37 degrees C.

terms.name: Achilles tendon calcification
terms.definition: Ectopic deposition of calcium salts in the Achilles tendon.

terms.name: Abnormal cardiac atrial physiology
terms.definition: An abnormality of the function of the cardiac atria.

terms.name: Reduced amygdala volume
terms.definition: A decrease in the volume (size) of the amygdyla.

terms.name: Abnormal papillary muscle morphology
synonyms: Morphological abnormality of the papillary muscles
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the papillary muscles of the left ventricle.

terms.name: Anomalous insertion of papillary muscle directly into anterior mitral leaflet
terms.name_zh: 乳头肌直接异常插入二尖瓣前叶
terms.definition: A congenital malformation in which one or both of the papillary muscles (posteromedial or anterolateral) insert directly (that is, without interpositioned chordae tendineae) into the anterior mitral leaflet.

terms.name: Displacement of the papillary muscles
terms.definition: Abnormal location of the insertion of a papillary muscle into the left ventricular wall.

terms.name: Anterior displacement of the papillary muscles
terms.definition: Abnormally anterior location of the papillary muscles of the left ventricle.

terms.name: Apically displaced anterolateral papillary muscle
terms.name_zh: 前外侧乳头肌心尖移位
terms.definition: Abnormal location of the insertion of the anterolateral papillary muscle near to the apex of the left ventricle. This feature may be appreciated by noting that this muscle is usually not seen in the apical level of the parasternal short-axis echocardiographic view,

terms.name: Testicular adrenal rest tumor
terms.definition: Testicular adrenal rest tumor (TART) is a abenign tumor of the testis. TART generally occurs multiply and bilaterally within the rete testis. Histologically, TART resemble adrenocortical tissue, which led to the name. The tumous are not encapsulated and consist of sheets or confluent cords of large polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm.

terms.name: Pyoderma gangrenosum
terms.definition: A deep skin ulcer with a well defined border, which is usually violet or blue. The ulcer edge is often undermined (worn and damaged) and the surrounding skin is erythematous and indurated. The ulcer often starts as a small papule or collection of papules, which break down to form small ulcers with a so called cat's paw appearance. These coalesce and the central area then undergoes necrosis to form a single ulcer.

terms.name: Delayed adrenarche
terms.definition: Occurrence of adrenarche at a later than normal age. Adrenarche normally occurs between six and eight years of age with increased adrenal androgen secretion; its exact biologic role is not well understood. It is accompanied by changes in pilosebaceous units, a transient growth spurt and the appearance of axillary and pubic hair in some children, but no sexual development.

terms.name: Abnormal CSF metabolite concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液代谢物浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal range of concentration of a metabolite in the cerebrospinal fluid.

terms.name: Decreased CSF 5-hydroxyindolacetic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液5-羟吲哚乙酸浓度降低
terms.definition: 5-HIAA (5-hydroxyindolacetic acid) concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal CSF protein concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal range of a protein concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid.

terms.name: Decreased CSF protein concentration
terms.definition: CSF total protein level is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Decreased CSF albumin concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液白蛋白浓度降低
terms.definition: CSF albumin level is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Increased CSF/serum albumin ratio
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液/血清白蛋白比值升高
terms.definition: An increase above normal limits of the ratio of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) albumin concentration to serum albumin concentration.

terms.name: High myoinositol in brain by MRS
synonyms: High myo-inositol in brain by MRS
terms.definition: An elevated level of myoinositol in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.name: Abnormal cell morphology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of cell structure.

terms.name: Abnormality of redox activity
terms.definition: An abnormality of the processes that maintain the redox environment of a cell or compartment within a cell, that is, the balance between reduction and oxidation chemical reactions.

terms.name: Increased reactive oxygen species production
terms.definition: An accumulation of free radical groups in the body inadequately neutralized by antioxidants, which creates a potentially unstable and damaging cellular environment linked to tissue damage.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating beta globulin concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of beta globulin in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Beta 2-microglobulinuria
terms.definition: Increased level of beta 2-microglobulins in the urine.

terms.name: Anagen effluvium
terms.definition: An abnormal loss of anagen (growth phase) hairs.

terms.name: Telogen effluvium
terms.definition: A type of hair loss characterized by an abnormal increase in dormant, telogen stage hair follicles.

terms.name: Congenital panfollicular nevus
terms.definition: A hamartomatous proliferation containing malformed hair follicles in various stages of development. Panfolliculomas are well-circumscribed lesions demonstrating all stages of follicular differentiation.

terms.name: Recurrent plantar mycosis
terms.definition: A history of repeated fungal infections located on the sole of the foot, usually manifested by scaling, maceration, and itching.

terms.name: Hyperpigmented papule
terms.definition: A papule (circumscribed, solid elevation of skin with no visible fluid, varying in size from a pinhead to less than 10mm in diameter at the widest point) that exhibits increased pigmentation (is darker) compared to the surrounding skin.

terms.name: Erythematous plaque
terms.definition: A plaque (a solid, raised, plateau-like (flat-topped) lesion greater than 1 cm in diameter) with a red or reddish color often associated with inflammation or irritation.

terms.name: Erythematous macule
terms.definition: A macule (flat, distinct, discolored area of skin less than 1 cm wide that does not involve any change in the thickness or texture of the skin) with a red or reddish color often associated with inflammation or irritation.

terms.name: Testicular lipomatosis
terms.definition: Multiple foci of adipocytes within the testicular interstitium, usually presenting as multiple bilateral ill-defined hyperechoic intratesticular lesions of different sizes but generally with maximum diameter of 4 mm.

terms.name: Periarticular calcification
terms.definition: Calcified deposits in soft tissue structures outside a joint.

terms.name: Atrial standstill
terms.definition: Atrial standstill or silent atrium is a rare condition presenting with the absence of electrical and mechanical activity in the atria. It presents with the absence of P waves, bradycardia, and wide QRS complex in the electrocardiogram.

terms.name: Self-neglect
terms.definition: A pathological neglect of personal needs and well-being that includes attending to self-grooming, personal care and the attention to cleanliness of personal space.

terms.name: Lipomyelomeningocele
terms.definition: A type of spinal dysraphism presenting as a subcutaneous fatty mass, that is, a spinal defect associated with lipomatous tissue, and covered by skin. The most usual location for lipomyelomeningocele is at the gluteal cleft.

terms.name: Cervical hemivertebrae
terms.definition: Absence of one half of the vertebral body in the cervical spine.

terms.name: Positive perchlorate discharge test
terms.definition: An abnormal result of the perchlorate discharge test. In this test, first radioactive iodine is administered, sufficient time is allowed to pass so that the radioactive iodine is captured by the thyroid,and then, perchlorate is administered orally. The perchlorate displaces non-organified iodide from the thyroid. The perchlorate discharge test is considered positive (abnormal) if there is an abnormally rapid loss of radioactive iodine from the thyroid.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating thyroglobulin concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环甲状腺球蛋白浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of thyroglobulin in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating thyroglobulin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血甲状腺球蛋白浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of thyroglobulin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Vaginal adenosis
terms.definition: Vaginal adenosis is defined by the presence of metaplastic cervical or endometrial epithelium within the vaginal wall, thought to be derived from persistent Müllerian (synonymous with paramesonephric) epithelium islets in postembryonic life.

terms.name: Fused labia majora
terms.definition: The outer labia are sealed together.

terms.name: Abnormal bladder morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the bladder.

terms.name: Detrusor sphincter dyssynergia
terms.name_zh: 逼尿肌括约肌协同失调
terms.definition: A urodynamic anomaly characterized by bladder outlet obstruction from detrusor muscle contraction with concomitant involuntary urethral sphincter activation.

terms.name: Bladder duplication
terms.definition: A congenital anomaly characterized by the presence of two bladders.

terms.name: Myocardial bridging
terms.definition: A congenital variant of a coronary artery in which a portion of an epicardial coronary artery (most frequently the middle segment of the left anterior descending artery) takes an intramuscular course.

terms.name: Venous stenosis
terms.definition: Narrowing of a vein due to intimal hyperplasia and fibrosis.

terms.name: Microcoria
terms.definition: A small pupil (typically diameter less than 2 mm) that dilates poorly or not at all in response to topically administered mydriatic drugs.

terms.name: Palmoplantar erythema
terms.definition: Redness of the skin of the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.

terms.name: Coated aorta
terms.definition: Regular circumferential periaortic fibrosis involving the whole aorta and leading to a coated aorta appearance on computed tomography scans

terms.name: Descending aorta hypoplasia
terms.definition: Significant luminal narrowing of a long segment of the descending aorta.

terms.name: Abnormal coronary artery physiology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the function of a coronary artery.

terms.name: Coronary artery spasm
terms.definition: A brief and sudden narrowing of a coronary artery.

terms.name: Aceruloplasminemia
terms.definition: Absence of ceruloplasmin in the blood.

terms.name: Class I obesity
terms.definition: Obesity with a body mass index of 30 to 34.9 kg per square meter.

terms.name: Class II obesity
terms.definition: Obesity with a body mass index of 35 to 39.9 kg per square meter.

terms.name: Class III obesity
terms.definition: Obesity with a body mass index of 40 kg per square meter or higher.

terms.name: Overweight
terms.definition: Increased body weight with a body mass index of 25-29.9 kg per square meter.

terms.name: Anomalous coronary artery arising from the opposite sinus
terms.name_zh: 对侧窦起源冠状动脉异常
terms.definition: Origin of the right coronary artery (RCA) from the left sinus of Valsalva or of the left main (LM) or left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery from the right sinus of Valsalva.

terms.name: Anomalous origin of the circumflex artery from the right sinus of Valsalva
terms.name_zh: 回旋支异常起源于右瓦氏窦
terms.definition: The circumflex coronary artery originates from the right aortic sinus of Valsalva.

terms.name: Coronary artery sandwich anomaly
terms.name_zh: 冠状动脉夹层三明治畸形
synonyms: Anomalous coronary artery with aortic origin and course between the great arteries
terms.definition: Origin of the right coronary artery (RCA) from the left sinus of Valsalva or of the left main (LM) or left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery from the right sinus of Valsalva, with the additional feature that the artery passes between the two great arteries. This carries a risk of the artery being compressed by these two vessels,

terms.name: Yellow papule
terms.definition: A papule with yellow color.

terms.name: Gottron's papules
terms.definition: Violaceous papules overlying the dorsal and lateral aspects of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints.

terms.name: Piezogenic pedal papules
terms.definition: Flesh-colored or yellowish papules, 2 mm or larger, that are responses to internal mechanical pressure and weakness in the connective tissue in the dermis, appear commonly over the medial aspect of the heel, but in some cases on the wrists. They are thought to represent herniations of adipose tissue through the plantar fascia retinaculum.

terms.name: Nevus spilus
terms.definition: A tan, regularly bordered patch with darker macules within the lesion.

terms.name: Nevus sebaceus
terms.definition: A solitary yellow-orange slightly raised plaque typically on scalp or face. The plaque typically thickens and becomes more verrucous or pebbly during childhood.

terms.name: Skin-colored papule
terms.definition: A papule with the same color as the surrounding skin.

terms.name: Scleral rupture
terms.definition: Breakage of the sclera.

terms.name: Morning glory anomaly
terms.definition: An abnormality of the optic nerve in which the optic nerve is large and funneled and displays a conical excavation of the optic disc. The optic disc appears dysplastic.

terms.name: Delayed thelarche
terms.definition: Later than normal development of the breasts.

terms.name: Coronary-pulmonary artery fistula
terms.definition: A congenital malformation with abnormal connection between one of the coronary arteries and the pulmonary artery.

terms.name: Hypoplastic hippocampus
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the hippocampus.

terms.name: Visual gaze preference
terms.definition: An abnormality of gaze that can be observed following an acute supranuclear cerebral lesion (e.g., stroke) that is characterized by an acute inability to direct gaze contralateral to the side of the lesion and is accompanied by a tendency for tonic deviation of the eyes toward the side of the lesion.

terms.name: Multiple biliary hamartomas
terms.definition: Multiple biliary hamartomas are a rare clinicopathologic entity, consisting of small (less than 1.5cm), usually multiple and nodular cystic lesions in the liver.

terms.name: Calcinosis cutis
terms.definition: Deposition of calcium in the skin.

terms.name: Increased body fat percentage
terms.definition: The percentage of fat as a part of total body weight above the norm, usually defined as 32% for females and 25% for males.

terms.name: Elongated chordae tendinae of the mitral valve
terms.definition: Abnormal increased in length of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve.

terms.name: Abnormal morphology of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve, whose main function is to transmit the contraction and relaxation of the papillary muscles during the cardiac cycle, thus ensuring the closing of the leaflets of the mitral valve.

terms.name: Palmoplantar scaling skin
terms.definition: Loss of the outer layer of the epidermis in large, scale-like flakes localized to the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot.

terms.name: Scaling skin on fingertip
terms.definition: Loss of the outer layer of the epidermis in large, scale-like flakes localized to one or more fingertips.

terms.name: Psoriasiform lesion
terms.definition: A skin lesions that resembles the lesions observed in psoriasis, viz., an erythematous plaque covered by fine silvery scales. Psoriasiform lesions can be observed in psoriasis as well as in other conditions including allergic contact dermatitis, seborrhoeic dermatitis, Atopic dermatitis, pityriasis rubra, and lichen simplex chronicus.

terms.name: Serpiginous cutaneous lesion
terms.definition: A skin lesion with a snake- or serpent-like distribution.

terms.name: Annular cutaneous lesion
terms.definition: A lesion of the skin with a ring-like distribution.

terms.name: Hyperpigmented nodule
terms.definition: A nodule of the skin that exhibits an increased amount of pigmentation.

terms.name: Xanthomas of the palmar creases
terms.definition: The presence of multiple xanthomas (xanthomata) in the skin distributed in the creases of the palm of the hand. Xanthomas are yellowish, firm, lipid-laden nodules in the skin.

terms.name: Harlequin phenomenon
terms.definition: The Harlequin phenomenon consists of a sudden change in skin color, resulting in two different body colors, one on each half of the body.

terms.name: Positive pathergy test
terms.definition: With the pathergy test, a small, sterile needle is inserted into the skin of the forearm. The site of injectionis circuled and observed after one and two days. If a small red bump or pustule at the site of needle insertion occurs, the pathergy test is considered to have a positive (abnormal) result.

terms.name: Ocular melanocytosis
terms.definition: A congenital lesion of the sclera characterized by unilateral patchy but extensive slate-gray or bluish discoloration of the sclera . The conjunctiva are spared.

terms.name: Shawl sign
terms.definition: Erythematous, poikilodermatous macules distributed in a shawl pattern over the shoulders, arms and upper back.

terms.name: V-sign
terms.definition: Erythematous, poikilodermatous macules distributed in a V-shaped distribution over the anterior neck and chest.

terms.name: Plantar edema
terms.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin on sole of the foot.

terms.name: Palmar edema
terms.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin on the palm of the hand.

terms.name: Abnormal B cell subset distribution
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of any B cell subpopulation, measured as percentage of total CD19+ or CD20+ B cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Abnormal T cell subset number
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of absolute number (either count per volume or percentage of total lymphocytes) of any T cell subpopulation, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Abnormal mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
terms.name_zh: 平均红细胞血红蛋白浓度异常
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal range of the average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell (27 to 31 picograms/cell). A reduced mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) may indicate a hypochromic anemia, but the MCH may be normal if both the total hemoglobin and the red blood cell count are reduced.

terms.name: Decreased mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
terms.name_zh: 平均红细胞血红蛋白浓度降低
terms.definition: A reduction from the normal range of the average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell (27 to 31 picograms/cell). A reduced mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) may indicate a hypochromic anemia, but the MCH may be normal if both the total hemoglobin and the red blood cell count are reduced.

terms.name: Increased mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
terms.name_zh: 平均红细胞血红蛋白浓度升高
terms.definition: An elevation over the normal range of the average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell (27 to 31 picograms/cell).

terms.name: Eccentric visual fixation
terms.definition: A uniocular condition in which there is fixation of an object by a point other than the fovea. This point adopts the principal visual direction. The degree of the eccentric fixation is defined by its distance from the fovea in degrees.

terms.name: Elevated circulating ribitol concentration
synonyms: Increased level of ribitol in serum
terms.definition: The concentration of ribitol in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Optic nerve misrouting
terms.definition: Abnormal decussation of the visual pathways, typically identified using visual evoked potentials (VEP) (asymmetrical distribution of the VEP over the posterior scalp).

terms.name: Periorbital purpura
terms.definition: Multiple red/purple spots on the skin that surrounds the eyes that do not blanch (whiten) upon pressure. Purpura is caused by subcutaneous bleeding.

terms.name: Periorbital ecchymosis with tarsal plate sparing
terms.definition: Subcutaneous bleeding with a diameter greater than 1 cm (ecchymosis). The bleeding does not extend into the tarsal plate (the comparatively thick, elongated plates of dense connective tissue within the eyelid) due to an anatomic structure called the orbital septum, which limits extravasation of blood beyond the tarsal plate.

terms.name: Yellow nodule
terms.definition: A type of skin nodule (a lesions that is greater than either 10mm in both width and depth, and most frequently centered in the dermis or subcutaneous fat) with a yellowish coloration (that reflects a high lipid content of the lesion).

terms.name: Periungual teleangiectasia
terms.definition: Telangiectasia (small dilated blood vessels) located near to the fingernails or toenails.

terms.name: Lamellar cataract with riders
terms.definition: Lamellar cataracts with associated linear lens opacities radially extending towards the periphery of the lens.

terms.name: Coronary cataract
terms.definition: A type of cataract characterized by club-shaped and dot opacities distributed radially in the deep cortex. These lens opacities surround the nucleus in an appearance that is though to resemble a crown.

terms.name: Anterior chamber cells
terms.definition: Tiny deposits corresponding to cells floating in the anterior chamber of the eye. This appearance is typically associated with intraocular inflammation leading to breakdown of the blood-aqueous barrier and resulting in an increase in the number of cells and in the aqueous humor. Grading (SUN Working Group) is performed by estimating the number of cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

terms.name: Anterior chamber cells grade 1+
terms.definition: Anterior chamber cells with 6-15 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

terms.name: Anterior chamber cells grade 0.5+
terms.definition: Anterior chamber cells with 1-5 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

terms.name: Anterior chamber cells grade 0
terms.definition: Anterior chamber cells with less than one cell in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

terms.name: Anterior chamber cells grade 2+
terms.definition: Anterior chamber cells with 16-25 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

terms.name: Anterior chamber cells grade 3+
terms.definition: Anterior chamber cells with 26-50 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

terms.name: Anterior chamber cells grade 4+
terms.definition: Anterior chamber cells with more than 50 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

terms.name: Central serous chorioretinopathy
terms.name_zh: 中心性浆液性脉络膜视网膜病变
terms.definition: An anomaly of the retina with serous detachment of the neurosensory retina secondary to one or more focal lesions of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), and associated with blurred vision, usually in one eye only and perceived typically by the patient as a dark spot in the center of the visual field with associated micropsia and metamorphopsia. Normal vision often recurs spontaneously within a few months.

terms.name: Polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy
terms.definition: The presence of aneurysmal 'polypoidal' lesions in the choroidal vasculature. The aneurysmal dilatations, also known as polyps, may be found at subfoveal, juxtafoveal, extrafoveal, peripapillary or even peripheral regions. These polypoidal dilatations may be visible as reddish-orange subretinal nodules during ophthalmoscopic examination. The polypoidal lesions are best detected on indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) and might be associated with a branching vascular network (BVN) of neovascularization.

terms.name: Choroidal vascular hyperpermeability
terms.definition: Increased tendency of choiroidal blood vessels to allow fluids to leak characterized by multifocal choroidal hyperfluorescence on indocyanine green angiography (ICGA).

terms.name: Christmas tree cataract
terms.definition: A type of cataract that shows a spectacular display of multiple colors that glitters with the change of incident light like an illuminated Christmas tree.

terms.name: Punctal stenosis
terms.definition: Punctal stenosis is a condition in which the external opening of the lacrimal canaliculus is narrowed or occluded.

terms.name: Mild myopia
terms.definition: A mild form of myopia with up to -3.00 diopters.

terms.name: Macular hemorrhage
terms.definition: Bleeding occurring within the macula lutea of the retina.

terms.name: Abnormal superior vena cava morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the principal vein draining blood from the upper portion of the body and delivering it to the right ventricle of the heart.

terms.name: Abnormal inferior vena cava morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the principal vein draining blood from the lower portion of the body.

terms.name: Aortic valve prolapse
terms.definition: Aortic valve prolapse can be diagnosed when either or both of the right or non-coronary aortic valve cusps (seen in the cross sectional echocardiographic long axis view) show backward bowing towards the left ventricle beyond a line joining the points of attachment of the aortic valve leaflets to the annulus.

terms.name: Abnormal left atrium morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the left atrium.

terms.name: Abnormal right atrium morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the right atrium.

terms.name: Foveal hemorrhage
terms.definition: Bleeding occurring within the fovea.

terms.name: Submacular hemorrhage
terms.definition: Bleeding between the neurosensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) arising from the choroidal or retinal circulation.

terms.name: Tapetal-like fundal reflex
terms.definition: Golden, scintillating, particulate reflection noted on fundus examination (typically in the macula and sparing the fovea). The term tapetal is used to describe this 'metallic' sheen appearance as it is thought to be similar to the 'tapetal' reflex seen in the eyes of certain animals.

terms.name: Hypotropia
terms.definition: A form of manifest strabismus (heterotropia) in which one eye is deviated downwards when both eyes are open.

terms.name: Hyperphoria
terms.definition: Tendency for the visual axis of one eye to be higher than that of the other.

terms.name: Hypertropia
terms.definition: A type of strabismus characterized by permanent upward deviation of the visual axis of one eye.

terms.name: Hyperdeviation
terms.definition: A type of strabismus in which the visual axis of one eye is higher than that of the other.

terms.name: Hypodeviation
terms.definition: A type of strabismus in which the visual axis of one eye is lower than that of the other.

terms.name: Cyclodeviation
terms.definition: Cyclodeviation is defined as the rotation of an eyeball along the anteroposterior axis and cyclotropia as a misalignment of cyclodeviation between the two eyes.

terms.name: Abnormal extraocular muscle physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the muscles of the eye.

terms.name: Abnormal superior oblique muscle physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the superior oblique muscle, a fusiform muscle that originates in the upper, medial side of the orbit. The superior oblique muscle abducts, depresses and internally rotates the eye, and is the only extraocular muscle innervated by the fourth cranial nerve.

terms.name: Superior oblique muscle weakness
terms.definition: Decreased strength of the superior oblique muscle.
