terms.name: Superior oblique muscle restriction
terms.definition: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the superior oblique muscle.

terms.name: Superior oblique muscle overaction
terms.definition: An ocular motility abnormality characterized by an overacting superior oblique muscle resulting to vertical incomitance of the eyes in lateral gaze. On examination, this is commonly seen as a downshoot of the adducting eye occurring when gaze is directed into the field of action of the inferior oblique muscle, producing a greater downward excursion of the adducted eye than of the abducted eye.

terms.name: Superior oblique muscle underaction
terms.definition: Reduced ocular movement of the superior oblique muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

terms.name: Abnormal inferior oblique muscle physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the inferior oblique muscle, an extraocular muscle that has its origin on the maxillary bone just posterior to the inferior medial orbital rim and lateral to the nasolacrimal canal and that is innervated by the inferior branch of the oculomotor nerve.

terms.name: Inferior oblique muscle restriction
terms.definition: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the inferior oblique muscle.

terms.name: Inferior oblique muscle weakness
terms.definition: Decreased strength of the inferior oblique muscle.

terms.name: Inferior oblique muscle overaction
terms.definition: A common ocular motility disorder characterized by vertical incomitance of the eyes in lateral gaze. In primary inferior oblique muscle overaction, an upshoot of the adducting eye occurs when gaze is directed into the field of action of the inferior oblique muscle, producing a greater upward excursion of the adducted eye than of the abducted eye.

terms.name: Abnormal inferior rectus muscle physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the inferior rectus muscle, which is innervated by the inferior division of oculomotor nerve and functions in the depression, adduction, and lateral rotation (extortion) of the eye.

terms.name: Inferior rectus muscle weakness
terms.definition: Decreased strength of the inferior rectus muscle.

terms.name: Inferior rectus muscle restriction
terms.definition: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the inferior rectus muscle.

terms.name: Abnormal superior rectus muscle physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the superior rectus muscle, an extraocular muscle that is innervated by the superior division of the oculomotor nerve, and whose primary function is the elevation of the globe.

terms.name: Orbital schwannoma
terms.definition: A schwannoma (benign, usually encapsulated slow growing tumor composed of Schwann cells) located in the orbit.

terms.name: Lid lag on downgaze
terms.definition: Delayed descent of the upper eyelid on downgaze. Also described by some authors as von Graefe sign.

terms.name: Abnormal medial rectus muscle physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the medial rectus muscle, an extraocular muscle that is innervated by the inferior division of the oculomotor nerve and whose sole action is the adduction of the eyeball.

terms.name: Upper eyelid entropion
terms.definition: An inward turning (inversion) of the margin of the upper eyelid.

terms.name: Cicatricial ectropion
terms.definition: An outward turning (eversion) or rotation of the eyelid margin (i.e., ectropion) caused by shortening or contraction of the anterior or middle lamellae related to scarring.

terms.name: Anterior blepharitis
terms.definition: A type of blepharitis that affects the eyelid skin, base of the eyelashes, and the eyelash follicles.

terms.name: Posterior blepharitis
terms.definition: A type of blepharitis that affects the meibomian glands and meibomian gland orifices. This abnormality can be associated with a spectrum of appearances ranging from meibomian seborrhoea (foaming meibomian gland secretions) and meibomianitis (inflamed meibomian glands), to chalazia.

terms.name: Epicanthus superciliaris
terms.definition: A type of epicanthus in which more extensive epicanthal folds with their origins in the eyebrow cover, pass in front of and lateral to the medial canthus (middle corner of the eye).

terms.name: Corneal astigmatism
terms.definition: A type of refractive error related abnormal curvatures on the anterior or posterior surface of the cornea.

terms.name: Focal emotional seizure
terms.definition: Seizures presenting with an emotion or the appearance of having an emotion as an early prominent feature, such as fear, spontaneous joy or euphoria, laughing (gelastic), or crying, (dacrystic). These emotional seizures may occur with or without objective clinical signs of a seizure evident to the observer.

terms.name: Abscess
terms.definition: An abscess is a localized collection of purulent material surrounded by inflammation and granulation.

terms.name: Sterile abscess
terms.definition: An abscess not caused by infection with pyogenic bacteria. Operationally, a sterile abscess is inferred if investigations of an abscess fail to reveal evidence of pathogenic organisms.

terms.name: Abnormal total plasma cell count
terms.definition: An abnormal number of plasma cells in the blood circulation. Plasma cells are terminally differentiated B cells dedicated to the production of a high amount of antibodies.

terms.name: Reduced plasma cell count
terms.definition: An abnormally low number of plasma cells in the blood circulation. Plasma cells are the the effector cells dedicated to the production of a high amount of antibodies.

terms.name: Elevated plasma cell count
terms.definition: An abnormally high number of plasma cells in the blood circulation. Plasma cells are the the effector cells dedicated to the production of a high amount of antibodies.

terms.name: Decreased effector memory CD4+ T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: 效应记忆CD4+T细胞比例降低
synonyms: Decreased proportion of CD4-positive effector memory T cells
Decreased proportion of effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
terms.definition: An abnormally decreased proportion of effector memory CD4+ T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These are memory cells that are short-lived cells that migrate to the site of an infection and attempt to eliminate the pathogen. These cells have the phenotype CD3-positive, CD4-positive, CD62L-negative, CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

terms.name: Increased effector memory CD4+ T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: 效应记忆CD4+T细胞比例升高
synonyms: Increased CD4+ effector memory T cell proportion
Increased effector memory CD4-positive T cell proportion
Increased proportion of CD4+ effector memory T cells
Increased proportion of CD4-positive effector memory T cells
Increased proportion of effector CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
terms.definition: An abnormally increased proportion of effector memory CD4+ T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These are memory cells that are short-lived cells that migrate to the site of an infection and attempt to eliminate the pathogen. These cells may have a CD3/CD4/CD62L-/CD45RA phenotype.

terms.name: Increased circulating oleate level
terms.definition: An abnormally high concentration of oleic acid (oleate) in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Increased circulating octadecanoate level
terms.name_zh: 血循环硬脂酸水平升高
terms.definition: An abnormally high concentration of octadecanoate in the blood circulation. Octadecanoate is a fatty acid anion 18:0 that is the conjugate base of octadecanoic acid (stearic acid).

terms.name: Increased circulating myristoleate level
terms.name_zh: 血循环肉豆蔻脑酸水平升高
terms.definition: An abnormally high concentration of myristoleate in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Anti-myelin-associated glycoprotein antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗髓鞘相关糖蛋白抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against myelin-associated glycoprotein (MAG).

terms.name: Argininosuccinic aciduria
terms.definition: Increased amount of argininosuccinate in the urine.

terms.name: Alpha-aminobutyric aciduria
terms.definition: Increased amount of alpha-aminobutyric acid in the urine.

terms.name: Abnormal ureter morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the ureter. The ureter is the duct by which urine passes from the kidney to the bladder.

terms.name: Abnormal ureter physiology
terms.definition: A functional abnormality of the ureter. The ureter is the duct by which urine passes from the kidney to the bladder.

terms.name: Ureteral polyp
terms.definition: A growth protruding from the mucous membrane of the ureter. Ureteral polyps can be attached to the ureter by a broad base or a thin stalk.

terms.name: Endometritis
synonyms: Inflammation of the inner lining of the uterus
terms.definition: Inflammation of the inner lining of the uterus (endometrium).

terms.name: Vasospasm
terms.definition: Narrowing of an artery due to constriction of the blood vessels.

terms.name: Elevated urinary N-butyrylglycine
terms.definition: An increased level of N-butyrylglycine in the urine.

terms.name: Increased urinary zinc level
terms.definition: An abnormally elevated amount of zinc in the urine, typically as assessed by a 24 hour urine collection.

terms.name: Abnormal urinary mineral level
terms.definition: An abnormal concentration or amount of a mineral in the urine. Medically relevant minerals include calcium, phosphorus, potassium, sodium, chloride, magnesium, iron, zinc, iodine, chromium, copper, fluoride, molybdenum, manganese, and selenium.

terms.name: Elevated circulating glycolate concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环乙醇酸浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of glycolate in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Tarlov cyst
terms.definition: A cerebrospinal fluid-filled nerve root cyst most often localized in the sacral spine.

terms.name: Fixation-off epileptiform discharges
terms.definition: Fixation off sensitivity (FOS) is characterized by posterior or generalized epileptiform discharges that consistently occur with conditions that eliminate central vision, such as closed eyes, complete darkness, modified Ganzfeld stimulation (using a large white surface without visual cues), and Frenzel lenses. The FOS electroencephalogram (EEG) pattern usually consists of spikes/polyspikes and waves localized in occipital regions (bilateral or unilateral) or generalized discharges. It is usually inhibited by fixation of gaze, observing patterns, or intermittent photic stimulation (e.g., flashing light or patterns used as stimuli during the recording of the EEG).

terms.name: Bilateral polymicrogyria
terms.definition: Polymicrogyria that affects all or some of both cerebral hemispheres.

terms.name: Steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome
terms.definition: A type of nephrotic syndrome in which complete remission (albumin urine dipstick negative/trace or proteinuria <4mg/m2/d or urinary protein to creatinine ratio <200mg/g (<20 mg/mmol) for 3 consecutive days) is achieved within initial 4 weeks of corticosteroid therapy.

terms.name: Steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome with infrequent relapses
terms.definition: A type of steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome in which relapses occur at a frequency of one relapse (albumin urine dipstick at least 3+ or proteinuria over 40 mg/m2/d or urinary protein to creatinine ratio at least 2000 mg/g for 3 consecutive days) within 6 months of initial response, or one to three relapses in any 12-month period.

terms.name: Steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome with frequent relapses
terms.definition: A type of steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome in which relapses occur at a frequency of two or more relapses (albumin urine dipstick at least 3+ or proteinuria over 40 mg/m2/d or urinary protein to creatinine ratio at least 2000 mg/g for 3 consecutive days) within 6 months of initial response or four or more relapses in any 12-month period.

terms.name: Steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome
terms.definition: A type of nephrotic syndrome in which two consecutive relapses (albumin urine dipstick at least 3+ or proteinuria greater than 40 mg/m2/d or urinary protein to creatinine ratio at least 2000 mg/g for 3 consecutive days) occur during corticosteroid therapy, or within 14 days of ceasing therapy.

terms.name: Abnormal placental adhesion into the uterine wall
terms.name_zh: 胎盘粘连入子宫壁异常
terms.definition: Abnormal placental adhesion is characterized by an anomalous adherence of the placenta to the uterine wall. Based on the degree of adhesion, placental invasion can be classified into accreta, increta, or percreta.

terms.name: Placenta percreta
synonyms: Abnormal placental pentration beyond the uterine wall
terms.definition: Placenta percreta is a rare form of morbidly adherent placenta with penetration through the myometrium reaching serosa and even adjacent pelvic organs.

terms.name: Placenta accreta
terms.definition: Abnormally firm adherence of the placenta to the uterine wall.

terms.name: Placenta increta
terms.definition: Abnormal placental pentration into but not beyond the uterine wall.

terms.name: Prenatal double bubble sign
terms.definition: Sonographic detection of a double bubble sign in the upper abdomen is strongly indicative of duodenal obstruction. One bubble represents fetal stomach, and the other is attributed to a dilated proximal part of the duodenum; continuity between both bubbles is required for the sign.

terms.name: Decreased circulating creatine kinase activity
terms.name_zh: 血循环肌酸激酶活性降低
synonyms: Decreased creatine kinase level in blood
Reduced creatine kinase level in blood
terms.definition: The activity of creatine kinase in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Chiari type II malformation
terms.definition: A type of Chiari malformation that consists of brainstem herniation and a towering cerebellum in addition to the herniated cerebellar tonsils and vermis due to an open distal spinal dysraphism/myelomeningocele.

terms.name: Chiari type III malformation
terms.definition: A type of Chiari malformation that involves herniation of the hindbrain (cerebellum with or without the brainstem) into a low occipital or high cervical meningoencephalocele.

terms.name: Abnormal fetal skeletal morphology
terms.definition: An anomalous structural finding of the fetal skeleton. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other terms from the skeletal hierarchy can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

terms.name: Reduced fetal femur/foot length ratio
terms.definition: This ratio relates the length of the fetal femur to that of the fetal foot. The ratio is approximately 1 throughout the age range of 14 to 40 weeks of gestation. A substantial reduction in the raio can help differentiate fetuses that have dysplastic limb reduction from those whose limbs are short because of constitutional factors or IUGR. It can reduce the problem of an unknown gestational age and help to distinguish between fetal skeletal dysplasia and intrauterine growth retardation caused by other factors.

terms.name: Moderate to late preterm birth
terms.definition: Birth at 32 to 36 completed weeks of gestation.

terms.name: Extremely preterm birth
terms.definition: Birth before 28 completed weeks of gestation (up to and including 27 weeks and 6 days of gestation).

terms.name: Very preterm birth
terms.definition: Birth before 32 completed weeks of gestation (28 up to but not including 32 weeks).

terms.name: Fetal neck anomaly
terms.definition: A structural anomaly in the fetal neck region. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

terms.name: Abnormal neck morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the neck region.

terms.name: Abnormal neck physiology
terms.definition: Any functional anomaly of the neck region.

terms.name: Syntelencephaly
terms.definition: Syntelencephaly is a rare malformation that consists of an abnormal midline connection of the cerebral hemispheres in the posterior frontal and parietal regions, with interhemispheric separation of the basal forebrain, anterior frontal lobes, and occipital regions.

terms.name: Fetal pericardial effusion
terms.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid in which the heart is partially or completely surrounded by fluid that is seen in all views and the thickness of the fluid as observed by prenatal ultrasound is above age-dependent norms.

terms.name: Fetal skin edema
terms.definition: A separation of skin in one or more regions of the body or even along the entire length of body wall (to a degree greater than gestational-age related norms) related to pathologically increased fluid accumulation in the subcutaneous tissue.

terms.name: Loculated ascites
terms.definition: A type of ascites (peritoneal fluid collection) that is divided into loculi (compartments) by septa (fibrous walls). Ascites fluid can become loculated when confined by adhesions, malignancy or infection.

terms.name: Meconium pseudocyst
terms.definition: A meconium-containing cyst in the peritoneal space . Meconium pseudocysts form in the presence of meconium peritonitis, which is defined as a sterile peritonitis caused by escape of meconium from the intestinal tract into the general peritoneal cavity during the fetal or perinatal period. When the extruded meconium becomes walled off, it can form a rim-calcified mass representing the meconium pseudocyst.

terms.name: Premature closure of the ductus arteriosus
synonyms: Idiopathic constriction of the fetal ductus arteriosus
Idiopathic constriction of the foetal ductus arteriosus
terms.definition: A prenatal partial or complete closure of the ductus arteriosus (i.e., prior to delivery).

terms.name: Fetal pleural effusion
terms.definition: Fetal pleural effusion is the accumulation of excess fluid in the layers of tissue (pleura) lining the lungs and wall of the chest. It may be primary, also termed hydrothorax, occurring as an isolated finding or it may be secondary, most commonly resulting from non-immune hydrops.

terms.name: Fetal chylothorax
terms.definition: The presence of chyle (a type of lipid-rich lymph) in the pleural space (the space surrounding the lung) as observed in a fetus.

terms.name: Fetal hydrothorax
terms.definition: Accumulation of lymphatic fluid in the pleural space. This finding is usually observed by prenatal sonography. Once neonatal feeding is established and the lymphatic fluid contains chyle, transformation to chylothorax may be observed.

terms.name: Diskitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of an intervertebral disk or disk space.

terms.name: Compound muscle action potential amplitude facilitation
terms.name_zh: 复合肌肉动作电位波幅易化
terms.definition: Compound muscle action potential amplitude (CMAP) facilitation denotes an increase in tendon reflexes, strength, or CMAP amplitude after 10 seconds of maximal voluntary contraction.

terms.name: Distal clavicular thinning
terms.definition: Abnormally reduced diameter (cross section) of the clavicles that is limited to the distal region.

terms.name: Crouch gait
terms.definition: A gait disturbance that is characterized by excessive ankle dorsiflexion, knee and hip flexion during the stance phase.

terms.name: Abnormal amyloid beta 42 peptide CSF concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液β淀粉样蛋白42浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of amyloid beta 42 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Amyloid beta is a peptide of 36-43 amino acids that is processed from the Amyloid precursor protein. ABeta42, which is 42 amino acids in length, is the longer form.

terms.name: Decreased amyloid beta 42 peptide CSF concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液β淀粉样蛋白42浓度降低
terms.definition: A reduction from the normal concentration of amyloid beta 42 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

terms.name: Increased amyloid beta 42 peptide CSF concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液β淀粉样蛋白42肽浓度升高
terms.definition: An elevation above the normal concentration of amyloid beta 42 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

terms.name: Abnormal amyloid beta 40 peptide CSF concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液β淀粉样蛋白40浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of amyloid beta 42 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Amyloid beta is a peptide of 36-43 amino acids that is processed from the Amyloid precursor protein. ABeta40, which is 40 amino acids in length, is the shorter form.

terms.name: Increased amyloid beta 40 peptide CSF concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液β淀粉样蛋白40肽浓度升高
terms.definition: An elevation above the normal concentration of amyloid beta 40 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

terms.name: Abnormal amyloid beta peptide CSF concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液β淀粉样蛋白浓度异常
terms.definition: Any anomaly in the concentration of a cleaved APP amyloid beta protein fragment in the cerebrospinal fluid.

terms.name: Extra-abdominal umbilical vein varix
terms.definition: Focal dilatation of the extra-abdominal portion of the umbilical vein. An extra-abdominal umbilical varix is difficult to diagnose prenatally as it can appear like a cyst on ultrasound prior to birth.

terms.name: Fetal intra-abdominal umbilical vein varix
terms.definition: Fetal intra-abdominal umbilical vein varix (FIUVV) is defined by the focal dilatation of the fetal umbilical vein between its entry in the abdomen and its ending in the portal system. The dilatation can be defined using one of the following criteria: a portion of intra-abdominal umbilical vein that is at least 50% wider than the non-dilated portion; a dilatation of 9 mm or more, or a dilatation greater than 2 SD above the mean value for gestational age.

terms.name: Impaired fasting glucose
terms.definition: Impaired fasting glucose (IFG) is indicated by a fasting plasma glucose above normal but below the diabetic range. Levels between 110 mg/dl (6.1 mmol/l) to 125 mg/dl (6.9 mmol/l) are diagnostic of IFG.

terms.name: Atelencephaly
terms.definition: A defect of development of the brain characterized by absence of the telencephalon (embryonic structure from which the mature cerebrum develops).

terms.name: Pituitary macroadenoma
terms.definition: A pituitary gland adenoma that is larger than 10mm.

terms.name: Pituitary microadenoma
terms.definition: A pituitary adenoma that is less than 10 mm in diameter.

terms.name: Mucus plug
terms.definition: Mucus that is abnormally thick in consistency (ie, inspissated) and plugs the airway is known as a mucus plug. Mucus plugs consist of mucins and cells and can partially or completely obstruct one or more airways and cause serious consequences, including atelectasis and recurrent infection.

terms.name: Airway casts
terms.definition: A replicate of airways from accumulated and condensed mucous and cellular material. These semisolid occlusions take the shape of the airway within they are formed, leading to obstruction of the tracheobronchial tree with consecutive respiratory insufficiency. Based on their principal composition, one can differentiate fibrin casts and mucin casts. Plastic bronchitis is the name of the condition characterized by the formation of airway casts.

terms.name: Fibrin casts
terms.definition: A type of airway casts that consist of plasma components and inflammatory cells.

terms.name: Mucin casts
terms.definition: A type of airway casts that consist of impacted mucus.

terms.name: Perisylvian FDG hypermetabolism
terms.definition: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography and computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT) evaluates the glucose metabolism of the brain. FDG uptake is interpreted to represent glycolysis. This term therefore represents an abnormally increased FDG uptake (increased glucose metabolism) in the region of the brain that surrounds the Sylvian fissure.

terms.name: Anhydramnios
terms.definition: A complete or near-complete lack of amniotic fluid surrounding a fetus. This finding can be observed sonographically in the third trimesters if the deepest pocket of amniotic fluid is less than or equal to 2 cm.

terms.name: Distended jugular lymphatic sacs
terms.definition: The jugular lymphatic sacs (JLS) are a physiological and temporary part of fetal lymphatic development. They are formed from small buds of lymphatic endothelial cells arising from the internal jugular veins. By 14 weeks gestation they have developed into lymphatic nodes which drain into the systemic circulation. Visibility of JLS on ultrasound past 14 weeks of gestation implies distension and this may be associated with raised nuchal translucency.

terms.name: Type 1 schizencephaly
terms.definition: A type of Schizencephaly in which there is a trans-mantle column of abnormal gray matter but no evidence of a CSF-containing cleft on MR imaging.

terms.name: Type 2 schizencephaly
terms.definition: A type of Schizencephaly in which CSF-containing cleft is present with abutting lining lips of abnormal gray matter that are opposed to each other.

terms.name: Type 3 schizencephaly
terms.definition: A type of Schizencephaly in which CSF-containing cleft present with non-abutting lining lips of abnormal gray matter.

terms.name: Abnormal fetal nasal bone visualization
terms.definition: Abnormal appearance or non-visualization (apparent absence) of the nasal bone of a fetus in first trimester sonographic screening. Assessment of the fetal nasal bone is generally performed at 11-14 weeks gestational age.

terms.name: Absent fetal nasal bone
terms.definition: The nasal bone is considered absent when it is not visualized on a midsagittal view of the profile. In the second trimester, a true midsagittal view of the fetal profile is obtained and magnified to fill the majority of the image space. The nasal bone appears as an echogenic linear structure below the skin edge. The optimal angle of insonation is 45 degrees to the longitudinal axis of the fetal nasal bone. If the angle of insonation is 0 or 180 degrees, the nasal bone may appear artificially absent. The presence or absence of the nasal bone may be determined at the time of the 11- to 14-week ultrasound examination and used as part of the risk assessment for aneuploidy.

terms.name: Hypoplastic fetal nasal bone
terms.definition: Length of the nasal bone below a predetermined cut-off as seen on antenatal ultrasound using standard imaging techniques.

terms.name: Early young adult onset
terms.definition: Onset of disease at an age of greater than or equal to 16 to under 19 years.

terms.name: Intermediate young adult onset
terms.definition: Onset of disease at an age of greater than or equal to 19 to under 25 years.

terms.name: Late young adult onset
terms.definition: Onset of disease at an age of greater than or equal to 25 to under 40 years.

terms.name: Convergence-retraction nystagmus
terms.definition: Convergence-retraction nystagmus is an irregular, jerky nystagmus in which both eyeballs rhythmically converge and retract into the orbit, particularly on attempting an upward gaze.

terms.name: Spontaneous chorioamniotic separation
terms.definition: Persistence separation of the chorionic and amnionic membranes after the 16th week of gestation (not as a result of a procedure such as amniocentesis).

terms.name: Neurite dystrophy
terms.definition: Dystrophic neurites are abnormal neuronal processes characterized microscopically by aberrant sprouting, dystrophic expansion, and accumulation of various cellular organelles and cytoskeletal/signaling proteins.

terms.name: Cerebral cortical microinfarct
terms.definition: An infarct located on the outer layer of the cerebrum that can only be observed microscopically. Cerebral microinfarcts are typically defined as sharply delimited microscopic regions of cellular death or tissue necrosis, sometimes with cavitation (that is, a central fluid-filled cavity). The term microscopic denotes that these lesions are not visible by gross inspection of the brain but seen by light microscopy. The term infarct is most commonly used for ischemia-related tissue loss, and indeed the pathologic appearance of microinfarcts is consistent with that of known ischemic infarctions.

terms.name: Abnormal umbilical artery doppler waveform during pregnancy
terms.name_zh: 妊娠期脐动脉多普勒波形异常
terms.definition: Abnormal waveforms the Doppler sonographic examination of bloodflow in the umbilical artery. vUmbilical arterial Doppler assessment is used in surveillance of fetal health in the third trimester.

terms.name: Fetal anemia
terms.definition: Low hemoglobin/hematocrit in a fetus as evidenced by percutaneous umbilical cord sampling and Doppler ultrasonographic assessment of the peak velocity of systolic blood flow in the middle cerebral artery.

terms.name: Skeletal muscle autophagosome accumulation
terms.definition: Abnormal accumulation of autophagosomes in skeletal muscle tissue.

terms.name: Skeletal muscle hyperechogenicity
terms.definition: An increased echo intensity of muscle tissue on sonography, defined as an increased amount of returning echoes per square area of muscle tissue. On cross-section, normal muscle appears as a relatively anechoic structure with hyperechoic speckles within the tissue representing perimysial septa, giving it a starry night appearance. The boundaries of each muscle are delineated by the presence of hyperechoic fascia. In muscle disorders, one of the hallmark findings is replacement of healthy muscle with fat and fibrosis, manifested by an increase in echogenicity from higher sound transitions in the muscle. This increase in echogenicity is most distinct in conditions that lead to chronic pathology, such as long-standing muscle inflammation, dystrophy, or denervation.

terms.name: Maternal vascular malperfusion
terms.definition: Gross findings of maternal vascular malperfusion include placental hypoplasia, placental infarction, and retroplacental hemorrhage. If information is available, it is preferable to annotate using the HPO terms that corresponding to the specific abnormalities.

terms.name: Limited horizontal extraocular movement
terms.name_zh: 水平向眼球外活动受限
terms.definition: Limited mobility of the eye to move from side to side (horizontally) within its socket.

terms.name: Limited vertical extraocular movement
terms.definition: Limited mobility of the eye to move up and down (vertically) within its socket.

terms.name: Cerebral infarct
terms.definition: A necrotic lesion in the cerebrum resulting from a sudden insufficiency of arterial or venous blood supply due to emboli, thrombi or mechanical factors.

terms.name: Abnormal fetal skin morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the skin of the fetus or newborn. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

terms.name: Caseous vernix-like desquamation
terms.definition: Vernix caseosa is a physiological, viscous biofilm that is produced by desquamated fetal skin and sebaceous glands covering the fetus at the third trimester in-utero. The substance's gross morphology in post-partum is described by the etymology, as vernix means varnish, and caseosa means cheesy-like matter. This finding refers to an abnormally thick and greasy vernix caseosa-like scale present at birth.

terms.name: Type 1 congenital pulmonary airway malformation
terms.definition: A type of congenital pulmonary airway malformation that is characterized by multiple large cysts or a single dominant cyst.

terms.name: Type 2 congenital pulmonary airway malformation
terms.definition: A type of congenital pulmonary airway malformation that is characterized by multiple evenly spaced cysts (sponge-like appearance).

terms.name: Type 3 congenital pulmonary airway malformation
terms.definition: A type of congenital pulmonary airway malformation that is characterized by a bulky firm mass with an adenomatoid appearance.

terms.name: Periventricular pseudocyst
terms.definition: Pseudocysts that lack an epithelial lining, PVPCs are frequently observed in the caudothalamic groove or in the infero-lateral aspect of the frontal horns of the lateral ventricles, but may also be located elsewhere along the periventricular germinal matrix, as in the temporal or occipital horns.

terms.name: Fetal vascular malperfusion
terms.definition: The term fetal vascular malperfusion (FVM) is used to describe placental pathology that is thought to result from an obstruction in fetal blood flow that could result from a number of conditions (eg, umbilical cord lesions, hypercoagulability, complications of fetal cardiac dysfunction, such as hypoxia, etc.).

terms.name: Foramen ovale aneurysm
terms.definition: Foramen ovale aneurysm (FOA) or atrial septal aneurysm is abnormal redundancy of the atrial septum primum, with bulging of the septum by at least half the width of the atrial chamber, or by at least 10 mm beyond the level of the atrial septum. The abnormal protrusion of the interatrial septum results in decreased left atrial volume. On color Doppler there is reduced left ventricular inflow.

terms.name: Anti-glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchored high-density lipoprotein binding protein 1 antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗糖基化磷脂酰肌醇锚定高密度脂蛋白结合蛋白1抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchored high-density lipoprotein binding protein 1.

terms.name: Abnormal social development
terms.definition: A substantial lag in the achievement of or divergence from typical milestones in social interaction and communication skills. Social-emotional competencies in young children include helping, sharing, comforting, and exhibiting empathy and compliance.

terms.name: Streak gonad
terms.definition: A type of gonadal dysgenesis in which the gonadal tissue is underdeveloped and appears as fibrous, streak-like structures instead of fully formed ovaries or testes.

terms.name: Elevated urinary 5-hydroxyhexanoic acid level
terms.definition: The amount of 5-hydroxyhexanoic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal third cranial nerve morphology
terms.definition: Any structural abnormality of the third (oculomotor) cranial nerve.

terms.name: Long-bone fracture
terms.definition: A partial or complete breakage of a lone bone (e.g., the femur, tibia, fibula, humerus, radius, and ulna).

terms.name: Abnormal subthalamic nucleus morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the subthalamic nucleus, a small lens-shaped structure located within the diencephalon near the junction with the midbrain. The subthalamic nucleus composes the majority of the subthalamus along with the subthalamic fasciculus, ansa lenticularis, and several other smaller structures.

terms.name: Ring-enhancing cerebral lesion
terms.definition: An abnormal neuroimaging finding consisting in an area of decreased density surrounded by a bright rim from concentration of the enhancing contrast dye.

terms.name: Optic nerve mass
terms.definition: A swelling or enlargement localized to the optic nerve. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

terms.name: Elevated brain succinate level by MRS
synonyms: Elevated brain succinate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy
terms.definition: An increase in the level of succinate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.name: Brainstem lucency
terms.definition: A lesion located in the brainstem that appears areas less dense on magnetic resonance imaging or lighter on computed tomography.

terms.name: Elevated urine L-xylulose level
terms.definition: The amount of L-xylulose in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated urine biliverdin level
terms.definition: The amount of biliverdin in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated urine dodecanedioic acid level
terms.name_zh: 尿十二烷二酸水平升高
terms.definition: The amount of dodecanedioic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Diminished urine glutamine level
terms.definition: The amount of glutamine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Tongue spasticity
terms.definition: Spasticity (velocity-dependent increase in tonic stretch reflexes with increased muscle tone and hyperexcitable tendon reflexes) in the muscles of the tongue.

terms.name: Restricted tongue movement
terms.definition: Limited ability to move the tongue related to mechanical restrictions such as akyloglossia and not associated with tongue muscle weakness.

terms.name: Asymmetric blood pressure between limbs
terms.definition: A substantial difference in blood pressure (e.g., 20 mmHg) between the right and left limb (arm or leg or both).

terms.name: Asymmetric blood pressure between legs
terms.definition: A substantial difference in blood pressure (e.g., 20 mmHg) between the right and left legs.

terms.name: Reduced anterior scleral thickness
terms.definition: A reduction in the height of the anterior portion of the sclera.

terms.name: Reduced posterior scleral thickness
terms.definition: A reduction in the height of the posterior portion of the sclera.

terms.name: Elevated urinary 2-aminoisobutyric acid
terms.definition: The amount of 2-aminoisobutyric acid in the urine, when normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Reduced beta-hexosaminidase A activity
terms.definition: The concentration or activity of beta hexosaminidase A in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal nail shape
terms.definition: An abnormality affecting the outline (shape) or contour of the nail.

terms.name: Abnormal nail attachment
terms.definition: An anomaly of the connection of the nail to the nailbed.

terms.name: Abnormal nail surface
terms.definition: An anomaly of the surface of the nail.

terms.name: Characteristic of mass
terms.definition: A mass is a general term for a lump or growth that may be caused by the abnormal growth of cells, a cyst, hormonal changes, or an immune reaction. This term refers to a property (characteristic) of a mass.

terms.name: Mobile lump
terms.definition: This modifier is applied to a palpable mass or swelling in the body that can be moved or shifted under the skin when pressed or manipulated.

terms.name: Immobile lump
terms.definition: This modifier is applied to a palpable mass or swelling in the body that cannot be moved or shifted under the skin when pressed or manipulated.

terms.name: Painless mass
terms.definition: This modifier is applied to a palpable mass or swelling in the body that does not elicit pain upon palpation.

terms.name: Anti-ganglionic acetylcholine receptor antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗神经节乙酰胆碱受体抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against acetylcholine receptors of the ganglionic type.

terms.name: Positive urine anion gap
terms.definition: The urine anion gap (UAG), calculated as [(Na+ + K+) - (Cl-)] has been used to roughly estimate whether urine ammonium is increased or decreased in the evaluation of hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis. The more ammonium in the urine, the lower the UAG is, which achieves negative values within a wide range (0 to -200 mEq/L) during hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis. In patients with distal renal tubular acidosis (RTA) of several etiologies, the UAG is positive, despite the prevailing metabolic acidosis, and this is a useful bedside diagnostic index of impaired ammonium excretion.

terms.name: Nasoethmoidal encephalocele
terms.definition: A type of encephalocele that is characterized by herniation through the foramen cecum into the prenasal space and nasal cavity under the nasal bones and above the nasal septum.

terms.name: Rubber-like lump
terms.definition: This modifier is applied to a palpable mass or swelling in the body that has a rubber-like consistency, that is, it is soft and somewhat compressible.

terms.name: Abnormal affect
terms.definition: An anomaly in intensity, frequency, or duration of the verbal or behavioral expression of emotions, feelings, or thoughts.

terms.name: Disordered formal thought process
terms.definition: An abnormality in the dynamic mode, rate, or form of thought processes as recognized from the flow of ideas expressed in speech. Successive thoughts and speech are easily diverted by external stimuli or internal superficial associations. Unable to maintain a constant train of thought and loose themselves in side issues, losing the thread and are unable to recover it. Superficial connections appear to drive the subject matter.

terms.name: Ruminations
terms.definition: Recurrent thoughts that have a thematic thread that is typically familiar to the individual and are often willfully brought forth or occur in the context of an anxious preoccupation or worry about a relevant concern which may be out of proportion to the context. Ruminations may be of normal thinking rate and are characterized by a recurring theme that usually has a negative connotation.

terms.name: Abnormal lexical patterns
terms.definition: A persistent abnormality in patterns or meanings of expressed language. Words and phrases are disorganized in relationship to each other and often used incorrectly or inappropriately for the context and background culture of the person.

terms.name: Abnormal semantics
terms.definition: Odd use of words that are out of context and inappropriate for the social situation.

terms.name: Idiosyncratic use of words
terms.definition: Words or phrases and their expression that are used in a manner that is not consistent with the current and accepted meaning for the context and social circumstance. This does not apply to peer or culture driven novel uses of words that are accepted within the given social circles.

terms.name: Tangential speech
terms.definition: Patterns of expressed speech that have many words to describe a feature, but are themselves vague and approximations. The speech does not get to the point, but rather seems to go around and around and is inconcise and difficult to grasp the primary issue or purpose of the communicated words.

terms.name: Thought insertion
terms.definition: The experience that thoughts are forced into the conscious awareness by external and foreign entities. The affected individual typically does not recognize the thoughts as coming from themselves and may develop secondary delusional ideas to explain the source of the process.

terms.name: Thought broadcasting
terms.definition: The experience that thoughts are being broadcasted from their head/conscious experience, some report that their thoughts are escaping, while others may believe that their thoughts are being picked up by a nearby receiver only to be further propagated. The person subsequently believes that everyone knows what they are thinking and feels that they have no privacy.

terms.name: Thought echo
terms.definition: The personal experience that thoughts are echoing around them and that they are hearing their own thoughts as they are experiencing them internally.

terms.name: Disorder of thought content
terms.definition: Thought content disorders are characterized by abnormal beliefs and convictions (that are to be assessed given the culture and personal background of the affected individual).

terms.name: Abnormal volitional state
terms.definition: An abnormality of internal states of motivation or drive that compromise, or interfere with, the ability of the person to attend to basic personal, social, or vocational activities.

terms.name: Abnormally rapid thought process
terms.definition: Increased rate or speed of thoughts.

terms.name: Abnormal syntax
terms.definition: Persistent abnormalities in sentence structure exceeding that of the context and background culture of the person.

terms.name: Diagnostic behavioral phenotype
terms.definition: The Human Phenotype Ontology provides terms to describe specific phenotypic abnormalities rather than disease diagnoses. Nevertheless, it is common for descriptions such as 'Autism' to be used to describe individuals affected with Mendelian forms of neurodevelopmental disease and many other conditions. If possible, we recommend annotation using specific terms in other branchs of the Atypical behavior subontology, but if this is not possible, then terms from this branch may be used.

terms.name: Word salad
synonyms: Random stream of words with no logic
terms.definition: Speech that consists of a series of recognizable words that are randomly strung together with no meaningful connection.

terms.name: Abnormal preoccupation
terms.definition: Preoccupations refers to being absorbed in any particular thought, activity, or concern that captures the attention of the individual. It may have a positive or negative connotation.

terms.name: Intraosseous lipoma
terms.definition: Intraosseous lipomas are rare benign lesions composed of mature fat that reside within the intramedullary canal.

terms.name: Paraphilia
terms.definition: Intense and typically recurring sexual arousal to atypical objects, fantasies, places, or individuals that frequently, but not always, lead to engagement of non-conventional sexual acts. This is a broad class of desires and behaviors that may include innocuous fetish behavior to illegal behaviors involving non-consenting individuals.

terms.name: Radiographic modifier
terms.definition: A characteristic of a lesion on radiography.

terms.name: Radiolucent
terms.definition: Applies to a lesion that allows x-rays to penetrate through them and expose the receptor (radiolucency). Soft tissues appear black or dark on the processed radiograph and are called radiolucent.

terms.name: Radiodense
terms.definition: Applies to a lesion that attenuates X-rays and appears radiodense (white) on a radiograph.

terms.name: Delusion of guilt
terms.definition: Delusional belief of one's personal guilt for an event, real or imagined, and that one caused an outcome that is somehow catastrophic. It is generally impossible or fantastical that this could have happened in the manner believed by the person, that they were somehow responsible for an event despite not be anywhere near where it allegedly occurred.

terms.name: Abnormal cognitive process
terms.definition: An abnormal cognitive process can be defined as a deviation from the typical development, structural organization, or functional execution of mental operations that connect informational inputs to behavioral outputs, typically involve at least one of the following processes: perception, memory, learning, emotion, intentionality, self-representation, rationality, and decision-making.

terms.name: Abnormal change in sexual drive
terms.definition: An abnormal change in libido (sexual desire), typically accompanied by an altered frequency of sexual activity compared to from a person's previous norm.

terms.name: Reduced MHC I cell surface expression
synonyms: Reduced cell surface expression of class I HLA antigens
terms.definition: Expression of major histocompatibility complex class I molecules at the cell surface is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Positive urine infectious agent test
terms.definition: Any kind of test for an infectious agent in the urine positive (abnormal).

terms.name: Positive urine Legionella pneumophila antigen test
terms.definition: Demonstration of an antigen specific to Legionella pneumophila in urine.

terms.name: Unilateral sensorineural hearing impairment
terms.definition: A form of sensorineural hearing impairment that affects one ear.

terms.name: Abnormal wrist morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the wrist.

terms.name: Abnormal wrist physiology
terms.definition: Any functional anomaly of the wrist.

terms.name: Wrist instability
terms.definition: Subjective or objective feeling of clunking/clicking in the wrist with movement, wrist giving way or difficulty twisting objects.

terms.name: Nail elevation
terms.definition: Elevation of the nail from the nail bed.

terms.name: Talipes varus
terms.definition: Inversion of the foot, resulting in the outer side of the sole only touching the ground; usually some degree of talipes equinus is associated with it, and often talipes cavus.

terms.name: Mucocutaneous lesion painful
terms.definition: Applies to pain that colocalizes with lesions in the skin or mucous membranes.

terms.name: Painful lymphadenopathy
terms.definition: Applies to pain that is localizes to a swollen lymph node.

terms.name: Absent circulating T cells
terms.definition: Absence of detectable circulating T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, in the blood. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells. Usually, less than 50 T cells per microlitre is considered to be an absence.

terms.name: Decreased natural killer cell degranulation
terms.name_zh: 自然杀伤细胞脱颗粒减少
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of NK cell degranulation in response to stimulation, commonly measured through surface CD107a expression in response to cocultivation with a murine cell line. Other methods may be used by different laboratories.

terms.name: Decreased natural killer cell-induced killing of target cells
terms.name_zh: 自然杀伤细胞靶细胞杀伤能力降低
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of natural killer (NK) cell cytotoxicity. Assaying NK cytotoxicity involves coculturing NK calls with target cells and measuring the extent of cell death by methods such as luminescence-based (luciferase) assays, biophotonic assays, and flow cytometry-based Cr-release assays.

terms.name: Generalized scaling
terms.definition: Desquamation (scaling) involving nearly all of the surface of the skin.

terms.name: Ichthyosis linearis circumflexa
terms.definition: A type of ichthyosis characterized by migratory, annular and polycyclic erythematous patches with double-edged scales at the periphery of the lesions.

terms.name: Trichorrhexis invaginata
terms.definition: A type of hair shaft dysmorphology in which the proximal part of the hair shaft overlaps the distal part, showing a bamboo-like appearance. This feature is pathognomic for Netherton syndrome, and can be ascertained by light microscopy.

terms.name: Seborrheic scales on scalp
terms.definition: Fine white-greasy scales on scalp.

terms.name: Eyebrow scaling skin
terms.definition: Loss of the outer layer of the epidermis in the area of the eyebrow in large, scale-like flakes.

terms.name: Patchy stratum granulosum of epidermis
synonyms: Patchy granular layer of the skin
terms.definition: The stratum granulosum of the epidermis (granular layer) displays areas of discontinuity.

terms.name: Absent stratum granulosum of epidermis
terms.definition: The stratum granulosum of the epidermis (granular layer) cannot be observed.

terms.name: Hypogranulosis
terms.definition: The height (thickness) of the stratum granulosum of the epidermis (granular layer) is below the lower limit of normal but the stratum granulosum is visible.

terms.name: Psoriasiform acanthosis
terms.definition: A type of epidermal acanthosis characterized by regular elongated rete ridges.

terms.name: Intraepidermal microabscess formation
terms.definition: Infiltrating neutrophils in the epidermis, mostly into the stratum corneum. Characteristic for psoriasis.

terms.name: Palmoplantar peeling
terms.definition: Splitting within the the upper lyer (stratum corneum) of the epidermis clinically characterized by shedding of dead cells from the outermost layer of skin.

terms.name: Offspring of consanguineous relationship
terms.definition: The parents of the index patient are related as second cousins or closer.

terms.name: Lower eyelid erythema
terms.definition: Redness of the skin of the lower eyelid, caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.

terms.name: Upper eyelid erythema
terms.definition: Redness of the skin of the upper eyelid, caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.

terms.name: Positive provocative functional shoulder test
terms.definition: Abnormal result of a physical test of the shoulder that attempts to provoke pain in order to diagnosis a specific injury.

terms.name: Decreased neutrophil phagocytosis
terms.name_zh: 中性粒细胞吞噬功能降低
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of neutrophil phagocytic activity, commonly measured after stimulation with E. coli using flow cytometry.

terms.name: Decreased neutrophil adhesion
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of neutrophil adhesion capacity, commonly measured as surface expression of CD18, CD11a or CD11b using flow cytometry.

terms.name: Severely decreased neutrophil count
terms.definition: Severe decrease in circulating neutrophils, usually characterized as fewer than 500 neutrophils per microlitre.

terms.name: Abnormal Th1 T cell proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of Th1 cells, commonly characterized through the intracellular synthesis of IFNg or surface expression of CXCR3, measured as proportion of total CD3+CD4+ T cells, usually after stimulation. The stimulation is usually unspecific and may include the use of anti-CD3 beads or antibodies or the use of phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA) with ionomycin. Length of incubation and strength of stimulation may vary between laboratories.

terms.name: Increased Th1 T cell proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of Th1 cells, commonly characterized through the intracellular synthesis of IFNg or surface expression of CXCR3, measured as proportion of total CD3+CD4+ T cells, usually after stimulation. The stimulation is usually unspecific and may include the use of anti-CD3 beads or antibodies or the use of phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA) with ionomycin. Length of incubation and strength of stimulation may vary between laboratories.

terms.name: Decreased Th1 T cell proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of Th1 cells, commonly characterized through the intracellular synthesis of IFNg or surface expression of CXCR3, measured as proportion of total CD3+CD4+ T cells, usually after stimulation. The stimulation is usually unspecific and may include the use of anti-CD3 beads or antibodies or the use of phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA) with ionomycin. Length of incubation and strength of stimulation may vary between laboratories.

terms.name: Abnormal Th17 T cell proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of Th17 cells, commonly characterized through the intracellular synthesis of IL-17 or surface expression of CCR6, measured as proportion of total CD3+CD4+ T cells, usually after stimulation. The stimulation is usually unspecific and may include the use of anti-CD3 beads or antibodies, the use of phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA) with ionomycin, or staphylococcal enterotoxin B (SEB). Length of incubation and strength of stimulation may vary between laboratories.

terms.name: Increased Th17 T cell proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of Th17 cells, commonly characterized through the intracellular synthesis of IL-17 or surface expression of CCR6, measured as proportion of total CD3+CD4+ T cells, usually after stimulation. The stimulation is usually unspecific and may include the use of anti-CD3 beads or antibodies, the use of phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA) with ionomycin, or staphylococcal enterotoxin B (SEB). Length of incubation and strength of stimulation may vary between laboratories.

terms.name: Decreased Th17 T cell proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of Th17 cells, commonly characterized through the intracellular synthesis of IL-17 or surface expression of CCR6, measured as proportion of total CD3+CD4+ T cells, usually after stimulation. The stimulation is usually unspecific and may include the use of anti-CD3 beads or antibodies, the use of phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA) with ionomycin, or staphylococcal enterotoxin B (SEB). Length of incubation and strength of stimulation may vary between laboratories.

terms.name: Decreased PMA/ionomycin-induced T-cell proliferation
terms.name_zh: 佛波酯/离子霉素诱导的T细胞增殖降低
synonyms: Decreased proliferation in response to PMA/ionomycin
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of T cell proliferation in response to phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA) and ionomycin stimulation. This is commonly measured through intracellular expression of Ki67, decreasing surface expression of carboxyfluorescein diacetate (CFSE), or 3H-thymidine incorporation. Length of incubation and strength of stimulation may vary between laboratories.

terms.name: Impaired phytohemagglutinin-induced T lymphocyte transformation
terms.name_zh: 植物血凝素诱导的T淋巴细胞转化障碍
synonyms: Decreased proliferation in response to PHA
Impaired T lymphocyte transformation with phytohemagglutinin
terms.definition: Def: A reduced rate of T lymphocyte transformation in response to in vitro stimulation to the mitogen phytohemagglutinin (PHA). Following PHA stimulation, T cells normally undergo morphological and biochemical alterations that reflect the transformation into lymphoblasts. There are several methods for quantifying this effect including measuring the uptake of the radioactive marker 3H-TdR, methyl thiazolyl tetrazolium colorimetric analysis (MTT assay), and morphological examination under the microscope or using a hematology analyzer. Various types of stimulation index compare the amount of proliferation between treated and control cells. An impaired test refers to a result in which the amount of stimulation is subnormal.

terms.name: Decreased CD8+ T cell degranulation
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of CD8-positive T cell degranulation in response to stimulation, commonly measured through surface CD107a expression in response to cocultivation with a murine cell line. Other methods may be used by different laboratories.

terms.name: Increased total CD8+ T cell proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells, measured as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Abnormal RTE CD4+ T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: 调节性T细胞CD4阳性T细胞比例异常
synonyms: Abnormal proportion of RTE CD4+ T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of the recent thymic emmigrant (RTE) CD4+ T cell subpopulation, commonly characterized as CD45RA+, CD45RO-, or CD27+, with the necessary expression of CD31+, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These cells are sometimes also characterized as CD62L+ and CCR7+.

terms.name: Increased RTE CD4+ T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: 调节性T细胞相关CD4阳性T细胞比例升高
synonyms: Increased proportion of RTE CD4+ T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of the recent thymic emmigrant (RTE) CD4+ T cell subpopulation, commonly characterized as CD45RA+, CD45RO-, or CD27+, with the necessary expression of CD31+, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These cells are sometimes also characterized as CD62L+ and CCR7+.

terms.name: Decreased RTE CD4+ T cell proportion
synonyms: Decreased proportion of RTE CD4+ T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of the recent thymic emmigrant (RTE) CD4+ T cell subpopulation, commonly characterized as CD45RA+, CD45RO-, or CD27+, with the necessary expression of CD31+, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These cells are sometimes also characterized as CD62L+ and CCR7+.

terms.name: Abnormal HLA-DR+ CD4+ T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: HLA-DR阳性CD4阳性T细胞比例异常
synonyms: Abnormal HLA DR+ CD4+ T cell proportion
Abnormal proportion of HLA DR+ CD4+ T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of the activated HLA-DR+ CD4+ T cell subpopulation, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Decreased HLA-DR+ CD4+ T cell proportion
synonyms: Decreased HLA DR+ CD4+ T cell proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal reduction of the activated HLA-DR+ CD4+ T cell subpopulation, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Abnormal HLA-DR+ CD8+ T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: HLA-DR阳性CD8阳性T细胞比例异常
synonyms: Abnormal proportion of HLA DR+ CD8+ T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of the activated HLA-DR+ CD8+ T cell subpopulation, measured as percentage of total CD8+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Increased HLA-DR+ CD8+ T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: HLA-DR阳性CD8阳性T细胞比例升高
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of the activated HLA-DR+ CD8+ T cell subpopulation, measured as percentage of total CD8+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Decreased HLA-DR+ CD8+ T cell proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of the activated HLA-DR+ CD8+ T cell subpopulation, measured as percentage of total CD8+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Abnormal TCR repertoire
terms.definition: Abnormal distribution of the TCR repertoire expressed on T cells. This usually means oligoclonality (fewer TCR clonotypes compared to a healthy age-matched control) or monoclonality (one dominant TCR clone detected). This may be measured through different methods depending on the lab, but commonly include TCR spectratyping or TCRB CDR3 sequencing.

terms.name: Decreased natural killer cell perforin expression
terms.name_zh: 自然杀伤细胞穿孔素表达降低
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of intracellular expression of perforin within NK cells, commonly characterized as CD3-CD19- and CD16+ or CD56+ lymphocytes, ex vivo.

terms.name: Fish allergy
terms.definition: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against fish.

terms.name: Shellfish allergy
terms.definition: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against shellfish (an aquatic shelled mollusc such as an oyster or mussel, or a crustacean such as a crab or shrimp).

terms.name: Localized along nerve distribution
terms.definition: Refers to findings sich as paresthesias or weakness that are distributed according to the anatomical location of a periperipheral nerve.

terms.name: EMG: repetitive nerve stimulation abnormality
terms.name_zh: 肌电图示重复神经刺激异常
terms.definition: Abnormality observed upon electromyography when nerve studied is electrically stimulated six to ten times at 2 or 3 Hertz.

terms.name: Lagophthalmos
terms.definition: A condition in which the eyelids do not close to cover the eye completely.

terms.name: Nocturnal lagophthalmos
synonyms: Inability to close the eyelids at night
terms.definition: The inability to close the eyelids during sleep.

terms.name: Paralytic lagophthalmos
terms.definition: A type of lagophthalmos that occurs in association with facial nerve palsy.

terms.name: Cicatricial lagophthalmos
synonyms: Eyelids stay open due to scarring
Inability to close the eyelids due to scarring
terms.definition: A type of lagophthalmos that occurs following trauma or surgery.

terms.name: Capillary leak
terms.definition: An acute phenomenon characterized by hypotension and anasarca due to the loss of plasma volume into peripheral tissues, with evidence of decreased plasma volume (hemoconcentration) and protein loss from the intravascular space (hypoalbuminemia) during acute episodes.

terms.name: Single fiber EMG abnormality
terms.definition: Abnormality in single fiber EMG recording, a technique that allows identification of action potentials (APs) from individual muscle fibers.

terms.name: EMG: positive sharp waves
terms.definition: These are spontaneous firing action potentials stimulated by needle movement of an injured muscle fiber. There is propagation to, but not past, the needle tip. This inhibits the display of the negative deflection of the waveform.

terms.name: Cervical agenesis
terms.definition: Congenital absence of the uterine cervix.

terms.name: Cervical insufficiency
terms.definition: A cervix that shows a painless dilation and shortening during the second trimester of pregnancy with resultant recurrent pregnancy loss or delivery is considered incompetent

terms.name: Hydrometrocolpos
terms.definition: Hydrometrocolpos is an accumulation of uterine and vaginal secretions as well as menstrual blood in the uterus and vagina.

terms.name: Imperforate hymen
terms.definition: A congenital disorder where the hymen (a membrane that surrounds or partially covers the external vaginal opening) does not have an opening and completely obstructs the vagina.

terms.name: Abnormal female reproductive system physiology
terms.name_zh: 女性生殖系统生理功能异常

terms.name: Female sexual dysfunction
terms.definition: A problem occurring during any phase of the female sexual response cycle that prevents the individual from experiencing satisfaction from the sexual activity

terms.name: Female anorgasmia
terms.definition: The persistent of recurrent difficulty, delay in, or absence of attaining orgasm following sufficient sexual stimulation and arousal.

terms.name: Dyspareunia
terms.definition: Recurrent or persistent genital pain associated with sexual intercourse.

terms.name: Vaginismus
terms.definition: Recurrent or persistent involuntary spasms of the musculature of the outer third of the vagina that interferes with vaginal penetration, and which causes personal distress.

terms.name: Decreased female libido
terms.definition: Diminished sexual desire in female.

terms.name: Increased female libido
terms.definition: Elevated sexual desire in female

terms.name: Auricular tag
terms.definition: Small protrusion within the pinna.

terms.name: Question mark ear
terms.definition: Cleft between the helix and the lobe.

terms.name: Quelprud nodule
terms.definition: Small cartilaginous prominence on the posterior concha.

terms.name: Pretragal ectopia
terms.definition: Variably shaped, cartilage-containing tissue anterior to the external auditory meatus.

terms.name: Auricular pit
terms.definition: Small indentation in the lower part of the ascending helix, concha, or in the crus helix.

terms.name: Squared superior portion of helix
terms.definition: Flattening instead of curving or rounded superior helix, allowing the superior helix to run more horizontally than usual.

terms.name: Abnormal nasal cartilage morphology
terms.definition: A morphological anomaly of the nasal cartilage.

terms.name: Absent nasal cartilage
synonyms: Failure of development of cartilage of nose
Failure of development of nasal cartilage
terms.definition: Lack of a palpable nasal cartilage.

terms.name: Splayed fingers
terms.definition: Divergence of digits along the A/P axis (in the plane of the palm).

terms.name: Absent ray
terms.definition: The absence of all phalanges of a digit and the associated metacarpal /metatarsal.

terms.name: Small toe
terms.definition: Significant reduction in both length and girth of the toe compared to the contralateral toe, or alternatively, compared to a typical toe size for an age-matched individual.

terms.name: Partial absence of foot
terms.definition: An incomplete absence of the foot, with no bony elements distal to the tarsals, but with preservation of some or all of the tarsals.

terms.name: Small finger
terms.definition: Significant reduction in both length and girth of the finger compared to the contralateral finger, or alternatively, compared to a typical finger size for an age-matched individual.

terms.name: Glomerular basement membrane lamellation
synonyms: Lamellation of the glomerular basement membrane
terms.definition: Presence of abnormal additional layers of the basement membrane of the glomerulus.

terms.name: Struvite nephrolithiasis
terms.definition: Presence of struvite (magnesium ammonium phosphate) containing calculi (kidney stones).

terms.name: Isothenuria
terms.definition: Inability of the kidneys to produce either concentrated or dilute urine.

terms.name: Bifid ureter
terms.definition: Incomplete duplication of the ureter.

terms.name: Enchondroma
terms.definition: A solitary, benign, intramedullary cartilage tumor that is often found in the short tubular bones of the hands and feet, distal femur, and proximal humerus.

terms.name: Fused thoracic vertebrae
terms.definition: A congenital anomaly characterized by a joining (fusion) of two or more thoracic vertebral bodies with one another.

terms.name: Fused lumbar vertebrae
terms.definition: A congenital anomaly characterized by a joining (fusion) of two or more lumbar vertebral bodies with one another.

terms.name: Schmorl's node
terms.definition: A Schmorl's node is the herniation of nucleus pulposus through the cartilaginous and bony end plate into the body of the adjacent vertebra.

terms.name: Incomplete ossification of pubis
synonyms: Incomplete maturation of the pubic bone
terms.definition: Failure to complete ossification (maturation and calcification) of the pubic bone.

terms.name: Hip subluxation
terms.definition: A partial dislocation of the hip joint, whereby the head of the femur is partially displaced from the socket.

terms.name: Flexion contracture of digit
terms.definition: A bent (flexed) finger or toe joint that cannot be straightened actively or passively. It is thus a chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement of joints.

terms.name: Serpentine fibula
terms.definition: Elongated curved (S-shaped) fibulae.

terms.name: Hypoglycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan
terms.name_zh: α-肌营养不良蛋白聚糖低糖基化
terms.definition: A reduction in the degree of glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan in muscle tissue.

terms.name: Abnormal lateral ventricle morphology
terms.definition: A morphological anomaly of the lateral ventricle.

terms.name: Colpocephaly
terms.definition: Colpocephaly is an anatomic finding in the brain manifested by occipital horns that are disproportionately enlarged in comparison with other parts of the lateral ventricles.

terms.name: Brain abscess
terms.definition: A collection of pus, immune cells, and other material in the brain.

terms.name: Tip-toe gait
terms.definition: An abnormal gait pattern characterized by the failure of the heel to contact the floor at the onset of stance during gait.

terms.name: Inguinal freckling
terms.definition: The presence in the inguinal region (groin) of an increased number of freckles, small circular spots on the skin that are darker than the surrounding skin because of deposits of melanin.

terms.name: Stiff skin
terms.definition: An induration (hardening) of the skin

terms.name: Perifollicular fibrosis
terms.definition: Presence of excess fibrous connective tissue surrounding hair follicules.

terms.name: Hyperconvex toenail
terms.definition: When viewed on end (with the tip of the toe pointing toward the examiner's eye) the curve of the toenail forms a tighter curve of convexity.

terms.name: Uncombable hair
terms.definition: Hair that is disorderly, stands out from the scalp, and cannot be combed flat.

terms.name: Autoimmune antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of an antibody in the blood circulation that is directed against the organism's own cells or tissues.

terms.name: Sickled erythrocytes
terms.definition: An irreversible distortion of the morphology of an erythrocyte such that the cells are elongated and curved, resembling the blade of a sickle (the hand-held agricultural tool traditionally used to harvest grains).

terms.name: Mitochondrial depletion
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction in mitochondrial DNA content of cells.

terms.name: Nervous tissue neoplasm
terms.definition: A neoplasm derived from nervous tissue (not necessarily a neoplasm located in the nervous system).

terms.name: Neuroectodermal neoplasm
terms.definition: A neoplasm arising in the neuroectoderm, the portion of the ectoderm of the early embryo that gives rise to the central and peripheral nervous systems, including some glial cells.

terms.name: Craniopharyngioma
terms.definition: A benign pituitary-region neoplasm that originates from Rathke's pouch. Craniopharyngiomas are benign slow growing tumors that are located within the sellar and para sellar region of the central nervous system.

terms.name: Neuroepithelial neoplasm
terms.definition: A neoplasm composed of neural epithelium, not necessarily a neoplasm located in the neural epithelium or neuroepithelium.

terms.name: Neurocytoma
terms.definition: A benign brain tumor composed of neural elements which most often arise from the septum pellucidum and the walls of the lateral ventricles.

terms.name: Primitive neuroectodermal tumor
terms.definition: A tumor that originates in cells from the primitive neural crest. This group of tumors is characteirzed by the presence of primitive cells with elements of neuronal and/or glial differentiation.

terms.name: Ependymoblastoma
terms.definition: A highly malignant embryonal tumor of infancy and young childhood characterized by neuroectodermal elements organized in distinctive multilayered rosettes. Ependymoblastomas are large lesions that occur in the supratentorial compartment, typically displaying a physical connection to the ventricular system.

terms.name: Peripheral primitive neuroectodermal neoplasm
terms.definition: A primitive neuroectodermal neoplasm that occurs extracranially in soft tissue and bone.

terms.name: Olfactory esthesioneuroblastoma
terms.definition: A malignant olfactory neuroblastoma arising from the olfactory epithelium of the superior nasal cavity and cribriform plate.

terms.name: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
terms.definition: A form of extranodal, high-grade non-Hodgkin B-cell neoplasm, usually large cell or immunoblastic type that originates in the brain, leptomeninges, spinal cord, or eyes and typically remains confined to the CNS.

terms.name: Central primitive neuroectodermal tumor
terms.name_zh: 中枢性原始神经外胚层肿瘤
terms.definition: A primitive neuroectodermal neoplasm that occurs in the central nervous system.

terms.name: Medulloepithelioma
terms.definition: A primitive neuroectodermal tumor that originates from the cells of the embryonic medullary canal.

terms.name: Paranasal sinus neoplasm
terms.definition: A tumor that originates in the paranasal sinus.

terms.name: Chemodectoma
terms.definition: A usually benign neoplasm originating in the chemoreceptor tissue of the carotid body, glomus jugulare, glomus tympanicum, aortic bodies, or the female genital tract.

terms.name: Ductal carcinoma in situ
terms.definition: Presence of abnormal cells inside a milk duct, that is, non-invasive breast cancer. Ductal carcinoma in situ is considered to be a precursor lesion to invasive breast cancer.

terms.name: Bronchial neoplasm
terms.definition: A tumor originating in a bronchus.

terms.name: Cervix cancer
terms.definition: A tumor of the uterine cervix.

terms.name: Burkitt lymphoma
terms.definition: A form of undifferentiated malignant lymphoma commonly manifested as a large osteolytic lesion in the jaw or as an abdominal mass.

terms.name: Punctate periventricular T2 hyperintense foci
terms.definition: Multiple pointlike areas of high T2 signal observed upon magnetic resonance imaging of the periventricular cerebral white matter.

terms.name: Abnormal drinking behavior
terms.definition: Abnormal consumption of fluids with excessive or insufficient consumption of fluid or any other abnormal pattern of fluid consumption.

terms.name: Salt craving
terms.definition: Hypersalivation, also known as salt craving, refers to an excessive desire to consume salt (sodium chloride) or salty foods.

terms.name: Clinodactyly
terms.definition: An angulation of a digit at an interphalangeal joint in the plane of the palm (finger) or sole (toe).

terms.name: Abnormal CSF lactate concentration
terms.definition: Abnormal concentration of lactate in the cerebrospinal fluid.

terms.name: Reduced CSF lactate
terms.definition: Decreased concentration of lactate in the cerebrospinal fluid.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating testosterone concentration
terms.definition: An anomalous concentration of testosterone in the blood.

terms.name: Increased serum testosterone level
terms.definition: An elevated circulating testosterone level in the blood.

terms.name: Abnormal muscle fiber protein expression
terms.definition: An anomalous amount of protein present in or on the surface of muscle fibers. This feature may be appreciate upon immunohistochemical investigation of muscle biopsy tissue.

terms.name: Abnormal muscle fiber merosin expression
terms.name_zh: 肌纤维层粘连蛋白表达异常
terms.definition: An anomalous amount of merosin in muscle fibers. Merosin is a basement membrane-associated protein found in placenta, striated muscle, and peripheral nerve.

terms.name: Absent muscle fiber merosin
terms.name_zh: 肌纤维层黏连蛋白缺如
synonyms: Absent merosin staining in muscle biopsy
terms.definition: Lack of merosin protein in the muscle biopsy.

terms.name: Reduced muscle fiber merosin
terms.definition: A reduced amount of merosin in muscle fibers. This feature is usually assessed by immunohistochemical examination of muscle biopsy tissue.

terms.name: Abnormal muscle fiber laminin beta 1
terms.name_zh: 肌纤维层粘连蛋白β1异常
terms.definition: A deviation from normal of the amount of laminin beta 1 in muscle fiber tissue. Laminin 2 is a major component of the basal lamina of skeletal muscle cells. It is a heterotrimer composed of 3 chains: merosin (laminin alpha 2 chain), beta 1, and gamma 1.

terms.name: Reduced muscle fiber laminin beta 1
terms.definition: A reduced amount of laminin beta 1 in muscle fiber tissue. Laminin 2 is a major component of the basal lamina of skeletal muscle cells. It is a heterotrimer composed of 3 chains: merosin (laminin alpha 2 chain), beta 1, and gamma 1.

terms.name: Reduced muscle collagen VI
synonyms: Reduced collagen VI immunolabeling in muscle biopsy
terms.definition: A decreased amount of collagen VI in muscle tissue. Collagen VI is a primarily associated with the extracellular matrix of skeletal muscle.

terms.name: Abnormal muscle fiber dystrophin expression
terms.name_zh: 肌纤维抗肌萎缩蛋白表达异常
terms.definition: A deviation from normal in the amount of dystrophin in muscle fiber tissue. Dystrophin is located at the muscle sarcolemma in a membrane-spanning protein complex that connects the cytoskeleton to the basal lamina.

terms.name: Absent muscle dystrophin expression
terms.name_zh: 肌抗肌萎缩蛋白表达缺如
terms.definition: Lack of dystrophin in muscle tissue. Immunohistochemistry reveals absent dystrophin protein in the muscle biopsy.

terms.name: Reduced muscle dystrophin expression
terms.definition: A decreased amount of dystrophin in muscle fiber tissue.

terms.name: Reduced muscle fiber alpha dystroglycan
terms.definition: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced alpha dystroglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.
