terms.definition: A type of brachydactyly characterized by brachymesophalangy affecting mainly the 2nd and 5th digits.

terms.name: Type A5 brachydactyly
terms.definition: A type of brachydactyly characterized by absent middle phalanges of digits 2 to 5.

terms.name: Acral blistering
terms.definition: Bullae (defined as fluid-filled blisters more than 5 mm in diameter with thin walls) of the skin with an acral distribution (affecting peripheral regions such as hands and feet).

terms.name: Absent soft palate
terms.definition: A developmental defect characterized by lack of a soft palate.

terms.name: Paraproteinemia
terms.definition: An abnormal immunoglobulin or part of an Ig (light chain) in the circulation. Paraproteins are typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

terms.name: Light-chain paraproteinemia
terms.definition: An abnormal immunoglobulin light chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

terms.name: Heavy-chain paraproteinemia
terms.definition: An abnormal immunoglobulin heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

terms.name: Whole-immunoglobulin paraproteinemia
terms.definition: An abnormal immunoglobulin (heavy and light chain) in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

terms.name: Tarsal sclerosis
terms.definition: An elevation in bone density in one or more tarsal bones of the foot. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.

terms.name: Elevated vascular endothelial growth factor level
terms.name_zh: 血管内皮生长因子水平升高
terms.definition: Increased blood concentration of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF).

terms.name: Coarctation in the transverse aortic arch
terms.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized to the region of the transverse aortic arch.

terms.name: Long segment coarctation of the aorta
terms.definition: Coarctation of the aorta is a narrowing or constriction of a long segment of the arch of the aorta.

terms.name: Abnormal branching pattern of left aortic arch
terms.name_zh: 左主动脉弓分支模式异常
terms.definition: A deviance from the norm of the origin or course of the right brachiocephalic artery, the left common carotid artery, the left subclavian artery or the proximal vertebral arteries, whereby the aortic arch descends on the left as normal (as opposed to right aortic arch).

terms.name: Fusiform cerebral aneurysm
terms.definition: A localized circumferential (i.e., bulges on all sides) dilatation or ballooning of a cerebral artery.

terms.name: Skin fissure
terms.definition: A clearly-defined and roughly linear cleavage in the skin that usually extends to the dermis.

terms.name: Impairment of activities of daily living
terms.name_zh: 日常生活活动能力受损
terms.definition: Difficulty in performing one or more activities normally performed every day, such as eating, bathing, dressing, grooming, work, homemaking, and leisure.

terms.name: Impaired ability to bathe oneself
terms.definition: This term applies to an individual who requires help to bathe more than one part of the body, get in or out of the tub or shower, or who requires total bathing.

terms.name: Impaired ability to dress oneself
terms.definition: This applies to an individual who needs help with dressing or needs to be completely dressed.

terms.name: Impaired toileting ability
terms.definition: This term applies to an individual who requires help transferring to the toilet, cleaning self or who uses bedpan or commode.

terms.name: Impaired transferring ability
terms.definition: Applies to an individual who needs help in moving from bed to chair or requires a complete transfer.

terms.name: Impaired feeding ability
terms.definition: Applies to an individual who needs partial or total help with feeding or requires parenteral feeding.

terms.name: Impaired continence
terms.definition: Partial or total incontinence of bowel or bladder.

terms.name: Abnormal ovarian physiology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of ovarian function.

terms.name: Empty ovarian follicle
terms.definition: A failure to collect oocytes after an apparently normal controlled ovarian hyperstimulation cycle for in vitro fertilization.

terms.name: Abnormal femoral torsion
terms.definition: Femoral torsion, also known as femoral rotation or femoral version, refers to the twist between the proximal and distal parts of the femur on the transverse plane. Femoral anteversion averages between 30-40 degrees at birth, and between 8-14 degrees in adults. This term applies if the amount of femoral torsion deviates from this range.

terms.name: Abnormal endocrine morphology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the structure of an organ ofthe endocrine system.

terms.name: Abnormal endocrine physiology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the function of the endocrine system.

terms.name: Abnormal response to endocrine stimulation test
terms.name_zh: 内分泌兴奋试验反应异常
terms.definition: An anomalous response to a test that is designed to probe the function of the endocrine system.

terms.name: Abnormal response to ACTH stimulation test
terms.name_zh: 促肾上腺皮质激素兴奋试验反应异常
synonyms: Abnormal response to adrenocorticotropic-hormone stimulation test
Abnormal response to corticotropin stimulation test
terms.definition: An anomalous response to stimulation by administration of the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH). ACTH stimulation normally stimulates the adrenal glands to release cortisol and adrenaline.

terms.name: Abnormal response to insulin tolerance test
terms.name_zh: 胰岛素耐量试验反应异常
terms.definition: An anomalous response to the insulin tolerance test (ITT), in which insulin is administered intravenously and blood glucose and potentially other compounds are measured at intervals. Insulin administration is intended to induce extreme hypoglycemia (bloodgluoce below 40 mg/dl), which in turn induces release of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and growth hormone (GH). ACTH induces the adrenal gland to release cortisol, which together with GH opposes the action of insulin on the blood glucose level.

terms.name: Impaired cortisol response to insulin stimulation test
terms.name_zh: 胰岛素刺激试验皮质醇应答障碍
terms.definition: Failure of cortisol levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the insulin tolerance test (ITT).

terms.name: Abnormal response to corticotropin releasing hormone stimulation test
terms.name_zh: 促肾上腺皮质激素释放激素兴奋试验反应异常
synonyms: Abnormal response to CRH stimulation test
terms.definition: An anomalous response to the corticotropin releasing hormone (CRH) stimulation test. Normally,CRH is released by the hypothalamus to induce adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) release by the anterior pituitary. In the stimulation test, CRH is administered intravenously and ACTH and cortisol are measured at intervals.

terms.name: Impaired cortisol response to corticotropin releasing hormone stimulation test
terms.name_zh: 促肾上腺皮质激素释放激素刺激试验皮质醇应答障碍
terms.definition: Failure of cortisol levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the corticotropin releasing hormone stimulation test.

terms.name: Impaired growth-hormone response to insulin stimulation test
terms.name_zh: 胰岛素刺激试验生长激素应答障碍
terms.definition: Failure of growth hormone levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the insulin tolerance test (ITT).

terms.name: Abnormal response to glucagon stimulation test
terms.name_zh: 胰高血糖素兴奋试验反应异常
terms.definition: An anomalous response to the glucagon stimulation test, which like the insulin tolerance test (ITT) stimulates the release of both adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and growth hormone (GH).

terms.name: Impaired cortisol response to glucagon stimulation test
terms.name_zh: 胰高血糖素刺激试验皮质醇应答障碍
terms.definition: Failure of cortisol levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the glucagon stimulation test.

terms.name: Impaired growth-hormone response to glucagon stimulation test
terms.name_zh: 胰高血糖素刺激试验生长激素应答障碍
terms.definition: Failure of growth hormone levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the glucagon stimulation test.

terms.name: Abnormal response to human chorionic gonadotrophin stimulation test
terms.name_zh: 人绒毛膜促性腺激素兴奋试验反应异常
synonyms: Abnormal response to hCG stimulation test
terms.definition: An anomalous response to intravenous stimulation by human chorionic gonadotrophin. Stimulation with hCG stimulates testicular Leydig cells to secrete androgens via the Leydig hormone receptors.

terms.name: Excessive insulin response to glucagon test
terms.name_zh: 胰高血糖素试验胰岛素反应过度
terms.definition: An abnormally high increase in insulin levels following a glucagon stimulation test.

terms.name: Decreased circulating prealbumin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环前白蛋白浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of prealbumin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Ectopic ovary
terms.definition: Undescended or ectopic ovaries are characterized by the attachment of the upper pole of the ovary to an area above the level of the common iliac vessels.

terms.name: Absent pubertal growth spurt
terms.definition: The abrupt and transient increase in the annual growth rate normally observed in adolescent individuals does not occur.

terms.name: Vaginal dryness
terms.definition: Persistent vaginal dryness.

terms.name: Palatal edema
terms.definition: Swelling related to fluid accumulation within the palate.

terms.name: Finger dactylitis
terms.definition: Fingers appear swollen and plump owing to inflammation of the complete finger.

terms.name: Toe dactylitis
terms.definition: Toes appear swollen and plump owing to inflammation of the complete toe.

terms.name: Spindle-shaped finger
terms.definition: Swelling of the hand at the knuckles, that gives the fingers a spindle shape (i.e., a round stick with tapered end and a broader base).

terms.name: Abnormal breast morphology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the structure of the breast.

terms.name: Abnormal breast physiology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the function of the breast.

terms.name: Abnormal humerus morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the structure of the humerus (i.e., upper arm bone).

terms.name: Delayed vertebral ossification
terms.definition: A decrease in the amount of mineralized bone in one or more vertebrae compared with that expected for a given developmental age.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating thyroid-stimulating hormone concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环促甲状腺激素浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal amount of the thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), which is produced by the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates the function of the thyroid gland.

terms.name: Decreased thyroid-stimulating hormone level
terms.name_zh: 促甲状腺激素水平降低
terms.definition: Reduced amount of the thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), which is produced by the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates the function of the thyroid gland.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating inhibin level
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of inhibins, which are heterodimeric protein hormones secreted by granulosa cells of the ovary in females and Sertoli cells of the testis in males. Inhibins suppress the secretion of pituitary follicle-stimulating hormone.

terms.name: Decreased circulating inhibin B concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环抑制素B浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of inhibin B in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating antimullerian hormone concentration
terms.name_zh: 血抗缪勒管激素浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal range of the antimullerian hormone, a peptide produced by the granulosa cells of follicles. Anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH), also known as Mullerian inhibiting substance, is produced by the granulosa cells of small antral follicles of the ovary. AMH has an inhibiting role in the ovary, contributing to follicular arrest. AMH levels in women are low until the age of 8, rise rapidly until puberty and decline steadily from the age of 25 until menopause, when AMH production ceases.

terms.name: Increased circulating antimullerian hormone concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环抗缪勒管激素浓度升高
terms.definition: An elevation above the normal range of the antimullerian hormone in the circulation.

terms.name: Decreased circulating antimullerian hormone circulation
terms.name_zh: 循环抗缪勒管激素浓度降低
terms.definition: A reduction below the normal range of the antimullerian hormone in the circulation.

terms.name: Insulin receptor antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against the insulin receptor.

terms.name: Abnormal uterus morphology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the structure of the uterus

terms.name: T-shaped uterus
terms.definition: An abnormality of the uterus characterized by a normal uterine outline but with an abnormal T-shaped uterine cavity with narrowing cavity due to thickened lateral walls with a correlation 2/3 uterine corpus and 1/3 cervix. The abnormlaity is said to resemble the letter T in hysterosalpingographic imaging.

terms.name: Decreased fibular diameter
terms.definition: Reduced width of the cross sectional diameter of the fibula.

terms.name: Triceps weakness
terms.definition: A lack of strength in the triceps muscle, which normally is responsible for extending (straightening) the elbow and mediating certain shoulder movements.

terms.name: Agalactia
terms.definition: Failure of secretion of milk following childbirth associated with an inability to breastfeed an infant.

terms.name: Twin-to-twin transfusion
terms.definition: As a result of sharing a single placenta, the blood supplies of monochorionic twin fetuses can become connected, so that they share blood circulation: although each fetus uses its own portion of the placenta, the connecting blood vessels within the placenta allow blood to pass from one twin to the other.Depending on the number, type and direction of the interconnecting blood vessels (anastomoses), blood can be transferred disproportionately from one twin (the donor) to the other (the recipient). This state of transfusion causes the donor twin to have decreased blood volume, retarding the donor's development and growth. The blood volume of the recipient twin is increased, which can strain the fetus's heart and eventually lead to heart failure.

terms.name: Cutaneous hamartoma
terms.definition: A hamartoma (tissue malformation consisting of an abnormal mixture of constitutive components) originating in the skin.

terms.name: Purely bicuspid aortic valve
terms.definition: A type of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) characterized by two equal-sized cusps, with no raphe and only two commissures. There is a lateral arrangement of the free edge of the cusps. Note that this differs from some other forms of BAV in which there are three commissures and two of the three cusps are joined by a raphe forming two functional leaflets. This type of BAV often is associated with aortic stenosis.

terms.name: Single raphe bicuspid aortic valve
terms.definition: A type of bicuspid aortic valvue (BAV) characterized by the presence of a single raphe that extends from the commissure to the free edge of the two underdeveloped, conjoint cusps, resulting in two leaflets of unequal size.

terms.name: Bicuspid aortic valve with right-left cusp fusion
terms.name_zh: 二叶式主动脉瓣伴右-左冠瓣融合
terms.definition: A type of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) characterized by a single raphe between the right and left cusps (RL fusion pattern). This results in two leaflefts with an anterior-posterior leaflet orientation (also called the typical pattern). There is thus one completely developed noncoronary cusp, two completely developed commissures, and one raphe between the underdeveloped left and right coronary cusps extending to the corresponding malformed commissure.

terms.name: Bicuspid aortic valve with right-noncoronary cusp fusion
terms.name_zh: 二叶式主动脉瓣伴右-无冠瓣融合
terms.definition: A type of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) characterized by a single raphe between the right and noncoronary cusps (RN fusion pattern). This results in two leaflets with right-left leaflet orientation (also called the atypical pattern). There is thus one completely developed left cusp, two completely developed commissures, and one raphe between the underdeveloped right and noncoronary coronary cusps extending to the corresponding malformed commissure.

terms.name: Bicuspid aortic valve with left-noncoronary cusp fusion
terms.name_zh: 二叶式主动脉瓣伴左-无冠瓣融合
terms.definition: A type of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) characterized by a single raphe between the left and noncoronary cusps (LN fusion pattern). There is thus one completely developed right cusp, two completely developed commissures, and one raphe between the underdeveloped left and noncoronary coronary cusps extending to the corresponding malformed commissure.

terms.name: Two-raphe bicuspid aortic valve
terms.definition: A type of bicuspid aortic valvue (BAV) characterized by the presence of two raphes that each extend from the commissure to the free edge of the two underdeveloped, conjoint cusps. This type of BAV has developmental anlagen of three cusps, commissures, and sinuses, but two commissures are more or less malformed and obliterated, giving rise to a raphe, a fibrous ridge, which extends from the commissure to the free edge of the two underdeveloped, conjoint cusps. This type of BAV is typically associated with a high degree of aortic stenosis.

terms.name: Recurrent gastroenteritis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to gastroenteritis, an infectious inflammationof the stomach and small intestines manifested by signs and symptoms such as diarheas and abdominal pain, as manifested by recurrent episodes of gastroenteritis.

terms.name: Decreased platelet thromboxane A2 receptor
terms.name_zh: 血小板血栓烷A2受体减少
terms.definition: Decreased cell membrane concentration of thromboxane A2 receptor that is stimulated by thromboxane A2 (TBXA2).

terms.name: Decreased platelet alpha-2A-adrenergic receptor
terms.name_zh: 血小板α-2A肾上腺素能受体减少
terms.definition: Decreased cell membrane concentration of alpha-2A adrenergic receptor that is stimulated by epinephrine.

terms.name: Impaired clot retraction
terms.definition: Platelets contain contractile proteins (actin and myosin) that induce clot retraction. As the platelets contract, they pull on the surrounding fibrin strands, squeezing serum form the mass, compacting the clot and drawing the ruptured edges of the blood vessel more closely together. Clot retraction is directly proportional to the platelet count and inversely proportional to the fibrinogen concentration.

terms.name: Impaired convulxin-induced platelet aggregation
terms.definition: Abnormal response to convulxin as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of convulxin.

terms.name: Impaired collagen-related peptide-induced platelet aggregation
terms.name_zh: 胶原相关肽诱导血小板聚集障碍
terms.definition: Abnormal response to collagen-related peptide (CRP) as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of CRP.

terms.name: Impaired phorbol myristate acetate-induced platelet aggregation
terms.name_zh: 佛波醇肉豆蔻酸乙酸酯诱导的血小板聚集障碍
terms.definition: Abnormal response to phorbol myristate acetate (PMA) as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of PMA.

terms.name: Impaired calcium ionophore-induced platelet aggregation
terms.name_zh: 钙离子载体诱导血小板聚集障碍
terms.definition: Abnormal response to calcium Ionophore (such as A23187) as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of the ionophore.

terms.name: Abnormal platelet phosphatidylserine exposure
terms.name_zh: 血小板磷脂酰丝氨酸暴露异常
terms.definition: An abnormality of phosphatidylserine (PS) on activated platelets. PS is normally located on the cytoplasmic face of the resting platelet membrane but appears on the plasma-oriented surface of discrete membrane vesicles that derive from activated platelets. Thrombin, the central molecule of coagulation, is produced from prothrombin by a complex (prothrombinase) between factor Xa and its protein cofactor (factor V(a)) that forms on platelet-derived membranes. This complex enhances the rate of activation of prothrombin to thrombin by roughly 150,000 fold relative to factor X(a) in solution. The negatively charged surface of PS-containing platelet-derived membranes is at least partly responsible for this rate enhancement.

terms.name: Impaired annexin V binding to platelet phosphatidylserine
terms.name_zh: 膜联蛋白V与血小板磷脂酰丝氨酸结合障碍
terms.definition: Reduced binding of annexin V to platelet membrane, which is mediated by exposed phosphatidylserine. This can be measured by flow cytometry.

terms.name: Increased annexin V binding to platelet phosphatidylserine
terms.name_zh: 膜联蛋白V与血小板磷脂酰丝氨酸结合增加
terms.definition: Elevated binding of annexin V to platelet membrane, which is mediated by exposed phosphatidylserine. This can be measured by flow cytometry.

terms.name: Cor triatriatum sinister
terms.definition: A developmental anomaly of the heart characterized by the presence of three atria because the left atrium is divided by an abnormal septum.

terms.name: Triggered by physical trauma
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a trauma (injury to tissue).

terms.name: Decreased acrosin in sperm head
terms.definition: A reduced amount of the enzyme acrosin in the sperm head acrosome. The acrosome is an organelle in the anterior half of the head of spermatozoa, and acrosin is a protease that contributes to the digestation of the zona pellucida in the fertilization process.

terms.name: Storage in hepatocytes
terms.definition: Hepatocytes (liver parenchymal cells) exhibit a bloated appearance because of expansion of the cytoplasm by accumulated material.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating B-type natriuretic peptide concentration
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal circulating concentration of B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP).

terms.name: Frog-leg posture
terms.definition: A type of rest posture in an infant that indicated a generalized reduction in muscle tone. The hips are flexed and the legs are abducted to an extent that causes the lateral thigh to rest upon the supporting surface. This posture is said to resemble the legs of a frog.

terms.name: Abnormal liver sonography
terms.definition: An abnormal appearance of the liver or any of its components on sonography (ultrasound).

terms.name: Increased hepatic echogenicity
terms.definition: Increased echogenicity of liver tissue on sonography, manifested as an increased amount of white on the screen of the sonography device.

terms.name: Abnormal hepatic echogenicity
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal degree of echogenicity of the liver on sonography. Echogenicity refers to the ability of a tissue to reflect or transmit ultrasound waves in the context of surrounding tissues. Whenever there is an interface of structures with different echogenicities, a visible difference in contrast will be apparent on the screen. Based on echogenicity, a structure can be characterized as hyperechoic (white on the screen), hypoechoic (gray on the screen) and anechoic (black on the screen).

terms.name: Decreased hepatic echogenicity
terms.definition: Reduced echogenicity of liver tissue on sonography, manifested as an increased amount of black on the screen of the sonography device.

terms.name: Coarsened hepatic echotexture
terms.definition: The appearance of the liver in sonographic images is normally uniform. This term applies when there is an irregular or non-uniform appearance of the liver parenchyma in liver sonography.

terms.name: Starry sky appearance on hepatic sonography
terms.definition: An abnormal echotexture visible in liver ultrasound manifesting as a diffuse hyperechoic liver echotexture with multiple, small hypoechoic lesions. The appearance is said to resemble a starry sky (multiple white spots on a dark background).

terms.name: Impaired oral bolus formation
terms.definition: An abnormality of swallowing characterized by reduced tongue coordination to form bolus after chewing. Food material spreads over the oral cavity instead of being concentrated into a bolus that is easily swallowed.

terms.name: Vitreomacular adhesion
terms.definition: Perifoveal vitreous separation with remaining vitreomacular attachment and unperturbed foveal morphologic features. It is an OCT finding that is almost always the result of normal vitreous aging, which may lead to pathologic conditions.

terms.name: Vitreomacular traction
terms.definition: Vitreomacular traction is characterized by anomalous posterior vitreous detachment accompanied by anatomic distortion of the fovea, which may include pseudocysts, macular schisis, cystoid macular edema, and subretinal fluid. Vitreomacular traction can be subclassified by the diameter of vitreous attachment to the macular surface as measured by OCT, with attachment of 1500 micrometers or less defined as focal and attachment of more than 1500 micrometers as broad.

terms.name: Full-thickness macular hole
terms.definition: Full-thickness macular hole (FTMH) is defined as a foveal lesion with interruption of all retinal layers from the internal limiting membrane to the retinal pigment epithelium. Full-thickness macular hole is primary if caused by vitreous traction or secondary if directly the result of pathologic characteristics other than vitreomacular traction. Full-thickness macular hole is subclassified by size of the hole as determined by OCT and the presence or absence of vitreomacular traction.

terms.name: Membranous vitreous appearance
terms.definition: Vitreous humor of the eye displaying consisting of a vestigial gel in the retrolental space bounded by a convoluted membrane.

terms.name: Beaded vitreous appearance
terms.definition: Vitreous humor of the eye displaying beaded bundles of irregular diameters.

terms.name: Increased Arden ratio of electrooculogram
terms.definition: An abnormal increase in the Arden ratio, which is the ratio between the light peak and the dark trough of the smoothed (physiologic) EOG record.

terms.name: Decreased platelet glycoprotein Ib
terms.definition: Decreased platelet cell membrane concentration of glycoprotein Ib.

terms.name: Carotid cavernous fistula
terms.definition: An abnormal connection between a carotid artery and the cavernous sinus.

terms.name: Widened atrophic scar
terms.definition: An atrophic scar (fibrous connective tissue resulting from incomplete healing of a wound) that has stretched (gotten wider), a manifestation of tissue fragility.

terms.name: Thinning of Descemet membrane
terms.definition: A reduction in the thickness of Descemet's membrane.

terms.name: Myelokathexis
terms.definition: Impaired egress of mature neutrophils from bone marrow causing neutropenia.

terms.name: Reduced brain glutamate level by MRS
terms.definition: An decrease in the level of glutamate (Glu) in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

terms.name: Impaired oropharyngeal swallow response
terms.definition: Delay or absence of the swallow response, reflexes triggered by the contact the food bolus makes with the anterior faucial pillars.

terms.name: Low femoral bone density
terms.definition: Reduced bone mineral density of the femur.

terms.name: Growth arrest lines
terms.definition: Growth arrest lines are alternating transverse rings of sclerosis at the metaphysis of a long bone.

terms.name: Multifocal seizures
terms.definition: Seizures that start from several different areas of the brain (i.e., with multiple ictal onset locations).

terms.name: Eyelid myokymia
terms.definition: Involuntary, fine, continuous, undulating contractions of the eyelid.

terms.name: Triggered by ingestion of potassium-rich food
synonyms: Triggered by ingestion of K-rich food
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking foods rich in potassium.

terms.name: Postterm pregnancy
terms.definition: A pregnancy that extends to 42 weeks of gestation or beyond.

terms.name: Female fetal virilization
terms.definition: Fetal masculinization of female external genitalia.

terms.name: Femoral spur
terms.definition: A bony projection (spur, osteophyte) originating from the femur, often in the medial femoral neck.

terms.name: Sectoral retinitis pigmentosa
terms.definition: A variant of retinitis pigmentosa in which there is a regional distribution of the retinal degeneration.

terms.name: Tibial spur
terms.definition: A bony projection (spur, osteophyte) originating from the tibia.

terms.name: Double-layered patella
terms.definition: An anomaly of the patella characterized by two layers visible on lateral knee X-ray such that one layer is in front of the other in the sagittal orientation (See Figure 2A and 3B of PMID:12966518). This finding persists into adulthood.

terms.name: Absent cervical vertebra
terms.definition: A developmental defect characterized by agenesis of one or more vertebral bodies of the cervical spine.

terms.name: Absent thoracic vertebra
terms.definition: A developmental defect characterized by agenesis of one or more vertebral bodies of the thoracic spine.

terms.name: Finger flexor weakness
terms.definition: Reduced ability to flex (bend) the fingers. This can manifest as incomplete closure of the hand due to weakness in finger flexion.

terms.name: Fixed head retroflexion
terms.definition: Head is bent in the posterior direction in a permanent fashion.

terms.name: Nuchal rigidity
terms.definition: Resistance of the extensor muscles of the neck to being bent forwards (i.e., impaired neck flexion) as a result of muscle spasm of the extensor muscles of the neck. Nuchal rigidity is not a fixed rigidity. Nuchal rigidity has been used as a bedside test for meningism, although its sensitivity for this purpose has been debated.

terms.name: Erythema migrans
terms.definition: An expanding erythematous (red) skin lesion, usually round or oval, by definition at least 5 cm in size (in largest diameter).

terms.name: Necrolytic migratory erythema
terms.definition: Acral or periorificial lesions that evolve in recurrent crops, with an annular and migratory distribution.

terms.name: Elevated circulating NT-proBNP concentration
terms.name_zh: 血N末端B型利钠肽原浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of NT-proBNP (= N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, = N-terminal prohormone of brain natriuretic peptide) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating deoxycorticosterone level
terms.name_zh: 血脱氧皮质酮水平异常
terms.definition: An abnormality of the concentration of deoxycorticosterone in the blood. Deoxycorticosterone comprises 11-deoxycorticosterone and 21-deoxycorticosterone.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating pregnenolone concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环孕烯醇酮浓度异常
terms.definition: An abnormality of the concentration of pregnenolone in the blood.

terms.name: Genital edema
terms.definition: A buildup of fluid that causes swelling in the soft tissues of the genital area.

terms.name: Wrist drop
terms.definition: A condition in which the affected individual cannot extend the wrist, which hangs flaccidly.

terms.name: Superficial dermal perivascular inflammatory infiltrate
terms.definition: Numerous lymphocytes surrounding blood vessels in the superficial part of the dermis.

terms.name: Deep dermal perivascular inflammatory infiltrate
terms.name_zh: 真皮深层血管周围炎症浸润
terms.definition: Numerous lymphocytes surrounding blood vessels in the deep part of the dermis.

terms.name: Abnormal morphology of left ventricular trabeculae
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the muscular columns which project from the inner surface of the left ventricle of the heart (cardiac trabeculae, trabeculae carneae).

terms.name: Abnormal morphology of right ventricular trabeculae
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the muscular columns which project from the inner surface of the right ventricle of the heart (cardiac trabeculae, trabeculae carneae).

terms.name: Increased density of left ventricular trabeculae
terms.name_zh: 左心室肌小梁密度增高
terms.definition: An increased density (number and tightness) of the muscular columns which project from the inner surface of the left ventricles of the heart (cardiac trabeculae, trabeculae carneae).

terms.name: Apical hypertrabeculation of the left ventricle
terms.name_zh: 左心室心尖部过度小梁化
terms.definition: An increased number and density of the trabeculae in the apex (tip) of the left ventricle.

terms.name: Thin myocardium compact layer
terms.definition: Reduced thickness of the outer, dense layer of the myocardium.

terms.name: Cellular urinary casts
terms.definition: A type of urinary cast composed of cells incorporated in a protein matrix. The cells can be those found in the urinary sediment (erythrocytes, leuklocytes, renal tubular epithelial cells).

terms.name: Renal tubular epithelial cell casts
terms.definition: A type of cellular urinary cast composed of renal tubular epithelial cells.

terms.name: Acellular urinary casts
terms.definition: A type of urinary cast composed of a proteinaceous matrix without a substantial number of cells.

terms.name: Hyaline casts
terms.definition: A type of acellular urinary cast that are composed only of Tamm-Horsfall glycoprotein, a fact which explains their low refractive index. Hyaline casts may display a spectrum of morphologies, which includes fluffy, compact, convoluted or wrinkled casts. Hyaline casts have a smooth texture and usually have parallel sides with clear margins and blunted ends.

terms.name: Granular casts
terms.definition: A type of acelluar casts that have a surface composed of granules, which can vary in size. The granules can be rather heterogeneous, ranging from fine (finely granular cast) up to coarse (coarsely granular cast), dark, clear, and pigmented.

terms.name: Waxy casts
terms.definition: A type of acellular urinary casts that display a melted wax (waxy) appearance, which gives them a high refractive index. They are frequently dark, with blunt extremities, indented and cracked edges and a large size, which is often several times that of other types of casts.

terms.name: Fatty casts
terms.definition: A type of acellular urinary casts that contain lipid droplets, oval fat bodies or cholesterol crystals, and are often associated with the free forms of these elements. Their identification may require the use of polarized light microscopy, under which fatty particles embedded into the cast matrix appear as Maltese crosses.

terms.name: Bacterial cell casts
terms.definition: A type of urinary cast that contain bacteria. Bacterial casts can be difficult to identify and can be distinguished from other types of casts using phase contrast microscopy. Bacterial casts are diagnostic of acute pyelonephritis or intrinsic renal infection.

terms.name: Reduced lysosomal acid lipase activity
terms.definition: Reduction in the activity of lysosomal acid lipase (LAL) in the blood. Lysosomal lipase activity is measured. LAL hydrolyzes cholesteryl esters derived from cell internalization of plasma lipoproteins.

terms.name: Striatal T2 hyperintensity
terms.definition: Abnormally bright T2 signal from the striatum on brain magnetic resonance imaging.

terms.name: Hepatic hemangioma
terms.definition: A congenital vascular malformation in the liver composed of masses of blood vessels that are atypical or irregular in arrangement and size.

terms.name: Increased pituitary glycoprotein hormone alpha subunit level
terms.name_zh: 垂体糖蛋白激素α亚基水平升高
synonyms: Increased pituitary glycoprotein alpha subunit level
Increased pituitary glycoprotein polypeptide alpha subunit level
terms.definition: An increased concentration of circulating alpha polypeptide of glycoprotein hormones (NCBI Gene 1081). This alpha subunit is common to luteinizing hormone (LH) , follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) , thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) and human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), which are glycoprotein hormones composed of an identical alpha subunit together with a beta subunit that confers biological specificity. The alpha subunit is used as a marker for tumors that produce these hormones.

terms.name: Decreased circulating lipoprotein lipase concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环脂蛋白脂酶浓度降低
terms.definition: Reduction in the level of lipoprotein lipase in the blood.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating hyaluronic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环透明质酸浓度异常
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of hyaluronic acid in the blood.

terms.name: Elevated cholesterol ester level
terms.definition: An elevated concentration of circulating cholesterol esters, which are fatty acid esters of cholesterol and make up about two-thirds of total plasma cholesterol.

terms.name: Elevated circulating 17-hydroxyprogesterone concentration
terms.definition: An increased level of 17-hydroxyprogesterone in the blood. 17-hydroxyprogesterone is an intermediate steroid in the adrenal biosynthetic pathway from cholesterol to cortisol and is the substrate for steroid 21-hydroxylase.

terms.name: Decreased circulating dehydroepiandrosterone concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环脱氢表雄酮浓度降低

terms.name: Decreased circulating dehydroepiandrosterone-sulfate concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环硫酸脱氢表雄酮浓度降低
terms.definition: A reduced concentration of dehydroepiandrosterone-sulfate in the blood.

terms.name: Increased circulating progesterone
terms.definition: An elevated concentration of progesterone in the blood.

terms.name: Hot flashes
terms.definition: Sudden feelings of warmth that are generally most pronounced over the face, neck and chest.

terms.name: Inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion
synonyms: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion
terms.definition: A state of increased circulating antidiuretic hormone despite hyponatremia and hypo-osmolality with normal or increased plasma volume.

terms.name: Reduced radioactive iodine uptake
terms.definition: A decreased amount of uptake on the radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) test, which utilizes a radioisotope of iodine to measure how much iodine the thyroid gland absorbs from the blood. The radioactive marker is measured 4-6 hours and in some cases also 24 hours after administration of the radioactive marker.

terms.name: Increased radioactive iodine uptake
terms.definition: An elevated amount of uptake on the radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) test, which utilizes a radioisotope of iodine to measure how much iodine the thyroid gland absorbs from the blood. The radioactive marker is measured 4-6 hours and in some cases also 24 hours after administration of the radioactive marker.

terms.name: Abnormal radioactive iodine uptake test result
terms.name_zh: 放射性碘摄取试验结果异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from normal in the amount of uptake on the radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) test, which utilizes a radioisotope of iodine to measure how much iodine the thyroid gland absorbs from the blood. The radioactive marker is measured 4-6 hours and in some cases also 24 hours after administration of the radioactive marker.

terms.name: Elevated circulating thyroxine-binding globulin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血甲状腺素结合球蛋白浓度升高
synonyms: Elevated thyroxine-binding globulin level in blood
Increased thyroxine-binding globulin level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of thyroxine-binding globulin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Focal pancreatic islet hyperplasia
terms.definition: Hyperplasia of the islets of Langerhans that affects only certain regions of the pancreas and not others.

terms.name: Diffuse pancreatic islet hyperplasia
terms.definition: Hyperplasia of the islets of Langerhans with a generalized distribution.

terms.name: Intrapulmonary shunt
terms.definition: Blood flow through a region of the lung in which little or no ventilation takes place, resulting in reduced oxygenation of the blood leaving the lungs.

terms.name: Perinephric fluid collection
terms.definition: An accumulation of fluid in one or more of the perinephric spaces, which consist of the subcapsular, perirenal, anterior and posterior pararenal spaces. This abnormality can be demonstrated by cross-sectional imaging, particularly computed tomography.

terms.name: Nasopharyngeal teratoma
terms.definition: A teratoma arising in the nasopharyngeal region.

terms.name: Abnormal incisura morphology
terms.definition: An abnormal shape of the incisura, defined as the narrowed downward continuation of the conchal space bounded anteriorly by the borders of the tragus, posteriorly by the antitragus, and along its lower lateral margins and inferior boundary by the connection between the first two. The upper boundary is a somewhat arbitrary line crossing from the apices of the antitragus and the tragus.

terms.name: Increased incisura length
terms.definition: The length of the incisura from the upper to lower border is greater than that observed in the average population.

terms.name: Decreased incisura length
terms.definition: The length of the incisura from the upper to lower border is less than that observed in the average population.

terms.name: Narrow incisura width
terms.definition: Width of the incisura from the anterior to posterior border less than that observed in the average population.

terms.name: Increased incisura width
terms.definition: Breadth of the incisura from the anterior to posterior border greater than that observed in the average population.

terms.name: Horizontal inferior border of scapula
terms.definition: A morphological abnormality of the scapula in which there is a flat (horizontal) inferior edge of the scapula. The entire scapula is said to resemble a square, leading to the designation sqaring of the scapula (in Figure 1 of PMID:24706940 the scapulae have a roughly rectangular shape).

terms.name: Neutrophilic infiltration of the skin
terms.definition: A predominantly neutrophilic infiltrate of the dermis and or epidermis (i.e., a large number of neutrophils inferred to have migrated into the skin).

terms.name: Predominantly epidermal neutrophilic infiltrate
terms.definition: Collection of neutrophils in the epidermis.

terms.name: Predominantly dermal neutrophilic infiltrate
terms.definition: Collection of neutrophils in the dermis.

terms.name: Internally nucleated skeletal muscle fibers
terms.definition: An abnormally increased proportion of nuclei of sarcomeres with an internal localization. Individual muscle fibers are syncytia, formed by embryonic fusion of many myoblasts or later, myosatellite cells. Each muscle fiber contains many nuclei, peripherally positioned immediately adjacent to the sarcolemmal membrane. In healthy muscle only 3-5% of fibers contain nuclei that are located internally, within the cell, but many disease processes lead to internal nuclei.

terms.name: Necklace skeletal muscle fibers
terms.definition: A histological alteration of muscle fibers that resembles a necklace (necklace fibers). A substantial proportion of fibers (4-20% in PMID:19084976) show internalized nuclei aligned in a basophilic ring (necklace) at 3 micrometers beneath the sarcolemma. Ultrastructurally, such necklaces consist of myofibrils of smaller diameter, in oblique orientation, surrounded by mitochondria, sarcoplasmic reticulum and glycogen granules.

terms.name: Extrafoveal choroidal neovascularization
terms.name_zh: 中心凹外脉络膜新生血管
terms.definition: A type of choroidal neovascularization in which the nearest edge of the area of neovascularization is located 200 to 1500 micrometers from the center of the fovea.

terms.name: Juxtafoveal choroidal neovascularization
terms.name_zh: 旁中心凹脉络膜新生血管
terms.definition: A type of choroidal neovascularization in which the nearest edge of the area of neovascularization is located 1 to 199 micrometers from the center of the fovea.

terms.name: Subfoveal choroidal neovascularization
terms.definition: A type of choroidal neovascularization in which the area of neovascularization overlaps with the center of the fovea.

terms.name: Decreased circulating chylomicron concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环乳糜微粒浓度降低
terms.definition: Reduced plasma concentrations of chylomicrons, the large lipid droplet (up to 100 mm in diameter) of reprocessed lipid synthesized in epithelial cells of the small intestine and containing triacylglycerols, cholesterol esters, and several apolipoproteins.

terms.name: Decreased circulating VLDL-C concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环极低密度脂蛋白胆固醇浓度降低
synonyms: Decreased very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level in blood
Reduced very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Swollen lip
terms.definition: Enlargement of the lip typically due to fluid buildup or inflammation.

terms.name: Productive cough
terms.definition: A cough that produces phlegm or mucus.

terms.name: Nonproductive cough
terms.definition: A cough that does not produce phlegm or mucus.

terms.name: Whooping cough
terms.definition: A type of cough characterized by a burst of numerous and rapid coughs followed by a long inhaling effort that is accompanied by a high-pitched whooping sound produced by the inhalation of air.

terms.name: Palmar pruritus
terms.definition: Pruritus is an itch or a sensation that makes a person want to scratch. This term refers to an abnormally increased sensation of itching over the palm(s) of the hand.

terms.name: Parageusia
terms.definition: A distortion of the sense of taste, often characterized by the sensation of a metallic taste.

terms.name: Lip fissure
terms.definition: A severe crack in a lip. A lip fissure may be painful, may bleed and often is a recurring manifestation.

terms.name: Abnormal subclavian artery morphology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of a subclavian artery.

terms.name: Dilated left subclavian artery
terms.definition: Abnormally increased caliber of the left subclavian artery.

terms.name: Anomalous origin of left subclavian artery
terms.name_zh: 左锁骨下动脉起源异常
terms.definition: Origin of the left subclavian artery from an anomalous anatomical location.

terms.name: Thalamic arteriovenous malformation
terms.definition: An arteriovenous malformation is a disruption of the normal vascular pattern in which arteries or arterioles connect directly to the venous collection system, bypassing any capillary bed. This term refers to an arteriovenous malformation located in the thalamus.

terms.name: Hypothalamic arteriovenous malformation
terms.definition: An arteriovenous malformation is a disruption of the normal vascular pattern in which arteries or arterioles connect directly to the venous collection system, bypassing any capillary bed. This term refers to an arteriovenous malformation located in the hypothalamus.

terms.name: Optic nerve arteriovenous malformation
terms.definition: An arteriovenous malformation is a disruption of the normal vascular pattern in which arteries or arterioles connect directly to the venous collection system, bypassing any capillary bed. This term refers to an arteriovenous malformation located in the optic nerve.

terms.name: Arteriovenous malformation of the maxilla
terms.definition: An arteriovenous malformation is a disruption of the normal vascular pattern in which arteries or arterioles connect directly to the venous collection system, bypassing any capillary bed. This term refers to an arteriovenous malformation located in the maxilla.

terms.name: Delirium
terms.definition: A state of sudden and severe confusion.

terms.name: Oophoritis
terms.definition: An inflammation of the ovary or ovaries.

terms.name: Triangular tibia
terms.definition: A short, dysplastic tibia with a triangular shape. Instead of the normal shaft configuration of the tibia, the tibia forms a triangle with the longest side corresponding to the proximal-distal dimension, and the apex of the triangle directed laterally.

terms.name: Bladder polyp
terms.definition: An abnormal growth that projects from the mucous membrane of the urinary bladder.

terms.name: Abnormal renal corpuscle morphology
terms.definition: Any anomalous structure of the renal corpuscle, which is the initial component of the nephron that filters blood. The renal corpuscle consists of a knot of capillaries (glomerulus) that is surrounded by a double-walled capsule (Bowman capsule) that opens into a renal tubule.

terms.name: Abnormal Bowman capsule morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the double-walled capsule (Bowman capsule) that opens into a renal tubule.

terms.name: Abnormal glomerular visceral epithelial cell morphology
terms.name_zh: 肾小球脏层上皮细胞形态异常
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the podocyte, which is a highly specialized cell of the Bowman capsule and which forms multiple interdigitating foot processes. Podocytes are interconnected by slit diaphragms and cover the exterior basement membrane surface of the glomerular capillary.

terms.name: Podocyte foot process effacement
terms.definition: An anomaly of podocyte morphology characterized by the loss of the interdigitating foot process pattern (generally called foot process effacement; FPE). The term FPE designates the loss of the usual interdigitating pattern of foot processes of neighboring podocytes, leading to relatively broad expanses of podocyte processes covering the glomerular basement membrane (GBM). It is widely viewed as a pathological derangement that is associated with leakage of macromolecules such as albumin through the glomerular filtration barrier.

terms.name: Abnormal CD69 upregulation upon TCR activation
terms.definition: Any abnormality in the upregulation of CD69 on T cells after activation via the T cell receptor (TCR). Upregulation of CD69 is one of the earliest and most sensitive measures of antigen recognition in the periphery, and transient expression of CD69 is associated with positive selection in the thymus.

terms.name: Decreased CD69 upregulation upon TCR activation
terms.definition: Reduced or impaired upregulation of CD69 on T cells after activation via the T cell receptor (TCR).

terms.name: Abnormal CD25 upregulation upon TCR activation
terms.definition: Any abnormality in the upregulation of CD25 on T cells after activation via the T cell receptor (TCR). CD25 is the alpha chain of the IL2 receptor. Ligation of the T cell antigen receptor leads to the induction of CD25 expression.

terms.name: Decreased CD25 upregulation upon TCR activation
synonyms: Poor CD25 upregulation upon TCR activation
Reduced IL2RA upregulation upon TCR activation
terms.definition: Decreased or impaired upregulation of CD25 on T cells after activation via the T cell receptor (TCR).

terms.name: Absent ankle pulse
terms.definition: The pulsation of the posterior tibial artery behind the internal malleolus, or of the dorsalis pedis artery, cannot be detected on physical examination.

terms.name: Pulmonary arterial atherosclerosis
terms.definition: Accumulation of lipids and inflammatory cells along the inner walls of the pulmonary artery.

terms.name: Shock
terms.definition: The state in which profound and widespread reduction of effective tissue perfusion leads first to reversible, and then if prolonged, to irreversible cellular injury.

terms.name: Hypovolemic shock
terms.definition: A state of shock characterized by decreased circulating blood volume in relation to total vascular capacity. This type of shock is characterized by a reduction of diastolic filling pressures.

terms.name: Distributive shock
terms.definition: A hyperdynamic process resulting from excessive vasodilatation. Impaired blood flow causes inadequate tissue perfusion, which can lead to end-organ damage

terms.name: Obstructive shock
terms.definition: A type of shock characterized by inadequate cardiac preload due to obstructed venous return (e.g. pericardial tamponade, tension pneumothorax, abdominal compartment) or obstruction of arterial blood flow (e.g. pulmonary embolism).

terms.name: Abnormal thoracic duct morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the thoracic duct.

terms.name: Abnormal response to gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulation test
terms.name_zh: 促性腺激素释放激素兴奋试验反应异常
synonyms: Abnormal response to GnRH stimulation test
terms.definition: An abnormal response to the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test. This test typically involves intravenous administration of GnRH followed by repeated blood sampling at various time points to measure the levels of luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).

terms.name: Increased LH response to gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulation test
terms.name_zh: 促性腺激素释放激素兴奋试验黄体生成素反应升高
terms.definition: An abnormally high amount of luteinizing hormone (LH) is released upon gonadotropin-releasing hormone stimulation test.

terms.name: Sialadenitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of a salivary gland.

terms.name: Malalignment of the great toenail
terms.definition: A lateral deviation of the nail plate of the great toe along the longitudinal axis due to the lateral rotation of the nail matrix. The nail plate grows out in ridges.

terms.name: Tufted hairs
terms.definition: The presence of tufts of 8-15 hairs that appear to emerge from a single follicular orifice.

terms.name: Flushing
terms.definition: Recurrent episodes of redness of the skin together with a sensation of warmth or burning of the affected areas of skin.

terms.name: Abnormal perifollicular morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly in the areas surrounding the hair follicles.

terms.name: Perifollicular erythema
terms.definition: Redness surrounding the hair follicles.

terms.name: Seborrheic keratosis
terms.definition: A raised growth on the skin of older individuals. The lesion usually is initially light tan and may darken to dark brown or nearly black. The consistent feature of seborrheic keratoses is their waxy, pasted-on or stuck-on look.

terms.name: Cobblestone-like hyperkeratosis
terms.definition: The presence of verrucous, cobblestone-like papules and nodules in a region of skin that is said to have an appearance like that of cobblestones.

terms.name: White papule
terms.definition: A papule with white color.

terms.name: Tuberous xanthoma
terms.definition: A type of xanthoma characterized by a nodular form. Tuberous xanthomas are firm subcutaneous nodules,whereby the overlying skin can have red or red-yellow color changes.

terms.name: Ichthyosis follicularis
terms.definition: Ichthyosis follicularis is characterized by widespread non inflammatory thorn-like follicular projections. Dyskeratotic papules are most pronounced over the extensor extremities and scalp and are symmetrically distributed.

terms.name: Cutaneous abscess
terms.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the skin (within the epidermis or dermis).

terms.name: Digital pitting scar
terms.definition: Pinhole-sized concave depressions with hyperkeratosis in the skin of a finger or toe.

terms.name: Hypoplastic right atrium
terms.definition: Underdeveloped, small right heart atrium.

terms.name: Left atrial enlargement
terms.definition: Increase in size of the left atrium.

terms.name: Atrial septal hypertrophy
terms.definition: An abnormal increase in the thickness of the atrial septum.

terms.name: Coronary sinus enlargement
terms.definition: Abnormal increase in size of the coronary sinus.

terms.name: Elevated left atrial pressure
terms.definition: An abnormal increase in magnitude of the pressure in the left atrium.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating properdin concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of properdin in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Peripheral arterial calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall.

terms.name: Lower extremity peripheral arterial calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall of the leg.

terms.name: Femoral arterial calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall of the femoral artery.

terms.name: Iliac arterial calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall of the iliac artery.

terms.name: Tibial arterial calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall of the tibial artery.

terms.name: Intracranial arterial calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in an artery that is located within the skull (intracranial).

terms.name: Internal carotid artery calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the internal carotid artery.

terms.name: Vertebral artery calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the vertebral artery.

terms.name: Cerebral artery calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in a cerebral artery.

terms.name: Basilar artery calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the basilar artery.

terms.name: Middle cerebral artery calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the middle cerebral artery.

terms.name: Abdominal aortic calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in abdominal aorta.

terms.name: Carotid artery calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in a carotid artery.

terms.name: External carotid artery calcification
terms.definition: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the external carotid artery.

terms.name: Abnormal ventricular myocardium morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the muscle layer of the heart wall of a cardiac ventricle.

terms.name: Fatty replacement of ventricular myocardial tissue
terms.name_zh: 心室心肌组织脂肪替代
terms.definition: Presence of an increased amount of fat tissue within a cardiac ventricle with corresponding reduction of muscle tissue.

terms.name: Myofiber disarray
terms.definition: A nonparallel arrangement of cardiac myocytes.

terms.name: Cardiomyocyte hypertrophy
terms.definition: An increase in cell size, enhanced protein synthesis, and heightened organization of the sarcomere within cardiac myocytes.

terms.name: Cardiomyocyte mitochondrial proliferation
terms.definition: An abnormal increase in the number of mitochondria per cardiac myocyte.

terms.name: Myocardial immune cell infiltration
terms.definition: An increase in the number of immune cells in myocardial tissue (which can be assumed to have migrated into the myocardium).

terms.name: Myocardial lymphocytic infiltration
terms.definition: An increase in the number of lymphocytes in myocardial tissue.

terms.name: Myocardial eosinophilic infiltration
terms.definition: An increase in the number of eosinophils in myocardial tissue.

terms.name: Myocardial multinucleated giant cells
terms.definition: The presence of extremely large cells with multiple nuclei. The so-called giant cells are thought to be of macrophage origin.

terms.name: Myocardial granulomatous infiltrates
terms.definition: The presence of multiple granulomata (small nodular inflammatory lesions containing grouped mononuclear phagocytes) in the myocardium.

terms.name: Monoclonal light chain cardiac amyloidosis
terms.name_zh: 单克隆轻链型心脏淀粉样变
terms.definition: A type of cardiac amyloidosis related to deposition of an immunoglobulin light chain. The current gold standard of amyloid typing is to determine the precursor protein using laser microdissection mass spectrometry.

terms.name: Cardiac transthyretin amyloid deposition
terms.name_zh: 心脏转甲状腺素蛋白淀粉样沉积
terms.definition: A type of cardiac amyloidosis related to deposition of transthyretin (TTR), which is identified by immunohistochemical staining.

terms.name: Perivascular cardiac fibrosis
terms.definition: A type of myocardial fibrosis characterized by excessive diffuse collagen accumulation concentrated in perivascular spaces.

terms.name: Interstitial cardiac fibrosis
terms.definition: A type of myocardial fibrosis characterized by excessive diffuse collagen accumulation concentrated in interstitial spaces.

terms.name: Perivascular myocardial immune cell infiltration
terms.definition: An increase in the number of immune cells in myocardial tissue concentrated in the spaces surrounding blood vessels.

terms.name: Abnormal cardiomyocyte morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of cardiomyocytes, which are terminally differentiated muscle cells in the heart that are interconnected end to end by gap junctions, which allows coordinated contraction of heart tissue.

terms.name: Cardiomyocyte degeneration
terms.definition: Deterioration of cardiomyocyte characterized by abnormal features such as loss of myofilaments, occurrence of cellular sequestration, decreased mitochondrial sizes and cellular debris.

terms.name: Myocardial sarcomeric disarray
terms.definition: A disruption of the structure of the sarcomeres of cardiomyocytes. The sarcomere is the repeating unit between two Z lines comprised largely of myosin and actin that mediates contractility, and normally sarcomeres are aligned with the long axis of cells, with the Z bands being in register throughout the length of the cardiac myocytes.

terms.name: Cardiomyocyte inclusion bodies
terms.definition: Nuclear or cytoplasmic aggregates of stainable substances within cardiomyocytes.

terms.name: Abnormal cardiomyocyte mitochondrial morphology
terms.name_zh: 心肌细胞线粒体形态异常
terms.definition: An anomaly of the structure of mitochondria within cardiomyocytes.

terms.name: Intranuclear cardiomyocyte mitochondria
terms.definition: Abnormal localization of mitochondria within the nuclei of cardiomyocytes.

terms.name: Abnormal cardiomyocyte connexin43 staining
terms.name_zh: 心肌细胞连接蛋白43染色异常
terms.definition: Anomalous staining of Connexin43 in cardiomyocytes. Connexin43 (Cx43) is the primary gap junction protein in the working myocardium. Cx43 exhibits increased localization at the lateral membranes of cardiomyocytes in a variety of heart diseases.

terms.name: Abnormal cardiomyocyte plakoglobin staining
terms.name_zh: 心肌细胞盘状球蛋白染色异常
terms.definition: Anomalous staining of plakoglobin in cardiomyocytes. Plakoglobin is a component of desmosomes in cardiomyocytes.

terms.name: Abnormal cardiomyocyte dystrophin staining
terms.name_zh: 心肌细胞抗肌萎缩蛋白染色异常
terms.definition: Anomalous staining of dystrophin in cardiomyocytes.

terms.name: Abnormal lysosomal morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of lysosomes, membrane-enclosed organelles that contain an array of enzymes capable of catabolizing proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids.

terms.name: Gastric arteriovenous malformation
terms.definition: An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries and that is located in the stomach.

terms.name: Duodenal arteriovenous malformation
terms.definition: An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries and that is located in the duodenum.

terms.name: Jejunal arteriovenous malformation
terms.definition: An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries and that is located in the jejunum.

terms.name: Pelvic arteriovenous malformation
terms.definition: An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries and that is located in the pelvis.

terms.name: Colonic arteriovenous malformation
terms.definition: An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries and that is located in the colon.

terms.name: Rectal arteriovenous malformation
terms.definition: An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries and that is located in the rectum.

terms.name: Uterine arteriovenous malformation
terms.definition: An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries and that is located in the uterus.

terms.name: Dextrotransposition of the great arteries
synonyms: D-loop transposition of the great arteries
terms.definition: A type of transposition of the great arteries (TGA) in which aorta is in front of and primarily to the right of the pulmonary artery. This is the most common kind of TGA.

terms.name: Cardiac sarcoma
terms.definition: A malignant soft tissue neoplasm that arises from the heart.

terms.name: Calcified amorphous tumor of the heart
terms.name_zh: 心脏钙化性无定形肿瘤
synonyms: Calcified amorphous tumour of the heart
terms.definition: A non-neoplastic cardiac tumor characterized by calcification and eosinophilic amorphous material in the background of dense collagenous fibrous tissue.

terms.name: Chest tightness
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation of tightness or pressure in the chest.

terms.name: Otitis media with effusion
terms.definition: Otitis media characterized by thick or sticky fluid behind the tympanic membrane.

terms.name: Sleep onset insomnia
terms.definition: Difficulty initiating sleep, that is, increased sleep onset latency, refers to the condition where it takes 30 minutes or more to fall asleep.

terms.name: Maintenance insomnia
synonyms: Waking up several times during the night
terms.definition: Individuals affected by abnormal difficulty in staying asleep tend to wake up at night and struggle to return to sleep. This condition typically involves spending more than 30 minutes awake during the night.

terms.name: Terminal insomnia
terms.definition: Waking up earlier than intended and being unable to return to sleep.

terms.name: Glomeruloid hemangioma
terms.definition: A histologically distinctive, cutaneous, benign vascular tumor that is characterized by a solitary or multiple blue-red papules and histologically resembles renal glomeruli.

terms.name: Vegetative state
terms.definition: The absence of wakefulness and consciousness, but in contrast to a coma, there is involuntary opening of the eyes and movements such as teeth grinding, yawning, or thrashing of the extremities.

terms.name: Cutaneous sclerotic plaque
terms.definition: A solid, raised, plateau-like (flat-topped) lesion greater than 1 cm in diameter that is characterized by hardening (sclerosis) of the affected skin area (related to collagen thickening).

terms.name: Yellow skin plaque
terms.definition: A solid, raised, plateau-like (flat-topped) lesion greater than 1 cm in diameter and that has a yellow color.

terms.name: Zebra bodies
terms.definition: Intralysosomal, osmiophilic, lamellated and sometimes concentric cytoplasmic inclusions comprised of broad transversely-stacked myelinoid membranes and said to resemble a zebra in electron microscopic images.

terms.name: Palpable purpura
terms.definition: A type of purpura in which the lesions are raised (and can therefore be appreciated upon palpation).

terms.name: Ecchymosis
terms.definition: A purpuric lesion that is larger than 1 cm in diameter.

terms.name: Macular purpura
terms.definition: Purpura that is flat (non-palpable, not raised).

terms.name: Palate neoplasm
terms.definition: A neoplasm that affects the hard palate, soft palate, or uvula.

terms.name: Metaphyseal striations
terms.definition: Longitudinal densities on radiographs located in a metaphysis (the narrow region of a long bone between the epiphysis and the diaphysis).

terms.name: Intestinal perforation
terms.definition: A hole (perforation) in the wall of the intestine.

terms.name: Colon perforation
terms.definition: A hole (perforation) in the wall of the colon.

terms.name: Small intestinal perforation
terms.definition: A hole (perforation) in the wall of the small intestine.

terms.name: Rectal perforation
terms.definition: A hole (perforation) in the wall of the rectum.

terms.name: Cold paresis
terms.definition: Increased muscle weakness upon exposure to cold temperatures.

terms.name: Stiff tongue
terms.definition: Increased rigidity and reduced mobility of the tongue.

terms.name: Ankle weakness
terms.definition: Reduced strength of the muscles that lift or otherwise move the foot at the ankle.

terms.name: Refractory
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is difficult to treat or cure.

terms.name: Abnormal cell proliferation
terms.definition: Any abnormality in the multiplication or reproduction of cells, which may result in the expansion of a cell population.

terms.name: Abnormal lymphocyte proliferation
terms.definition: Any abnormality in the multiplication or reproduction of lymphocytes, which results in the expansion of a cell population.

terms.name: Abnormal T cell proliferation
terms.definition: Any abnormality in the multiplication or reproduction of T cells, which results in the expansion of a cell population.

terms.name: Abnormal B cell proliferation
terms.definition: Any abnormality in the multiplication or reproduction of B cells, which results in the expansion of a cell population.

terms.name: Decreased mitogen-induced T-cell proliferation
terms.name_zh: 丝裂原诱导T细胞增殖降低
synonyms: Decreased lymphocyte proliferation in response to mitogen
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of T cell proliferation in response to mitogenic stimuli. This is commonly measured through intracellular expression of Ki67, decreasing surface expression of carboxyfluorescein diacetate (CFSE), or 3H-thymidine incorporation. Length of incubation, specific stimulus and strength of stimulation may vary between laboratories.

terms.name: Decreased anti-CD3/28-induced T-cell proliferation
synonyms: Decreased lymphocyte proliferation in response to anti-CD3
Defective proliferation of lymphocytes following anti-CD3 stimulation
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of T cell proliferation in response to anti-CD3/28 stimulation. This is commonly measured through intracellular expression of Ki67, decreasing surface expression of carboxyfluorescein diacetate (CFSE), or 3H-thymidine incorporation. Length of incubation and strength of stimulation may vary between laboratories.

terms.name: Abnormal lymphocyte surface marker expression
terms.name_zh: 淋巴细胞表面标志物表达异常
terms.definition: Abnormal amount of a protein that is normally present on the cell surface of lymphocytes.

terms.name: Reduced T cell CD40 expression
terms.definition: A deficiency in the expression of the CD40 ligand on the surface of activated T-lymphocytes.

terms.name: Megakaryocyte nucleus hypolobulation
terms.definition: The presence of megakaryocytes in the bone marrow whose nuclei are less lobulated than expected for the size of the nucleus.

terms.name: Increased micromegakaryocyte count
terms.definition: The presence of abnormally high numbers of micromegakaryocytes in the bone marrow. Micromegakaryocytes are mononuclear diploid cells, with a nucleus similar in size to that of a myeloblast or promyelocyte with the cell being less than 30 micrometers in diameter.

terms.name: Increased multinucleated megakaryocyte count
terms.name_zh: 多核巨核细胞计数升高
terms.definition: The presence of abnormally high numbers of multinucleated megakaryocytes in the bone marrow.

terms.name: Megakaryocyte nucleus hyperlobulation
terms.definition: The presence of megakaryocytes in the bone marrow whose nuclei are more lobulated than expected for the size of the nucleus.

terms.name: Abnormal MHC II cell surface expression
terms.name_zh: 主要组织相容性复合体II类细胞表面表达异常
synonyms: Abnormal human leukocyte antigen class II surface expression
Abnormal major histocompatibility complex class II surface expression
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal level of major histocompatibility complex class II molecules expressed at the cell surface.

terms.name: Reduced MHC II cell surface expression
synonyms: Abnormal HLA class II surface expression
Reduced human leukocyte antigen class II surface expression
terms.definition: Expression of major histocompatibility complex class II molecules at the cell surface is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated MHC II cell surface expression
terms.name_zh: MHC II类细胞表面表达升高
terms.definition: An increase above the normal level of major histocompatibility complex class II molecules expressed at the cell surface.

terms.name: Abnormal CD4+ T cell subset proportion
synonyms: Abnormal proportion of CD4+ T cells
Abnormal proportion of CD4-positive T cells
Abnormal proportion of CD4-positive helper T cells
Abnormal proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Abnormal proportion of circulating T-helper cells
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of any CD4+ T cell subpopulation, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Abnormal total CD8+ T cell number
synonyms: Abnormal proportion of CD8+ T cells
Abnormal proportion of CD8-positive T cells
Abnormal proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of the absolute number of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells (measured the absolute count per volume or as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Abnormal CD4:CD8 ratio
terms.definition: Any abnormality in the relative amount of CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes.

terms.name: Abnormal naive T cell proportion
synonyms: Abnormal proportion of naive T cells
Abnormal proportion of naive thymus-derived, alpha-beta T cells
terms.definition: Any abnormality in the proportion of naive T cells relative to the total number of T cells.

terms.name: Decreased naive T cell proportion
synonyms: Decreased proportion of naive T cells
Decreased proportion of naive thymus-derived, alpha-beta T cells
Reduced proportion of naive T cells
terms.definition: An abnormally decreased proportion of naive T cells relative to the total number of T cells.

terms.name: Increased naive T cell proportion
synonyms: Elevated proportion of naive T cells
Increased proportion of naive T cells
Increased proportion of naive thymus-derived, alpha-beta T cells
terms.definition: An abnormally increased proportion of naive T cells relative to the total number of T cells.

terms.name: Abnormal double-negative T cell proportion
synonyms: Abnormal CD4-negative, CD8-negative regulatory T cell distribution
Abnormal double-negative regulatory T cell distribution
Abnormal proportion of double-negative regulatory T cell
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of double-negative (DN) CD3+CD4-CD8- T cells, measured either as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, or as absolute number per microliter of blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Decreased double-negative T cell number
synonyms: Reduced proportion of CD4-negative, CD8-negative T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of double negative (DN) CD3+CD4-CD8- T cells, measured as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Decreased antigen-specific T cell proliferation
terms.name_zh: 抗原特异性T细胞增殖降低
terms.definition: Impaired proliferation and expansion of a T cell population following activation by an antigenic stimulus.

terms.name: Impaired pathogen-specific CD8 cytoxicity
terms.name_zh: 病原体特异性CD8细胞毒性受损
terms.definition: Impaired response of CD8 T cells to pathogens. CD8 T cells direct the killing of a target cell through the release of granules containing cytotoxic mediators or through the engagement of death receptors.

terms.name: Impaired antigen-specific response
terms.definition: An impaired immune response mediated by cells expressing specific receptors for antigen produced through a somatic diversification process, and allowing for an enhanced secondary response to subsequent exposures to the same antigen (immunological memory).

terms.name: Poroma
terms.definition: A benign, well circumscribed sweat gland neoplasm with eccrine or apocrine differentiation. It usually presents as a solitary, dome-shaped papule, nodule, or plaque on acral sites. It is characterized by a proliferation of uniform basaloid cells in the dermis and it is associated with the presence of focal ductal and cystic structures [NCIT:C27273].

terms.name: Abnormal cytokine signaling
terms.name_zh: 细胞因子信号传导异常
terms.definition: Any abnormality in the series of molecular signals initiated by the binding of a cytokine to a receptor on the surface of a cell, and ending with regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

terms.name: Impaired cytokine signaling
terms.name_zh: 细胞因子信号传导障碍
terms.definition: A defect or impairment in the series of molecular signals initiated by the binding of a cytokine to a receptor on the surface of a cell, and ending with regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

terms.name: Increased CD25+ mast cell proportion
terms.definition: An increased proportion of mast cells are positive for the cell surface marker CD25 (also called interleukin-2 receptor alpha chain).

terms.name: Abnormal lymphocyte physiology
terms.definition: Any anomaly of lymphocyte function.

terms.name: Abnormal distribution of CD56 bright/dim natural killer cells
terms.name_zh: CD56亮/暗自然杀伤细胞分布异常
synonyms: Abnormal distribution of CD56 bright/dim NK cells
terms.definition: An abnormal distribution in the number of CD56 bright NK cells, as measured by flow cytometry. CD56, an adhesion molecule mediating homotypic adhesion, is used as a functional marker for NK cells.

terms.name: Abnormal chromosome morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of a chromosome, which is a thread like molecule consisting of DNA and proteins (chromatin) that contains DNA sequences for genes and other genetic elements in linear order.

terms.name: Short telomere length
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction in telomere length.
