terms.name: Abnormally loud pulmonic component of the second heart sound
terms.name_zh: 第二心音肺动脉瓣成分异常亢进
synonyms: Accentuation of the pulmonic component of the second heart sound

terms.name: Erythroid dysplasia
terms.definition: Dysplasia in the erythroid lineage, which presents with a variety of morphological changes in the bone marrow, including nuclear budding or irregular nuclear contour in erythroblasts.

terms.name: Megakaryocyte dysplasia
terms.definition: The presence of micro-megakaryocytes, hypo-lobed, or non-lobed nuclei in megakaryocytes of all sizes and multiple, widely-separated nuclei.

terms.name: Opportunistic infection
terms.definition: An infection that is caused by a pathogen that would generally not be able to cause an infection in a host with a normal immune system. Such pathogens take advantage of the opportunity, so to speak, that is provided by a weakened immune system.

terms.name: Severe viral infection
terms.definition: An unusually severe viral infection.

terms.name: Severe cytomegalovirus infection
terms.definition: An unusually severe infection by cytomegalovirus.

terms.name: Severe Epstein Barr virus infection
terms.definition: An unusually severe Epstein Barr virus (EBV) infection.

terms.name: Severe adenovirus infection
terms.definition: An unusually severe adenovirus infection.

terms.name: Severe parainfluenza infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to parainfluenza virus infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with parainfluenza virus.

terms.name: Disseminated viral infection
terms.definition: A viral infection that fails to be contained by the immune system and spreads throughout the body.

terms.name: Disseminated infection with live vaccine virus
terms.name_zh: 活疫苗病毒播散性感染
terms.definition: A dissemination viral infection caused by a live attenuated vaccine virus.

terms.name: Disseminated cryptosporidium infection
terms.definition: Disseminated infection with Cryptosporidium species, involving organs beyond the gastrointestinal tract such as the biliary tree, respiratory tract, or pancreas.

terms.name: Invasive parasitic infection
terms.definition: A parasitic infection whereby the parasite invades (migrates through) tissues of the infected host.

terms.name: Anterior chamber inflammatory cells
terms.definition: The presence of inflammatory cells in the aqueous humor of the anterior chamber of the eye.

terms.name: Anterior chamber red blood cells
terms.definition: The presence of erythrocyte in the aqueous humor of the anterior chamber of the eye.

terms.name: Abnormal ear morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the ear.

terms.name: Abnormal ear physiology
terms.definition: Any functional anomaly of the ear.

terms.name: Compensatory head posture
terms.definition: A compensatory head posture occurs when the head is deviated out of the normal primary straight head position in order to compensate for an ocular problem.

terms.name: Compensatory chin depression
terms.definition: A tendency to hold the chin depressed (lowered) to compensate for a limitation of eye movement.

terms.name: Compensatory face turn to the right
terms.definition: A tendency to turn the face to the right to compensate for a limitation of eye movement.

terms.name: Compensatory face turn to the left
terms.definition: A tendency to turn the face to the left to compensate for a limitation of eye movement.

terms.name: Compensatory head tilt to the right shoulder
terms.definition: A tendency to tilt the head towards the right shoulder to compensate for a limitation of eye movement.

terms.name: Compensatory head tilt to the left shoulder
terms.definition: A tendency to tilt the head towards the left shoulder to compensate for a limitation of eye movement.

terms.name: Asymmetric abdominal aortic aneurysm
terms.name_zh: 腹主动脉不对称性动脉瘤
terms.definition: An abdominal aortic aneurysm that is not symmetric around its axis (not axisymmetric).

terms.name: Constant exotropia
terms.definition: A form of divergent strabismus (exotropia) in which the eye turns outward at all distances and at all times.

terms.name: Distance exotropia
terms.definition: A type of divergent strabismus (exotropia) in which an eye tends to turn outwards (i.e., the eye squints) mainly when looking at distant objects. The eyes tend to remain straight when they look at near objects. Distance exotropia may be constant or intermittent.

terms.name: Near exotropia
terms.definition: An intermittent exotropia where there is binocular single vision on distance fixation and exotropia at near (intermittent or constant).

terms.name: Cyclic exotropia
terms.definition: A type of exotropia (divergent strabismus) in which binocular single vision alternates with large angle exotropia in rhythmic cycle.

terms.name: Alternating exotropia
terms.definition: A type of exotropia in which either eye may be used for fixation.

terms.name: Consecutive exotropia
terms.definition: Exotropia in an individual who has previously had esotropia or esophoria.

terms.name: True distance exotropia
terms.definition: Exotropia (intermittent or constant) on distance fixation with binocular single vision on near fixation under all testing conditions. The accommodative convergence/accommodation (AC:A) ratio is within normal limits.

terms.name: Simulated distance exotropia
terms.definition: Exotropia (intermittent or constant) worse for distance fixation in which the near angle of deviation increases (or near exophoria becomes exotropia) with: (1) prolonged disruption of fusion and/or (2) elimination of accommodation.

terms.name: Sensory exotropia
terms.definition: A type of divergent strabismus (exotropia) that develops in a poorly seeing eye.

terms.name: Near esotropia
terms.definition: An intermittent esotropia where there is binocular single vision on distance fixation and esotropia at near even when the accommodation is relieved.

terms.name: Secondary esotropia
terms.definition: Convergent squint which follows loss or impairment of vision.

terms.name: Microtropia
terms.definition: A small angle heterotropia (usually of 10 diopters or less) in which a form of binocular single vision occurs.

terms.name: Hypophoria
terms.definition: A form of latent strabismus (heterophoria) in which, on dissociation, the occluded eye deviates downwards.

terms.name: Incyclotropia
terms.definition: A type of cyclotropia (torsion of one or both eye around the visual axis of the eyes) in which the upper poles of the globes are rotated inward (medially) to each other.

terms.name: Excyclotropia
terms.definition: A type of cyclotropia (torsion of one or both eye around the visual axis of the eyes) in which the upper poles of the globes are rotated outward (laterally) to each other.

terms.name: Mild hypermetropia
terms.definition: A form of hypermetropia with not more than +2.00 diopters.

terms.name: Moderate hypermetropia
terms.definition: A form of hypermetropia with more than +2.00 diopters but not more than +5.00 diopters.

terms.name: Axial myopia
terms.definition: A form of myopia related to an axial length above the norm and too long for the refractive power of the whole optical system of the eye.

terms.name: Increased tear production
terms.definition: Increased lacrimation owing to overproduction of tears.

terms.name: Increased basal tear production
terms.definition: A form of watery eye associated with overproduction of tears due to an increased parasympathetic drive to the secretory component of the lacrimal system (lacrimal gland); this could be due to pro-secretory drug use (e.g. pilocarpine) or autonomic disturbance.

terms.name: Reflex tearing
terms.definition: A form of watery eye associated with overproduction of tears due to reflex tearing in response to a local irritant (e.g. trichiasis or foreign body), chronic ocular surface disease (e.g. blepharitis) or systemic disease (e.g. thyroid eye disease).

terms.name: Lacrimal pump failure
terms.definition: A form of watery eye associated with abnormal lid tone and/or lid position. The former is due to lid laxity (common involutional change in the elderly) or a weak orbicularis muscle (e.g. due to VII cranial nerve palsy). The latter is typically associated with ectropion causing punctal eversion.

terms.name: Involutional entropion
terms.definition: An abnormal inversion of the eyelid towards the globe resulting from inferior retractor muscle dysfunction with tissue laxity and, possibly, overriding of the preseptal orbicularis muscle over the pretarsal orbicularis muscle.

terms.name: Cicatricial entropion
terms.definition: Abnormal inversion (turning inward) of the eyelid towards the globe associated with scarring that vertically shortens the posterior lamella of the eyelid.

terms.name: Mechanical entropion
terms.definition: A type of entropion (abnormal inversion of the eyelid towards the globe) that is related to a mass effect of a lesion (e.g., a tumor) that pulls the eyelid margin away from the globe.

terms.name: Abnormal oblique muscle physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the inferior or superior oblique muscle.

terms.name: Abnormal horizontal rectus muscle physiology
terms.name_zh: 水平直肌生理功能异常
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the medial rectus muscle or lateral rectus muscle.

terms.name: Inferior oblique muscle underaction
terms.definition: Reduced ocular movement by the inferior oblique muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

terms.name: Inferior rectus muscle underaction
terms.definition: Reduced movement by the inferior rectus muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

terms.name: Inferior rectus muscle overaction
terms.definition: Excessive action of the inferior rectus muscle caused by increased innervation typically as a consequence of palsy or limitation to the ipsilateral antagonist or contralateral synergist.

terms.name: Superior rectus muscle weakness
terms.definition: Decreased strength of the superior rectus muscle.

terms.name: Superior rectus muscle overaction
terms.definition: Excessive action of the superior rectus muscle caused by increased innervation typically as a consequence of palsy or limitation to the ipsilateral antagonist or contralateral synergist.

terms.name: Superior rectus muscle restriction
terms.definition: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the superior rectus muscle.

terms.name: Superior rectus muscle underaction
terms.definition: Reduced movement of the superior rectus muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

terms.name: Abnormal vertical rectus muscle physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the superior or inferior rectus muscle.

terms.name: Abnormal lateral rectus muscle physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the lateral rectus muscle.

terms.name: Lateral rectus muscle weakness
terms.definition: Decreased strength (ability to move) of the lateral rectus muscle.

terms.name: Lateral rectus muscle underaction
terms.definition: Reduced movement of the lateral rectus muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

terms.name: Lateral rectus muscle overaction
terms.definition: Excessive action of the lateral rectus muscle caused by increased innervation typically as a consequence of palsy or limitation to the ipsilateral antagonist or contralateral synergist.

terms.name: Medial rectus muscle weakness
terms.definition: Decreased strength of the medial rectus muscle.

terms.name: Medial rectus muscle overaction
terms.definition: Excessive action of the medial rectus muscle caused by increased innervation typically as a consequence of palsy or limitation to the ipsilateral antagonist or contralateral synergist.

terms.name: Abnormal rectus muscle physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of a vertical or horizontal rectus muscle.

terms.name: Medial rectus muscle underaction
terms.definition: Reduced movement of the medial rectus muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

terms.name: Medial rectus muscle restriction
terms.definition: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the medial rectus muscle.

terms.name: Lateral rectus muscle restriction
terms.definition: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the lateral rectus muscle.

terms.name: Basic constant esotropia
terms.definition: A form of convergent strabismus (esotropia) in which the deviation is present under all conditions (ie at all distances and at all times).

terms.name: Non-accomodative esotropia
terms.definition: A form of esotropia in which the angle of deviation is not affected by accommodative effort.

terms.name: Infantile constant esotropia
terms.definition: Constant esotropia occurring before 6 months of age. It is typically associated with a large angle of deviation, alternating fixation (therefore low risk of amblyopia) and poor potential for binocular single vision. Other features that might be present in individuals with infantile (constant) esotropia include latent nystagmus or manifest latent nystagmus, dissociated vertical divergence, cyclotropia, abnormal head posture, limited abduction.

terms.name: Distance esotropia
terms.definition: An intermittent esotropia where binocular single vision is present on near fixation and an esotropia on distance fixation. Often associated with myopia and aging.

terms.name: Cyclic esotropia
terms.definition: Convergent strabismus in which normal binocular single vision is alternating with large angle esotropia in rhythmic cycle.

terms.name: Fully accomodative esotropia
terms.definition: Esotropia in which normal binocular single vision is present for all distances when the hypermetropic refractive error is corrected. Esotropia is present for near and distance on accommodation without correction.

terms.name: Partially accomodative esotropia
synonyms: Constant esotropia with an accommodative component
Constant esotropia with an accommodative element
terms.definition: A form of constant esotropia in which the angle of deviation is partially affected by accommodative effort. Typically there is esotropia at near and distance with hypermetropic correction and the angle of deviation increases without glasses.

terms.name: Convergence excess esotropia
terms.definition: An intermittent esotropia with binocular single vision present at distance fixation but esotropia on accommodation for near fixation. Usually associated with hypermetropia but patients can be emmetropic and rarely myopic. Associated with a high accommodative convergence/accommodation (AC/A) ratio.

terms.name: Consecutive esotropia
terms.definition: Esotropia in a patient who has previously had exotropia or exophoria; may be constant or intermittent and usually follows surgical overcorrection.

terms.name: Parafoveal fixation
terms.definition: Fixation of an object in the area adjacent to the fovea.

terms.name: Peripheral fixation
terms.definition: Fixation of an object in a peripheral area of the retina.

terms.name: Epicanthus palpebralis
terms.definition: A type of epicanthus in which a medial vertical fold is present between upper and lower lids.

terms.name: Epicanthus tarsalis
terms.definition: A type of epicanthus in which a primarily upper lid fold is present.

terms.name: Abnormal posterior circulating artery morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the posterior circulating artery (PCOM).

terms.name: Posterior communicating artery aneurysm
terms.definition: A widening (ballooning) localized in the wall of the posterior communicating artery.

terms.name: Posterior communicating artery infundibulum
terms.definition: A funnel-shaped symmetrical enlargement of the origin of the posterior communicating artery at its junction with the internal carotid artery.

terms.name: Neurogenic strabismus
terms.definition: An ocular deviation caused by a palsy to one or more of the extraocular muscles or nerves supplying them.

terms.name: Cyclotropia
terms.definition: A form of manifest strabismus (heterotropia) in which the one eye is wheel rotated so that the upper end of its vertical axis is nasal (incyclotropia) or temporal (excyclotropia).

terms.name: Cyclophoria
terms.definition: A form of latent strabismus (heterophoria) in which the occluded eye wheel-rotates on dissociation.

terms.name: Incyclophoria
terms.definition: A type of cyclophoria (latent strabismus in which the occluded eye wheel-rotates on dissociation.) in which the upper poles of the globes are rotated inward (medially) to each other.

terms.name: Excyclophoria
terms.definition: A type of cyclophoria (latent strabismus in which the occluded eye wheel-rotates on dissociation.) in which the upper poles of the globes are rotated outward (laterally) to each other.

terms.name: Eosinophilic ascites
terms.definition: A type of ascites in which there are large numbers of eosinophils in the ascitis fluid.

terms.name: Microtropia with identity
terms.definition: A type of microtropia with no manifest movement on cover test, the eccentric fixation point coinciding with the angle of ARC.

terms.name: Microtropia without identity
terms.definition: A type of microtropia in which the manifest movement is demonstrated on the cover-uncover test.

terms.name: Absent coronary sinus
terms.definition: A developmental defect in which the coronary sinus fails to form.

terms.name: Abnormal ascending aorta morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the portion of the aorta that arises from the base of the left ventricle and extends upward to the aortic arch and from which the coronary arteries arise.

terms.name: Abnormal eyelid movement
terms.definition: An abnormality in voluntary or involuntary eyelid movements or their control.

terms.name: Cogan lid twitch
terms.definition: Transient eyelid retraction during refixation from down to straight ahead.

terms.name: Oblique astigmatism
terms.definition: Astigmatism in which the refractive power of the vertical meridian is the greatest.

terms.name: With the rule astigmatism
terms.definition: Refractive error in which the vertical meridian is relatively hypermetropic and the horizontal meridian is relatively myopic (or ocular astigmatism in which the refractive power of the horizontal meridian is the greatest).

terms.name: Against the rule astigmatism
terms.definition: Astigmatism with more plus power on the horizontal meridian.

terms.name: Mixed astigmatism
terms.definition: A type of astigmatism in which an unequal curvature of the cornea and some cases additionally of the lens causes one meridian of the eye to be hyperopic (farsighted) and a second meridian that is perpendicular to the first to be myopic (nearsighted).

terms.name: Lenticular astigmatism
terms.definition: A type of astigmatism related to an irregular shape of the lens.

terms.name: Irregular astigmatism
terms.definition: A type of astigmatism in which the principle meridians are not 90 degrees apart and which is associated with loss of vision.

terms.name: Increased serum leptin
terms.definition: An increased concentration of leptin in the blood.

terms.name: Decreased circulating glycerol level
terms.definition: A decrease below the normal concentration of glycerol in the blood.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating glycerol level
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of glycerol in the blood.

terms.name: Recurrent
terms.definition: Applies to a sign, symptom or manifestation that occurs multiple times separated by intervals in which the sign, symptom, or manifestation is not present.

terms.name: Clinical course
terms.definition: The course a disease typically takes from its onset, progression in time, and eventual resolution or death of the affected individual.

terms.name: Elevated circulating apolipoprotein B concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环载脂蛋白B浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of apolipoprotein B in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Decreased circulating apolipoprotein A-I concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环载脂蛋白A-I浓度降低
synonyms: Decreased apolipoprotein A-I level in blood
Reduced apolipoprotein A-I level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of apolipoprotein A-I in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating apolipoprotein A-II concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环载脂蛋白A-II浓度升高
synonyms: Elevated apolipoprotein A-II level in blood
Increased apolipoprotein A-II level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of apolipoprotein A-II in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Vocal cord dysfunction
terms.definition: Any functional anomaly of the vocal cord.

terms.name: Fundus hemorrhage
terms.definition: Bleeding within the fundus of the eye.

terms.name: Intraretinal hemorrhage
terms.definition: A subtype of fundus hemorrhage occurring within the neurosensory retina. Intraretinal hemorrhages may be 'dot' or' blot' shaped, flame shaped or confluent depending upon their depth within the retina.

terms.name: Abnormal total basophil count
terms.name_zh: 总嗜碱性粒细胞计数异常
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of absolute number of basophils in the blood, per microliter, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Increased total basophil count
terms.name_zh: 总嗜碱性粒细胞计数升高
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of absolute number of basophils in the blood, per microliter, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Decreased total basophil count
terms.name_zh: 总嗜碱性粒细胞计数降低
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of absolute number of basophils in the blood, per microliter, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Archibald's sign
terms.definition: Shortening of the fourth and fifth metacarpals when the fist is clenched.

terms.name: Anti-ganglioside antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗神经节苷脂抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react to gangliosides.

terms.name: Bilirubinuria
terms.definition: Presence of conjugated bilirubin in the urine.

terms.name: Nitrituria
terms.definition: Presence of nitrites in the urine.

terms.name: Colonic eosinophilia
terms.name_zh: 结肠嗜酸性粒细胞增多
terms.definition: An excess of eosinophilic cells in colonic tissue, i.e., eosinophilic infiltration in the colon.

terms.name: Palilalia
terms.definition: Palilalia is the involuntary repetition of one's own phrases, words, or syllables 2 or more times in a row. Typically, palilalic utterances decrease in volume with the increasing number of repetitions. Sometimes, the repetitions are also uttered with an accelerating speed.

terms.name: Abnormal oral physiology
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the mouth (which is also known as the oral cavity).

terms.name: Abnormal oral morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the mouth, which is also known as the oral cavity.

terms.name: Decreased circulating parathyroid hormone level
terms.name_zh: 血循环甲状旁腺激素水平降低
terms.definition: An abnormally decreased concentration of parathyroid hormone.

terms.name: Abnormal waist to hip ratio
terms.definition: A deviation from normal of the waist to hip ratio, defined as the waist measurement divided by hip measurement.

terms.name: Increased waist to hip ratio
terms.definition: Increased waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) is a measurement above the average for the dimensionless ratio of the circumference of the waist to that of the hips. WHR is calculated as waist measurement divided by hip measurement.

terms.name: Decreased waist to hip ratio
terms.definition: Decreased waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) is a measurement below the average for the dimensionless ratio of the circumference of the waist to that of the hips. WHR is calculated as waist measurement divided by hip measurement.

terms.name: Abnormal hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase level
terms.name_zh: 次黄嘌呤-鸟嘌呤磷酸核糖转移酶水平异常
terms.definition: Altered level of the enzyme that catalyzes conversion of hypoxanthine to inosine monophosphate and guanine to guanosine monophosphate via transfer of the 5-phosphoribosyl group from 5-phosphoribosyl 1-pyrophosphate.

terms.name: Elevated hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase level
terms.name_zh: 次黄嘌呤-鸟嘌呤磷酸核糖转移酶水平升高
terms.definition: Abnormally increased level of the enzyme that catalyzes conversion of hypoxanthine to inosine monophosphate and guanine to guanosine monophosphate via transfer of the 5-phosphoribosyl group from 5-phosphoribosyl 1-pyrophosphate.

terms.name: Reduced hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase level
terms.definition: Abnormally decreased level of the enzyme that catalyzes conversion of hypoxanthine to inosine monophosphate and guanine to guanosine monophosphate via transfer of the 5-phosphoribosyl group from 5-phosphoribosyl 1-pyrophosphate.

terms.name: Hepatic mastocytosis
terms.definition: Liver mast cell infiltration.

terms.name: Freezing of gait
terms.definition: Freezing of gait is defined as a brief, episodic absence or marked reduction of forward progression of the feet despite the intention to walk.

terms.name: Abnormal reflex
terms.definition: Any anomaly of a reflex, i.e., of an automatic response mediated by the nervous system (a reflex does not need the intervention of conscious thought to occur).

terms.name: Absent abdominal reflex
terms.definition: Lack of contraction of abdominal muscles in the quadrant of the abdomen that is stimulated by scraping the skin tangential to or toward the umbilicus.

terms.name: Abnormal superficial reflex
terms.definition: An anomaly of a reflex that is elicited as a motor response to scraping of the skin. They are generally graded as present or absent. They differ from tendon reflexes in that the sensory signal must ascend the spinal cord to reach the brain and then descend the spinal cord to reach the motor neurons.

terms.name: Absent cremaster reflex
terms.definition: Lack of response to scratching of the skin of the medial thigh, which in males normally elicits a brisk, short elevation of the ipsilateral testis, a phenomenon that is referred to as the cremaster reflex.

terms.name: Pinguecula
terms.definition: A pinguecula is a yellowish to brown protruding lesion in the conjunctiva that is easily seen on the nasal and temporal sides of the cornea.

terms.name: Decreased serum zinc
terms.definition: A reduced concentration of zinc in the blood.

terms.name: Hypermetric downward saccades
terms.definition: Overshoot of downward saccadic eye movements.

terms.name: Hypometric upward saccades
terms.definition: Saccadic undershoot of upward saccadic eye movements, i.e., an upward saccadic eye movement that has less than the magnitude that would be required to gain fixation of the object.

terms.name: Aortopulmonary collateral arteries
terms.definition: Small ectopic arteries or arterial branches that connect the aorta, aortic branches and/or subclavian artery regions directly to the lung parenchyma, usually seen in conjunction with pulmonary atresia, ventricular septal defect (VSD) and/or closed ductus arteriosus.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating superoxide dismutase activity
terms.name_zh: 循环超氧化物歧化酶活性异常
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of superoxide dismutase is above or below the limits of normal in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Increased circulating superoxide dismutase concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环超氧化物歧化酶浓度升高
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of superoxide dismutase is above the upper limit of normal in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Decreased circulating superoxide dismutase concentration
terms.name_zh: 血超氧化物歧化酶浓度降低
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of superoxide dismutase is below the lower limit of normal in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Presence of xenobiotic
terms.definition: Presence of a chemical substance found within an individual that is not naturally produced or expected to be present in human tissues or bodily fluids.

terms.name: Urine xenobiotic
terms.definition: The presence of a xenobiotic in urine.

terms.name: Positive urine methadone test
terms.definition: Detection of methadone or its metabolite 2-ethylidene-1,5-dimethyl-3,3- diphenylpyrrolidine (EDDP) in urine.

terms.name: Lymphangiectasis
terms.definition: Dilation of the lymphatic vessels, the basic process that may result in the formation of a lymphangioma.

terms.name: Abnormally slow thought process
terms.definition: An inner sense from the self that thoughts are abnormally slow and the individual feels that they are unable to increase their rate of thinking. The primary pathology is the decreased rate and other qualities of thinking (e.g. naming of objects) are intact, just slowed. This may be associated with slowed speech, but may be internal and masked by speech that is limited to brief (yes or no) answers.

terms.name: Euphoria
terms.definition: Elevation of emotional tone or mood that significantly deviates from normative affective functioning. This state is characterized by an overwhelming and all-encompassing sense of joyous well-being; it is associated with unfounded grandiosity, or grossly inflated self-esteem, rapid speech, impulsivity, and an impaired capacity for self-regulation, irrespective of context.

terms.name: Abnormal libido
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal sexual drive or desire for sexual activity.

terms.name: Femur fracture
terms.definition: A break or crush injury of the thigh bone (femur).

terms.name: Difficulty walking backward
terms.definition: Reduced ability to walk (ambulate) in a backwards direction.

terms.name: Cock-walk gait
terms.definition: An abnormality of gait that can be observed in individuals with dystonic posture in which the individual walks with an extended trunk and flexed arms, while strutting on the toes without the heels touching the floor.

terms.name: Sleep-wake inversion
terms.definition: A reversal of sleeping habits, with a tendency to sleep during the day and be awake at night.

terms.name: Abnormal hematocrit
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal ratio of the volume of red blood cells to the total volume of blood.

terms.name: Reduced hematocrit
terms.definition: A reduction below the normal ratio of the volume of red blood cells to the total volume of blood.

terms.name: Isomerism
terms.definition: Isomerism in the context of the congenitally malformed heart is defined as a situation where some paired structures on opposite sides of the left-right axis of the body are, in morphologic terms, symmetrical mirror images of each other.

terms.name: Left Isomerism
terms.definition: A type of heterotaxy where some paired structures on opposite sides of the left-right axis of the body are symmetrical mirror images of each other, and have the morphology of the normal left-sided structures.

terms.name: Right isomerism
terms.definition: A type of heterotaxy where some paired structures on opposite sides of the left-right axis of the body are symmetrical mirror images of each other, and have the morphology of the normal right-sided structures.

terms.name: Hobby horse gait
terms.definition: An abnormal gait characterized by toe walking, stiff legs, and skipping. The gait pattern has some resemblance to cock-walk gait, but affected individuals are able to improve their dystonic gait by walking backward.

terms.name: Ineffective esophageal peristalsis
terms.definition: Reduced or inadequate esophageal peristalsis, with resultant slow passage of contents through the esophagus.

terms.name: Esophageal furrows
terms.definition: Longitudinal grooves in the surface of the esophagus arranged in a longitudinal fashion (from top to bottom of the esophagus).

terms.name: Abnormal heart rate variability
terms.definition: Any abnormality in the variability of the time interval between successive heartbeats.

terms.name: Decreased heart rate variability
terms.definition: Reduced variation of beat-to-beat intervals of the heart that occurs in conjunction with the respiratory cycle.

terms.name: Increased heart rate variability
terms.definition: Increased variation of beat-to-beat intervals of the heart that occurs in conjunction with the respiratory cycle.

terms.name: Bloodstream infectious agent
terms.definition: The presence of an infectious agent in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Bacteremia
terms.definition: Presence of viable bacteria in the blood.

terms.name: Abnormal liver physiology
terms.definition: Any functional anomaly of the liver.

terms.name: Clasp-knife sign
terms.definition: Clasp-knife phenomenon refers to increased muscle tone while bending or stretching a limb, whereby there is a sudden relaxation (decrease in resistance) as the muscle continues to be stretched. This phenomenon has been likened to opening a clasp knife.

terms.name: Neck hypertonia
terms.definition: Increased passive stiffness or tightness of the neck musculature.

terms.name: Optic ataxia
terms.definition: Difficulty reaching visually guided goals in peripheral vision, with the deficit, leaves voluntary eye movements largely unaffected.

terms.name: Recurrent joint dislocation
terms.definition: Dislocation of a given joint repeated times.

terms.name: Phosphohydroxylysinuria
terms.definition: An elevated concentration of phosphohydroxylysine in the urine.

terms.name: Abnormal Langerhans cell morphology
terms.name_zh: 朗格汉斯细胞形态异常
terms.definition: Any functional anomaly of Langerhans cells, which are dendritic cells in the epidermis and some other locations. Langerhans cells play roles in immune surveillance and homeostasis.

terms.name: Absent Birbeck granules in Langerhans cells
terms.name_zh: 朗格汉斯细胞伯贝克颗粒缺失
terms.definition: Birbeck granules (BG) are cytoplasmic organelles that are only found in Langerhans cells (LC). The function of BG is still not completely understood, although most studies point toward an active role in receptor-mediated endocytosis and participation in the antigen-processing/presenting function of LC. This feature refers to the absence of BG in LC, a feature that can be documented by means of electron microscopy.

terms.name: Early chronotype
terms.definition: A tendency towards rising very early in the morning and going to bed early in the evening.

terms.name: Late chronotype
terms.definition: A tendency towards waking up very late in the morning and staying up late at night.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating hepcidin concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of hepcidin in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Decreased circulating hepcidin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环铁调素浓度降低
terms.definition: Concentration of hepcidin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating hepcidin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环铁调素浓度升高
terms.definition: Concentration of hepcidin in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Acromicria
terms.definition: Small hands and feet in proportion to the rest of the body.

terms.name: Abnormal eyelid physiology
terms.definition: Any functional abnormality of the eyelid.

terms.name: Eyelid laxity
terms.definition: Abnormally lax eyelid associated with tissue relaxation; it can be demonstrated by the eyelid distraction test and/or the eyelid snap test.

terms.name: Decreased tear drainage
terms.definition: A form of watery eye associated with obstruction of the nasolacrimal system. This may arise at the level of the punctum, the canaliculi, the sac or the nasolacrimal duct.

terms.name: Agyria
terms.definition: A congenital abnormality of the cerebral hemisphere characterized by lack of gyrations (convolutions) of the cerebral cortex. Agyria is defined as cortical regions lacking gyration with sulci great than 3 cm apart and cerebral cortex thicker than 5 mm.

terms.name: Increased proinsulin:insulin ratio
terms.name_zh: 胰岛素原/胰岛素比值升高
terms.definition: An elevated concentration of proinsulin (the prohormone precursor to insulin) to mature insulin in the circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal CSF glucose concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液葡萄糖浓度异常
terms.definition: A deviation from normal concentration of glucose content in the cerebrospinal fluid.

terms.name: Hyperglycorrhachia
terms.definition: Abnormally high glucose concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid.

terms.name: Abnormal LDL cholesterol concentration
terms.name_zh: 低密度脂蛋白胆固醇浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal chylomicron concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal circulating concentration of chylomicrons.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating HDL-C concentration
terms.name_zh: 血高密度脂蛋白胆固醇浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating VLDL-C concentration
terms.name_zh: 血极低密度脂蛋白胆固醇浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Increased urine urobilinogen
terms.definition: An elevated concentration of urobilinogen in the urine.

terms.name: Decreased total eosinophil count
terms.name_zh: 总嗜酸性粒细胞计数降低
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of absolute number of eosinophils in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Rouleaux formation
terms.definition: Increased amount of stacking of erythrocytes into long chains. Rouleaux (singular: rouleau) is derived from a French word that can refer to a stack of coins put into a cylindircal paper roll. Rouleaux formation is observed with increased serum proteins, particularly fibrinogen and globulins, and represents the cause of increased erythrocte sedimentation rate because rouleaux sediment more readily than isolated red blood cells.

terms.name: Abnormal coagulation factor V activity
terms.definition: Any deviation from the activity of coagulation factor V.

terms.name: Elevated total serum tryptase
terms.name_zh: 血清总类胰蛋白酶升高
terms.definition: An abnormally elevated concentration of total tryptase (alpha and beta tryptase) in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating selenium concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal circulating concentration of selenium.

terms.name: Abnormal total hemolytic complement activity
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal total hemolytic complement activity in the circulation.

terms.name: Increased total hemolytic complement activity
terms.definition: An abnormally elevated total hemolytic complement activity in the circulation.

terms.name: Anti-mitochondrial M2 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of M2 anti-mitochondrial antibody (immunoglobulins) in the serum.

terms.name: Micrographia
terms.definition: Abnormally small-sized handwriting is formally defined as an impairment of fine motor skills, which mainly manifests as a progressive or stable reduction in amplitude during a writing task.

terms.name: Unicornuate uterus
terms.definition: A uterus that has a single horn, with a banana-like shape that may or may not have a secondary rudimentary uterine horn.

terms.name: Abnormal cranial nerve physiology
terms.definition: A functional abnormality affecting one or more of the cranial nerves, which emerge directly from the brain stem.

terms.name: Trigeminal anesthesia
terms.definition: Decreased or absent sensation in the distribution of the trigeminal nerve, which provides tactile, proprioceptive, and nociceptive sensation in the area of the face and mouth.

terms.name: Rhombencephalosynapsis
terms.definition: Rhombencephalosynapsis is a rare brain malformation defined by midline fusion of the cerebellar hemispheres with partial or complete loss of the intervening vermis.

terms.name: Fluctuating
terms.definition: Varying irregularly over time in severity, amount, or amplitude.

terms.name: Stable
terms.definition: This modifier can be applied to a phenotypic feature that does not vary in severity or amount over time.

terms.name: Digital ulcer
terms.definition: An open sore on the surface of the skin of a finger or toe.

terms.name: Ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor
terms.definition: A benign or malignant neoplasm that arises from the ovary and is composed of granulosa cells, Sertoli cells, Leydig cells, theca cells, and fibroblasts.

terms.name: Juvenile type ovarian granulosa cell tumor
terms.name_zh: 幼年型卵巢颗粒细胞瘤
synonyms: Juvenile type ovarian granulosa cell tumour
terms.definition: Juvenile granulosa cell ovarian tumor (JGCOT) is a rare sex cord stromal tumor, occurring most frequently in premenarchal girls or young women. In contrast to adult granulosa cell tumor, JGCOT has a high mitotic index and more aggressive tumor growth. Microscopically it is seen as diffuse and regularly distributed neoplastic cells with a wide cytoplasm and pleomorphic hyperchromatic nucleus. Follicle formation, in various sizes and shapes, is important in JGCOT. Call-Exner bodies are infrequently seen in JGCOT in contrast to the adult type.

terms.name: Malignant ovarian granulosa cell tumor
terms.definition: An aggressive granulosa cell tumor that arises from the ovary.

terms.name: Gastrocnemius myalgia
terms.definition: Pain of the gastrocnemius muscle.

terms.name: Renal artery duplication
terms.definition: The renal arteries carry blood from the aorta to the kidney; normally one renal artery is present on each side of the body. Renal artery duplication refers to the presence of two rather than one renal artery on a given side of the body.

terms.name: Hematocolpos
terms.definition: Accumulation of blood in the vagina usually due to vaginal obstruction.

terms.name: Rope sign
terms.definition: The presence of linear erythematous palpable cords, often on the lateral trunk.

terms.name: Rosette
terms.definition: A halo or spoke-wheel arrangement of cells surrounding a central core or hub. The central hub may consist of an empty-appearing lumen or a space filled with cytoplasmic processes. The cytoplasm of each of the cells in the rosette is often wedge-shaped with the apex directed toward the central core; the nuclei of the cells participating in the rosette are peripherally positioned and form a ring or halo around the hub.

terms.name: Homer Wright rosette
terms.definition: A type of rosette in which the central lumen or hub is filled with fiber-like processes.

terms.name: Flexner-Wintersteiner rosette
terms.definition: The tumor cells that form the Flexner-Wintersteiner rosette circumscribe a central lumen that contains small cytoplasmic extensions of the encircling cells; however, unlike the center of the Homer Wright rosette, the central lumen does not contain the fiber-rich neuropil.

terms.name: True ependymal rosette
terms.definition: A type of rosette in which a halo of cells surrounds an empty lumen.

terms.name: Perivascular pseudorosette
terms.definition: A type of rosette in which a spoke-wheel arrangement of cells with tapered cellular processes radiates around a wall of a centrally placed vessel.

terms.name: Neurocytic rosette
terms.definition: A type of rosette that is similar to the Homer Wright rosette, but the central fiber-rich neuropil island is larger and more irregular.

terms.name: Ocular flutter
terms.definition: Ocular flutter is an abnormal eye movement consisting of repetitive, irregular, involuntary bursts of horizontal saccades without an intersaccadic interval. It is generally superimposed on normal oculomotor behavior and its occurrence may be favored by various events, such as blinks, the triggering of normal saccades or optokinetic stimulation.

terms.name: Aorto-left ventricular tunnel
terms.definition: Aorto-left ventricular tunnel (ALVT) is a congenital extracardiac channel connecting the ascending aorta above the sino-tubular junction to either left or right ventricular cavity.

terms.name: Aorto-right ventricular tunnel
terms.definition: The presence of an extracardiac channel that connects the ascending aorta above the sinotubular junction to the cavity of the right ventricle.

terms.name: Abnormal descending aorta morphology
terms.definition: A structural abnormality of the part of the aorta that begins at the aortic arch and then descends through the chest and abdomen.

terms.name: Ascending aorta hypoplasia
terms.definition: Significant luminal narrowing of a long segment of or the entire ascending aorta.

terms.name: Delayed ability to walk
terms.definition: A failure to achieve the ability to walk at an appropriate developmental stage. Most children learn to walk in a series of stages, and learn to walk short distances independently between 12 and 15 months.

terms.name: Tachylalia
terms.definition: Speech that is abnormally fast as compared to the perceived cultural norm.

terms.name: Abnormal conus terminalis morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the conus terminalis, which is the distal bulbous part of the spinal cord at the location where the spinal cord tapers and ends (usually between the L1 and L2 lumbar vertebrae).

terms.name: Abnormal portal venous system morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the portal venous system, which comprises all of the veins draining the abdominal part of the digestive tract, including the lower esophagus but excluding the lower anal canal. The portal vein conveys blood from viscera and ramifies like an artery at the liver, ending at the sinusoids. Tributaries of the portal vein, which make up the portal venous system, are the splenic, superior mesenteric, left gastric, right gastric, paraumbilical, and cystic veins.

terms.name: Congenital absence of portal vein
terms.definition: Anomaly where the intestinal and the splenic venous drainage bypass the liver and drain into systemic veins through other possible venous shunts.

terms.name: Akathisia
terms.definition: A state of motor restlessness, usually in the lower extremities, that is often but not always accompanied by a subjective sense of inner restlessness, an urge to move, and anxiety or dysphoria.

terms.name: Pleural thickening
terms.definition: An increase in the thickness of the pleura, generally related to scarring of the pleural tissue.

terms.name: Elevated circulating N,N-dimethylglycine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血N,N-二甲基甘氨酸浓度升高
terms.definition: An increased concentration of N,N-dimethylglycine in the circulation.

terms.name: Elevated urinary N,N-dimethylglycine level
terms.name_zh: 尿N,N-二甲基甘氨酸水平升高
terms.definition: An increased concentration of N,N-dimethylglycine in the urine.

terms.name: Tongue tremor
terms.definition: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement affecting the tongue.

terms.name: Snowball lesion of corpus callosum
terms.definition: Centrally located corpus callosum hyperintensities said to resemble snowballs upon magnetic resonance imaging (with T2 or Sagittal fluid attenuated inversion recovery [FLAIR] sequences). The central location in the callosum makes them pathognomonic for Susac syndrome.

terms.name: Recurrent bacterial upper respiratory tract infections
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to bacterial upper respiratory tract infections as manifested by a history of recurrent bacterial upper respiratory tract infections (running ears - otitis, sinusitis, pharyngitis, tonsillitis).

terms.name: Usual interstitial pneumonia
terms.definition: Temporal and spatial heterogeneity in lungs based on presence of fibrosis and honeycombing.

terms.name: Nocturnal seizures
terms.definition: Seizures that occur while the affected individual is sleeping.

terms.name: Neurogenic claudication
terms.definition: Lumbar spinal stenoses may induce symptoms following an individually typical latency on standing or when walking due to swelling of the cauda equina, which leads to compression. This is referred to as neurogenic claudication. The symptoms of lumbar spinal stenosis can be explained by an increase in lumbar lordosis and spinal canal stenosis in an upright position compared to the sitting position or if spondylolisthesis is present by a shift of the vertebrae while standing and walking. Following an individually characteristic distance, walking becomes associated with deep muscular pain and with neurological deficits, such as sensory deficits and paresis in the lower limbs, which resolve within minutes when the affected person sits or lies down. Activities performed in a flexed posture, such as cycling often cause less problems than walking. For the same reason, walking uphill may be tolerated better than walking downhill. Clinical neurological examination at rest may be entirely normal but there is usually pain on hyperextension of the lumbar spine.

terms.name: Cautious gait
terms.definition: Cautious gait refers to an excessive degree of age-related changes in walking and fear of falling. The walking difficulties seem out of proportion when considering the patient's actual sensory or motor deficits. The gait appears slow, with a wider base than normal, reduced arm swing bilaterally and a slightly stooped posture. This type of gait change often occurs after the first time a patient has fallen.

terms.name: Dystonic gait
terms.definition: Dystonic gait disorders frequently appear bizarre, particularly because activity increases dystonic tonus and posture. The abnormal posture of the foot in dystonic gait typically involves inversion, plantar flexion and tonic extension of the big toe. In many patients complex types of walking, such as walking backwards and running are paradoxically less impaired than walking forward and may seem completely unaffected. Sensory tricks, for instance, if the affected individual rests a hand on his or her neck, may improve or even normalize dystonic gait in some patients.

terms.name: Antalgic gait
terms.definition: To avoid pain weight is put on the affected leg for as short a time as possible, resulting in a limp. The patients appear to be walking as if there were a thorn in the sole of the foot. To reduce the load on the affected leg the patients lift and lower their foot in a fixed ankle position.

terms.name: Elevated circulating aspartate aminotransferase concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环天冬氨酸氨基转移酶浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Spastic hemiparetic gait
terms.definition: Spastic hemiparesis is characterized by a dominance of the tonus in the upper limb flexor muscles: the arm is held in an adducted posture and is bent and rotated inwards, the forearm is pronated and the hand and the fingers are flexed. The leg is slightly bent at the hip, the knee cannot be extended fully at the end of the stance phase and the foot is inverted and in a plantar flexed position. Gait is slow, with a wide base and asymmetrical with a shortened weight-bearing phase on the paretic side. During the swing phase, the paretic leg performs a lateral movement (circumduction) which is characteristic of this gait disorder, also termed Wernicke-Mann gait. Spastic gait problems typically worsen on attempts to walk faster.

terms.name: Spastic paraparetic gait
terms.definition: A type of spastic gait in which the legs are usually slightly bent at the hip and in an adducted position. The knees are extended or slightly bent and the feet are in a plantar flexion position. This posture requires circumduction of the legs during walking. The gait may appear stiff (spastic gait disorder) or stiff as well as insecure (spastic ataxic gait disorder). In spastic paraparetic gait, each leg appears to be dragged forward. If the muscle tone in the adductors is marked, the resulting gait disorder is referred to as scissor gait.

terms.name: Leg dystonia
terms.definition: A type of dystonia (abnormally increased muscular tone causing fixed abnormal postures) that affects muscles of the legs.

terms.name: Arm dystonia
terms.definition: A type of dystonia (abnormally increased muscular tone causing fixed abnormal postures) that affects muscles of the arms.

terms.name: Abnormal serum anion gap
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal value of the serum anion gap, which is calculated from the electrolytes measured in the chemical laboratory, is defined as the sum of serum chloride and bicarbonate concentrations subtracted from the serum sodium concentration.

terms.name: Elevated serum anion gap
terms.definition: An abnormally high value of the serum anion gap (the sum of serum chloride and bicarbonate concentrations subtracted from the serum sodium concentration).

terms.name: Decreased serum anion gap
terms.definition: An abnormally low value of the serum anion gap (the sum of serum chloride and bicarbonate concentrations subtracted from the serum sodium concentration).

terms.name: Elevated circulating alanine aminotransferase concentration
terms.name_zh: 血丙氨酸氨基转移酶浓度升高
terms.definition: An abnormally high concentration in the circulation of alanine aminotransferase (ALT).

terms.name: Increased RBC distribution width
synonyms: Increased red blood cell distribution width
terms.definition: Red blood cell distribution width (RDW) is a simple parameter of the standard full blood count and a measure of heterogeneity in the size of circulating erythrocytes. It is provided by automated hematology analyzers and it reflects the range of the red cell size. It is calculated by dividing the standard deviation of erythrocyte volume by the mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and multiplied by 100 to convert to a percentage.

terms.name: Cloudy urine
terms.definition: The appearance of the urine having visible material in suspension, i.e., appearing cloudy.

terms.name: Reduced blood urea nitrogen
terms.definition: An abnormally low concentration of urea nitrogen in the blood.

terms.name: Abnormal blood urea nitrogen concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of urea nitrogen in the blood.

terms.name: Subaortic ventricular septal bulge
terms.definition: A localized hypertrophy of the subaortic segment of the ventricular septum has been frequently described in elderly persons, and variously termed subaortic ventricular septal bulge (VSB), sigmoid-shaped septum, localized or discrete upper septal hypertrophy.

terms.name: Presyncope
terms.definition: Presyncope is a state of lightheadedness, muscular weakness, blurred vision, and feeling faint. Presyncope is most often cardiovascular in cause.

terms.name: Increased vertical cup-to-disc ratio
terms.definition: An abnormal increase in the ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disk.

terms.name: Increased vertical cup-to-disc ratio - 0.6
terms.definition: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disk is 0.6 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

terms.name: Increased vertical cup-to-disc ratio - 0.7
terms.definition: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disk is 0.7 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

terms.name: Increased vertical cup-to-disc ratio - 0.8
terms.definition: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disk is 0.8 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

terms.name: Increased vertical cup-to-disc ratio - 0.9
terms.definition: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disk is 0.9 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

terms.name: Increased vertical cup-to-disc ratio - 1.0
terms.definition: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disk is 1.0 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

terms.name: Abnormal urine carbohydrate level
terms.name_zh: 尿碳水化合物水平异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a carbohydrate in the urine.

terms.name: Abnormal urine carboxylic acid level
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a carboxylic acid in the urine.

terms.name: Elevated urine glycolate
terms.definition: An increased concentration of glycolate in the urine.

terms.name: Abnormal putamen morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the putamen, a brain nucleus which together with the caudate nucleus and fundus striati makes up the striatum.

terms.name: Abnormal pulmonary thoracic imaging finding
terms.name_zh: 肺胸部影像学表现异常
terms.definition: This term groups terms representing abnormal findings derived from chest X-ray investigation of the lung. In general, lung abnormalities can manifest as opacities (areas of increased density) or as regions with decreased density.

terms.name: Esophageal food impaction
terms.definition: A piece of food that has gotten stuck in the esophagus and prevents further swallowing.

terms.name: Esophageal exudate
terms.definition: An exudate is a mass of fluid and cells that has seeped out of blood vessels or an organ, usually related to inflammation. In the esophagus, exudates usually present as whitish plagues on the surface of the esophageal mucosa.

terms.name: Polyminimyoclonus
terms.definition: Minipolymyoclonus or polyminimyoclonus is a hyperkinetic movement disorder phenomenology characterized by intermittent, low-amplitude, arrhythmic movements of the hands, commonly of several fingers, with amplitudes just sufficient to produce visible and palpable movements of the joints. It is mostly noticed while the individual is maintaining a posture (commonly outstretched hands) or during action (especially the initial phase of movement).

terms.name: Diminished ability to concentrate
terms.definition: The inability to focus or concentrate on a specific task, activity, or object. The subject may find themselves unable to grasp or understand written text and re-reads frequently without understanding. Familiar tasks or activities are severely compromised due to the lack of ability to concentrate. Thinking through multi-step problems is typically very difficult or impossible, leading to avoidance of such activities.

terms.name: Perioral spasm
terms.definition: A sudden involuntary contraction of the musculature surrounding the mouth.

terms.name: Chvostek sign
terms.definition: A contraction of ipsilateral facial muscles subsequent to percussion over the facial nerve.

terms.name: Increased urinary excretion of galactosyl hydroxylysine
terms.name_zh: 尿半乳糖基羟赖氨酸排泄增加
terms.definition: An increased concentration of beta-1-galactosyl-O-hydroxylysine (Gal-Hyl) in the urine. This is a biochemical marker of bone resorption.

terms.name: Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
terms.definition: Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (AHCM) is diastolic dysfunction due to abnormal stiffness of the left ventricle during diastole, with resultant impaired ventricular filling. In AHCM thickened apical segments produce a crowded, spade-shaped, small apical cavity.

terms.name: Hoffmann sign
terms.definition: A Hoffmann test is performed by flicking the fingernail of the long finger, from dorsal to volar, on each hand while the hand was supported by the examiner's hand. The test was done with the neck in the neutral position and then with the neck maximally forward flexed. Any flexion of the ipsilateral thumb and/or index finger was interpreted as a positive test.

terms.name: Bronchial breath sound
terms.definition: Bronchial breath sounds contain much higher frequency components than normal breath sounds due to alteration of the low pass filtering function of the alveoli, as occurs in consolidation. It is loud, hollow, and high pitch. Expiratory phase is longer than inspiratory phase with the inspiratory-expiratory ratio (I:E) changing from normal 3:1 to 1:2. There is distinct pause between inspiration and expiration due to absent alveolar phase. It is associated with whispering pectoriloquy.

terms.name: Squawks
terms.definition: Squawks are short inspiratory wheezes of less than 200 ms duration and are also known as squeaks. Acoustic analysis shows the fundamental frequency varying between 200 and 300 Hz. Squawks usually occur in late inspiration and are often preceded by late inspiratory crackles.

terms.name: Inspiratory crackles
terms.definition: Crackles that are heard during the inspiratory phase.

terms.name: Early inspiratory crackles
terms.definition: Crackles that appear at the beginning of inspiration and end before mid-inspiration.

terms.name: Late inspiratory crackles
terms.definition: Crackles that appear any time after the beginning of inspiration and last till the end of inspiration.

terms.name: Expiratory crackles
terms.definition: Crackles that occur during expiration.

terms.name: Pleural rub
terms.definition: An abnormal breath sound that is nonmusical, short and explosive. It is grating, rubbing, creaky, or leathery in character and present in both phases of respiration. Typically the expiratory component mirrors the inspiratory component. It occurs due to inflamed pleural surface rubbing each other during breathing. Clinically, it is important to differentiate it from crackles

terms.name: Pink urine
terms.definition: An abnormal pink color of urine.

terms.name: Orange urine
terms.definition: An abnormal orange color of urine.

terms.name: Green urine
terms.definition: An abnormal green color of urine.

terms.name: Pruritus vulvae
terms.definition: A sensation of itching in the vulvar region.

terms.name: Hemidystonia
terms.definition: Hemidystonia refers to dystonia which involves the ipsilateral face, arm, and leg.

terms.name: Lip tremor
terms.definition: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement affecting the lip.

terms.name: Maceration
terms.definition: A softening and breaking down of skin resulting from prolonged exposure to moisture. Macerated skin becomes soft and wrinkly and takes on a whitish hue.

terms.name: Pulmonary fat embolism
terms.definition: The release of fat globules into the venous circulation, thereby blocking blood circulation to the lung.

terms.name: Infantile constant exotropia
terms.definition: Constant exotropia occurring before 6 months of age.; often associated with a large angle of deviation and ocular/CNS abnormalities.

terms.name: Basic constant exotropia
terms.definition: Constant exotropia for near and distance, presenting after 6 months of age.

terms.name: Heterophoria
terms.definition: Heterophorias are latent deviations that are controlled by fusion. In certain circumstances (specific visual tasks, fatigue, illness, etc.), fusion can no longer be maintained and decompensation occurs.

terms.name: Heterotropia
terms.definition: Manifest deviation of the visual axes not controlled by fusion.

terms.name: Hypermetric horizontal saccades
terms.definition: Overshoot of horizontal (sideways) saccadic eye movements.

terms.name: Dysmetric vertical saccades
terms.definition: Inaccurate saccades (rapid movement of the eye between fixation points) in the vertical direction.

terms.name: Dysmetric horizontal saccades
terms.definition: Inaccurate saccades (rapid movement of the eye between fixation points) in the horizontal direction.

terms.name: Abnormal sputum
terms.definition: Abnormal appearance of material expectorated (coughed up) from the respiratory system and that is composed of mucus but may contain other substances such as pus, blood, microorganisms, and fibrin.

terms.name: Sputum eosinophilia
terms.definition: An increased proportion of eosinophils in sputum in the differentiated cell count.

terms.name: Multiple mononeuropathy
terms.definition: A type of peripheral neuropathy that happens when there is damage to two or more different nerve areas characterized by peripheral neuropathy of both the motor and sensory nerves of at least two different nerve trunks. Different nerves are affected either simultaneously or sequentially.

terms.name: Muscle eosinophilia
terms.definition: Eosinophil infiltration of skeletal muscle.

terms.name: Eosinophilic bladder infiltration
terms.name_zh: 嗜酸性粒细胞膀胱浸润
terms.definition: Transmural inflammation of the bladder predominantly with eosinophils, associated with fibrosis with or without muscle necrosis.

terms.name: Eosinophilic liver infiltration
terms.name_zh: 肝脏嗜酸性粒细胞浸润
terms.definition: Cellular infiltration of the liver parenchyma with a preponderance of eosinophils.

terms.name: Eosinophilic dermal infiltration
terms.name_zh: 嗜酸性粒细胞皮肤浸润
terms.definition: Presence of abnormally increased amounts of intraepidermal inflammatory cells with a predominance of eosinophils.

terms.name: Eosinophilic gallbladder infiltration
terms.name_zh: 嗜酸性粒细胞胆囊浸润
terms.definition: Cellular infiltrate confirmed by a cellular infiltrate comprised of mainly eosinophils in the gallbladder wall on histological examination.

terms.name: Ileal ulcer
terms.definition: An erosion of the mucous membrane in a portion of the ileum.

terms.name: Decreased circulating alpha-1-antitrypsin concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环α1-抗胰蛋白酶浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of alpha-1-antitrypsin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Anetoderma
terms.definition: Circumscribed area of flaccid skin due to the loss of elastic tissue in the dermis.

terms.name: Retinal dots
terms.definition: Yellow, white or grayish lesions in the retina that are well-defined/distinct, individual and mostly uniform in size.

terms.name: Macular dots
terms.definition: Yellow, white or grayish lesions in the macula that are well-defined/distinct, individual and mostly uniform in size.

terms.name: Floppy eyelid
terms.definition: Excessive eyelid tissue laxity, typically affecting both upper eyelids and associated with spontanteous tarsal eversion during sleep. It is more common in the obese, it may be associated with obstructive sleep apnea and it may result in corneal exposure or chronic papillary conjunctivitis.

terms.name: Lateral canthal tendon laxity
terms.definition: Laxity of the tendon stabilizing the lateral aspect of the tarsal plate to the zygomatic bone. This can result in rounded appearance of the lateral canthus. Also, when the eyelid is pulled medially, more than 2 mm movement of the canthal angle may be observed.

terms.name: Medial canthal tendon laxity
terms.definition: Laxity of the tendon stabilizing the medial aspect of the tarsal plate to the anterior and posterior lacrimal crests. This may lead to more than 2mm movement of the punctum when the eyelid is pulled laterally.

terms.name: Horizontal eyelid laxity
terms.definition: Abnormally lax eyelid associated with tissue relaxation, predominantly in the horizontal plane. It can be demonstrated by the horizontal eyelid distraction test (e.g. by pulling the eyelid medially and laterally). Medial and/or lateral canthal tendon laxity are often present.

terms.name: Vertical eyelid laxity
terms.definition: Abnormally lax eyelid associated with tissue relaxation, predominantly in the vertical plane. It can be demonstrated by vertical lid pull. Loosening of vertical stabilizing structures (e.g. lower lid retractors) or tarsal atrophy are often present.

terms.name: Upper eyelid laxity
terms.definition: Abnormally lax upper eyelid associated with tissue relaxation.

terms.name: Lower eyelid laxity
terms.definition: Abnormally lax lower eyelid associated with tissue relaxation.

terms.name: Reduced contrast sensitivity
terms.definition: An abnormality in perception of contrast. Spatial contrast is a physical dimension referring to the light-dark transition of a border or an edge in an image that delineates the existence of a pattern or an object. Contrast sensitivity refers to a measure of how much contrast a person requires to see a target. Contrast-sensitivity measurements differ from acuity measurements; acuity is a measure of the spatial-resolving ability of the visual system under conditions of very high contrast, whereas contrast sensitivity is a measure of the threshold contrast for seeing a target.

terms.name: Mildly reduced visual acuity
terms.definition: Mild reduction of the ability to see. On the 6m visual acuity scale, mild reduction is defined as less than 6/12 but at least 6/18. On the 20ft visual acuity scale, mild reduction is defined as less than 20/40 but at least 20/70. On the decimal visual acuity scale, mild reduction is defined as less than 0.5 but at least 0.3.

terms.name: Abnormality of the ocular adnexa
terms.definition: An anomaly of the adjacent structures (i.e., adnexa) of the eye, defined as the lacrimal apparatus, the extraocular muscles and the eyelids, eyelashes, eyebrows and the conjunctiva.

terms.name: Abnormal ocular adnexa physiology
terms.name_zh: 眼附属器生理功能异常
terms.definition: A functional anomaly of the adjacent structures (i.e., adnexa) of the eye, defined as the lacrimal apparatus, the extraocular muscles and the eyelids, eyelashes, eyebrows and the conjunctiva.

terms.name: Vocal cord polyp
terms.definition: A small growth on a vocal cord that may appear as pedunculated or sessile and have varying size, shape, and color.

terms.name: Odynophagia
terms.definition: Pain experienced with swallowing.

terms.name: Decreased vigilance
terms.definition: A decrease in the ability to maintain sustained attention is characterized by reduced alertness.

terms.name: Hypoplastic carotid canal
terms.definition: Underdevelopment of the carotid canal, which normally is a circular aperture in the temporal bone of the skull through which the internal carotid artery and the carotid plexus of nerves traverse.

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia
terms.definition: A type of malformation of cortical development that primarily affects areas of neocortex. It can be identified on conventional magnetic resonance imaging as focal cortical thickening, abnormal gyration, and blurring between gray and white matter, often associated with clusters of heterotopic neurons.

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia type I
terms.name_zh: Ⅰ型局灶性皮质发育不良
terms.definition: A type of focal cortical dysplasia that is characterized by abnormal cortical layering.

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia type Ia
terms.name_zh: Ⅰa型局灶性皮质发育不良
terms.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type I that is characterized by abnormal radial cortical lamination.

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia type Ib
terms.name_zh: Ⅰb型局灶性皮质发育不良
terms.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type I that is characterized by abnormal tangential cortical lamination.

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia type Ic
terms.name_zh: Ⅰc型局灶性皮质发育不良
terms.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type I that is characterized by abnormal radial and tangential cortical lamination.

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia type II
terms.name_zh: Ⅱ型局灶性皮质发育不良
terms.definition: A type of focal cortical dysplasia that is characterized by disrupted cortical lamination and specific cytological abnormalities.

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia type IIa
terms.name_zh: Ⅱa型局灶性皮质发育不良
terms.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type II that is characterized by dysmorphic neurons, which present with a significantly enlarged cell body and nucleus, malorientation, abnormally distributed intracellular Nissl substance and cytoplasmic accumulation of neurofilament proteins.

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia type IIb
terms.name_zh: Ⅱb型局灶性皮质发育不良
terms.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type II that is characterized by dysmorphic neurons (significantly enlarged with accumulation of neurofilament proteins) and balloon cells.

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia type III
terms.name_zh: Ⅲ型局灶性皮质发育不良
terms.definition: A type of focal cortical dysplasia that is characterized by cortical lamination abnormalities associated with a principal lesion, usually adjacent to or affecting the same cortical area/lobe.

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia type IIIa
terms.name_zh: Ⅲa型局灶性皮质发育不良
terms.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type III that is characterized by alterations in architectural organization (cortical dyslamination) or cytoarchitectural composition (hypertrophic neurons outside Layer 5) in patients with hippocampal sclerosis (also known as Ammon's horn sclerosis).

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia type IIIb
terms.name_zh: Ⅲb型局灶性皮质发育不良
terms.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type III that is characterized by altered architectural (cortical dyslamination, hypoplasia without six-layered structure) and/or cytoarchitectural composition (hypertrophic neurons) of the neocortex, which occur adjacent to glial or glioneuronal tumor.

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia type IIIc
terms.name_zh: Ⅲc型局灶性皮质发育不良
terms.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type III that is characterized by alterations in architectural (cortical dyslamination, hypoplasia) or cytoarchitectural composition of the neocortex (hypertrophic neurons), which occur adjacent to vascular malformations (cavernomas, arteriovenous malformations, leptomeningeal vascular malformations, telangiectasias, meningioangiomatosis).

terms.name: Focal cortical dysplasia type IIId
terms.name_zh: Ⅲd型局灶性皮质发育不良
terms.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type III that is characterized by altered architectural (cortical dyslamination, hypoplasia without six-layered structure) or cytoarchitectural composition (hypertrophic neurons) of the neocortex, which occur adjacent to other lesions acquired during early life (not included into FCD Type IIIa-c). These lesions comprise a large spectrum including traumatic brain injury, glial scarring after prenatal or perinatal ischemic injury or bleeding, and inflammatory or infectious diseases, i.e. Rasmussen encephalitis, limbic encephalitis, bacterial or viral infections.

terms.name: Mild malformation of cortical development
terms.definition: A malformation of cortical development characterized by mild abnormalities of the cortex: excessive heterotopic neurons in Layer 1 or microscopic neuronal clusters or excess of single neurons of normal morphology in deep white matter.

terms.name: Epithelioid hemangioma
terms.definition: A benign neoplasm that includes blood vessel proliferation and a dense eosinophilic inflammatory infiltrate, manifesting as flesh/plum-colored pruritic nodules and papules, most commonly affecting the ear and the periauricular area.

terms.name: Severely increased total eosinophil count
terms.definition: Severe increase in circulating eosinophils, usually characterized as more than 1500 eosinophils per microlitre.

terms.name: Mallory-Weiss tear
terms.definition: Vomiting-induced mucosal laceration at the esophago-gastric junction.

terms.name: Ankle joint effusion
terms.definition: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in or around the ankle joint.

terms.name: Gastrointestinal eosinophilia
terms.name_zh: 胃肠道嗜酸性粒细胞增多症
terms.definition: Eosinophilic infiltration of one or more gastrointestinal organs. Gastrointestinal eosinophilia is a broad term for abnormal eosinophil accumulation in the GI tract, involving many different disease identities. These diseases include primary eosinophil associated gastrointestinal diseases, gastrointestinal eosinophilia in HES and all gastrointestinal eosinophilic states associated with known causes. Each of these diseases has its unique features but there is no absolute boundary between them.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating bicarbonate concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of bicarbonate, HCO3[-], in the circulation.

terms.name: Decreased serum bicarbonate concentration
terms.name_zh: 血清碳酸氢盐浓度降低
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction of the concentration of bicarbonate, HCO3[-], in the circulation.

terms.name: Elevated serum bicarbonate concentration
terms.name_zh: 血清碳酸氢盐浓度升高
terms.definition: An abnormal increase in the concentration of bicarbonate, HCO3[-], in the circulation.

terms.name: Increased urinary mucus
terms.definition: An increased amount of urinary mucus. A small amount of mucus is produced by mucous membrane epithelial cells of the urinary tract. An increased amount of mucus can be detected upon urinalysis or other assays and may indicate conditions such as urinary tract infection, urinary tract reconstruction involving the use of bowel segments, or contamination of the urine sample prior to urinalysis.

terms.name: Anti-thyroglobulin antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗甲状腺球蛋白抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react to thyroglobulin.

terms.name: Leptomeningeal enhancement
terms.definition: Contrast material enhancement of the pia mater or enhancement that extends into the subarachnoid spaces of the sulci and cisterns is leptomeningeal enhancement. Leptomeningeal enhancement is usually associated with meningitis, which may be bacterial, viral, or fungal. The primary mechanism of this enhancement is breakdown of the blood-brain barrier without angiogenesis.

terms.name: Eosinophilic pneumonia
terms.definition: The presence of eosinophils in lung tissue, generally as detected by tissue biopsy, with or without blood eosinophilia.

terms.name: Popliteal synovial cyst
terms.definition: A fluid-filled mass that is a distention of a preexisting bursa in the popliteal fossa, most commonly the gastrocnemio-semimembranosus bursa. This bursa is unique in that it communicates with the knee joint, unlike other periarticular bursae, via an opening in the joint capsule posterior to the medial femoral condyle.

terms.name: Aplasia of the fallopian tube
terms.definition: Aplasia, that is failure to develop, of the fallopian tube.

terms.name: Splenopancreatic fusion
terms.definition: Fusion of the pancreatic tail and spleen.

terms.name: Male urethral meatus stenosis
terms.definition: An abnormal narrowing of the urethral opening (meatus) of the penis.

terms.name: Angel-shaped phalanx
terms.definition: A phalangeal malformation that is termed angel-shaped phalanx (ASP), because of its resemblance to the angels used for decoration of Christmas trees. The various components of an angel-shaped phalanx are: diaphyseal cuff (wings), surrounding a meta-diaphyseal core (body), which may appear empty or structured with a cone-shaped epiphysis (skirt) and pseudoepiphysis (head).

terms.name: Medial degeneration
terms.definition: Medial degeneration of the aorta is to be used as an overarching term for any aortic surgical specimens that demonstrate one or more of the specific histopathologies mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation, elastic fiber fragmentation and/or loss, elastic fiber thinning, elastic fiber disorganization, smooth muscle cell nuclei loss, laminar medial collapse, smooth muscle cell disorganization, medial fibrosis. Grading of medial degeneration is based on the average overall severity of specific histopathologies as described, considering the worst area(s) sampled from multiple slides and aorta sections.

terms.name: Intralamellar mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation
terms.name_zh: 板层内黏液样细胞外基质积聚
terms.definition: A type of mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation in which the increase in mucoid extracellular matrix does not significantly alter the arrangement of the lamellar units.

terms.name: Translamellar mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation
terms.definition: A type of mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation in which the increase in mucoid extracellular matrix alters the arrangement of the lamellar units to varying degrees.

terms.name: Aortic elastic fiber fragmentation
