terms.definition: Loss and/or fragmentation of elastic fibers of the media of the aorta creating increasingly extended translamellar spaces, with absence of elastic fibers, and increased gaps in elastic fiber lamellae as identified on a stain for elastic fibers.

terms.name: Aortic elastic fiber thinning
terms.definition: A thinning out of elastic fibers of the media of the aorta that creates widening of intralamellar spaces, as identified on a stain for elastic fibers.

terms.name: Aortic elastic fiber disorganization
terms.name_zh: 主动脉弹力纤维排列紊乱
terms.definition: Nonparallel arrangement/disarray of elastic fibers of the media of the aorta as identified on a stain for elastic fibers.

terms.name: Aortic smooth muscle cell nuclei loss
terms.name_zh: 主动脉平滑肌细胞核缺失
terms.definition: A region of the aortic media in which smooth muscle cell nuclei, involving multiple lamellae, are not clearly identifiable on an hematoxylin and eosin stain.

terms.name: Aortic laminar medial collapse
terms.definition: Architecturally, a compaction of aortic medial elastic fibers that creates thinning of the lamellar unit secondary to a band-like smooth muscle cell loss identified using a stain for elastic fibers.

terms.name: Aortic smooth muscle cell disorganization
terms.name_zh: 主动脉平滑肌细胞排列紊乱
terms.definition: Nonparallel arrangement/disarray of smooth muscle cells of the aortic media creating focal/multifocal disarray or sometimes nodular aggregates of smooth muscle cells.

terms.name: Aortic medial fibrosis
terms.definition: An increase in collagen fibers creating areas of substitutive fibrosis or a widening of intralamellar spaces in the media of the aorta. This can be seen in conjunction with a loss to varying degrees of parallel arrangement of the elastic lamellae (or lamellar units).

terms.name: Intralamellar aortic medial fibrosis
terms.name_zh: 板层内主动脉中层纤维化
terms.definition: A type of aortic medial fibrosis in which the increase in collagen does not significantly alter the arrangement of the lamellar units.

terms.name: Translamellar aortic medial fibrosis
terms.definition: A type of aortic medial fibrosis in which the increase in collagen is more scar-like, altering the arrangement of the lamellar units.

terms.name: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
terms.definition: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction can occur at the valvular, subvalvular, or supravalvular level. In general, there is an obstruction to forward flow which increases afterload, and if untreated, can result in hypertrophy, dilatation, and eventual failure of the left ventricle.

terms.name: Elevated circulating surfactant protein concentration
terms.name_zh: 血表面活性蛋白浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of surfactant protein in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating manganese concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of manganese cation in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Hypermanganesemia
synonyms: Elevated manganese cation level in blood
Increased manganese cation level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of manganese cation in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Hypomanganesemia
synonyms: Decreased manganese cation level in blood
Reduced manganese cation level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of manganese cation in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Perioral radial furrowing
terms.definition: The presence of radial grooves in the skin surrounding the mouth (see Figure 4 of PMID:27833976).

terms.name: Abnormal doll's eye reflex
terms.definition: The doll's eye reflex (also known as oculocephalic reflex) is a test of brain function that is performed in comatose patients by elevating the head roughly 30 degrees and rapidly rotating the head from side to side with the eyes kept open. A normal response is for the eyes to move in the opposite direction. If the eyes do not move in the opposite direction this may indicate severe brain damage.

terms.name: Unusual infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection, as manifested by recurrent infection, severe or invasive infection, infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location, or infection with opportunistic organisms, that is unusual for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Wilson sign
terms.definition: Wilson sign is defined as the elicitation of pain by internally rotating the patient's tibia during knee extension between 90 degrees and 30 degrees of flexion and then relieving that pain by externally rotating the tibia.

terms.name: Saccadic oscillation
terms.definition: An involuntary abnormality of fixation in which there is an abnormal saccade away from fixation followed by an immediate corrective saccade.

terms.name: Macrosaccadic oscillations
terms.definition: A type of saccadic oscillations with brief periods of fixation between saccades (intersaccadic interval approximately 200 msec). Macrosaccadic oscillations (up to 40 degrees) straddle the intended fixation position and show a crescendo-decrescendo pattern.

terms.name: Conjunctival icterus
synonyms: Yellowing of the whites of the eyes
terms.definition: Conjunctival icterus is a condition where there is yellowing of the whites of the eyes. This is most commonly seen in patients who have liver disease.

terms.name: Limbal stem cell deficiency
terms.definition: A condition characterized by a loss or deficiency of the stem cells in the limbus that are vital for re-population of the corneal epithelium and to the barrier function of the limbus.

terms.name: Mildly reduced contrast sensitivity
terms.definition: A mild reduction in the ability to perceive visual contrast characterized by 0.20-0.59 log unit contrast sensitivity loss.

terms.name: Moderately reduced contrast sensitivity
terms.definition: A moderate reduction in the ability to perceive visual contrast characterized by 0.60-0.99 log unit contrast sensitivity loss.

terms.name: Severely reduced contrast sensitivity
terms.definition: A severe reduction in the ability to perceive visual contrast characterized by 1.00 log unit or more contrast sensitivity loss.

terms.name: Abnormal Vistech contrast sensitivity test
terms.definition: An abnormality in perception of contrast as measured by the Vistech wall chart sine wave grating test.

terms.name: Abnormal Pelli Robson contrast sensitivity chart test
terms.name_zh: 佩利-罗布森对比敏感度表检查异常
terms.definition: An abnormality in perception of contrast as measured by the Pelli-Robson contrast sensitivity chart, which is a large wall-mounted chart, with letters of a fixed size (comprising spatial frequencies appropriate for estimating peak contrast sensitivity) that decrease in contrast.

terms.name: Semidominant inheritance
terms.definition: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on chromosomes in which a trait can manifest in a monoallelic (e.g. heterozygotes) and biallelic (e.g. homozygotes, compound heterozygotes) state, with similar or differing phenotype severity present dependent on the number of alleles affected.

terms.name: Saccadic intrusion
terms.definition: An involuntary abnormality of fixation in which there is an abnormal saccade away from fixation followed by a delayed corrective saccade.

terms.name: Macrosquare-wave jerks
terms.definition: Horizontal 10-40 degree excursions from fixation and back again.

terms.name: Retinitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the retina of the eye.

terms.name: Abnormal peripheral nervous system physiology
terms.name_zh: 周围神经系统生理异常
terms.definition: Any functional abnormality of the part of the nervous system that consists of the nerves and ganglia outside of the brain and spinal cord.

terms.name: Froment sign
terms.definition: An abnormal result of a physical examination of the the hand that tests for palsy of the ulnar nerve. This nerve innervates the adductor pollicis and interossei muscles and thereby enables adduction of the thumb and extension of the interphalangeal joint. An abnormal result consists in reduced functionality and muscular weakness in the pinch grip between the thumb and index finger of the affected hand as the patient attempts to pinch a piece of paper that the examiner tries to pull away. The flexor pollicis longus muscle tries to compensate for the weakness by flexing the tip of the thumb at the interphalangeal joint.

terms.name: Very low visual acuity
terms.definition: A reduction in visual acuity with best corrected visual acuity between 1.40 (20/500) and 1.89 logMAR (up to roughly 20/1590).

terms.name: Ultra-low vision
terms.definition: Best corrected visual acuity worse than 1.90 logMAR (roughly 20/1590).

terms.name: Abnormal unswitched memory B cell proportion
terms.name_zh: 未转换记忆B细胞比例异常
synonyms: Abnormal proportion of non-class-switched memory B cells
Abnormal proportion of unswitched memory B cells
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of the unswitched memory B cell subpopulation, commonly characterized as CD27+IgM+, measured as percentage of total B cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Increased unswitched memory B cell proportion
terms.name_zh: 未转换记忆B细胞比例升高
synonyms: Elevated proportion of unswitched memory B cells
Increased proportion of non-class-switched memory B cells
Increased proportion of unswitched memory B cells
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of the unswitched memory B cell subpopulation, commonly characterized as CD27+IgM+, measured as percentage of total B cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Decreased unswitched memory B cell proportion
terms.name_zh: 未转换记忆B细胞比例降低
synonyms: Decreased proportion of non-class-switched memory B cells
Decreased proportion of unswitched memory B cells
Reduced proportion of unswitched memory B cells
terms.definition: Abnormal reduction of the unswitched memory B cell subpopulation, commonly characterized as CD27+IgM+, measured as percentage of total B cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Abnormal plasmablast proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of plasmablasts, commonly characterized as CD27+CD38hi and sometimes additionally as IgMlowCD24-, measured as percentage of total B cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Increased plasmablast proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of plasmablasts, commonly characterized as CD27+CD38hi and sometimes additionally as IgMlowCD24-, measured as percentage of total B cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Decreased plasmablast proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of plasmablasts, commonly characterized as CD27+CD38hi and sometimes additionally as IgMlowCD24-, measured as percentage of total B cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Mycobacterium abscessus abscessus infection
terms.definition: Mycobacterium abscessus complex comprises a group of rapidly growing, multidrug-resistant, nontuberculous mycobacteria that are responsible for a wide spectrum of skin and soft tissue diseases, central nervous system infections, bacteremia, and ocular and other infections.

terms.name: Cervical dysplasia
terms.definition: Cervical dysplasia is the precursor to cervical cancer. It is caused by the persistent infection of the human papillomavirus (HPV) into the cervical tissue. Affected cells develop morphologic features with immature basaloid- type squamous cells and mitotic figures in the upper half of the cervical epithelium.

terms.name: Decreased circulating total IgG concentration
terms.definition: A reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin G (IgG) in the blood.

terms.name: Transient decreased circulating total IgG concentration
terms.definition: A temporary reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin G (IgG) in the blood.

terms.name: Chronic decreased circulating total IgG concentration
synonyms: Chronic decreased total IgG in blood
terms.definition: A lasting reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin G (IgG) in the blood.

terms.name: Decreased circulating IgG subclass concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环免疫球蛋白G亚类浓度降低
synonyms: Decreased IgG subclass level in blood
terms.definition: A reduction below the normal concentration of a subclass of immunoglobulin G (IgG) in the blood.

terms.name: Decreased circulating IgG1 concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环免疫球蛋白G1浓度降低
terms.definition: A reduction in immunoglobulin levels of the IgG1 subclass in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Decreased circulating IgG3 concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环免疫球蛋白G3浓度降低
terms.definition: A reduction in immunoglobulin levels of the IgG3 subclass in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Decreased circulating IgG4 concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环免疫球蛋白G4浓度降低
terms.definition: A reduction in immunoglobulin levels of the IgG4 subclass in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Decreased circulating isohemagglutinin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环同族血凝素浓度降低
synonyms: Decreased natural antibody to blood group agents
terms.definition: Level of isohemagglutinin reduced below expected concentration. An isohemagglutinin refers to the naturally occurring antibodies in the ABO blood group system (i.e., anti-A in a group B person, anti-B in a group A person, and anti-A, anti-B, and anti-A,B in a group O person).

terms.name: Decreased specific antibody response to vaccination
terms.name_zh: 疫苗接种特异性抗体反应降低
terms.definition: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against toxoids and polysaccharides in vaccines, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

terms.name: Precordial pain
terms.definition: A type of chest pain that arises in the or under the left breast and often described as throbbing, stabbing, or burning, and lasting hours or longer. The pain may arise with or after effort, and may spread to the left arm or left side of the neck.

terms.name: Fetor hepaticus
terms.definition: Fetor hepaticus is the characteristic breath of patients with severe parenchymal liver disease, which has been said to resemble the odor of a mixture of rotten eggs and garlic.

terms.name: Burning mouth
terms.definition: An intense sensation of burning, scalding, or tingling feeling of the tongue or other regions of the oral mucosa.

terms.name: Coffee ground vomitus
terms.definition: Vomit that has the appearance of coffee grounds, which occurs due to the presence of coagulated blood in the vomit.

terms.name: Sural nerve atrophy
terms.definition: Wasting of the sural nerve, a sensory nerve in the calf region of the leg.

terms.name: HbC hemoglobin
terms.definition: Presence of an abnormal type of hemoglobin characterized by the substitution of a glutamic acid residue at position 7 following the initial methionine residue by a lysine (6GAG>6AAG). The presence of HbC can be determined by hemoglobin electrophoresis.

terms.name: Erythromelalgia
terms.definition: Recurrent episodes of redness, burning pain, and warmth of the extremities following exposure to heat or exercise with symptoms predominantly involving the feet.

terms.name: Episodic pain
terms.definition: Intermittent pain, i.e., pain that occurs occasionally and at irregular intervals.

terms.name: Breakthrough pain
terms.definition: A episode of severe pain that breaks through (i.e., temporarily exacerbates) a period of persistent pain.

terms.name: Paroxysmal rectal pain
terms.definition: Excruciating burning pain in the rectal area that may be triggered by defecation.

terms.name: Episodic eosinophilia
terms.name_zh: 发作性嗜酸粒细胞增多
terms.definition: Recurrent episodes of marked eosinophilia that resolve spontaneously.

terms.name: Keratosis pilaris
terms.definition: An anomaly of the hair follicles of the skin that typically presents as small, rough, brown folliculocentric papules distributed over characteristic areas of the skin, particularly the outer-upper arms and thighs.

terms.name: Joint subluxation
terms.definition: A partial dislocation of a joint.

terms.name: Aphthous ulcer
terms.definition: Oral aphthous ulcers typically present as painful, sharply circumscribed fibrin-covered mucosal defects with a hyperemic border.

terms.name: Abdominal cramps
terms.definition: A type of abdominal pain characterized by a feeling of contractions and typically fluctuating in intensity.

terms.name: Skin detachment
terms.definition: Loss of sections of skin either spontaneously or after gentle handling.

terms.name: Recurrent genital herpes
terms.definition: Recurrent episodes of genital herpes, typically characterized by stages of erythema, papules, short-lived vesicles, painful ulcers, and crusts on the skin of the genitals and surrounding area, and that typically resolve over a period of 2 to 3 weeks.

terms.name: Unusual infection by anatomical site
terms.definition: An unusual infection classified by the affected body part.

terms.name: Fungal meningitis
terms.definition: A meningitis caused by fungal infection, with the principal causative organism being Cryptococcus neoformans (cryptococcal meningitis); other causes include Candida and Coccidioides species. A fungal meningitis is most often a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in severe T-cell deficiencies.

terms.name: Cryptococcal meningitis
terms.definition: A type of fungal meningitis caused by an encapsulated yeast that belongs to the genus Cryptococcus. Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are responsible for the majority of cases of human cryptococcosis.

terms.name: Coccidioidal meningitis
terms.definition: A type of fungal meningitis caused by dissemination of coccidioides to basilar meninges.

terms.name: Unusual skin infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection of the skin, nails, or mucous membranes, as manifested by recurrent or severe cutaneous or mucosal infection, or by skin or mucous membrane infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual molluscum contagiosum
terms.definition: Molluscum contagiosum is a cutaneous viral infection that is commonly observed in both healthy and immunocompromised children. The infection is caused by a member of the Poxviridae family, the molluscum contagiosum virus. Molluscum contagiosum presents as single or multiple small white or flesh-colored papules that typically have a central umbilication. The central umbilication may be difficult to observe in young children and, instead, may bear an appearance similar to an acneiform eruption. The lesions vary in size (from 1 mm to 1 cm in diameter) and are painless, although a subset of patients report pruritus in the area of infection. On average, 11-20 papules appear on the body during the course of infection and generally remains a self-limiting disease. However, in immunosuppressed patients, molluscum contagiosum can be a severe infection with hundreds of lesions developing on the body. Extensive eruption is indicative of an advanced immunodeficiency state.

terms.name: Increased circulating folate concentration
terms.definition: The concentration of folic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Placental mesenchymal dysplasia
terms.definition: Placental mesenchymal dysplasia is a rare anomaly characterized by placentomegaly, dilatation of chorionic vessels and hydropic stem villi with cistern-like formation. It is often clinically mistaken for a partial hydatidiform mole but there is no trophoblastic proliferation. P57 immunohistochemical expression is discordant, showing a normal positive expression in the cytotrophoblastic cells, and loss of expression in the stromal cells.

terms.name: Clostridium difficile enteritis
terms.definition: An infection of the small intestine (enteritis) by clostridium difficile.

terms.name: Clostridium difficile colitis
terms.definition: An infection of the colon (colitis) by clostridium difficile.

terms.name: Severe infection
terms.definition: A type of infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection because of unusual severity or intensity of the infection.

terms.name: Severe varicella zoster infection
terms.definition: An unusually severe form of varicella zoster virus (VZV) infection. In the majority of the cases, especially in children, varicella is a very mild infection characterized by skin lesions, low grade fever and malaise. Severe infection is characterized by manifestations including VZV pneumonia, hepatitis, meningitis, and disseminated varicella.

terms.name: Bladder pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the urinary bladder. Bladder pain may be more pronounced with a full bladder and relieved upon urination, but this is not always the case.

terms.name: Continuous diaphragm sign
terms.definition: This sign is seen in pneumomediastinum in which air accumulates between the lower border of the heart and the superior part of the diaphragm, which results in complete visualization of the diaphragm in chest X-ray, hence named continuous diaphragm sign.

terms.name: Tree-in-bud pattern
terms.definition: The tree-in-bud pattern represents centrilobular branching structures that resemble a budding tree. The pattern reflects a spectrum of endo- and peribronchiolar disorders, including mucoid impaction, inflammation, and/or fibrosis (See Figure 70 of PMID:18195376).

terms.name: Signet ring sign
terms.definition: This finding is composed of a ring-shaped opacity representing a dilated bronchus in cross section and a smaller adjacent opacity representing its pulmonary artery, with the combination resembling a signet (or pearl) ring. It is the basic sign of bronchiectasis in pulmonary computed tomography imaging.

terms.name: Apical pulmonary opacity
terms.definition: An apical cap is a caplike lesion at the lung apex, usually caused by intrapulmonary and pleural fibrosis pulling down extrapleural fat or possibly by chronic ischemia resulting in hyaline plaque formation on the visceral pleura. The prevalence increases with age. It can also be seen in hematoma resulting from aortic rupture or in other fluid collection associated with infection or tumor, either outside the parietal pleura or loculated within the pleural space.

terms.name: Parenchymal consolidation
terms.definition: Consolidation refers to an exudate or other product of disease that replaces alveolar air, rendering the lung solid (as in infective pneumonia).

terms.name: Flaky paint dermatosis
terms.definition: A dermatosis characterized by generalized shiny, enamel-like, hyperpigmented scales in an irregular pattern. The scales may peel or desquamate, rather like old, sun-baked blistered paint, often with areas of underlying hypopigmentation. This has led to the terms peeling paint or flaky paint dermatosis (See the Figure in PMID:24285001).

terms.name: Abnormal circulating globulin concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of globulins in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating metabolite concentration
terms.definition: An abnormal level of an analyte measured in the blood.

terms.name: Anomalous hepatic venous drainage into the left atrium
terms.name_zh: 肝静脉异常引流入左心房
terms.definition: An abnormality of the hepatic veins, which normally drain de-oxygenated blood from the liver into the inferior vena cava, whereby the hepatic veins drain into the left atrium.

terms.name: Abnormal memory T cell proportion
synonyms: Abnormal proportion of memory T cells
terms.definition: An abnormal proportion of memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. Memory T cells have previously encountered and responded to their cognate antigen and upon a repeated encounter with the antigen can mount a faster and stronger response.

terms.name: Decreased memory T cell proportion
synonyms: Decreased proportion of memory T cells
terms.definition: An abnormally reduced proportion of memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood.

terms.name: Increased memory T cell proportion
synonyms: Increased proportion of memory T cells
terms.definition: An abnormally elevated proportion of memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood.

terms.name: Disseminated molluscum contagiosum
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Molluscum contagiosum infections as manifested by a severe, invasive, or disseminated infection with Molluscum contagiosum over the body.

terms.name: Anal neoplasm
terms.definition: A benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the anal canal or anal margin.

terms.name: Anal intraepithelial neoplasia
terms.definition: Anal intraepithelial neoplasia (AIN) is a premalignant lesion of the anal mucosa that is a precursor to anal cancer.

terms.name: Cellular hypersensitivity to mitomycin C
terms.definition: An increased cellular sensitivity to the DNA cross-linking agent, mitomycin C (MMC). In the presence of increased sensitivity, MMC causes increased cell death, chromosome breakage, and accumulation in the G2 phase of the cell cycle.

terms.name: Cellular hypersensitivity to diepoxybutane
terms.name_zh: 细胞对二环氧丁烷超敏
terms.definition: An increased cellular sensitivity to the DNA cross-linking agent, diepoxybutane (DEB). In the presence of increased sensitivity, DEB causes cell death, chromosome breakage, and accumulation in the G2 phase of the cell cycle.

terms.name: Abnormal meniscus morphology
terms.definition: Abnormal structure of the meniscus of the knee, two crescent shape fibrocartilaginous pads that disperse the weight of the body and reduce friction of the knee joint during movement.

terms.name: Torn meniscus
terms.definition: A tear in the cartilaginous pad (meniscus) of the knee.

terms.name: Hydatidiform mole
terms.definition: Hydatidiform mole (HM) is an aberrant human pregnancy with absence of, or abnormal embryonic development, hydropic degeneration of chorionic villi, and excessive proliferation of the trophoblast.

terms.name: Decreased low-density lipoprotein particle size
terms.name_zh: 低密度脂蛋白颗粒粒径减小
terms.definition: An abnormal decrease in the average size of low-density lipoprotein particle size in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal S wave
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the S wave, which is the third component of the QRS wave complex. The S wave signifies the final depolarization of the ventricles at the base of the heart.

terms.name: Prominent S wave in lead I
terms.definition: Increased amplitude (0.1 mV or more) and/or duration (40 ms or more) of the S wave as measured in lead I of the electrocardiogram.

terms.name: Deep S wave in lead V5
terms.definition: Abnormal depth of the S wave in lead V5 of the electrocardiogram.

terms.name: Decreased prothrombin time
terms.definition: Abnormally short time to coagulation in the prothrombin time test, which is a measure of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation. The results of the prothrombin time test are often expressed in terms of the International normalized ratio (INR), which is calculated as a ratio of the patient's prothrombin time (PT) to a control PT standardized for the potency of the thromboplastin reagent developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) using the formula: INR is equal to Patient PT divided by Control PT.

terms.name: Abnormal prothrombin time
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal amount of time to coagulation in the prothrombin time test, which is a measure of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation. The results of the prothrombin time test are often expressed in terms of the International normalized ratio (INR), which is calculated as a ratio of the patient's prothrombin time (PT) to a control PT standardized for the potency of the thromboplastin reagent developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) using the formula: INR is equal to Patient PT divided by Control PT.

terms.name: Perivascular fibrosis
terms.definition: The presence of thick collagen bundles around blood vessels, often in an onion-skin type whorling pattern.

terms.name: Rotator cuff tear
terms.definition: The term rotator cuff describes the tendons connecting the infraspinatus, supraspinatus, teres minor, and subscapularis muscles to the humeral head.Traumatic tears of the rotator cuff tend to occur at the tendon-bone junction of the supraspinatus and greater tuberosity of the humerus whereas degenerative tears tend to be seen posteriorly at the junction of the supraspinatus and infraspinatu A rotator cuff tear is when one or more of these tendons tears or detaches from the humerus.

terms.name: Vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia
terms.definition: Vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN) is widely accepted as the precursor lesion of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC). VSCC arises via either a human papilloma virus (HPV)-associated pathway, or more commonly, via a mechanism independent of HPV, often being linked to chronic inflammatory conditions such as lichen sclerosus (LS). Accordingly, two distinct subtypes of VIN are recognized: the HPV-associated high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion/usual VIN (HSIL/uVIN) and the non-HPV-associated differentiated VIN (dVIN). HSIL is clinically identified by its multifocal, warty appearance and on histology by conspicuous cytological and architectural atypia. Differentiated VIN, on the other hand, often produces ill-defined lesions, and on histology, notoriously mimics non-neoplastic epithelial disorders (NNED), particularly LS. As a result, dVIN is rarely identified in advance of a diagnosis of invasive malignancy, despite being the precursor lesion of the majority of VSCC.

terms.name: Lymphoid nodular hyperplasia
terms.definition: Lymphoid nodular hyperplasia (LNH) of the terminal ileum and colon has been considered a mucosal response to nonspecific stimuli, most often infections, and consequently has been regarded as a pathophysiologic phenomenon during infancy and childhood. LNH can be ascertained by colonoscopy, whereby a lymphoid nodule is defined as an extruding follicle with a diameter of not more than 2 mm, and LNH is defined as a cluster of not more than 10 of such extruding lymphoid nodules (see Figure 1 of PMID:17368236).

terms.name: Chronic active EBV infection
terms.definition: Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is an uncommon outcome of EBV infection and may present as a waxing and waning or fulminant syndrome. Unlike acute infectious mononucleosis, wherein EBV establishes lifelong infection and survives by maintaining a delicate balance with the host as a latent infection, in chronic active EBV infection the host-virus balance is disturbed.

terms.name: Elevated circulating galectin-3 concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环半乳糖凝集素3浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of galectin-3 in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Increased urinary type 1 collagen N-terminal telopeptide level
terms.name_zh: 尿1型胶原N端肽水平升高
synonyms: Increased collagen crosslinked N-telopeptide [Moles/volume] in 24 hour urine
terms.definition: An increased concentration of type 1 collagen N-terminal telopeptide (NTx) level in the urine. Generally the test is performed over a period of time, for instance, 10 cc of morning urine can be collected following 12 hours overnight fasting or for 24 hours.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating free T3 concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环游离三碘甲状腺原氨酸浓度异常
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of free triiodothyronine (T3) in the blood circulation. A proportion of T3 is bound to plasma proteins in the blood, including mainly thyroxine binding globulin, transthyretin, and albumin. T3 that is not bound to a protein is referred to as free T3.

terms.name: Decreased circulating free T3
terms.name_zh: 血循环游离三碘甲状腺原氨酸降低
terms.definition: A reduced concentration of free 3,3',5-triiodo-L-thyronine in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Increased urinary epithelial cell count
terms.definition: An increased number of epithelial cells per high-power field in urinanalysis.

terms.name: Increased urinary squamous epithelial cell count
terms.name_zh: 尿鳞状上皮细胞计数增多
terms.definition: An increased number of squamous epithelial cells per high-power field in urinanalysis.

terms.name: Increased urinary renal tubular epithelial cell count
terms.name_zh: 尿肾小管上皮细胞计数增多
terms.definition: An increased number of renal tubular epithelial cells per high-power field in urinanalysis.

terms.name: Increased urinary transitional epithelial cell count
terms.name_zh: 尿移行上皮细胞计数增多
terms.definition: An increased number of transitional epithelial cells per high-power field in urinanalysis.

terms.name: Disseminated cutaneous warts
terms.definition: Multiple skin warts located in multiple parts of the body, e.g., neck, trunks, and extremities.

terms.name: Lymphocytic infiltration of the colorectal mucosa
terms.name_zh: 结直肠黏膜淋巴细胞浸润
terms.definition: Abnormally increased intraepithelial lymphocyte count. This finding may be appreciated as large numbers of surface intraepithelial lymphocytes as seen (for instance) with hematoxylin and eosin staining of a colonic biopsy sample taken during colonoscopy.

terms.name: Indurated nodule
terms.definition: A skin nodule that is unusually hard (indurated).

terms.name: Decreased total CD4+ T cell proportion
synonyms: Decreased proportion of CD4+ T cells
Decreased proportion of CD4-positive T cells
Decreased proportion of CD4-positive helper T cells
Decreased proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells, measured as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Increased total CD4+ T cell proportion
synonyms: Elevated proportion of CD4-positive T cells
Increased proportion of CD4+ T cells
Increased proportion of CD4-positive T cells
Increased proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells, measured as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Interface hepatitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the liver characterized by a mononuclear cell infiltrate whereby portal inflammatory cells extend through the limiting plate between the portal tract and liver parenchyma.

terms.name: Periportal emperipolesis
terms.definition: The engulfing of lymphocytes by hepatocytes, which typically occurs in the interface hepatitis area.

terms.name: Serrated intestinal polyps
terms.definition: The presence of multiple serrated polyps in the intestine. Unlike conventional adenomas, which are uniformly dysplastic, the vast majority of serrated lesions contain no dysplasia. The serrated class includes the hyperplastic polyps, which are not considered precancerous; sessile serrated polyps (also called sessile serrated adenomas); and traditional serrated adenomas. Sessile serrated polyps are larger on average and more often located in the proximal colon. Sessile serrated polyps have a more irregular surface, a pattern to the surface that has been called cloudlike, and indistinct edges compared with hyperplastic polyps. Sessile serrated polyps also have large open pits on the surface (type O pits) when viewed with magnification.

terms.name: Blood group
terms.definition: Any of the various types of human blood whose antigen characteristics determine compatibility in transfusion. While the ABO and Rhesus systems are the most well known, there are in total about 300 different blood type antigens distributed across 34 different blood type systems.

terms.name: ABO blood group
terms.definition: The ABO system consists of A and B antigens and antibodies against these antigens.

terms.name: Perifollicular fibroma
terms.definition: Perifollicular fibroma is a rare cutaneous hamartoma that shows differentiation in the connective tissue sheath of hair follicles. It can occur as a solitary papule or as multiple lesions. Histologically, the lesion consists of a concentric arrangement of cellular fibrous tissue around a normal hair follicle.

terms.name: Abnormal sebaceous gland morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the sebaceous glands.

terms.name: Sebaceous hyperplasia
terms.definition: A common, benign skin condition involving hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands characterized by single or multiple lesions that manifest as yellow, soft, small papules with umbilication. The lesions are located commonly on the central face (specifically, the nose, cheeks and forehead) but may also occur elsewhere, including the chest, mouth, scrotum, foreskin, penile shaft, vulva, and areola.

terms.name: Trichodiscoma
terms.definition: A small benign fibrovascular tumor of the dermal part of the hair disk. Trichodiscoma is rather simple in appearance and consists of a dome-shaped fibrous tumor with a prominent vascular component that fills the papillary dermis under an atrophic epidermis. As in a normal hair disk, a hair follicle may be present at one edge of the papular lesion.

terms.name: Perinuclear antineutrophil antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against proteins predominantly expressed in perinuclear region of neutrophils.

terms.name: Cytoplasmic antineutrophil antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 胞浆型抗中性粒细胞抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against proteins predominantly expressed in cytoplasmic granules of neutrophils.

terms.name: Hypochromia
terms.definition: A qualitative impression that red blood cells have less color than normal when examined under a microscope, usually related to a reduced amount of hemoglobin in the red blood cells.

terms.name: Elevated circulating CK-MB concentration
terms.definition: The concentration of CK-MB (= creatine kinase MB) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating creatine kinase BB isoform concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环肌酸激酶BB同工酶浓度升高
synonyms: Elevated circulating creatine kinase BB isoform concentration
Elevated creatine kinase B-type level in blood
Increased creatine kinase B-type level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of creatine kinase BB isoform in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating creatine kinase MM isoform concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环肌酸激酶MM同工酶浓度升高
synonyms: Elevated circulating creatine kinase MM isoform concentration
Elevated creatine kinase M-type level in blood
Increased creatine kinase M-type level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of creatine kinase MM isoform in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Anti-La/SS-B antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against La/SSB autoantigens.

terms.name: Increased circulating immature neutrophil count
terms.name_zh: 血循环未成熟中性粒细胞计数升高
terms.definition: An abnormally increased number of immature neutrophils in the peripheral blood circulation.

terms.name: Increased circulating myelocyte count
terms.name_zh: 血循环中幼粒细胞计数升高
terms.definition: The number of myelocytes in the peripheral blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. Myelocytes are immature neutrophils with a size of 12-18 micrometers, a round or oval nucleus with no nucleoli, bluish-pink staining cytoplasm with primary and secondary granules, and a nucleus:cytoplasm ratio of 2:1.

terms.name: Increased circulating metamyelocyte count
terms.name_zh: 血循环晚幼粒细胞计数升高
terms.definition: The number of metamyelocytes in the peripheral blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. Metamyelocytes are immature neutrophils with a size of 10-18 micrometers, an indented or kidney-shaped nucleus, pinkish-blue staining cytoplasm with secondary granules, and a nucleus:cytoplasm ratio of 1.5:1.

terms.name: Increased circulating band cell count
terms.name_zh: 血循环杆状核细胞计数升高
terms.definition: The number of band cells in the peripheral blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. Band cells are immature neutrophils with a size of 10-18 micrometers, a horseshoe-shaped nucleus with no nucleoli, light-pink staining cytoplasm with many small secondary granules, and a nucleus:cytoplasm ratio of 1:2.

terms.name: Elevated circulating E-selectin concentration
terms.definition: The concentration of E-selectin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Cervical neoplasm
terms.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the uterine cervix.

terms.name: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia
terms.definition: A precancerous condition characterized by dysplasia of the cervical epithelium. Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) 1, 2 and 3 based on its relationship with the prognosis. CIN 1 is mild dysplasia, which is mostly observed because it disappears as part of its natural course. CIN 3 includes severe dysplasia and carcinoma in situ, and management involves treatment because it is highly likely to develop into invasive cancer.

terms.name: Abnormal tissue metabolite concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a metabolite in a tissue.

terms.name: Decreased serum thromboxane B2
terms.definition: A reduction in the concentration of thromboxane B2 in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal metabolism
terms.definition: An abnormality in the function of the chemical reactions related to processes including conversion of food to enter, synthesis of proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, and carbohydrates, or the elimination of waste products.

terms.name: Persistent CMV viremia
terms.definition: Persistent or recurrent detection of cytomegalovirus (CMV) in the blood that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Persistent viremia
terms.definition: Persistence of virus in the blood circulation longer than would be normal in an immunocompetent host.

terms.name: Coccidioidomycosis
terms.definition: Infection by a Coccidioides species fungus. These are dimorphic, soil-dwelling, fungi known to cause a broad spectrum of disease, ranging from a mild febrile illness to severe pulmonary manifestations or disseminated disease. The genus Coccidioides is comprised of two genetically distinct species: Coccidioides immitis and C. posadasii.

terms.name: Acinetobacter infection
terms.definition: An infection by Acinetobacter baumannii, a Gram-negative bacillus that is aerobic, pleomorphic and non-motile. An opportunistic pathogen, A. baumannii has a high incidence among immunocompromised individuals, particularly those who have experienced a prolonged (over 90 d) hospital stay.

terms.name: Granuloma
terms.definition: A compact, organized collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes, which may be but is not necessarily accompanied by accessory features such as necrosis.

terms.name: Eosinophilic granuloma
terms.definition: A type of granuloma characterized morphologically by the predominance of Langerhans cells with characteristic grooved, folded, indented nuclei in the appropriate milieu that includes variable numbers of eosinophils and histiocytes including multinucleated forms, often appearing similar to osteoclasts or touton like giant cells, neutrophils and small lymphocytes. The concentration of the eosinophilic infiltrate varies from scattered mature cells to sheet-like masses of cells. Occasionally, areas of bone necrosis may interrupt the cellular infiltrate. The foamy cells may also be amassed in clumps, which are of no clinical significance because these clumps represent phagocytosis of lipid debris.

terms.name: Elevated circulating copper concentration
synonyms: Elevated copper cation level in blood
Increased copper cation level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of copper cation in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. This term refers to the total copper concentration.

terms.name: Opportunistic fungal infection
terms.definition: An infection that is caused by a fungus that would generally not be able to cause an infection in a host with a normal immune system. Such fungi take advantage of the opportunity, so to speak, that is provided by a weakened immune system.

terms.name: Unusual Histoplasma capsulatum infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Histoplasma capsulatum infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Histoplasma capsulatum, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Histoplasma capsulatum infection
terms.definition: Histoplasmosis infection involving multiple sites of the body. Disseminated histoplasmosis can involve various organs, including reticuloendothelial organs, gastrointestinal tract, adrenal glands, central nervous system, endovascular structures, kidney, and skin. It typically presents with systemic symptoms like fever, generalized fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and the symptoms related to the specific organ involved. Severe disseminated disease can manifest as septic shock, multi organ failure, and ARDS.

terms.name: Pulmonary histoplasmosis
terms.definition: Infection of the lungs with Histoplasma capsulatum. Symptoms may include fever, headache, weakness, chest pain and dry cough. When imaging is done, chest radiographs may show patchy pneumonia involving one or more lobes with adenopathy of the mediastinum or hilum.

terms.name: Chronic tinea infection
terms.definition: The term tinea means fungal infection, whereas dermatophyte refers to the fungal organisms that cause tinea. This term refers to a tinea infection that is chronic or recalcitrant to treatment and may be reflective of an immune defect.

terms.name: Opportunistic bacterial infection
terms.definition: An infection that is caused by a bacterium that would generally not be able to cause an infection in a host with a normal immune system. Such bacteria take advantage of the opportunity, so to speak, that is provided by a weakened immune system.

terms.name: Nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary infection
terms.definition: An infection of the lung caused by environmental mycobacteria. Such infections can occur in individuals with predisposing lung disease or immune disease.

terms.name: Pulmonary tuberculosis
terms.definition: A lung infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis a slightly curved non-motile, aerobic, non-capsulated and non-spore forming strains of mycobacteria.

terms.name: Increased blood pressure
terms.definition: Abnormal increase in blood pressure. An individual measurement of increased blood pressure does not necessarily imply hypertension. In practical terms, multiple measurements are recommended to diagnose the presence of hypertension.

terms.name: Anti-NMDA receptor antibody positivity
synonyms: Presence of anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate Receptor antibody in blood
Presence of anti-NMDAR antibody in blood
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against the NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate)-type glutamate receptor.

terms.name: CSF autoimmune antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of an antibody in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that is directed against the organism's own cells or tissues.

terms.name: CSF anti-NMDA receptor antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液抗NMDA受体抗体阳性
synonyms: Presence of NMDAR antibody in CSF
Presence of anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate Receptor antibody in CSF
Presence of anti-NMDAR antibody in cerebrospinal fluid
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against the NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate)-type glutamate receptor.

terms.name: Empty delta sign
terms.definition: This sign is created by a nonenhancing thrombus in the dural sinus surrounded by triangular enhancing dura as seen on cross-section. The sign, seen on contrast-enhanced CT scan images, suggests dural sinovenous thrombosis. It is best seen on wider window settings. It is a reliable sign of sinus thrombosis but is seen only in 25-30% of these cases.

terms.name: Dural tail sign
terms.definition: This sign represents thickening and enhancement of the dura mater in continuity with a mass, which on MR images, gives the appearance of a tail arising from the mass. The dural tail is thought to represent reactive change; however, it may also be due to tumor invasion. Three criteria need to be met for a positive dural tail sign: the tail should be seen on two successive images through the tumor, it should taper away from the tumor, and it must enhance more than the tumor.

terms.name: Lemon sign
terms.definition: The lemon sign refers to the shape of the fetal skull at ultrasonography (US) when the frontal bones lose their normal convex contour and appear flattened or inwardly scalloped. This gives the skull a shape that is said to resemble a lemon.. The sign is seen on transverse sonograms of the fetal cranium obtained at the level of the ventricles.

terms.name: Optic nerve tram-track sign
terms.definition: A tram-track sign is composed of two enhancing areas of tumor separated from each other by the negative defect of the optic nerve. It is seen on contrast-enhanced CT scan and MRI images, in optic nerve sheath meningioma. The sign helps distinguish between optic nerve sheath meningioma and optic glioma. Optic glioma arises from glial cells within the optic nerve and there is no clear separation between the nerve and the tumor; hence the tram-track sign is not seen in optic gliomas. Calcification may be seen in optic nerve sheath meningiomas in 20-50% of cases and hence the tram-track sign may be seen on nonenhanced CT scan images as a linear calcification around the nerve, but this is less common.

terms.name: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis
terms.definition: A type of tubercular infection located outside of the lung, which is the most common location of tuberculosis. There are two types of clinical manifestation of tuberculosis (TB) are pulmonary TB (PTB) and extrapulmonary TB (EPTB). The former is most common. EPTB refers to TB involving organs other than the lungs (e.g., pleura, lymph nodes, abdomen, genitourinary tract, skin, joints and bones, or meninges). A patient with both pulmonary and EPTB is classified as a case of PTB.

terms.name: Increased circulating N-acetylaspartic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环N-乙酰天冬氨酸浓度升高
synonyms: Increased circulating N-acetyl aspartic acid level
terms.definition: Concentration of N-acetylaspartic acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Increased CSF N-acetylaspartic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液N-乙酰天冬氨酸浓度升高
synonyms: Increased N-acetyl aspartate levels in CSF
Increased N-acetyl aspartic acid levels in CSF
Increased N-acetyl-L-aspartic acid levels in CSF
terms.definition: An abnormally increased concentration of N-acetylaspartic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

terms.name: Recurrent shingles
terms.definition: Repeated episodes of a localized, painful cutaneous eruption related to reactivation of varicella zoster virus (VZV) and characterized by a characteristic rash in one or two adjacent dermatomes.

terms.name: Prominent subcalcaneal fat pad
terms.definition: Abnormally increased prominence of the fat pad underneath the heal. This feature can be appreciated in figure 1 of PMID:26769062.

terms.name: 2-hydroxyglutarate aciduria
terms.definition: The concentration of 2-hydroxyglutaric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal base excess
terms.definition: Deviation from the normal quantity of base excess, defined as the amount of strong acid (in millimoles per liter) that needs to be added in vitro to 1 liter of fully oxygenated whole blood to return a blood sample to standard conditions (pH of 7.40, Pco2 of 40 mm Hg, and temperature of 37 degrees C).

terms.name: Contact dermatitis
terms.definition: An inflammatory process in skin caused by an exogenous agent that directly or indirectly injure the skin. If the offending agent is identified and removed, the eruption will resolve. An unusual or patterned eruption may be a clue to the presence of a contact dermatitis. Patch testing may be helpful in the differential diagnosis.

terms.name: Disseminated non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection
terms.name_zh: 播散性非结核分枝杆菌感染
terms.definition: Disseminated infection with non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), involving multiple organ systems that occurs in the context of immune deficiency.

terms.name: Ultra-low vision with retained motion projection
terms.definition: Ultra-low vision but with retained ability to identify a moving object (typically hand motion at distance of 30 cm).

terms.name: Ultra-low vision with retained light projection
terms.definition: Ultra-low vision but with retained ability to perceive the difference between light and dark. Also when light is projected in each of the four quadrants of the visual field, the individual is able to correctly identify the origin of the light stimulus.

terms.name: Ultra-low vision with retained light perception
terms.definition: Ultra-low vision but with retained ability to perceive the difference between light and dark.

terms.name: Ultra-low vision with no light perception
terms.definition: Ultra-low vision with complete lack of light and form perception.

terms.name: Polyclonal elevation of circulating IgG concentration
synonyms: Polyclonal elevation of circulating IgG level
terms.definition: An increase in polyclonal immunoglobulins resulting from many different plasma cells. On serum electrophoresis, a polyclonal gammopathy is characterized by a broad diffuse band with one or more heavy chains and kappa and lambda light chains.

terms.name: Oligoclonal elevation of circulating IgG concentration
synonyms: Oligoclonal elevation of circulating IgG level
terms.definition: An increase in circulating immunoglobulins characterized by two or more bands in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase in circulating immunoglobulins.

terms.name: Monoclonal elevation of circulating IgG concentration
synonyms: Monoclonal elevation of circulating IgG level
terms.definition: An increase in circulating immunoglobulins characterized by a single band in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase in circulating immunoglobulins.

terms.name: Monoclonal elevation of circulating intact IgG concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环完整IgG单克隆性升高
synonyms: Monoclonal elevation of circulating intact IgG level
terms.definition: A type of monoclonal elevation of IgG in which the involved immunoglobulin has a normal structure with a light and heavy chain.

terms.name: Monoclonal elevation of circulating IgG light chain concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环IgG轻链单克隆性升高
synonyms: Monoclonal elevation of circulating IgG light chain level
terms.definition: A type of monoclonal elevation of IgG in which the involved immunoglobulin has an abnormal structure with a light chain but not a heavy chain.

terms.name: Monoclonal elevation of circulating IgG heavy chain concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环IgG重链单克隆性升高
synonyms: Monoclonal elevation of circulating IgG heavy chain level
terms.definition: A type of monoclonal elevation of IgG in which the involved immunoglobulin has an abnormal structure with a heavy chain but not a light chain.

terms.name: Monoclonal elevation of IgG kappa chain
terms.definition: A type of monoclonal elevation of IgG in which the involved immunoglobulin has an abnormal structure with a kappa light chain but not a heavy chain.

terms.name: Monoclonal elevation of IgG lambda chain
terms.definition: A type of monoclonal elevation of IgG in which the involved immunoglobulin has an abnormal structure with a lambda light chain but not a heavy chain.

terms.name: Increased circulating IgG subclass concentration
terms.definition: An elevation of circulating IgG level predominantly related to an elevation of one of the four IgG subclasses.

terms.name: Increased circulating IgG3 concentration
terms.definition: An abnormally increased concentration of the IgG3 subtype in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Increased circulating IgG1 concentration
terms.definition: An abnormally increased concentration of the IgG1 subtype in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Increased circulating IgG2 concentration
terms.definition: An abnormally increased concentration of the IgG2 subtype in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Increased circulating IgG4 concentration
terms.definition: An abnormally increased concentration of the IgG4 subtype in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Genital warts
terms.definition: Warts affecting the skin in the genital area (penile shaft, scrotum, vagina, or labia majora). Warts can be small, beginning as a pinhead-size swelling that may become larger and take on a pedunculated appearance. Warts can spread and coalesce into large masses in the genital or anal area. Their color is variable but tends to be skin colored or darker, and they may occasionally bleed. Warts may cause itching, redness, or discomfort. An outbreak of genital warts may also cause psychological distress.

terms.name: Kappa Bence Jones proteinuria
terms.definition: The presence of free monoclonal kappa immunoglobulin light chains in the urine.

terms.name: Lambda Bence Jones proteinuria
terms.definition: The presence of free monoclonal lambda immunoglobulin light chains in the urine.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating mannose-binding protein concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环甘露糖结合蛋白浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of mannose-binding protein in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Decreased circulating mannose-binding protein concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环甘露糖结合蛋白浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of mannose-binding protein in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating mannose-binding protein concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环甘露糖结合蛋白浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of mannose-binding protein in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Increased circulating procalcitonin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环降钙素原浓度升高
terms.definition: An elevated concentration of procalcitonin in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Abnormal granulocyte count
terms.definition: Abnormal increase or decrease of absolute number of granulocytes in the blood, per microliter, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.

terms.name: Increased total granulocyte count
terms.definition: An increased count of granulocytes in the peripheral blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating globulin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环球蛋白浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of globulins in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Decreased circulating globulin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环球蛋白浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of globulins in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Frontotemporal hypertrichosis
terms.definition: Excessive, increased hair growth located in the region of the forehead and temple.

terms.name: Abnormal areolar morphology
terms.definition: An abnormal appearance or structure of the ring of pigmented skin that surrounds the nipple.

terms.name: Areolar fullness
terms.definition: The areola (ring of pigmented skin surrounding the nipple) is filled out so as to produce a rounded shape.

terms.name: Family history
terms.definition: Information about close relatives of an individual who is the proband of a study or who is being investigated with the goal of identifying a medical diagnosis. Usually, the family history includes information from three generations of relatives, including children, brothers and sisters, parents, aunts and uncles, nieces and nephews, grandparents, and cousins.

terms.name: Family history of cancer
terms.definition: A close blood relative had cancer.

terms.name: Family history of heart disease
terms.definition: A close blood relative had heart disease.

terms.name: Health status
terms.definition: Health status of a family member with respect to the disease being investigated in a proband.

terms.name: Affected
terms.definition: This term applies to a family member who is diagnosed with the same condition as the individual who is the primary focus of investigation (the proband).

terms.name: Unaffected
terms.definition: This term applies to a family member in whom the diagnosis that is the primary focus of investigation is excluded.

terms.name: Healthy
terms.definition: No history of any serious disease, including the disease being investigated in the proband.

terms.name: Periodic fever
terms.definition: Episodic fever that recurs at regular intervals.

terms.name: Non-periodic recurrent fever
terms.definition: Episodic fever that recurs at irregular intervals.

terms.name: Lacunar stroke
terms.definition: A stroke related to a small infarct (2-20 mm in diameter) in the deep cerebral white matter, basal ganglia, or pons, that is presumed to result from the occlusion of a single small perforating artery supplying the subcortical areas of the brain.

terms.name: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection
terms.name_zh: 耐甲氧西林金黄色葡萄球菌感染
terms.definition: Infection with staphylococcus aureus resistant to the antibiotic methicillin (MRSA). MRSA can infect any individual but is more common among hospitalized patients, and can also occur as an opportunistic infection.

terms.name: Interhemispheric cyst
terms.definition: Cystic collection (sac-like, fluid containing pocket of membranous tissue) located in the interhemispheric fissure, with or without communication with the ventricular system.

terms.name: Temporomandibular joint adhesion
terms.definition: Formation of one or more fibrous bands within the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) with resulting limitation of movement of the TMJ. Adhesions may be seen in degenerative processes that involve the TMJ.

terms.name: Increased urinary 11-deoxycortisol level
terms.name_zh: 尿11-脱氧皮质醇水平升高
terms.definition: An abnormally elevated concentration of 11-deoxycortisol in the urine.

terms.name: Increased urinary 11-deoxycorticosterone level
terms.name_zh: 尿11-脱氧皮质酮水平升高
terms.definition: An abnormally elevated concentration or amount of 11-deoxycorticosterone in the urine.

terms.name: Increased urinary 11-deoxytetrahydrocorticosterone level
terms.name_zh: 尿11-脱氧四氢皮质酮水平升高
terms.definition: An abnormally elevated concentration or amount of 11-deoxytetrahydrocorticosterone the urine.

terms.name: Oligoclonal elevation of circulating IgM concentration
terms.definition: An increase in circulating IgM characterized by two or more bands in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase.

terms.name: Polyclonal elevation of circulating IgA
terms.definition: A heterogeneous increase in IgA mmunoglobulins characterized by a diffuse band on serum electrophoresis.

terms.name: Oligoclonal elevation of circulating IgA
terms.definition: An increase in circulating IgA characterized by two or more bands in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase in circulating immunoglobulins.

terms.name: Monoclonal elevation of circulating IgA
terms.definition: An increase in circulating IgA characterized by one predominant band in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase in circulating immunoglobulins.

terms.name: Increased circulating specific IgE antibody concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环特异性IgE抗体浓度升高

terms.name: Monoclonal elevated circulating IgE concentration
terms.definition: An increase in circulating IgE characterized by one predominant band in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase in circulating immunoglobulins.

terms.name: Oligoclonal elevated circulating IgE concentration
terms.definition: An increase in circulating IgE characterized by two or more bands in serum electrophoresis but not the broad diffuse band that characterizes a polyclonal increase in circulating immunoglobulins.

terms.name: Polyclonal elevated circulating IgE concentration
terms.definition: A heterogeneous increase in IgE mmunoglobulins characterized by a diffuse band on serum electrophoresis.

terms.name: Reduced forced vital capacity
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can expel following maximal inspiration.

terms.name: Reduced forced expiratory volume in one second
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can forcefully expel in one second.

terms.name: Upslanting toenail
terms.definition: Upturned concavity of toenails.

terms.name: Elevated circulating CA19-9 concentration
synonyms: Elevated circulating sialylated Lewis a antigen concentration
terms.definition: The concentration of carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. CA 19-9, also known as sialyl Lewis A, is a tetrasaccharide overexpressed on a wide range of cancerous cells. CA 19-9 is a tumor-associated carbohydrate antigen (TACAs) that is both a local (anchored on cell surface or tumor site) and shed (in systemic circulation) antigen. CA 19-9 is expressed at low levels in normal tissues but overexpressed in cancer cells.

terms.name: Cutaneous lichen amyloidosis
terms.name_zh: 皮肤苔藓样淀粉样变性
terms.definition: Lichen amyloidosis presents with multiple localized or rarely generalized, hyperpigmented grouped papules with a predilection for the shins, calves, ankles, and dorsa of the feet and thighs.

terms.name: Cutaneous macular amyloidosis
terms.definition: A type of cutaneous amyloidosis that is characterized by hyperpigmented patches with indefinite margins composed of grayish brown macules, often with a reticulated or rippled appearance.

terms.name: Cutaneous nodular amyloidosis
terms.name_zh: 皮肤结节状淀粉样变性
terms.definition: A type of cutaneous amyloidosis that is characterized clinically by waxy, purpuric plaques and nodules and histologically by amyloid deposits in the dermis and subcutaneous tissue.

terms.name: Serinuria
terms.definition: A increased concentration of serine in the urine.

terms.name: Sulfocysteinuria
terms.definition: A increased concentration of sulfocysteine in the urine.

terms.name: Phenylalaninuria
synonyms: Increased level of phenylalanine in urine
terms.definition: Increased level of phenylalanine in urine.

terms.name: Methioninuria
terms.definition: Level of methionine in urine above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Leucinuria
terms.definition: Increased level of leucine in urine.

terms.name: Decreased peak expiratory flow
terms.definition: A reduction in the maximum expiratory flow per minute, which can be used to measure how fast a subject can exhale as well as to judge the strength of the expiratory muscles and the condition of the large airways.

terms.name: Decreased pre-bronchodilator forced vital capacity
terms.name_zh: 支气管扩张剂前用力肺活量降低
synonyms: Decreased pre bronchodilator forced vital capacity
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can expel following maximal insipiration, with the test being performed before the administration of a bronchodilating medication.

terms.name: Decreased post-bronchodilator forced vital capacity
terms.name_zh: 支气管扩张剂后用力肺活量降低
synonyms: Decreased post bronchodilator forced vital capacity
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can expel following maximal insipiration, with the test being performed after the administration of a bronchodilating medication.

terms.name: Decreased post-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second
terms.name_zh: 支气管扩张剂后一秒用力呼气容积降低
synonyms: Decreased post bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second
Decreased postbronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can forcefully expel in one second, with the test being performed after the administration of a bronchodilating medication.

terms.name: Decreased forced expiratory flow 25-75%
terms.definition: A reduction compared to the predicted value of the forced expiratory flow over the middle one-half of the FVC; the average flow from the point at which 25% of the FVC has been exhaled to the point at which 75% of the FVC has been exhaled.

terms.name: Decreased pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25-75%
terms.name_zh: 支气管扩张剂前用力呼气流量25-75%降低
synonyms: Decreased pre bronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25-75%
terms.definition: A reduction compared to the predicted value of the forced expiratory flow over the middle one-half of the FVC; the average flow from the point at which 25% of the FVC has been exhaled to the point at which 75% of the FVC has been exhaled. Here, the test is performed before the administration of a bronchodilating medication.

terms.name: Decreased post-bronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25-75%
terms.name_zh: 支气管扩张剂后用力呼气流量25-75%降低
synonyms: Decreased post bronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25-75%
terms.definition: A reduction compared to the predicted value of the forced expiratory flow over the middle one-half of the FVC; the average flow from the point at which 25% of the FVC has been exhaled to the point at which 75% of the FVC has been exhaled. Here, the test is performed after the administration of a bronchodilating medication.

terms.name: Increased circulating corticosterone level
terms.name_zh: 血循环皮质酮水平升高
terms.definition: An abnormally elevated concentration of corticosterone in the blood.

terms.name: Decreased circulating corticosterone level
terms.name_zh: 血循环皮质酮水平降低
terms.definition: An abnormally reduced concentration of corticosterone in the blood.

terms.name: Exacerbated by aspirin exposure
terms.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by ingestion of aspirin.

terms.name: Positive direct antiglobulin test
terms.definition: A positive result of the direct antiglobulin test (DAT), a method of demonstrating the presence of antibody or complement bound to red blood cell (RBC) membranes by the use of anti-human globulin to form a visible agglutination reaction.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating growth hormone concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环生长激素浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal level of growth hormone (GH) in the blood circulation. GH or somatotropin is a peptide hormone that stimulates growth, cell reproduction, and cell regeneration. Its secretion from the pituitary is regulated by the neurosecretory nuclei of the hypothalamus, which can release Growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH or somatocrinin) and Growth hormone-inhibiting hormone (GHIH or somatostatin) into the hypophyseal portal venous blood surrounding the pituitary. GH is secreted in a pulsatile manner, which is one of the reasons why an isolated measurement of its blood concentration is not meaningful.

terms.name: Acidemia
terms.definition: An abnormally low blood pH (usually defined as less than 7.35).

terms.name: Alkalemia
terms.definition: An abnormally high blood pH (usually defined as 7.41 or above).

terms.name: Blood group A
terms.definition: ABO phenotype A, corresponding to the genotype AO or AA.

terms.name: Isoleucinuria
terms.definition: An increased concentration of isoleucine in the urine.

terms.name: Increased peripheral blast count
terms.name_zh: 外周血原始细胞计数升高
terms.definition: An increased count in the peripheral blood of cells that are precursors to mature circulating blood cells such as neutrophiles, monocytes, lymphocutes, and erythrocytes. Blasts are not usually found in significant numbers in the peripheral blood circulation, but can be observed in hematopoietic neoplasms such as leukemia, severe infections, and as a result of certain medications.

terms.name: Duffy blood group
terms.definition: The Duffy blood group system is based on the presence of a glycoprotein termed Fy that is on the surface of erythrocytes and some other cells. There are two Duffy antigens named Fya and Fyb, and thus there are four Duffy phenotypes: a+b+, a+b-, a-b+,a-b-.

terms.name: Duffy Fya positivity
terms.definition: Presence of the Duffy Fya antigen.

terms.name: Duffy Fyb positivity
terms.definition: Presence of the Duffy Fyb antigen.

terms.name: Anti-beta 2 glycoprotein I antibody positivity
terms.definition: Presence of antibodies against beta 2 glycoprotein I in the circulation. Beta-2 glycoprotein I (beta2GPI) is the principal target of autoantibodies in the antiphospholipid syndrome (APS).

terms.name: Increased urinary orosomucoid
terms.definition: An increased concentration in the urine of alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP), also known as orosomucoid (ORM). AGP is a 41-43-kDa glycoprotein with a pI of 2.8-3.8. AGP is an acute-phase protein that has many activities including, but not limited to, acting as an acute-phase reactant and disease marker, modulating immunity, binding and carrying drugs, maintaining the barrier function of capillary, and mediating the sphingolipid metabolism.

terms.name: Immediate-type hypersensitivity drug reaction
terms.definition: Hypersensitivity that is observed within 1 hr of exposures. A variety of adverse reactions can occur within minutes to hours of exposure to a drug. Some can be related to the pharmacological action of the drug (WHO Adverse Reaction Terminology type A for augmented) and usually have a low mortality. Others are not readily predictable based on the structure and pharmacological action of the drug and have a relatively high mortality risk (Type B for bizarre). The most serious form of immediate onset drug hypersensitivity reaction, anaphylaxis. Other reactions including itching, dizziness/light-headedness, nausea, chest discomfort but without any objective skin features, physical signs or physiological compromise. Skin only reactions include generalized erythema, urticaria or angioedema without any sentinel features (see below) of other organ involvement.

terms.name: Polymorphous light eruption
terms.definition: The cardinal symptom is severely pruritic skin lesions. Macular, papular, papulovesicular, urticarial, multiforme- and plaque-like variants are differentiated morphologically, hence the name polymorphous. Usually one morphology dominates in a single individual (monomorphous). The skin lesions develop a few hours to several days after sun exposure. Initially, patchy erythema develops, accompanied by pruritus. Distinct lesions then develop. The upper chest, upper arms, backs of the hands, thighs, and the sides of the face are the primary localizations. The skin lesions resolve spontaneously within several days of ceasing sun exposure and do not leave behind any traces.

terms.name: Hydroa vacciniforme
synonyms: Acute vesiculation and crusting and scarring following sun exposure
terms.definition: In response to the spring sun distinct inflamed reddened skin develops on the ears, nose, cheeks, fingers, backs of the hands, and the lower arms, on which blisters with serous or hemorrhagic content develop. These dry out with the formation of a blackish scab. After shedding of the scab, depressed, varioliform, often hypopigmented scars remain. In addition, hyper- and hypopigmentation are present together, resulting in a polymorphous skin presentation.

terms.name: Uniparental disomy
terms.definition: Inheritance of both homologues of a chromosome pair from the same parent.

terms.name: Uniparental heterodisomy
terms.definition: A type of uniparental disomy in which the two different chromosomes (or chromosome segments) of the same parent are transmitted.

terms.name: Uniparental isodisomy
terms.definition: A type of uniparental disomy in which the two identical chromosomes (or chromosome segments) of the same parent are transmitted.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating transferrin concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环转铁蛋白浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of transferrin in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating transferrin concentration
terms.definition: The concentration of transferrin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Decreased circulating transferrin concentration
terms.definition: The concentration of transferrin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Periventricular nodular heterotopia
terms.definition: Nodules of heterotopia along the ventricular walls. There can be a single nodule or a large number of nodules, they can exist on either or both sides of the brain at any point along the higher ventricle margins, they can be small or large, single or multiple.

terms.name: Periventricular laminar heterotopia
terms.definition: A large mass of heterotopia in a laminar configuration along the ventricular walls. Usually bilateral.

terms.name: Periventricular ribbonlike heterotopia
terms.definition: Heterotopia that forms a continuous wavy line along the ventricular wall.

terms.name: Subcortical heterotopia
terms.definition: A form of heterotopia were the mislocalized gray matter is located deep within the white matter.

terms.name: Nodular subcortical heterotopia in peritrigonal regions
terms.definition: Solid nodular heterotopia situated in the region of the peritrigonal optic pathway posterior to the deep gray nuclei.

terms.name: Diffuse ribbon-like subcortical heterotopia
terms.name_zh: 弥漫性带状皮质下异位
terms.definition: Subcortical heterotopia consisting of a bilateral and symmetric single continuous, undulating ribbon-like layer of gray matter located in the frontal, parietal and occipital lobes. It has no visible connection to the overlying cortex.

terms.name: Mesial parasagittal subcortical heterotopia
terms.name_zh: 近中线矢状旁皮质下异位
terms.definition: Subcortical heterotopia extending along the mesial aspect of the lateral ventricles, with direct connection to mesial polymicrogyria-like cortex at the anterior and posterior limits of the heterotopia.

terms.name: Curvilinear subcortical heterotopia
terms.definition: Large subcortical heterotopia of variable morphology with streaks and swirls. These always connect to the overlying cortex in at least one, but usually in multiple, locations. Spaces with the signal intensity of CSF are usually seen within the heterotopia.

terms.name: Transmantle columnar heterotopia
terms.definition: Linear heterotopia spanning from the cerebral mantle from the pia to the ependyma.

terms.name: Citrullinuria
terms.definition: The amount of citrulline in the urine, when normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Dysgyria
terms.definition: An abnormal gyral pattern characterized by abnormalities of sulcal depth or orientation.

terms.name: Dysgyria with normal cortical thickness
terms.name_zh: 皮质厚度正常型脑回发育不良
terms.definition: An abnormal gyral pattern characterized by abnormalities of sulcal depth or orientation but with a normal thickness of the cortex.

terms.name: Dysgyria with thickened cortex
terms.name_zh: 皮质增厚型脑回发育不良
