terms.definition: Increased caliber of a bronchial artery, which can be defined as a bronchial artery diameter that exceeds 2 mm.

terms.name: Bronchial artery hypertrophy
terms.definition: Increase in the volume of bronchial artery wall due to the enlargement of its component cells.

terms.name: Perivascular pre-capillary pulmonary artery inflammation
synonyms: Perivascular inflammation of arterioles in the pulmonary circulation
Perivascular inflammation of pre-capillary pulmonary arteries
terms.definition: Inflammatory cell infiltration surrounding precapillary pulmonary arteries (arterioles; 20-70 micrometer).

terms.name: Irregularly shaped sperm tail
terms.definition: Irregular or changing caliber (diameter) along the tail of the sperm.

terms.name: Anti-carbonic anhydrase II antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against carbonic anhydrase II.

terms.name: Antilactoferrin antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against lactoferrin.

terms.name: Glomerular extracapillary fibrin
terms.name_zh: 肾小球毛细血管外纤维蛋白
terms.definition: Presence of ropey, eosinophilic material (brght red on Trichrome staining) consistent with extracapillary fibrin outside of capillary lumina.

terms.name: Bowman-space proteinaceous debris
terms.definition: The presence of eosinophilic Periodic Acid Schiff (PAS)-positive cell free, protein-derived material occupying Bowman's space.

terms.name: Pleural plaque
terms.definition: Deposits of hyalinized collagen fibers in the parietal pleura (preferentially pleura adjacent to ribs, particularly the sixth through ninth ribs).

terms.name: Persistent fever
terms.definition: Fever that persists longer than expected for an acute infectious disease. No precise threshold exists, and the clinical interpretation of fever is context-dependent, but as a rule of thumb, this term refers to fever that persists longer than 2-3 weeks.

terms.name: Acute abdomen
terms.definition: A sudden onset of abdominal pain with associated nausea or vomiting. The acute abdomen may be caused by an infection, inflammation, vascular occlusion, or obstruction.

terms.name: Tissue ischemia
terms.definition: Ischemia is defined as a restriction of arterial blood supply to a tissue associated with insufficient oxygenation to support the metabolis requirements of the tissue. Depending on the involved tissues, clinical manifestations may include pain, pallor, lack of pulse, coldness, paresthesia, and paralysis. Additional associated manifestations include hemodynamic parameters (reduced blood pressure distal to the site of restricted arterial supply) and angiographic evidence of arterial occclusion.

terms.name: Digital ischemia
terms.definition: Restriction of arterial blood supply to a digit (finger or toe) associated with insufficient oxygenation to support the metabolic requirements of the digit. Clinical manifestations may include pain, pallor, lack of pulse, coldness, paresthesia, and paralysis.

terms.name: Testicular ischemia
terms.definition: Restriction of arterial blood supply to a testis associated with insufficient oxygenation to support the metabolic requirements of the tissue. Clinical manifestations may include pain and swelling of the affected testis.

terms.name: Intestinal ischemia
terms.definition: Restriction of arterial blood supply to the intestine associated with insufficient oxygenation to support the metabolic requirements of the tissue. Acute intestinal ischemia can involve the small or large intestine, and usually presents with sudden severe non-specific abdominal pain.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating organic amino compound concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环有机氨基化合物浓度异常
synonyms: Abnormal circulating organic amino compound concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of organic amino compound in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating phosphoethanolamine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血磷酸乙醇胺浓度升高
terms.definition: An increased concentration of o-phosphoethanolamine in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated urine acetoacetic acid level
terms.definition: Elevated amount of acetoacetic acid in the urine.

terms.name: Elevated circulating acetoacetic acid concentration
terms.definition: An increased level of acetoacetic acid in the blood circulation. Acetoacetic acid is one of the predominant ketone bodies.

terms.name: Elevated urinary 2-hydroxybutyric acid
terms.definition: An increased amount of 2-hydroxybutyric acid in the urine.

terms.name: Elevated circulating cartilage oligomeric matrix protein concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环软骨寡聚基质蛋白浓度升高
synonyms: Elevated cartilage oligomeric matrix protein concentration
Elevated cartilage oligomeric matrix protein level
Elevated cartilage oligomeric matrix protein level in blood
Elevated circulating cartilage oligomeric matrix protein concentration
Increased cartilage oligomeric matrix protein concentration
Increased cartilage oligomeric matrix protein level
Increased cartilage oligomeric matrix protein level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of cartilage oligomeric matrix protein in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Lower extremity akinesia
terms.definition: Inability to initiate changes in activity or movement and to perform ordinary volitional movements rapidly and easily in the lower extremities.

terms.name: Upper extremity akinesia
terms.definition: Inability to initiate changes in activity or movement and to perform ordinary volitional movements rapidly and easily in the upper extremities.

terms.name: Upper extremity hypokinesia
terms.definition: Abnormally diminished movement of the upper extremities. In contrast to paralysis, hypokinesia is not characterized by a lack of motor strength, but rather by a poverty of movement. The typical habitual movements (e.g., folding the arms, crossing the legs) are reduced in frequency.

terms.name: Lower extremity hypokinesia
terms.definition: Abnormally diminished movement of the lower extremities. In contrast to paralysis, hypokinesia is not characterized by a lack of motor strength, but rather by a poverty of movement. The typical habitual movements (e.g., folding the arms, crossing the legs) are reduced in frequency.

terms.name: Cardiac tamponade
terms.definition: The accumulation of pericardial fluid with subsequent compression of all cardiac chambers which prevents cardiac filling.

terms.name: Hip adductor weakness
terms.definition: Reduced ability to bring the leg toward the midline of the body.

terms.name: Elevated circulating hydroxybutyric acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环羟丁酸浓度升高
terms.definition: An increased concentration in the blood circulation of a hydroxybutyric acid, that is, of a compound comprising a butyric acid core carrying at least one hydroxy substituent.

terms.name: Elevated circulating 2-hydroxybutyric acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环2-羟基丁酸浓度升高
terms.definition: Elevation of the 2-hydroxybutyric acid concentration in the blood above the normal range.

terms.name: Elevated circulating 3-hydroxybutyric acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环3-羟基丁酸浓度升高
terms.definition: Elevation of the 3-hydroxybutyric acid concentration in the blood above the normal range.

terms.name: Pulmonary arterial plexiform lesion
terms.definition: Focal proliferation of pulmonary artery endothelial cells, leading to the formation of complex capillary-like channels.

terms.name: Pulmonary artery intimal thickening
terms.definition: Increased thickness of the intimal layer of the pulmonary artery. Throughout the pulmonary arterial tree, the thin intima consists of a non-fenestrated monolayer of endothelial cells lining the vessel lumen, as well as a sub-endothelial interstitium that extends to the internal elastic lamina. Intimal thickness in human lung ranges from 1-16% of total wall thickness. Pulmonary artery intimal thickening can be defined as a relative intima thickness to the thickness of the vessel wall of over 10%.

terms.name: Pulmonary artery adventitial fibrosis
terms.definition: Increased amount of collagen, proteoglycans, and other extracellular matrix proteins resulting in scarring and thickening in the adventia of the pulmonary arterial tree.

terms.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension with positive acute response to NO challenge
terms.definition: A form of pulmonary arterial hypertension in which there is a reduction of mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) at least 10 mmHg to reach an absolute value of mPAP not more than 40 mmHg with an increased or unchanged cardiac output (CO) in response to inhaled nitric oxide at 10-20 ppm.

terms.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension with lack of acute response to NO challenge
terms.definition: A form of pulmonary arterial hypertension with lack of adequate hemodynamic response to NO challenge (adequate response is defined as a reduction of mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) of at least 10 mmHg to reach an absolute value of mPAP 40 mmHg or less with an increased or unchanged cardiac output (CO) in response to inhaled nitric oxide at 10-20 ppm).

terms.name: Periungual erythema
terms.definition: Erythema (redness of the skin caused by hyperemia in superficial capillaries) in the region surrounding a fingernail or toe nail.

terms.name: Pulmonary air embolism
terms.definition: Venous air embolism is a consequence of air being introduced into the venous circulation, and subsequently to the right heart, and pulmonary circulation. When small amounts of air reach pulmonary circulation they can be removed by gas diffusion across the arteriolar wall into the alveoli, amounts of gas exceeding 50 ml can cause pulmonary outflow tract obstruction with or without concomitant arterial embolisation.

terms.name: Pulmonary capillary angioectasia
terms.definition: Focal accumulation of dilated pulmonary capillaries.

terms.name: Systemic autoinflammation
terms.definition: Dysregulation of the innate immune system characterized by systemic pathobiology, i.e., with symptoms that can affect the entire body.

terms.name: Neuroinflammation
terms.definition: Activation of the brain's innate immune system in response to an inflammatory challenge and is characterized by a host of cellular and molecular changes within the brain.

terms.name: Non-infectious meningitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the layers of tissue that cover the brain and spinal cord (meninges) and of the fluid-filled space between the meninges (subarachnoid space) when it is caused by disorders that are not infections or by drugs or vaccines.

terms.name: Cytomegalovirus colitis
terms.definition: Infection and inflammation of the colon caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Ileocecal ulcer
terms.definition: An erosion of the mucous membrane in the region connecting the ileum and cecum.

terms.name: Nasal septum perforation
terms.definition: A full-thickness defect of the nasal septum.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating keto acid concentration
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a keto acid (also called ketoacid or oxo carboxylic acid) in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating 3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环3-甲基-2-氧代戊酸浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of 3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acidin the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 血4-甲基-2-氧代戊酸浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating myoglobin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环肌红蛋白浓度升高
terms.definition: An increased blood concentration of myoglobin.

terms.name: Elevated circulating decenoylcarnitine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环癸烯酰肉碱浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of decenoylcarnitine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating octenoylcarnitine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血辛烯酰肉碱浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of O-octenoylcarnitine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating hexanoylcarnitine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环己酰肉碱浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of hexanoylcarnitine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating glutarylcarnitine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环戊二酰肉碱浓度升高
terms.definition: Concentration of glutarylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating propionylcarnitine concentration
terms.definition: The concentration of propionylcarnitine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating dodecanoylcarnitine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环十二烷酰肉碱浓度升高
terms.definition: Concentration of dodecanoylcarnitine (C12:0) in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Reduced circulating acylcarnitine concentration
terms.definition: An abnormally reduced concentration in the blood circulation of acylcarnitine, which is produced by reversible esterification of the 3-hydroxyl group of carnitine.

terms.name: Elevated circulating butyrylcarnitine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环丁酰肉碱浓度升高
terms.definition: Concentration of O-butyrylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating isovalerylcarnitine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环异戊酰肉碱浓度升高
terms.definition: Concentration of O-isovalerylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Increased mid-arm muscle circumference
terms.definition: Elevation of the midupper arm circumference midway between the acromion and olecranon processes of the ulna with the use of a steel or fiberglass tape. This measure is a proxy for the muscle mass of the upper arm and can be used as a part of the assessment of nutritional status in children.

terms.name: Decreased mid-arm muscle circumference
terms.definition: Reduction of the midupper arm circumference midway between the acromion and olecranon processes of the ulna with the use of a steel or fiberglass tape. This measure is a proxy for the muscle mass of the upper arm and can be used as a part of the assessment of nutritional status in children.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating prealbumin concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环前白蛋白浓度异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of prealbumin in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating prealbumin concentration
terms.definition: The concentration of prealbumin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Limited neck extension
terms.definition: Reduced ability to move the head back towards the ceiling so that one is looking upwards.

terms.name: Tube feeding
terms.definition: Feeding problem necessitating food and nutrient delivery via a tube.

terms.name: Elevated urine keto acid level
terms.definition: Increased amount of a keta acid in the urine.

terms.name: Elevated urine 3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid level
terms.name_zh: 尿3-甲基-2-氧代戊酸水平升高
terms.definition: Increased amount of 3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid in the urine.

terms.name: Elevated urine 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoic acid level
terms.name_zh: 尿4-甲基-2-氧代戊酸水平升高
terms.definition: Increased amount of 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoic acid in the urine.

terms.name: Decreased circulating apolipoprotein concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环载脂蛋白浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of apolipoprotein in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating apolipoprotein concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环载脂蛋白浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of apolipoprotein in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating 3-hydroxylinoleylcarnitine concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环3-羟基亚油酰肉碱浓度升高
terms.definition: Increased concentration of 3-hydroxylinoleylcarnitine in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating oleylcarnitine concentration
terms.definition: Increased concentration of oleylcarnitine in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating 3-hydroxypalmitoleylcarnitine concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环3-羟基棕榈油酰肉碱浓度升高
terms.definition: Concentration of 3-hydroxypalmitoleylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating tetradecanoylcarnitine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血十四烷酰肉碱浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of tetradecanoylcarnitine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Weak grip
terms.definition: Reduced grip strength. Gripping is the motion by which the hand tightly grasps an object or other hand.

terms.name: Low 10-minute APGAR score
terms.definition: A normal APGAR score can be coded as 'not Low 10-minute APGAR score'.

terms.name: Limited shoulder abduction
terms.definition: Decreased ability to move the arm away from the midline of the body.

terms.name: Extractable nuclear antigen positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against extractable nuclear components that are referred to as extractable because they can be extracted from cell nuclei with saline solution.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating lipoprotein lipase concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环脂蛋白脂酶浓度异常
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of lipoprotein lipase in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Increased circulating lipoprotein lipase concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环脂蛋白脂酶浓度升高
terms.definition: Increased concentration of lipoprotein lipase in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Hypobilirubinemia
terms.definition: Concentration of bilirubin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Limited lateral neck flexion
terms.definition: Reduced range of motion resulting in decreased ability to move the ear toward the top of the shoulder.

terms.name: Limited shoulder flexion
terms.definition: A reduced ability to flex the shoulder. Shoulder flexion is the motion that moves the arms from a resting position by the side of the body to a position above the head.

terms.name: Podocyte infolding
terms.definition: Folding of cytoplasmic processes of podocytes into the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) with thickening of the lamina densa and microspheres and/or microtubular structures within the GBM.

terms.name: Elevated circulating linoleylcarnitine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环亚油酰肉碱浓度升高
terms.definition: Increased concentration of linoleylcarnitine in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Glomerular basement membrane disruption
synonyms: Disruption of the glomerular basement membrane
terms.definition: A point of rupture in the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) where the discontinuous portions of GBM are still identifiable with a basement membrane stain such as Periodic acid Schiff (PAS) or silver.

terms.name: Abnormal glomerular basement membrane texture
terms.name_zh: 肾小球基底膜质地异常
terms.definition: Anomalous appearance or structure of the surface of the glomerular basement membrane.

terms.name: Glomerular basement membranes powdery deposit
terms.name_zh: 肾小球基底膜粉末状沉积
synonyms: Glomerular basement membranes with powdery deposit
terms.definition: Punctate electron-dense material typically in a band-like distribution along the lamina rara interna and within tubular basement membranes within the subendothelial aspect of the glomerular basement membrane.

terms.name: Glomerular endocapillary leukocyte hypercellularity
terms.name_zh: 肾小球毛细血管内白细胞增多
synonyms: Glomerular endocapillary hypercellularity consisting of leukocytes
terms.definition: Increased number of leukocytes internal to the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), but not limited to within glomerular capillaries.

terms.name: Glomerular endocapillary neutrophil hypercellularity
terms.name_zh: 肾小球毛细血管内中性粒细胞增多
terms.definition: Increased number of neutrophils internal to the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), but not limited to within glomerular capillaries.

terms.name: Glomerular endocapillary foam-cell hypercellularity
terms.name_zh: 肾小球毛细血管内泡沫细胞增多
terms.definition: Presence of lipid-filled cells, often a macrophage, with a vacuolated appearance in the glomerulus often occupying the endocapillary space.

terms.name: Global mesangial sclerosis
terms.definition: A generalized global (over 80%) increase of mesangial matrix that is present throughout the mesangial stalk (with or without associated mesangial hypercellularity).

terms.name: Podocyte cytoskeletal condensation
terms.definition: Reorganization of podocyte cytoskeletal proteins at the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) aspect of the cell, with associated cytoplasmic electron density at the GBM aspect of the podocyte.

terms.name: Mesangial matrix expansion
terms.definition: Increased mesangial extracellular material with interspace width of over 2 mesangial cell nuclei, in one or more peripheral mesangial areas.

terms.name: Glomerular basement membrane amyloid spicule
terms.name_zh: 肾小球基底膜淀粉样刺突
terms.definition: Amyloid spicules are projections of typically silver-positive material from the outer aspect of the glomerular capillary wall, perpendicular to the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), most often caused by amyloidosis with the latter confirmed by additional stains.

terms.name: Segmental glomerulosclerosis
terms.definition: Segmental solidification of the glomerular tuft by increased extracellular matrix, causing glomerular capillary obliteration and can include hyalinosis, foam cells, hypertrophy of overlying glomerular epithelial cells, podocyte depletion, halo and adhesion of the tuft to the Bowman capsule.

terms.name: Perihilar segmental glomerulosclerosis
terms.definition: Segmental solidification of the glomerular tuft by increased extracellular matrix, causing glomerular capillary obliteration is present at the vascular pole, involving less than 50% of the tuft. It can be accompanied by other descriptors such as hyalinosis, foam cells, hypertrophy of overlying glomerular epithelial cells, podocyte depletion, halo and adhesion of the tuft to the Bowman's capsule.

terms.name: Tip variant segmental glomerulosclerosis
terms.definition: Segmental solidification of the glomerular tuft characterized by an adhesion at the tip of the glomerular tuft abutting the proximal tubular taek-off can be accompanied by increased extracellular matrix, causing glomerular capillary obliteration at the glomerular tip. Features including hyalinosis, foam cells, hypertrophy of overlying glomerular epithelial cells can also be observed.

terms.name: Segmental glomerulosclerosis away from the vascular and tubular poles
terms.definition: Segmental solidification of the glomerular tuft characterized by increased extracellular matrix, causing glomerular capillary obliteration at neither the tubular or vascular poles. Features including hyalinosis, foam cells, hypertrophy of overlying glomerular epithelial cells can also be observed.

terms.name: Glomerular basement membrane electron dense deposits
terms.name_zh: 肾小球基底膜电子致密沉积
terms.definition: Electron-dense deposits in the lamina densa with a ribbon or a sausage structure.

terms.name: Subendothelial glomerular basement membrane electron dense deposits
terms.definition: Electron dense deposits in the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) subendothelial space associated with a prominent GBM reflecting an increase in thickness. This feature can be associated with GBM remodeling along the endothelial aspect.

terms.name: Subepithelial glomerular basement membrane electron dense deposits
terms.definition: Prominent glomerular basement membrane (GBM) reflecting a diffuse and relatively uniform increase in thickness (subjective estimate) with exogenous material deposited between the outer (epithelial) aspect of the GBM and the visceral epithelial cell, with varying degrees of incorporation into the GBM.

terms.name: Abnormal esterified to free carnitine ratio
terms.name_zh: 酯化/游离肉碱比值异常
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal ratio of acylcarnitine (i.e., esterified carnitine) to free carnitine.

terms.name: Elevated CSF fumarate concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液延胡索酸浓度升高
terms.definition: An increased concentration of fumarate, an intermediate in the citric acid cycle, in the cebrebrospinal fluid.

terms.name: Elevated circulating fumarate concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环富马酸浓度升高
terms.definition: An increased concentration of fumarate, an intermediate in the citric acid cycle, in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Livedo reticularis
terms.definition: Livedo reticularis is characterized by the presence of a bluish purple, mottled or netlike pattern in unbroken circles on the skin. Exposure to cold environments usually intensifies the vascular pattern. Presumably, the condition results from slow or stagnant blood flow, vessel-wall pathology, and decreased oxygen tension.

terms.name: Increased esterified to free carnitine ratio
terms.name_zh: 酯化/游离肉碱比值升高
terms.definition: An elevated ratio of acylcarnitine (i.e., esterified carnitine) to free carnitine.

terms.name: Decreased esterified to free carnitine ratio
terms.name_zh: 酯化/游离肉碱比值降低
terms.definition: A reduced ratio of acylcarnitine (i.e., esterified carnitine) to free carnitine.

terms.name: EBV meningitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the meninges related to infection by Epstein-Barr virus.

terms.name: EBV encephalitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the brain related to infection by Epstein-Barr virus.

terms.name: Cutaneous horn
terms.definition: A cutaneous horn is a keratinized non-malignant protrusion on the surface of the skin. Diagnosis is established by biopsy of the horn and biopsy of the horn and the underlying skin.

terms.name: Addictive substance use
terms.definition: Chronic compulsive drug seeking and continued use despite harmful consequences.

terms.name: Addictive stimulant use
terms.definition: Addiction to a stimulant drug is defined as a drug that typically increases alertness, attention, and energy while also elevating blood pressure, heart rate, and breathing.

terms.name: Addictive cocaine use
terms.definition: Addiction to cocaine.

terms.name: Addictive amphetamine use
terms.definition: Addiction to amphetamine or dextroamphetamine is a serious concern.

terms.name: Addictive opioid use
terms.name_zh: 阿片类物质成瘾性使用
terms.definition: Addiction to opioids.

terms.name: Addictive benzodiazepine use
terms.name_zh: 成瘾性苯二氮䓬类药物使用
terms.definition: Addiction to a benzodiazepine.

terms.name: Addictive heroin use
terms.definition: Addiction to heroin.

terms.name: Addictive methylphenidate use
terms.definition: Addiction to methylphenidate.

terms.name: Addictive methamphetamine use
terms.name_zh: 甲基苯丙胺成瘾性使用
terms.definition: Addiction to methamphetamine.

terms.name: Paradoxical embolism
terms.definition: Paradoxical embolism describes the passage of a venous or right-sided cardiac thrombus into the arterial or systemic circulation.

terms.name: Nasal dryness
terms.definition: A lack of humidification of the nasal mucosa.

terms.name: Cerebral cavernous malformation
terms.definition: A cerebral cavernous malformation (also known as cavernoma, cavernous angioma, cavernous hemangioma) is a collection of structurally abnormal slow-flow capillaries predominantly in the central nervous system. These are multiple mulberry-like distended caverns of dilated thin-walled capillaries without the normal intervening brain parenchymal architecture. Often, individual cavernomas are surrounded by hemosiderin representing remote oozing due to the abnormal capillaries.

terms.name: Abnormal sperm principal piece morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the part of the sperm flagellum that is distal to the sperm midpiece and mitochondrial sheath and which leads into the end piece.

terms.name: Abnormal sperm axoneme morphology
terms.definition: Abnormal structure of the sperm axonemal structure which consists of a ring of nine microtubular doublets and a central pair of microtubules, giving the classical 9+2 microtubular arrangement. The axoneme contains a central pair of microtubules (C1 and C2) that are connected by a bridge-like structure forming the central pair complex (CPC). Each of the nine outer doublets is composed of type A and B microtubules and connected by radial spokes to the CPC.

terms.name: Absent sperm axoneme central pair complex
terms.name_zh: 精子轴丝中央对复合体缺失
terms.definition: Absence of the central pair of microtubules in the sperm axoneme, thereby forming a 9+0 pattern instead of the normal 9+2 pattern.

terms.name: Limited ankle dorsiflexion
terms.definition: Reduced ability to move the foot up toward the shin.

terms.name: Decreased gonadotropin-stimulated testosterone-to-androstenedione ratio
terms.name_zh: 促性腺激素刺激的睾酮/雄烯二酮比值降低
terms.definition: A reduced amount of testosterone relative in androstenedione in the blood circulation following administration of hCG (Human Chorionic Gonadotropin).

terms.name: Abnormal cardiac output
terms.definition: A deviation from normal Cardiac output, which is defined as the amount of blood pumped by the heart minute and is the mechanism whereby blood flows around the body, especially providing blood flow to the brain and other vital organs.

terms.name: Abnormal cardiac index
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal value of the cardiac index, defined as cardiac output divided by body surface area.

terms.name: Increased cardiac index
terms.definition: An elevated cardiac index, defined as cardiac output divided by body surface area.

terms.name: Decreased cardiac index
terms.definition: A reduced cardiac index, defined as cardiac output divided by body surface area.

terms.name: Decreased cardiac output
terms.definition: A decreased volume of blood pumped by the left and right ventricle, per unit time. Cardiac output (CO) is the product of the heart rate (HR), i.e. the number of heartbeats per minute (bpm), and the stroke volume (SV), which is the volume of blood pumped from the ventricle per beat.

terms.name: Increased cardiac output
terms.definition: An increased volume of blood pumped by the left and right ventricle, per unit time. Cardiac output (CO) is the product of the heart rate (HR), i.e. the number of heartbeats per minute (bpm), and the stroke volume (SV), which is the volume of blood pumped from the ventricle per beat.

terms.name: Increased circulating brain natriuretic peptide concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环脑钠肽浓度升高
terms.definition: An increased concentration of brain natriuretic peptide in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Reduced platelet dense granules
terms.definition: Decreased number of platelet dense granules, a type of platelet organelle.

terms.name: Reduced platelet alpha granules
terms.definition: A reduced number of platelet alpha granules.

terms.name: Mosaic pulmonary attenuation pattern
terms.definition: Mosaic attenuation refers to heterogeneous areas of differing pulmonary attenuation on CT imaging.

terms.name: Aortic annulus calcification
terms.definition: Pathological deposition of calcium salts in the aortic annulus, a fibrous ring-like structure found at the insertion point of the basal attachments of the aortic valve leaflets within the left ventricular outflow tract.

terms.name: Bilateral apical pulmonary fibrosis
terms.definition: A reticular pattern of linear or lineonodular densities in apical portions of both the right and left lungs seen initially on high-resolution computed tomography and in case of progression also on standard chest x-ray.

terms.name: Reversible airflow obstruction
terms.definition: Airflow obstruction with a significant response to a bronchodilator defined as an increase in FEV1 and/or FVC by 12 percent or more and by at least 200 mL.

terms.name: Irreversible airflow obstruction
terms.definition: Airflow obstruction without significant response to a bronchodilator defined as an increase in FEV1 and/or FVC by 12 percent or more and by at least 200 mL.

terms.name: Bronchial wall thickening
terms.definition: Radiological appearance of increased density around the walls of a bronchus or large bronchiole. This feature is thought to be related to edema involving the bronchial wall as well as the peribronchial interstitial space. If the cross section of a bronchus is captured in a radiograph or computed tomography image, it is said to have the appearance of a donut because of the central lucency representing the airway of the bronchus surrounded by a circular region of increased density.

terms.name: Addictive nicotine use
terms.definition: Nicotine addiction can be defined as a chronic, compulsive craving for nicotine and continued usage despite harmful consequences.

terms.name: Mesangial fibril deposition
terms.definition: Extracellular mesangial accumulation of slender proteinaceous fibers.

terms.name: Mesangial fibrillary deposits
terms.definition: Extracellular mesangial aggregates composed of randomly arranged, straight, non-branching fibrils that are thicker than amyloid fibrils (average diameter about 20 nm) and are often admixed with smudgy, electron-dense material.

terms.name: Mesangial microfibril deposition
terms.definition: Unbranched noncollagenous microfibrils within the mesangial matrix, composed of proteins not present within the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), most notably fibrillin-1, that attach to mesangial cells and GBM structural proteins.

terms.name: Mesangial immunotactoid deposits
terms.name_zh: 系膜免疫触须样沉积物
terms.definition: Extracellular mesangial aggregates composed of non-branching fibrils, focally parallel over 30 nM in diameter. The term immunotactoid refers to highly organized immune depositions appearing as rod-like microtubular structures in ultrastructural examination.

terms.name: Mesangial amyloid deposition
terms.definition: Extracellular mesangial aggregates composed of fine, randomly oriented, non-branching fibrils 8-12 nm in diameter, often forming a cottony mass.

terms.name: Nodular mesangiosclerosis
terms.definition: Lobular, round to oval mesangial lesions with an acellular hyaline/matrix core surrounded by compressed mesangial nuclei.

terms.name: Necrotizing pulmonary granulomatosis
terms.definition: A granuloma that is associated with necrotic changes. Caseation necrosis is defined as a region in granulomas with eosinophilic, granular and cheese-like cellular debris with necrosis. The word caseous itself means pertaining or related to cheese, and comes from the Latin word caseus, meaning cheese.

terms.name: Non-necrotizing pulmonary granulomatosis
terms.definition: A granuloma located in the lung that is not associated with necrotic changes.

terms.name: Chronic villitis
terms.definition: Villitis of unknown etiology (synonymous with villitis of unknown etiology) is a histologic diagnosis and, although it may have a variable distribution, evidence indicates that 3 parenchymal blocks will identify 62% of villitis, reaching an asymptote of 6 and 7 blocks identifying 85% of villitis. Villitis of unknown etiology by definition excludes those cases where an etiology is identified, such as viral or acute infections, and thus is preferred to the term nonspecific chronic villitis. It is usually lymphohistiocytic: although the presence of rare plasma cells does not exclude the diagnosis, thorough evaluation for an infectious etiology, such as cytomegalovirus, is required in a predominantly plasma cell villitis.

terms.name: Septic embolism
terms.definition: Embolization of intravascular thrombus containing microorganisms into the distant tissues via arterial system.

terms.name: Anti-Mi2 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against the Mi-2 antigen.

terms.name: Anti-Ro/SS-A antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against Ro/SSA autoantigens.

terms.name: Anti-nucleoporin 62 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against nucleoporin 62.

terms.name: Anti-proteinase 3 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against proteinase 3. Proteinase 3 (PR3) antigen is a 29-kD serine protease that exists as a protein triplet in human neutrophils

terms.name: Anti-histone antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against histone antigens.

terms.name: Anti-myeloperoxidase antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗髓过氧化物酶抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against myeloperoxidase.

terms.name: Anti-PM-Scl antibody positivity
terms.definition: Anti-PM-Scl antibodies target components of RNA-processing exosome complex in the nucleolus. There are ten proteins in this complex and antibodies to eight of them are found at varying frequencies; PM/Scl-100, PM/Scl-75, hRrp4, hRrp42, hRrp46, hCs14, hRrp41, and hRrp40.

terms.name: Anti-bactericidal/permeability-increasing protein antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗杀菌/通透性增加蛋白抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against bactericidal/permeability-increasing protein (BPI). BPI is an endotoxin-binding host protein with important antibacterial effects against Gram-negative bacteria, such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa. BPI is a 55 kDalton protein that is most abundant in the azurophilic granules of neutrophils. BPI also acts as a target antigen for antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibodies.

terms.name: Anti-glycoprotein-210 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against glycoprotein-210.

terms.name: Anti-tissue transglutaminase antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗组织转谷氨酰胺酶抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against tissue transglutaminase.

terms.name: Stasis dermatitis
terms.definition: Stasis dermatitis commonly occurs in older age. It is caused by venous hypertension resulting from retrograde flow due to incompetent venous valves, valve destruction, or obstruction of the venous system. Further tissue changes arise from an inflammatory process mediated by metalloproteinases, which are up-regulated by ferric ion from extravasated red blood cells. Stasis dermatitis presents initially as poorly demarcated erythematous plaques of the lower legs bilaterally, classically involving the medial malleolus.

terms.name: Anti-epidermal transglutaminase antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗表皮转谷氨酰胺酶抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against epidermal transglutaminase.

terms.name: Abnormal ventricular axis
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal direction of the ventricular axis. The left ventricle makes up most of the heart muscle under normal circumstances and therefore generates the most electrical force visible on the EKG. The normal ventricular axis is directed downward and slightly towards the left. The ventricular axis can be determined by analyzing the QRS complex, which represents ventricular depolarization.

terms.name: Right axis deviation
terms.definition: A kind of abnormal ventricular axis in the EKG whereby the QRS axis falls between +90 degrees and 180 degrees, or beyond +100 degrees if the adult range is used.

terms.name: Left axis deviation
terms.definition: A kind of abnormal ventricular axis in the EKG whereby the QRS axis falls between -30 degrees and -90 degrees.

terms.name: Extreme axis deviation
terms.definition: A kind of abnormal ventricular axis in the EKG whereby the QRS axis fall sbetween -90 degrees and 180 degrees. In this case, the ventricular vector is directed upward and to the right.

terms.name: Indeterminate ventricular axis
terms.definition: A kind of abnormal ventricular axis in the EKG whereby the QRS complex is isoelectric or equiphasic in all leads with no dominant QRS deflection.

terms.name: Peripheral lung neovascularity
terms.definition: The presence of small, tortuous, micronodular, serpiginous intrapulmonary vessels often in the subpleural lung or in proximity to centrilobular arterioles, coursing in directions inconsistent with known arteriolar anatomy.

terms.name: Anti-H1 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against histone H1.

terms.name: Anti-H4 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against histone H4.

terms.name: Anti-H3 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against histone H3.

terms.name: Anti-H2A antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against histone H2A.

terms.name: Anti-H2B antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against histone H2B.

terms.name: In situ pulmonary artery thrombosis
terms.definition: Localized thrombosis in pulmonary arteries frequently found in patients with idiopathic and hereditary pulmonary arterial hypertension and pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease.

terms.name: Pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension
terms.definition: Pre-capillary pulmonary hypertension is a haemodynamic condition characterized by elevated mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP over 20 mmHg) and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR 3 Wood units or more) accompanied by normal pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP not more than 15 mmHg).

terms.name: Decreased growth hormone responses to growth hormone-releasing hormone challenge
terms.name_zh: 生长激素释放激素激发试验生长激素反应降低
synonyms: Impaired growth hormone secretory responses after growth hormone-releasing hormone challenge
terms.definition: Insufficient growth hormone secretion following administration of growth hormone-releasing hormone.

terms.name: Compound motor action potential abnormality
terms.name_zh: 复合运动动作电位异常
terms.definition: An abnormal finding in a compound motor action potential measurement in EMG. Nerve conduction studies involve the application of a depolarising square wave electrical pulses to the skin over a peripheral nerve producing: (1) a propagated nerve action potential (NAP) recorded at a distant point over the same nerve: and (2) a compound muscle action potential (CMAP) arising from the activation of muscle fibers in a target muscle supplied by the nerve. In both cases these may be recorded with surface or needle electrodes. The CMAP is a summated voltage response from the individual muscle fiber action potentials. The shortest latency of the CMAP is the time from stimulus artifact to onset of the response and is a biphasic response with an initial upward deflection followed by a smaller downward deflection. The CMAP amplitude is measured from baseline to negative peak (the neurophysiological convention is that negative voltage is demonstrated by an upward deflection) and measured in millivolts (mV).

terms.name: Absent peripheral lymph nodes in presence of infection
terms.name_zh: 感染时外周淋巴结缺如
terms.definition: The absence of any palpable lymph nodes in the presence of symptoms suggesting infection in that drainage area should raise suspicion for immunodeficiency diseases.

terms.name: Pulmonary interstitial lymphocyte infiltration
terms.definition: Abnormal accumulation of lymphocytes in the interstitium of the lung.

terms.name: Follicular bronchiolitis
terms.definition: Follicular bronchiolitis is a polyclonal hyperplasia of bronchiolar associated lymphoid tissue characterized by the is characterized by the development of lymphoid follicles with germinal centers in walls of the small airways.

terms.name: Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
terms.definition: Temporally uniform (all lesions are in the same stage of evolution) pattern of diffuse inflammatory interstitial process, mostly symmetric over the entire lung, involving mainly the alveolar septa.

terms.name: Fibrotic non-specific interstitial pneumonia
terms.name_zh: 纤维化性非特异性间质性肺炎
terms.definition: A type of non-specific interstitial pneumonia in which interstitial thickening is due to uniform dense or loose fibrosis and mild chronic inflammation.

terms.name: Cellular non-specific interstitial pneumonia
terms.name_zh: 细胞型非特异性间质性肺炎
terms.definition: A type of non-specific interstitial pneumonia in which interstitial thickening is mainly due to infiltration of inflammatory cells and type II pneumocyte hyperplasia.

terms.name: Vulvar abscess
terms.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the vulvar region.

terms.name: Labial adhesion
terms.definition: Synechia vulvae (adhesions of the labia minora) are characterized by a complete or partial fusion of the labia minora in the midline.

terms.name: Flatulence
terms.definition: Passage of excessive amounts of gas and the feeling of abdominal fullness and bloating.

terms.name: Inguinal abscess
terms.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the groin (inguinal region).

terms.name: Staghorn calculus
terms.definition: Large branching stones that fill part of all of the renal pelvis and renal calyces and they can be complete or partial depending on the level of occupancy of the collecting system.

terms.name: Anti-H3-H4 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against the H3-H4 histone dimer.

terms.name: Anti-H2A-H2B antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against the H2A-H2B histone dimer.

terms.name: Elevated urinary 7-biopterin level
terms.definition: An abnormally increased amount of 7-biopterin in the urine.

terms.name: Elevated circulating globotriaosylceramide concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环球三糖神经酰胺浓度升高
terms.definition: Increased concentration of globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) in the blood circulation. Globotriaosylceramide, also named ceramidetrihexoside, is the primary lipid storage in Fabry disease.

terms.name: Elevated urinary 3-methylcrotonylglycine level
terms.name_zh: 尿3-甲基巴豆酰甘氨酸水平升高
terms.definition: An abnormally increased amount of 3-methylcrotonylglycine in the urine.

terms.name: Decreased mucosal sucrase-isomaltase activity
terms.name_zh: 黏膜蔗糖酶-异麦芽糖酶活性降低
terms.definition: Reduced activity of the linked disaccharidase, sucrase-isomaltase, which is a glycoprotein localized to the brush border membrane of small intestinal villi.

terms.name: Fibrillar glomerular subepithelial deposits
terms.name_zh: 肾小球上皮下纤维样沉积物
terms.definition: Fibrillar deposits located between the outer (epithelial) aspect of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) and the visceral epithelial cell, with varying degrees of incorporation into the GBM. This feature is associated with a prominent GBM reflecting an diffuse and relatively uniform increase in thickness (subjective estimate).

terms.name: Glomerular amyloid subepithelial deposits
terms.name_zh: 肾小球淀粉样上皮下沉积
terms.definition: A type of fibrillar glomerular subepithelial deposit characterized by extracellular aggregates composed of fine, randomly oriented, non-branching fibrils 8-12 nm in diameter, often forming a cottony mass. This feature is associated with a prominent glomerular basement membrane (GBM) reflecting an diffuse and relatively uniform increase in thickness (subjective estimate).

terms.name: Fibrillary glomerular subepithelial deposits
terms.name_zh: 肾小球上皮下原纤维沉积物
terms.definition: A type of fibrillar glomerular subepithelial deposit characterized by extracellular aggregates of randomly arranged, straight, non-branching fibrils that are thicker than amyloid fibrils (average diameter about 20 nm) and are often admixed with smudgy, electron-dense material. This feature is associated with a prominent glomerular basement membrane (GBM) reflecting an diffuse and relatively uniform increase in thickness (subjective estimate).

terms.name: Glomerular subepithelial immune-complex deposits
terms.name_zh: 肾小球上皮下免疫复合物沉积
terms.definition: A type of glomerular subepithelial deposit characterized by finely granular material deposited between the outer (epithelial) aspect of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) and the visceral epithelial cell, with varying degrees of incorporation into the GBM and corresponding to immunoglobulin and/or complement by immunofluorescence/immunohistochemistry. This feature is associated with a prominent GBM reflecting an diffuse and relatively uniform increase in thickness (subjective estimate).

terms.name: Glomerular hyaline subepithelial deposits
terms.name_zh: 肾小球上皮下透明沉积物
terms.definition: A type of glomerular subepithelial deposit characterized by a moderately electron-dense, generally homogenous, amorphous-appearing extracellular material located between the outer (epithelial) aspect of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) and the visceral epithelial cell, with varying degrees of incorporation into the GBM. This feature is associated with a prominent GBM reflecting an diffuse and relatively uniform increase in thickness (subjective estimate).

terms.name: Glomerular subepithelial deposits
terms.definition: Deposits located between the outer (epithelial) aspect of the glomerular basement membrane (GBM) and the visceral epithelial cell, with varying degrees of incorporation into the GBM. This feature may be associated with a prominent GBM reflecting an diffuse and relatively uniform increase in thickness (subjective estimate).

terms.name: Glomerular capillary wire loop deposits
terms.name_zh: 肾小球毛细血管铁丝圈沉积
terms.definition: Glomerulus showing markedly and irregularly thickened capillary walls with massive fuchsinophilic subendothelial deposits, resulting in narrowing of capillary lumina. This feature is said to resemble a wire loop.

terms.name: Pustular rash
terms.definition: A rash composed of pustular lesions. A pustule is defined as a vesicle or bulla containing purulent material. It varies in size and may occur at different levels within the epidermis: subcorneal, intraepidermal, or basement membrane zones. The pustules may or may not be sterile and are normally filled with neutrophils.

terms.name: Bone marrow maturation arrest
terms.definition: Interruption of the procecss of diffferentiation of hematopoietic cells in the bone marrow, manifested by an increased proportion of immature cells in the bone marrow.

terms.name: Bone marrow arrest at the promyelocytic stage
terms.name_zh: 骨髓早幼粒细胞阶段发育停滞
terms.definition: A type of bone marrow maturation arrest characterized by accumulation of neutrophil precursor cells in the bone marrow.

terms.name: Pulmonary nodule
terms.definition: Focal rounded or ovoid opacity, not more than 3 cm in diameter. Pulmonary nodules are typically observed by chest radiography or computer tomography imaging.

terms.name: Solid pulmonary nodule
terms.definition: A type of pulmonary nodule whose density obscures the underlying parenchyma and thus has a \

terms.name: Subsolid pulmonary nodule
terms.definition: Pulmonary subsolid nodules (SSNs) refer to pulmonary nodules with pure ground-glass nodules and part-solid ground-glass nodules. A ground-glass nodule (GGN) is the morphologic description of a pulmonary nodule category on thin-section chest computed tomography (CT). During the past decade, the natural history, management strategy and long-term prognosis in the case of GGNs have attracted attention.

terms.name: Part-solid pulmonary nodule
terms.definition: Part-solid pulmonary nodules are nodules that present with both ground-glass and solid components in which the underlying lung architecture cannot be visualized.

terms.name: Pure ground-glass pulmonary nodule
terms.definition: Pure ground-glass pulmonary nodules (GGNs) are defined as focal nodular areas of increased lung attenuation through which lung parenchymal structures, such as the pulmonary vessels or bronchial structures, can be observed.

terms.name: Perifissural pulmonary nodule
terms.definition: Solid, homogenous nodules characterized by a smooth margin and oval, rounded, lentiform or triangular shape. They are typically located within 15 mm from the issue or the pleura. Perifissural nodules may be further differentiated into typical (have contact with interlobar septum) and atypical (do not have contact with interlobar septum). They likely represent intrapulmonary lymphnodes.

terms.name: Tracheal bronchus
terms.definition: Aberrant or accessory bronchus supplying the upper lobe originating from the lateral wall of the trachea. The tracheal bronchus is more commonly right-sided, has a variable length and may be blind-ended. Two common types of tracheal bronchus are: supernumerary and displaced.

terms.name: Displaced tracheal bronchus
terms.definition: Accessory bronchus originating from trachea replacing one of the segmental branches of the anatomically normal upper lobe bronchus.

terms.name: Accessory cardiac bronchus
terms.definition: Accessory bronchus originating from the medial wall of the right or left ban bronchus or bronchus intermedius. A cardiac bronchus is usually blind-ended.

terms.name: Supernumerary tracheal bronchus
terms.definition: Accessory bronchus which exits the trachea in addition to an anatomically normal branching upper lobe bronchus.

terms.name: Displaced lobar tracheal bronchus
terms.definition: Accessory entire right upper lobe bronchial system originating from the trachea with absent anatomically normal upper lobe bronchus.

terms.name: Typical perifissural nodule
terms.definition: A perifissural nodule that has contact with the interlobar septum (and is therefore considered typical).

terms.name: Atypical perifissural nodule
terms.definition: A perifissural nodule that does not have contact with the interlobar septum (and is therefore considered atypical).

terms.name: Bronchial diverticula
terms.definition: Bronchial diverticula are blind-ended outpouchings arising from the bronchial tree. They are commonly pulsion diverticula acquired related to chronic cough. Subcarinal air cyst is thought to represent a small main bronchial diverticulum.

terms.name: Migratory erythematous plaque
terms.definition: A migratory, centrifugal, erythematous, tender, non-purpuric, and well-demarcated plaque. This feature may be observed in TNF receptor-associated periodic syndrome, in which it often occurs together with migratory myalgia in muscles located underneath the affected areas of skin.

terms.name: Birth history
terms.definition: Information about the delivery and health status at birth typically elicited as a part of the past medical history.

terms.name: History of congenital CMV infection
terms.name_zh: 先天性巨细胞病毒感染史
terms.definition: A congenital cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection of the newborn can follow either a primary or recurrent maternal infection. Jaundice, petechiae, and hepatosplenomegaly are the most frequently noted clinical triad in symptomatic infants. Affected infants may develop permanent disabilities such as hearing loss, vision loss, motor and cognitive deficits.

terms.name: Emotional insecurity
terms.definition: A feeling of general unease or nervousness that may be triggered by a sense of vulnerability or instability, which is perceived as threatening.

terms.name: Increased non-HDL cholesterol concentration
terms.name_zh: 非高密度脂蛋白胆固醇浓度升高
terms.definition: Increase above normal levels of non-HDL cholesterol in the blood. Non-HDL cholesterol is total cholesterol minus high-density lipoprotein HDL-cholesterol (high-density lipoprotein-cholesterol).

terms.name: Increased urine harderoporphyrin level
terms.definition: Concentration of harderoporphyrin in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Bowel irritability
terms.definition: Intermittent abdominal pain with diarrhea and/or constipation.

terms.name: IgG4 autoimmune antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of an antibody of subclass IgG4 in the blood circulation that is directed against the organism's own cells or tissues.

terms.name: Brain fog
terms.definition: Brain fog is a type of transient cognitive dysfunction that comprises a constellation of symptoms that impair intellectual functioning to a level that interferes with daily activities, commonly including forgetfulness, mental slowness, difficulty thinking or focusing, a perceived slowing of mental processing speed, inability to find the right words, a sensation that the mind went blank or is \

terms.name: Spondylitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the vertebrae (vertebral bodies) or spine.

terms.name: Abnormal alveolar volume
terms.definition: Alveolar volume (VA) is a volume accessible during 10-second breath-hold, measured during a single breath maneuver. VA is calculated by knowing the fractional concentration of the tracer gas (eg helium) and the volume of the gas inhaled. VA = Vi*(Fi tracer/Fa tracer). In this equation, Vi = inspired volume of tracer gas, Fi tracer= inspired fraction of tracer gas, Fa tracer = alveolar (exhaled) fraction of tracer gas.

terms.name: Decreased alveolar volume
terms.definition: An abnormal reduction in alveolar volume.

terms.name: Increased alveolar volume
terms.definition: An abnormal elevation in alveolar volume.

terms.name: Post-capillary pulmonary hypertension
terms.definition: Post-capillary pulmonary hypertension is a hemodynamic condition characterized by elevated mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP greater than 20 mmHg) and pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP greater than 15 mmHg) and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR less than 3 Wood units).

terms.name: Combined pre- and post-capillary pulmonary hypertension
terms.name_zh: 毛细血管前后混合型肺动脉高压
terms.definition: Combined pre- and post-capillary pulmonary hypertension is a haemodynamic condition characterized by elevated mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP over 20 mmHg) and pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP over 15 mmHg) and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR at least 3 Wodd units).

terms.name: Anti-endomysial antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against endomysial tissue transglutaminase 2 (tTG2).

terms.name: Intralobular septal thickening
terms.definition: Intralobular septal thickening is a computed tomography finding of increased width of the walls (septa) within a pulmonary lobule. Secondary pulmonary lobules represent a cluster of up to 30 acini 9 supplied by a common distal pulmonary artery and bronchiole. These clustered acini are bounded by interstitial fibrous septa (interlobular septa) which outline an irregular polyhedron of varying size between 1 and 2.5 cm. Interlobular septal thickening is seen on chest radiographs as thin linear opacities at right angles to and in contact with the lateral pleural surfaces near the lung bases. In contrast, intralobular septal thickening are visible as fine linear opacities in a lobule when the intralobular interstitial tissue is abnormally thickened. When numerous, they may appear as a fine reticular pattern.

terms.name: Septic pulmonary embolism
terms.definition: Embolization of intravascular thrombus containing microorganisms into the pulmonary parenchyma via arterial system. Septic pulmonary embolism (PE) can be associated with multiple additional clinical manifestations such as fever, tachypnea, and hemoptysis. This HPO term refers to the finding of the septic embolus in the lung, which can be inferred from radiological findings. Typical radiographic features of septic PE include patchy air space lesions simulating non-specific bronchopneumonia; multiple ill defined round or wedge shaped densities of varying sizes from approximately 0.5 to 3.5 cm located peripherally; lesions abutting the pleura and located at the end of vessels (feeding vessel sign) seen on chest CT scans. Other pulmonary features suggesting septic PE include bilateral, occasional unilateral, rapid progression of cavities or abscess formations.

terms.name: Acetabular erosions
terms.definition: Erosion (loss of substance) of the acetabular subchondral cortical bone. The acetabulum is the concave surface that meets with the head of the femur, forming the hip joint.

terms.name: Aortic valve leaflet calcification
terms.definition: Deposition of calcium salts in the leaflets (cusps) of the aortic valve.

terms.name: Mitral valve leaflet calcification
terms.definition: Deposition of calcium salts in the leaflets (cusps) of the mitral valve.

terms.name: Increased circulating very long-chain fatty acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环极长链脂肪酸浓度升高
synonyms: Increased plasma levels of very long-chain fatty acid
terms.definition: Increased concentration of very long-chain fatty acids in the blood circulation. Very long-chain fatty acids are fatty acids (FAs) with a chain-length of 22 or more carbons.

terms.name: Elevated circulating erythropoietin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环促红细胞生成素浓度升高
terms.definition: Increased concentration of erythropoietin in the blood circulation. Erythropoietin is a glycoprotein hormone produced by the peritubular cells of the kidney that stimulates red blood cell production.

terms.name: Midline brainstem cleft
terms.definition: A developmental defect characterized by an abnormal cleft (V-shaped indentation of the stalklike part of the brain consisting of the medulla oblongata, the midbrain, and the pons.

terms.name: Absent hippocampal commissure
terms.definition: Absence of the fibers that connect the contralateral hippocampi via the crura of the fornix and run beneath the posterior portion of the corpus callosum.

terms.name: Silhouette sign
terms.definition: The silhouette sign is the absence of depiction of an anatomic soft-tissue border. It is caused by consolidation and/or atelectasis of the adjacent lung, by a large mass, or by contiguous pleural fluid. The silhouette sign results from the juxtaposition of structures of similar radiographic attenuation. The sign actually refers to the absence of a silhouette.

terms.name: Pulmonary pseudocavity
terms.definition: A pseudocavity appears as an oval or round area of low attenuation in lung nodules, masses, or areas of consolidation that represent spared parenchyma, normal or ectatic bronchi, or focal emphysema rather than cavitation. These pseudocavities usually measure less than 1 cm in diameter. They have been described in patients with adenocarcinoma, bronchioloalveolar carcinoma, and benign conditions such as infectious pneumonia.

terms.name: Paraseptal emphysema
terms.definition: Paraseptal emphysema is characterized by predominant involvement of the distal alveoli and their ducts and sacs. It is characteristically bounded by any pleural surface and the interlobular septa. This emphysema is characterized by subpleural and peribronchovascular regions of low attenuation separated by intact interlobular septa, sometimes associated with bullae.

terms.name: Pulmonary parenchymal band
terms.definition: A parenchymal band is a linear opacity, usually 1-3 mm thick and up to 5 cm long that usually extends to the visceral pleura (which is often thickened and may be retracted at the site of contact). It reflects pleuroparenchymal fibrosis and is usually associated with distortion of the lung architecture. Parenchymal bands are most frequently encountered in individuals who have been exposed to asbestos.

terms.name: Pulmonary mycetoma
terms.definition: A mycetoma is a discrete mass of intertwined hyphae, usually of an Aspergillus species, matted together by mucus, fibrin, and cellular debris colonizing a cavity, usually from prior fibrocavitary disease (eg, tuberculosis or sarcoidosis). A mycetoma may move to a dependent location when the patient changes position and may show an air crescent sign. CT scans may show a spongelike pattern and foci of calcification in the mycetoma.

terms.name: Broncholith
terms.definition: A broncholith, a calcified peribronchial lymph node that erodes into an adjacent bronchus, is most often the consequence of Histoplasma or tuberculous infection. The imaging appearance is of a small calcific focus in or immediately adjacent to an airway, most frequently the right middle lobe bronchus. Broncholiths are readily identified on CT scans. Distal obstructive changes may include atelectasis, mucoid impaction, and bronchiectasis

terms.name: Bronchocele
terms.definition: A bronchocele is bronchial dilatation due to retained secretions (mucoid impaction) usually caused by proximal obstruction, either congenital (eg, bronchial atresia) or acquired (eg, obstructing cancer). A bronchocele is a tubular or branching Y-or V-shaped structure that may resemble a gloved finger. The CT attenuation of the mucus is generally that of soft tissue but may be modified by its composition (eg, high-attenuation material in allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis). In the case of bronchial atresia, the surrounding lung may be of decreased attenuation because of reduced ventilation and, thus, perfusion.

terms.name: Beaded septum sign
terms.definition: Irregular and nodular thickening of interlobular septa reminiscent of a row of beads.

terms.name: Pulmonary cavity
terms.definition: A gas-filled space, seen as lucency or low-attenuation area, within a nodule, mass or area of parenchymal consolidations. It has a clearly defined wall over 4 mm thick.

terms.name: Juxtaphrenic peak
terms.definition: A juxtaphrenic peak is a small triangular opacity based at the apex of the dome of a hemidiaphragm, associated with upper lobe volume loss of any cause (eg, postirradiation fibrosis or upper lobectomy). It is most readily appreciated on a frontal chest radiograph. The peak is caused by upward retraction of the inferior accessory fissure or an intrapulmonary septum associated with the pulmonary ligament.

terms.name: Linear atelectasis
terms.definition: Linear atelectasis is a focal area of subsegmental atelectasis with a linear configuration, almost always extending to the pleura. It is commonly horizontal but sometimes oblique or vertical. The thickness of the atelectasis may range from a few millimeters to more than 1 cm.

terms.name: Rounded atelectasis
terms.definition: Rounded atelectasis is rounded collapsed lung associated with invaginated fibrotic pleura and thickened and fibrotic interlobular septa. Most frequently, it is the consequence of an asbestos-induced exudative pleural effusion with resultant pleural scarring, but it may occur with any cause of pleural fibrosis. On chest radiographs, rounded atelectasis appears as a mass abutting a pleural surface, usually in the posterior part of a lower lobe. Distorted vessels have a curvilinear disposition as they converge on the mass (the comet tail sign). The degree of lobar retraction depends on the volume of atelectatic lung. It is almost invariably associated with other signs of pleural fibrosis (eg, blunting of costophrenic angle). CT is more sensitive for the detection and display of the characteristic features of rounded atelectasis. An additional sign is homogeneous uptake of contrast medium in the atelectatic lung.

terms.name: Hand paresthesia
terms.definition: Tingling (often referred to as a pins and needles feeling) and numbness in the hand.

terms.name: Air crescent
terms.definition: An air crescent is a collection of air in a crescentic shape that separates the wall of a cavity from an inner mass. The air crescent sign is often considered characteristic of either Aspergillus colonization of preexisting cavities or retraction of infarcted lung in angioinvasive aspergillosis. However, the air crescent sign has also been reported in other conditions, including tuberculosis, Wegener granulomatosis, intracavitary hemorrhage, and lung cancer. The crescent can be seen in both plain X-ray and CT scan.

terms.name: Air bronchogram
terms.definition: An air bronchogram is a pattern of air-filled (low-attenuation) bronchi on a background of opaque (high-attenuation) airless lung. The sign implies (a) patency of proximal airways and (b) evacuation of alveolar air by means of absorption (atelectasis) or replacement (eg, pneumonia) or a combination of these processes. In rare cases, the displacement of air is the result of marked interstitial expansion (eg, lymphoma).

terms.name: Air trapping
terms.definition: Air trapping is retention of air in the lung distal to an obstruction (usually partial). Air trapping is seen on end-expiration CT scans as parenchymal areas with less than normal increase in attenuation and lack of volume reduction. Comparison between inspiratory and expiratory CT scans can be helpful when air trapping is subtle or diffuse.

terms.name: Ganglioglioma
terms.definition: Gangliogliomas are rare tumors of the central nervous system. The are WHO grade I and considered low grade. They are well differentiated neuroepithelial tumors consisting of both dysplastic neuronal and neoplastic glial cells.

terms.name: Diminished health-related quality of life
terms.name_zh: 健康相关生活质量下降
terms.definition: A reduction in an individual's subjective assessment of his or her sense of well-being and ability to perform social roles.

terms.name: Diminished physical functioning
terms.definition: A reduction in the ability to perform activities of daily living as compared to previous abilities because of functional deficits due to illness. The 36-item Short Form (SF-36) health survey questionnaire is one of many methods used to measure patients' perceptions of diminished physical functioning.

terms.name: Diminished mental health
terms.definition: A reduction in the subjective feeling of mental well being.

terms.name: Abnormal amygdala morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the amygdala.

terms.name: Enlarged amygdala
terms.definition: A increase in the volume (size) of the amygdyla.

terms.name: Organizing pneumonia
terms.definition: Organizing pneumonia manifests as a histologic pattern characterized by loose plugs of connective tissue in the airspaces and distal airways. Interstitial inflammation and fibrosis are minimal or absent. Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia, or COP, is a distinctive clinical disorder among the idiopathic interstitial pneumonias, but the histologic pattern of organizing pneumonia is encountered in many different situations, including pulmonary infection, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, and collagen vascular diseases. Airspace consolidation is the cardinal feature of organizing pneumonia on chest radiographs and CT scans. In COP, the distribution is typically subpleural and basal and sometimes bronchocentric. Other manifestations of organizing pneumonia include groundglass opacity, tree-in-bud pattern, and nodular opacities.

terms.name: Pulmonary oligemia
terms.definition: Oligemia is a reduction in pulmonary blood volume. Most frequently, this reduction is regional, but occasionally it is generalized. Regional oligemia is usually associated with reduced blood flow in the oligemic area. Oligemia appears as a regional or widespread decrease in the size and number of identifiable pulmonary vessels, which is indicative of less than normal blood flow.

terms.name: Positive carpal Tinel sign
terms.definition: The Tinel test is performed by lightly tapping (percussing) over the median nerve. It is positive (abnormal) if the patient experiences pain and paresthesias (tingling, numbness) along the distribution of the median nerve.

terms.name: Positive Phalen test
terms.definition: The Phalen maneuver is performed by having the patient hold both wrists in complete and forced flexion (pushing the dorsal surfaces of both hands together) for 30-60 seconds. This can increase the pressure in the carpal tunnel. The test is positive (abnormal) if the patient experiences characteristic symptoms of carpal tunnel syndrome (pain and paresthesias along the distribution of the median nerve, i.e., thumb, index finger, and middle finger).

terms.name: Pulmonary blood flow redistribution
terms.definition: Pulmonary blood flow redistribution refers to any departure from the normal distribution of blood flow in the lungs that is caused by an increase in pulmonary vascular resistance elsewhere in the pulmonary vascular bed. Pulmonary blood flow redistribution is indicated by a decrease in the size and/or number of visible pulmonary vessels in one or more lung regions, with a corresponding increase in number and/or size of pulmonary vessels in other parts of the lung.

terms.name: Frailty
terms.definition: A clinically recognizable state of increased vulnerability resulting from a decline in reserve and function across multiple physiologic systems such that the ability to cope with everyday or acute stressors is compromised.

terms.name: Posttraumatic stress symptom
terms.definition: A behavioral or psychological symptom that typically occurs following exposure to one or more traumatic events is posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Symptoms of PTSD include intrusive recollections, such as re-experiencing the trauma through flashbacks, memories, or nightmares. Additionally, individuals may experience avoidant and numbing symptoms, which can include diminished emotions and avoidance of situations that serve as reminders of the traumatic event. Hyperarousal is another symptom, characterized by increased irritability, exaggerated startle reactions, and difficulties with sleeping or concentrating.

terms.name: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
terms.definition: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is defined as an acute disorder that starts within seven days of the inciting event and is characterized by bilateral lung infiltrates and severe progressive hypoxemia in the absence of any evidence of cardiogenic pulmonary edema. ARDS is defined by the patient's oxygen in arterial blood (PaO2) to the fraction of the oxygen in the inspired air (FiO2). These patients have a PaO2/FiO2 ratio of less than 300.

terms.name: Acute coronary syndrome
terms.definition: The term acute coronary syndrome (ACS) refers to any group of clinical symptoms compatible with acute myocardial ischemia and includes unstable angina (UA), non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), and ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).

terms.name: Abnormal red nucleus morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the red nucleus, a part of the midbrain involved in control of movement.

terms.name: Pilocytic astrocytoma
terms.definition: The most common form of astrocytoma (WHO Grade I) in childhood. These typically have MAPK signaling pathway abnormalities.

terms.name: Oligodendroglioma
terms.definition: Oligodendroglioma is a type of diffusely infiltrating glioma and constitutes approximately 5% of primary intracranial tumors. They often involve the cortical gray matter and are most commonly seen in the frontal lobes. OGs are generally low grade WHO grade II neoplasms that are slow-growing tumors and have a favorable treatment response when compared to other gliomas. Grade III anaplastic OG is a more malignant form of the tumor which portends a less favorable prognosis and may occur de novo or as degeneration from the lower grade OG.

terms.name: Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma
terms.definition: Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytomas (PXA) are rare low-grade astrocytomas (WHO Grade II) typically found in the temporal lobe and classically presenting with epilepsy. PXA is an astrocytic neoplasm that most often presents in children or young adults but can also occur in adults. The diagnosis of anaplastic PXA is made based upon tumor histopathologic characteristics and requires increased proliferative activity (mitotic index at least 5 mitoses/10 HPF), which is associated with worse overall survival. In general, anaplastic PXAs acquire features of a more aggressive astrocytic neoplasm that can include increased proliferation, necrosis, microvascular proliferation, loss of pericellular reticulin, and increased infiltrative growth.

terms.name: Jaw hyperreflexia
terms.definition: Increased intensity of muscle tendon reflexes in jaw.

terms.name: Abnormal muscle fiber-type distribution
terms.definition: Ay deviation from the normal distribution of fiber types in skeletal muscle. The skeletal muscle groups of the mammalian body are made up of bundles of muscle fibers. These fibers can be assigned to different Types, with characteristic movement rates, response to neural inputs, and metabolic styles. Skeletal muscle fibers are broadly classified as slow-twitch (type 1) and fast-twitch (type 2). Multiple fiber types are generally intermingled within a single muscle group, and different muscle groups have varying proportions of fiber types

terms.name: Fiber type grouping
terms.definition: An abnormal distribution of muscle fiber types in muscle tissue. Human skeletal muscle contains at least two fiber types recognizable by histochemical techniques. In transverse sections of normal skeletal muscle, type 1 and type 2 fibers are distributed in a random fashion. Grouping of fibers of the same type can be seen in certain peripheral neuropathies, thought to be due to reinnervation of denervated muscle fibers by sprouting axons. With grouping, motor units enlarge. The fibers of a motor unit, which are normally scattered, come to lie adjacent to one another. Histochemical examination shows groups of muscle fibers of the same histochemical type.

terms.name: Mitochondrial hypertrophy
terms.definition: Enlargement of mitochondria. Mitochondrial hypertrophy is not discernible by light microscopy. By electron microscopy (EM), hypertrophic mitochondria have normal cristae and normal matrix density. In contrast, swollen mitochondria display swollen cristae and irregular matrix densities in EM.

terms.name: Short term memory impairment
terms.definition: A deficit in the retention of pieces of information (memory chunks) for a relatively short time (usually up to 30 seconds).

terms.name: Long term memory impairment
terms.definition: A deficit in the ability to retrieve information from long-term memory, which can be defined as a seemingly unlimited capacity to store memories can last years and relate to the performance of actions or skills (i.e., procedural memories, knowing how) and memories of facts, rules, concepts, and events (i.e., declarative memories, knowing that).

terms.name: Anterograde memory impairment
terms.definition: The impaired ability to establish new long-term memories.

terms.name: Retrograde memory impairment
terms.definition: Inability to retrieve information from the long-term memory that was acquired before the onset of amnesia.

terms.name: Procedural memory loss
terms.definition: A reduction in the ability to retrieve information about how to perform activities, such as how to ride a bike or drive a car, how to perform activities of daily living, or how to play a musical instrument.

terms.name: Declarative memory loss
terms.definition: Impaired ability to remember facts and events.

terms.name: Phantosmia
terms.definition: Perception of an odor in the absence of any stimuli in the surrounding environment that could emit the odor.

terms.name: Tactile hallucination
terms.definition: Perception of touch without a tactile stimulus.

terms.name: Occupational disability
