terms.definition: Concentration or activity of cathepsin D as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal. The reduction in cathepsin D activity can also be measured in fibroblasts.

terms.name: Reduced leukocyte N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase activity
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal.

terms.name: Pseudohyperkalemia
terms.definition: Pseudohyperkalemia describes a falsely elevated potassium level upon measurement of the serum electrolyte concentration due to disruption of cells during the collection or processing of the sample.

terms.name: Abnormal enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts
terms.name_zh: 培养成纤维细胞酶活性异常
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of an enzyme is above or below the limits of normal in cultured fibroblasts. Fibroblasts are easy to grow in culture and are the main cell type involved in producing extracellular matrix. They are used as a convenient model system for measuring enzyme activity for enzymes that are not expressed in blood cells. Usually, the test is done in fibroblasts for convenience rather than for the investigation of a pathophysiology specific to fibroblasts.

terms.name: Reduced heparan-alpha-glucosaminide N-acetyltransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

terms.name: Reduced N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase in cultured fibroblasts
synonyms: Reduced N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfate sulfatase in cultured fibroblasts
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

terms.name: Reduced acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase activity in cultured fibroblasts
synonyms: Reduced acetylglucosamine-6-sulfate sulfatase activity in cultured fibroblasts
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase (EC 3.1.6.14) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal. N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase hydrolyzes heparan sulfate and keratan sulfate.

terms.name: Reduced erythrocyte porphobilinogen deaminase activity
terms.definition: Activity or concentration of in the level of porphobilinogen deaminase (EC 4.3.1.8) in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Reduced holocarboxylase synthetase activity in cultured fibroblasts
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of holocarboxylase synthetase (EC 6.3.4.10) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating alpha mannosidase activity
terms.name_zh: 血α-甘露糖苷酶活性异常
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of alpha mannosidase outside of the limits of normal in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Reduced tissue alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase activity
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase (EC 3.2.1.49) is below the limits of normal. The activity can be measured in multiple tissues including cultured fibroblasts.

terms.name: Reduced erythrocyte arginase activity
terms.definition: Activity or concentration of arginase (EC 3.5.3.1) in red blood cells below the lower limit of normal. Arginase catalyzes the last step of the urea cycle.

terms.name: Reduced mitochondrial acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of mitochondrial acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.9) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

terms.name: Reduced tissue beta-mannosidase activity
terms.definition: Concentration or activity of beta-mannosidase (EC 3.2.1.25) below the lower limit of normal. Beta-mannosidas enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes and cultured fibroblasts.

terms.name: Reduced 3-methylcrotonyl CoA carboxylase activity in cultured fibroblasts
terms.definition: Activity of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase (EC 6.4.1.4) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

terms.name: Reduced branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase activity in cultured fibroblasts
terms.definition: Activity of branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex (EC 1.2.4.4) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

terms.name: Reduced erythrocyte galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase activity
terms.definition: Activity or concentration of in the level of galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase (GALT; EC 2.7.7.12) in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal erythrocyte adenosine deaminase activity
terms.name_zh: 红细胞腺苷脱氨酶活性异常
terms.definition: Activity of adenosine deaminase in red blood cells outside the limits of normal.

terms.name: Reduced isovaleryl CoA dehydrogenase activity in cultured fibroblasts
terms.definition: Activity of isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase (EC 1.3.99.10) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

terms.name: Reduced glycerol kinase activity in cultured fibroblasts
terms.definition: Activity of glycerol kinase (EC 2.7.1.30) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

terms.name: Increased circulating vitamin A concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环维生素A浓度升高
terms.definition: Concentration of vitamin A above the upper limit of normal in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating hyaluronic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环透明质酸浓度升高
terms.definition: Concentration of hyaluronic acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Diminished breath sounds
terms.definition: A reduction in the intensity of the breath sound as ascertained by auscultation of the lung.

terms.name: Anti-AK5 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against anti-adenylate kinase 5 (AK5).

terms.name: Anti-AMPAR antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against anti-alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR).

terms.name: Anti-Amphiphysin antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Amphiphysin.

terms.name: Anti-ARHGAP26 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Rho GTPase-activating protein 26 (ARHGAP26).

terms.name: Anti-CARP VIII antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Carbonic anhydrase-related protein VIII (CARPVIII).

terms.name: Anti-CASPR2
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against contactin-associated protein-like 2 (CASPR2).

terms.name: Anti-CV2/CRMP5 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against CV2/CRMP5. Anti-CV2/CRMP5 autoantibody is the most commonly detected anti-neuronal autoantibody. Patients with typical paraneoplastic chorea show fully developed chorea in the course of weeks to months with acute inflammation in the striatum.

terms.name: Anti-DPPX antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against dipeptidyl-peptidase-like protein 6 (DPPX).

terms.name: Anti-FGFR3 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against FGFR3.

terms.name: Anti-GABA(A)R antibody
synonyms: Anti-gamma amino butyric acid type A receptors antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against gamma-aminobutyric acid A receptor, i.e., GABA(A)R.

terms.name: Anti-GABA(B)R antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against gamma-aminobutyric acid B receptor, i.e., GABA(B)R.

terms.name: Anti-GAD65 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glutamic acid decarboxylase 65 (GAD65).

terms.name: Anti-Gephyrin antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Gephyrin.

terms.name: Anti-GFAP antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP).

terms.name: Anti-GlyR antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Glycine receptor (GlyR).

terms.name: Anti-Homer-3 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Homer-3.

terms.name: Anti-Hu antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Hu.

terms.name: Anti-Iglon5 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against immunoglobulin-like cell adhesion molecule 5 (IgLON5).

terms.name: Anti-ITPR1 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor 1 (ITPR1).

terms.name: Anti-Kelch like protein 11 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against kelch-like protein 11 (KLHL11).

terms.name: Anti-LGI1 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against leucine-rich glioma-inactivated 1 (LGI1).

terms.name: Anti-Ma antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ma.

terms.name: Anti-Ma2 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ma2.

terms.name: Anti-Ma1 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ma1.

terms.name: Anti-mGluR1 antibody
terms.name_zh: 抗代谢型谷氨酸受体1抗体
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against metabotropic glutamate receptor 1 (mGluR1).

terms.name: Anti-mGluR5 antibody
terms.name_zh: 抗代谢型谷氨酸受体5抗体
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5).

terms.name: Anti-neurexin-3alpha antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗神经连接蛋白3α抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against neurexin-3alpha.

terms.name: Anti-P/Q-type VGCC antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCCs).

terms.name: Anti-MAP1B antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against microtubule-associated protein 1B (MAP1B).

terms.name: Anti-PKCgamma antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against protein kinase Cgamma.

terms.name: Anti-Ri antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ri, an antineuronal antibody.

terms.name: Anti-Septin-5 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Septin-5.

terms.name: Anti-SEZ6L2 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against seizure-related 6 homolog like 2 (SEZ6L2).

terms.name: Anti-SOX1 antibody
synonyms: Anti-Sry-like high mobility group box (SOX) 1 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against SOX1. Anti-SOX1 antibodies, also known as antiglial nuclear antibody (AGNA), are specifically found in paraneoplastic neurological disorders. Since SOX1 is expressed in neuronal precursor cells in the developing central nervous system, it has been used as an early marker of neural stem cells.

terms.name: Anti-Tr/DNER antibody
synonyms: Anti-delta/notch-like epidermal growth factor-related receptor antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Tr/DNER. Anti-Tr antibodies are directed against cerebellar Purkinje cells (termed anti-Tr or PCA-Tr). Anti-Tr autoantibodies are frequently associated with Hodgkin lymphoma (HL). Anti-Tr antibodies are defined by a specific staining pattern in cerebellar tissue that is characterized by punctate immunoreactivity in both the dendritic tree and soma of Purkinje cells but not in their axons. This characteristic pattern is indicative of the presence of anti-Tr antibodies. The Delta/Notch-like epidermal growth factor-related receptor (DNER) was identified as the target antigen of anti-Tr.

terms.name: Anti-TRIM46 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against the axon initial segment protein tripartite motif 46 (TRIM46).

terms.name: Anti-TRIM9/TRIM67 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against TRIM9/TRIM67.

terms.name: Anti-Yo antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Yo.

terms.name: Anti-titin antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against titin.

terms.name: Anti-Zic4 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Zic family member 4 (ZIC4).

terms.name: Distal radioulnar joint space widening
terms.name_zh: 桡尺远端关节间隙增宽
terms.definition: Increased space between the distal radius and distal ulna at sigmoid notch (radioulnar distance more than 6 mm at the sigmoid notch).

terms.name: Anti-Sj/ITPR1 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Sj/inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor.

terms.name: Anti-D2 R antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against dopamine-2 receptor.

terms.name: Anti-GluK2 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glutamate kainate receptor subunit 2 (GluK2).

terms.name: Anti-Lrp4 antibody positivity
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against low-density lipoprotein receptor (Lrp4).

terms.name: Anti-ryanodine receptor antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against ryanodine receptor.

terms.name: Anti-Kv1.4 antibody
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against the voltage-gated potassium channel Kv1.4.

terms.name: Distal radioulnar joint translation
terms.definition: Abnormal linear movement or displacement of the ulnar head relative to the radius at the wrist, indicating instability of the distal radioulnar joint, which is the distal articulation between the radius and ulna, acting as a major weight-bearing joint at the wrist and distributing forces across the forearm bones.

terms.name: Selective mutism
terms.definition: Voluntary failure to use spoken language (at whatever level attained) in selective social contexts over a period of time.

terms.name: Limited repertoire of facial expression
terms.name_zh: 面部表情 repertoire 受限
terms.definition: An abnormally limited range of facial expressions demonstrated by a lack of nuance of facial expression to match specific social situations or an inability to demonstrate a normal range of emotions with one's face.

terms.name: Excessive interest in others
terms.definition: A strong desire to interact and engage with others that is perceived to be inappropriate or excessive in the context of cultural norms.

terms.name: Abnormal pitch
terms.definition: Persistently abnormally high or low-pitched vocalization or speech than is considered the norm for the context of social situation or significantly different from baseline of the individual.

terms.name: Disjointed sentences
terms.definition: Persistent abnormalities in the sentence structure in speech, phrases may not be logically connected to each other, gives the impression of rambling. This may be a characteristic feature of the individual or may be a change from the norm of the affected individual.

terms.name: Neologism
terms.definition: Consistent use of an invented word that is unique to an individual.

terms.name: Overly formal/pedantic language
terms.definition: Use of language that is overly formal, precise, detailed, or pedantic for the social context.

terms.name: Midline hand movements
terms.definition: Hand stereotypies within the medial plane of the body.

terms.name: Abnormal Intonation
terms.definition: Abnormal rise and fall of the voice in speech and vocalization for the context and cultural situation.

terms.name: Abnormal speech rate
terms.definition: Speech that is abnormally fast or slow as compared to the perceived cultural norm.

terms.name: Abnormal speech rhythm
terms.definition: Speech with persistent abnormal rhythm or pattern for the context and cultural situation. This may occur constantly throughout conversations with the person or may occur in periodic bursts lasting several minutes to hours.

terms.name: Ambiguous facial expression
terms.definition: Spontaneous production of communicative facial expressions that have poor quality or are perceived as odd or mechanical. This may include inaccurate mimicry of typical facial expressions. These expressions may be difficult to interpret for someone who is not familiar with the individual making the expression.

terms.name: Exaggerated facial expression
terms.definition: A tendency to make facial expressions that are exaggerated and a failure to make subtle facial expressions in a social context when a subtle expression is more appropriate.

terms.name: Muted facial expression
terms.definition: A tendency to produce facial expressions with decreased intensity or expressivity which appear muted or flat.

terms.name: Abnormal peer relationships
terms.definition: The state of having abnormal relationships with others. This does not describe specific aspects of one's social aptitudes but rather a state which may come about from these aptitudes, such as lacking peer relationships or lacking close friends.

terms.name: Stereotypic movements of face and head
terms.definition: Abnormal movements of face and head.

terms.name: Stereotypic upper-extremity movements
terms.definition: Abnormal movements of the upper extremities.

terms.name: Stereotypic whole-body movements
terms.definition: Abnormal movements of the whole body.

terms.name: Abnormal interest in others
terms.definition: A deviation from typical perceived social engagement with other individuals given the social context. This may manifest as either an excessive interest (e.g., persistent preoccupation with another person, excessive attempts to engage) or an abnormal lack of interest (e.g., minimal or absent social curiosity) in others.

terms.name: Reduced social insight
terms.definition: A lack of awareness of social rules in multiple social settings, which are simple or intuitive to others in the same social setting.

terms.name: Reduced awareness of convention
terms.definition: Reduced awareness of expected conventions, which are normal and expected for particular social settings or interactions.

terms.name: Abnormal HLA-DR+ T cell proportion
synonyms: Abnormal HLA-DR expression on T cells
Abnormal proportion of DR+ T cells
terms.definition: The proportion of peripheral blood T lymphocytes expressing HLA-DR (CD3+HLA-DR+) is outside of the reference limit for age.

terms.name: Abnormal relationship
terms.definition: The state of having abnormal relationships with others. This does not describe specific aspects of one's social aptitudes but rather a state which may come about from these aptitudes, such as lacking peer relationships, lacking close friends, or having a relational network that is abnormal given one's cultural context.

terms.name: Impaired social imitation
terms.definition: Reduced use of imitation of tasks or movements of others in play or learning.

terms.name: Infrequent social initiations
synonyms: Infrequent attempts to direct the attention of another person
Reduced attempt to get or direct the attention of another person
terms.definition: Social initiation refers to the ability to begin interactions with other people. This term refers to a reduction in the frequency with which an individual attempts to begin interactions. The term should only be used for individuals who are assessed to have sufficient intellectual and language skills to interact with others.

terms.name: Reduced responsiveness to social cues
terms.definition: A tendency to display responces to social cues that are interpreted (e.g., by family members, peers, or caregivers) as diminished compared to what would be expected based on the developmental stage and cultural context of an individual.

terms.name: Social disinhibition
terms.definition: A tendency to violate social norms because of a failure to resist temptations or urges in social settings.

terms.name: Diminished integration of verbal and non-verbal communicative behavior
terms.name_zh: 言语与非言语交流行为整合减退
terms.definition: A communicative abnormality where one's nonverbal and verbal communication are poorly integrated. This may occur when verbal and nonverbal communication are intact alone but are abnormal when used together, or an abnormality in the use of typically integrated communication such as the use of beat gestures during speech.

terms.name: Increased HLA-DR+ T cell proportion
synonyms: Elevated proportion of DR+ T cells
Elevated proportion of HLA-DR expressing T cells
terms.definition: The proportion of peripheral blood T lymphocytes expressing HLA-DR (CD3+HLA-DR+) is above the upper reference limit for age.

terms.name: Decreased HLA-DR+ T cell proportion
synonyms: Reduced proportion of DR+ T cells
Reduced proportion of HLA-DR expressing T cells
terms.definition: The proportion of peripheral blood T lymphocytes expressing HLA-DR (CD3+HLA-DR+) is below the upper reference limit for age.

terms.name: Reduced cooperative imaginative play
terms.definition: Failure of a child to engage with peers games that involve creating imaginary scenarios or narratives, for instance, in which children pretend to be characters or act out adventurous scenarios.

terms.name: Lack of expressed empathy
terms.definition: The observation that an affected person tends not to provide situationally appropriate responses to other people in times when these people are in emotional need. For instance, failure to provide comfort to a person who is sad or crying.

terms.name: Bradylalia
terms.definition: Speech that is abnormally slow as compared to the perceived cultural norm.

terms.name: Excessively loud speech
terms.definition: Speech which is persistently abnormally and noticeably loud or high volume for the social and cultural context and is not due to a structural or muscular abnormality. Those around the person often consider them to be shouting.

terms.name: Excessively quiet speech
terms.definition: Speech which is persistently abnormally quiet, or of low in volume for the social and cultural context. This includes persistent and inappropriate whispering. It is not due to a medical or surgical condition that results in hoarseness, nor structural or muscular abnormality that results in low speech volume.

terms.name: Abnormal speech volume
terms.definition: Speech that is abnormally loud or quiet for the social and cultural context in which it is spoken. It is clinically noted by others, including family, friends, or clinical providers.

terms.name: Reduced attention regulation
terms.definition: An abnormality in one's ability to control their attention towards a specific subject or task can include difficulties in changing or maintaining attention.

terms.name: Reduced impulse control
terms.definition: Reduced ability to control, or a failure to resist a temptation, urge, or impulse.

terms.name: Sensory behavioral abnormality
terms.definition: Abnormal sensory behavior, including avoiding or seeking sensory input or difficulty modulating sensory stimuli.

terms.name: Idiosyncratic gesture
terms.definition: When one uses gestures that are unique to them and have no apparent meaning to others.

terms.name: Atypical sorting
terms.definition: Atypical focus on arranging, balancing, or positioning objects; may be atypical in focus or intensity.

terms.name: Excessive checking
terms.definition: Checking behavior that is excessive for the situational context.

terms.name: Excessive hand washing
terms.definition: Hand washing behavior that is excessive for the situational context.

terms.name: Resistance to trivial environmental changes
terms.definition: Distress in response to minor changes in one's environmental expectations.

terms.name: Reduced co-speech gestures
terms.definition: Reduced use of speech-integrated gestures such as the use of beat gestures.

terms.name: Limited head nodding or shaking
terms.definition: Absence or reduction in the use of head nodding to indicate agreement or head shaking to indicate disagreement.

terms.name: Limited pointing
terms.definition: Absence or reduction in the use of pointing to request or direct another's attention.

terms.name: Sensory hypersensitivity
terms.definition: A decreased tolerance to sensory stimuli that triggers emotional and/or physical distress.

terms.name: Sensory hyposensitivity unexplained by sensory deficit
terms.definition: Increased tolerance to sensory stimuli due to diminished sensory ability.

terms.name: Auditory hypersensitivity
terms.definition: Hyperresponsive to sound that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

terms.name: Tactile hypersensitivity
terms.definition: A decreased tolerance to physical touch.

terms.name: Auditory sensory seeking
terms.definition: Pursuit of specific sounds or noises that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

terms.name: Gustatory sensory seeking
terms.definition: Pursuit of a particular taste that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

terms.name: Olfactory sensory seeking
terms.definition: Pursuit of specific scents, smells, or fragrances that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

terms.name: Tactile sensory seeking
terms.definition: Pursuit of a specific texture that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

terms.name: Vestibular sensory seeking
terms.definition: Pursuit of vestibular stimulation that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

terms.name: Visual sensory seeking
terms.definition: Pursuit visual stimulation by looking at specific sights, images, and/or colors that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

terms.name: Socially inappropriate questioning
terms.definition: A tendency to ask questions that are overly personal or otherwise inappropriate in the social situation in which they are asked.

terms.name: Spinning
terms.definition: An excessive frequency of spinning one's body.

terms.name: Delayed Echolalia
terms.definition: Repetition of borrowed words or phrases outside of the context in which they were originally heard. E.g., scripting from TV shows or movies.

terms.name: Immediate Echolalia
terms.definition: Immediate repetition of another person's speech.

terms.name: Excessive cleaning
terms.definition: Excessive cleaning of surfaces, living space, or environment that is excessive for the situational context.

terms.name: Facial expressions not directed to others
Reduced social smiling
terms.definition: Reduced production of smiles during engagement with an interactive parent, caregiver, or peer.

terms.name: Abnormal play
terms.definition: An abnormality in a child's ability play.

terms.name: Reduced imaginative play skills
terms.definition: Reduced or lack of pretending in play (does not assign abstract properties to objects, use invisible objects, or use objects in nonliteral ways other than their intended purpose in play).

terms.name: Nonfunctional or atypical use of objects in play
terms.definition: Use of objects in atypical, unimaginitive ways other than for which they are intended (banging, throwing, shaking, sorting, lining up, spinning).

terms.name: Infrequent social engagement with peers
terms.definition: Lower than typical number of attempts to engage peers in conversation, play, or other interactions.

terms.name: Avoidance of emotional intimacy
terms.definition: An atypically high tendency to avoid interpersonal exchanges characterizing by sharing of personal feelings, expressions of understanding, affirmation, and demonstrations of caring.

terms.name: Failure to offer information to initiate social interaction
terms.name_zh: 主动发起社交信息提供障碍
terms.definition: An atypically low tendency to offer information as a means to initiate or sustain social interactions or direct another's attention.

terms.name: Difficulty understanding nonliteral meaning of conversation
terms.name_zh: 会话非字面意义理解困难

terms.name: Difficulty recognizing another's emotions
terms.definition: A difficulty in recognizing or interpreting the emotional states of other individuals.

terms.name: Abnormal social emotional interactions
terms.definition: An atypically low production of emotion social communications including those produced by communicative behaviors such as facial expressions, body language, and verbal communication.

terms.name: Objectification of others
terms.definition: A tendency to interact with others as if they are objects with functional purpose rather than engaging in social/emotional interactions.

terms.name: Abnormal response to social norms
terms.definition: An atypical understanding or application of social rules and conventions that guide interpersonal behavior. This may include reduced awareness of social norms or rigid, context-insensitive adherence to them.

terms.name: Indifference to social norms
terms.definition: Failure to follow social norms (shared standards of acceptable behavior) even though one has awareness of these norms and the ability to follow them.

terms.name: Aggression towards others
terms.definition: Aggression that is directed towards other individuals, as opposed to oneself.

terms.name: Aggression towards caregivers
terms.definition: Aggression that is directed towards caregivers.

terms.name: Aggression toward non-caregivers
terms.definition: Aggression that is directed towards non-caregivers.

terms.name: Abnormal rituals
terms.definition: Insistence on rituals which are self-imposed on a person's environment including directing the behavior of those around them.

terms.name: Jumping
terms.definition: An excessive frequency of jumping in place.

terms.name: Delay in the acquisition of cooperative play skills
terms.name_zh: 合作游戏技能习得延迟
terms.definition: Failure to acquire the ability to play cooperatively, a type of play in whichchildren work together towards a common goal and in which a child displays interest both in the play and in the the other child or children involved in playing. This ability is observed in neurotypical children from the age of 3 to 6 years.

terms.name: Reduced social reciprocity
terms.definition: Reduced responses to other people's emotions and/or a lack of modulation of behaviour according to social context.

terms.name: Olfactory hallucination
terms.definition: Perception of smell without olfactory stimulus.

terms.name: Gustatory hallucination
terms.definition: Perception of taste without gustatory stimulus.

terms.name: Abnormal interpretation of external stimuli
terms.definition: Abnormal perception of reality is characterized by an abnormal or inaccurate experience of external stimuli.

terms.name: Proprioceptive hallucination
terms.definition: A type of hallucination that involves the perception of distorted or abnormal sensations related to one's body position or movement.

terms.name: Disturbed perception with a stimulus
terms.definition: A perceptual experience in which an individual's perception of sensory stimuli is altered or disrupted in some way, resulting in abnormal or distorted sensory perceptions despite the presence of actual external stimuli.

terms.name: Illusions
terms.definition: Perceptual experiences that involve misinterpretations or distortions of sensory stimuli.

terms.name: Inattentiveness illusion
terms.definition: Instances in which individuals fail to perceive or notice salient or significant stimuli in their visual field due to a lack of attention.

terms.name: Illusions due to affect
terms.definition: Perceptual distortions or misinterpretations of sensory information arise as a result of the individual's emotional or affective state.

terms.name: Pareidolia
terms.definition: Apophenia is a psychological phenomenon in which individuals perceive familiar patterns or meaningful images in random or ambiguous stimuli, such as clouds, shadows, or inanimate objects.

terms.name: Autoscopy
terms.definition: A phenomenon in which an individual perceives themselves from an external perspective, as if they are observing their own body or self from a location outside of their physical body.

terms.name: Subjective eidetic images
terms.definition: A mental phenomenon is when an individual can vividly visualize or recall visual information from memory with exceptional detail and accuracy. These images are experienced subjectively by the individual, meaning they are not physically present or visible to others.

terms.name: Amplification of social interactions
terms.definition: A increase in the tendency of a person to seek or maintain social connections or interactions with others compared to previous norms for an individual.

terms.name: Diminishment of emotional responsiveness
terms.definition: A reduction in the tendency of a person to display emotional responsiveness or empathy towards others during interpersonal interactions as compared to that person's previous norm.

terms.name: Somatic hallucination
terms.definition: A type of hallucination that involves the perception of sensory experiences related to the body or its internal organs, systems, or processes. It is a hallucinatory experience that primarily affects bodily sensations rather than external sensory perceptions.

terms.name: Visceral hallucination
terms.definition: A type of hallucination that involves the perception of internal bodily sensations or processes that do not actually exist.

terms.name: Abnormal perceptual state
terms.definition: Temporary alteration of the awareness of reality or self-perception.

terms.name: Depersonalization
terms.definition: A psychological experience or symptom characterized by a sense of detachment or estrangement from oneself or one's surroundings.

terms.name: Derealization
terms.definition: A subjective experience in which an individual feels a sense of detachment or estrangement from their surroundings, leading to a distorted perception of the external world. It is characterized by a feeling of unreality or unfamiliarity with one's environment, as if things are dreamlike, artificial, or lacking in significance.

terms.name: Decreased facial expression mirroring
terms.definition: Diminished mirroring or reflection of facial expressions in another person during social interactions.

terms.name: Diminishment of comfort with casual physical contact
terms.name_zh: 随意肢体接触舒适度下降
terms.definition: A reduction in the tendency of a person to accept casual physical contact with others as compared to that person's previous norm.

terms.name: Thought blocking
terms.definition: The experience of sudden cessation of the thought/thinking process, the person often describes the mind going blank and there is frequently a period of silence that is accompanied by a perplexed state, not understanding what transpired. Some may describe the experience as an abrupt emptying of the mind or the belief that an external force removed their thoughts from their head.

terms.name: Maladaptive fear-related cognitions
terms.name_zh: 适应不良性恐惧相关认知
terms.definition: Threat-based cognitive biases result in a skewed perception, experience, or processing of internal or external stimuli.

terms.name: Hypervigilance
terms.definition: A heightened alertness is characterized by a broad awareness and/or excessive scanning of environmental stimuli.

terms.name: Phobia
terms.definition: Extreme, irrational, and persistent fears of certain objects, situations, activities, or persons can impede functioning in day-to-day life.

terms.name: Anticipatory anxiety
terms.definition: A state characterized by future-oriented worry, accompanied by negative affect and autonomic arousal.

terms.name: Flight of ideas
terms.definition: Successive thoughts and speech are easily diverted by external stimuli or internal superficial associations. Unable to maintain a constant train of thought and lose themselves in side issues, losing the thread and are unable to recover it. Superficial connections appear to drive the subject matter.

terms.name: Recurrent maladaptive behavior
terms.definition: A repeating behavior that is either immediately unproductive or has negative long-term consequences. This includes harmful coping mechanisms such as addictive behavior and failure to control impulses and compulsions.

terms.name: Cognitive distortion
terms.definition: A cognitive distortion is a maladaptive, exaggerated, or irrational thought pattern.

terms.name: Abnormal change in social behavior
terms.definition: An alternation in the habits and emotional tendencies of an individual with a change in behavior that is typically noticed by family members or peers.

terms.name: Abnormal demeanor
terms.definition: An anomaly in demeanor, which refers to the outward behavior, manner, or conduct of a person. It encompasses how an individual presents themselves to others in terms of attitude, posture, and general comportment.

terms.name: Abnormally increased volition
terms.definition: An excessive increase in motivated and goal directed as well as non-goal directed behaviors that are usually accompanied by elevated energy and interest that allows individuals to get started, be energized to perform a sustained and directed action. The increase is often disruptive and typically results in unfavorable consequences.

terms.name: Pressured speech
terms.definition: Speech pattern that is excessive and intense that often imparts a sense of urgency, the individual appears to be driven to communicate with many words that are spoken very quickly and may run into each other. The person is frequently difficult to interrupt and appears to not respond to social cues for the conversational partner(s) to take their turn in speaking.

terms.name: Leaden paralysis
terms.definition: The sensation of having heavy arms and legs, or feeling a heaviness in the limbs.

terms.name: Grandiosity
terms.definition: Persistently exaggerated feelings and thoughts of an inflated sense of self-importance, superiority, uniqueness, or invulnerability. The affected individual may project arrogance with a dismissive behavioral pattern towards others the individual deems inferior.

terms.name: Hopelessness
terms.definition: Persistent and excessive feelings of despair with an overwhelming lack of hope. While hopelessness is primarily a personal experience, the sense of hopelessness becomes pervasive and affects most aspects of the personal experience in relation to the world. For example the person may communicate a sense of hopelessness for family and friends (who themselves do not experience hopelessness), as well as the world in general.

terms.name: Pathological sadness
terms.definition: A negative emotional state characterized by sadness, unhappiness, or sorrow that is excessive in intensity, duration, or resistance to self-regulation compared with culturally appropriate norms or the individual's usual emotional range. It may arise spontaneously or in response to significant life events, but when reactive, it is disproportionate to or persists beyond what is typically expected for the context. Pathological sadness can be associated with feelings of hopelessness, helplessness, anhedonia, and a pessimistic outlook, but these features are not invariably present. It may also be accompanied by increased tearfulness, low energy, cognitive difficulties such as impaired concentration, and somatic changes including disrupted sleep or appetite.

terms.name: Decreased need for sleep
terms.definition: There has been a noticeable decrease in the need for sleep, where individuals feel refreshed even with minimal or no sleep.

terms.name: Sleep-related breathing disorders
terms.definition: Conditions of abnormal and difficult respiration during sleep, including chronic snoring and sleep apnea.

terms.name: Recurrent distressing nightmares
terms.definition: Repeated occurrence of nightmares that cause clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational or other important areas of functioning, which are not attributable to the physiological effects of a substance (e.g. drug abuse or medication) and which cannot be adequately explained by coexisting mental and medical disorders.

terms.name: Sleep-related eating behavior
terms.definition: Eating during sleep with limited to no recall of involuntary eating while asleep.

terms.name: Microsleep
terms.definition: Sudden onset of extreme drowsiness or falling asleep during the day for a short period of time.

terms.name: Exploding head syndrome
terms.definition: Sleep disorder in which one hears a loud noise or explosive crashing sound in one's head. The sound is not real or heard by anyone else. The episode typically happens suddenly, either when beginning to fall asleep or when waking up during the night.

terms.name: REM sleep behavior disorder
synonyms: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder
Rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder
terms.definition: REM Sleep Behavior Disorder (RBD) is a chronic sleep condition characterized by dream enactment and loss of REM atonia.

terms.name: Non-restorative sleep
terms.definition: Sleep that is subjectively reported as unrefreshing even though the duration is adequate.

terms.name: Sleep-wake transition abnormality
synonyms: Disturbance during transitions between sleep and wake states
terms.definition: A parasomnia that occurs with awareness and recollection during the transition between sleep and and awake states.

terms.name: Sexsomnia
terms.definition: Unintentional sexual behavior during sleep, such as masturbation, initiation of sex, or making sexual noises, is known as sexsomnia. Sexsomnia predominantly occurs during NREM sleep.

terms.name: Periodic limb movements of sleep
terms.definition: Repetitive, stereotyped limb movements occurring during sleep, typically involving brief flexion of the toes, ankles, knees, or hips. These movements recur at regular intervals, often every 20-40 seconds, and may cause sleep fragmentation or daytime fatigue. PLMS commonly co-occurs with restless legs syndrome but may also occur independently.

terms.name: Abnormal transition from sleep to wakefulness
terms.definition: Abnormal transition of consciousness from sleeping to wakefulness.

terms.name: Abnormal transition from wakefulness to sleep
terms.definition: Abnormal transition of consciousness from wakefulness to sleep.

terms.name: Abnormal sleep architecture
terms.definition: Interruptions during the various stages of sleep.

terms.name: REM parasomnia
terms.definition: Parasomnia occurs during REM sleep.

terms.name: Abnormal movement during sleep
terms.definition: Periodic Limb Movement Disorder, also known as Sleep-Related Myoclonus Syndrome or Nocturnal Myoclonus Syndrome, refers to the periodic and stereotypic movements of the legs or upper limbs during sleep.

terms.name: Short N1 sleep
terms.definition: Decreased duration of phase N1 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.

terms.name: Paradoxical insomnia
synonyms: Disturbance in perception related to sleep
terms.definition: Paradoxical insomnia is a condition in which individuals with a normal or near-normal sleep macrostructure tend to severely underestimate the quantity and quality of their sleep.

terms.name: Short N2 sleep
terms.definition: Decreased duration of phase N2 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.

terms.name: Short N3 sleep
terms.definition: Decreased duration of phase N3 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.

terms.name: Diminishment of social interactions
synonyms: Reduced, declined or lessened social interactions
terms.definition: A reduction in the tendency of a person to seek or maintain social connections or interactions with others compared to previous norms for an individual.

terms.name: Amplification of interpersonal communication
synonyms: Heightened, amplified social expression and social connectedness
terms.definition: An increase in the tendency of a person to share information or emotions compared to that person's previous norms.

terms.name: Amplification of relationship seeking
terms.definition: Increased frequency or duration in social outings and interactions as part of relationship-seeking or maintenance compared to the previous norms of an individual. May be considered to be overfamiliar and have a tendency to engage strangers in a presumptive manner.

terms.name: Diminishment of interpersonal communication
synonyms: A decline or reduced social expression and social connectedness
terms.definition: A reduction in the tendency of a person to share information or emotions compared to that person's previous norms.

terms.name: Diminishment of relationship seeking
terms.definition: A reduction in the tendency of a person to seek new interpersonal relationships or maintain existing relationships.

terms.name: Amplification of sexual behavior
terms.definition: An abnormal increase of libido (sexual desire), typically accompanied by a higher frequency of sexual activity compared to from a person's previous norm.

terms.name: Amplification of emotional expression
terms.definition: An increase in the tendency of a person to express emotions compared to that person's previous norm.

terms.name: Amplification of emotional responsiveness
terms.definition: An increase in the tendency of a person to display emotional responsiveness or emotional empathy towards others during interpersonal interactions as compared to that person's previous norm. May be considered to be overreactive or over-engaged with interpersonal situations that may take on a persistent preoccupation and would appear to be relatively unrelated to the person, and beyond the expression of normal empathy.

terms.name: Amplification of comfort with casual physical contact
terms.name_zh: 随意肢体接触舒适感增强
synonyms: Increase in comfort with casual physical contact
terms.definition: An increase in the tendency of a person to be comfortable with physical contact with others compared to that person's previous norm. Often considered to be intrusive and encroaching on personal space of others less known to the person, frequently causing discomfort and may result in argument or altercation.

terms.name: Diminishment of sexual behavior
terms.definition: A reduction of libido (sexual desire), typically accompanied by a reduction in the frequency of sexual activity , and/or activity compared to the affected individual's previous state.

terms.name: Diminishment of emotional expression
terms.definition: A reduction in the tendency of a person to express emotions that is typically noticed as a change in behavior by family members or peers.

terms.name: Problematic alcohol consumption
terms.definition: Impaired ability to stop or control alcohol use despite adverse social, occupational, or health consequences.

terms.name: Suicide behaviors
terms.definition: Suicide attempts or preparations

terms.name: Addictive sedative use
terms.definition: Misuse and/or abuse of sedative drugs.

terms.name: Addictive non-substance behaviors
terms.definition: Uncontrolled use or problematic behaviors of dependency without the use of drugs or substances can be detrimental.

terms.name: Addictive spending behavior
terms.definition: An uncontrollable urge to shop and spend money can lead to distress or impairment.

terms.name: Addictive gambling behavior
terms.definition: The act of taking chances or engaging in behaviors without restraint, typically involving the wagering of something valuable, in pursuit of acquiring something of higher value.

terms.name: Addictive sex behavior
terms.definition: Inability to control or manage sexual urges, fantasies, or behaviors that impair one's ability to function.

terms.name: Addictive video game use
terms.definition: The inability to regulate persistent gaming behavior is characterized by a heightened prioritization of gaming activities over regular daily tasks and responsibilities.

terms.name: Compulsive stealing
terms.definition: Irresistible impulses to take easily affordable items.

terms.name: Excessive fire setting
terms.definition: The inability to control urges of deliberately setting fires for pleasure and gratification, without any criminal intent.

terms.name: Self-cutting
terms.definition: Deliberate harm to one's body, in the form of cutting that results in tissue damage, without a conscious intent to die.

terms.name: Addictive cannabis use
terms.definition: A persistent and compulsive need to use cannabis, despite negative consequences.

terms.name: Autophagia
terms.definition: The habitual action of inflicting pain upon oneself by biting and/or devouring portions of one's body.

terms.name: Hypnagogic sleep paralysis
synonyms: Inability to move while falling asleep
terms.definition: Sleep paralysis that occurs when falling asleep.

terms.name: Hypnopompic sleep paralysis
terms.definition: Sleep paralysis that occurs when waking up from sleep.

terms.name: Sleep onset rapid eye movement period
terms.definition: Entering REM sleep immediately upon falling asleep.

terms.name: Prolonged N1 sleep
terms.definition: Increased duration of phase N1 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.

terms.name: Prolonged N2 sleep
terms.definition: Increased duration of phase N2 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.

terms.name: Prolonged N3 sleep
terms.definition: Increased duration of phase N3 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.

terms.name: Abnormal judgment
terms.definition: Beliefs that deviate from what is considered rational or within the range of normal human judgment and belief formation.

terms.name: Overvalued idea
terms.definition: A solitary belief that may be held by others in the society that is maintained by the person to an abnormal and morbid degree and overtly drives behaviors that are considered unhealthy, intrusive, or illegal. This includes fads and cults that the person may adhere to and practice to a morbid degree. The content may vary and ranges from religion, health, romance, or politics.

terms.name: Time agnosia
terms.definition: The inability to perceive the passage of time is usually due to a disorder involving the temporal area of the brain.

terms.name: Olfactory agnosia
terms.definition: The inability to recognize certain smells or types of odors that you previously recognized.

terms.name: Tactile agnosia
terms.definition: The inability to recognize objects by touch is called tactile agnosia.

terms.name: Topographical agnosia
terms.definition: The inability to rely on visual cues to guide one's direction is due to the inability to recognize objects.

terms.name: Delusional memory
terms.definition: Delusional memory is a memory that is false or fantastically distorted, but held with firm and irrefutable conviction despite evidence to the contrary. It is often seen in psychiatric conditions such as delusional disorders, schizophrenia, and sometimes in severe mood disorders. These memories can be completely fabricated or have a basis in an actual event that has been grossly misinterpreted or altered by the individual's mind.

terms.name: Auditory agnosia
terms.definition: The condition is characterized by the inability to recognize spoken languages and/or nonverbal environmental sounds and music, despite having adequate hearing. However, spontaneous speech, reading, and writing abilities remain intact.

terms.name: Gustatory agnosia
terms.definition: People cannot identify tastes, even though they can experience them.

terms.name: Allesthesia
terms.definition: Referral of a sensory stimulus from one side of the body to the other.

terms.name: Autotopagnosia
terms.definition: The loss of the ability to localize, recognize, or identify specific parts of one's body.

terms.name: Persecutory delusion
terms.definition: False beliefs (or judgements) that are held with extraordinary conviction and subjective certainty that are impervious to other experiences or counterarguments and the content is generally considered impossible for the context and circumstance. Delusional beliefs may arise meaningfully from personal or social experiences, yet are impossible, held with conviction, and irrefutable; more commonly they may be psychologically irreducible, appearing with no logical or meaningful connection to the individual experience.

terms.name: Morbid jealousy
terms.definition: A disorder of delusional content wherein the affected individual believes they are a victim of their partner's infidelity. It is often based on delusional evidence of an erotic or romantic nature. There may be an affective (mood related) component or may be associated with substance use disorders. It may also occur on its own. There may be associated behaviors to monitor or gather evidence of the perceived infidelity.

terms.name: Grandiose delusion
terms.definition: Delusional beliefs of a fantastical, expansive, or supernatural quality related to power, ability, wealth, or station. They are often related to origin (aristocratic lineage, royal birth, being raised as a foster child), possessions (owning vast estates, castles, etc., which are withheld through intrigue), abilities (being great inventors, discoverers, artists, possessors of special wisdom, gifted with inspiration), and status (adviser to prominent diplomats, the true director of political destinies). Grandiose delusions may be related to affective states, substance use, or may occur independently.

terms.name: Folie à deux
terms.definition: Delusional beliefs are transmitted from one individual to another.

terms.name: Disorder of thought control
terms.definition: A false belief that another person, group of people, or external force controls one's general thoughts, feelings, impulses, or behaviors.

terms.name: Delusion of love
terms.definition: A delusional belief that the person is secretly loved by another individual who is often of recognized fame or authoratative significance. There is typically no overt evidence and the delusional belief may be driven by falsely perceived indicators. Often there is a blend of erotic delusions and morbid infatuation.

terms.name: Nihilistic delusion
terms.definition: A delusion that elements of the self, body, or world no longer exist. The person typically recognizes that the entity did in fact exist at one time, but has ceased to exist. The cause of which may be related to disease, decay, or may have been removed or taken by unknown forces.

terms.name: Cotard delusion
terms.definition: A false belief that you or your body parts are dead, dying, or do not exist.

terms.name: Abnormal experience of reality
terms.definition: Subjective phenomena or perceptions that deviate from what is considered correct or are outside the range of normal human experiences.

terms.name: Delusional perception
terms.definition: A true perception, to which a patient attributes a false and usually bizarre meaning or interpretation. It is often a revelatory experience that is sudden and is a profound realization of the delusional belief. It often occurs in the context of delusional mood or atmosphere wherein vague and mysterious hunches or concerns with nebulous meaning evolve into clear, delusional observations, and expresses delusions of reference.

terms.name: Hypochondriac delusion
terms.definition: Delusion quality to belief that one is suffering from an illness despite reassurances based on medical examination and testing. The person may (or not) express pain or discomfort that they attribute to the disease. They are frequently treatment seeking, but do not induce illness features (which is termed Munchhausen syndrome).

terms.name: Delusions of infestation
terms.definition: A persistent belief that a person is infested with living or non-living pathogens, such as parasites, insects, or bugs, when no such infestation is present.

terms.name: Delusional atmosphere
terms.definition: A persistent sense or a hunch that something is different in an imperceptible manner. Typically the perception is one of a sinister, portentous , uncanny, mysterious, or peculiar sense of foreboding in an indefinable way. There is an innate sense of inexplicable self-relevance to the person. There is often a feeling of anticipation, sometimes even excitement, that soon the mystery may be revealed and all the separate parts of their experience will fit together to reveal something immensely significant. The duration of this experience may vary, lasting from hours to days. It may be intermittent over an extended period of time (months to years).

terms.name: Delusional misidentification
terms.definition: A group of complex, monothematic delusional phenomena in which subjects hold a belief that the identity of a familiar person, object, location, or self has been altered or replaced. The majority of misidentifications are spouses or first degree relatives, i.e. someone well-known to the person.

terms.name: Religious delusion
terms.definition: Delusions with a religious content that are considered delusional in nature based on how the belief is held and the evidence offered to support it, which is generally considered impossible or fantastical in the cultural setting of the person. It differs from unusual beliefs that are held with tenacity or conviction and are typically associated with other phenomena consistent with mental illness.

terms.name: Abnormal psychotic pattern
terms.definition: Any abnormal pattern of psychotic experiences, where an individual has significant disturbances in their thoughts, perceptions, emotions, and behavior, resulting in a loss of touch with reality.

terms.name: Incomplete unilateral cleft lip
terms.definition: Unilateral cleft lip cleft that starts from the bottom of the upper lip but does not reach the nasal cavity.

terms.name: Complete unilateral cleft lip
terms.definition: Unilateral cleft lip cleft that starts from the bottom of the upper lip and reaches the nasal cavity.

terms.name: Microform unilateral cleft lip
terms.definition: Notch, groove, or scar of the upper lip without noticeable rupture of the lip. Microforms are sometimes associated with disruption of the continuity of the orbicularis oris muscle.

terms.name: Complete cleft hard palate
terms.definition: Cleft hard palate in which the cleft goes through the entire length of the hard palate, ie. from the incisor foramen to the anterior border of the soft palate.

terms.name: Incomplete cleft hard palate
terms.definition: Cleft hard palate in which the cleft does not go through the entire length of the hard palate, ie. the cleft does not go from the incisor foramen to the anterior border of the soft palate.

terms.name: Complete cleft soft palate
terms.definition: Cleft soft palate in which the cleft goes through the entire length of the soft palate, i.e. from the posterior border of the hard palate until the uvula.

terms.name: Incomplete cleft soft palate
terms.definition: Cleft soft palate in which the cleft does not go through the entire length of the soft palate, i.e. the cleft does not go from the posterior border of the hard palate until the uvula.

terms.name: Incomplete cleft maxillary alveolar ridge
terms.name_zh: 不完全性上颌牙槽嵴裂
terms.definition: Cleft maxillary alveolar ridge in which the cleft does not go through the entire length of the maxillary alveolar ridge.

terms.name: Complete cleft maxillary alveolar ridge
terms.definition: Cleft maxillary alveolar ridge in which the cleft goes through the entire length of the maxillary alveolar ridge.

terms.name: Complete cleft of the upper lip
terms.definition: Cleft of the upper lip that starts from the bottom of the upper lip and reaches the nasal cavity.

terms.name: Microform cleft of the upper lip
terms.definition: Notch, groove, or scar of the upper lip without noticeable rupture of the lip.

terms.name: Complete bilateral cleft lip
terms.definition: Bilateral cleft lip in which the cleft lip on both sides is complete, i.e. start from the bottom of the upper lip and reach the nasal cavity.

terms.name: Incomplete bilateral cleft lip
terms.definition: Bilateral cleft lip in which the cleft lip on both sides are incomplete (i.e. start from the bottom of the upper lip but do not reach the nasal cavity), or the cleft lip on one is incomplete and a microform on the other side.

terms.name: Microform bilateral cleft lip
terms.definition: Bilateral cleft lip in which the cleft lip on both sides are microform, i.e. a notch, groove, or scar without noticeable rupture of the lip.

terms.name: Asymmetric bilateral cleft lip
terms.definition: Bilateral cleft lip in which the cleft lip on one side is complete (i.e. starts from the bottom of the upper lip and reaches the nasal cavity), and the one on the other side is incomplete (i.e. starts from the bottom of the upper lip but does not reach the nasal cavity) or microform (i.e. a notch, groove, or scar without noticeable rupture of the lip).

terms.name: Craniofacial cleft
terms.definition: Congenital abnormality with cleft (gap or opening) in the craniofacial bones. Craniofacial cleft includes facial cleft, orofacial clef, and cleft of the jaw.

terms.name: Submucous cleft palate
terms.definition: A cleft of the muscular portion of the palate that is covered by mucous membrane.

terms.name: Unusual gram-positive bacterial infection

terms.name: Unusual gram-negative bacterial infection

terms.name: Severe Staphylococcus aureus infection

terms.name: Chronic absent circulating IgA

terms.definition: A reduction in the total concentration of immunoglobulin M (IgM) in the circulation that persists for more than 6 months.

terms.name: Chronic absent circulating IgM

terms.name: Transient decreased circulating IgM concentration

terms.name_zh: 伤寒沙门菌非结合疫苗特异性抗体应答完全或近完全缺失

Specific Haemophilus influenzae type b antibody deficiency
terms.definition: The concentration in the blood circulation of specific immunoglobulins directed against the capsular polysaccharide of Haemophilus influenzae type b is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Legionella pneumophila infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Legionella pneumophila infection.

terms.name: Unusual Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Neisseria gonorrhoeae infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Neisseria gonorrhoeae, or by Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Neisseria gonorrhoeae infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

terms.name: Recurrent Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Neisseria gonorrhoeae infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection.

terms.name: Unusual Neisseria meningitidis infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Neisseria meningitidis infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Neisseria meningitidis, or by Neisseria meningitidis infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Neisseria meningitidis infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Neisseria meningitidis infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Neisseria meningitidis.

terms.name: Unusual Haemophilus influenzae infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Haemophilus influenzae infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Haemophilus influenzae, or by Haemophilus influenzae infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Haemophilus influenzae infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Haemophilus influenzae infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Haemophilus influenzae.

terms.name: Unusual Moraxella catarrhalis infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Moraxella catarrhalis infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Moraxella catarrhalis, or by Moraxella catarrhalis infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Moraxella catarrhalis infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Moraxella catarrhalis infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Moraxella catarrhalis.

terms.name: Recurrent Moraxella catarrhalis infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Moraxella catarrhalis infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Moraxella catarrhalis infection.

terms.name: Unusual Vibrio cholerae infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Vibrio cholerae infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Vibrio cholerae, or by Vibrio cholerae infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Vibrio cholerae infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Vibrio cholerae infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Vibrio cholerae.

terms.name: Recurrent Vibrio cholerae infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Vibrio cholerae infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Vibrio cholerae infection.

terms.name: Unusual Burkholderia cepacia infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Burkholderia cepacia infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Burkholderia cepacia, or by Burkholderia cepacia infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Burkholderia cepacia infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Burkholderia cepacia infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Burkholderia cepacia.

terms.name: Unusual Bacteroides infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Bacteroides infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Bacteroides, or by Bacteroides infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Bacteroides infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Bacteroides infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Bacteroides.

terms.name: Recurrent Bacteroides infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Bacteroides infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Bacteroides infection.

terms.name: Unusual Fusobacterium infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Fusobacterium infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Fusobacterium, or by Fusobacterium infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Fusobacterium infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Fusobacterium infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Fusobacterium.

terms.name: Recurrent Fusobacterium infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Fusobacterium infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Fusobacterium infection.

terms.name: Unusual Prevotella infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Prevotella infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Prevotella, or by Prevotella infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Prevotella infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Prevotella infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Prevotella.

terms.name: Recurrent Prevotella infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Prevotella infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Prevotella infection.

terms.name: Unusual Escherichia coli infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Escherichia coli infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Escherichia coli, or by Escherichia coli infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Escherichia coli infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Escherichia coli infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Escherichia coli.

terms.name: Unusual Salmonella infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Salmonella infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Salmonella, or by Salmonella infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Salmonella infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Salmonella infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Salmonella.

terms.name: Recurrent Salmonella infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Salmonella infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Salmonella infection.

terms.name: Unusual Pneumocystis jirovecii infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Pneumocystis jirovecii infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Pneumocystis jirovecii, or by Pneumocystis jirovecii infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Pneumocystis jirovecii infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Pneumocystis jirovecii infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Pneumocystis jirovecii.

terms.name: Recurrent Pneumocystis jirovecii infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Pneumocystis jirovecii infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Pneumocystis jirovecii infection.

terms.name: Unusual Aspergillus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Aspergillus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Aspergillus, or by Aspergillus infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Aspergillus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Aspergillus infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Aspergillus.

terms.name: Unusual adenovirus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to adenovirus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with adenovirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Unusual Candida infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Candida infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Candida, or by Candida infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Cytomegalovirus hepatitis
terms.definition: Hepatitis caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual BK virus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to BK polyomavirus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with BK polyomavirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Unusual Cryptococcus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Cryptococcus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Cryptococcus, or by Cryptococcus infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent Cryptococcus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Cryptococcus infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Cryptococcus infection.

terms.name: Disseminated Cryptococcus infection
terms.definition: Disseminated infection with Cryptococcus, involving multiple organ systems that occurs in the context of immune deficiency.

terms.name: Sclerosing cholangitis due to Cryptococcus
terms.definition: Sclerosing cholangitis caused by Cryptococcus infection that occurs in the context of immune deficiency.

terms.name: Chronic hepatitis due to Cryptococcus
terms.definition: Chronic hepatitis caused by Cryptococcus infection that occurs in the context of immune deficiency.

terms.name: Unusual mycobacterial infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to mycobacterial infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/disseminated infection with mycobacterial organisms, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis, non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM), or BCG.

terms.name: Tuberculosis infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium tuberculosis infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis, or by Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Disseminated tuberculosis infection
terms.definition: Disseminated infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis, involving multiple organ systems. Organ-specific manifestations of disseminated tuberculosis include renal tuberculosis (tuberculous pyelonephritis, presenting with sterile pyuria and hematuria), hepatic tuberculosis, adrenal tuberculosis, and tuberculous osteomyelitis.

terms.name: Recurrent tuberculosis infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium tuberculosis infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection.

terms.name: Tuberculous osteomyelitis
terms.definition: Osteomyelitis caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with NTM, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Unusual VZV infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with VZV, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) infection.

terms.name: Opportunistic mycobacterial infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to mycobacterial infections that rarely cause disease in immunocompetent individuals.

terms.name: Unusual Cryptosporidium infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Cryptosporidium infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Cryptosporidium, or by Cryptosporidium infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent Cryptosporidium infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Cryptosporidium infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Cryptosporidium infection.

terms.name: Unusual upper respiratory tract infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection of the upper respiratory tract, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the nose, sinuses, pharynx, larynx, or middle ear, or by infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Sclerosing cholangitis due to Cryptosporidium infection
terms.definition: Sclerosing cholangitis caused by Cryptosporidium infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual lower respiratory tract infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection of the lower respiratory tract, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, or lung parenchyma, or by infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual Giardia lamblia infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Giardia lamblia, or by Giardia lamblia infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Persistent Giardia lamblia infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infections as manifested by a chronic or persistent Giardia lamblia infection.

terms.name: Recurrent Giardia lamblia infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Giardia lamblia infection.

terms.name: Unusual Toxoplasma infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Toxoplasma gondii infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Toxoplasma gondii, or by Toxoplasma gondii infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Unusual cardiovascular system infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection involving the heart or major vessels, as manifested by recurrent or severe endocarditis, myocarditis, pericarditis, or infectious vasculitis, or by cardiovascular infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Toxoplasma infection of the central nervous system (CNS)
terms.definition: Infection of the central nervous system with Toxoplasma gondii, typically presenting as cerebral toxoplasmosis.

terms.name: Unusual Leishmania infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Leishmania infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Leishmania, or by Leishmania infection occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe Leishmania infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Leishmania infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Leishmania.

terms.name: Recurrent Leishmania infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Leishmania infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Leishmania infection.

terms.name: Opportunistic parasitic infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to parasitic infections that rarely cause disease in immunocompetent individuals.

terms.name: Unusual cholangitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious cholangitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the biliary tract, or by cholangitis occurring in an unusual clinical context such as absence of cholelithiasis or biliary obstruction. Causative agents include bacteria (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterococcus species) and fungi (Candida species).

terms.name: Unusual genitourinary infection
