terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection of the genitourinary tract, as manifested by recurrent or severe cystitis, pyelonephritis, kidney abscess, or vaginal infection, or by genitourinary infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual eye infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection of the eye or its adnexa, as manifested by recurrent or severe conjunctivitis, keratitis, retinitis, or other ocular infection, or by ocular infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual liver infection
terms.definition: An atypical or infrequent infectious process affecting the liver parenchyma that deviates from common viral or bacterial patterns. This may include infections caused by rare pathogens (e.g., specific fungi, parasites, or rare bacteria) or infections presenting with atypical clinical or pathological features.

terms.name: Infectious hepatitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the liver tissue caused by an infectious agent, most commonly viruses (e.g., Hepatitis A, B, C), but also potentially by bacteria, parasites, or fungi. It is characterized by diffuse involvement of the liver parenchyma.

terms.name: Bacterial sepsis
terms.definition: Sepsis caused by bacterial infection, characterized by a dysregulated host response to a bacterial pathogen with systemic inflammation, organ dysfunction, and potential progression to septic shock.

terms.name: Fungal sepsis
terms.definition: Sepsis caused by fungal infection, characterized by a dysregulated host response to a fungal pathogen with systemic inflammation, organ dysfunction, and potential progression to septic shock.

terms.name: Viral sepsis
terms.definition: Sepsis or sepsis-like syndrome caused by viral infection, characterized by a dysregulated host response to a viral pathogen with systemic inflammation, multi-organ involvement, and potential progression to circulatory and respiratory failure.

terms.name: Mycobacterial sepsis
terms.definition: Sepsis or sepsis-like systemic illness caused by mycobacterial infection, characterized by a dysregulated host response with systemic inflammation, multi-organ involvement, and disseminated mycobacterial disease.

terms.name: Pneumonia with consolidation
terms.definition: Pneumonia characterized by lobar or segmental consolidation on radiographic imaging, reflecting alveolar filling with inflammatory exudate that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual cytomegalovirus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to cytomegalovirus (CMV) infections as manifested by severe, invasive, persistent, or disseminated CMV infection.

terms.name: Unusual pleural empyema
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to pleural empyema, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the pleural space, or by empyema occurring in an unusual clinical context such as an atypical causative organism or failure to resolve with standard therapy.

terms.name: Severe pleural empyema
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to pleural empyema, as manifested by a severe or life-threatening infection of the pleural space requiring surgical drainage, decortication, or intensive care.

terms.name: Recurrent pleural empyema
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to pleural empyema, as manifested by recurrent episodes of pleural space infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Unusual endocarditis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious endocarditis, as manifested by recurrent or severe endocardial infection, or by endocarditis caused by an unusual organism.

terms.name: Severe endocarditis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious endocarditis, as manifested by severe or complicated endocarditis with valvular destruction, systemic emboli, or heart failure requiring surgical intervention.

terms.name: Recurrent endocarditis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious endocarditis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of endocardial infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Unusual myocarditis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious myocarditis, as manifested by recurrent or severe inflammation of the myocardium caused by infection, or by myocarditis caused by an unusual organism.

terms.name: Severe myocarditis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious myocarditis, as manifested by severe myocardial inflammation with haemodynamic compromise, arrhythmia, or fulminant heart failure.

terms.name: Recurrent myocarditis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious myocarditis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of myocardial inflammation caused by infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Unusual pericarditis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious pericarditis, as manifested by recurrent or severe inflammation of the pericardium caused by infection, or by pericarditis caused by an unusual organism.

terms.name: Severe pericarditis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious pericarditis, as manifested by severe inflammation of the pericardium with pericardial effusion, tamponade, or constrictive pericarditis.

terms.name: Recurrent pericarditis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious pericarditis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of pericardial inflammation caused by infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Unusual infectious vasculitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to vasculitis caused by infection, as manifested by recurrent or severe vascular inflammation of infectious aetiology, or by infectious vasculitis caused by an unusual organism.

terms.name: Severe infectious vasculitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to vasculitis caused by infection, as manifested by severe vascular inflammation with ischaemia, infarction, or end-organ damage.

terms.name: Recurrent infectious vasculitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to vasculitis caused by infection, as manifested by recurrent episodes of vascular inflammation of infectious etiology that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Bacterial liver abscess
terms.definition: Abscess of the liver caused by bacterial infection. Principal causative agents include Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Bacteroides species, and Staphylococcus aureus.

terms.name: Staphylococcal liver abscess
synonyms: Liver abscess due to Staphylococcus aureus
terms.definition: A liver abscess caused by Staphylococcus aureus infection that may arise from hematogenous spread, biliary infection, or contiguous spread.

terms.name: Klebsiella liver abscess
terms.definition: Abscess of the liver caused by Klebsiella species infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Fungal liver abscess
terms.definition: A liver abscess caused by fungal infection, with common causative organisms including Candida species (often as part of hepatosplenic candidiasis) and Aspergillus species.

terms.name: Hepatic candidiasis
terms.definition: Infection of the liver caused by Candida species that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Parasitic liver abscess
terms.definition: A liver abscess or cystic hepatic lesion caused by parasitic infection, with principal causative organisms being Entamoeba histolytica (amoebic liver abscess) and Echinococcus species (hepatic hydatid disease).

terms.name: Amoebic liver abscess
synonyms: Liver abscess due to Entamoeba histolytica
terms.definition: Abscess of the liver caused by Entamoeba histolytica infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Echinococcal liver cyst
terms.definition: Cystic or alveolar lesion of the liver caused by Echinococcus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Hepatic schistosomiasis
terms.definition: Infection of the liver caused by Schistosoma species, occurring in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection, typically presenting with periportal fibrosis or hepatosplenomegaly.

terms.name: Bacterial splenic abscess
terms.definition: A splenic abscess caused by bacterial infection, typically with organisms such as Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella species, and gram-negative enteric bacteria. It may arise from hematogenous seeding, contiguous spread, or trauma.

terms.name: Fungal splenic abscess
terms.definition: A splenic abscess caused by fungal infection, often as part of hepatosplenic candidiasis.

terms.name: Parasitic splenic abscess
terms.definition: A splenic abscess or cystic splenic lesion caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Echinococcus species (splenic hydatid disease) and Entamoeba histolytica.

terms.name: Unusual infectious gastroenteritis
synonyms: Unusual infectious infection of the gastrointestinal tract
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to gastroenteritis of infectious etiology, as manifested by a recurrent or severe gastroenteritis, a prolonged diarrhoeal illness, or a gastroenteritis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual bacterial gastroenteritis
terms.definition: A gastroenteritis caused by bacterial infection, with common causative organisms including Salmonella species, Shigella species, Campylobacter, and pathogenic Escherichia coli.

terms.name: Unusual viral gastroenteritis
terms.definition: A gastroenteritis caused by viral infection, with common causative organisms including rotavirus, norovirus, adenovirus, astrovirus, and enterovirus.

terms.name: Unusual fungal gastroenteritis
terms.definition: A gastroenteritis caused by fungal infection, most often by Candida species. A fungal gastroenteritis can occur in any host with severely disrupted mucosal immunity or following prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure, and can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual parasitic gastroenteritis
terms.definition: A gastroenteritis caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Giardia lamblia, Cryptosporidium species, and Microsporidia.

terms.name: Unusual infectious colitis
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to colitis of infectious etiology, as manifested by a recurrent or severe colonic infection, or by an infectious colitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual bacterial colitis
terms.definition: A colitis caused by bacterial infection, with common causative organisms including Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, enteroinvasive Escherichia coli, and Clostridioides difficile.

terms.name: Unusual viral colitis
terms.definition: A colitis caused by viral infection, with causative organisms including cytomegalovirus, adenovirus, norovirus, and enterovirus.

terms.name: Unusual fungal colitis
terms.definition: A colitis caused by fungal infection, most commonly by Candida species.

terms.name: Unusual parasitic colitis
terms.definition: A colitis caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Entamoeba histolytica, Cryptosporidium species, and Strongyloides stercoralis.

terms.name: Unusual infectious pancreatitis
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to pancreatitis of infectious etiology, as manifested by a recurrent or severe infectious pancreatitis, or by a pancreatitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual bacterial pancreatitis
terms.definition: A pancreatitis caused by bacterial infection, which may occur as a complication of bacteraemia, ascending biliary infection, or invasive abdominal infection.

terms.name: Unusual viral pancreatitis
terms.definition: A pancreatitis caused by viral infection, with causative organisms including mumps virus, cytomegalovirus, coxsackievirus, and other enteroviruses.

terms.name: Unusual fungal pancreatitis
terms.definition: A pancreatitis caused by fungal infection. Such cases are rare and typically occur as a manifestation of disseminated invasive fungal disease (with Candida or Aspergillus species) in severely immunocompromised hosts.

terms.name: Unusual parasitic pancreatitis
terms.definition: A pancreatitis caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Cryptosporidium species, Ascaris lumbricoides, and Echinococcus species.

terms.name: Unusual bacterial cholangitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to bacterial cholangitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the biliary tract, or by cholangitis occurring in an unusual clinical context such as absence of cholelithiasis or biliary obstruction. Principal causative agents include Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Enterococcus species.

terms.name: Unusual cystitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to cystitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the urinary bladder, or by cystitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual hemorrhagic cystitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to haemorrhagic cystitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe bladder infection with frank haematuria caused by viral or other atypical organisms. Its occurrence is inherently unusual and can indicate significant immune deficiency.

terms.name: Unusual fungal cystitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to fungal cystitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the urinary bladder caused by fungal organisms.

terms.name: Unusual bacterial cystitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to bacterial cystitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the urinary bladder caused by bacteria, or by bacterial cystitis caused by an atypical organism.

terms.name: Unusual pyelonephritis
terms.definition: An inflammation of the kidney involving the renal parenchyma, pelvis, and calices, occurring in a manner unusual for a healthy individual of the same age, as manifested by recurrent or severe episodes of pyelonephritis, or by pyelonephritis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism

terms.name: Unusual kidney abscess
terms.definition: Abscess of the kidney occurring in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection, as manifested by renal abscess caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism, or by renal abscess occurring in the absence of the usual predisposing factors such as urinary tract obstruction or urolithiasis.

terms.name: Bacterial kidney abscess
terms.definition: Abscess of the kidney caused by bacterial infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Fungal kidney abscess
terms.definition: Abscess of the kidney caused by fungal infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Parasitic kidney abscess
terms.definition: Abscess of the kidney caused by parasitic infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual vaginal infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to vaginal infection, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the vagina or vulvovaginal area caused by bacterial, viral, fungal, or parasitic organisms, or by vaginal infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual bacterial vaginal infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to bacterial vaginal infection, as manifested by recurrent or severe bacterial vaginosis or vaginal bacterial infection that is unusual in frequency or severity for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Unusual viral vaginal infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to viral vaginal infection, as manifested by recurrent or severe herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection of the vaginal or vulvovaginal area that can occur in the context of immune deficiency.

terms.name: Unusual fungal vaginal infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to vulvovaginal candidiasis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the vagina or vulvovaginal area caused by Candida species. Predominantly caused by Candida albicans, with Candida glabrata in azole-resistant cases.

terms.name: Unusual parasitic vaginal infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to parasitic vaginal infection, as manifested by recurrent or severe trichomoniasis or other parasitic vaginal infection. A common causative agent is Trichomonas vaginalis, which has been documented in immunocompromised hosts.

terms.name: Unusual bacterial osteomyelitis
terms.definition: An osteomyelitis caused by bacterial infection, with common causative organisms including Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus species, and gram-negative bacilli such as Salmonella and Serratia marcescens.

terms.name: Unusual fungal osteomyelitis
terms.definition: An osteomyelitis caused by fungal infection, with causative organisms including Candida species, Aspergillus species, and the dimorphic fungi.

terms.name: Unusual infectious arthritis
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to arthritis of infectious etiology, as manifested by a recurrent or severe septic arthritis, or by an infectious arthritis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual bacterial arthritis
terms.definition: An arthritis caused by bacterial infection, with common causative organisms including Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus species, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Haemophilus influenzae.

terms.name: Unusual fungal arthritis
terms.definition: An arthritis caused by fungal infection, with causative organisms including Candida species, Aspergillus species, and Cryptococcus.

terms.name: Unusual mycobacterial arthritis
terms.definition: An arthritis caused by mycobacterial infection, with causative organisms including Mycobacterium tuberculosis (tuberculous arthritis) and non-tuberculous mycobacteria.

terms.name: Unusual infectious myositis
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to myositis of infectious aetiology, as manifested by a recurrent or severe inflammation of skeletal muscle caused by infection, or by an infectious myositis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism. Common causative organisms include Staphylococcus aureus (pyomyositis), Streptococcus pyogenes, and Clostridium species (gas gangrene), as well as viral, fungal, and parasitic agents.

terms.name: Unusual bacterial myositis
terms.definition: A myositis caused by bacterial infection, with common causative organisms including Staphylococcus aureus (pyomyositis) and Streptococcus species.

terms.name: Unusual fungal myositis
terms.definition: A myositis caused by fungal infection, with causative organisms including Candida species, Aspergillus species, and the Mucorales. A fungal myositis is rare and typically a manifestation of severe immunocompromise.

terms.name: Unusual mycobacterial myositis
terms.definition: A myositis caused by mycobacterial infection, with causative organisms including Mycobacterium tuberculosis and non-tuberculous mycobacteria.

terms.name: Unusual viral myositis
terms.definition: A myositis caused by viral infection, with causative organisms including enterovirus, influenza virus, coxsackievirus, and HIV.

terms.name: Viral meningitis
terms.definition: A meningitis caused by viral infection, with common causative organisms including herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus, enterovirus, and CMV. A recurrent or chronic viral meningitis (particularly chronic enteroviral meningoencephalitis) can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Bacterial meningitis
terms.definition: A meningitis caused by bacterial infection, with common causative organisms including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Haemophilus influenzae type b. A recurrent or invasive bacterial meningitis with encapsulated organisms can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in antibody deficiencies, complement deficiencies, and asplenia.

terms.name: Parasitic meningitis
terms.definition: A meningitis caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Toxoplasma gondii, Acanthamoeba, and Naegleria fowleri. A parasitic meningitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Mycobacterial meningitis
terms.definition: A meningitis caused by mycobacterial infection, with the principal causative organism being Mycobacterium tuberculosis (tuberculous meningitis). A non-tuberculous mycobacterial meningitis is rare and can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease.

terms.name: Fungal encephalitis
terms.definition: An encephalitis caused by fungal infection, with causative organisms including Cryptococcus neoformans, Aspergillus species, Candida species, and the Mucorales. A fungal encephalitis is most often a manifestation of disseminated invasive fungal disease in severely immunocompromised hosts.

terms.name: Parasitic encephalitis
terms.definition: An encephalitis caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Toxoplasma gondii (toxoplasmic encephalitis), Acanthamoeba, and Naegleria fowleri. A parasitic encephalitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Mycobacterial encephalitis
terms.definition: An encephalitis caused by mycobacterial infection, with the principal causative organism being Mycobacterium tuberculosis (tuberculous encephalitis, often as part of CNS tuberculosis). A mycobacterial encephalitis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease.

terms.name: Bacterial brain abscess
terms.definition: A brain abscess caused by bacterial infection, with causative organisms including Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus species, anaerobes, and gram-negative bacilli. It may arise from contiguous spread (sinusitis, otitis) or hematogenous seeding, and a bacterial brain abscess can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in phagocyte defects.

terms.name: Fungal brain abscess
terms.definition: A brain abscess caused by fungal infection, with causative organisms including Aspergillus species, Cryptococcus, Candida, and the Mucorales. A fungal brain abscess is most often a manifestation of disseminated invasive fungal disease in severely immunocompromised hosts.

terms.name: Parasitic brain abscess
terms.definition: A brain abscess caused by parasitic infection, with causative organisms including Toxoplasma gondii, Entamoeba histolytica, and Echinococcus species. A parasitic brain abscess can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Mycobacterial brain abscess
terms.definition: A brain abscess caused by mycobacterial infection, with the classic manifestation being a tuberculoma caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. A mycobacterial brain abscess can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease.

terms.name: Unusual spinal cord infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection of the spinal cord, as manifested by infectious myelitis, spinal epidural or intradural abscess, or spinal cord compression due to infectious spondylodiscitis occuring in an unusual clinical context such as an atypical causative organism, absence of the usual predisposing factors, or by occurrence in the context of immune deficiency. Principal causative agents include bacteria (Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Mycobacterium tuberculosis), fungi (Aspergillus species, Candida species), and viruses (enteroviruses, VZV, CMV).

terms.name: Unusual bacterial skin infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to bacterial infection of the skin, as manifested by a recurrent or severe cutaneous bacterial infection, or by a skin infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism. Common causative organisms include Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species. A recurrent bacterial skin infection can be a manifestation of phagocyte defects, hyper-IgE syndrome, and atopic dermatitis-related immune defects.

terms.name: Unusual bacterial skin abscess
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to bacterial skin abscesses, as manifested by recurrent, multifocal, or unusually severe collections of pus within the dermis or deeper skin layers. While common causative organisms include Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species, this term also encompasses abscesses caused by opportunistic or atypical bacteria, or those that are refractory to standard antibiotic therapy.

terms.name: Recurrent boils
terms.definition: A recurrent infection of hair follicles producing furuncles (boils), with common causative organisms being Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species. A recurrent boil can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in chronic granulomatous disease, hyper-IgE syndrome (STAT3 deficiency), leukocyte adhesion deficiency, and atopic dermatitis-related immune defects.

terms.name: Bacterial cellulitis
terms.definition: A cellulitis caused by bacterial infection of the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, with common causative organisms including Streptococcus pyogenes and Staphylococcus aureus.

terms.name: Unusual viral skin infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to viral infection of the skin, as manifested by a recurrent or severe cutaneous viral infection, or by a skin infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism. Common causative organisms include herpes simplex virus, varicella-zoster virus, human papillomavirus, and Molluscum contagiosum.

terms.name: Unusual HSV skin infection
terms.definition: A herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection of the skin, which may present as localised vesicular lesions in any host. A severe, persistent, or disseminated cutaneous HSV infection (including eczema herpeticum and chronic ulcerative herpes) can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual parasitic skin infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to parasitic infection of the skin or subcutaneous tissue, as manifested by a recurrent, severe, or atypically distributed parasitic skin lesion, or by a cutaneous parasitic infection occurring in an unusual clinical context. Causative organisms include Leishmania species, Onchocerca volvulus, and Ancylostoma species. An atypical or disseminated cutaneous leishmaniasis can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual VZV skin infection
terms.definition: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) skin infection including chickenpox or herpes zoster that is unusually severe or persistent.

terms.name: Unusual fungal skin infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to fungal infection of the skin or subcutaneous tissue, as manifested by a recurrent, severe, or atypically distributed fungal lesion, or by an infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism. Common manifestations include chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis or subcutaneous mycoses (such as sporotrichosis caused by Sporothrix species.

terms.name: Recurrent diaper rash
terms.definition: Recurrent nappy (diaper) rash of infectious aetiology, typically caused by Candida.

terms.name: Unusual nail infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection of the nail apparatus, including the nail plate, nail bed, nail matrix, and proximal nail fold, as manifested by recurrent or severe nail infection, or by nail infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual bacterial nail bed infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to bacterial infection of the nail bed and proximal nail fold (paronychia), as manifested by recurrent or severe episodes that are unusual in frequency or severity for a healthy individual of the same age. Principal causative agents include Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus species.

terms.name: Unusual HSV infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to herpes simplex virus (HSV) infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with HSV, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent onychomycosis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to recurrent fungal nail infection (onychomycosis), as manifested by recurrent or persistent infection of the nail plate, nail bed, or nail matrix caused by dermatophytes (Trichophyton species) or Candida species.

terms.name: Unusual mycobacterial skin infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to mycobacterial infection of the skin, as manifested by persistent, disseminated, or multifocal cutaneous lesions occurring in an unusual clinical context. This includes skin involvement in tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis) or infections caused by atypical mycobacteria (nontuberculous mycobacteria), such as M. marinum, M. avium complex, or M. chelonae.

terms.name: Unusual fascia infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection of the fascia and surrounding soft tissue, as manifested by necrotizing fasciitis or other invasive fascial infection occurring in an unusual clinical context. Necrotizing fasciitis is a rapidly progressive, life-threatening infection of the superficial fascia and subcutaneous tissue.

terms.name: Unusual cutaneous larva migrans
terms.definition: Infestation of the skin by migrating hookworm larvae (principally Ancylostoma braziliense and Ancylostoma caninum), causing serpiginous, pruritic, erythematous cutaneous tracks. Although typically self-limited in immunocompetent hosts, cutaneous larva migrans may follow a prolonged or atypical course in the context of immune deficiency, including HIV/AIDS and other T-cell defects.

terms.name: Unusual cutaneous leishmaniasis
synonyms: Unusual susceptibility to cutaneous Leishmania infection
terms.definition: Infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue by Leishmania species, as manifested by cutaneous or mucocutaneous leishmaniasis occurring in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection. Cutaneous leishmaniasis presents with chronic, non-healing ulcerative skin lesions.

terms.name: Severe gingivitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to gingivitis, as manifested by severe or necrotising gingival infection, including necrotising ulcerative gingivitis, associated with significant tissue destruction.

terms.name: Recurrent periodontitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to periodontitis, as manifested by recurrent or chronic periodontal infection that is unusual in frequency or severity for a healthy individual of the same age

terms.name: Severe dental abscess
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to dental abscess, as manifested by a severe or invasive dental abscess with systemic spread or requiring hospitalisation.

terms.name: Recurrent dental abscesses
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to dental abscess, as manifested by recurrent episodes of dental abscesses that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Severe stomatitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious stomatitis, as manifested by severe or invasive oral mucosal infection causing necrosis or aphthous ulceration of tissue, or requiring systemic antiviral or antimicrobial therapy.

terms.name: Recurrent stomatitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious stomatitis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of oral mucosal infection that are unusual in frequency or severity for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Unusual oral thrush
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to oral candidiasis caused by Candida albicans, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the oral mucosa, or by oral thrush occurring beyond the neonatal period without an identifiable predisposing cause.

terms.name: Severe oral thrush
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to oral candidiasis, as manifested by severe or invasive oropharyngeal infection with Candida albicans, including extension to the oesophagus or systemic spread.

terms.name: Severe pharyngitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to pharyngitis, as manifested by a severe episode of pharyngeal infection requiring hospitalisation or intravenous antimicrobial therapy, or complicated by peritonsillar abscess, retropharyngeal abscess, or invasive spread.

terms.name: Severe otitis media
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to otitis media, as manifested by a severe episode of middle ear infection requiring hospitalisation, intravenous antibiotics, or surgical intervention, or complicated by mastoiditis, meningitis, or other invasive spread.

terms.name: Severe otitis externa
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to otitis externa, as manifested by a severe or invasive infection of the external ear canal, including necrotising (malignant) otitis externa with involvement of surrounding bone or soft tissue.

terms.name: Recurrent otitis externa
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to otitis externa, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection of the external ear canal that are unusual in frequency or severity for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Unusual conjunctivitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious conjunctivitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the conjunctiva, or by conjunctivitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Severe conjunctivitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious conjunctivitis, as manifested by a severe episode with corneal involvement (keratoconjunctivitis), subepithelial infiltrates, or requiring systemic antiviral or antimicrobial therapy.

terms.name: Recurrent conjunctivitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious conjunctivitis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of conjunctival infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Unusual keratitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious keratitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the cornea, or by keratitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Severe keratitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious keratitis, as manifested by a severe episode of corneal infection with stromal involvement, corneal ulceration, perforation, or significant visual impairment.

terms.name: Recurrent keratitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious keratitis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of corneal infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Unusual retinitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious retinitis, as manifested by recurrent or severe infection of the retina, or by retinitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Severe retinitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious retinitis, as manifested by severe or extensive retinal infection with rapid progression, retinal detachment, or significant visual loss.

terms.name: Recurrent retinitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infectious retinitis, as manifested by recurrent episodes of retinal infection that are unusual in frequency for a healthy individual of the same age.

terms.name: Family history of unusual infection
terms.definition: A family history (in a first- or second-degree relative) of unusually severe, recurrent, or opportunistic infection.

terms.name: Family history of immune deficiency
synonyms: Familiy history of primary immunodeficiency disorders (PID)
Family history of an inborn error of imunity (IEI)
terms.definition: A family history (in a first- or second-degree relative) of an immune deficiency.

terms.name: Family history of autoimmunity
terms.definition: A family history (in a first- or second-degree relative) of an autoimmune disease.

terms.name: Family history of death due to infection
terms.definition: A family history of death of a first- or second-degree relative caused by infection.

terms.name: Family history of lymphoma
terms.definition: A family history (in a first- or second-degree relative) of a lymphoma.

terms.name: Family history of leukaemia
terms.definition: A family history (in a first- or second-degree relative) of a leukaemia.

terms.name: Maternal history of recurrent miscarriage
synonyms: Maternal history of recurrent spontaneous abortion
terms.definition: A maternal history of recurrent miscarriage, defined as two or more pregnancy losses.

terms.name: Unexplained sibling death
terms.definition: Death of a sibling that remains unexplained despite investigation, which may indicate an undiagnosed disease in the family.

terms.name: Consanguinity
terms.definition: A reproductive relationship between two individuals who are related by blood as second cousins or closer. In a medical and genetic context, consanguinity increases the coefficient of inbreeding, raising the probability that an offspring will inherit identical alleles from a common ancestor (homozygosity by descent). This significantly increases the risk for autosomal recessive disorders, such as inborn errors of immunity, metabolic diseases, and rare neurodevelopmental syndromes. A history of consanguinity serves as a vital clinical marker for directing diagnostic investigations toward recessive genetic etiologies, especially in the presence of rare phenotypes or unexplained family medical history.

terms.name: Unusual mycobacterial osteomyelitis
terms.definition: An osteomyelitis caused by mycobacterial infection, with causative organisms including Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Mycobacterium bovis BCG (typically as a complication of BCG vaccination), and non-tuberculous mycobacteria.

terms.name: Unusual musculoskeletal infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection of bones, joints, or muscles, as manifested by recurrent or severe osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, or infectious myositis, or by musculoskeletal infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual infectious osteomyelitis
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to osteomyelitis of infectious aetiology, as manifested by recurrent or severe bone infection, multifocal osteomyelitis, or osteomyelitis caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual lymphatic system infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to infection involving lymph nodes or lymphatic vessels, as manifested by recurrent or severe lymphadenitis or lymph node abscess, or by lymphatic infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism.

terms.name: Unusual oral cavity infection
terms.definition: Infection of the oral cavity including the gingiva, periodontium, teeth, tongue, or oral mucosa that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Post-vaccination mumps
terms.definition: Infection with attenuated mumps vaccine virus following mumps vaccination, occurring in the context of unusual susceptibility to live viral vaccines.

terms.name: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
terms.name_zh: 巨细胞病毒性视网膜炎
terms.definition: Retinitis caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Cytomegalovirus pneumonitis
terms.definition: Pneumonitis caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Cytomegalovirus encephalitis
terms.definition: Encephalitis caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual EBV infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infections as manifested by severe or disseminated disease or impaired control of EBV infection.

terms.name: EBV-driven HLH
terms.name_zh: EB病毒相关噬血细胞性淋巴组织细胞增生症
terms.definition: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) triggered by Epstein-Barr virus infection.

terms.name: Disseminated herpes simplex virus infection
terms.name_zh: 播散性单纯疱疹病毒感染
terms.definition: Disseminated infection with herpes simplex virus (HSV), involving multiple organ systems.

terms.name: Recurrent herpes simplex virus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to herpes simplex virus (HSV) infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of HSV infection.

terms.name: Persistent adenovirus viremia
terms.definition: Persistent or recurrent detection of adenovirus in the blood that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Adenovirus colitis
terms.definition: Colitis caused by adenovirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Adenovirus hepatitis
terms.definition: Hepatitis caused by adenovirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Adenovirus encephalitis
terms.definition: Encephalitis caused by adenovirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Adenovirus pneumonitis
terms.definition: Pneumonitis caused by adenovirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Recurrent chickenpox infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to varicella (chickenpox) infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of chickenpox infection.

terms.name: Severe chickenpox infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to varicella (chickenpox) infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with varicella (chickenpox).

terms.name: VZV encephalitis
terms.definition: Encephalitis caused by varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: VZV pneumonitis
terms.definition: Pneumonitis caused by varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual warts
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to human papillomavirus (HPV) causing warts infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with HPV causing warts, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Disseminated warts
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to human papillomavirus (HPV) manifested by unusually severe, extensive, or invasive warts.

terms.name: Recurrent warts
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to human papillomavirus (HPV), manifested by recurrent episodes of warts.

terms.name: Chronic warts
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to chronic or persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection causing warts that fail to clear over an extended period or recur after treatment that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Persistent molluscum infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Molluscum contagiosum infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of Molluscum contagiosum infection.

terms.name: Unusual norovirus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to norovirus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with norovirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Chronic norovirus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to chronic or persistent norovirus infection, as manifested by prolonged viral shedding and recurrent or unremitting gastrointestinal symptoms beyond the typical course of acute infection.

terms.name: Unusual Aichi virus hepatitis
terms.definition: Hepatitis caused by Aichi virus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual enterovirus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to enterovirus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with enterovirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Enteroviral central nervous system infection
terms.name_zh: 肠道病毒中枢神经系统感染
terms.definition: Infection of the central nervous system by enterovirus that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Enteroviral sepsis
terms.definition: Sepsis or sepsis-like syndrome caused by enterovirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual astrovirus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to astrovirus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with astrovirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Disseminated astrovirus infection
terms.definition: Disseminated infection with astrovirus involving organs beyond the gastrointestinal tract that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Astrovirus central nervous system infection
terms.name_zh: 星状病毒中枢神经系统感染
terms.definition: Infection of the central nervous system by astrovirus that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual influenza infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to influenza virus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with influenza virus.

terms.name: Persitent influenza viremia
terms.definition: Persistent or recurrent detection of influenza virus in the blood or prolonged shedding in respiratory secretions that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual parainfluenza infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to parainfluenza virus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with parainfluenza virus.

terms.name: Recurrent parainfluenza virus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to parainfluenza virus infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of parainfluenza virus infection.

terms.name: Chronic SARS-CoV-2 infection
terms.name_zh: 慢性新型冠状病毒感染
terms.definition: A persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection with prolonged active viral replication and continuous detection of virus beyond the typical duration of acute COVID-19, typically lasting several weeks or longer, often with culturable virus and intra-host viral evolution. A chronic COVID-19 infection is distinct from post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (long COVID), which represents a post-infectious syndrome after viral clearance, and from recurrent COVID-19 reinfections, which are common in the general population.

terms.name: Severe seasonal coronavirus infection
terms.definition: A severe infection caused by a seasonal coronavirus (HCoV-229E, HCoV-OC43, HCoV-NL63, or HCoV-HKU1), characterized by lower respiratory tract involvement, hypoxia, or systemic illness beyond that typically seen with these viruses in immunocompetent hosts.

terms.name: Chronic seasonal coronavirus infection
terms.name_zh: 慢性季节性冠状病毒感染
terms.definition: A persistent infection with a seasonal coronavirus (HCoV-229E, HCoV-OC43, HCoV-NL63, or HCoV-HKU1) with prolonged active viral replication beyond the typical duration of acute infection.

terms.name: Unusual HHV6 infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with HHV-6, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location, such as the brain.

terms.name: Unusual HHV8 infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with HHV-8, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: BK virus nephropathy
synonyms: Nephropathy caused by a Human polyomavirus 1 infection
terms.definition: Nephropathy caused by BK polyomavirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: BK virus encephalitis
synonyms: Encephalitis caused by a Human polyomavirus 1 infection
terms.definition: Encephalitis caused by BK polyomavirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: Unusual JC virus infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to JC polyomavirus infections as manifested by recurrent or severe/invasive infection with JC polyomavirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: JC nephropathy
synonyms: Nephropathy caused by a Human polyomavirus 2 infection
terms.definition: Nephropathy caused by JC polyomavirus infection that occurs in the context of unusual susceptibility to infection.

terms.name: JC encephalitis
synonyms: Encephalitis caused by a Human polyomavirus 2 infection
terms.definition: Encephalitis caused by JC polyomavirus infection, typically presenting as progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML).

terms.name: Infectious granulomatosis
terms.definition: Granulomatous inflammation with multiple granuloma formation attributable to a causative infectious agent, including bacteria, mycobacteria, fungi, or parasites.

terms.name: Non-infectious granulomatosis
terms.definition: Granulomatous inflammation involving the formation of multiple granulomas not attributable to a causative infectious agent, arising in the context of immune dysregulation, foreign-body reactions or idiopathic.

terms.name: Caseating granulomatosis
terms.definition: Granulomatous inflammation characterized by the formation of multiple granulomas exhibiting caseation necrosis, in which the necrotic tissue acquires an amorphous, cheese-like appearance.

terms.name: Non-caseating granulomatosis
terms.definition: Granulomatous inflammation characterized by the formation of multiple granulomas without central caseation necrosis.

terms.name: Granulomatous lymphocytic interstitial lung disease
terms.name_zh: 肉芽肿性淋巴细胞性间质性肺病
terms.definition: An interstitial lung disease, characterized by lymphocytic infiltration and/or granulomatous inflammation of the lung after exclusion of infection and alternative causes, often associated with multisystem inflammatory or granulomatous disease in patients with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID).

terms.name: Granulomatous lymphadenopathy
terms.definition: Lymph node enlargement resulting from granulomatous inflammation, characterized by compact aggregates of epithelioid macrophages and giant cells within the lymph node parenchyma.

terms.name: Granuloma annulare
terms.definition: A non-infectious inflammatory granulomatous dermatosis characterized by annular or disseminated erythematous plaques resulting from palisading granulomas with central mucin deposition in the dermis.

terms.name: Granulomatous synovitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the synovial membrane characterized by granuloma formation within synovial tissue, consisting of aggregates of epithelioid histiocytes with or without multinucleated giant cells.

terms.name: Granulomatous uveitis
terms.definition: Uveitis characterized by granulomatous inflammatory pattern of the uveal tract, with clinical findings that may include large keratic precipitates, iris nodules, or other signs of intraocular granulomatous inflammation.

terms.name: Granulomatous gingivitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the gingiva characterized by granulomatous tissue reaction, with compact aggregates of epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleate giant cells within the gingival lamina propria.

terms.name: Granulomatous iritis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the iris characterized by granulomatous tissue reaction, with compact aggregates of mononuclear phagocytes within the iris stroma.

terms.name: Unusual Burkholderia pseudomallei infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Burkholderia pseudomallei infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Burkholderia pseudomallei, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Unusual coagulase-negative Staphylococcus infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to coagulase-negative staphylococci infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with coagulase-negative staphylococci, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent coagulase-negative Staphylococcus infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to coagulase-negative staphylococci infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of coagulase-negative staphylococci infection.

terms.name: Severe coagulase-negative Staphylococcus infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to coagulase-negative staphylococci infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with coagulase-negative staphylococci.

terms.name: Unusual Enterococcus faecalis infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Enterococcus faecalis infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Enterococcus faecalis, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent Enterococcus faecalis infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Enterococcus faecalis infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.

terms.name: Severe Enterococcus faecalis infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Enterococcus faecalis infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Enterococcus faecalis.

terms.name: Unusual Enterococcus faecium infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Enterococcus faecium infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Enterococcus faecium, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent Enterococcus faecium infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Enterococcus faecium infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.

terms.name: Severe Enterococcus faecium infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Enterococcus faecium infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Enterococcus faecium.

terms.name: Unusual Viridans Streptococci infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to viridans group streptococci infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with viridans group streptococci, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Endocarditis caused by Streptococcus viridans infection
terms.name_zh: 草绿色链球菌感染性心内膜炎
synonyms: Subacute bacterial endocarditis due to viridans streptococci
terms.definition: An endocarditis caused by infection with viridans group streptococci, which are a characteristic causative agent of subacute bacterial endocarditis.

terms.name: Liver abscess due to Streptococcus viridans
terms.name_zh: 草绿色链球菌性肝脓肿
synonyms: Hepatic abscess due to Streptococcus viridans
terms.definition: A liver abscess caused by infection with viridans group streptococci, which may arise from hematogenous spread, biliary infection, or contiguous spread.

terms.name: Unusual Mycobacterium abscessus infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium abscessus infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Mycobacterium abscessus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent Mycobacterium abscessus infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium abscessus infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.

terms.name: Severe Mycobacterium abscessus infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium abscessus infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Mycobacterium abscessus.

terms.name: Unusual Mycobacterium avium complex infection
synonyms: Unusual susceptibility to Mycobacterium avium complex
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium avium complex infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Mycobacterium avium complex, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent Mycobacterium avium complex infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium avium complex infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.

terms.name: Severe Mycobacterium avium complex infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Mycobacterium avium complex infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Mycobacterium avium complex.

terms.name: Unusual Mycoplasma infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Mycoplasma infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Mycoplasma, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent Mycoplasma infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Mycoplasma infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.

terms.name: Severe Mycoplasma infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Mycoplasma infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Mycoplasma.

terms.name: Unusual Ureaplasma infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Ureaplasma infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Ureaplasma, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Pulmonary cryptococcosis
terms.definition: An infection of the lungs caused by Cryptococcus species, which is the most common entry portal for cryptococcal disease and may present as nodules, consolidation, or interstitial infiltrates.

terms.name: Cryptococcoma
terms.definition: A granulomatous mass-like lesion caused by Cryptococcus infection, which may occur in the lung, brain, skin, or other organs.

terms.name: Unusual mucormycosis
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Mucorales infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Mucorales, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Unusual Talaromyces marneffei infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Talaromyces marneffei infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Talaromyces marneffei, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Unusual dermatophyte infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to dermatophytes infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with dermatophytes, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent dermatophyte infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to dermatophytes infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.

terms.name: Increased CD4+ TEMRA T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: CD4+终末分化效应记忆T细胞比例升高
terms.definition: An abnormally increased proportion of CD4-positive TEMRA T cells (terminally differentiated effector memory T cells re-expressing CD45RA), relative to total CD4-positive T cells in the blood. These cells have a CD45RA-positive, CD45RO-negative, CCR7-negative phenotype.

terms.name: Unusual mold infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to mould infection, as manifested by a recurrent or severe invasive infection with filamentous fungi other than Aspergillus, or by a mould infection caused by an atypical or opportunistic organism. Common causative organisms include Fusarium species, Scedosporium species, and Lomentospora prolificans.

terms.name: Unusual Blastomyces dermatitidis infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Blastomyces dermatitidis infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Blastomyces dermatitidis, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent Blastomyces dermatitidis infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Blastomyces dermatitidis infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.

terms.name: Severe Blastomyces dermatitidis infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Blastomyces dermatitidis infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Blastomyces dermatitidis.

terms.name: Unusual Coccidioides infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Coccidioides infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Coccidioides, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent Coccidioides infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Coccidioides infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.

terms.name: Severe Coccidioides infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Coccidioides infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Coccidioides.

terms.name: Unusual Paracoccidioides brasiliensis infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Paracoccidioides brasiliensis infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Paracoccidioides brasiliensis, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Recurrent Paracoccidioides brasiliensis infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Paracoccidioides brasiliensis infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.

terms.name: Severe Paracoccidioides brasiliensis infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Paracoccidioides brasiliensis infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Paracoccidioides brasiliensis.

terms.name: Recurrent Histoplasma capsulatum infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Histoplasma capsulatum infections as manifested by recurrent episodes of infection with this pathogen.

terms.name: Unusual Candida auris infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Candida auris infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with Candida auris, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Chronic Candida auris infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to chronic or persistent Candida auris infection, as manifested by prolonged infection with this multi-drug-resistant emerging Candida species.

terms.name: Severe Candida auris infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to Candida auris infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Candida auris.

terms.name: HSV hepatitis
terms.definition: A hepatitis caused by herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection, which may present as a severe or fulminant hepatitis with elevated transaminases, coagulopathy, and hepatic failure.

terms.name: VZV meningitis
terms.definition: A meningitis caused by varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection, which may occur as part of primary varicella, herpes zoster, or zoster sine herpete (without rash).

terms.name: Giant molluscum
terms.definition: A molluscum contagiosum lesion exceeding one centimetre in diameter, which may present as an unusually large, persistent, or atypical lesion.

terms.name: Unusual HHV7 infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to human herpesvirus 7 (HHV-7) infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with HHV-7, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: BK virus cystitis
terms.definition: A cystitis caused by BK polyomavirus infection, typically presenting as haemorrhagic cystitis with macroscopic haematuria.

terms.name: Unusual poliovirus infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to poliovirus infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with poliovirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Chronic poliovirus excretion
terms.name_zh: 慢性脊髓灰质炎病毒排出
terms.definition: A chronic shedding of poliovirus in stool over an extended period, typically following vaccination with live attenuated oral poliovirus vaccine, with viral excretion persisting for months or years. A chronic poliovirus excretion is characteristic of antibody deficiencies including X-linked agammaglobulinaemia and common variable immunodeficiency, in which patients may shed vaccine-derived poliovirus indefinitely.

terms.name: Severe rotavirus infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to rotavirus infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with rotavirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Unusual respiratory syncytial virus infection
synonyms: Unusual susceptibility to respiratory syncytial virus
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with RSV, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Severe respiratory syncytial virus infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).

terms.name: Chronic respiratory syncytial virus infection
terms.name_zh: 慢性呼吸道合胞病毒感染
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to chronic or persistent respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, as manifested by prolonged viral shedding and persistent or recurrent respiratory symptoms beyond the typical course of acute infection.

terms.name: Chronic rhinovirus infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to rhinovirus infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with rhinovirus, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Unusual human metapneumovirus infection
terms.definition: An increased susceptibility to human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infections as manifested by a recurrent or severe/invasive infection with hMPV, or occurring in an unusual anatomical location.

terms.name: Toxoplasma eye infection
terms.definition: An ocular infection caused by Toxoplasma gondii, typically presenting as chorioretinitis with characteristic retinal lesions and potential progression to vision loss.

terms.name: BCG-associated disease
terms.definition: An adverse disease following vaccination with the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) live attenuated Mycobacterium bovis vaccine, ranging from local BCGitis (regional lymphadenitis or injection-site abscess) to disseminated BCGosis. BCG associated disease can be a manifestation of unusual susceptibility to infection, particularly in severe combined immunodeficiency, Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (MSMD), and chronic granulomatous disease.

terms.name: Abnormal effector memory CD4+ T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: 效应记忆CD4+T细胞比例异常
terms.definition: An abnormal proportion of effector memory CD4-positive memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These are memory cells that are short-lived cells that migrate to the site of an infection and attempt to eliminate the pathogen. These cells may have a CD3/CD4/CD62L-/CD45RA phenotype.

terms.name: Abnormal central memory CD4+ T cell proportion
terms.name_zh: 中央记忆CD4+T细胞比例异常
terms.definition: An abnormal proportion of central memory CD4-positive memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

terms.name: Decreased total T cell number
synonyms: Decreased numbers of circulating T cells
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of absolute number (either count per volume or proportion of total lymphocytes) of T cells or of a subset of T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.

terms.name: Increased total T cell number
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of absolute number (either count per volume or proportion of total lymphocytes) of T cells or of a subset of T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.

terms.name: Decreased total T cell proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease in the proportion of T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, measured as a percentage of total lymphocytes in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.

terms.name: Increased total T cell proportion
terms.definition: Abnormal increase in the proportion of T cells, commonly characterized as CD3+ lymphocytes, measured as a percentage of total lymphocytes in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These may include both TCR alpha/beta and gamma/delta T cells.

terms.name: Decreased total CD4+ T cell number
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of absolute number of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells (either count per volume or percentage of total lymphocytes), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Increased CD4+ T cell number
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of absolute number of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells (either count per volume or percentage of total lymphocytes), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Increased total CD4+ T cell count
synonyms: Increased circulating CD4+ T cell count
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of absolute count of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells (quantified as count per volume), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Decreased total CD4+ T cell count
synonyms: Decreased circulating CD4+ T cell count
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of absolute count of helper CD3+CD4+ T cells (quantified as count per volume), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Autoimmune cytopenia
terms.name_zh: 自身免疫性血细胞减少
terms.definition: A reduction in one or more peripheral blood cell lineages resulting from immune-mediated destruction or impairment caused by an autoimmune process.

terms.name: Severe eczema
terms.definition: A severe form of eczema characterised by extensive skin involvement and/or persistent or recurrent symptoms requiring intensive treatment.

terms.name: Autoimmune hepatitis
terms.definition: A chronic inflammatory liver disease characterised by immune-mediated hepatocellular injury resulting from an autoimmune process.

terms.name: Non-infectious encephalitis
terms.definition: A disorder of the brain not caused by an infectious agent, characterised by inflammation of the brain parenchyma. It may present with an altered level of consciousness, focal or multifocal neurologic deficits, and seizures; unlike infectious encephalitis, fever is often absent, and autoimmune forms frequently present subacutely with cognitive, psychiatric, or behavioural changes.

terms.name: Autoimmune encephalitis
terms.definition: An inflammation of the brain parenchyma caused by an autoimmune process directed against neuronal or glial antigens.

terms.name: Increased total CD8+ T cell number
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of the absolute number of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells (measured the absolute count per volume or as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Decreased total CD8+ T cell number
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of the absolute number of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells (measured the absolute count per volume or as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood), compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Decreased total CD8+ T cell count
synonyms: Decreased circulating CD8+ T cell count
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells, measured as the total count per volumne in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: Increased total CD8+ T cell count
terms.definition: Abnormal increase of cytotoxic CD3+CD8+ T cells, measured as the total count per volumne in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

terms.name: HSV pneumonia
synonyms: Pneumonia due to herpes simplex virus
terms.definition: Infection of the lung parenchyma with herpes simplex virus, resulting in inflammation of the lung parenchyma with impaired respiratory function.

terms.name: Recurrent Haemophilus influenzae conjunctivitis
terms.definition: Recurrent episodes of conjunctivitis caused by infection with Haemophilus influenzae, characterised by inflammation of the conjunctiva associated with conjunctival injection and purulent ocular discharge.

terms.name: Hindfoot deformity
terms.definition: A structural deformity of the hindfoot, the posterior region of the foot formed by the talus and calcaneus.

terms.name: Left-right disorientation
terms.definition: A tendency to mix up left and right in one's own body space, typically elicited by asking a person to perform a two-stage command involving specified lateralized anatomy.

terms.name: Elevated circulating DNAJB9 concentration
synonyms: DNAJB9 protein level in serum elevated
Elevated DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 concentration
Elevated DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 level
Elevated DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 level in blood
Increased DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 concentration
Increased DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 level
Increased DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 level in blood
terms.definition: The concentration of DNAJB9 in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Olecranon fracture
terms.definition: A partial or complete break in the olecranon,which is the proximal articular portion of the ulna and makes up part of the elbow.

terms.name: History of mastectomy
terms.definition: Past medical history of surgical breast removal.

terms.name: Lymphangiosarcoma
terms.definition: A malignant neoplasm arising from the endothelial cells of the lymphatic vessels.

terms.name: Exposure to inhaled lipids
terms.definition: Aspiration or inhalation of lipid-containing products.

terms.name: Holster sign
terms.definition: Symmetric poikiloderma of hips and lateral thighs below the greater trochanter.

terms.name: Salivary basal cell adenoma
terms.definition: A rare neoplasm consisting of a monomorphic population of basaloid epithelial cells, and it accounts for approximately 1-2% of all salivary gland tumors.

terms.name: Hemidiaphragm elevation
terms.definition: Elevated Hemidiaphragm is a condition where one portion of the diaphragm is higher than the other. Elevated hemidiaphragm occurs when one side of the diaphragm becomes weak from muscular disease or loss of innervation due to phrenic nerve injury.

terms.name: Cerebriform connective tissue nevus
terms.definition: The cerebriform connective tissue nevus (CCTN) is one of the most characteristic skin findings. It commonly occurs on the soles of the feet, and frequently causes problems because of pain, pruritus, infection, bleeding,exudation, odor, and walking impairment.

terms.name: Linear Hyperpigmentation along Blaschko's lines
terms.definition: Linear streaks and swirls of macular hyperpigmentation along the lines of Blaschko.

terms.name: Guilt
terms.definition: The experience of remorse, self-reproach, or perceived culpability for a real or perceived unfavorable outcome. Guilt may be proportionate to the context or disproportionate, and it may occur in the absence of an identifiable act, event, or offense. It reflects the interplay of cognitive processes, such as judgments about responsibility, and emotional responses, which can lead to persistent rumination or preoccupation. Guilt may extend to situations outside the individual's control and, in some cases, be accompanied by inaccurate or exaggerated beliefs about one's role in an outcome.

terms.name: Mediastinal shift
terms.definition: A deviation of the mediastinum from its normal position in the midline of the thoracic cavity. The mediastinum is a compartment of the thoracic cavity that contains the heart and its blood vessels, the esophagus, trachea, thymus, as well as nerves and lymph nodes.

terms.name: Bendopnea
terms.definition: Dyspnea as a result of bending forward while not holding one's breath; dyspnea or shortness of breath onset within 30 seconds of bending forward.

terms.name: Pain worse when lying flat
terms.definition: Refers to pain that is worse when the affected individual lies down (flat).

terms.name: Tympanic membrane hypermobility
terms.definition: Abnormally increased ability to move of the tympanic membrane.

terms.name: Elevated circulating vitamin B12 concentration
terms.definition: Concentration of vitamin B12 in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating sFASL concentration
terms.name_zh: 血可溶性FAS配体浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of sFASL (soluble FASL, soluble FAS-ligand) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Internal anal sphincter achalasia
terms.name_zh: 肛门内括约肌失弛缓症
terms.definition: A disorder of the internal anal sphincter (IAS) in which the IAS fails to relax that manifests clinically as intractable constipation.

terms.name: Anthracycline exposure
terms.definition: History of treatment with an anthracycline chemotherapy agent.

terms.name: Binge drinking
terms.definition: A pattern of episodic heavy alcohol use characterized by the consumption of a high number of drinks per occasion.

terms.name: Decreased circulating thrombopoietin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血血小板生成素浓度降低
terms.definition: Concentration of thrombopoietin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal. Thrombopoietin is a glycoprotein hormone produced by the liver and kidney that stimulates the production and differentiation of megakaryocytes.

terms.name: Collagenoma
terms.definition: A rare hamartomatous malformation characterized by the predominant proliferation of normal collagen fibers and normal, decreased, or increased elastic fibers. Collagenomas may be solitary or multiple, sporadic, acquired or inherited.

terms.name: Lack of sufficient daily physical activity
terms.definition: Physical activity levels less than those required for optimal health and prevention of premature death.

terms.name: Synesthesia
terms.definition: A phenomenon whereby stimulation of one sensory or cognitive pathway leads to automatic, involuntary experiences in a second sensory or cognitive pathway. For instance, people with synaesthesia may experience unusual colors, tastes, and other sensations when engaged in everyday activities like reading or listening to music.

terms.name: Dark cerumen
terms.definition: Abnormally dark color of cerumen (earwax), which is a waxy substance secreted in the ear canal that normally has a brown, orange, red, yellowish or gray.

terms.name: History of spicy food intake
