Desmoid tumors do not metastasize but can arise in any part of the body: extra-abdominal (appear in the head and neck, chest, extremities), and abdominal wall or intra-abdominal (originating in tissue that connects abdominal organs).

terms.name: Tubular jejunal duplication
terms.definition: A segment of the jejunum that runs parallel to the normal jejunum and communicates with the jejunal lumen at one or both ends.

terms.name: Left ventricular rupture
terms.definition: A full thickness tear or breakage of the myocardium of the left ventricle.

terms.name: Punctate pontine perivascular enhancement
terms.definition: Multiple punctate (speckled, patchy spot-like) and/or curvilinear areas of gadolinium enhancement distributed around blood vessels in the pons.

terms.name: Intestinal worm
terms.definition: Presence of one or more adult worms in the intestine as demonstrated by sonography or passage of a worm in the stool. On sonography, worms may appear as linear, echogenic structures within the intestines.

terms.name: Scrotal worm
terms.definition: Demonstration of one or more worms in the scrotum. This finding can be appreciated by sonography, where echogenic, linear structures could be seen moving within the scrotum.

terms.name: Small intestinal adenoma
terms.definition: A small bowel tumor with adenomatous epithelium.

terms.name: Maternal retinal mottling
terms.name_zh: 母体视网膜斑驳样改变
terms.definition: Mottling (spots or blotches with different shades) of the retinal pigment epithelium in the mother of the index patient. Retinal mottling may indicate a mosaic X-linked inactivation state in the mother.

terms.name: Twisted gallbladder pedicle
synonyms: Conical structure at the gallbladder neck
terms.definition: A stretched conical-shaped structure found at the gallbladder neck with several linear echoes converging towards its tip. This finding is demonstrated by sonography and can indicate gallbladder volvulus.

terms.name: Cholecyst-enteric fistula
terms.definition: Fistula between the gallbladder and the intestine.

terms.name: Dyschronometria
terms.definition: Impaired ability to accurately measure or estimate time intervals.

terms.name: History of recent intermittent breastfeeding
terms.definition: History of recently intermittent breastfeeding an infant (i.e., on and off).

terms.name: Breast cyst
terms.definition: A benign, fluid-filled sac in the breast.

terms.name: Circumscribed
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance are well-defined and localized to a specific area.

terms.name: Lobulated
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality that displays multiple indentations and/or elevations producing an irregular surface contour.

terms.name: Spiculated
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality with irregular, radiating, or spiky edges.

terms.name: Whorled
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance resembles series of a concentric circles or spirals.

terms.name: Delta brush pattern on EEG
terms.definition: Delta brushes are transient patterns characterised by a slow delta wave with superimposed fast activity.

terms.name: Tibiotalar synostosis
terms.definition: Fusion of the junction between the distal tibia, fibula and the talus.

terms.name: Vertebra plana
terms.definition: he term given when a vertebral body has lost almost its entire height anteriorly and posteriorly, representing a very advanced compression fracture.

terms.name: Intoeing
terms.definition: An abnormal gait caused by a rotational variation anywhere in the lower extremity that causes the foot to point inward, instead of pointing straight ahead or outward, when walking or running.

terms.name: Palpable thrill on extremity
terms.definition: A vibration felt upon palpation of a blood vessel over an extremity.

terms.name: Out-toeing
terms.definition: The feet turn excessively outward when walking, caused by a rotational variation in the leg.

terms.name: Ankle dislocation
terms.definition: An abnormal separation between the talo-tibial joint.

terms.name: Anti-neuronal intermediate filament antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗神经元中间丝抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against neuronal intermediate filament.

terms.name: Anti-DREBRIN antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗脑发育调节蛋白抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against dendritic spine scaffolding protein Drebrin.

terms.name: Anti-lipoprotein lipase autoantibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗脂蛋白脂酶自身抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against anti-lipoprotein lipase.

terms.name: Anti-apolipoprotein CII autoantibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗载脂蛋白CII自身抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against apoCII.

terms.name: Eosinophilic neuronal inclusion bodies
terms.definition: The presence of intracellular inclusion bodies (aggregates of stainable substances, usually proteins) in neurons that stain with eosin, a red or pink dye.

terms.name: Sweaty foot-like odor
terms.definition: A characteristic smell said to resemble the odor of dirty socks.

terms.name: Anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 抗乙酰胆碱受体抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against acetylcholine receptor.

terms.name: Hair shaft lesion
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality that is located on hair shafts.

terms.name: Prolonged use of tightly fitting footwear
terms.definition: History of use of tightly fitting shoes for a long period of time.

terms.name: Triggered by high protein intake
terms.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about ingestion of high quantities of protein.

terms.name: Thickened tricuspid valve cusp
terms.definition: An abnormally increased thickness of a leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

terms.name: Displaced anterior fontanelle
terms.definition: Abnormal shifting of the anterior fontanelle fropm its normal central position.

terms.name: Subdural hygroma
terms.definition: Accumulation of cerebral spinal fluid in the subdural space.

terms.name: Incus ankylosis
terms.definition: Incus ankylosis refers to congenital or acquired fixation of the incus, which is associated with conductive hearing resulting from impairment of the sound-conduction mechanism (the external auditory canal, tympanic membrane, and/or middle-ear ossicles).

terms.name: Excessive diet restriction
terms.definition: A tendency to reject a variety of foods and/or to eat a restricted range of foods.

terms.name: Left ventricular apical dyskinesis
terms.name_zh: 左心室心尖部运动障碍
terms.definition: Dyskinesis is used to describe ventricular muscle segments that bulge outside the left ventricular cavity during systole, as opposed to contracting inwards with the rest of the segments.

terms.name: Longitudinal erythronychia
terms.definition: A longitudinal red band extending from the proximal nail fold or lunula to the distal nail plate.

terms.name: Exacerbated by exposure to sunlight
terms.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by exposure to sunlight.

terms.name: Exacerbated by heat
terms.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is made worse by exposure to heat (high ambient temperatures).

terms.name: Exacerbated by excessive sweating
terms.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is made worse by excessive sweating.

terms.name: Malignant pleural effusion
terms.definition: The accumulation of a significant amount of exudate in the pleural space, accompanied by the presence of malignant cells or tumour tissue.

terms.name: Inappropriately low urine osmolality following challenge
terms.name_zh: 激发后尿渗透压不当降低
terms.definition: In diabetes insipidus, affected individuals produce large quantities of dilute urine. In nephrogenic DI, the kidneys do not respond to vasopressin. In a water deprivation test or with administration of exogenous vasopressin, the osmolaltiy of the urine does not increase as normally.

terms.name: Reduced urine tetrahydrocortisol plus 5-alpha-THF to tetrahydrocortisone ratio
terms.definition: Abnormally low ratio of tetrahydrocortisol (THF) plus 5-alpha-THF to tetrahydrocortisone (THE).

terms.name: Elevated urinary 2,4-dihydroxyglutarate level
terms.name_zh: 尿2,4-二羟基戊二酸水平升高
terms.definition: The amount of 2,4-dihydroxyglutarate in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal urine D-xylose test
terms.definition: An abnormal result of the xylose absorption test that is used to assess the ability of the intestines to absorb D-xylose. D-xylose is a five-carbon monosaccharide found in some plants. The patient drinks a solution containing a specific amount of D-xylose and the concentration of xylose is measured in the blood circulation and then in the urine. A low amount of D-xylose indicates reduced small intestinal absorbtion.

terms.name: Cerebral hemisphere mass lesion
terms.definition: An abnormal growth or accumulation of tissue in a hemisphere of the cerebrum. Typically a mass is an initial finding that will lead to additional workup.

terms.name: T2-hyperintense putaminal rim
terms.definition: Increased signal on T2 magnetic resonance imaging characterized by a linear region of high signal surrounding the lateral aspect of the putamen at 1.5 Tesla.

terms.name: Posterior fossa mass lesion
terms.definition: An abnormal growth or accumulation of tissue in the posterior fossa, affecting the cerebellum or fourth ventricle. Typically a mass is an initial finding that will lead to additional workup.

terms.name: Irregular RR interval
terms.definition: Abnormal increased variability in the timing between consecutive R-waves on an electrocardiogram.

terms.name: Irregular P-P interval
terms.definition: Abnormally increased variability in the timing between consecutive P-waves on an electrocardiogram.

terms.name: Fungal hair infection
terms.definition: Demonstration of fungi growing on hair by a method such as microscopy of hairs mounted on slides with 10% potassium hydroxide.

terms.name: Long hairstyle
terms.definition: A past medical history of having long, full hair.

terms.name: Conjunctival subepithelial fibrosis
terms.definition: fine white linear scars under intact conjunctival epithelium. This scarring appears in areas of previous conjunctival ulceration or pseudomembrane formation, weeks to months after the insult is healed.

terms.name: Conjunctival fornix foreshortening
terms.definition: Abnormal reduction in depth of the fornix of the conjunctiva. The fornix is the area where the conjunctiva folds back upon itself, thereby creating a recessed space.

terms.name: Strong ultraviolet light exposure
terms.definition: History of exposure to ultraviolet light, such as may be encountered with outdoor activities, living near equator, radiation.

terms.name: Exposure to vaginal douching
terms.definition: A history of intravaginal cleansing with a liquid solution for personal hygiene or aesthetic reasons.

terms.name: Exposure to oily lotions or creams
terms.definition: A history of applying oily lotions or creams to the skin.

terms.name: Elevated circulating pristanic acid concentration following branched-chain fatty acid ingestion
terms.name_zh: 支链脂肪酸摄入后血降植烷酸浓度升高
terms.definition: Concentration of pristanic acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. This finding can be observed in Zellweger syndrome. Note that branched-chain fatty acid accumulation depends on dietary intake of phytanic acid, which is minimal in formula- and breast-fed infants. Thus, phytanic and pristanic acid levels are normal in a neonate with Zellweger spectrum disorder.

terms.name: Decreased CD4+ T cell ZAP-70 protein expression
synonyms: Decreased T-cell ZAP-70 protein expression in CD4-positive T cells
terms.definition: Reduction in the level of ZAP-70 protein CD4-positive T cells.

terms.name: Dorsal flexion contracture of the ankle
terms.definition: A type of contracture in which the dorsal flexion muscles of the ankle are contracted.

terms.name: Metaphyseal undermodelling
terms.definition: Lack of the normal diaphyseal constriction (thinning of long bones toward the midshaft area) giving the submetaphyseal areas an abnormally wide appearance.

terms.name: Iliac vein compression
terms.definition: Compression of the common iliac vein against the spine by the contralateral common iliac artery.

terms.name: Positive serum amyloid P scintigraphy
terms.definition: Detection of abnormal amyloid deposits in the body by 123I-labeled serum amyloid P component (SAP) scintigraphy.

terms.name: Crossed brainstem sign
terms.definition: Motor and/or sensory cranial nerve findings ipsilateral to the lesion, and at the same time motor and/or sensory findings on the contralateral side of the body.

terms.name: Inability to puff cheeks
terms.definition: Reduced ability to inflate the cheeks by blowing air into them while keeping the lips closed.

terms.name: Entoptic phenomenon
terms.definition: Visual sensations caused by changes within the eye itself, rather than by the normal light stimulation process. Entoptic phenomena are classified in the syndrome as floaters, blue field entoptic phenomenon, photopsia and self-light of the eye.

terms.name: Abnormal vestibulo-spinal reflex
terms.definition: An abnormality of the vestibulospinal (VS) reflexes, which contribute to the control of postural orientation. In this task, they continuously collaborate with reflexes elicited by stimulation of visual and somatosensory receptors. Labyrinthine receptors are sensitive to modifications (i) of the head position with respect to the earth vertical or (ii) of the angular/linear velocity of head motion in space. This information can be used to monitor deviations from the maintained body position.

terms.name: Positive probe-to-bone test
terms.definition: An abnormal result of the probe-to-bone (PTB) test. The PTB test is performed by inserting a sterile, metal surgical probe into the ulcer and is positive if a hard, gritty surface is felt inside. For large wounds, this may require gentle exploration of the wound with the probe.

terms.name: Exposure to repetitive hand impact
terms.definition: A history of exposure to repetitive impact on palm or hand, such as working with a jackhammer.

terms.name: Fractured scaphoid bone
terms.definition: A partial or complete breakage of the scaphoid bone.

terms.name: Local anesthetic ineffectiveness
terms.definition: Resistance to the effects of local anaesthesia, with delayed onset or failure of local anesthetics to incude numbness or relieve pain.

terms.name: Palmoplantar location
terms.definition: Applied to lesions whose distribution is confined or restricted to the palms of the hands and soles of the feet.

terms.name: Oral mucosa plaque
terms.definition: A raised, flat-topped lesion with a diameter of one centimeter or more that is located in the mucosa of the mouth.

terms.name: Positive saliva rabies nucleic acid test
terms.definition: Detection of rabies nucleic acid in saliva by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.

terms.name: Elevated tissue arylsulfatase A activity
terms.name_zh: 组织芳基硫酸酯酶A活性升高
terms.definition: Activity of arylsulfatase A (EC 3.1.6.8) above the upper limit of normal. The activity can be measured in multiple tissues including culutured fibroblasts and leukocytes or in the blood circulation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating methysterol concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环甲基甾醇浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of a methysterol in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated urinary adipic acid
terms.definition: The amount of adipic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal. Adipic acid is an alpha,omega-dicarboxylic acid that is the 1,4-dicarboxy derivative of butane.

terms.name: EEG with temporal slowing
synonyms: EEG with slow activity in temporal lobes
EEG with slow-wave activity involving the temporal lobes
terms.definition: Slow-wave activity observed in the temporal area of the scalp electro-encephalogram (EEG).

terms.name: History of high-pressure injection injury of the hand
terms.definition: Medical history of the hand having come into contact with the nozzle of a high-pressure injecting system such as a paint gun or air compressor.

terms.name: Hypertrophic ulnar styloid process
terms.definition: Excessively long styloid process of the ulna.

terms.name: History of recent peripheral venous catheter
terms.name_zh: 近期外周静脉导管置管史
terms.definition: A history of placement of a peripehral venous catheter in the hours, days, or weeks before the current presenting complaint.

terms.name: Purulent drainage from skin
terms.definition: Exudation of a thick, opaque fluid from a wound or skin lesion, typically as a result of infection and draining pus, i.e., dead white blood cells, bacteria, and tissue debris.

terms.name: Occupational history of putting fingers in other people's mouths
terms.definition: A history of exposure of fingers by putting them in other peoples' mouths occupationally, e.g., as a dentist or physician.

terms.name: Single-finger involvement
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance are limited to or predominantly affect a single finger.

terms.name: Multiple-finger involvement
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance affect more than one finger.

terms.name: Pain disproportionate to abnormality on physical exam
terms.definition: Exquisite tenderness in a specific region, beyond what one would surmise from examination.

terms.name: Sphenoid wing dysplasia
terms.definition: Hypoplasia or aplasia of the greater or lesser wing of the sphenoid bone, typically resulting in widening of the superior orbital fissure, elevation of the [lesser sphenoid wing, and ipsilateral orbital enlargement.

terms.name: Skin laceration
terms.definition: An injury in which skin and underlying tissues are cut or torn.

terms.name: Metacarpal fracture
terms.definition: A partial or complete breakage of a metacarpal bone.

terms.name: Pain at the base of the thumb
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort localized to the base of the thumb, over thenar eminence or thumb metacarpal.

terms.name: History of recent participation in athletics
terms.definition: Medical history of participation in sports (football, basketball, soccer, skiing) in the hours, days, or weeks prior to the current presenting complaint.

terms.name: Remote trauma history
terms.definition: History of trauma months to years ago, including but not limited to fracture or other orthopedic injury at the symptomatic area.

terms.name: Distal radioulnar joint arthritis
synonyms: Arthritis of the distal radioulnar joint
terms.definition: An inflammatory condition of the joint that connects the far ends of the radius and the ulna, known as the distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ). DRUJ arthritis may be characterized by widening of the DRUJ interval, volar/dorsal displacement of the distal ulna, radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis at the DRUJ joint including osteophytes, subchondral cysts, subchrondal sclerosis, and joint space narrowing.

terms.name: Radial head fracture
terms.definition: Fracture of the proximal end of the radius involving the radial head.

terms.name: Elbow lateral collateral ligament tear
synonyms: Ligamentous tear on the lateral aspect of the elbow
terms.definition: An injury to the lateral collateral ligament (LCL) of the elbow. The LCL is a complex capsuloligamentous structure critical in stabilizing the ulnohumeral and radiocapitellar articulations. LCL injury can result in elbow instability, allowing the proximal radius and ulna to externally rotate away from the humerus as a supination stress is applied to the forearm.

terms.name: Elbow medial collateral ligament tear
synonyms: Ligamentous tear on the medial aspect of the elbow
terms.definition: An injury to the medial collateral ligament (MCL) of the elbow.

terms.name: Coronoid fracture
terms.definition: Fracture of the coronoid process on the proximal ulna.

terms.name: History of spinal cord injury
terms.definition: A medical history of hving had a spinal cord injury prior to the presenting complaint.

terms.name: Femoral nerve distribution
terms.definition: Paresthesias in anterior/medial aspect of the thigh (anterior and medial cutaneous nerves of the thigh) and/or medial aspect of the lower leg and foot (saphenous distribution). May be accompanied by weakness in the quadriceps.

terms.name: Triceps tendon rupture
terms.definition: Breakage (tear) of the triceps tendon.

terms.name: Digoxin exposure
terms.definition: History of having been treateed with digoxin.

terms.name: Upper arm pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the upper arm.

terms.name: Capitellum fracture
terms.definition: A partial or complete breakage of the capitulum of the humerus, which is a smooth, rounded eminence on the lateral portion of the distal articular surface of the humerus.

terms.name: Anterior shoulder pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the anterior (front) part of the shoulder.

terms.name: Pain at the anterior aspect of the elbow
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the front part of the elbow front part of the elbow, that is, on the ventral side of the arm where the arm bends.

terms.name: Posterior fat pad sign of the elbow
terms.definition: Lateral elbow x-ray showing lucent crescent of fat that indicates a joint effusion in the elbow .

terms.name: Pain at the anterior aspect of the knee
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the front part of the knee, that is, the side of the knee where the patella is located.

terms.name: Pain at the posterior aspect of the knee
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the back part of the knee, that is, opposite to the side of the knee where the patella is located.

terms.name: Biceps tendonitis
terms.definition: Biceps tendinitis is inflammation of the tendon around the long head of the biceps muscle.

terms.name: Increased peripheral nerve cross sectional area
terms.name_zh: 周围神经横截面积增大
terms.definition: Ultrasonography showing increased cross sectional area (CSA) of a peripheral nerve as it travels through a potential site of compression.

terms.name: Pain exacerbated by passive flexion at joint
terms.definition: Pain in extremity that worsens with joint is passively flexed.

terms.name: Positive hook test at the elbow
terms.definition: With forearm fully supinated and elbow flexed to 90 degrees, examiner hooks a finger a bit around the distal biceps tendon at the anterior aspect of the elbow. Test is positive when there is lack of appreciable cord like structure to hook around.

terms.name: Positive Speed's test
terms.definition: Manual downward pressure on the arm with the shoulders flexed forward to 90 degrees, elbows fully extended, and palm facing up recreates pain in the anterior shoulder region; named after Dr. Speed.

terms.name: Triangular lunate bone
synonyms: Piece of pie sign of lunate bone
terms.definition: A disruption of the greater and lesser arcs of the lunate bone, with the lunate having a triangular silhouette, know as the piece of pie sign. Often caused by falling on an outstretched hand, patients will have tenderness to palpation over the dorsum of the wrist and may have sensory deficits in the median nerve distribution.

terms.name: Pain exacerbated by wrist deviation
terms.definition: Pain worsens with wrist ulnar or radial deviation.

terms.name: Pain on the lateral aspect of the foot
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the side of the foot nearest to the little (fifth) toe.

terms.name: Pain at the medial aspect of the knee
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the inner side of knee, that is, the region of the knee that faces the other knee.

terms.name: Pain at the lateral aspect of the knee
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the outer side of knee, that is, the region of the knee that faces away from the other knee.

terms.name: Occupational exposure to frequent kneeling
terms.definition: A history of exposure to frequent squatting/kneeling and/or heavy lifting.

terms.name: Trochanteric pain
synonyms: Pain at the lateral aspect of the hip
Pain on the outside of the hip
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the structures around the greater trochanter (the bony prominence on the outer part of the femur).

terms.name: Pulsatile mass in extremity
terms.definition: A noticeable lump or swelling in the arm or leg that you can feel with you fingers and this lump is beating or pulsating, similar to the feeling of a heartbeat.

terms.name: Abnormal R wave
terms.definition: Any anomaly of the R wave of the EKG, which is the first upward deflection after the P wave. The R wave reflects early ventricular depolarisation.

terms.name: Poor R-wave progression
terms.definition: Absence of the normal increase in size of the R wave in the precordial leads when advancing from lead V1 to V6 of the electrocardiogram.

terms.name: Prominent V1-V2 R wave
synonyms: High voltage R wave in V1/V2
Prominent R wave in lead V1
terms.definition: The R wave in leads V1-V2 is normally considerably smaller in amplitude than the S wave in the same leads. Prominent R wave in these leads implies the R wave is larger than the S-wave, which may indicate cardiovascular pathology. This term includes Tall R wave in lead V1, which is defined by a R/S ratio greater than 1.

terms.name: Finger mass
terms.definition: An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to a finger.

terms.name: Foot mass
terms.definition: An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to a foot.

terms.name: Abnormal retinal vein morphology
terms.definition: A condition characterized by structural abnormalities of the retinal veins, including tortuosity, dilation, narrowing, or irregularities in branching patterns. These changes may be associated with systemic or ocular diseases such as retinal vein occlusion, diabetic retinopathy, or hypertensive retinopathy.

terms.name: Spongiosis
terms.definition: Spongiosis refers to the increased intercellular edema in the epidermis resulting in the pulling away of the keratinocytes from their surrounding desmosomes. Histologically, the spongiotic tissue reaction pattern involves the accumulation of fluid in the intercellular spaces of the epidermis, making the desmosomes junctions more easy to appreciate. Parakeratosis forms above the areas of spongiosis. The foci of spongiosis can be microscopic to grossly identifiable clinically with vesicles or bullae.

terms.name: Discoid adrenal gland
terms.definition: A congenital finding where the adrenal gland does not form it's typical triangular, Y or V shape and is instead discoid, straight or elongated in shape. It is often found incidentally on renal ultrasound and is associated with renal agenesis and other renal congenital anomalies.

terms.name: Abnormal optic disc vasculature morphology
terms.name_zh: 视盘脉管系统形态异常
terms.definition: A structural abnormality in the blood vessels of the optic disc, including bleeding, tortuosity, dilation, shunting, or other unusual branching patterns.

terms.name: Supraclavicular nerve distribution
terms.definition: Localization of symptoms such as numbness or paresthesias on the skin over the upper chest, specifically above the clavicle and over the lateral aspect of the neck, corresponding to the distribution of the supraclavicular nerve.

terms.name: Limited shoulder internal rotation
terms.definition: Difficulty rotating the lower part of the arm towards the body (tested with the elbow flexed and the elbow held next to the side of the body or shoulder 90 degrees abducted to the side) secondary to pain, weakness, or mechanical block.

terms.name: Superior displacement of the humeral head
synonyms: Proximal subluxation of the humeral head
terms.definition: An anterior posterior (AP) shoulder radiograph shows distance between the the proximal aspect of the humeral head and inferior aspect of the acromion of less than 7 mm.

terms.name: Increased compartment pressure
terms.definition: intracompartmental pressure (ICP) over 30 mmHg. Acute compartment syndrome occurs when there is increased pressure within a closed osteofascial compartment, resulting in impaired local circulation. Acute compartment syndrome is considered a surgical emergency since, without proper treatment, it can lead to ischemia and eventually necrosis. Generally, acute compartment syndrome is considered a clinical diagnosis. However, ICP over 30 mmHg can be used as a threshold to aid in diagnosis.

terms.name: Pain at the lateral aspect of the elbow
terms.definition: Pain localized to the radial aspect of the elbow.

terms.name: Pain at the posterior aspect of the elbow
terms.definition: Pain localized to the posterior aspect of the elbow.

terms.name: Pain at the medial aspect of the elbow
terms.definition: Pain localized to the medial aspect of the elbow.

terms.name: Radial nerve distribution
terms.definition: Applies to the localization of findings corresponding to the distribution of the radial nevrve, such as (i)paresthesias on the dorsoradial aspect of the hand and wrist, including the dorsal thumb, index finger and middle finger and (ii) Weakness in elbow extension, wrist extension, finger extension, thumb extension and/or supination of the forearm.

terms.name: Omovertebral bone
terms.definition: An osseous connection between the superomedial border of the right scapula and C5-C6 spinous processes.

terms.name: Clavicular edema
terms.definition: Swelling on the chest between the neck and the shoulder, above the clavicel (collar bone).

terms.name: Positive CSF anti-measles antibody test
synonyms: Elevated measles antibody titer in cerebrospinal fluid
terms.definition: The presence of antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against a component of measles virus.

terms.name: Vogt striae
terms.definition: Vertical lines in the posterior stroma of the cornea, aligned with Descemet membrane. These lines temporarily disappear with pressure applied to the cornea. Vogt striae are a hallmark feature of keratoconus but have also been observed in healthy eyes. Rare cases of horizontal striae have been reported.

terms.name: Choroid thickening
terms.definition: A condition characterized by an abnormal increase in the thickness of the choroid, which may be associated with various ocular or systemic conditions. Choroid thickening can be measured using imaging techniques such as optical coherence tomography (OCT).

terms.name: Corneal epithelial edema
terms.definition: A condition characterized by accumulation of fluid within the corneal epithelium, leading to swelling, blurred vision, and discomfort. It is often associated with increased intraocular pressure, endothelial dysfunction, or contact lens overuse. Clinical features may include a hazy cornea and microcystic changes visible on slit-lamp examination.

terms.name: Retinal shunt vessels
terms.definition: bnormal blood vessels in the retina that form as a response to vascular occlusion, serving as bypass channels to redirect blood flow around obstructed or damaged retinal vessels. Retinal shunt vessels are often associated with conditions like retinal vein occlusion or diabetic retinopathy and may appear as tortuous or dilated vessels on fundoscopic examination.

terms.name: Filamentary keratitis
terms.definition: A condition characterized by the formation of filaments composed of degenerated epithelial cells and mucus attached to the corneal surface. It is associated with symptoms such as pain, foreign body sensation, photophobia, and tearing. Filamentary keratitis is often linked to underlying conditions such as dry eye disease, post-surgical ocular surface disorders, or systemic diseases like Sjoegren syndrome.

terms.name: Elevated circulating glucosylsphingosine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环葡萄糖基鞘氨醇浓度升高
terms.definition: Concentration of D-glucosylsphingosine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Optic disc hemorrhage
terms.definition: A condition characterized by bleeding at or near the optic disc, visible as a flame-shaped or splinter hemorrhage on fundoscopic examination.

terms.name: Decreased circulating progranulin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环颗粒蛋白前体浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of progranulin in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Preauricular lymphadenopathy
terms.definition: Enlargement of one or more lymph nodes located in front of the ear.

terms.name: Onychoheterotopia
terms.definition: Growth of nail tissue outside the ungual plate, generally in the finger.

terms.name: Abnormal MHC surface expression
terms.name_zh: 主要组织相容性复合体表面表达异常
terms.definition: A deviation from the normal level of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules expressed at the cell surface. The cell-mediated adaptive immune response is regulated by the MHC, which is called human leukocyte antigen (HLA) in humans. HLA molecules are cell surface glycoproteins whose primary function is to present endogenous and exogenous antigens to T lymphocytes for recognition and response. The HLA molecules that present antigen to T lymphocytes are divided into two main classes: HLA class I and HLA class II molecules.

terms.name: Forward displacement of posterior cervical dura mater on neck flexion
terms.name_zh: 颈屈曲时颈后硬膜前移
terms.definition: Flexion MRI (imaging with neutral and flexed about 30-40 degrees neck position) reveals an anterior shift of the cervical dural sac from the lamina in the region of C4 to C7.

terms.name: Corneal dellen
terms.definition: A localized area of corneal thinning typically occurring adjacent to an elevated lesion, such as a conjunctival scar, pterygium, or poorly fitting contact lens. Corneal dellen result from tear film instability and localized dehydration. Without timely treatment, they may progress to epithelial defects or corneal ulceration.

terms.name: Conjunctival xerosis
terms.definition: A condition characterized by dryness of the conjunctiva, often associated with keratinization of the conjunctival epithelium. Conjunctival xerosis is commonly linked to vitamin A deficiency, severe dry eye disease, or systemic conditions such as Sjogren syndrome. Clinical features may include a dull, rough conjunctival surface and reduced mucosal secretions.

terms.name: Limited shoulder external rotation
terms.definition: Difficulty rotating the lower part of the arm away from the body (tested with the elbow flexed and the elbow held next to the side of the body) secondary to pain, weakness, or mechanical block.

terms.name: Occupational exposure to frequent hand trauma
terms.definition: A history of exposure to repeated hand trauma as observed with occupations in which use of hands is frequent such as construction, food preparation and serving related occupations, and transportation and material moving occupations.

terms.name: Inability to fully extend finger at metacarpophalangeal joint
terms.name_zh: 掌指关节指不能完全伸直
synonyms: Inability to fully extend finger at MCP joint
Inability to fully extend finger from base
terms.definition: An inability to fully extend the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint of a finger (extension of an MCP joint straightens the finger).

terms.name: Wrist arthritis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the wrist joint.

terms.name: Scapholunate interval widening
terms.definition: Widening of the space between the scaphoid and lunate on x-ray; scapholunate dissociation.

terms.name: FInger pulp localization
synonyms: Symptoms localized to pulp of the finger
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution is limited to or predominantly affects the fleshy mass on the volar (palmar) aspect of the digit, distal to the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint (known as the pulp of the finger).

terms.name: Ulnar wrist pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the ulnar side of the wrist.

terms.name: Lunotriquetral interval widening
terms.definition: Radiographic widening of the space between the lunate and triquetrum bones.

terms.name: Ulnar translocation of the carpus
terms.definition: Anteroposterior wrist radiograph showing ulnar translocation of the carpus from the distal radius with widening of the radial styloid-scaphoid space.

terms.name: Snapping sensation at time of injury
terms.definition: A popping or snapping sensation (noise or feeling) at the time of an injury.

terms.name: Pagetoid spread
terms.definition: Pagetoid spread connotes the spread of single neoplastic cells, and small nests of them above the basal layer in a variety of melanocytic and nonmelanocytic neoplasms similar to the pattern seen in Paget's and in extramammary Paget disease.

terms.name: Central scarring
terms.definition: Central scarring of skin lesions.

terms.name: Scapholunate ligament tear
terms.definition: A breakage (partial or complete tear) of the scapholunate ligament. The most common cause is physical trauma to the wrist such as a fall onto an outstretched hand. Tear of the scapholunate ligament may lead to carpal instability.

terms.name: Lunotriquetral ligament tear
terms.definition: A breakage (partial or complete tear) of the lunotriquetral ligament. The most common cause is physical trauma to the wrist such as a fall onto an outstretched hand. Rupture or tear of the the lunotriquetral ligament may lead to carpal instability.

terms.name: Pisotriquetral arthritis
terms.definition: Arthritis at the pisotriquetral joint. Radiographic evidence of arthritis at the pisotriquetral joint includes joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral cysts, and/or subchondral sclerosis.

terms.name: Volar intercalated segment instability
terms.definition: A type of carpal instability characterized by volar tilt of the lunate bone.

terms.name: Inaccurate finger pulse oximetry oxygen saturation measurement
terms.name_zh: 指脉氧饱和度测量不准确
terms.definition: Any substantial discrepancy between the measurement of oxygen saturation with finger probe pulse oximetry as compared to an arterial blood gas, which is considered the gold standard.

terms.name: Finger pulse oximetry lower than arterial blood gas analysis measurement of oxygen saturation
terms.name_zh: 指脉氧饱和度低于动脉血气分析氧饱和度
terms.definition: Inaccurately reduced oxygen saturation as measured by finger or toe pulse oximetry compared to oxygen saturation as measured by venous or arterial blood gas analysis.

terms.name: Finger pulse oximetry higher than arterial blood gas analysis measurement of oxygen saturation
terms.name_zh: 指脉氧饱和度高于动脉血气分析氧饱和度
terms.definition: Inaccurately elevated oxygen saturation as measured by finger or toe pulse oximetry compared to oxygen saturation as measured by venous or arterial blood gas analysis.

terms.name: History of thumb sucking past the age of four years
terms.definition: Thumb sucking is a behavior that ceases spontaneously in most children between 2 and 4 years of age. If thumb sucking continues, negative consequences can occur, such as a deformity of the nail or paronychia. This term refers to a history of habitual thumb sucking past the age of 4 years of life.

terms.name: Cutaneous granulomatosis
terms.definition: Skin inflammatory reaction triggered by a wide variety of stimuli, including infections, foreign bodies, malignancy, metabolites, and chemicals. From a pathogenic point of view, they are divided into non-infectious and infectious granulomas. From a clinical point of view, it is useful to divide cutaneous granulomatosis into localized and more disseminated forms, although this distinction can be sometimes artificial.

terms.name: Ureteric stricture
terms.definition: Obstruction of urine flow through one or both ureters caused by issues such as injury, infection, tumours and surgery.

terms.name: Arteriovenous crossing sign
terms.definition: A retinal vascular abnormality characterized by indentation or compression of a retinal vein at an arteriovenous crossing, leading to changes in venous caliber. AV crossing signs are commonly associated with hypertensive retinopathy and may contribute to retinal vein occlusion. They are indicative of vascular remodeling due to chronic hypertension or other systemic vascular diseases.

terms.name: Haab striae
terms.definition: Curvilinear or circumferential breaks in Descemet membrane, typically associated with congenital glaucoma. Haab striae result from elevated intraocular pressure during corneal development, leading to the formation of horizontal or arcuate lines that may be visible on slit-lamp examination. They can contribute to corneal astigmatism and visual impairment.

terms.name: Positive Legionella sputum culture
terms.definition: Growth of Legionella bacteria in a sputum culture.

terms.name: Positive Streptococcus pneumoniae sputum culture
terms.definition: Streptococcus pneumoniae growth in sputum culture.

terms.name: Positive Blastomyces dermatitidis sputum fungal stain
synonyms: Blastomyces dermatitidis on sputum fungal stain
terms.definition: Demonstration of Blastomyces dermatitidis by microscopic examination of a stained sputum specimen.

terms.name: Posterior shoulder pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the posterior (back) part of the shoulder.

terms.name: Superior shoulder pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the superior or proximal aspect of the shoulder over the acromion, distal clavicle, and/or acromioclavicular (AC) joint.

terms.name: Lateral shoulder pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the localized aspect (on the side) of the shoulder.

terms.name: Shoulder instability
terms.definition: Subjective or objective feeling of clunking/clicking in the shoulder with movement, shoulder 'giving way', or sensation of shoulder dislocating.

terms.name: Shoulder labrum tear
terms.definition: A injury with a team (rip, split, or disruption) to the labrum, which is the ring of cartilage that surrounds the socket of the shoulder joint (the glenoid).

terms.name: Positive modified dynamic labral shear test
terms.definition: Sensation of a pain with or without clicking or clunking sensation with the following test. Flex patients elbow to 90 degrees and abduct the arm 120 degrees while maximally externally rotating the arm, then examiner lowers the arm to 60 degrees of abduction. A positive test occurs with pain and/or a painful click along the posterior joint line between 120 degrees and 90 degrees of abduction.

terms.name: Positive O'Brien active compression test
terms.definition: Pain in shoulder reproduced when examiner applies downward pressure on the arm while patient resists pressure in the following position: elbow extended, shoulder forward flexed to 90 degrees and 10-15 degrees adducted with palm facing down. This can be compared to the same position but with the palm facing up which should be less painful.

terms.name: Positive shoulder apprehension test
terms.definition: The individual being investigated displays noticeable apprehension (unease) during a test for shoulder instability in which the individual is laying supine with shoulder abducted to 90 degrees, elbow flexed to 90 degrees, and an external rotation pressure with combined downward pressure is applied on the upper arm.

terms.name: Foamy tear film
terms.definition: A condition characterized by the presence of foam or bubbles within the tear film, often associated with meibomian gland dysfunction or ocular surface diseases.

terms.name: Salzmann corneal nodules
terms.definition: The formation of large, bluish, nodular lesions in the superficial corneal stroma, often associated with chronic keratitis or aging. These nodules may lead to visual impairment.

terms.name: Corneal stromal vascularisation
terms.definition: The abnormal growth of blood vessels into the corneal stroma, often associated with ocular herpes, chronic inflammation, infection, or hypoxia. This condition can lead to corneal scarring and vision impairment.

terms.name: Corneal iron line
terms.definition: Linear or arcuate deposition of iron within the corneal epithelium or stroma, typically associated with conditions such as keratoconus, corneal degeneration, or postsurgical corneal changes.

terms.name: Conjunctivochalasis
terms.definition: A condition characterized by redundant, loose conjunctival tissue, typically located between the globe and the lower eyelid, which may cause ocular discomfort, tear film instability, or epiphora.

terms.name: Conjunctival hyperpigmentation
terms.definition: Increased pigmentation of the conjunctiva, characterized by brown or black discoloration due to melanocytic proliferation or pigment deposition. It may be associated with benign conditions such as primary acquired melanosis or malignant transformation into conjunctival melanoma.

terms.name: Anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies
terms.definition: Antibodies against antigens presented by the cell wall of the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

terms.name: Elevated fraction exhaled nitric oxide
terms.name_zh: 呼出气一氧化氮分数升高
terms.definition: The fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is elevated above the upper limit of normal. FeNO is an endogenous gaseous molecule which can be measured in the human breath test because of airway inflammation. It has been studied extensively as a marker of inflammation and has been incorporated into an algorithm for asthma management.

terms.name: Iris hyperemia
terms.definition: A condition characterized by increased blood flow and congestion of the iris vasculature, leading to a reddish discoloration of the iris. Iris hyperemia is commonly associated with anterior uveitis, angle-closure glaucoma, or ocular inflammation.

terms.name: Elevated circulating reticulated platelet count
terms.name_zh: 血网织血小板计数升高
terms.definition: The number of reticulated platelets per volume of blood in the peripheral circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Reduced circulating reticulated platelet count
terms.definition: The number of reticulated platelets per volume of blood in the peripheral circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating reticulated platelet count
terms.name_zh: 循环网织血小板计数异常
terms.definition: The number of reticulated platelets per volume of blood in the peripheral circulation is outside the limits of normal.

terms.name: Flexed posturing of finger
terms.definition: A sign that can be observed in diseases such as Pyogenic or suppurative flexor tenosynovitis in which the affected finger is held in a flexed position. Often, there is pain on any attempt at passive finger extension. This finding is to be distinguished from a contracture of a finger joint in which the flexed positions is fixed.

terms.name: Positive synovial fluid alpha-defensin
terms.definition: Elevation of the the alpha-defensin concentration in synovial aspirate is above the upper limit of normal. The alpha-defensin test is a qualitative immunoassay optimized and validated for synovial fluid. The alpha-defensin protein is an antimicrobial peptide that is naturally released by neutrophils responding to a pathogen in the synovial fluid.

terms.name: Physeal fracture
terms.definition: Salter-Harris fractures (physeal fractures) refer to fractures through a growth plate (physis) and are, therefore, specifically applied to bone fractures in children.

terms.name: Salter I fracture
terms.definition: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture line extends through the physis or within the growth plate. Type I fractures are due to the longitudinal force applied through the physis, which splits the epiphysis from the metaphysis.

terms.name: Salter II fracture
terms.definition: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture extends through both the physis and metaphysis. These are most common and occur away from the joint space. When the small corner of the metaphysis is visible, this is known as a corner sign or Thurston-Holland fragment.

terms.name: Salter III fracture
terms.definition: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture is intra-articular and extends from the physis into the epiphysis.

terms.name: Salter IV fracture
terms.definition: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture in which the fracture is intra-articular and passes through the epiphysis, physis, and metaphysis.

terms.name: Salter V fracture
terms.definition: A type of physeal (Salter-Harris) fracture that is due to a crush or compression injury of the growth plate. In type V, the force is transmitted through the epiphysis and physis, potentially disrupting the germinal matrix, hypertrophic region, and vascular supply.

terms.name: Nail bed laceration
terms.definition: A cut or injury to the soft tissue under the fingernail or toenail.

terms.name: History of distal radius fracture
terms.definition: Recent or remote history of distal radius fracture of the symptomatic arm.

terms.name: History of triangular fibrocartilage complex tear
terms.name_zh: 三角纤维软骨复合体撕裂史
terms.definition: Recent or remote history of a tear in the triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC). The TFCC is a load-bearing structure between the lunate, triquetrum, and ulnar head. The function of the TFCC is to act as a stabilizer for the ulnar aspect of the wrist. The TFCC is at risk for either acute or chronic degenerative injury.

terms.name: Reduced plantar creases
terms.definition: The creases (wrinkles) on the soles of the feet are less pronounced than normal, or absent.

terms.name: Skin burn
terms.definition: Damage to the skin and underlying tissues caused by an agents such as heat, chemicals, electricity, radiation, or friction, resulting in pain, redness, swelling, and sometimes blisters or charring.

terms.name: Elevanted carboxysterol concentration in cultured lymphoblasts
terms.name_zh: 培养淋巴母细胞羧甾醇浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of carboxysterols in lymphoblastoid cells cultured in cholesterol-depleted medium is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition
terms.definition: An anomaly that can be ascertained by iron-specific magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences such as gradient-echo (GRE) and susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI). Superficial siderosis of the central nervous system is a chronic condition due to persistent or repeated long-term bleeding into the subarachnoid space, leading to subpial hemosiderin deposition. Hemosiderin deposition on MRI is seen as a T2 hypointensity and preferentially outlines the cerebellum and brainstem surface.

terms.name: Cortical superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition
terms.name_zh: 中枢神经系统皮质浅表含铁血黄素沉积
terms.definition: A type of superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition that most commonly occurs due to iron deposits in the superficial cortical layers following bleeding from leptomeningeal vessels, most often from cerebral amyloid angiopathy in patients aged 55 or older.

terms.name: Infratentorial superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition
terms.name_zh: 幕上中枢神经系统浅表含铁血黄素沉积
terms.definition: A type of superficial CNS hemosiderin deposition that involves the cerebellum and brainstem, most commonly the superior vermis, quadrigeminal plate, and basal cerebral surfaces. Cerebellar atrophy, particularly the superior vermis and anterior cerebellar hemispheres, can also be seen on a computed tomography scan of the head. The MRI of the spinal cord may reveal myelomalacia, syringomyelia, owl-eyes, or snake-eyes signs. The most common etiology for classic or primary infratentorial superficial siderosis is spinal dural defects, often dural tears.

terms.name: Pulmonary hyperplasia
terms.definition: Pulmonary Hyperplasia is an absolute increase in the number of alveoli, which are mildly enlarged. Pulmonary hyperplasia has been also referred to as polyalveolar lobe and type 3 cystic adenomatoid malformation.

terms.name: Positive protozoan parasite CSF wet mount test
terms.definition: Demonstration of protozoan parasites in a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) specimen by microscopy.

terms.name: Gallbladder polyp
terms.definition: A gallbladder (GB) polyp is a growth that projects from the lining of the inside wall of the gallbladder into the lumen of the GB. GB polyps are a common incidental sonographic finding, the vast majority of which are benign.

terms.name: Gallbladder polyposis
terms.definition: Multiple polyps arising from the gallbladder mucosal wall.

terms.name: Biceps tendon rupture
terms.definition: Discontinuity of the biceps tendon as observed by ultrasound or magnetic resonance (MR) imaging.

terms.name: Medial epicondyle apophysitis
terms.definition: Medial epicondyle apophysitis (MEA), also known as little league elbow, is an overuse injury prevalent among adolescent athletes whose sport involves repetitive overhand throwing, racket use, or other overhead arm motions. The medial epicondyle is a bony protrusion on the medial elbow with its own ossification center, separate from the main distal humeral physis, known as an apophysis. Medial epicondyle apophysitis occurs due to excessive and repetitive valgus stress placed on the apophysis before its closure. Over time, the repetitive strain results in a traction-type injury and may cause pathologic widening and inflammation of the apophysis or even an avulsion fracture.

terms.name: Thumb carpometacarpal subluxation
terms.definition: A partial (subluxation) loss of alignment at the base of the thumb, where the first metacarpal bone meets the trapezium bone of the wrist. Thumb radiographs showing carpometacarpal (CMC) joint space widening and/or incongruity of the joint space between thumb metacarpal bone and the trapezium bone.

terms.name: Localized to lower eyelid
terms.definition: A descriptor indicating that a condition, lesion, or abnormality is confined to the lower eyelid. This localization may be relevant for various ocular conditions, including infections, structural abnormalities, or dermatological diseases affecting the lower eyelid region.

terms.name: Localized to eyelid
terms.definition: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in an eyelid.

terms.name: Halo vision
terms.definition: A visual phenomenon characterized by the perception of bright rings or halos surrounding light sources. Halo vision is often associated with optical irregularities such as corneal edema, cataracts, or intraocular lens complications. It may also occur in conditions affecting the tear film or due to the presence of glare from light scattering within the ocular media.

terms.name: Hematospermia
terms.definition: The presence of blood in the seminal fluid.

terms.name: Choledocholithiasis
terms.definition: Choledocholithiasis is the presence of stones within the common bile duct.

terms.name: Axillary nerve distribution
terms.definition: Paresthesias on the lateral aspect of the shoulder and upper arm. Weakness in shoulder abduction (deltoid) and shoulder external rotation (teres minor).

terms.name: Pelvic ring fracture
terms.definition: X-ray of the pelvis (AP, inlet, and outlet views) showing fracture of the pelvic ring, including iliac wing (ilium), superior or inferior pubic ramus, or ischium, and/or displacement of the pubic symphysis or sacroiliac joints.

terms.name: Scapulothoracic dissociation
terms.definition: An injury consisting of a laterally displaced scapula with separation of the ipsilateral acromioclavicular joint, disruption of the ipsilateral subclavian vessels and brachial plexus, and an intact overlying skin.

terms.name: Pain exacerbated by weight bearing
terms.definition: Refers to pain that is worse when the individual bears weight with the affected body part.

terms.name: Thumb sign
terms.definition: The distal phalanx of the adducted thumb extends beyond the ulnar border of the palm (The thumb protrudes from the clenched fist).

terms.name: Tibialis anterior tendon rupture
terms.definition: Partial or complete breakage (rupture) of the tibialis anterior tendon (TAT). The TAT is the principal dorsiflexor of the ankle joint and secondary invertor of the foot. It has important roles in the different stages of gait; in the swing phase, it concentrically dorsiflex the ankle for foot clearance and during plantarflexion of the ankle in the stance phase, it eccentrically contract to stabilize the ankle and prevent damage to the foot and ankle. Clinically, presentations in acute lacerations or direct trauma cases are straight forward, in chronic and atraumatic cases usually the symptoms at the time of TAT rupture are more subtle. Other manifestations include mild pain, localized mass, palpable gap, loss of strength, instability during gait, gait disturbances with forefoot dropping and stumbling and high stepping gait.

terms.name: Decreased circulating ADAMTS13 activity
terms.definition: Activity of the enzyme von Willebrand factor-cleaving protease (ADAMTS13) in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal methacholine challenge test
terms.name_zh: 醋甲胆碱激发试验异常
terms.definition: An abnormal result of the methacholine challenge test, which is a bronchoprovocation technique used to evaluate airway hyperresponsiveness, particularly in patients with suspected asthma.

terms.name: Positive stool glutamate dehydrogenase test
synonyms: Detection of C. difficile glutamate dehydrogenase
Positive C. difficile glutamate dehydrogenase test
terms.definition: Detection of the presence of glutamate dehydrogenase produced by Clostridium difficile in a stool sample.

terms.name: Retrocorneal membrane
terms.definition: A retrocorneal membrane is an abnormal, fibrous or cellular tissue layer that forms on the posterior surface of the cornea, typically on or adjacent to the Descemet membrane. It may result from trauma, surgery (e.g., penetrating keratoplasty), inflammation, or endothelial cell dysfunction, and can lead to visual impairment depending on its density and extent.

terms.name: Adrenal hemorrhage
terms.definition: Adrenal hemorrhage is bleeding within the capsule of the adrenal gland.

terms.name: Optic nerve sheath dilatation
synonyms: Dilation of the optic nerve sheath
terms.definition: An abnormal increase in the diameter of the optic nerve sheath, typically due to elevated intracranial pressure or local pathology affecting cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics. It can be detected via imaging modalities such as ultrasound or MRI and may be associated with papilledema, idiopathic intracranial hypertension, or optic nerve tumors.

terms.name: Right ventricular thrombus
terms.definition: A blood clot (thrombus) localized in the right ventricle.

terms.name: Severe Candida infection
terms.definition: Increased susceptibility to Candida infections as manifested by a severe or invasive infection with Candida. Severe manifestations include invasive candidiasis with hematogenous spread (candidaemia), hepatosplenic candidiasis, renal candidiasis, Candida endophthalmitis, and Candida endocarditis.

terms.name: Phrenic neuropathy
terms.definition: A functional deficit of the phrenic nerve. Phrenic neuropathy (PhN) is a debilitating condition characterized by impairment of the diaphragm muscle, the primary inspiratory muscle. Diaphragm muscle ultrasound is a noninvasive tool that appears to offer both high sensitivity and specificity for diagnosis. Alternatively, electrodiagnostic studies can assess phrenic nerve health. PhN is commonly diagnosed via diaphragm muscle US or fluoroscopy (sniff test) with paradoxical or significantly decreased diaphragm muscle movement.

terms.name: Glomerular basement membrane subendothelial remodeling
terms.name_zh: 肾小球基底膜内皮下重塑
terms.definition: New glomerular basement membrane matrix formation under the endothelial cell.

terms.name: Glomerular endothelium swelling
terms.definition: Enlargement of the glomerular endothelium (the innermost layer of the glomerular filtration barrier) causing capillary lumen narrowing and loss of fenetrations.

terms.name: Medullary collecting duct ectasia
terms.definition: Widening of the lumen of the lumen of the collecting ducts in the renal medulla.

terms.name: Corneal keloid
terms.definition: A raised, opaque, and fibrous lesion on the cornea resembling a dermal keloid, typically composed of disorganized collagen and fibrovascular tissue. Corneal keloids can impair vision and are often secondary to trauma, surgery, or underlying congenital disorders.

terms.name: Podocytic mitochondrial proliferation
terms.definition: An ultrastructural abnormality of the kidney glomeruli characterized by an excessive number or abnormal aggregation of mitochondria in podocytes.

terms.name: Elevated vitamin D metabolite ratio
terms.name_zh: 维生素D代谢物比值升高
terms.definition: The ratio of 24,25(OH)2D to 25(OH)D (also known as vitamin D metabolite ratio or VMR) is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Aggravated by vitamin D supplementation
terms.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment or supplementation with vitamin D.

terms.name: Aggravated by sun exposure
terms.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that becomes worse with exposure to sunlight.

terms.name: Tubular accumulation of uromodulin
terms.definition: Accumulation of uromodulin within renal tubular cells or lumina.

terms.name: Elevated stool reducing substances
terms.definition: Elevated level of reducing substances in the feces. If carbohydrate malabsorption is suspected, a reducing substance should be investigated in the stool using the Benedict or Fehling test. The presence of reducing substances may indicate an abnormality in carbohydrate (e.g., sucrose, lactase) metabolism. The unabsorbed sugars in stool are measured as reducing substances.

terms.name: Osteochondral lesion of talus
terms.definition: Osteochondral lesion of the talus (OLT) is an injury involving the articular cartilage and subchondral bone, defined as any damage involving both articular cartilage and subchondral bone of the talar dome. OLT can cause ankle joint pain and can sometimes lead to instability and manifest as an area of abnormal, damaged cartilage and bone on the top of the talus bone (the lower bone of the ankle joint).

terms.name: Mallet toe
terms.definition: A mallet toe involves the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint [such that] the distal phalanx is flexed on the middle phalanx.

terms.name: Bunionette deformity
terms.definition: The bunionette, or tailor's bunion, is a lateral prominence of the fifth metatarsal head. Most commonly, bunionettes are the result of a widened 4-5 intermetatarsal angle with associated varus of the metatarsophalangeal joint.

terms.name: Elevated CSF beta chorionic gonadotropin concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液β-绒毛膜促性腺激素浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of beta chorionic gonadotropin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Pigment epithelium detachment
terms.definition: Separation of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) from the underlying Bruch membrane.

terms.name: Retinal gliosis
terms.definition: A pathological condition characterized by the proliferation of glial cells in the retina, often occurring as a reactive response to injury, inflammation, or degenerative changes, and typically resulting in structural and functional alterations in the retina.

terms.name: Aphakia
terms.definition: Absence of the crystalline lens in the eye, which may be congenital or acquired (e.g., following surgical removal of the lens for cataracts or trauma).

terms.name: Pain on thumb extension
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort that is triggered upon extension (straightening) of the thumb.

terms.name: Fractured lunate bone
terms.definition: A partial or complete breakage of the lunate bone.

terms.name: Fractured triquetrum bone
terms.definition: A partial or complete breakage of the triquetrum bone.

terms.name: Fractured pisiform bone
terms.definition: A partial or complete breakage of the pisiform bone.

terms.name: Fractured trapezium bone
terms.definition: A partial or complete breakage of the trapezium bone.

terms.name: Fractured trapezoid bone
terms.definition: A partial or complete breakage of the trapezoid bone.

terms.name: Fractured capitate bone
terms.definition: A partial or complete breakage of the capitate bone.

terms.name: Fractured hamate bone
terms.definition: A partial or complete breakage of the hamate bone.

terms.name: Pulsatile abdominal mass
terms.definition: An abnormal enlargement or swelling in the abdomen that pulses or throbs.

terms.name: Nonpulsatile abdominal mass
terms.definition: An abnormal enlargement or swelling in the abdomen that does not pulse or throb.

terms.name: Iatrogenic anophthalmos
terms.definition: A form of acquired anophthalmos resulting from surgical removal of the eye (enucleation or evisceration), typically performed due to trauma, intraocular tumors, intractable pain in a blind eye, or severe infection. Unlike congenital anophthalmos, the orbit may have previously developed normally and prosthetic rehabilitation is often pursued.

terms.name: Reduced erythrocyte glutathione peroxidase
terms.definition: Activity or concentration of in the level of glutathione peroxidase (EC 1.11.1.9) in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating malonyl carnitine concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环丙二酰肉碱浓度升高
synonyms: Elevated levels of malonylcarnitine in blood acylcarnitine profile
terms.definition: The concentration of malonylcarnitine in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Sertoli cell hypoplasia
terms.definition: Abnormal decrease in the number of Sertoli cells in the testis.

terms.name: Positive talar tilt test
terms.definition: An abnormal result of the talar tilt test. This test assesses ankle ligament integrity, particularly the calcaneofibular ligament (CFL) and the deltoid ligaments. To perform the test, the foot is placed at an angle of 90 degrees with the leg, the calcaneofibular ligament is perpendicular and the anterior talofibular ligament is parallel to the long axis of the talus. Therefore, inversion in this position results in strain on the calcaneofibular ligament.

terms.name: Plantar ecchymosis
terms.definition: A purpuric lesion that is larger than 1 cm in diameter and is located on the sole of the foot.

terms.name: Prolonged exposure to axillary pressure
terms.definition: History of prolonged compressive pressure in the axillary region.

terms.name: Lateral ankle pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the outer side of the ankle.

terms.name: Medial ankle pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the inner side of the ankle.

terms.name: Posterior ankle pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the back of the ankle.

terms.name: Anterior ankle pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the front of the ankle.

terms.name: Exacerbated by colchicine
terms.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment with colchizine.

terms.name: Retinal periphlebitis
terms.definition: A condition characterized by inflammation of the outer walls of retinal veins, often presenting as vascular sheathing or exudates along the venous walls.

terms.name: Purulent pericardial effusion
terms.definition: Elevated leukocyte count in the pericardial fluid ranging from a a microscopic purulent pericardial effusion to gross pus in the pericardial space.

terms.name: Conjunctival erosion
terms.definition: A condition characterized by the localized loss or breakdown of the conjunctival epithelium, often resulting in exposure of the underlying tissue. Conjunctival erosion may cause symptoms such as redness, irritation, foreign body sensation, and tearing. It can result from trauma, chemical injuries, ocular surface diseases, or prolonged use of contact lenses.

terms.name: Positive Mycobacterium tuberculosis sputum culture
terms.definition: Growth of mycobacterium tuberculosis in a sputum culture.

terms.name: Increased external rotation of shoulder
terms.definition: Increased rotation of the lower part of the arm away from the body (tested with the elbow flexed and the elbow held next to the side of the body or shoulder 90 degrees abducted to the side).

terms.name: Positive trunk flexion test
synonyms: Abnormal forward flexion of the trunk manoeuvre
Increased forward flexion of the trunk
Trunk flexion with palms on floor
terms.definition: The proband is asked to flex the trunk forward with knees straight. The result of the test is considered positive (abnormal) if the palms can be made to rest flat on the floor.

terms.name: Tibiotalar arthritis
terms.definition: AP, oblique, or lateral view x-ray of the ankle showing radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis such as joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, and/or osteophyte formation in the tibiotalar joint.

terms.name: Anterior ankle osteophyte
terms.definition: Imaging study of the ankle revealing osteophyte (bone spur) formation at the anterior aspect of the ankle (tibial or talar neck).

terms.name: Midfoot arthritis
terms.definition: AP, oblique, or lateral view x-ray of the foot showing radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis in the midfoot (tarsometatarsal (TMT) joints, naviculocuneiform joint, intercuneiform joints, and/or metatarsal cuneiform joints), such as joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, and/or osteophyte formation in the tibiotalar joint.

terms.name: Decreased circulating reverse T3 concentration
terms.definition: Concentration of reverse T3 (3,3',5'-triiodothyronine or rT3) in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Stocking-glove distribution
terms.definition: Distribution of findings in hands and feet with a distal to proximal gradient of severity (being more severe in the more distal locations).

terms.name: Hairy kidney sign
terms.definition: A radiological sign related to infiltration of histiocytes into the kidneys and perirenal fat. This infiltration, along with thickening of fibrous bands within the perirenal fat, creates a hairy appearance on cross-sectional imaging studies.

terms.name: White appearance of duodenal mucosa
synonyms: Gelee blanche appearance of duodenal mucosa
White hoar frosting appearance of duodenal mucosa
terms.definition: On a typical diet (e.g., no dietary fat restriction), the intestinal mucosa may have a gelee blanche or white hoar frosting appearance on endoscopy.

terms.name: Acromioclavicular joint separation
terms.definition: An acromioclavicular (AC) joint joint separation, often called a shoulder separation, is a dislocation of the clavicle from the acromion. This feature is ascertainable radiographically by AC joint x-ray views including bilateral anteroposterior (AP) view, axillary lateral view, and/or Zanca view showing either superior, posterior, or inferior displacement of the distal clavicle in relation to the acromion at the AC joint.

terms.name: Acromioclavicular joint arthritis
terms.definition: Degenerative disease of the acromioclavicular (AC) joint that manifests radiographically as Zanca view X-ray of the AC joint showing radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis such as joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, and/or osteophyte formation in the AC joint.

terms.name: Positive shoulder cross-body adduction test
terms.definition: A test used with suspected chronic acromioclavicular joint lesions (which are a common source of pain and disability in the shoulder). The test is considered positive with pain in the ipsilateral acromioclavicular joint when patient straightens the affected arm forward and reaches for the contralateral shoulder with extra manual cross body (adduction) pressure on the arm from the examiner.

terms.name: Proximal humeral epiphysiolysis
terms.definition: Proximal humeral epiphysiolysis (Little League shoulder) is a shear or stress injury of the epiphyseal cartilage of the proximal humerus. Anteroposterior (AP) view of the shoulder in external rotation showing widening of the proximal humerus physis in comparison to contralateral shoulder with possible metaphyseal bony irregularity.

terms.name: Positive anterior drawer test
terms.definition: A test for ankle instability in which an anterior pull on the calcaneus with is applied with one hand while stabilizing the end of the tibia/fibula with the other hand. The test is considered positive (abnormal) if it results in more than one cm of anterior translation of the foot compared to the healthy, contralateral ankle.

terms.name: Peroneal tendon tear
terms.definition: Injury to a peroneal tendon, as can be ascertained by an MRI study of the ankle showing partial or complete tear of one or both of the peroneal tendons.

terms.name: Fifth metatarsal apophysitis
terms.definition: Iselin's disease is a traction apophysitis of base of fifth metatarsal. The apophysis is within the peroneus brevis tendon insertion site and appears radiographically at about age 10 in female and age 12 in male and usually fuses by age 11 in female and by age 14 in male. Repetitive microtrauma from the peroneus brevis tendon, as occurs in sports activities is the cause of traction apophysitis. It can be ascertained by oblique foot radiographs showing apophyseal irregularity (enlarged apophysis, disordered ossification, widened chondro-osseous junction) at the base of the fifth metatarsal.

terms.name: Tibial tubercle apophysitis
terms.definition: Lateral knee radiograph showing tibial tuberosity apophysis irregularity and fragmentation; tibial tubercle osteochondrosis; traction apophysitis of the tibial tubercle.

terms.name: Enteric anendocrinosis
terms.definition: Near absence of small intestinal and colonic endocrine cells. This feature can be ascertained histopathologically and may also be manifested as a lack of staining for enteroendocrive markers such as synaptophysin.

terms.name: Metatarsal head osteochondrosis
terms.definition: Avascular necrosis of a metatarsal head, most commonly involving the second, but also the third or fourth, metatarsal.\nComment: Affected individuals may present with foot pain on weight-bearing, swelling, and tenderness. Radiological features include widening of the metatarsophalangeal joint space and flattening of the affected metatarsal head, at later stages metatarsal head sclerosis, cortical thickening, and intra-articular loose bodies. Osteochondrosis is a condition resulting from an epiphysis injury that alters enchondral ossification and produces irregularity at the joint surface. Freiberg disease is characterized as osteochondrosis of the metatarsal heads (primarily the second).

terms.name: Hallux sesamoiditis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the sesamoid bones of the hallux ( two ovoid-shaped ossicles embedded within the tendons under the big toe). This feature can be ascertained by MRI of the foot, revealing edema within one or both of the hallux sesamoids.

terms.name: Os trigonum
terms.definition: Os trigonum (OT) is one of the most common accessory ossicles in the foot and ankle region. In clinical practice, OT is a considerable factor that may predispose patients to posterior ankle impingement syndrome (PAIS). Lateral ankle x-ray with foot in plantarflexion reveals an accessory ossicle at the posterior aspect of the talus, between the posterior distal tibia and calcaneal tuberosity.

terms.name: Positive heel squeeze test
terms.definition: The squeeze test is the most common examination for diagnosing calcaneal apophysitis (Sever disease) and is conducted by compressing the medial and lateral aspects of the calcaneus. The test is considered positive (abnormal) if squeezing elicits pain.

terms.name: Calcaneal apophysitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the calcaneal apophysis (bony projection where the Achilles tendon attaches to the heel). Lateral foot x-ray shows increased density in the calcaneal apophysis or fragmentation of the apophysis.

terms.name: Decreased circulating guanidinoacetic acid concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环胍基乙酸浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of guanidinoacetic acid in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating C-triol concentration
terms.definition: The concentration of cholestane-3beta, 5alpha, 6beta-triol (C-triol) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. C-triol is a diagnostic biomarker for Niemann-Pick disease type C.

terms.name: Germinal vesicle oocyte maturation arrest
terms.name_zh: 生发泡卵母细胞成熟停滞
terms.definition: A type of oocyte maturation arrest that occurs prior to the breakdown of the germinal vesicle (which is a hallmark of reinitiation of meiosis I and entry into M phase).

terms.name: Metaphase II oocyte maturation arrest
terms.name_zh: 第二次减数分裂中期卵母细胞成熟阻滞
terms.definition: The morphologic classification of MII generally denotes an oocyte that is mature, having arrested in metaphase II and is presumed to be capable of fertilization. However, there are subsets of women who produce oocytes with MII morphology that are not capable of embryo formation even with fertilization. This incongruence between morphologic maturity and capacity could be attributed to either the inclusion within the morphologic classification immature oocytes arrested at any stage between PBI formation and metaphase II, which are not capable of fertilization, or oocytes arrested normally at metaphase II that do not possess the ability to complete meiosis.

terms.name: Mixed oocyte maturation arrest
terms.name_zh: 混合性卵母细胞成熟阻滞
terms.definition: A type of oocyte maturation failure whereby oocytes arrest at more than one stage of meiosis.

terms.name: Dorsal forearm pain
terms.definition: Pain localized to dorsal (non-palmar) aspect of the forearm.

terms.name: Volar forearm pain
terms.definition: Pain on the volar (palmar) aspect of the forearm.

terms.name: Cholesterol gallbladder polyp
