terms.definition: A non-neoplastic gallbladder polyp that is hyperplastic and consists of a lipid deposit. Cholesterol polyps are generally less than 10 mm. often multiple cholesterol polyps are present. They are often associated with vesicular cholesterolosis and are thought to have no malignant potential.

terms.name: Hyperlordotic gait
terms.definition: A gait abnormality characterized by excessive lumbar lordosis (swayback posture, i.e., an inward curvature of the lower spine) and gait pattern with forward tilt of the pelvis and increased lumbar curvature. Hyperlordotic gait is often as a compensatory mechanism for hip extensor weakness, proximal muscle weakness, or hip flexion contracture.

terms.name: Radioulnar interosseous membrane tear
terms.definition: A tear in the fibrous sheet connecting the radius and ulna bones in the forearm.

terms.name: Fleck sign of elbow
terms.definition: A radiograpzhic sign in which small bone fragments detached from the olecranon are seen on lateral radiographs in cases with avulsion of the tendon.

terms.name: Resisted wrist flexion provokes pain
terms.definition: Active wrist flexion against resistance increases pain in the arm.

terms.name: Lateral epicondylitis of the elbow
terms.definition: A chronic symptomatic degeneration of the wrist extensor tendons involving their attachment to the lateral epicondyle of the humerus, and is associated clinically with lateral elbow pain (tennis elbow). This term refers to the associated imaging finding. Ultrasound imaging showing extensor carpi radialis brevis (ECRB) tendon thickening and hypoechoic areas with increased vascularity or MRI showing increased signal intensity or tear at the insertion site of the ECRB on the lateral aspect of the elbow.

terms.name: Medial epicondylitis of the elbow
terms.definition: Medial epicondylitis, often referred to as golfer's elbow, is a common pathology. Flexor-pronator tendon degeneration occurs with repetitive forced wrist extension and forearm supination during activities involving wrist flexion and forearm pronation. This term refers to the associated imaging finding. Ultrasound imaging showing ECRB tendon thickening and hypoechoic areas with increased vascularity or MRI showing increased signal intensity or tear at the insertion site of the common flexor tendon.

terms.name: Popeye sign
terms.definition: Exaggerated bulging of the belly of the biceps muscle upon contraction.

terms.name: Distal biceps tendon rupture
terms.name_zh: 肱二头肌远端肌腱断裂
terms.definition: Rupture (tear) of the distal biceps tendon. Ultrasound imaging showing complete discontinuity of the distal biceps tendon or MRI revealing complete distal biceps tendon discontinuity or increased signal intensity in the distal biceps tendon.

terms.name: Proximal biceps tendon rupture
terms.definition: Rupture (tear) of the proximal biceps tendon. MRI reveals a tear of the proximal aspect of the biceps tendon near its site of origin at the supraglenoid tubercle.

terms.name: Positive bursal fluid infectious agent test
terms.definition: Detection of an infectious agent, or evidence thereof, in aspirated bursal fluid using microbiological, molecular, or antigen-based testing methods.

terms.name: Acute retinal necrosis
terms.definition: A condition characterized by the death of retinal tissue due to ischemia, infection, or inflammation.

terms.name: Cystic changes in greater tuberosity of the humerus
terms.definition: Cystic lesions of the proximal humerus are commonly encountered on routine shoulder magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). True cysts are defined as fluid-filled structures or lesions with an epithelial lining, whereas pseudocysts are fluid-filled lesions without epithelial lining. Cystic lesion encompasses both true cysts, pseudocysts and other lesions which could mimic the appearance of a cyst on MRI, with increased signal on fluid sensitive sequences.

terms.name: Positive Hawkins test
terms.definition: Manual internal rotation on the forearm with the shoulders flexed forward to 90 degrees, elbows bent to 90 degrees so that the forearm is parallel to the ground, and palm facing down recreates pain in the shoulder region; named after Dr. Hawkins.

terms.name: Hallux weakness
terms.definition: Reduced ability to exert force or power with the hallux (big toe), i.e., reduced strength of the hallux.

terms.name: Hallux dorsiflexion weakness
terms.definition: Reduced ability to lift the big toe (hallux) upward toward the shin.

terms.name: Hallux plantarflexion weakness
terms.definition: Reduced ability to push the big toe (hallux) downward, away from the shin.

terms.name: Forefoot pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized about the metatarsal heads in the front part of the foot.

terms.name: Spur at inferior pole of patella
terms.definition: A bone spur (osteophyte), i.e., de novo bone formation at the lower edge of the patella (knee cap). Radiographically, it is visible as calcification at inferior pole of the patella.

terms.name: Urinary ascites
terms.definition: The presence of urine in the peritoneal cavity, an entity that typically results from bladder rupture or damage to the ureters.

terms.name: Abnormal mixed venous oxygen saturation
terms.name_zh: 混合静脉血氧饱和度异常
terms.definition: Abnormal oxygen saturation in mixed venous blood (SvO2). SvO2 can be measured in a sample of mixed venous blood drawn from the distal lumen of a catheter placed in the pulmonary artery. The SvO2 is dependent on arterial oxygen saturation, hemoglobin concentration, cardiac output, and tissue oxygen demands.

terms.name: Elevated circulating lysosphingomyelin concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环溶血鞘磷脂浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of lysosphingomyelin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. Acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD) or Niemann-Pick type A/B is a lysosomal disorder caused by the deficiency of acid sphingomyelinase (ASM) due to pathogenic variants in the SMPD1 gene. Sphingomyelin (SM) is the substrate for ASM that cleaves the phosphorylcholine linkage of SM producing ceramide. SM is a major compound of most cell membranes and coupled with cholesterol constitutes most of the membrane rafts. In the deficiency of ASM, there is primary storage of SM, and the concentration of lysosphingomyelin in dried blood spots and in the blood circulation is typically elevated.

terms.name: Abnormal lens capsule morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the lens capsule, the smooth, transparent, acellular basement membrane that envelops the lens of the eye and serves as the attachment site for the lens zonules and the lens epithelium.

terms.name: Posterior capsule opacification
terms.definition: Posterior capsule opacification, also known as secondary cataract, is the most frequent complication following manual extracapsular cataract extraction. Secondary cataract results from the proliferation and migration of residual epithelial cells in the posterior region of the lens capsule into the visual axis, leading to thickening and reduction in transparency (opacification), which in turn can cause a decrease in visual acuity.

terms.name: Bronchial stenosis
terms.definition: A narrowing (constriction) of the lumen of a bronchus, which may involve one or more of the major airways branching from the trachea.

terms.name: Skin tenting due to fracture
terms.definition: Skin tenting may occur in the setting of a fracture when a displaced bone fragment pushes on the skin, causing it to bulge outward in a tent-like shape.

terms.name: Follicular conjunctivitis
terms.definition: A type of conjunctivitis characterized by the formation of conjunctival follicles, which appear as raised domes on the are round collections of lymphocytes, and are often most prominent in the inferior fornix (interior part of the lower eyelid).

terms.name: Granulomatous conjunctivitis
terms.definition: A type of conjunctivitis characterized by the formation of conjunctival granulomata, i.e., localized nodular inflammatory lesions of the conjunctiva, characterized histologically by aggregates of epithelioid histiocytes, often with multinucleated giant cells, surrounded by lymphocytes and fibroblasts.

terms.name: Areas of hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation that follow Blaschko lines
terms.name_zh: 沿Blaschko线分布的色素减退及色素沉着区
terms.definition: Linear streaks of hypopigmentation or hyperpigmentation that are distributed according to Blaschko lines, which are V-shaped, S-shaped, or linear patterns on the skin that reflect the embryonic migration pathways of epidermal cells (keratinocytes, melanocytes, etc.) during early development.

terms.name: Retinal drusen
terms.definition: Small focal extracellular deposits underneath the retina, visible ophthalmoscopically as yellow dots.

terms.name: Intrauterine amputation
terms.definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by partial or complete absence of a limb or digit at birth, resulting from interruption of normal limb development in utero.

terms.name: Intrauterine digital amputation
terms.definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by partial or complete absence of a finger or toe at birth, resulting from interruption of normal development in utero.

terms.name: Intrauterine limb amputation
terms.definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by partial or complete absence of an arm or leg at birth, resulting from interruption of normal development in utero.

terms.name: Proximal interphalangeal joint arthritis
terms.definition: Inflammation and deterioration of the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints. Radiographically, PIP arthritis can be characterized by PIP joint space narrowing, subchondral cysts, and osteophytes.

terms.name: Dorsal intercalated segment instability
terms.definition: A nondissociative form of carpal instability, in which the lunate bone angulates to the dorsal side of the hand.

terms.name: Disruption of carpal arcs
terms.definition: The arcs of the Gilula are used on PA wrist radiographs as part of assessing the normal alignment of the carpus. The 1st arc (red) outlines the proximal surfaces and the 2nd arc (yellow) the distal surfaces of the scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum. The 3rd arc (white) outlines the proximal surfaces of the capitate and hamate. Disruption of carpal arcs (i.e., the arcs appear broken or discontinuous on radiographs) indicates a fracture or ligamentous injury in the wrist.

terms.name: Spilled teacup sign of the wrist
terms.definition: Dislocation of the lunate bone, generally as a result of trauma. Volar displacement of the lunate is said to result a tipped teacup.

terms.name: Positive Finkelstein sign
terms.definition: Finkelstein's test produces severe tenderness and usually pain on the radial aspect of the wrist when the thumb is flexed into the palm and the wrist is ulnar deviated.

terms.name: Forefoot abduction
terms.definition: Outward deviation or turning of the front part of the foot away from the body's midline. An anteroposterior foot x-ray shows increased Simmon angle (angle between the talus and first metatarsal, normal is 7 degrees plus/minus 4 to 5 degrees) or increased talonavicular uncoverage of over 30 to 40 percent. A common clinical observation is the too many toes sign; when viewed from behind, more than two toes will flare out laterally due to the valgus alignment of the foot.

terms.name: Posterior tibial tendon injury
terms.definition: Damage to the posterior tibialis tendon, which runs along the inside of the ankle and foot, supporting the arch of the foot. MRI or ultrasound of the ankle/foot shows posterior tibial tendon degeneration such as tendinosis, tenosynovitis, edema around the tendon, or tendon tear.

terms.name: Plantar pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to palpation of plantar aspect of the foot (the sole).

terms.name: Flexor hallucis longus tendon injury
terms.definition: Damage to the flexor hallucis longus (FHL) tendon. The FHL tendon is a long tendon that runs from the deep calf muscle down through the ankle to the big toe, enabling toe flexion and supporting foot mechanics.. MRI or ultrasound of the ankle/foot shows degenerative changes of the FHL tendon such as fluid around the tendon at the level of the ankle joint, intra-substance tendinous signal, tendon thickening, tendonitis, or tenosynovitis, or tendon rupture.

terms.name: Hallux pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the big toe (hallux).

terms.name: Pain on the medial aspect of the foot
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the side of the foot nearest to the big toe (hallux).

terms.name: Hallux sesamoid injury
terms.definition: Damage affecting one or both of the two small, pea-shaped bones (sesamoids) embedded in the tendons beneath the first metatarsophalangeal joint of the big toe. Foot x-ray shows fracture, subluxation, or dislocation of the sesamoid of the hallux.

terms.name: Radial wrist pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the radial side of the wrist.

terms.name: Volar wrist pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the volar side of the wrist (i.e., to the palm side - front - of the wrist).

terms.name: Dorsal wrist pain
terms.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the dorsal side (back) of the wrist.

terms.name: Peroneal tendon tenderness
terms.definition: Pain elicited with palpation along the course of the peroneal tendons, located posterior to the lateral malleolus and extending distally toward the base of the fifth metatarsal.

terms.name: Peroneal tendon subluxation
terms.definition: Dynamic ultrasound of the lateral ankle showing subluxation or dislocation of one or both of the peroneal tendons out of the peroneal groove.

terms.name: Peroneal tendon injury
terms.definition: Ankle MRI or ultrasound showing edema or thickening of peroneal tendon(s), fluid within peroneal tendon sheath, or a partial or complete tear in one or both of the peroneal tendons.

terms.name: Elevated circulating succinylacetone concentration
terms.name_zh: 血琥珀酰丙酮浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of succinylacetone in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Flat palate
terms.definition: Reduced height of the palate. A flat palate is present with a palatal index angle below 30 degrees, a normal palate with an angle between 30 and 45 degrees, and a steep palate with an angle above 45 degrees.

terms.name: Elevated circulating C-terminal telopeptide cross-link of type1 collagen concentration
terms.name_zh: 血Ⅰ型胶原C端交联肽浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of C-terminal telopeptide cross-link of type1 collagen in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Exacerbated by pulmonary vasodilator exposure
terms.name_zh: 肺血管扩张剂暴露加重
terms.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment with a pulmonary vasodilator medication such as prostacyclin analogs, endothelin receptor antagonists, and phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE5) inhibitors.

terms.name: Mercury exposure
terms.definition: History of exposure to mercury.

terms.name: Urinoma
terms.definition: Encapsulated collections of urine around the kidney in the retroperitoneum, most commonly in the perirenal space, as a consequence of renal tract leakage caused by urinary obstruction, trauma, or post-instrumentation.

terms.name: Umbilical discharge
terms.definition: Abnormal fluid draining from the umbilicus (from wounds, surgical sites, or fistulas).

terms.name: Abnormal biparietal diameter
terms.definition: Abnormal biparietal diameter (BPD) refers to a fetal head width measurement, taken between the outer edge of the proximal parietal bone and the inner edge of the distal parietal bone on an ultrasound image, that lies outside the expected range for a given gestational age. The expected range typically falls between the 10th and 90th percentiles, with microcephaly defined as a BPD below the 3rd percentile (or more than 2 standard deviations below the mean) and macrocephaly defined as a BPD above the 97th percentile (or more than 2 standard deviations above the mean).

terms.name: Abnormal fetal femur length
terms.definition: Femur length is measured between the outer border of one end of the the femoral diaphysis to the other outer border, excluding the epiphysis or other artifact. Abnormal femur length is defined as being more than two standard deviations away from the mean.

terms.name: Pain exacerbated by wrist ulnar deviation
terms.definition: Pain worsens with wrist ulnar deviation (i.e., the pain is exacerbated if the hand is moved towards the side with the fifth finger).

terms.name: Pain exacerbated by wrist radial deviation
terms.definition: Pain worsens with wrist radial deviation (i.e., the pain is exacerbated if the hand is moved towards the side with the thumb).

terms.name: Ulnar positive variance
terms.definition: A phenomenon whereby the distal ulna articular surface is more distal than the distal radius articular surface.

terms.name: Negative ulnar variance
terms.definition: Negative ulnar variance is a condition in which the ulna is relatively shorter than the radius at the carpus. AP wrist X-ray shows the distal ulna articular surface more proximal than the distal radius articular surface.

terms.name: Flexor carpi radialis tendonitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the flexor carpi radialis (FCR) tendon, which traverses the carpus through a narrow fibro-osseous tunnel.

terms.name: Transillumination test shows high light transmission
terms.definition: A transillumination test involves shining light through an area of the body or a mass. This term refers to a transillumination test that shows especially high (positive) transillumination, which may be observed when a mass or swelling contains clear fluid rather than solid tissue or blood.

terms.name: Hyperleukocytosis
terms.definition: Hyperleukocytosis is commonly defined as a white blood cell (WBC) count of greater than 100,000 luekocytes per microliter.

terms.name: Elbow instability
terms.definition: Impairment of the ability of the elbow joint to maintain proper anatomical alignment and functional mechanics. Elbow instability is a spectrum from subluxation to dislocation, with corresponding clinical and pathologic features and therapeutic implications.

terms.name: Valgus instability of the elbow
terms.definition: A type of elbow instability that arises through injuries to the medial collateral ligament (MCL), specifically the anterior bundle (AMCL). In the valgus stress test, the elbow is placed in 20 to 30 degrees of flexion with the forearm supinated and a valgus stress is applied. The test is positive when no firm end point is palpated, greater than 1 mm of medial joint opening is noted (fluoroscopically), or there is reproduction of the patient's pain.

terms.name: Varus instability of the elbow
terms.definition: A type of elbow insttability characterized by abnormal widening or gapping of the lateral (radial) side of the elbow joint when a varus stress is applied, due to insufficiency of the lateral collateral ligament complex.

terms.name: Limited foot eversion
terms.definition: Decreased foot eversion secondary to pain, weakness, or mechanical block.

terms.name: Limited foot inversion
terms.definition: Decreased foot inversion secondary to pain, weakness, or mechanical block.

terms.name: Positive synovial Tropheryma whipplei bacteria microscopy
terms.definition: Demonstration of Tropheryma whipplei bacteria in the synovial (joint) fluid by microscopic analysis.

terms.name: Positive calf squeeze test
terms.definition: An abnormal result of the calf-squeeze test (also known as the Thompson test), which is considered a sign of Achilles tendon rupture. The test is positive (abnormal) if no plantar flexion of the foot occurs at calf squeezing.

terms.name: Achilles tendon tear
terms.definition: A partial or complete break in the Achilles tendon (the tendon that connects the gastrocnemius and soleus to the calcaneus). This feature can be ascertained by magnetic resonance imaing (MRI) of the foot/ankle showing partial or complete tear of the achilles tendon.

terms.name: Positive bursa fluid gram stain
terms.definition: Demonstration of the presence of bacteria by gram staining of bursa fluid. The sample is generally obtained by bursal fluid aspiration.

terms.name: Abnormal medial epicondyle morphology
terms.definition: A structural anomaly of the medial epicondyle, which is the site of the attachment of various muscles, including the radial and ulnar flexor of the wrist, the superficial flexor of the fingers, the palmaris longus and the pronator teres muscle.

terms.name: Medial humerus epicondyle avulsion fracture
terms.definition: An avulsion fracture of the medial epicondyle of the elbow. Radiological examination in the anteroposterior and lateral projection can be used to make the diagnosis and to determine the degree and direction of the fracture displacement.

terms.name: Hand mass
terms.definition: A swelling or enlargement localized to the hand. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

terms.name: Tenosynovitis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the synovial sheath that surrounds a tendon.

terms.name: Tigroid fundus
terms.definition: Enhanced visibility of large choroidal vessels through the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). This reticulated pattern is commonly observed on fundus examination and color fundus photography. Such hypopigmented areas alternate with hyperpigmented zones in a tigroid pattern. Fundus tessellation is often associated with myopia and choroidal thinning.

terms.name: Decreased myocardial glycogen content
synonyms: Glycogen depletion in cardiac muscle tissue
terms.definition: The amount of glycogen in the myocardial tissue of the heart is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: CSF anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody positivity
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液抗髓鞘少突胶质细胞糖蛋白抗体阳性
terms.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein.

terms.name: Spinal cord H sign
synonyms: H sign in the spinal cord
terms.definition: The H sign can be ascertained by spinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and represents spinal cord myelitis isolated to the gray matter. A longitudinally extensive T2 hyperintense spinal cord lesion from C6 to T10, predominantly involving the gray matter. The appearance of the anomaly is said to resemble the letter H.

terms.name: Abnormal testosterone: estradiol ratio
terms.definition: Any deviation from the normal ratio of testosterone and estradiol (the primary sex steroids) to each other. The testosterone:estradiol ratio is derived from total testosterone in ng/dL and total estradiol in pg/mL, and expressed as T:E. Normal ranges are affected by sex, age, and other factors.

terms.name: Abnormal circulating insulin-like growth factor 3 concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环胰岛素样生长因子3浓度异常
terms.definition: The concentration of IGFBP-3 (Insulin-like Growth Factor-Binding Protein 3) in the blood circulation is outside the limits of normal.

terms.name: Decreased circulating insulin-like growth factor 3 concentration
terms.name_zh: 血循环胰岛素样生长因子3浓度降低
terms.definition: The concentration of insulin-like growth factor 3 concentration (IGF3) in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Airway chondritis
terms.definition: Inflammation of the cartilage of the airway, including especially the trachea and bronchi.

terms.name: Costochondritis
synonyms: Inflammation of he cartilage that connects the ribs to the sternum (breastbone)
terms.definition: inflammation of the costal cartilage (the cartilage that connects the ribs to the sternum). The typical presentation of costochondritis is bilateral parasternal chest wall pain exacerbated by deep breaths, coughing, and stretching. The upper (predominantly second through fifth) costochondral and/or costosternal junctions are most commonly involved. The areas of tenderness are not generally accompanied by heat, erythema, or localized swelling.

terms.name: History of ocular surgery
terms.definition: Past medical history of surgical procedure on the eye or its surroundings.

terms.name: Increased plantar fascia thickness
terms.definition: Increased thickness of the plantar fascia. This finding can be ascertained by ultrasound or magnetic resonance imaging.

terms.name: Increased mixed venous oxygen saturation
terms.name_zh: 混合静脉血氧饱和度升高
terms.definition: Oxygen saturation in mixed venous blood (SvO2), as measured in a sample of mixed venous blood drawn from the distal lumen of a catheter placed in the pulmonary artery, is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Decreased mixed venous oxygen saturation
terms.name_zh: 混合静脉血氧饱和度降低
terms.definition: Oxygen saturation in mixed venous blood (SvO2), as measured in a sample of mixed venous blood drawn from the distal lumen of a catheter placed in the pulmonary artery, is below the lower limit of normal.

terms.name: Chocolate brown blood
terms.definition: Characteristic chocolate-brown color of circulating blood with an elevated methemoglobin content.

terms.name: Elevated pCO2 gap
terms.definition: The difference between the venous-to-arterial carbon dioxide saturation (Pv-aCO2) is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Putaminal eye sign
terms.definition: An imaging anomly of the putamen that is thought to be pathognomic for MEGDEL syndrome (3-MethylGlutaconic aciduria, Deafness, Encephalopathy, Leigh-like syndrome MIM #614739). In stage 1 of the disease, T2 signal changes of the pallidum are present. In stage 2, swelling of the putamen and caudate nucleus is seen. The dorsal putamen contains an eye that shows no signal alteration and (thus) seems to be spared during this stage of the disease. It later increases, reflecting progressive putaminal involvement. Sparing of the mid dorsal putamen (showing normal signal surrounded by T2 hyperintense signal) is referred to as the putaminal eye.

terms.name: Decreased coracohumeral distance
terms.definition: Axial view on shoulder X-ray or MRI showing decreased distance between posterior border of the coracoid process and anterior border of the humeral head of less than 6 mm; subcoracoid impingement; decreased coracohumeral interval.

terms.name: Abnormal deltoid muscle morphology
terms.definition: Any structural anomaly of the deltoid muscle, the large triangular intrinsic shoulder muscle, so named because its shape resembles the inverted Greek letter delta.

terms.name: Deltoid muscle tear
terms.definition: An injury of the deltoid muscle of the shoulder or its tendon characterized by partial or complete rupture.

terms.name: Glenohumeral arthritis
terms.definition: Anteropostrior (AP), axillary, or Grashey (true AP) view X-ray of the shoulder showing radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis such as joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, subchondral cysts, and/or osteophyte formation in the glenohumeral joint.

terms.name: Dental root fusion
terms.definition: An anomaly of the roots of a multi-rooted tooth (such as a molar) in which the roots are not physically divided by bone or periodontal ligament space.

terms.name: Difficulty floating in water
terms.definition: A phenomenon whereby an individual struggles to float, cannot swim despite adequate training, or simply sinks. This phenomenon may be observed in individuals with conditions such as osteopetrosis that are characterized by substantially increased bone mineral density (which implies reduced bouyancy).

terms.name: Aortitis
terms.definition: Aortitis refers to inflammatory changes to the wall of the aorta and incorporates both infectious and non-infectious etiologies.

terms.name: Upper extremity claudication
terms.definition: Pain in an arm that is triggered by muscular exertion.

terms.name: Tongue claudication
terms.definition: Pain in the tongue induced by speaking or chewing.

terms.name: Cerebral perivascular enhancement pattern
terms.definition: Focal, regional or diffuse magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) enhancement of intracranial perivascular spaces (PVS). This enhancement pattern is recognizable by its topography that follows PVS distribution, particularly identifiable in regions where PVS predominate (centra semiovalia, basal ganglia and the brachium pontis)15 although it can be found throughout the whole brain. Depending on the perpendicular or parallel orientation of MRI sections to the long axis of PVS, enhanced PVS appear as dots or curvilinear elements respectively. Depending on the causal pathology, PVE may appear more linear or nodular.

terms.name: Long head of biceps tendon dislocation
terms.definition: Dislocation or subluxation of the long head of the biceps tendon out of the bicipital groove (as documented by magnetic resonance imaging of the shoulder) or dynamic ultrasound of the shoulder showing subluxation or dislocation of the long head of the biceps tendon out of the bicipital groove.

terms.name: Elevated circulating somatostatin concentration
terms.definition: The concentration of somatostatin in the blood corculation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Lack of attached gingiva
terms.definition: Absence of attached gingiva. The gingiva is subdivided into the nonattached free gingiva (which includes the gingival margin and the papillae) and the attached gingiva. The attached gingiva is tightly and unmovably bound to the periosteum via collagen type I fibers. The gingiva is keratinized and thicker than the mucosa to provide mechanical protection. The border between attached gingiva and mucosa constitutes the mucogingival junction. In vivo, it is sometimes visible as a white line . The oral mucosa is loosely connected to the periosteum and nonkeratinized. It is movable, thin, more fragile, translucent, and blood vessels are visible.

terms.name: Spontaneous diaphragmatic rupture
terms.definition: A full thickness tear of the diaphragm without significant trauma.

terms.name: Elevated alveolar-arterial (A-a) oxygen gradient
terms.name_zh: 肺泡-动脉氧分压差升高
terms.definition: An increase in the difference between the oxygen concentration in the alveoli and arterial system above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Abnormal concentration of circulating metanephrines
terms.name_zh: 循环甲氧基肾上腺素浓度异常
terms.definition: Adrenaline, noradrenaline and dopamine are degraded by catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) to form their inactive metabolites metanephrine, normetanephrine and 3-methoxytyramine (3-MT). When there is an indication for biochemical testing, such as suspicion of pheochromocytoma, metanephrine and normetanephrine metabolites are measured in plasma or 24-hour urine. This term represents an elevation of the concentration of metanephrine and normetanephrine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated circulating 3-O-methyldopa concentration
terms.name_zh: 循环3-O-甲基多巴浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of 3-O-methyldopa in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Elevated CSF 3-O-methyldopa concentration
terms.name_zh: 脑脊液3-O-甲基多巴浓度升高
terms.definition: The concentration of 3-O-methyldopa in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is above the upper limit of normal.

terms.name: Fixed fetal head flexion
terms.definition: An unchanging bending forward of the fetal head in the uterus as visualized by prenatal sonography. This sign can be defined as a lack of change in this position during the 30 min of observation. Additionally, identical head flexion is observable several times at intervals.

terms.name: Abnormal rectosigmoid index
terms.name_zh: 直肠乙状结肠指数异常
terms.definition: The rectosigmoid (R/S) ratio, a measure comparing rectal to sigmoid colon diameter, is below the lower limit of normal on prenatal ultrasound. The rectosigmoid is normally the widest segment of the fetal colon. If the rectosigmoid is narrower than the ascending or transverse colon above it), this is called a reversed rectosigmoid ratio or abnormal rectosigmoid index. The RS ratio is calculated by dividing the transverse rectal diameter by the sigmoid diameter. An R/S ratio of 1 or more is considered normal.

terms.name: Umbilical cord edema
terms.definition: Visible edema (swelling) in a cord with a minimal cross sectional area of 1-3 cm2. This may result from an excessive accumulation of Wharton jelly, resulting in a thick or edematous umbilical cord.

terms.name: Fetal enterolithiasis
terms.definition: Enterolithiasis (concretions or stones forming within the gastrointestinal tract) is a prenatal sonographic sign defined by hyperechogenic foci within the - often distended - fetal bowel.

terms.name: Malignant cells in CSF
terms.definition: The identification of malignant cells in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), generally by microscopic examination of the CSF.

terms.name: Greek warrior helmet sign
terms.definition: A prenatal sonographic finding characterized by a high forehead, prominent glabella, and a broad, un-tapered nasal bridge that merges directly into the brow line. This appearance is said to resemble a Greek (Corinthian) warrior helmet because the wide, solid vertical column down the center of the face is said to resemble the fixed, protective nose guard of a Corinthian helmet.

terms.name: Somatostatinoma
terms.definition: Somatostatinoma is a rare, functional neuroendocrine tumor (NET) that primarily arises in the pancreas and duodenum, characterized by excessive production of somatostatin.

terms.name: Erythematous scalp plaque
terms.definition: A circumscribed, palpable, potentially elevated, erythematous lesion > 1 cm in diameter and localized to the scalp. Erythematous plaques exhibiting erythema, i.e., abnormal redness of the skin due to localized dilation and congestion of superficial dermal capillaries, typically as a result of inflammation, irritation, infection, or vasodilation, and usually blanching with pressure.

terms.name: Positive hair pull test
terms.definition: An abnormal result of the hair pull test, in which the clinician selects 50 to 60 hairs and holds the bundle close to the scalp between the thumb, index finger, and long finger. The clinician then firmly pulls on the bundle using slow traction as the fingers slide down the hair shaft, avoiding a fast and forceful tug. The hair pulls are performed at the vertex, parietal areas, and the occipital area of the scalp. Next, the pulled hairs are counted. Any broken hairs that were extracted from the bundle during the pull are discarded. If more than 10 percent of the hairs in each bundle are removed from a scalp area, the hair pull test is considered positive.

terms.name: Loss of acquired purposeful hand skills
terms.name_zh: 获得性目的性手部技能丧失
terms.definition: A type of neurodevelopmental regression characterized by deterioration or disappearance of previously acquired voluntary, goal-directed hand movements, such as reaching, grasping, manipulating objects, or self-feeding.

terms.name: Loss of acquired spoken language
terms.definition: A type of neurodevelopmental regression characterized by deterioration or disappearance of previously acquired expressive verbal communication, including words, phrases, or sentences the individual had used meaningfully, after these skills had been acquired during development.

terms.name: Postnatal deceleration of headgrowth
terms.definition: Slowing of the rate of head circumference growth occurring after birth, in an individual with normal head circumference at birth, leading to progressive deviation from normal growth curves and, in many cases, acquired (postnatal, secondary) microcephaly.

terms.name: Foot small muscle atrophy
terms.definition: Wasting of the small muscles of the foot such as the abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, and the interossei muscles.
